madam president, the fundamental objective of the directive we are voting on today is to give greater flexibility and freedom to those member states which decide to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos on their territory. the agreement reached with the council, with its strengths and weaknesses, remains the heir to the three main principles of the european union in the management of gmos: the principles of precaution, transparency and protection of health and the environment. when the reforms are put into effect, it will be necessary to see, on the basis of experience, whether the mandatory coexistence measures are viable or whether they present the difficulty of how to put barriers in the field. what is clear is that conventional and organic farming must also be protected. we already have one of the most comprehensive regulations in the world on gmos, which the new proposed directive will serve to complete. we also have the european food safety authority, which has always been completely independent and must work continuously on risk assessment.
madam president, commissioner, i am sorry to have to tell you that we are being presented with a farce today. you know better than anyone that the freedom of a state to allow gm crops is a widespread imposition of gm food. because they know - as well as i do - that it is not possible to preserve peasant agriculture, organic or conventional agriculture, free of gmos unless in their delusions they think they will be able to stop the wind or the insects. because biodiversity, health, the environment, farming without dependence on multinationals, healthy food and food sovereignty remain among our main objectives, we want a directive to ban gmos and also to close the free trade agreement with the united states.
madam president, first of all i would like to congratulate the parties to this agreement, because we were faced with a very ideological and emotional debate and that makes solutions very difficult. in accordance with our legislation, the marketing of gmos is only allowed in the european union, with the utmost respect for human health and the environment, and always with the scientific support of the risk assessment of the european food safety authority, which is independent and rigorous. it is logical and legitimate, however, that there are countries opposed to their cultivation and that legal certainty had to be given to the companies that market them and to the states that want to exercise this right, because we were in an unsustainable situation because of the absence of an effective decision-making system that undermined our strength on the international scene. that is why i am very pleased about this agreement. this agreement will unlock a situation which was not acceptable, so that member states which want to grow gmos, previously always authorized, will be able to continue to do so, while those which do not want to do so will also be able to ban it. the text adopted ensures that the principles of the treaty on the functioning of the european union are respected.
in writing. the report approves the protocol setting out the fishing opportunities and financial contribution provided for in the fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe. its objective is to bring european tuna fishing in são tomé and príncipe into line with the scientific recommendations of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat). the rapporteur has inserted in the text a request to the commission and the council that parliament be kept informed of all stages of implementation and renewal of the protocol. the democratization of control of fisheries policy and its environmental sustainability are necessary conditions for securing employment and development in this sector. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and the democratic republic of são tomé and príncipe is part of the network of tuna fisheries agreements in west africa and allows eu vessels to fish in its waters. the previous protocol was in force from 13 may 2011 to 12 may 2014 and allowed 40 eu tuna vessels to fish. the financial contribution was €682 500 per year, of which approximately 35% was used to support são tomé and príncipe's fisheries policy. a new protocol was initialled on 19 december 2013 and will be valid for four years from 23 may 2014 and will allow 34 eu vessels to fish. the annual financial contribution is set at € 710 000 for the first three years and € 675 000 for the fourth year, of which € 325 000 will be used to support the sectoral policy of são tomé and príncipe. i think it is a balanced agreement and i have therefore voted in favour of approving the protocol, although i note, as does the rapporteur, the need to consider that the achievements in the field of sectoral cooperation are limited, a reality which must be changed.

in writing. we voted in favour of this recommendation because we think it is a balanced partnership agreement, as it emphasises support for the development of the fishing sector in são tomé, which has been very limited in the last twenty years. the aspects to which special attention is recommended include those related to the reliability of the assessment of são toméan fisheries resources, the development of control capacity by local authorities, the obligation to declare catches and the development of infrastructure in the sector. it requires a greater commitment on the part of the commission to verify the principles necessary for the correct absorption of aid, respecting the sovereignty and the choices and priorities of são tomé. the need to strengthen cooperation in the development of the são toméan fisheries sector is therefore emphasized as a prerequisite for achieving joint and sustainable exploitation of são toméan fisheries resources.

in writing. this report refers to the agreement signed between the republic of seychelles and the territory of mayotte, which acceded to the status of outermost region on 1 january 2014. the fishery resources in mayotte's exclusive economic zone have thus come under eu jurisdiction, which has required the adaptation of the old fisheries contracts to the rules of the common fisheries policy. due to the proximity between seychelles and mayotte, a limited number of seychelles vessels had traditionally fished in mayotte waters. the agreement allows this practice to continue, bringing it into line with european fishing rules. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. an eu-seychelles fisheries agreement has been in place since may 2003. it is the eu's most important agreement in the indian ocean. a 'access agreement' is now being drawn up between the two parties so that seychelles vessels can continue to fish in mayotte, a french outermost region for which territorial development is also being pursued. the agreement is for six years and provides for france, on behalf of the eu, to manage the agreement and the economic counterparts. it has no financial impact on the eu. it provides for a joint monitoring committee and places particular emphasis on the question of respect for human rights. the european fisheries sector has expressed interest in the agreement. it seems to be a balanced agreement, and that is why i voted in favour of it, in accordance with the recommendation of the european parliament's committee on fisheries and whereas the rapporteur of parliament has stressed in his report that the local population of mayotte should receive the full benefits of the agreement and, as it could not be otherwise, that the funds should be managed in a transparent and effective manner.

in writing. we have voted in favour of this recommendation endorsing the eu-republic of seychelles agreement as it is mutually beneficial, positive for the economic development of mayotte and seychelles, and complies with the rules of the common fisheries policy and the indian ocean tuna commission (iotc) on the protection of resources. the agreement will allow the continuation of traditional economic activity in the region, taking account of criteria of good management and protection of resources. it will also support the local economy and the development of the fishing infrastructure of mayotte and the republic of seychelles and strengthen the good relations between the latter and the eu.
in writing. the territory of mayotte became an outermost region of the eu on 1 january 2014. consequently, the exclusive economic zone of mayotte is now an integral part of union waters. the eu is therefore responsible for managing its fisheries resources. given the geographical proximity of mayotte and the seychelles, before the change in the status of mayotte, relations between european and seychelles fishing vessels with mayotte were governed by a private agreement which allowed some 30 vessels in total, including eight from the seychelles, to fish for migratory species in mayotte's waters, while at the same time allowing the development of mayotte's fisheries thanks to fees paid directly by shipowners to the french state services in mayotte. in view of these circumstances, i have voted to allow a limited number of seychelles-flagged vessels which have traditionally fished in mayotte's waters to continue to fish in mayotte's eez in accordance with the rules of the common fisheries policy.

in writing. the eu association treaties contain, in article 2, a clause which makes their validity conditional on respect for human rights. this condition is routinely violated: in the case of tunisia, from its very negotiations with the ben ali regime. this is yet another example of the hypocrisy of european foreign policy, which uses this article to legitimize or withdraw support for the signatory governments. in contrast, the economic objectives of these treaties are very clear: to deepen the economic liberalisation and dependence of the eu's associated states, to the benefit of european capital. this report is presented as a technical formality extending the existing eu-tunisia association treaty to bulgaria and romania. a vote against would mean further discrimination against the status of the other member states. however, i cannot vote in favour of a report which ratifies the current eu-tunisia association treaty. for all these reasons, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. the eu and tunisia signed a euro-mediterranean association agreement in 1995, which has been in force since 1998, and which includes a regular dialogue on political and security issues, economic, trade and financial cooperation - focusing mainly on the progressive liberalisation of trade - sustainable development of the region and investment, and social, cultural and educational cooperation, in particular through intercultural dialogue, control of migration, skills development, promotion of labour law and gender equality. the participation of bulgaria and romania in this euro-mediterranean association agreement with tunisia is a natural consequence of their accession to the eu and therefore the conclusion of this protocol to the euro-mediterranean agreement with tunisia should be approved, and i have therefore voted in favour of it.

in writing. - we abstained in the vote on euromed. the protocol that is being adopted is a formal procedure with no major practical consequences, but we wanted to express our disagreement with the eu's policy towards tunisia. for example, with the loan agreed last year, which was granted on similar conditions to those usually set by the imf, and with the mobility agreement, which opens the way to admission agreements that delegate the management of migration flows in the african country.

in writing. the spanish socialist delegation supports the agreement to give flexibility to member states wishing to ban gmos on their territory because it considers that the new directive complies with the eu's basic principles regarding gmos: the precautionary principle, transparency and the protection of health and the environment. we believe that more could have been done in some safeguard measures, but the agreement reached corresponds to the current scientific evidence and, above all, will serve to unblock the situation of unprotected member states who did not want to include gmos in their crops and who had to appear before the courts at the request of some biotechnology companies. in this period, which will begin next spring, it will be necessary to take note of the effectiveness of the coexistence measures which will now be binding in order to see whether the directive actually fulfils its task of preventing unwanted pollution, especially in the case of traditional and organic farming.
in writing. following an initial commission proposal, the european parliament voted in 2011 to extend the list of cases where the cultivation of genetically modified organisms (gmos) is restricted or prohibited. in 2014, the council adopted a radically different proposal, which greatly limited the cases of gmo crop bans. while parliament was able to partially restore its initial position through the amendments made to the report as it was passed by the environment committee, the final wording departs from what was approved in 2011 and introduces a huge ambiguity with regard to the cases in which states could ban the cultivation of a gmo. the regulation of gmos was also returned to the internal market and the financial liability regime previously advocated by parliament was almost completely diluted. the new wording makes it easier for the large multinational gmo companies to market their crops despite the opposition of european states and peoples concerned about their consequences, without there being an adequate mechanism to compensate for the risks arising from this liberalization. for these reasons, i have voted against.
in writing. the adoption of the european parliament and council directive amending directive 2001/18/ec will give flexibility to the eu states to restrict or prohibit crops containing genetically modified organisms (gmos) on their own territories. the disagreements between pro- and anti-gmo countries have blocked this proposal since 2010. this new legislation achieves a balance and simplifies the procedure so that countries can choose the regime to follow without interfering with or clashing with the criteria for the approval of the body in question issued by the european food safety authority. for all these reasons, and in line with the position of the alde group, i have voted in favour of this legislation.
in writing. i voted against the compromise reached on consistency. the basque country is a declared gmo-free territory and that is the policy we believe europe should promote and approve

in writing. the neoliberal majority has voted in favour of a directive giving more power to multinational biotechnology companies. we voted against because we believe that the amendment of the directive would speed up the authorisation process for new gmos at european level, which represents a risk to the environment, biodiversity and human and animal health. for spain, the country with the largest area of gm crops in the eu, this would mean the uncontrolled entry of gm crops, gm contamination of the food chain, as well as impacts on the organic farming sector. the new directive does not provide any compensation for farmers whose crops have been contaminated with gm varieties. there is a danger of creating a 'two-speed europe': those states most sensitive to the sustainability of their agriculture would be able to ban these crops, while the entry of new transgenic varieties would be given free rein in those states where the interest of the biotechnology industry prevails. the agribusiness lobby has long been pushing for the relaxation of restrictions and the liberalisation - through treaties such as atci and ceta - of the entry of unauthorised gm food into the eu.

in writing. i voted in favour of this recommendation at second reading, taking into account that the main objective of this legislative change is to give more flexibility and legal certainty to member states wishing to ban, in all or part of their territory, the cultivation of gmos authorised at european level, including on environmental grounds such as the protection of biodiversity and the maintenance of habitats and ecosystems. it is important to include in the legislation the obligation of the member states to ensure the coexistence of crops and to avoid, in particular, any cross-border pollution. it is also important to bear in mind the growing disapproval of gmos, and in particular of their presence in human food, by european public opinion. the text submitted for the vote in the european parliament is intended to clarify certain aspects of the council's position which have not been sufficiently clear to parliament, as well as the proposals submitted at first reading which the council did not have to consider but which are of particular importance.

in writing. - euskal herria bildu voted against the report on the possibility for member states to restrict or prohibit the cultivation of gmos because the outcome raises a scenario in which, on the one hand, the right of member states to prohibit the cultivation of gmos is restricted but, on the other, the rights of multinational companies are strengthened. in our opinion, opting out of gm cultivation needs to be absolutely legally watertight – and, unfortunately, in the legislation before us this is far from being the case. what we are left with are legal loopholes enabling biotech companies to take countries to court. the concept of a private company being placed on the same footing as a sovereign country is deeply undemocratic and this is a worrying precedent. furthermore, the liability system has also been removed so that no compensation will be offered to non-gm farmers whose produce is contaminated by gmos. the european parliament entered the negotiations with a very good text which could and should have been defended but parliament has not managed to defend it. eh bildu is deeply disappointed by the text adopted today, as we simply believe that we must stop gmos in the eu.

in writing. the new regulatory framework on the authorisation of gm crops not only fails to address the shortcomings of the previous system, but also renationalizes an issue which, by its nature, must be dealt with at european level. the pollution of crops, the threat to biodiversity and other effects of gmos need european solutions. the cases in which the prohibition is to be applied do not include health risks. finally, this new scheme facilitates the approval of new gmos beyond the only currently permitted gmo, mon810 maize, by giving multinationals a great deal of power in the european authorisation process. i have therefore voted against.

in writing. the aim of the report is to transpose into european law a number of provisions applicable to fisheries in the gfcm (general fisheries commission for the mediterranean) agreement area, to which the eu and several member states (including spain) are parties. while the commission's proposal was even more restrictive than the gfcm recommendations in areas such as the protection of red coral and other marine animals, the report was diluted in its parliamentary procedure, which added to other shortcomings already present initially (such as inadequate monitoring of compliance with the recommendations) justifies my vote against it.
in writing. the main functions of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm), set up in 1949, are to promote the development, conservation and management of living biological resources, to develop and recommend conservation measures and to promote cooperation projects for training in the mediterranean, the black sea and adjacent waters. the last transposition of gfcm measures into eu law took place in 2011. subsequently, in 2011 and 2012, the gfcm adopted new management measures for the sustainable exploitation of red coral which should be incorporated into our legislation. other recommendations adopted by the gfcm include measures to reduce incidental catches of seabirds, sea turtles, monk seals and cetaceans; measures to ensure a high level of protection for sharks and rays; and measures for fisheries of small pelagic stocks in the adriatic sea. in order to incorporate these recommendations into eu law, it is proposed to amend regulation (eu) no 1343/2011, which is why i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. the aim of the report is to transpose into european law a number of provisions applicable to fisheries in the gfcm (general fisheries commission for the mediterranean) agreement area, to which the eu and several member states (including spain) are parties. while the commission's proposal was even more restrictive than the gfcm recommendations in areas such as the protection of red coral and other marine animals, the report was diluted in its parliamentary procedure, which added to other shortcomings already present initially (such as inadequate monitoring of compliance with the recommendations) justifies my vote against it.
in writing. we voted against the report presented because it sought to lower, by way of derogations, the level of protection measures proposed by the commission, on the basis of the recommendations of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm), for the sustainable exploitation of red coral, to reduce incidental catches of seabirds, sea turtles, monk seals and cetaceans in fishing activities in the gfcm agreement area, and to strengthen the protection of endangered species of sharks and rays. the commission is not overzealous in protecting the environment and any protection of the biological resources of the mediterranean is not very much in the way of the devastation of the sea by human activity. there are therefore no compelling reasons to amend the commission's original proposal.
in writing. the main functions of the gfcm are to promote the development, conservation and management of living biological resources, to develop and recommend conservation measures and to promote cooperation projects for training. at its annual sessions in 2011 and 2012, the gfcm adopted technical measures for the sustainable exploitation of red coral, the reduction of incidental catches of seabirds, sea turtles and cetaceans, and the conservation of monk seals, sharks and rays, which are recommendations to be incorporated into union law. i have therefore voted in favour of amending this regulation to include the measures contained in the recommendations of the gfcm and thus ensure the present and future sustainability of the resources of the mediterranean sea, the black sea and the adjacent waters.

in writing. the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) was established in 1949 by an international agreement. its area of competence covers the mediterranean, the black sea and adjacent waters. its main functions are to promote the development, conservation and management of living biological resources, to develop and recommend conservation measures and to promote cooperation projects for training. the european parliament and the council intend to amend this regulation to include the measures set out in the recommendations of the gfcm. the cgpm recommendations establish a sufficient level of legislative protection which must be applied first by the contracting parties, before further measures are taken. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution to transpose the recommendations of the gfcm into union law.
in writing. the aim of the report is to transpose into european law the recommendations adopted by the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean in 2011-2013. these recommendations relate to the sustainable exploitation of red coral, the mitigation of bycatch of seabirds, sea turtles, monk seals and cetaceans and the protection of sharks and rays, fragile species and ecosystems that we need to protect and carefully manage. the commission's proposal is therefore welcome, even if it is three years after the adoption of the recommendations. in the meantime, some member states have already transposed and applied the recommendations. implementation at eu level must, on the one hand, take due account of existing national measures and, on the other, reflect the spirit and the letter of these recommendations, which are the result of long negotiations between the contracting parties. that is what motivated my report, which was adopted by the committee on fisheries by a large majority (20 in favour, 4 against and one abstention). today i have received an important negotiating mandate for the first tripartite dialogue with the council and the commission, which will take place on 2 march.
in writing. the objective of this proposal is to transpose into union law the recommendations of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm). in particular, it includes measures for the sustainable exploitation of red coral, the reduction of incidental catches of seabirds, sea turtles, monk seals and cetaceans in fishing activities in the gfcm agreement area and protection against fishing activities for sharks and rays. all of these go beyond the protection provided at community level by the habitats directive and are in line with the efforts made by many member states. for all these reasons, the vote was in favour.
in writing. - we voted against the report because it sought to lower, by way of derogation, the level of protection measures proposed by the commission, on the basis of the recommendations of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm), for the sustainable exploitation of red coral, to reduce incidental catches of seabirds, sea turtles, monk seals and cetaceans in fishing activities in the gfcm agreement area, and to strengthen the protection of endangered species of sharks and rays. the commission is not overzealous in protecting the environment and any protection of the biological resources of the mediterranean is not very much in the way of the devastation of the sea by human activity. there are therefore no compelling reasons to amend the commission's original proposal.

in writing. the conservation of red coral in mediterranean waters should be a key objective of european fisheries legislation. we must pursue the furtive practices and strengthen the legislation on sanctions. in addition, european legislation must ensure the social sustainability of fishing activities. fisheries must be environmentally sustainable, but small-scale and shallow-water fishing must also be allowed. we must remember that this activity is the livelihood of many families on the mediterranean coast.

in writing. the european council conclusions of 18 december stated that the new investment approach, together with the commitment of member states to intensify structural reforms and to pursue growth-friendly fiscal consolidation, will provide the basis for growth and jobs in europe. however, it is clear that the obsession with structural reforms and fiscal adjustment policies has not improved the economic performance of the eu and the euro area since 2010, as evidenced by low economic growth, high unemployment figures - unbearable in countries like spain - and the near-deflation scenario. that approach is not working, even if we add the investment plan for europe, because structural reforms and rapid fiscal consolidation are procyclical policies. instead, the pace of fiscal adjustment must be slowed down and policies capable of generating short-term growth must be put on the table. the council should propose new broad guidelines for the union, focusing on countercyclical productive reforms and the implementation of new fiscal policies. the european council should support increased flexibility in the interpretation of the stability and growth pact.
in writing. – on page 1 of the conclusions of the european council dated 18 december 2014, it is stated that ‘the new focus on investment, coupled with member states’ commitment to intensifying structural reforms and to pursuing growth-friendly fiscal consolidation, will provide the foundation for growth and jobs in europe’. however, if we note the low economic growth, high unemployment figures and near-deflation scenario in our continent, it is clear that the focus on structural reforms and fiscal adjustment policies has not improved the economic performance of the eu or the eurozone since 2010. it is pretty clear that the current policy mix is not working, even if we add to it the investment plan for europe, because structural reforms and rapid fiscal consolidation are pro-cyclical policies. instead, the pace of fiscal adjustment must be reduced and policies capable of generating growth in the short term should be put in place. thus, the european council should come up with new general orientations for the union focusing on anti-cyclical productive reforms and the implementation of new fiscal policies. the european council should support increased flexibility of interpretation of the stability and growth pact.

flows of regular migrants and also smuggling. it has been said during this meeting today that cooperation with third countries is of great importance. there is no doubt about this. i just want to nature of such criteria, although elements such as the total number of asylum seekers per capita and gdp will certainly be included. our objective at this stage is to avoid extensive negotiations on a comprehensive list of criteria and instead to agree on a minimum set of criteria. this will allow us to launch a pilot as soon as possible. this pilot phase will give us the opportunity to adjust the practical modalities of the implementation of the distribution key. in the light of experience acquired last time, we will consider any possible further criteria in order to take into account the president-in-office of the council. - mr president, honourable members, i would like to thank you for giving me the opportunity to intervene on the recent events of people-smuggling in the mediterranean region. i could not agree more with the view that abusing the hopes of desperate people is a crime. we are speaking of a true human tragedy. the council, of course, is fully aware of the grave risks to human lives and to the fundamental rights of thousands of immigrants, as well of as the challenges for the union emerging from this new route used by smugglers who ferry out their passengers, mainly from turkey, towards italy. the council’s competent bodies, in close cooperation with the other institutions, agencies and stakeholders concerned, intend to address this issue as a matter of priority. in the context of fighting the smuggling of immigrants on the criminal level, i would like to point out that the council adopted in 2010 the eu policy cycle for organised and serious international crime, which established a multiannual policy cycle and a clear methodology for setting, implementing and elevating priorities in the fight against organised and serious international crime. in the framework of this policy cycle, the council set priorities for the fight against serious and organised crime for the cycle 2014-2017, including the fight against facilitation of illegal immigration and trafficking of human beings in the following terms: to disrupt organised crime groups involved in facilitation of illegal immigration operating in the source countries, at the main entry points to the eu, on the main route and, where evidence-based, on alternative channels; to reduce organised crime groups and the abuse of legal channels for migration, including the use of fraudulent documents as a means for facilitating illegal immigration; and to disrupt organised crime groups involved in intra-eu human trafficking and human trafficking from the most prevalent external source countries for the purpose of labour exploitation and sexual exploitation, including those groups using legal business structures to facilitate their criminal activities. during the cycle, four-year strategic goals are defined for each crime priority, which are implemented by operational action plans, one per priority and per year. honourable members, the very important and fruitful debate that we had today clearly proved that it is our joint challenge and joint priority to step up efforts to prevent the smuggling of immigrants, to fight it and to prosecute those involved in such activities. we look forward with great interest to the commission’s assessment of the existing instruments as announced by commissioner avramopoulos just now. to achieve the objectives of fighting against these criminal situations, it is crucial that all stakeholders make an active contribution. along with the council and the commission, the european parliament has a fundamental role to play in this respect. the council stands ready to consider all the necessary actions and measures and to report to the european parliament on their adoption and implementation.

president-in-office of the council. - madam president, honourable members, the council has been asked to speak on the issue of surveillance of lawyers in the european union. we understand that an oral question on the subject has also been presented by honourable member sargentini, who referred to the alleged surveillance of a law firm by a national security agency of a member state. first of all, i would like to point out that the council presidency is not in a position to make any comments about an allegation that a member state’s secret services carry out secret surveillance of lawyers and their clients. under the lisbon treaty the maintenance of law and order and, in particular, the safeguarding of internal security are responsibilities of the member states. the council is therefore not informed of any surveillance activities carried out by the national departments responsible for safeguarding national security. i would also like to point out that the collection and processing of personal data by such national security services is currently not regulated by eu law, as neither the 1995 data protection directive nor the 2008 framework decision on data protection applies to them. the 2012 commission proposal for a directive on data protection by competent authorities for the purpose of prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences explicitly states that the directive shall not apply to the processing of personal data in the course of an activity concerning national security. for the same reason the presidency is not in a position to express itself as to the compatibility of these alleged activities with the charter of fundamental rights. the eu directive on the right of access to a lawyer states that member states shall respect the confidentiality of communication between suspects or accused persons and their lawyers in the exercise of their right of access to a lawyer. however, this provision, like the whole directive, is without prejudice to the work carried out, for example, by national intelligence services to safeguard national security in accordance with the treaties.
member of the commission. - madam president, the commission is concerned about media reports of member states’ intelligence services putting client-lawyer communications under surveillance. the right to privacy, including communication between clients and lawyers, as protected by article 7, and the procedural rights protected by articles 47 and 48 of the charter are of the utmost importance in the eu. however, it should be pointed out that the charter is applicable only to the member states where eu law is implemented. the matter of national security remains within the competences of the member states so, where the member states initiate secret surveillance activities for national security reasons, these fall outside eu law. consequently the charter is generally not applicable. that being said, the exemption clause needs to be interpreted strictly. in the light of settled case law of the court of justice, any member state which seeks to take advantage of an exemption needs to prove that it is necessary to have recourse to it in order to protect the state’s essential security interests. where the charter does not apply, the national systems provide fundamental rights protection procedures that are applicable in these cases. the commission also aims at a high level of protection of fair trial rights in the european union. since 2009 we have made considerable progress in this direction, with the adoption of three directives: on the right of interpretation and translation in 2010; on the right to information in 2012; and, recently, on the right of access to a lawyer. the directive on the right of access to a lawyer needs to be transposed by member states by 27 november 2016 and the commission will closely monitor this process. article 4 of the directive clearly sets out the principle of respect for the confidentiality of communication between suspects or accused persons and their lawyer in the exercise of the right of access to a lawyer. however, it should be underlined that the directive focuses on the rights of suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings. this is why it clarifies, in its recitals, that confidentiality applies only to genuine communication in the exercise of the rights of defence between the lawyer and a suspect and/or accused person. it does not apply to lawyers who are involved in the alleged criminal activities of the suspect or accused person.

in writing. the european ombudsman has during this period successfully fulfilled his mission to investigate complaints against eu institutions, bodies, offices and agencies. as you know, the european ombudsman's office initiates inquiries following complaints received (341 in 2013) or on its own initiative (9 in 2013). i consider the european ombudsman to be an example of independence and transparency, and to ensure full respect for the rights of citizens and the right to good administration. i would like to highlight in this connection the presentation of the new version of the european code of good administrative behaviour, which calls on the new commission to adopt binding rules and principles on administrative procedures in the eu and to present a draft regulation.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report after assessing the work carried out by the european ombudsman, ms emily o'reilly, during 2013, and after examining how the daily work of this institution contributes to remedying maladministration in the actions of the union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies towards citizens. in my view, this institution must continue to play a key role within the union, always offering the citizen the greatest possible accessibility and ease of contact. in 2013, the ombudsman registered contacts with 23 245 citizens who requested her services through the ombudsman's portal. the growing impact of this institution is shown by the fact that, as regards the breakdown of claims by country, spain topped the list with 416 claims.
in writing. the spanish socialists have voted in favour of the ombudsman's 2013 activity report. i would like to make it clear that we voted against amendments nos 5, 6 and 7 by the ecr group because, although we share the need to put an end to the troika and the harmful effects of 'austerity' policies, the troika is not part of the union's treaties and is therefore not under the supervision of the european ombudsman. the eurosceptic parties want to weaken the european institutions by demagogy and that cannot be supported; that is why we voted against these amendments. we demand greater transparency in the functioning of all the institutions in order to build a socially engaged, just and equal europe.

in writing. we have abstained. we welcome the work of the ombudsman and support any changes that would improve the effectiveness, efficiency and impact of her fundamental work. however, it abstained from voting on this resolution because it believes that the ombudsman's task of monitoring the transparency processes should be able to be carried out without any limitation and should be enforceable against the institutions themselves. the ombudsman should not only be able to access more information and documentation than that provided by the commission, but should also be able to access 'all the information' of the ongoing negotiations, so as to ensure that the form and content of the negotiations do not breach the law or infringe the rights of citizens. the ombudsman should place particular emphasis on investigating and being able to act against the austerity policies promoted by the troika, both from the formal point of view (since they undermine any process of legitimate justification for them) and from the point of view of their impact on the guarantee of the economic and social rights of europeans and european women.

in writing. the european ombudsman, emily oreilly, was elected by the european parliament on 3 july 2013 and sworn in before the court of justice of the european union on 30 september 2013. the annual report for 2013 therefore covers only part of the work of the european ombudsman's office under its mandate. it was submitted to the president of the european parliament on 15 september 2014 and to the committee on petitions on 24 september 2014. the annual report has been updated to make it as accessible and easy to contact as possible. the ombudsman also outlined her new strategy towards 2019. the strategy is based on three key concepts: impact, relevance and visibility. it aims to carry out more strategic research on systemic problems, to strengthen the role of the ombudsman by actively contributing to key debates in the eu, and to increase the institution's visibility by encouraging its outreach to stakeholders and by highlighting and drawing public attention to important issues. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal.
in writing. i voted in favour of this report on the activities of the european ombudsman in 2013, which validates the good management of nikiforos diamandouros, outgoing european ombudsman, and emily oreilly, the first woman elected to the post in july 2013. in 2013, 23 245 citizens requested assistance from the ombudsman's services, 350 investigations were initiated and 461 were concluded. i would like to highlight some important inquiries initiated by the ombudsman, such as those concerning transparency in the negotiations on the atci, the reporting of irregularities in the eu institutions, transparency in the commission's expert groups, the 'revolving doors' cases, fundamental rights in cohesion policy or the european citizens' initiative. the ombudsman's work contributes to strengthening the structures and institutions of accountability and transparency at european level, to promoting good administration for all eu citizens and residents, and to improving the quality of democracy in the eu, playing a key role in addressing citizens' concerns.

in writing. libya is a chaotic state that has practically failed. the socialists and democrats call on the eu to do everything possible to support stabilisation in libya and the un-led talks in geneva, to bring together all the factions in the country and to put an end to what could become a full-blown civil war. it is essential for the country to be secure again in order to restore the democratic transition process which the libyan people need and for which they have mobilised. i voted in favour of the resolution on the situation in libya because we cannot allow another scenario of war, suffering and destruction in libya, which could lead to the disintegration of the country. we cannot allow the proliferation of weapons or the country to become a sanctuary for terrorist organizations. european and regional security is threatened in libya. the eu should contribute to a un-mandated intervention in the country, in cooperation with the african union and the arab league, to achieve security conditions and a return to the democratic transition process.
in writing. the resolution on the situation in libya contains statements with which we do not disagree and which are obvious at this stage. it also stressed that 'there is no military solution to the current conflict' and supported the negotiations under the auspices of the united nations. i think, however, that parliament's position should be more forceful and critical. the military solution is not acceptable, but the text does not mention - much less condemn - the fact that the current situation is also a consequence of a nato intervention, which not only did not achieve its stated objective but also contributed to the increase in violence and, in the process, destroyed libyan state structures. i also believe that support for the un negotiations must go hand in hand with initiatives such as those being taken by the neighbouring countries, particularly algeria, to initiate a dialogue between the rival factions, which have in fact created two parallel state structures. the shortcomings of the resolution put to the vote forced me to abstain.

in writing. i voted in favour, considering that since the fall of colonel gaddafi, libya has been experiencing great political instability and serious internal divisions, circumstances which have facilitated the growth of terrorist groups, putting the very security of the state at serious risk. the growing humanitarian crisis and the political polarisation of the conflict in libya, which risks reaching a point of no return in the dialogue between the parties to the conflict, are of great concern. the various libyan factions must make every effort to redress the situation and establish a road map leading to a ceasefire. the search for solutions through political dialogue is the only possible solution to the conflict. it is also of great concern that reports show that isil is training fighters in libya and establishing a branch in the eastern part of the country, posing a risk to the stability of the entire region. the international community must assist libya in rebuilding the state and in creating effective national forces capable of ensuring security, order and peace in the country, all of which are crucial elements for democratic governance.

in writing. we socialists support the sovereignty, territorial integrity, unity and independence of ukraine. that is why we support the new government of ukraine, which is trying to reform the country. i voted for the resolution because i believe that the best defence of ukraine's sovereignty and independence will be to carry out swiftly those reforms which are necessary to have a reliable and impartial judicial system, to promote the rule of law, to eradicate corruption, to decentralize power and to protect press freedom and the rights of minorities. the minsk protocol is the reference document for achieving peace. we urge all parties to fully implement the protocol. we stand with the innocent civilians who are suffering in the areas affected by the conflict in eastern ukraine. we call for more humanitarian aid to reach them and urge all parties to immediately stop the fighting. there is no military solution to that crisis. a peaceful solution must be found through an inclusive national dialogue for reconciliation.
in writing. the resolution on the situation in ukraine put to the vote brings together all the falsehoods that have been spread in the media about the conflict in that country and makes an analysis whose sole purpose is to justify, on the one hand, the european trade policy towards eastern europe and, on the other, the geopolitical reasoning of the united states, which is why i voted against it with full conviction. thus, the text focuses on attacking the russian-speaking militants, calling them terrorists, and condemns their criminal conduct, while the use of force by the ukrainian authorities does not deserve the slightest reproach. nowhere in the text is there any mention of a coup d'état. on the other hand, the resolution opens the door to ukraine's accession to nato and, whenever the opportunity arises, russia's attitude is blamed for the situation, while the united states, a country involved in the coup d'état, is not mentioned in the entire text.
in writing. we socialists support the sovereignty, territorial integrity, unity and independence of ukraine. that is why we support the new government of ukraine, which is trying to reform the country. i voted for the resolution because i believe that the best defence of ukraine's sovereignty and independence will be to carry out swiftly those reforms which are necessary to have a reliable and impartial judicial system, to promote the rule of law, to eradicate corruption, to decentralize power and to protect press freedom and the rights of minorities. the minsk protocol is the reference document for achieving peace. we urge all parties to fully implement the protocol. we stand with the innocent civilians who are suffering in the areas affected by the conflict in eastern ukraine. we call for more humanitarian aid to reach them and urge all parties to immediately stop the fighting. there is no military solution to that crisis. a peaceful solution must be found through an inclusive national dialogue for reconciliation.

in writing. we voted against the resolution on the situation in ukraine because, in the face of the conflict situation that has been going on for months, and in the face of the current weakness of the ceasefire, it continues to consider russia as the sole responsible party for the conflict, while the european union maintains a defiant position by insisting on sanctions against russia, which so far have only led to a crisis situation in the agricultural sector with significant consequences for farmers.

in writing. i voted in favour to show the european parliament's willingness to contribute to the resolution of the conflict in eastern ukraine. the conflict situation, far from improving, continues to experience a ceaseless deterioration, a sign of which is the continuous drop of deaths that occur in the east of the country as a result of the clashes. according to a united nations report, 4,317 people have lost their lives in eastern ukraine, including nearly 1,000 since the minsk ceasefire agreement of 5 september 2014, which remains unimplemented months after its signing. the human rights violations in eastern ukraine and crimea, where tatars and other minorities, particularly religious ones, are the object of concrete human rights violations, are also of great concern. the illegal annexation of the crimean peninsula by russia is contrary to international law and constitutes a violation of international treaties to which russia is a party. the european union must continue its diplomatic efforts to ease the conflict and support the ukrainian government in the process of political and economic reforms it has embarked upon.

in writing. the resolution on the situation in ukraine put to the vote brings together all the falsehoods that have been spread in the media about the conflict in that country and makes an analysis whose sole purpose is to justify, on the one hand, the european trade policy towards eastern europe and, on the other, the geopolitical reasoning of the united states, which is why i voted against it with full conviction. thus, the text focuses on attacking the russian-speaking militants, calling them terrorists, and condemns their criminal conduct, while the use of force by the ukrainian authorities does not deserve the slightest reproach. nowhere in the text is there any mention of a coup d'état. the resolution also opens the door to ukraine's accession to nato. at the same time, the european union's role is limited to helping ukraine implement the association agreement, which will undoubtedly contribute to widening inequalities in ukraine and subjecting that country to the interests of the european powers.
in writing. the situation in ukraine is still very delicate and much work remains to be done to ensure a positive resolution of the conflict in the region. despite this situation, the democratically elected ukrainian government's firm political commitment to peace on its territory and the planning of a process of stabilising reforms for the country should be positively noted. the present government must strive to get its nation back on track, thus guaranteeing the well-being of its citizens. to this end, it must carry out important reforms, including the need to create an independent anti-corruption office, which would serve to eradicate systematic corruption in the country. the european institutions must give their full support to the efforts of the new government, which will benefit ukrainians, their neighbours and all other european citizens. the continuation of russia's aggressive and expansionist policy is also totally reprehensible. the eu must continue to encourage diplomatic channels, but also maintain existing sanctions and avoid as far as possible abuses of power by russia. that is why i am voting in favour of this proposal.

in writing. for european socialists the internal situation in egypt since the revolution, its process of democratization and stability are very important. our group calls on the egyptian authorities to release immediately and unconditionally all those detained for exercising their right to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly. i voted for the resolution on the situation in egypt because it is a key country for the european union because of its regional role and its continuing contribution to the israeli-palestinian conflict, as has been so clearly demonstrated in the negotiation of the recent ceasefire in gaza and also in cooperation and the fight against the islamic state and other regional threats. we want to see egypt in the right direction for the democratic transition. we urge the egyptian authorities to work with respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. the eu does not accept harassment, intimidation or censorship of political opponents, representatives of civil society and minorities. the parliamentary elections called for march are essential to give a real boost to the democratic process, and they must be guaranteed to be free and fair.
in writing. the resolution proposed for vote in the case of egypt contains key issues, such as denouncing the introduction of new legislation on public order which, among other things, may make a citizen liable to prosecution in military jurisdiction in the event that there are indications of a crime committed in the public domain. it also calls for the release of the 167 mps elected in 2011 who are currently in prison, condemns the mass death sentences and denounces the situation of the lgbt community, in which the government's repression has reached the point of passing a "law on libertinaje" that condemns the free expression of sexual orientation of people. however, the resolution does not include an express request for the opening of the rafah crossing, which prevents the inhabitants of gaza from communicating with the outside world and is of a markedly intrusive nature, which is why i abstained.

in writing. since the uprising that overthrew hosni mubarak in january 2012, egypt has experienced times of great political turmoil, yet remains one of the few countries in the region that enjoys political stability. in recent months, measures have been implemented in egypt which have raised concerns about the human rights situation in the country. however, we have seen some very positive developments in the last week: the call for parliamentary elections on 21 march, the release of jaled al qazzaz, former adviser to president morsi, and the men arrested in a cairo bathhouse on 7 december are examples of this. i understand and share the concern of parliament about the developments in egypt, but there are also signs of improvement in the human rights situation in the country in the light of recent events, so that while we must be forceful in demanding respect for fundamental rights, we must at the same time encourage the steps that egypt is taking in this direction.

in writing. the fact that we are currently discussing so many points in the european parliament on international affairs and human rights issues is a testament to the complexity of the world situation. this includes the current situation in egypt, which is the subject of our resolution. i am following the situation in egypt and i personally appreciate its role as a certain element of stability on a regional scale. however, in my view, the limitation of fundamental freedoms and human rights should not be a barrier to this stability. unfortunately, this is happening in egypt in some cases at the moment, and i agree that the european parliament is reacting to this in the form of a resolution.

in writing. the resolution proposed for vote in the case of egypt contains key issues, such as denouncing the introduction of new legislation on public order which, among other things, may make a citizen liable to prosecution in military jurisdiction in the event that there are indications of a crime committed in the public domain. it also calls for the release of the 167 mps elected in 2011 who are currently in prison, condemns the mass death sentences and denounces the situation of the lgbt community, in which the government's repression has reached the point of passing a "law on libertinaje" that condemns the free expression of sexual orientation of people. however, the resolution does not include an express request for the opening of the rafah crossing, which prevents the inhabitants of gaza from communicating with the outside world and is of a markedly intrusive nature, which is why i abstained.
in writing. egypt has experienced two revolutions in just over two years. al sisi's government has created the architecture to implement a repressive legal framework that frontally attacks the fundamental freedoms of association, expression and press, the building blocks of any democratic state, which is a serious obstacle to the consolidation of a democratic and rule of law state in egypt. the interference of military courts in civil matters is another example of the serious situation of violation of basic rights that the country is going through. similarly, the discrimination suffered by women and the lgbt community is alarming. the egyptian state has an obligation to protect all its fellow citizens, regardless of political ideology, gender, sexual orientation or religion.
in writing. — i vote in favour and support this resolution fully. i express my grave concern about the on-going restrictions of fundamental democratic rights, notably the freedom of expression, association and assembly, political pluralism and rule of law in egypt; i call for an end to all acts of violence, incitement, hate speech, harassment, intimidation or censorship against political opponents, protesters, journalists, bloggers, students, trade unionists, women’s rights activists, civil society actors and minorities by state authorities, security forces and services, and other groups in egypt; i condemn the excessive use of violence against protesters. i want to emphasise that respect for freedom of the press, information and opinion (online and offline) and political pluralism are fundamental to democracy; i call on the egyptian authorities to guarantee that those freedoms can be exercised without arbitrary limitations and censorship in the country, and i call on authorities to ensure freedom of expression. i call for the immediate and unconditional release of all those detained for peacefully exercising their rights to freedom of expression, assembly and association, including the journalists mohammed fahmy, peter greste and baher mohamed, as well as those detained for their alleged membership of the muslim brotherhood; i call on the egyptian authorities to ensure the right to a fair trial in accordance with international standards.
in writing. for european socialists the internal situation in egypt since the revolution, its process of democratization and stability are very important. our group calls on the egyptian authorities to release immediately and unconditionally all those detained for exercising their right to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly. i voted for the resolution on the situation in egypt because it is a key country for the european union because of its regional role and its continuing contribution to the israeli-palestinian conflict, as has been so clearly demonstrated in the negotiation of the recent ceasefire in gaza and also in cooperation and the fight against the islamic state and other regional threats. we want to see egypt in the right direction for the democratic transition. we urge the egyptian authorities to work with respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. the eu does not accept harassment, intimidation or censorship of political opponents, representatives of civil society and minorities. the parliamentary elections called for march are essential to give a real boost to the democratic process, and they must be guaranteed to be free and fair.

in writing. i voted for this resolution thinking of the families of the two italian marines who have been imprisoned in india for more than two years. his case is controversial from the point of view of international law and the law of the sea. but they were going as military personnel on an official mission to protect a ship from their country, with all the authorizations. unfortunately, in the course of their mission, two indian fishermen were killed. the responsibility must be the italian state, the italian army or the superiors of the two imprisoned sailors. or the owner of the ship they were protecting against the threat of piracy in the indian ocean. there must be accountability and reparation for the families of the fishermen who were tragically killed in a misunderstanding between two boats. the indian government has still not filed charges after two years. to avoid further tragedy, the marines must return to their homes in italy. one of them seriously ill. and any dispute must be resolved in accordance with international law.

in writing. we abstained on this resolution. even understanding the importance of the common points that all the resolutions presented on this case had, such as that one of the marines suffers from a serious illness or that they have been imprisoned without being charged for the three years since the two soldiers allegedly killed two indian fishermen by confusing them with pirates, the podemos delegation has decided to abstain to point out that the process has met with an absolute lack of transparency, including the international dispute over the jurisdiction of the facts or the non-imputation of formal charges to the marines.
in writing. i voted in favour of requesting the indian authorities to resolve the case of the two italian marines arrested after being found guilty of the deaths of two fishermen on 15 february 2012, when an incident occurred in indian waters. it should be borne in mind that the two officers were on board an italian oil tanker in the framework of operations against piracy. on 10 may 2012, parliament adopted a resolution on maritime piracy, paragraph 30 of which stated that 'in accordance with international law, on the high seas, in all cases, including measures taken in the fight against piracy, the national jurisdiction of the flag state shall apply to the vessels concerned and to the military personnel employed on board', and noted that 'no authority other than the flag state may order the arrest or detention of the vessel, even as an investigative measure'. furthermore, delays in the process have resulted in the fact that, after almost three years, no official indictment has yet been made in connection with the shootings.

in writing. i regret the way the indian authorities are handling the case of the two italian sailors, who are still waiting to know what their fate will be, after three years. the delays that are taking place are violations of human rights. in addition to supporting the italian government, i consider that the eu must intervene to protect the rights of its citizens by calling for the application of the national jurisdiction of the flag state in accordance with international law, as already called for in the resolution of 10 may 2012, and urging the vp/hr to take all necessary measures to protect them and to seek to resolve this case urgently and satisfactorily. the commission and the council are also asked to attach the utmost importance to the case in their bilateral relations with india and, if necessary, to consider the adoption of restrictive measures to find a solution. i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.
in writing. on the night of 15 february 2012, the italian oil tanker enrica lexie crossed paths with the fishing vessel st. anthony off the coast of kerala, india. fearing a pirate attack, the italian military aboard the enrica lexie opened fire on the fisherman, resulting in the deaths of two indian fishermen. four days later, two italian sailors identified as the shooters were arrested by indian authorities. three years later, the indian authorities have still not filed charges and have denied the extension of the two detainees' residence permits in italy. since international law provides that criminal and disciplinary proceedings against an accused person must be brought before the authorities of the flag state - in this case the same as that of the accused - and that no other national authority has the right to exercise jurisdiction or to carry out investigative tasks, the human rights of seafarers must be respected and the european union external action service must ensure that they are respected and that a speedy and satisfactory resolution of the conflict is reached, as reflected in this resolution, which i voted in favour of.

in writing. we voted against the resolutions tabled by the other groups on the juncker commission's work programme because none of them adequately reflects the fundamental flaw in the programme: that it does not address the fundamental problems affecting the daily lives of the citizens of the union. this work programme does not provide viable and effective solutions to tackle the macroeconomic problems of debt, corruption, tax evasion and unemployment, nor does it promote a sustainable renewable energy policy, nor does it propose the deep democratisation that is necessary to ensure the viability of the european institutions, nor does it transform the main lines of a foreign and trade policy that does not seek to promote effectively the union's fundamental values and the rights of its citizens. we have voted in favour of our group's resolution because we believe that it reflects a democratic, viable and sustainable political vision for providing solutions to the economic and social emergency our peoples are suffering as a result of austerity policies, the changes in social protection and the lack of democracy in the political institutions that govern their destinies.
in writing. despite the s&d group's efforts, there was no common resolution with the other groups. our group therefore voted its own resolution, which in this context of low growth, high unemployment, social exclusion, inequality and a real risk of economic deflation states as urgent priorities for 2015: an investment plan to generate more jobs and more growth, a fiscal environment that favours member states' investment in the european fund for strategic investments or the inclusion of a social dimension in eu policies. it is also essential to move towards an energy union that overcomes energy dependence or the determined fight against tax fraud and tax havens.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution after assessing the european commission's priorities for work. it is very positive that the commission has promptly presented its work programme for 2015, clearly targeting jobs, growth and investment as key factors in consolidating economic recovery in europe. the need to fully implement existing legislation in areas such as the single market, environmental law, the financial and banking sectors, etc. should be stressed. similarly, a significant reduction in the administrative burden on citizens and businesses by reducing the number of legislative proposals and focusing on the main priorities is necessary in order to contribute to the elimination of red tape at all levels and to continue the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion.

in writing. — in the absence of a joint motion for a resolution on the commission work programme 2015, eh bildu has voted against the motions for resolutions presented by the epp, greens/efa, alde, s&d, ecr and efdd, and in favour of the motions for resolution presented by our group, gue/ngl. in our opinion, the cwp 2015 does not include legislative proposals worked out and discussed in the previous term, and we are deeply dissatisfied about that fact. indeed, we strongly condemn the commission’s principle of political discontinuity as it completely undermines the european parliament’s rights as co-legislator; insisting that the decision to withdraw a legislative file must be the result of decision-making procedures. in that line, we strongly oppose the proposed withdrawal of the waste package, the clean air policy review, and the circular economy initiative, identified as crucial for sustainable growth and the well-being and health of eu citizens, as well as the maternity leave proposal. it is true that the commission’s work programme for 2015 is not the item to be voted, but no other motion than that proposed by gue/ngl expresses the deep dissatisfaction that eh bildu feels about the cwp 2015, and hence the direction of our vote.

in writing. i can argue that i am satisfied with the commission's 2015 work programme for a number of reasons. the first is that it keeps the political priorities in line with the availability of financial resources. the second is to reduce the number of legislative proposals, which will allow us to focus on the main priorities for european citizens and avoid wasting resources on obsolete or inadequate legislative proposals. finally, i welcome the fact that the commission, in its work programme for 2015, is focusing its efforts on jobs, growth and investment. in spite of this, i would remind the commission that, if these good objectives are to be achieved, it must not neglect the rapid and effective use of existing legislation in areas such as the single market, environmental law, the financial and banking sectors, cohesion policy and the recently revised common agricultural and fisheries policies. it must also be particularly firm in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion. i therefore vote in favour of this resolution and i encourage the commission to continue its best efforts.

in writing. i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on freedom of expression in turkey because it condemns the police raids and detention of journalists and media representatives in december 2014 and points to a general trend towards a backsliding of democracy and the tolerance of the turkish government towards public protests and critical media.
in writing. - we voted in favour because this joint resolution condemns the arrests of journalists in turkey and the systematic persecution of journalists and the media by the turkish government, which has led to self-censorship by some media. the commission is also calling for a full trial of the detainees and expressing concern at the lack of independence of the judiciary in turkey. the joint resolution also calls on turkey to respect fundamental rights and freedoms: the rule of law, international law, freedom of expression. the right to freedom of the press is reiterated as a mechanism to guarantee pluralism, which is necessary in democratic societies. the importance of civil society organisations is also emphasised, as only a transparent society can foster trust between the different components of a democratic society.
in writing. freedom of thought and expression is the very foundation of democracy. the media play an essential role in ensuring a strong democracy, as an independent and pluralistic press helps citizens to participate in public affairs. the detention of several journalists last december in turkey is therefore of particular gravity, as it is not an isolated incident but is part of a process of increasing deterioration of freedom of expression, with attempts by the government to ban access to social networks, disproportionate bans on websites and increasing pressures on the media and journalists. as this resolution, on which i voted in favour, states, it is therefore urgent that the judicial authorities in turkey review and deal with these cases as soon as possible and that the detainees be given full knowledge of the charges against them and full access to the incriminating evidence, as well as full guarantees for their defence and the impartiality of justice. the eu should also strengthen dialogue and cooperation with turkey, particularly in all matters relating to the rule of law and respect for the fundamental rights of citizens.

in writing. i believe that freedom of expression and media pluralism are the pillars of an independent press. this is essential in any democratic society, as an uninformed citizen cannot consistently exercise his rights and obligations in decision-making processes. i therefore think it is appropriate to condemn the recent police raids and the arrest of journalists and media representatives in turkey. these actions undermine respect for freedom of the press and i therefore urge the turkish authorities to make efforts to develop reforms which establish, within their legal framework, mechanisms and balances aimed at guaranteeing freedom of the press and expression. i would like to stress again the importance of ensuring these guarantees in order to promote and defend democracy, and for these reasons i am voting in favour of this proposal.

in writing. in his speech on wednesday, vice-president katainen did not bring any new information on the commission's legislative proposal on the european fund for strategic investments (efsi), the complex text of which we have known since the last plenary session. it should be noted that this draft regulation is not a clear legislative proposal but a financial nonsense which obscures the very important political and social dimension of the investment plan for europe, which has been achieved thanks to the constant work of the group of the european socialists and democrats. it is up to this parliament to correct and improve this draft, making it at least intelligible and internally consistent. it is also important to ensure that the european investment bank exercises its role as lender in a rational manner, taking a certain level of risk and not multiplying the fees charged to beneficiaries or inflating the administrative costs of the efsi. finally, it is striking, if not worrying, that mr katainen has appeared in his appearances both before the committee on economic and monetary affairs and before the european parliament's plenary with empty hands on possible national contributions to the efsi.
in writing. europe needs investment to revive activity and employment. years of misguided austerity policies have led to unbearable rates of unemployment, especially youth unemployment, and to lacerating increases in inequality and poverty, particularly in the countries of the south. a 180-degree turn is required. the new european fund for strategic investments is going in the right direction and, together with the flexibility introduced in the interpretation of tax rules, should be a starting point for abandoning austerity and placing a clear focus on growth, employment and the recovery of welfare. however, the lack of capital commitments to the fund by member states is a cause for concern, which may discourage private investment. we need greater commitment to strengthen the fund's capacity to boost job creation and to undertake strategic investments that enable europe to overcome its deficits, such as the current fragmentation of the energy market, which must be given priority attention.

mr president, in 2011 the commission committed itself to presenting a european law on accessibility. it was to recommend to the member states minimum standards so that all disabled people could have access to all services in general: we are talking about transport, we are talking about education, we are talking about work, we are talking about new technologies - all sectors of society. a study was commissioned on the socioeconomic impact of the new measures to improve the accessibility of goods and services for disabled people. in short, a study to gauge the advantages of adopting these measures. this study was due to be delivered in 2013, it was awarded in 2012 and we still don't know the conclusions of this study. i therefore ask the commission and parliament to report back to us as soon as possible on this study, particularly to assess the many positive advantages, because in the end it will certainly improve the quality of life for all disabled people.
