mr president, in 2006 the european investment bank granted €800 million in loans to the generalitat valenciana to finance the crea escola programme, for the renovation and improvement of educational centres. nine years later, the program is suffering a major setback. almost a hundred schools have not received a single euro and, what is worse, thousands of pupils study in schools in deplorable conditions. it is time for the eib to take action to ensure that the generalitat valenciana fulfils its part and carries out the school renovation works. i would like to draw particular attention to one school, the ciutat school in cremona, alaquàs, whose pupils have been studying in barracks for eight years, in deplorable conditions. they have created a platform to claim an educational center because the valencian government does not give them answers, does not fulfill its promises and, what is worse, has been two years suppressing places to get the center to end up disappearing. we cannot allow public schools to be abolished because governments are unable to deliver on their promises.
mr president, we should also thank mr svoboda, mr cavada and mr dzhambazki for having opened this debate on intellectual property and its protection. the point is that the approach of the question overlooks the real problem, because, to have a global debate, we should be talking about guaranteeing universal access to culture, the violation of the right to privacy on the internet, freedom of expression - i have to say that in my country, spain, websites can be closed without a court order - or the lack of support for creators, while laws are made to favor large distribution companies. let's open a comprehensive debate about companies bearing the cost of royalties so that creators are fairly paid; let's discuss the entity in charge of protecting copyright - which, in our opinion, should be a public entity guaranteeing access to culture - and let's give a boost to alternative methods, such as creative commons licenses, so that authors can decide how they want to exploit their work.
mr president, our laws enshrine private property as one of the fundamental pillars of our coexistence. this is all very well, but there are other rights that sometimes clash with this and, furthermore, not all private property is respected equally. in my country, for example, if a humble family cannot pay the mortgage, the private property of the bank is respected, and the family goes to the streets. however, if a large corporation wants to build a dam in a valley and recreate a swamp, they can expropriate entire villages and nothing happens. the same is true of the information and knowledge economy. intellectual property may be a good general principle, but it cannot serve to prevent hepatitis c patients from receiving the medication they urgently need. it cannot be used to prevent visually impaired people from accessing written works, in clear violation of the marrakesh treaty. the economy and the principles that underpin it should be at the service of the people, not the other way around.
mr president, the european observatory on infringements of intellectual property rights was indeed set up in 2012 as a network of experts and stakeholders, and this observatory was regulated by regulation. it was certainly trying to protect intellectual property rights. the office for harmonization in the internal market was responsible for financing the activities of this observatory. now, as decided in september 2014, it seems that a complementary group of experts is going to be created - as the commissioner told us - with a political but complementary task; but the question is very timely to be able to call for avoiding duplication of functions, given that public money is scarce and, therefore, we want to emphasize that there should be no duplication. the observatory's task is to advise and assist the national authorities, to raise awareness of this issue and, ultimately, of its work as such. i would like to conclude by saying that spain has indeed ratified the marrakesh treaty, which is very important for visually impaired people, although i understand that it has nothing to do with the subject under discussion today.
mr president, i too would like to join those who are calling for more efforts to be made in the fight against infringement of intellectual property rights. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the rights of the authors are protected. the cultural sector is essential for economic development and for the image of the european union and its member states; a sector that generates 6.5% of gross domestic product and a lot of jobs. clear regulatory frameworks are needed. the rights of authors and artists cannot continue to be devalued, in a way that is often at odds with community legislation. clear frameworks are needed to prevent attacks such as those in countries like my own, spain, which imposes a law on intellectual property without dialogue, of dubious constitutionality and which certainly violates european legislation.

vice-president of the commission. - mr president, honourable members, the commission welcomes the initiative of the european parliament to adopt a resolution on the renewal of the internet governance forum. this also highlights many important aspects for the current global discussions on internet governance. this topic remains a priority for the european commission. i look forward to working with you to further promote and improve the multi-stakeholder model for internet governance, which is such an important resource for europe’s economy and society. last year the commission adopted its communication on internet governance and policy. the council conclusions adopted in november will certainly help us to position ourselves in the global debate. the european parliament and commission have been working side by side on these issues, in particular in the context of the igf. we wish to promote a unified internet based on the respect of human rights and fundamental freedoms. the commission looks forward to continuing in these efforts with you. this parliamentary resolution is another step in this direction. it also comes at the right moment because 2015 will be a critical year for internet governance and there are important developments ahead. the text of the resolution rightly acknowledges this and reflects the importance and impact of the current discussions for the eu. our main common objective is to make sure that the internet remains a truly global resource, free from being captured by a few or by specific economic or political interests. the internet is for everyone. we need a system built on cooperation, trust and the clear rules that can safeguard them. this is why a greater global balance should increase the legitimacy of the existing governance arrangements. as you know, the commission welcomed last year’s decision of the united states government to transfer key internet domain name functions to the multi-stakeholder community, known as the iana (internet assigned numbers authority) transition. an important icann (internet corporation for assigned names and numbers) meeting is now taking place in singapore. i hope that there will be substantial progress made, including on the most sensitive issues such as those related to icann’s accountability. after all, icann cannot be itself the final judge in its own disputes with other parties. icann accountability and the iana transition are closely interlinked. they are two sides of the same coin. the main challenge ahead is to ensure that the rights checks and balances are in place. at the same time we should stay focused on what is happening in the context of the review of the outcomes of the world summit on the information society. as you know, the renewal of the igf is at stake and it will be addressed in this context. i see some worrying signs coming from this process with constant pushes towards stronger multilateral approaches. on substance we must ensure that the world summit on the information society will not lead to the introduction of stronger governmental control over the internet. we also support a stronger igf, stronger financially, stronger in substance. this is essential to guarantee the stability that it needs to keep up with increased expectations from the international community. we also need other platforms to complement the current discussions on internet governance but without duplicating the existing efforts. since the commission supports the implementation of the netmundial outcomes i am honoured to belong to the coordination council of the netmundial initiative. i look forward to working with you to further promote and improve the multi-stakeholder model for internet governance.

the rapporteur. - madam president, i must say that i am quite excited that we are ending today in this house. i hope that we will have a long-term dossier, which has a long history, but which will ultimately be successful. and, as shakespeare said, all's well that ends well. in 2008, under the french presidency, we were able to put the first proposal into practice, which was precisely the decision to end impunity, to reduce discrimination between road safety offenders across borders. it is therefore an essentially european, crossborder dossier which also aims to improve road safety and reduce road fatalities and injuries. but it is true that in that year, 2008, we launched a comprehensive, bold procedure that really was based on the information and support of the victims' family associations, in important and european bodies, like the etsc, or in european associations of traffic authorities, like tispol. we were therefore able to implement this formula, this procedure, so that crossborder offenders would first be informed of their offence when they returned home, and then appropriate fines could be imposed on them to put an end to their impunity. but, as so often, the commission and parliament were not accompanied by the council. the council, for various reasons, blocked the procedure and we were not able to resume it until 2011. and here i pay tribute to the belgian presidency which, with its creativity and its tenacity and courage, was able to resurrect this dossier on a new legal basis: the legal basis for police cooperation. but it was the way to get a process and procedure back on track, which is so important in putting an end to impunity in traffic matters. and it was the belgian presidency, together with the hungarian presidency, which re-launched the procedure, on a different legal basis, it is true, although we were able to improve some aspects. we were losing, for example, the presence of important member states such as ireland, the united kingdom and denmark, but instead we were able to broaden the list of cases and improve some of the proposals for police cooperation. the commission has also been asked to provide information on the implementation of the new rules on the protection of personal data. and at that time, shortly afterwards, in may 2014, the court of justice warned us of something that we had already been anticipating, but that we had not been able to overlook, which was that the initial legal basis, which had been envisaged by the commission and supported by parliament, was the basis of road safety. that was obviously an obstacle in the sense that the member states were already implementing the directive on the exchange of information with good results, but we had to follow the decision of the court of justice, as we have always done. i must say that the court of justice was particularly clever in giving us a few months to get the text back on track. the commission did so, and i am very grateful to it, and so did parliament, and i must say that in this case we were and have been particularly generous, and i emphasize this because i want to ask the commissioner later on for something in return for this generosity of parliament. parliament did not want to reopen the whole dossier this time, to re-write the directive, which we did not like one hundred percent, because the procedure is only an information procedure, but it does not include the penalty. that is why i ask you, madam commissioner, to get on with the evaluation report as soon as possible and above all to be courageous and to make new proposals to us to close and complete the procedure. i think we owe it to the families of the trafficking victims. we owe it to all the european citizens who, through instruments such as these, must be able to believe that europe really protects them, and protects them against something as important as the loss of life in traffic.

inequality between the sexes and constitutes an extreme form of discrimination against women. it is always done to minors and therefore also constitutes a violation of the rights of the child. it also violates the rights to health, safety and physical integrity. some 140 million women worldwide are currently suffering the consequences of this practice. in december 2014, the united nations general assembly adopted a resolution to step up efforts to eliminate female genital mutilation. it calls on states to develop, support and implement strategies to prevent the practice, including training of medical staff, social workers and local and religious leaders, to ensure that they provide competent support and care services to women and girls at risk of female genital mutilation. i will bring to this debate the words of khadi diallo, an activist of the association women's group for the abolition of sexual mutilations: "i will never forget that day. i was 12 years old, and my sister was 10. like every summer, we were at our paternal grandparents' house. early one morning, we went to see my aunt, my father's sister, whom we always wanted to visit. i didn't suspect anything. my aunt took me to the bathroom and she and several women rushed at me, grabbed me, put me down and split my legs. i was screaming. i didn't see the knife, but i felt it cut me. there was a lot of blood. i cried, but they said, "you shouldn't cry. it's a shame when a woman cries. you're a woman now". our mother used to come to see us. the first time he cried and kissed us. but there was nothing i could do. in africa, the father's family has a life-or-death right over the child. we were told that a woman should be strong, suffered, reserved and not very talkative. this is a real testimony, as is that of millions of women around the world, including in europe, who continue to be victims of injustice and inequality. in the countries of the union where female genital mutilation victims live, the practice is carried out in most cases during a stay in the country of origin, although there is evidence that it also occurs in the territory of the union. a recent study by the european institute for gender equality concluded that there are victims of mutilation in at least thirteen countries of the european union. the european commission published a communication in november 2013 entitled 'towards the elimination of female genital mutilation', which takes a cross-cutting approach to eliminating the practice. we therefore want to take this opportunity to ask the commission what action it has taken in this area and how it will help the member states to develop specific indicators, to adopt and implement legislation, and how it will contribute to this policy in its external relations. we also want to know how you will ensure that your work on operational planning in the field of justice is connected to existing commitments to end gender-based violence. there is another question which deserves our attention and to which i would like to hear your answer, which is: what concrete measures will the commission take to ensure the protection of asylum seekers on grounds relating to female genital mutilation, within the framework of the recast asylum seekers directive? as you can see, there are many questions which concern us as to whether we can put an end to this practice by taking concrete action within our competence. eliminating female genital mutilation must be a priority on the international agenda. if the laws are not firmly enforced and are not very strict, the effort will be in vain. it is a practice that violates the most basic rights of girls and women, and it has serious physical and psychological consequences. when a woman is informed about this, she herself protects her daughters and other girls in her community. nor can we forget the work of cooperation between public institutions and organisations working in civil society, because it is fundamental to achieving the objective of putting an end to a brutal practice of violence in europe, which has no place in the europe of the 21st century. because if anyone tries to justify this practice under some excuse, let us say very loudly and very clearly that respect for traditions and cultures has as an insurmountable limit the respect for human rights.
member of the commission. - madam president, i want to thank parliament, and particularly ms garcía pérez, for its efforts to eliminate female genital mutilation and its support for the work of the commission and the european external action service outlined in the communication entitled ʽtowards the elimination of female genital mutilationʼ and adopted on 25 november 2013. the commission strongly reaffirms its stance against all forms of violence against women, including female genital mutilation. this practice is a violation of human rights and of the rights of the child. it violates women’s and girls’ physical integrity, causing profound and life-long impacts on their health and their well-being, and can even led to death. currently the commission, together with the european external action service, is following up on the actions that we committed to in the communication. what are we doing on increasing knowledge? estimates show that there may be as many as 125 million victims worldwide and 500 000 victims in the european union alone. we have very little reliable information about how, by whom and where female genital mutilation is carried out. therefore, improving knowledge is one of our main priorities. together with the european institute for gender equality, we will develop a common methodology and indicators to estimate the risk of female genital mutilation in all eu member states. the european institute studies will tell us more about the reasons behind female genital mutilation being continued or abandoned among migrants in the european union. this will help us to create an effective strategy for ending the practice. now, what are we doing or what are we going to do on prevention? to bring about the social change necessary for families to abandon this tradition, legal action alone is not enough. this is why the commission is supporting and will continue to support work at grassroots level, engaging communities that practise female genital mutilation both in the eu and abroad. to this end, the commission will very shortly open a call for proposals for eur 4.5 million for transnational projects aiming to prevent, inform about and combat harmful practices in the european union. the commission is currently funding four national awareness-raising campaigns run by member states that specifically target female genital mutilation. in our external actions we also support grassroots projects that aim at the abandonment of female genital mutilation. this includes projects with a specific component on justice or creating a protective environment for women’s rights. thanks to the support of parliament, a web-based platform will be developed for professionals who come into contact with girls at risk and victims of female genital mutilation. i would like to thank you for that here today. the commission is working to include female genital mutilation in the development of a communication providing guidance for eu member states on integrated child protection systems. how are we protecting victims? the victims’ rights directive should be transposed in november 2015. this directive ensures victims of female genital mutilation easy access to well-functioning specialised support services and protects them against any threat of physical or emotional harm during criminal investigations and trial. the commission has organised several workshops with member states on the implementation of the directive. the most recent one took place last week on 6 february, the international day of zero tolerance for female genital mutilation. the commission is also disseminating training materials on female genital mutilation for legal practitioners through its e-justice platform. let me end with a few words regarding the external dimension of our work. access to justice and the promotion of laws protecting all the rights of women, including the right not to suffer from traditional harmful practices, are priorities also encompassed in the euʼs policy strategy in its external action for women. to promote gender equality we use political and human rights dialogues with partner governments where we bring up women’s empowerment, human rights and women’s health issues. secondly, we also support advocacy and lobbying initiatives to improve national legislation and the development of suitable national policies on women’s rights. thirdly we support capacity-building initiatives for government officials and advocacy and awareness-raising for all sectors of society. once a year a gender-specific training course is organised in the external action service. this training is targeted at staff from the external action service, the commission and parliament based in their headquarters, in eu delegations and in missions related to the common security and defence policy and in member states. since 2012, amnesty international has been invited to present a session on ending female genital mutilation.

mr president, the attack in paris is the first to be interpreted not as an attack on a specific european country but as an attack on europe as a whole. that is why we are right in the european parliament today to adopt a joint resolution of all the political forces against terrorism. we are not voting for a resolution on the pnr, we are voting for a resolution against terrorism. and i think that anyone who doesn't sign the resolution against terrorism because of the pnr will have a very hard time explaining it to their constituents. we have our differences, we do, but terrorism has to unite us in the fight against it. terrorists don't win when they kill. the terrorists win when they separate us from the democrats. i will also speak about greece. i believe that we are at a historic moment and that the european union's response to the situation raised by the greek government is a response which will determine the future of europe. and i ask everyone not to confuse the new greek government with the greek people, because they are completely different things. i believe that if one country gains from defaulting, all countries will default. loyalty will be broken. i think that if in one country you win the elections by saying that you do not have to pay germany or portugal or spain or france, in france, spain, portugal, germany you will win the elections by saying that you do not have to give more money to greece. i believe that if we awaken the nationalist spectre of the far left in one part of europe, the nationalist spectre of the far right will awaken in the opposite part of europe. i believe that if one country does not repay what it has borrowed, no other country will ever lend again. i think rules are either for everyone, or they're just not for anyone. i think that this european parliament can never support those who say that europe is the problem, because we are here because we believe that europe is the solution.
first vice-president of the commission. - mr president, i have listened very carefully to the honourable members’ contributions. i have a few comments to make in reaction to what was said. first of all, do not get me wrong: the passenger name record (pnr) scheme is not the solution to all our problems. pnr is no more than a building block in a huge construction that we need in order to fight radicalisation and terrorism in europe. mr lamassoure hit the nail on the head when he said that we need a european pnr scheme because the alternative will be that member states will take individual steps, and that is not a good alternative. however, i also believe that we need to put more effort into improving the situation of data protection at european level. here again, i believe it is better to act collectively in order to make sure that our citizens’ fundamental rights are guaranteed at european level. that is why i believe we need increased efforts on data protection reform. moving on to the issue of greece, so much was said about that, and i want to repeat that the commission is open for dialogue with greece – on the basis of respect for the greek people – to look for common solutions. i have to tell you that i was thinking back exactly 40 years to when i was 13 years old and one of my first moments of political consciousness was that i saw the greek people getting rid of a very ugly military regime that had trampled on their freedoms and rights. from that moment on, we saw european solidarity. it was the efforts of the council of europe at the time that helped the greek people rid themselves of dictatorship. it is too easy to say that there has been no solidarity with the greek people since then because, for me personally, those 40 years have been marked by the fact that there was a conscious decision by the greek people for europe and a conscious decision by europe to stand next to greece: to reform and to improve the situation of its citizens. that, in my view, has not changed. so even though there might be a huge debate about the merits of the programmes and the merits of what was done in the past, i would not accept a caricature narrative that the people elsewhere in europe have not shown solidarity with greece in the past couple of years. it is not right to say that. there has been a show of solidarity, including by other people in europe living in conditions not much better than those of the greeks themselves. that solidarity – if it is up to the commission – will not change. moving finally to the issue of fundamental values – and i do not like to put frames on political parties and call them ‘extreme left’ or ‘extreme right’ – let us look at facts and at declarations. it is not, i believe, asking too much of ms zimmer to look too at certain utterances by a coalition partner of one of her parties, in this case in greece. is it not part of the duty of a coalition partner to tell another partner that, in europe, we do not say that jews do not pay taxes? it is not a contribution to tolerance or respect in europe to say such things. we in europe, in the european parliament, in european political parties, do not accept homophobia as an institutional element in another political party. we will oppose that in discussion with coalition partners. i do not think this is too much to ask of a political party which calls itself left-wing. it is not too much to ask if you look back at our european history. it is not too much to ask if you look at what the colonels and their regime did to the greek people 40 years ago. (applause)
president-in-office of the council. - mr president, this morning’s debate spared no emotions. divisions of views among the political groups reflect general divisions of views in europe, and this is clear evidence that we need to continue our discussions to find a compromise. i have listened attentively to the debate and will ensure that the issues and points raised will be relayed to president tusk. meanwhile, i will use the opportunity to reply to some points raised during the debate. as we are short of time, unfortunately, i will not be able to reply to all the points. many of you referred to the situation in greece. the eurogroup is meeting tonight and will address this question. i understand that the eurogroup president will brief leaders tomorrow. it will also be the first time prime minister tsipras meets his european council counterparts. the eurogroup then meets again on 16 february. all in all, we agree that existing agreements should be respected. at the same time, i believe we all agree that greece is facing profound challenges. it is important to find a solution that will bring greece back to the path of economic growth. i also believe you will all agree that a solution found for greece will have to be accepted by all parties. i will dare to compare the eu to a marriage. you bind yourself to someone for better or for worse. you have your disagreements, but in a good marriage you survive the storm, being stronger and wiser, and so should the union. exclusion will not lead to a solution. we should not lose sight of our common goals: stability and unity. we have heard many critical remarks addressed to greece this morning. however, greece is not the only country in the eu to have a high debt level. the level of public debt in the eurozone in general is very high and it is rising. it is expected to be more than 94% this year – well over the 60% laid down in our stability and growth pact. high debt levels hamper growth in the european union. we all agree that bringing back growth is the most important challenge we face today. the right policy mix is the answer. the commitment to boosting investment is a step in the right direction. we need to accelerate the implementation of structural reforms in order to strengthen europe’s competitiveness and growth. it is essential that our public spending should stay on a sustainable path. today we discussed possible steps to fight against terrorism. i would like to refer once again to the informal justice and home affairs (jha) ministerial meeting in riga on 29 january and to the general affairs council meeting yesterday, where member states reiterated the need to put in place an eu passenger name record (pnr) system. we, as the presidency, are convinced that you understand how crucial pnr information is in detecting travel movements and patterns, and, in particular, monitoring and identifying foreign terrorist fighters and returnees. we believe that the growing number of member states setting up national pnr systems is in itself a valid reason for harmonisation at eu level. if we fail to do this it might lead to incompatible national systems with very different levels of data protection. we understand that this is a difficult issue for some of you, but we are encouraged by the more positive comments made by several members. we recognise the importance of the data protection package and the relevant instruments. we believe that, in the digital age, a single data protection regulation will strengthen data protection in europe. the latvian presidency will devote significant efforts to the regulation of data protection, with the aim of achieving a general approach during the jha council in march. at the same time we recognise the difficulties of the remaining issues and of horizontal questions. once a general approach is reached, we will start a trialogue with parliament. i fully share the view expressed by mr weber and mr kamall that we need to tackle the problem of propaganda and radicalisation. to address the factors underlying radicalisation we shall seek to develop a comprehensive cross-sectoral approach involving all the policies concerned, including measures to promote a culture of inclusion and tolerance through, for instance, education, youth, social and regional policies. the issue of communication in the context of combating foreign terrorist fighters is challenging and sensitive. we all recognise that the internet plays a central role in radicalisation and in the recruitment of potential foreign terrorist fighters. distinguished members, as many of you mentioned, all our thoughts are today with ukraine. we are, i hope, in a negotiations window. today further talks are due to take place in minsk. it is difficult to discuss this today as the situation is so fluid. obviously the council and all the eu institutions support the ongoing diplomatic efforts and i hope they will deliver progress for the population on the ground in eastern ukraine and in a wider perspective. there is no alternative to a diplomatic solution to the crisis, based on respect for ukraine’s independence, sovereignty and territorial integrity. the eu is ready to assist in these diplomatic efforts. finally, i would like to use the opportunity provided by this morning’s debate to express our deep appreciation of the personal efforts made during the last few days by mr hollande and ms merkel in seeking a peaceful solution for ukraine. we remain united in our efforts to withstand the aggressor. europeans should not forget the tragic historic events of the 20th century. in this regard, our discussion tomorrow will continue in the presence of mr poroshenko, who has been invited by president tusk to the informal meeting of heads of state or government. honourable members, the council will work speedily with the other union institutions to make sure that the eu leaders’ policy guidelines are acted upon. thank you very much for your attention.
in writing. the first vice-president of the european commission, in his speech to the informal european council of 12 february 2015, expressed the need to find an appropriate solution to the greek public debt problem. greece will need a new multilateral financial assistance programme as of 28 february 2015 as it cannot obtain financing on the financial markets at reasonable interest rates. at the same time, the conditions of the new loan should be more favourable than in the past in terms of interest rates and repayment terms, as well as in terms of conditionality, which should be less intrusive and ideological, and more focused on the reform of public administration and the tax system, and on the fight against corruption. the european stability mechanism can raise capital from the financial markets on a long-term basis and at a very low interest rate thanks to the ecb's monetary policy and low inflation. in addition, in order to preserve the necessary expenditure on social services and the fight against poverty and social exclusion, the annual primary budget surplus target needs to be reduced.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the common rules for exports from the committee on legal affairs of the european parliament as it is a technical report which makes it easier to codify. i have therefore supported the proposal that parliament should take a decision in this case by a single vote, without amendments or debate, since this is a procedure which is not linked to the content of the text but to formal measures to simplify its treatment, since if these texts are not codified, the different amended versions of the text remain, making it difficult to access them.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal because the advisory group said that it is only the codification of council regulation (ec) no 1061/2009 of 19 october 2009 establishing a common export regime, without any substantial amendments to it.
in writing. in the interests of simplification and clarity of union law, so that it is more accessible and understandable to the citizen, i voted in favour of the codification of regulation no 625/2009 on the common system of export refunds. the regulation has been substantially amended by various legislative acts in recent years and, in order to improve the clarity and the easy comprehensibility of the legislative text, it is appropriate to recast all those provisions in a new regulation, respecting the content of the codified texts and making only the relevant formal amendments.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the common rules for exports from the committee on legal affairs of the european parliament as it is a technical report which makes it easier to codify. i have therefore supported the proposal that parliament should take a decision in this case by a single vote, without amendments or debate, since this is a procedure which is not linked to the content of the text but to formal measures to simplify its treatment, since if these texts are not codified, the different amended versions of the text remain, making it difficult to access them.
in writing. codification provides legal certainty as to the law applicable in a given area and at a given time. such codification should be carried out in full compliance with the procedure for the adoption of union acts. this proposal, which codifies council regulation (ec) no 1061/2009 of 19 october 2009 establishing common rules for exports, respects the principle that no substantive amendment may be made to the acts to be codified, and is therefore part of the codification methods established by the commission, which aim to determine the provisions in force resulting from the numerous amendments to european legislation.
in writing. the codification of regulation (ec) no 1061/2009 of 19 october 2009 establishing common rules for exports is an urgent need. it has been amended several times over the years and is now codified to ensure the clarity and transparency of eu law. it should be recalled that the content of the codified texts is still respected, since the amendments incorporated are limited to the needs of the codification process. important elements of this regulation include: (1) the eu information and consultation procedure, whereby states which, as a result of exceptional market developments, consider that protective measures may be necessary, inform the commission, which in turn decides and informs the other member states of the measures taken; and (2) the safeguard measures, which aim to restrict the free export (except with the commission's authorisation) of essential products whose occasional shortage may pose a problem for one or more eu states. i therefore vote in favour of this proposal for a regulation.

in writing. i voted in favour of the report on gabon's accession to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction, as i support the objective of this convention to avoid the conflict between two national legal systems which only defend the interests of their own national, and not the interests of the child in the event of abduction by one of his or her parents when they are nationals of different states. this conflict between legal systems must be avoided in order to ensure that the rights of the child, including access to both parents, prevail. i therefore supported the report from the committee on legal affairs in favour of granting gabon accession to the convention.
in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal because it will solve the problems that are often suffered when couples from different states separate and fight over the custody of their children, even going so far as to take them away from them. this convention will resolve situations at international level and, more importantly, children will be protected against illegal abduction. i thank gabon for its accession to the hague convention.
in writing. i voted in favour of this council decision inviting the member states to accept, each for its territory, the accession of gabon to the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction and thus the effective entry into force of the convention between the european union and that country. this convention establishes a system that allows states parties to cooperate in finding a solution to situations of international child abduction, and has been ratified by all eu member states. the convention aims to resolve these situations at international level by providing that the competent courts and the applicable law are those of the state of residence of the child. the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of the abducted child. i welcome the accession of gabon to the convention. thanks to the convention, children linked to the gabonese community will be protected against illegal abduction.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on gabon's accession to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction, as i support the objective of this convention to avoid the conflict between two national legal systems which only defend the interests of their own national, and not the interests of the child in the event of abduction by one of his or her parents when they are nationals of different states. this conflict between legal systems must be avoided in order to ensure that the rights of the child, including access to both parents, prevail. i therefore supported the report from the committee on legal affairs in favour of granting gabon accession to the convention.
in writing. we voted in favour of the report on child abduction. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction has been ratified by all member states. the eu currently has exclusive external competence in this area. the member states can therefore no longer act on their own. the problem is that the convention does not provide for the autonomous action of international organisations. this problem has necessitated the council decision inviting the member states to accept, each for its territory, the accession of russia, andorra, the seychelles, albania, singapore, morocco, armenia and gabon. our position is to vote in favour.
in writing. international child abduction is a matter of the utmost importance. many children are immersed in such situations year after year. globalisation has led to an increasing number of children with parents of different nationalities. and this has led to an increase in child abductions. we must act with diligence.
in writing. for the institutions of the european union, the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a crucial instrument that has been ratified by all eu member states. this convention establishes a system which allows the states parties to cooperate in finding a solution to situations of international child abduction, a problem which unfortunately we have to face very often and which entails great suffering for the parties involved. the convention aims to resolve this problem at international level by providing that the competent courts and the applicable law are those of the state of residence of the child. similarly, the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of the abducted child. i therefore, after having analysed the decision and the case law of the court of justice of the eu, have decided to vote in favour of gabon's accession to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a multilateral treaty which aims to protect children from the harmful effects of abduction and detention across international borders by providing a procedure for their prompt return. gabon has ratified the convention, but its application between gabon and the european union requires 'acceptance' by all eu member states. as it is an exclusive competence of the eu, the report refers to the council decision asking the member states about their acceptance, and that is why i have supported it.

in writing. — this file suggested that parliament approve the council proposal to allow gabon to access the un convention that regulates civil aspects on child abduction, mostly concerning cooperation of authorities in case of return of wrongfully-removed children and issues of conflict of laws. as the prevention of child abduction is, since the brussels regulations on matrimonial matters and parental responsibility, an exclusive competence of the eu policy to promote the rights of the child, the eu is the actor at international level to improve the application of the 1980 convention and to encourage third states to accede to it. article 38(4) of the 1980 convention stipulates that the convention applies between the acceding country and such contracting states as will have declared their acceptance of the accession. therefore, the eu has to decide whether or not to accept the accession of a country. when affirmative, member states should make the declaration of acceptance concerning the accession in the interest of the eu, because, as the convention dates from 1980, it does not recognize international organisations such as the eu as an accessing party. eh bildu has voted in favour, as the primary matter is broadening the application of the un convention on child abduction.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a multilateral treaty which aims to protect children from the harmful effects of abduction and detention across international borders by providing a procedure for their prompt return. the following eight countries have ratified the convention, but for its application between them and the european union it is necessary for all eu member states to accept it. the countries are singapore, russia, albania, andorra, the seychelles, gabon, armenia and morocco. as this is a positive step forward in the international protection of children, i have voted in favour of the report.

in writing. - we voted in favour of the report on child abduction. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction has been ratified by all member states. the eu currently has exclusive external competence in this area. the member states can therefore no longer act on their own. the problem is that the convention does not provide for the autonomous action of international organisations. this problem has necessitated the council decision inviting the member states to accept, each for its territory, the accession of russia, andorra, the seychelles, albania, singapore, morocco, armenia and gabon. our position is to vote in favour.
in writing. - we voted in favour of the report on child abduction. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction has been ratified by all member states. the eu currently has exclusive external competence in this area. the member states can therefore no longer act on their own. the problem is that the convention does not provide for the autonomous action of international organisations. this problem has necessitated the council decision inviting the member states to accept, each for its territory, the accession of russia, andorra, the seychelles, albania, singapore, morocco, armenia and gabon. the convention aims to protect children from the harmful effects of abduction and detention across international borders by providing a procedure for their prompt return.
in writing. — this file suggested that parliament approve the council proposal to allow the seychelles to access the un convention that regulates civil aspects on child abduction, mostly concerning the cooperation of the authorities in case of the return of wrongfully-removed children and issues of conflict of laws. as the prevention of child abduction is, since the brussels regulations on matrimonial matters and parental responsibility, an exclusive competence of the eu policy to promote the rights of the child, the eu is the actor at international level to improve the application of the 1980 convention and to encourage third states to accede it. article 38(4) of the 1980 convention stipulates that the convention applies between the acceding country and such contracting states as will have declared their acceptance of the accession. therefore, the eu has to decide whether or not to accept the accession of a country. when affirmative, member states should make the declaration of acceptance concerning the accession in the interest of the eu, because, as the convention dates from 1980, it does not recognise international organisations such as the eu as an accessing party. eh bildu has voted in favour, as the primary matter is broadening the application of the un convention on child abduction.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a multilateral treaty which aims to protect children from the harmful effects of abduction and detention across international borders by providing a procedure for their prompt return. the following eight countries have ratified the convention, but for its application between them and the european union it is necessary for all eu member states to accept it. the countries are singapore, russia, albania, andorra, the seychelles, gabon, armenia and morocco. as this is a positive step forward in the international protection of children, i have voted in favour of the report.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the accession of the seychelles to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction, as i support the objective of this convention to avoid the conflict between two national legal systems which only defend the interests of their own national, and not the interests of the child in the event of abduction by one of his or her parents when they are nationals of different states. this conflict between legal systems must be avoided in order to ensure that the rights of the child, including access to both parents, prevail. i therefore supported the report from the committee on legal affairs in favour of granting the seychelles accession to the convention.
in writing. in connection with the above arguments on the proposal for a council decision on the declaration by the member states of acceptance, in the interest of the european union, of gabon's accession to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction, i consider equally important the accession of the republic of seychelles to that convention. for this reason, and in view of the fact that many people in the eu are of seychelles origin, i am voting in favour of this proposal, considering that with such accession we can guarantee greater protection for minors.
in writing. as former minister of justice, i dealt with bilateral relations between the czech republic and the seychelles. i therefore welcome the extension of the scope and effect of this convention to the island country in question.
in writing. i voted in favour of this council decision inviting the member states to accept, each for its territory, the accession of seychelles to the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction and, therefore, the effective entry into force of the convention between the european union and seychelles. this convention establishes a system that allows states parties to cooperate in finding a solution to situations of international child abduction, and has been ratified by all eu member states. the convention aims to resolve these situations at international level by providing that the competent courts and the applicable law are those of the state of residence of the child. the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of the abducted child. i welcome the accession of the seychelles to the convention. the convention will protect minors linked to the seychelles community against illegal abduction.

in writing. i voted in favour of the eight reports accepting the accession of armenia, morocco, singapore, albania, russia, the seychelles, andorra and gabon to the 1980 hague convention. this convention establishes the framework of private international law for the recovery of abducted children. it aims to ensure that judicial and administrative cooperation is effectively applied to ensure the rights of the child, and mutual respect of judgments in relation to custody.

in writing. i voted in favour of this proposal because it will solve the problems that are often suffered when couples from different states separate and fight over the custody of their children, even going so far as to take them away from them. this convention will resolve situations at international level and, more importantly, children will be protected against illegal abduction. i thank singapore for joining the hague convention.
in writing. i voted in favour of this council decision inviting the member states to accept, each for its territory, the accession of singapore to the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction and thus the effective entry into force of the convention between the european union and that country. this convention establishes a system that allows states parties to cooperate in finding a solution to situations of international child abduction, and has been ratified by all eu member states. the convention aims to resolve these situations at international level by providing that the competent courts and the applicable law are those of the state of residence of the child. the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of the abducted child. i welcome the accession of singapore to the convention. under the convention, children linked to the singaporean community will be protected against illegal abduction.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the accession of singapore to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction, as i support the objective of this convention to avoid the conflict between two national legal systems which only defend the interests of their own national, and not the interests of the child in the event of abduction by one of his or her parents when they are nationals of different states. this conflict between legal systems must be avoided in order to ensure that the rights of the child, including access to both parents, prevail. i have therefore supported the report from the committee on legal affairs in favour of singapore's accession to the convention.
in writing. we voted in favour of the report on child abduction. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction has been ratified by all member states. the eu currently has exclusive external competence in this area. the member states can therefore no longer act on their own. the problem is that the convention does not provide for the autonomous action of international organisations. this problem has necessitated the council decision inviting the member states to accept, each for its territory, the accession of russia, andorra, the seychelles, albania, singapore, morocco, armenia and gabon. our position is to vote in favour.
in writing. the eu should continue its efforts at international level to improve the implementation of the 1980 convention and encourage other states to accede to it. we therefore welcome the news that eight new states (gabon, andorra, seychelles, russia, albania, singapore, morocco and armenia) are now subject to the common legal framework resulting from this convention.
in writing. for the institutions of the european union, the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a crucial instrument that has been ratified by all eu member states. this convention establishes a system which allows the states parties to cooperate in finding a solution to situations of international child abduction, a problem which unfortunately we have to face very often and which entails great suffering for the parties involved. the convention aims to resolve this problem at international level by providing that the competent courts and the applicable law are those of the state of residence of the child. similarly, the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of the abducted child. therefore, after having analysed the decision and the case law of the court of justice of the eu, i have decided to vote in favour with a view to facilitating singapore's accession to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a multilateral treaty which aims to protect children from the harmful effects of abduction and detention across international borders by providing a procedure for their prompt return. singapore has ratified the convention, but its application between singapore and the european union requires 'acceptance' by all eu member states. as it is an exclusive competence of the eu, the report refers to the council decision asking the member states about their acceptance, and that is why i have supported it.

in writing. — this file suggested that parliament approve the proposal for a council decision to allow singapore to access the un convention that regulates civil aspects of child abduction, mostly concerning cooperation of authorities for the return of wrongfully removed children and issues of conflict of laws. as the prevention of child abduction is, since the brussels regulations on matrimonial matters and parental responsibility, an exclusive competence of the eu policy to promote the rights of the child, the eu is the player at international level to improve application of the 1980 convention and to encourage third states to accede it. article 38(4) of the 1980 convention stipulates that the convention applies between the acceding country and such contracting states as will have declared their acceptance of the accession. therefore, the eu has to decide whether to accept the accession of a country. when it does so, member states should make the declaration of acceptance concerning the accession in the interest of the eu; because as the convention dates from 1980, it does not recognise international organisations such as the eu as an accessing party. eh bildu has voted in favour, as the primary matter is broadening of the application of the un convention on child abduction.
in writing. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction is a multilateral treaty which aims to protect children from the harmful effects of abduction and detention across international borders by providing a procedure for their prompt return. the following eight countries have ratified the convention, but for its application between them and the european union it is necessary for all eu member states to accept it. the countries are singapore, russia, albania, andorra, the seychelles, gabon, armenia and morocco. as this is a positive step forward in the international protection of children, i have voted in favour of the report.

in writing. i voted in favour of this council decision inviting the member states to accept, each for its territory, the accession of armenia to the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction and, therefore, the effective entry into force of the convention between the european union and armenia. this convention establishes a system that allows states parties to cooperate in finding a solution to situations of international child abduction, and has been ratified by all eu member states. the convention aims to resolve these situations at international level by providing that the competent courts and the applicable law are those of the state of residence of the child. the convention also establishes a system to ensure the immediate return of the abducted child. i welcome the accession of armenia to the convention. thanks to the convention, minors linked to the armenian community will be protected against illegal abduction.
in writing. - we voted in favour of the report on child abduction. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction has been ratified by all member states. the eu currently has exclusive external competence in this area. the member states can therefore no longer act on their own. the problem is that the convention does not provide for the autonomous action of international organisations. this problem has necessitated the council decision inviting the member states to accept, each for its territory, the accession of russia, andorra, the seychelles, albania, singapore, morocco, armenia and gabon. our position is to vote in favour.
in writing. - we voted in favour of the report on child abduction. the hague convention of 25 october 1980 on the civil aspects of international child abduction has been ratified by all member states. the eu currently has exclusive external competence in this area. the member states can therefore no longer act on their own. the problem is that the convention does not provide for the autonomous action of international organisations. this problem has necessitated the council decision calling on the member states to accept, each for its territory, the accession of armenia.
in writing. i voted in favour of the report on the accession of armenia to the 1980 hague convention on the civil aspects of international child abduction, as i support the objective of this convention to avoid the confrontation between two national legal systems which only defend the interest of their own national, and not the interest of the child in the event of abduction by one of his or her parents when they are nationals of different states. this conflict between legal systems must be avoided in order to ensure that the rights of the child, including access to both parents, prevail. i therefore supported the report from the committee on legal affairs in favour of armenia's accession to the convention.
in writing. i voted in favour of the eight reports accepting the accession of armenia, morocco, singapore, albania, russia, the seychelles, andorra and gabon to the 1980 hague convention. this convention establishes the framework of private international law for the recovery of abducted children. it aims to ensure that judicial and administrative cooperation is effectively applied to ensure the rights of the child, and mutual respect of judgments in relation to custody.

in writing. i voted in favour because, after four years of institutional blockage and after making the necessary changes to adjust the legal basis, we can now count on an instrument which will enable us to fight against the impunity of foreign drivers and which will guarantee that all europeans, regardless of the registration of their vehicle, are treated equally. the directive will enable road authorities to automatically identify the owners of vehicles, irrespective of their country of registration, when they have committed offences which are responsible for more than 75% of road deaths. it will go a long way towards meeting the challenge of halving the number of road fatalities by 2020 and avoiding 350 to 400 deaths a year on our roads, the equivalent of a passenger plane. the european citizens will also be able to continue to move about our roads feeling protected and in complete safety. given the strong support of parliament, the commissioner has acceded to parliament's request and has publicly committed to accompany the evaluation report for 2016, which has already been launched, with new proposals to complete the procedure, as we had asked her from the beginning.
in writing. i have supported this report on the proposal for a directive to facilitate the crossborder exchange of information on road safety traffic offences on the basis that this process should be carried out through mechanisms that ensure the protection of personal data by sharing the report's objective of ending the anonymity of drivers who are not resident in the state in which they commit the offence and ensuring that they are not left unpunished. i am convinced that when it comes into force, this directive will discourage reckless and dangerous behaviour on the road, which will save many lives, which is why i support the text.

in writing. we voted in favour of this report because we urgently need to adopt a proposal with a broad consensus, which will avoid creating a legal vacuum in a mechanism which has already been transposed into national law in different eu member states and is producing good results in road safety. this mechanism has a strong deterrent effect by removing the impunity granted by anonymity for serious traffic offences committed by drivers from a country other than the country where the offence was committed. the proposal also incorporates and reinforces the suggestions of the european data protection supervisor.
in writing. the study of traffic offences data in the eu shows that the percentage of non-residents involved in traffic offences is higher than that of national traffic, especially in relation to speeding. one of the main reasons for the increase in the number of infringements involving foreign vehicles is that the authorities, not knowing the address of the owner of the vehicle, cannot notify the owner of the penalty, especially when it comes to infringements detected by automatic radar systems. although attempts have been made to resolve the problem through bilateral treaties, experience has shown that they have not worked properly and must therefore be addressed jointly at european level. we must make progress in the analysis of the proposal and reach an agreement which will make it possible to adopt a new directive in order to avoid leaving in legal limbo practically all the member states which have already incorporated the provisions of the repealed directive into national law, thus contributing to a reduction in road accidents and deaths as a result of road accidents.

in writing. — the new directive comes at a critical time. even if the eu is on target with its aim of cutting road deaths by 50% by 2020, in past years and months there has been an increase in the number of road accident victims for various reasons: people’s cars are getting older; there have been swingeing cuts in infrastructure maintenance spending thanks to the economic crisis; there is a lack of funding for infrastructure and development geared towards improving road safety, etc. this directive should come into force as soon as possible; this cross-border motoring penalties directive should serve as a non-discriminatory deterrent in countering impunity on the eu’s roads. despite the fact that people are of course never thrilled to receive a letter telling them they have committed a traffic offence, they will however welcome the fact that everyone in the eu will be treated equally, no matter where their vehicle is registered. moreover, the road accident victims’ associations, traffic authorities, road traffic offence prosecutors and road safety associations will warmly welcome parliament’s vote.

in writing. i voted in favour of the sustainable fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of senegal as it is part of the type of agreements which aim to enhance sustainable fisheries by promoting better exploitation of available stocks through the use of industry best practices. i also believe that it would benefit both sides: senegal, given the financial contribution of around eur 14 million it would receive over the five years of the agreement, and the eu, since the agreement will allow european vessels, mainly spanish and french tuna vessels, to fish in senegalese waters. in addition, the satellite vessel tracking system and the cooperation between the authorities of both parties established by the protocol will help senegal to combat illegal, unreported and irregular fishing. for these and other reasons i have considered it appropriate to support this agreement.
in writing. senegal is a key partner of the eu. the previous agreement on fisheries dates from 1980 (the oldest in force). eight years after the expiry of the previous protocol, on 25 april, new agreements and protocols were agreed, which is good news in line with the increase in fisheries agreements we have been calling for. now, for a period of stability in the sector (five years, renewable), fishing opportunities (14 000 tonnes of tuna and 2 000 tonnes of hake) are being offered to 38 european vessels for a consideration of eur 8 690 000: a fair price. spain has sixteen search vessels (out of twenty-eight in total, twelve for france), seven barges (out of eight in total, one for france) and two trawlers. it is a balanced protocol, in line with the principles of the reformed common fisheries policy. it is part of the new generation of agreements in which the biological welfare of species with fishing potential has been scientifically documented. all parties benefit, including local artisanal fishermen, who receive a significant part of the sectoral aid, while, in support of the local economy, the catch of tuna seiners and line tuna vessels must be landed in the port of dakar.
in writing. the republic of senegal is a key partner of the eu with whom we have longstanding fisheries relations. the previous agreement dates from 1980. it was the oldest agreement in force. eight years after the expiry of the previous protocol, a new agreement and its corresponding implementing protocol were initialled on 25 april. this is good news, in line with the increase in fisheries agreements and protocols in force which we have been calling for since the beginning of the legislature. this is a balanced protocol, which will promote the responsible and sustainable exploitation of resources in the common interest of senegal and the eu, in accordance with the principles of the reformed cfp and its external dimension.
in writing. i voted in favour of the sustainable fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of senegal as it is part of the type of agreements which aim to enhance sustainable fisheries by promoting better exploitation of available stocks through the use of industry best practices. i also believe that it would benefit both sides: senegal, given the financial contribution of around eur 14 million it would receive over the five years of the agreement, and the eu, since the agreement will allow european vessels, mainly spanish and french tuna vessels, to fish in senegalese waters. in addition, the satellite vessel tracking system and the cooperation between the authorities of both parties established by the protocol will help senegal to combat illegal, unreported and irregular fishing. for these and other reasons i have considered it appropriate to support this agreement.
in writing. we have voted in favour of this recommendation. this is a sustainable fisheries partnership agreement which replaces the one that expired in 2006. it lays down new conditions concerning, among others, the volume of catches and the economic contribution. the agreement allows 38 vessels of three types (catching tuna vessels, reelers and trawlers) to fish in senegalese waters during the five years of its validity, 25 of which are spanish. the agreement is positive as it benefits both parties. it will support the development of sustainable fisheries policies in the republic of senegal and will enable the senegalese authorities to improve the surveillance of their territorial waters, through a satellite monitoring system, to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.
in writing. fisheries relations between the european union and the republic of senegal have been developing since 1981, during which time the european union has signed several agreements with senegal in this field. the last of these agreements expired in 2006, resulting in a severe reduction in the number of tuna vessels in senegalese waters. the commission is now proposing that the council conclude the agreement and the protocol which are intended to create a new framework for cooperation between the eu and the republic of senegal. this protocol will last for five years, will have a financial contribution of eur 13 930 000 and will be beneficial to both parties, as it will help both the republic of senegal and the european union to create new jobs and will advance sustainable fisheries and good governance. for all these reasons i voted in favour of the partnership agreement.
in writing. the republic of senegal is a key fisheries partner of the eu. the new agreement replaces the 1980 agreement for a renewable period of five years and allows the return of the european fleet to this fishery, from which it had been excluded since the suspension of the previous agreement in 2006. i voted in favour of this because it is a protocol of great importance for the spanish freezer tuna fleet, which will have 16 fishing licences, and will offer permits for seven spanish tuna-fishing vessels, based in bermeo (vizcaya), which already used the port of dakar as a base for their operations in the atlantic and operated in senegal under private agreements. the agreement will promote the responsible and sustainable exploitation of resources in the common interest of senegal and the eu, in accordance with the principles of economic and environmental sustainability of the new common fisheries policy and its external dimension. in addition, it is an agreement that benefits all stakeholders, including local artisanal fishermen, who will receive a significant part of the sectoral aid integrated in it.

in writing. - we voted in favour of this recommendation. this is a sustainable fisheries partnership agreement which replaces the one that expired in 2006. it lays down new conditions concerning, among others, the volume of catches and the economic contribution. the agreement allows 38 vessels of three types (catching tuna vessels, reelers and trawlers) to fish in senegalese waters during the five years of its validity, 25 of which are spanish. the agreement is positive as it benefits both parties. it will support the development of sustainable fisheries policies in the republic of senegal and will enable the senegalese authorities to improve the surveillance of their territorial waters, through a satellite monitoring system, to combat illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.
in writing. the republic of senegal is a key partner of the eu with whom we have longstanding fisheries relations. eight years after the expiry of the previous protocol, a new agreement and its corresponding implementing protocol were initialled on 25 april. this is good news, in line with the increase in fisheries agreements and protocols in force which we have been calling for since the beginning of the legislature. it is a balanced protocol, which will promote the responsible and sustainable exploitation of resources in the common interest of senegal and the eu, in accordance with the principles of the reformed cfp and its external dimension, and i have therefore decided to vote in favour.
in writing. i voted in favour of the sustainable fisheries partnership agreement between the european union and the republic of senegal as it is part of the type of agreements which aim to enhance sustainable fisheries by promoting better exploitation of available stocks through the use of industry best practices. i also believe that it would benefit both sides: senegal, given the financial contribution of around eur 14 million it would receive over the five years of the agreement, and the eu, since the agreement will allow european vessels, mainly spanish and french tuna vessels, to fish in senegalese waters. in addition, the satellite vessel tracking system and the cooperation between the authorities of both parties established by the protocol will help senegal to combat illegal, unreported and irregular fishing. for these and other reasons i have considered it appropriate to support this agreement.
in writing. the republic of senegal is a coastal state in west africa. the port of dakar, its commercial port, is internationally important because of its geographical location. fisheries relations between the eu and the republic of senegal began on 1 june 1981, with the signing in 2002 of the renewal of a series of protocols which expired in 2006, resulting in a severe reduction in the number of eu tuna seiners in senegalese waters. in this context, it was proposed to renegotiate the partnership agreement. i voted in favour, because i believe that the agreement will be beneficial to both sides, as it will help to create new jobs. in addition, the satellite tracking system and the cooperation between the eu and the republic of senegal in relation to vessel monitoring and tracking in senegalese waters will help the local authorities to strengthen their fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. it will also increase the economic activity of the eu fleet and help local seafarers who, under the provisions of the protocol, will be part of the crews of eu vessels.
in writing. senegal is a key partner of the eu. the previous agreement on fisheries dates from 1980 (the oldest in force). eight years after the expiry of the previous protocol, new agreements and protocols were agreed on 25 april, which is good news in line with the increase in fisheries agreements we have been calling for. now, for a period of stability in the sector (five years, renewable), 38 european vessels are being offered fishing opportunities (14 000 tonnes for tuna and 2 000 tonnes for hake) for a price of eur 8 690 000, a fair price. spain has sixteen (out of twenty-eight, with twelve for france), seven (out of eight, with one for france) and two trawlers. it is a balanced protocol, in line with the principles of the reformed cfp. it is part of the new generation of agreements whereby the biological welfare of species with fishing potential has been scientifically documented. all parties benefit, including local artisanal fishermen, with a significant part of the sectoral aid, while, to support the local economy, the catch of tuna longliners and tuna seiners must be landed in the port of dakar.

in writing. the european parliament voted this week on the use of torture by the cia. the joint resolution b8-0098/2015 of the s&d, alde, gue/ngl, efdd and greens/efa groups is the only one that explicitly condemns the use of torture. the european parliament has therefore voted in favour of the resolution and against resolutions rc-b8-0123/2015, b8-0123/2015 and b8-0133/2015 tabled by ecr and ppe. but the eu must not look only to the outside - the us and the cia in this case - when tackling the scourge of torture. torture is practised within the community; spanish security forces torture in euskal herria, as has been confirmed by successive judgments of the court of human rights in strasbourg. what the eu demands of the rest of the world must first be guaranteed on its own territory: the eradication of the use of torture and action against member states that practice it.
