in writing. — i firmly believe that respect for fundamental rights and the rule of law is an essential element in successful counterterrorism policies. in past resolutions, parliament has repeatedly condemned the cia’s secret detention and extraordinary rendition programme, which resulted in multiple human-rights violations, including the use of torture and other inhumane or degrading treatment, abduction, secret detention, detention without trial, and violations of the non-refoulement principle. despite their particular nature, national-security and counterterrorism policies are not exempt from the principle of accountability, and there can be no impunity for violations of international law and human rights. i therefore call on our american allies to investigate and prosecute the multiple human rights violations resulting from the cia rendition and secret detention programmes, and to cooperate with all requests from eu member states for information, extradition or effective remedies for victims in connection with the cia programme. eu member states should also investigate the allegations that there were secret prisons on their territory where people were held under the cia programme, and prosecute those involved in these operations, taking into account all the new evidence that has come to light.

in writing. i voted in favour because the text includes an absolute condemnation of terrorism, a phenomenon which cannot be justified in any way, and new measures to prosecute and punish terrorist crimes. it also includes measures to strengthen the existing legislative framework for combating terrorism in order to adapt it to new realities on the basis of proportionality and necessity, and always on the basis of respect for public freedoms and fundamental rights under the rule of law. the resolution calls for greater cooperation between european judicial and police authorities in the fight against terrorism. it is a very strong resolution on prevention, addressing the root causes of terrorism by proposing measures in the socio-educational field and in the field of 'de-radicalization' and the promotion of a culture of tolerance in europe. the resolution strikes a good balance between the security dimension and respect for freedoms. that is an act of political responsibility which is required in the face of a matter as serious as terrorism. the resolution has put a value on the unity of the democrats to defeat terrorism in the face of the threat it poses today to our security, our freedoms, and our model of coexistence.
in writing. we strongly condemn the terrorist acts perpetrated in france against the workers of charlie hebdo. we condemn all acts of terrorism in a multitude of countries. and we do not exclude from this condemnation - as does the majority of this house - the state terrorism practiced by countries such as israel against palestine, practiced in syria, in lebanon, nor the use of drones by the united states against populations in africa or the middle east. defending the need to take action against the financing of terrorism and at the same time maintaining privileged relations with countries like saudi arabia that finance, train and support terrorist groups is another of the contradictions and another example of hypocrisy of the majority of the right in this house. i have therefore voted against. the fight against terrorism requires that the root causes of terrorism be tackled; it requires a profound change in policies and respect for international law. and it can in no way legitimize the wave of repression and violation of rights and freedoms which is contained in this resolution.

in writing. i want to express my agreement with the resolution adopted this morning on counter-terrorism measures. we cannot rely on a rhetorical debate, often far removed from reality, between freedom and security. this equation must always be solved in favour of security with freedom, knowing that there is no one without the other. today, european citizens are demanding from their governments more effective security measures and measures which respect freedom, and it is up to the european parliament to balance these mutual demands. we socialists cannot leave the banner of security in the hands of the right because they will end up imposing a model that will diminish the broad concept of freedom and citizenship that we have on the left. that is why we have agreed a balanced resolution with them. but we cannot stand with other groups who are demanding freedom without understanding the time we are living in, the real risks we are facing, and therefore assuming an insecurity that the citizens do not want.

in writing. we strongly condemn the terrorist acts perpetrated in france against the workers of charlie hebdo. we condemn all acts of terrorism in a multitude of countries. and we do not exclude from this condemnation - as does the majority of this house - the state terrorism practiced by countries such as israel against palestine, practiced in syria, in lebanon, nor the use of drones by the united states against populations in africa or the middle east. defending the need to take action against the financing of terrorism and at the same time maintaining privileged relations with countries like saudi arabia that finance, train and support terrorist groups is another of the contradictions and another example of hypocrisy of the majority of the right in this house. i have therefore voted against. the fight against terrorism requires that the root causes of terrorism be tackled; it requires a profound change in policies and respect for international law. and it can in no way legitimize the wave of repression and violation of rights and freedoms which is contained in this resolution.

in writing. — the greens/efa group today voted against the joint motion for resolution on anti-terrorism measures, as the resolution is sending the wrong message at the wrong time. the resolution agreed by the four bigger political groups provides a carte blanche for eu governments to scale back personal freedoms with measures that will fail to properly respond to the terrorist threat. instead of pushing for effective measures, the usual suspects who have been continually pushing for mass surveillance and data retention are using the paris attacks as an excuse to bulldoze through these measures, despite any evidence that they will prove effective in countering the terrorist threat. a coherent counter-terrorism strategy would focus on targeted surveillance of real suspects and ensuring security authorities have the means and resources to focus on specific risks and concrete suspicions, to follow any leads immediately, and to efficiently exchange information about dangerous individuals. this is what we should be trying to achieve. there is also a need to tackle radicalisation in schools and prisons. finally we are missing a call for a legal definition of profiling. stepping up mass surveillance will undermine security and is instead a victory for fundamentalists, who are combating precisely such democratic freedoms.
in writing. — i supported this motion because terrorism, radicalisation and violent extremism are some of the major threats to our security and our freedoms and therefore affect our fundamental rights. today, more than ever, we reaffirm european values to defend freedom of expression, fundamental rights, democracy and tolerance without using violence. there must be coordination of measures and anti-terrorist policy control in all member states to deal with this global threat.
in writing. i voted against this resolution on counter-terrorism measures. the text essentially gives the commission and the council free rein to continue their mass surveillance strategy, even in the absence of evidence, and authorises the use of measures which clearly constitute a violation of fundamental rights and freedoms.

in writing. the objective of the internet governance forum (igf) is to implement the mandate of the world summit on the information society (wsis) as a contribution to a democratic, transparent and multilateral political dialogue, which broadens the range of issues of economic governance on the internet. this resolution aims to pressure the un general assembly to renew the igf's mandate, strengthen its resources and maintain the multilateral model of internet governance. it also proposes that the eu institutions concerned maintain financial support for its secretariat to ensure the development of an efficient and independent organisation and thus contribute to the democratisation, openness and neutrality of the internet. all of these are objectives which we consider appropriate and fair, and that is why i voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. the internet has been the great invention of the last twenty years. it is the responsibility of the european union to support the internet governance forum and to raise the impact of these exchanges in policy debates. it is essential to improve internet access worldwide, as well as to continue efforts to ensure the legal protection of net neutrality, which is an indispensable condition for safeguarding freedom of information and expression.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution because i share the need to renew the mandate of the forum of which the eu is also the main contributor, funding 30% of its activities - and the multi-stakeholder negotiation approach as a pillar of internet governance. i also believe it is essential to ensure, as the resolution calls for, the principle of net neutrality as an indispensable condition for ensuring freedom of information and expression, and for boosting innovation, growth and employment. without neutrality there is no network, so it is essential to ensure an open and independent internet. europe cannot be left behind when in the united states president obama has clearly committed to the creation of the strictest possible measures to protect neutrality, and the fcc chairman has proposed to prevent network access providers from discriminating against content or applications, appealing to the regulation of the internet as a basic public service. europe should also take advantage of the investment plan to maximise broadband networks and ensure a connected continent, while tackling the digital divide. it is also necessary to complete the process of globalisation of icann's functions.
in writing. the agreed resolution stresses that the european parliament has always defended this forum and has always participated in its meetings, and that its mandate should be renewed and its resources strengthened. on a crucial issue such as net neutrality, it underlines the need to ensure an open and independent internet and stresses the 'crucial' importance of continuing efforts to ensure the legal protection of net neutrality as 'a prerequisite' to ensure freedom of information and expression and to boost growth and jobs. it is therefore in line with the group's position, as opposed to positions such as that held by the spanish government, in favour of opening the door to the 'development of business models based on reasonable traffic management', i.e. differentiated services that take precedence over each other, as highlighted by the minister of industry in his contribution to the european commission's strategy to complete the digital single market. the resolution also highlights the process of globalisation of icann's functions.
in writing. the objective of the internet governance forum (igf) is to implement the mandate of the world summit on the information society (wsis) as a contribution to a democratic, transparent and multilateral political dialogue, which broadens the range of issues of economic governance on the internet. this resolution aims to pressure the un general assembly to renew the igf's mandate, strengthen its resources and maintain the multilateral model of internet governance. it also proposes that the eu institutions concerned maintain financial support for its secretariat to ensure the development of an efficient and independent organisation and thus contribute to the democratisation, openness and neutrality of the internet. all of these are objectives which we consider appropriate and fair, and that is why i voted in favour of the resolution.
in writing. we abstained from voting on this resolution. we understand the importance of discussion forums on internet governance and more, if appropriate, the important role that the representation of the plurality of parliamentary delegations has to play within them. however, we do not share the governance model applied so far in internet governance, nor the preponderant role of icann, centered in the us, and the big tech companies. we value very positively the presence of organised civil society, but we understand that it is in a situation of total asymmetry in relation to the big internet companies. in this sense, we understand that internet governance must be strongly democratized and internationalized and must have an increasing participation of users.
in writing. the main role of the internet governance forum is to hold forward-looking discussions on a wide range of issues concerning internet governance, as well as to make recommendations to the international community. the renewal of the igf's mandate will be discussed at the un general assembly in 2015. it is therefore important to bear in mind that the internet is a pillar of the digital single market and that, according to various forecasts, the relative growth of the internet economy will be almost 11% in the eu and its contribution to gdp will increase from 3,8% in 2010 to 5,7% in 2016. the internet must remain an open, neutral resource that allows us to advance transparency, governance, security and data privacy, as well as ensuring non-discriminatory access to knowledge, respect for fundamental freedoms and human rights, and freedom of expression. for these reasons, i think it is important that the european parliament continues to support the igf.

in writing. the internet governance forum (igf) is a multilateral forum for policy discussion among various sectors with interests in internet governance. it was created in late 2005 by the secretary-general of the united nations following a resolution by governments at the world summit on the information society (wsis). the resolution agreed on stresses that the european parliament has always defended this forum and has always participated in its meetings, and that its mandate should be renewed and its resources strengthened. on a crucial issue such as net neutrality, it underlines the need to ensure an open and independent internet and stresses the 'crucial' importance of continuing efforts to ensure the legal protection of net neutrality as 'a prerequisite' to ensure freedom of information and expression and to boost growth and jobs. for these reasons i voted in favour of the resolution.

in writing. the internet governance forum (igf) promotes discussions on a wide range of issues related to internet governance and, where appropriate, makes recommendations to the international community. the most recent igf meeting, held in september 2014 ('connecting continents for improved multistakeholder internet governance'), is a case in point. the work and topics of the igf are of considerable interest to the eu. economically, the internet-related economy is forecast to grow by almost 11% in the eu and its contribution to gdp will increase from 3,8% in 2010 to 5,7% in 2016 and the internet is a key pillar of the digital single market and promotes, among other things, innovation, growth, trade, democracy, cultural diversity and human rights. i therefore consider the work of the igf to be invaluable and i am voting in favour of this petition to the un general assembly, calling for the igf to be renewed and for more resources to be allocated to it.

in writing. — in the coming years, the digital market in the eu will be one of the keys in order to achieve sustainable economic growth. at the same time, it is our responsibility to be sure that fundamental rights and freedoms are protected on the internet, as well as net neutrality. expanding the access to internet around the world is the way forward to extend knowledge and future growth, and so this is why i voted in favour of renewing the mandate for the internet governance forum.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the renewal of the mandate of the internet governance forum, which had broad consensus among the groups. the criteria for the european parliament's participation in this forum, which was set up to implement the mandate of the world summit on the information society (wsis), are set out. the united nations general assembly decided on 20 december 2010 to extend the mandate of the forum for a period of five years and, by the end of 2015, the general assembly will discuss and decide on the renewal of the mandate.
in writing. the objective of the internet governance forum (igf) is to implement the mandate of the world summit on the information society (wsis) as a contribution to a democratic, transparent and multilateral political dialogue, which broadens the range of issues of economic governance on the internet. this resolution aims to pressure the un general assembly to renew the igf's mandate, strengthen its resources and maintain the multilateral model of internet governance. it also proposes that the eu institutions concerned maintain financial support for its secretariat to ensure the development of an efficient and independent organisation and thus contribute to the democratisation, openness and neutrality of the internet. all of these are objectives which we consider appropriate and fair, and that is why i voted in favour of the resolution.
mr president, i voted against this resolution because it is based and justified on two premises which are totally false. the first is that labelling will prevent fraud like that of horse meat: fake. the second is that labelling improves food quality and safety: false and childish. food quality and safety are not dependent on a label, but on legislation that we have in the european union to ensure both. we need not more labels, but more controls and more effective sanctions to deter those who break the law. we already have mandatory labelling for fresh meat, and voluntary labelling for processed meat. going further means more red tape and costs - especially for small and medium-sized enterprises - which, at the end of the food chain, have to be paid by the consumer. and we shouldn't make that mandatory. nothing is free, but there are costs that are necessary, and superfluous costs like this.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution on the country of origin labelling of meat in processed foods because it improves the information received by consumers on the origin of food. the meat sector has been the scene of numerous scandals due to the practices of large industries that seek to maximize their profits without regard to food safety and quality and their impact on the territory. consumers are becoming increasingly aware of the need to know the origin of the food they consume as a way of reappropriating food. in april, the indication of the origin of meat in unprocessed food will be compulsory, and this resolution calls on the commission to develop legislative measures to make the indication of the origin of meat also compulsory in processed food, in order to oblige the large agri-food industry and not only producers with smaller capital. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this resolution.
in writing. - this motion for a resolution on the country of origin labelling of meat in processed foods seeks to improve consumer information. the compulsory labelling is intended to help improve transparency and restore consumer confidence after scandals such as the horse meat scandal. however, it is not clear what the economic impact will be on the final price of the product and how the introduction of this proposal will affect the competitiveness of companies. we have abstained pending further studies by the european commission, which we hope will be carried out in collaboration with consumer and business organisations.
in writing. this has been a very passionate debate, as it concerns the country of origin labelling of meat on processed foods. i voted in favour of the obligation to indicate the country of origin on the labelling because of the need for consumers to know the origin of the meat in question. the obligation for fresh meat will also come into force from april.
in writing. the parliament resolution calls on the commission to take legislative measures to ensure that the place of origin of meat used in processed foods is indicated on the labelling. the socialists have always defended the labelling of origin for primary products as a quality element, while at the same time we have supported any balanced measure aimed at ensuring a traceability system which makes it possible to easily discover at what point in the chain fraud or falsification may have occurred.
in writing. food labelling should always be considered as an added value in the marketing process and in providing guarantees to the consumer; this compensates for what may be considered bureaucratic obstacles or possible price increases, which are also not clear that they will occur. moreover, knowledge of the origin of food can be an advantage in the marketing of products and not a handicap.
in writing. i would like to express my reluctance to support the mandatory requirement to incorporate a product origin labelling on processed food. in my view, the costs and effects of this measure on the product processing chain are not sufficiently discussed, nor are the advantages for the consumer specified, and the strength of the single market is jeopardised by the introduction of nationalism and the reference to geographical origin within the eu.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution on the country of origin labelling of meat in processed foods because it improves the information received by consumers on the origin of food. the meat sector has been the scene of numerous scandals due to the practices of large industries that seek to maximize their profits without regard to food safety and quality and their impact on the territory. consumers are becoming increasingly aware of the need to know the origin of the food they consume as a way of reappropriating food. in april, the indication of the origin of meat in unprocessed food will be compulsory, and this resolution calls on the commission to develop legislative measures to make the indication of the origin of meat also compulsory in processed food, in order to oblige the large agri-food industry and not only producers with smaller capital. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this resolution.
in writing. european citizens are increasingly demanding in terms of the safety and composition of the food products they consume, and therefore have certain expectations regarding the information available on the origin of products, in particular on the origin of fresh meat and meat used as an ingredient in processed foods. consumers want to be informed, to have all the elements possible when deciding what to consume and what not to consume. similarly, mandatory labelling requirements should take into account the principle of proportionality and the administrative burden they impose on food business operators and the authorities responsible for their application.
in writing. - we voted for this resolution. the place of origin of unprocessed meat is now compulsory when sold in the eu. after the horse meat scandal in frozen lasagna and other processed meat products, the commission raised with parliament the possibility of introducing this obligation also for processed meat products. of course, the indication of the type of meat is already mandatory, but it is understood that introducing the obligation to indicate the place of origin would help to ensure the traceability of the meat ingredients used. the proposed resolution calls on the commission to take the necessary measures to ensure that this is compulsory. we have voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. - eh bildu has voted in favour of the motion for a resolution on country labelling of meat in processed food as such a regulation could provide greater transparency and help in addressing the potential impact of food fraud in food safety, consumer health and consumer confidence by strengthening traceability systems and the information provided to consumers. indeed 90% of consumers consider origin labelling important for the food they consume. the recent horsemeat scandal helped to reveal the murky and complex character of our food chains and heightened consumer demands for better information on where the food they eat comes from. we believe that the commission must listen to these voices and finally come forward with origin labelling proposals for all meat products, including processed foods. eh bildu hence considers that a legislative proposal stating that the origin of meat in processed foods should be mandatory is needed.

in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution on the country of origin labelling of meat in processed foods because i understand that people, as consumers, have the right to decide what we want to eat and also whether with our decision we want to support the local economy and production, as well as whether we want to contribute to the fight against climate change by buying in short circuits. short-term purchases help to reduce energy waste, which is no less important given that we have reached peak oil. to make responsible decisions we need to know the countries of origin of food. in april, the indication of the origin of meat in unprocessed foods will be compulsory, and this resolution calls on the commission to develop legislative measures to make the indication of origin compulsory also for meat in processed foods.
in writing. — i am aware that asking for a mandatory labelling of meat for processed food can create an administrative burden and some economic cost to companies. nonetheless, from a consumer perspective, giving this information can surely bring a positive outcome. this resolution is a request to the european commission to assess the possible consequences of mandatory labelling of meat for processed food and to inform the european parliament of its conclusions. hence, i do believe that with the approval of this resolution, we move into the right direction. only after we evaluate the assessment we have requested to the european commission, will we decide which decision to take.
in writing. i voted in favour of the resolution on the country of origin labelling of meat in processed foods. it is not the first time that a resolution of this kind has been adopted, although the commission has not yet moved a single point. we are again sending the message that we want legislative proposals whereby country of origin labelling is mandatory for processed food, and not just fresh food.
in writing. i voted in favour of this resolution on the country of origin labelling of meat in processed foods because it improves the information received by consumers on the origin of food. the meat sector has been the scene of numerous scandals due to the practices of large industries that seek to maximize their profits without regard to food safety and quality and their impact on the territory. consumers are becoming increasingly aware of the need to know the origin of the food they consume as a way of reappropriating food. in april, the indication of the origin of meat in unprocessed food will be compulsory, and this resolution calls on the commission to develop legislative measures to make the indication of the origin of meat also compulsory in processed food, in order to oblige the large agri-food industry and not only producers with smaller capital. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this resolution.
in writing. this resolution deals with the annual report drawn up by the development committee on the work of the joint parliamentary assembly of the african, caribbean and pacific states, on the one hand, and of the european union, on the other. however, this text has not taken account of my group's proposal to point out that the cotonou agreement also contains economic association agreements which are detrimental to the acp countries. nor does it contain a fundamental element for us, which is the need to denounce the fact that the european development fund is being used to finance military and security operations on the african continent, which contradicts the main objective of european development aid. it is for these two main reasons that i could not vote in favour of this resolution, but abstained.

in writing. with frontex we are building a fortress europe where migration policy is simply a part of security policy: visa restrictions, building of murderous walls and fences, militarization of border control, forced repatriations, subcontracting of migration control to non-democratic countries... we are systematically violating human rights, not only by returning people to their homes, but also by installing knives in fences, by mistreating people in detention centres for foreigners, by ramming our fragile patrol boats into boats full of migrants, and there have even been cases where the european authorities have pulled the trigger. enough of the incoherence and cynicism! it is our policies, foreign policy in general and trade policy in particular, that are driving the people of the south to desperation and forcing them to emigrate. have you given any thought to the effect of ttip on migration? ttip will further impoverish the south and force more people to emigrate. let us be consistent, let us get to the root of the migration problem and promote the development and well-being of the people of the countries of the south and stop impoverishing them.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, sovaldi is the name under which the pharmaceutical company gilead markets sofosbuvir. this medicine increases the chance of curing hepatitis c by up to 95%. but despite the existence of this medicine, hundreds of people die every day from this disease. why would you do that? because, for example, in spain, a 12-week course of treatment with this medicine costs 25 000 euros. the people's party government doesn't subsidize sovaldi for all the patients who need it. there's a cap on spending for the drug. they have put a price on people's lives, although with the 47 million euros of bárcenas, of the people's party, in switzerland, 783 treatments could have been paid for. or, for example, the 40 billion that are not collected each year for tax evasion could pay for 666,000 treatments. and it's true that our governments are inhuman and decide who lives and who dies, and who dies is who doesn't have the money to pay for this treatment when social security doesn't fund it. but we must aim higher: if a sovaldi treatment, of this medicine, has this absolutely outrageous price, it is because patents protect the profits of pharmaceutical companies. patents are a death sentence for millions of people in the world and those who are allowing it are accomplices in murder. the law allows gilead to make a profit of 13.3 billion dollars last year and today, as every day, 12 people have died in spain.
mr president, i want to start on the positive side and say that what i have heard from the council and the commission is good words and good intentions. but more must be done, especially in the light of the recent announcement that the directive on the transparency of the pricing of medicinal products will be withdrawn. this debate affects us all: today it is hepatitis c, tomorrow it will be cancer drugs. patients suffer from it and it puts the different health systems of our member states in jeopardy. my group has promoted this debate because it defends the right to health as a fundamental right which we have enshrined in the treaties and we cannot allow it to be marketed. that said, i would also like to begin by saying that today the member states have the obligation to ensure access to this medicine and to all the innovations that are given to the different patients in their member states, while at the same time they have the obligation, together with the european parliament, the commission and the council, to seek mechanisms for transparency in the setting of prices, to see the results of all the clinical trials and to confirm what the real added value is that these new medicines bring and to see what percentage actually corresponds to research within those prices. we need new powers for the european medicines agency and new measures to enable coordinated purchasing, or measures such as auctions, which are already being implemented in countries like my own, andalusia. i also want to acknowledge the role of the ngos, which have taught us a lesson today and have been at the forefront of many governments in the member states; and i want, and i ask, and i demand, finally, the necessary political will, because i think we have powers to spare.
mr president, 2 billion people lack access to medicines, either because of their high cost or because there is no adequate medication. this is the consequence of drug development being oriented towards market priorities rather than public health requirements. in europe, disparities in access to medicines are increasingly widening between and within countries. in spain, between ten and twelve people die every day from hepatitis c, and access to the most effective medicine to combat this disease is restricted by its excessive price. however, the company that markets this drug earned in one year more than it cost to purchase the patent. the current model of biomedical research corners knowledge through intellectual property rights, conceals risks and places knowledge generated through eu funding, everyone's money, in private hands. the european union must ensure that citizens benefit from investments by improving public health, by changing the research model, by initiatives such as free and socially responsible licensing, open source research, open access to research, and by ensuring that states can put health protection ahead of patents and the profits of a few. we cannot allow only those who can afford to live to have the right to live.
mr president, we should call this debate 'the case for the best cost-benefit ratio in the world'. europe cannot leave this question to a social confrontation between heroic and heroic individuals and state and private powers acting against the general interest. the member states are dependent on the large pharmaceutical industry, which controls the markets and stifles social security systems. that's why we have to act now. we don't need experts or reports. we know everything. we can make decisions right away. and this must be done in the short term in the face of social emergencies, such as hepatitis c, and more thoroughly in order to adopt the urgent legislative reform that europe needs, a reform based on four concepts: properly compensated public research, full transparency of processes and associated costs, decoupling of prices and development costs, extensive use of generics. parliament must now take the initiative to lead this dual strategy, which has now been frozen by the council and the commission. and we shall do so, first, by means of the specific resolution which develops these points and formulates the corresponding mandate.
mr president, mr stylianides, mrs kalniņa-lukaševica, hepatitis c has put europe in front of the mirror, and what the mirror shows us is that our model of access to medicines does not work. nine million european citizens, hundreds of thousands in spain, are crying out for a medicine that saves their lives. a chronic, incurable, deadly disease now has a cure. and governments are obliged to provide it. it is up to the states to set prices and to finance public health, but the european union has a mandate to ensure the protection of human health. i therefore call on the commission and the council today to draw up as a matter of urgency a european plan for access to medicines, including a new structure for the relationship with the pharmaceutical industry, which is an essential partner in fulfilling this mandate; a review of the directive on price transparency; a thorough review of the current patent model, which separates the costs of research from the final price of medicines; and a policy of aggregate purchases that strengthens the negotiating position of the states in the procurement of key medicines. and it's not an emotional thing, it's a right.
mr president, hepatitis c patients are dying in spain, abandoned by their government, without access to life-saving and very expensive treatments. in addition to the irresponsibility of the spanish government, this case confronts us with a debate: patients or patents? multinationals or people? under pressure from civil society movements, the world trade organization adopted the doha declaration in 2001. it was clear that intellectual property rights in medicines should not be an obstacle to access to medicines by the world's population. ngos soon denounced that this declaration was not being fulfilled and that millions of people were dying every year because of it. this problem, which used to affect only the impoverished countries, has now reached europe. that, ladies and gentlemen, is also globalisation. the european commission is to blame for this. in 2013 he pressured india not to export generic drugs. and he also pressured the governments of the european union not to import much cheaper indian medicines, including those that cure hepatitis c. you have to choose. what is the position of the commission and the large coalition supporting it? citizens or multinationals? and when you make that decision, remember that thousands of people die in europe because of hepatitis c, and millions worldwide.
mr president, in view of the late hour and the debate, allow me to make a few remarks on this very important subject. first of all, i would like to say that we must realize, and this has been said here, that health policy, pharmaceutical policy, is in the hands of the national states of the member countries. this is, in my opinion, the right thing to do, and it is up to each country, its administration, to decide in the national elections how much money to allocate to public health systems and how much money to provide for expensive medicines. this is very important. i think the european union can do something about it, though. it is not by accumulating powers, but by promoting cooperation and cooperation between the individual member states, as the commissioner and the council representative have indicated in their speeches here. so cooperation, support, that's what should come from the european level. more support for research and innovation, that is the theme that was also raised here. the eu can play a rather significant role here. the promotion of generics and the debate on what patent protection should look like in general is also an important topic. there is a need to guarantee that intellectual property is protected, but i think generics are a good thing, where the eu can play a strong role. and also in the area of those approval procedures already mentioned. so this is an important issue, we should talk about it, we should encourage cooperation between member countries, not delegate authority.
mr president, today millions of european citizens have no access to medicines that can cure them and save their lives. those affected by hepatitis c in spain are the most visible face of this drama, but there are also millions of people affected by rare diseases who suffer in silence from this problem. the exorbitant prices imposed by the pharmaceutical industry monopolies prevent all patients who need treatment from paying for it, denying them the right to health and breaking the principle of equity. this is so for three main reasons: because there is a pricing system that lacks the information and transparency needed to know the costs and profitability achieved by companies; because there is inadequate regulation and control of r & d and patents that benefits multinationals against the sick; and because the european union - i am sorry to say - does not exercise its ability to influence negotiations to lower industry prices. ladies and gentlemen, the rules of the game must be changed and that requires political will. the european union needs to manage intellectual property more efficiently, it needs to demand transparency and the information needed to know the costs of innovation and reward it in a fair way, and it needs to put in place a centralised purchasing mechanism. look, we don't accept the death penalty, but we are able to accept deferred executions for millions of people who can't afford the medicine they need to stay alive. i hope that none of you will find yourselves in that situation and that we will be able to resolve this real drama as soon as possible.
mr president, the matter before us today is not a minor one. we talk about people, we talk about health, we talk about knowledge, we talk about transparency. today we are faced with unfair situations where european citizens are restricted in their access to the medicines they need to survive. a few weeks ago, this member asked the commission about this very issue, which is of great concern to catalonia, the whole of spain and the rest of the union. and one of the questions was whether the commission intends to promote or establish a common position among the member states so that no patient in the union is discriminated against on the grounds of belonging to one or another state, or is limited in his access to public health care by his level of income. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. and while we say this with full conviction, we must be aware that we must find a balance which in turn guarantees pharmaceutical laboratories continuity of research and non-abusive protection of their patents and universal access to prescribed treatment in health care. without affordable medication, we cannot cure. if we don't heal, we fail. but without a return on labor, there are no new drugs, and without new drugs, there are no affordable drugs. we must break this vicious circle without breaking the fragile balance in the content. all of this should make us ask ourselves what kind of society we want to leave behind: ask ourselves, answer ourselves and work to make our proposals a reality.
member of the commission. - mr president, i very much appreciate the views expressed here tonight, which i can assure you will be conveyed to the relevant colleagues within the commission. i can also assure you that the commission will continue to work hard in support of member states to improve patient access to medicines across the european union. as i already explained in my earlier speech, a great deal of preparatory work has already been delivered since the commission declaration was made here in strasbourg in september last year. on tuesday next week, the working party on public health at senior level will convene in brussels. that is very important. the latvian presidency of the council has already proposed a discussion document for the member states, which will serve as the basis for future work, for which i would like to thank it very much. the commission will, naturally, continue to actively support these and other discussions. this is the situation. of course, all of us already recognise the difficulties, but let me close by thanking parliament once again for its interest and its activities in support of our common objective in this important area of access to medicines for patients.
president-in-office of the council. - mr president, i would like to thank the members of the european parliament for their views and suggestions for the future work to be conducted by the council and the member states, and i also thank you, commissioner, for mentioning the presidency document. a number of you have raised the issue of pricing and reimbursement of medicinal products. there is a widespread view that more transparency on pricing decisions by member states for reimbursement proposals, as well as the pricing of medicinal products by the industry, would contribute to lowering prices. while pricing for proposals of reimbursement is an exclusive competence of the member states, the only way forward is a voluntary exchange of information on member states’ pricing and reimbursement models, and involvement of the industry. this was one of the objectives of the council conclusions on innovation for the benefit of patients, adopted on 1 december 2014. such information-sharing between the member states’ competent authorities could take place in the network of competent authorities on pricing and reimbursement established in 2008. i can assure you that the presidency will inform the council about the views expressed during this debate in order to feed them into the ongoing debate in the council and in other relevant fora on the issue of access to medicines. thank you very much for today’s debate. it was a very important debate.
in writing. access to medicines is discussed in plenary at the initiative of our delegation in response to the social demand for hepatitis c treatment, although it has already been under discussion, as it is a major problem both for the sustainability of health systems and for ensuring equity; in short, we consider that it infringes the fundamental right to health. we propose action on several fronts, one of the most important being price transparency. the prices of medicines in the twenty-eighties should be made public and the full results of clinical trials should be known in order to determine their true added value and the percentage of research costs in the price of medicines. this requires a european agency for the evaluation of new technologies or at least new powers for the eea. other measures would be coordinated purchases and auctions, with which there is already experience in spain (andalusia). however, this work cannot absolve member states of the obligation to ensure access to new medicines, beyond promoting measures to ensure the sustainability of health systems.

in writing. i support the resolution on the establishment of a special committee for tax rulings and other measures similar in nature or effect. however, i must express my view that it must operate on the basis, in particular, of the principle that tax competition between states is beneficial. tax harmonisation, on the other hand, would not, in my view, help european economies. on the other hand, i am of course in favour of the effort to expose tax evasion and injustice.
in writing. i voted in favour of the special committee on tax rulings and other measures similar in nature or effect, set up in the wake of the luxleaks case, which will have to present its proposals within a maximum of one year to build a genuine tax union and put an end to tax havens, tax evasion, privileges and fraudulent tax competition in the eu. the spanish socialists are committed to ending banking secrecy, getting companies to pay taxes where they make their profits and creating a common corporate tax for the eu.
in writing. - we voted in favour of the proposal to set up a committee to investigate, from a general point of view, the various types of problems relating to european taxation. we believe, however, that the creation of this committee comes after the impossibility of an inquiry into the tax regimes under which members who are now leading figures in the european institutions have been able to facilitate tax engineering maneuvers for different companies or private entities of various kinds.
in writing. - we voted in favour of the proposal to set up a committee to investigate, from a general point of view, the various types of problems relating to european taxation. we believe, however, that the proposal to set up this committee comes after the fact that it has become impossible to carry out an inquiry into the tax regimes under which members who are now leading figures in the european institutions have been able to facilitate tax engineering maneuvers for different companies or private entities of various kinds.
in writing. - the european parliament has approved the creation of a special committee on the luxleaks case. we have abstained from this vote because we consider that this is not a sufficient measure. our group is calling for a commission of inquiry into the case, which has been blocked again by the grand coalition (popular, socialist and liberal).

on behalf of the ppe group mr president, the request has been made by the honourable member in very clear terms: we ask for the agenda to be changed, for a debate on venezuela to be opened and for a motion for a resolution to be tabled for the next strasbourg plenary. the reasons - to be brief - are very clear. in december this house already adopted a resolution, with very broad support, on the situation in venezuela, but not three months have passed and the situation has not only not improved, but in all the media of the world it is clearly seen that there is an exceptional situation: new imprisonments, political persecution of the opposition and a credible risk of involution, so that our request is more than justified. just yesterday, a poor boy of fourteen died in the streets as a result of a confrontation. mr president, we believe that this debate is more than justified in the terms envisaged.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, we in the group of the european united left oppose the inclusion of this item on the agenda because we believe that the only reason for wanting to debate today in this house the arrest of the mayor of caracas (who has been arrested for alleged involvement in an attempted coup d'état) is that you are engaged in a campaign against the venezuelan government and against the processes of transformation in latin america, with the aim of contributing to the plans of the venezuelan extreme right which, by the hand of the united states, wants to overthrow a government legitimately elected by the people, as happened in 2002 in the coup d'état against president chávez. a government whose only sin has been to lift millions of people out of poverty and hunger... because - let's be clear - mr ledesma is being arrested for coup d'état: for allegedly being involved in a coup d'état.
mr president, the commission is using the limits of state policies to impose its own liberalizing agenda. the specific problems of some highly dependent states such as cyprus or the baltic states become the lever of a project which combines an aggressive policy of resource hoarding with the development of private mega-infrastructures which require high demand to become profitable. the commission is committed, in words only, to an energy model based on energy saving and clean energy, but it is hard to believe that the transition can be made through market mechanisms. in spain, forced liberalisation and overcapacity have particularly penalized renewable and innovative energy in reducing carbon emissions, creating serious legal uncertainty in the sector, where the government accumulates multiple demands. all this without any concrete benefits for consumers. the result is the one set by the oligopoly. they talk about smart meters when there are four million people without heating and an industry threatened by energy surcharges. they are hostages to a system which the commission intends to copy at european level.
mr president, mr šefčovič, i commend you and acknowledge your commitment and will, and i quote the part of your speech where you are committed to renewable energy and to the empowerment of citizens and the local level. i listen to his words and then i look at reality. in some member states, such as spain, where investment in renewables is falling and almost disappearing in r & d & i, and where little or no consideration is given to citizens and municipalities, the trend is rather the opposite: strengthening the control of large companies over energy and citizens while penalizing sovereign practices such as self-consumption. what steps will the european commission take to prevent some governments from leaving their guidelines or good wishes on renewable energies on wet paper, as is happening now?
mr president, commissioner, i can only welcome the communication we are discussing here today. but i would like to see it translated into action, and into ambitious action, because it is obvious that we need a new energy model, decentralized and sustainable. and i say that it should be translated into action because so far the commission has not made it clear when it has reduced targets on renewable energy or energy efficiency or has paralysed directives such as air quality or the circular economy. but i still say, and i repeat, that i take it very positively and optimistically. i am also glad that it has included socialist proposals such as the carrying out of audits or reports on prices which show that energy sources such as renewable energy are not only environmentally sustainable but also economically sustainable and thus demonstrate this for countries such as my own, spain. i would also like to see self-consumption included, but i would ask that it be - if we are to achieve a truly decentralised model - toll-free. finally, i want to say that i miss the energy poverty that has already been shown here. if we want a real energy union, energy cannot be left on the doorstep of millions of europeans who suffer from energy poverty, but we must make it reach their homes.
mr president, energy is fundamental to the functioning of any society and its economy, and especially in societies as highly complex as ours. energy policies are therefore crucial to guaranteeing the sovereignty of peoples. we are now facing a major historical challenge, having reached peak oil extraction and being close to natural gas. the european union's solution to these problems is the creation of a liberalised common market, without legal or physical barriers so that the large energy companies can continue to do their business, leaving in private hands - with the collaboration of state regulators - almost exclusive control of something so vital, at the same time as in some countries, for example in the spanish state, regulations are being advanced that prevent distributed production and citizens from increasing their capacity for self-sufficiency in energy. and it also does not solve the energy poverty situation. meanwhile, policies to save energy, decarbonise and shift to a renewable energy model remain too timid or simply ignored.
mr president, the resolution on counter-terrorism measures adopted by almost all the political forces in this parliament at its last session and the declaration against terrorism which came out of the last council meeting are clear signs that we are moving in the right direction. in spain too, an agreement has been reached between the governing party and the main opposition party, the socialist party, to combat terrorism. now that we are moving in the right direction, we cannot just talk. it is time that the unity that we have shown in the three institutions and that has been seen in this parliament, was translated into action. we are starting with what we are directly responsible for, namely the approval of a european pnr to help us monitor the movements of so-called foreign fighters with scrupulous respect for fundamental rights. the implementation of this tool does not depend on our words, it depends on our actions and it depends on us. we would also like to remind you that everything that is done in the fight against terrorism must always take account of the victims. i would like to conclude by adding that my country, which i represent here, spain, is committed to a true energy union. spain and portugal have always called for increased energy connections with europe. and now europe is also interested in increasing energy connections with spain and portugal. no one in europe can be an energy island, but the very idea of europe says that no one in europe can be an island in any sense. greece, mr president-in-office of the council, is not an island either.
in writing. the last informal european council dealt with, among other issues, the greek public debt crisis and the follow-up to the new report on economic and monetary union, which now belongs to the five presidents, as it joins the european parliament, which is good news. as regards greece, i think that the four-month extension of the financial assistance programme and the list of reforms presented by the greek government are indeed positive, and i hope, on the other hand, that greater flexibility will be introduced with regard to the primary budget surplus targets. however, serious doubts remain about the long-term sustainability of the overall greek public debt. that is why i suggest that the commission prepare a feasibility study on how to establish, on the basis of the european stability mechanism, a debt amortization fund for the euro area. i also think it is urgent to draw up a list of priority investments for greece under the proposed european fund for strategic investments, especially in the renewable energy sector, which can become a driving force behind the new development model in greece, creating qualified and quality jobs in the process.
rapporteur. - madam president, mr draghi, as always it is a pleasure to have you in this house. ladies and gentlemen, i would like to begin by thanking the rapporteurs, with whom it has been an honour to work, and together we have made an effort to get a report as fair as possible. let's look at 2013, which was a difficult year for the euro area: gross domestic product fell by 0.4% and unemployment peaked at 12% at the end of the year. instead, in 2014 the economic recovery has begun. the euro area's gross domestic product has risen by 0.9%, and the forecasts for 2015 are even more encouraging. as regards inflation, in 2013 the average inflation rate was 1,3%. instead, in 2014 we ended the year with negative inflation rates, that is, not meeting the target we have set of having inflation below but close to 2%. credit to the private sector remains negative, closing at a negative rate of -2.4%. we must be aware that without credit there will be no consolidation of economic recovery. i think that the european central bank and its president are doing a great job in achieving stability in the euro area and they are also doing a great job both the ecb and its president in getting the actors involved to do their job as well. but it is also true that the measures taken by the european central bank could have been more effective and more efficient in restoring credit to the real economy. we are aware that the financial markets in the euro area are fragmented and there is no proper transmission of monetary policy. but we must also be aware that the european central bank has had to face a very difficult environment as a result of an unprecedented financial, political and economic crisis and an incomplete economic union. it is not the task of the european central bank to complete economic union, but to give time to the other actors involved in consolidating economic union and, ultimately, political union. i think it is fair to point out the rapid reaction of the european central bank. this rapid reaction has reduced stress levels in the euro area financial markets and has also helped to restore confidence in the single currency. this is evidenced by the interest rates and risk premiums at which member states finance themselves, especially those which have been more ambitious in structural reforms. ladies and gentlemen, it is time for joint action. an expansionary monetary policy must be accompanied by reforms at both national and european level. a good example of this is my country, spain, one of the most ambitious countries in terms of reforms on behalf of the alde group. – madam president, if the ecb is to expand its balance sheet, it is better if the quantitative easing (qe) enhances the potential of the real economy in europe. in this respect, mr draghi, i am particularly pleased by the ecb commitment to buy european investment bank (eib) bonds in the coming programme of bond purchases. three weeks ago the committee on economic and monetary affairs voted by a very large majority to call on the ecb to buy eib bonds, especially those related to investment in infrastructures, such as energy and transport interconnections europe-wide. eib bonds based on those projects should be prioritised in those buyings, as clear projects with proven european added value and a positive cost-benefit analysis. for instance, it is strategic for europe to connect by freight transport the mediterranean ports with the european markets. this real-economy-oriented bonds purchase is very important because the qe has to operate on different national markets, each with varying degrees of risk. thus, it is possible that the qe mainly generates a hike in the stock market without effects on the real economy. there is also the risk that buying corporate bonds will only serve for big enterprises to arrange buybacks without an increase in investment. in contrast, i think that buying securitised loans to smes is an important step forward. i hope that its relative importance inside your programme will evolve positively as the market grows. on the other hand, some voices in the financial markets are claiming that they do not want to sell their government bonds to the ecb. it is due to possible losses in the transaction, as most bonds are yielding much less nowadays than the moment when they were bought and a relevant part of bonds today are in a negative territory. mr draghi, one final question. in case government bonds targets are not accomplished due to shortages in the markets, is the ecb ready to buy more bonds from the eib and abs?

in writing. one of the most important elements of the president of the european central bank's speech at the plenary session on 25 february was the one on the need to increase shared sovereignty in the euro area. monetary union is not sound in the long term unless it is accompanied by an economic, fiscal and budgetary union capable of offsetting the macroeconomic disturbances that occur within it, which in turn requires a federal political union. as mr draghi has rightly explained, integration based on common institutions, such as the currency, is more effective than integration structured through rules, such as the stability and growth pact. concrete steps are therefore needed to build a fiscal capacity for the euro area, fuelled by taxes such as the international financial transaction tax, and able to support a treasury that issues public debt denominated in euro, which in turn contributes to increasing the liquidity and financial stability of the monetary union.
