member of the commission.– mr president, the commission very much welcomes the constructive approach to this important file both under the current rapporteur mr lamassoure and under mrs kratsa—tsaragopoulou in the previous parliament. in particular, we are very thankful for parliament’s willingness to compromise on issues such as the european investment quota to ensure that the european long-term investment funds are in place and in a form that is both attractive for potential managers and investors. the european long—term investment funds will invest in a wide range of underlying assets – infrastructure, real assets and other long-term projects, unlisted companies, listed small and medium—sized enterprises capitalised up to eur 500 million and intellectual property. it is a unique opportunity for asset managers to give investors access to a far wider range of assets than has hitherto been available, in a robustly regulated legal framework. as such, it is a key component in our work on the financial markets union to increase the amounts of market financing going into the real economy. this regulation is one of the first concrete expressions of our work with capital markets. at the moment, private investors interested in committing money for the long term face a set of fragmented national markets which can make it hard for them to invest in one single member state or across borders within the union. this in turn restricts the amount of private investment for jobs and growth. the european long-term investment funds are designed to solve this problem, creating a uniform set of rules that allows all types of investors to invest in smes, long-term projects and companies. this makes it a first mover in a true capital markets union as it creates a robust and reliable framework for investors who want to make long—term commitments of capital. members probably know even better than me that there is a pressing need to do exactly that. as mr lamassoure has just pointed out, the winds are a little milder these days with the euro going down and with energy pricing being more favourable to growth but, at the same time, we need investment. the estimated investment is about eur 1 500 billion to eur 2 000 billion by the year 2020 to finance infrastructure projects which are so keenly needed. the european long-term investments funds have a role to play here and in other parts of the economy where long-term committed capital is needed. our commitment to market-based financing, channelled through these funds, does not exclude the role that banks can play in long-term financing. banks continue to play a very important role in financing long-term businesses and projects in many member states. the european long-term investment funds are therefore complementary to this activity. parliament and the council have always agreed that smes are crucially important to the european economy and so their inclusion as an asset within this is key. i would like to pay tribute to parliament’s farsightedness in including intellectual, as well as physical, property within these funds. research and development play a vital role in our economies and they are as much in need of financing as physical infrastructures for example. ensuring that all types of investors – retail investors as well as major institutions such as insurance companies and pension funds – can access our european long-term investment funds has always been a key element of the commission proposal. parliament’s support for retail access has proven vital in ensuring that this remains the case in the final result. i also commend the house’s willingness to accept the extra safeguards proposed, such as only allowing investors with less than eur 500 million in assets to invest and not to put more than 10% of their savings into these funds.
the commission's investment plan is intended to work the miracle of the multiplication of the loaves and fishes, by leveraging just 21 billion of public money into a total of 315 billion of private investment. its flagship products include european long-term investment funds which can be marketed by both institutions and individuals. however, the regulation before us does not provide for appropriate safeguards, safeguards which protect the purpose of the saver's contribution. there are too many doors open for participation and management of vulture funds and venture capital. we cannot put people's savings at risk and put them at the service of a failed macroeconomic policy. in my country we have some very bad examples, such as the "preferences", where small savers invested in products that were presented as promising but whose opacity and risk have ended up ruining tens of thousands of people. ladies and gentlemen, on the one hand, the ambition of this false european new deal known as the 'juncker plan' is frankly ridiculous in terms of reviving a community economy that is absolutely anaemic from neoliberal policies. but, moreover, to trust that products like the filpe can be rented in just three years is not credible. let us not again feed casino capitalism from the institutions, let us not again inflate a new bubble of financial speculation by playing with people's savings, let us not mortgage the future of our citizens.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, commissioners, i would first of all like to congratulate mr lamassoure on his work on this report, which i believe opens the door to a new way of financing to restore the effective demand that we so badly need in this europe. and this new stage in which europe is putting the emphasis on growth and investment should not make us forget the last years of adjustment, of cuts and of an absolutely narrow view of economic policy which, as mrs berès has pointed out, has prevented europe from recovering growth, investment and job creation. in any case, we welcome the european longterm investment funds. we welcome this project, which must go hand in hand with the european fund for strategic investments, the so-called 'juncker plan', so that we in europe can put growth and investment first and channel the huge amount of savings, the huge amount of liquidity that the ecb is putting into the market, to make it work in the real economy. and let it go hand in hand with the commission's project also to promote the capital market union, so that among all these elements we are able to boost growth in europe, we are able to put investment, demand and job creation first, and forget about the last legislature, that legislature in which the conservative and neoliberal majority in this house was brutal, and put growth and job creation on the back foot.
mr president, the european union continues to insist on the liberalization of capital markets, even as we are still suffering from the outbreak of the financial crisis. and it does so through a new type of european investment fund, a tool to enable large groups of anonymous investors to position themselves in the lush investment and public supply market - the only one that can guarantee the long-term contracts that this initiative wants to feed off. the complex network of national and international regulators is becoming more complex, with a very high degree of discretion in the use of funds; we even question the appropriateness of the fund itself when the state or the industrial bank could regularly finance this type of initiative with greater control. once again, financial liberalisation is moving forward alongside a privatisation agenda. but we do not want roads, hospitals, prisons or universities in the hands of rent-seekers who are not interested in the public interest, because our europe is not the europe of finance but the europe of the working men and women.
king of the hashemite kingdom of jordan.– bismillah ar-rahman ar-rahim. mr president, distinguished members, jordan treasures its long ties of friendship with this great institution, and i appreciate your invitation to speak here today. permettez-moi aussi de remercier les citoyens de strasbourg pour leur hospitalité chaleureuse. cette ville représente toujours un symbole du passage de la guerre à la paix, un symbole de la réconciliation et de l'unité de l'europe. (l'assemblée, debout, applaudit l'orateur) my friends, people thrive where there is mutual respect. civilisation is built on it and futures are better for it, but co-existence must be made, and made again, in every generation. the common good is defended only by vigilance and action, and this means more than security measures. humanity must arm itself with ideas, with justice, and with economic and social inclusion. today these challenges have a special importance. our world faces an assault by terrorists with ruthless ambition. the motive is not faith: it is power pursued by ripping countries and communities apart in sectarian conflicts and inflicting suffering across the world. (applause)the savage murder by daesh of jordan’s hero pilot outraged all jordanians and horrified the world. jordan’s response has been swift, serious and determined, and our fight will continue. (applause)we and other arab and muslim states defend not only our people but our faith. this is a fight that has to be carried out by muslim nations first and foremost. (applause)this is a fight within islam. at the same time, the danger of extremism must be seen for what it is: global. the threat is not only in syria and in iraq. it has struck libya, yemen, sinai, mali, nigeria, the horn of africa, asia, the americas and australia. europe has suffered despicable attacks and shown unbeatable courage. your friends are with you. in january, rania and i joined millions of people in france who marched, united, against violence and intimidation. my friends, there are those living in europe today who remember the ravages that struck the continent in the late 1930s and the world war that followed, because of an aggressive, expansionist ideology based on hatred and disregard for the very essence of humanity. europe’s war became the world’s war. today we are fighting a similar war, a war against an expansionist ideology that feeds on hate, that is committing murder in the name of god and religion, to justify evil actions that no religion tolerates – a war against terrorists who disrespect islam’s values and humanity’s values. our victory now depends on our unity and europe’s role is vital. only by cooperation can our regions shut down the sources of terrorist support and defeat their purposes. and it is also essential that our regions renew the source of our great strength: the mutual respect that binds and sustains us. young people especially must be inspired by values that reject violence, create peace and build inclusive societies. (applause)let me suggest three areas of importance. the first is meaningful interfaith outreach, engaging people where they live. a dialogue of respect is the rock—bed of all societies. attacking and excluding others, insulting other peoples and their faith and their convictions – this is no way forward. the future lies in unity and respect, not division and stereotypes. (applause)europe is an important partner in this effort, especially in helping to stop the global rise of islamophobia. this poison is based on false ideas and helps play into the hands of these extremists. this is why it is important to clarify what it really means to be a muslim. i and countless other muslims have been taught from our earliest years that our religion demanded respect and caring for others. the prophet mohammad, peace and blessings be upon him, said: ‘none of you has faith until you love for your neighbour what you love for yourself.’ this is what it means to be a muslim. among the very names of god we hear the compassionate, the all-merciful. all my life, every day, i have heard and used the greeting assalamu aleikum – a wish for the other to be blessed with peace. this is what it means to be a muslim. (applause)more than a thousand years ago, before the geneva conventions, muslim soldiers were ordered not to kill a child, a woman or an old person, not to destroy a tree, not to harm a priest, not to destroy a church. these are the same values of islam we were taught in school as children: not to destroy or desecrate a place where god is worshipped, not a mosque, not a church, not a synagogue. (applause)this is what it means to be a muslim. these are the values i teach my children and that they will hand on to theirs. my friends, i am outraged and grieved by the recent attacks in some countries against christian and minority communities. this is an offence against humanity as well as islam. arab christians are an integral part of our region’s past, present and future. (applause)jordan is a muslim country with a deeply—rooted christian community. together the jordanian people make up an indivisible society – friends and partners in building our country. the world’s muslims have a critical role in global understanding. our faith, like yours, commands mercy, peace and tolerance. it upholds, as yours does, the equal human dignity of every person – men and women, neighbours and strangers. those outlaws of islam who deny these truths are vastly outnumbered by the ocean of believers – 1.6 billion muslims worldwide. in fact these terrorists have made the world’s muslims their greatest target. we will not allow them to hijack our faith. (applause)my friends, the second area key to global harmony is an international system that gives all people the respect they want and deserve. again and again i hear the question: why does the world not defend palestinian rights? time after time the peace process has stalled. let me say what the situation looks like in reality – more israeli settlement-building, less respect for the occupied palestinians. this failure sends a dangerous message. it erodes trust in international law and community. it threatens a pillar of world peace: that conflict must be solved by political means, not by force, not by violence, and it has given the extremists a powerful rallying cry. they exploit the injustices and the lingering conflict, to build legitimacy and recruit foreign fighters across europe and the world. (applause)it is time to think about the future and how this ongoing conflict will breed further hate, violence and terror across the world. how can we fight the ideological battle if we do not chart the way forward towards palestinian—israeli peace? our countries, united, must provide the momentum and chart the way forward towards a final comprehensive settlement. (applause)ladies and gentlemen, a third critical effort is creating deeper hope. radicalisation thrives on economic insecurity and exclusion. to create stakeholders in a peaceful world, people need opportunities to fulfil their potential and build good lives. helping them is a powerful message of respect. the european parliament has recognised the importance of creating social and economic opportunities in naming 2015 the year of development. for jordan, development is a priority and despite all the regional challenges we have pressed forward to meet urgent needs, to grow jobs, to improve the quality of life through continued reforms and partnerships such as yours. jordan values our strong partnership with the european union and its member states. we are committed, with your support, to work together towards more advanced levels of partnership. (applause)jordan also takes seriously our moral obligations to others. despite scarce resources, the people of jordan have opened their arms to refugees fleeing regional violence. as the president mentioned earlier, jordan has taken in thousands of iraqi christians over the past year. this in addition to giving shelter to 1.4 million syrian refugees, which is 20% of the population, over the past few years. (applause)this is more than the equivalent of france hosting the entire population of belgium. our small country is now the world’s third largest refugee host and i thank all of you who are helping us to uphold this global responsibility. (applause)my friends, your support sends a message, not only to my people but to all those who seek to move forward in peace and moderation. europe is with you. our regions, our people, can find no better partners and neighbours than each other. history, geography and future bind us. let no one separate us because together we can create pillars of mutual respect that will support the common good for generations to come. (loud and sustained applause) (the house accorded the speaker a standing ovation)
in writing. i voted in favour of the report as it allows for the mobilisation of resources following the redundancies in zaklady chemiczne zachem and two suppliers due to the cessation of production operations and the restructuring of the zachem corporation, classified in nace revision 2 division 20 (manufacture of chemicals) in the nuts 2 region of the province of kuyavia-pomerania. the commission also found that the union industry had a significant market share in the union market, which was below the level of the union industry's market share in the union. this mobilization of funds is due to the disastrous consequences of the internationalisation of the productive sectors in the eu. these funds are not able to solve the problems of these workers in the context of unemployment in poland, but at least they give the possibility of alleviating a small part of the human drama. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund to alleviate the problems arising from the redundancies at zaklady chemiczne zachem and two of its suppliers due to the cessation of production operations and the corporate restructuring of zachem, the chemical company. poland has the right to access such aid which i hope will alleviate the situation of the workers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to approve the mobilisation of eur 115 205 from the globalisation adjustment fund for 615 workers who have lost their jobs at the zaklady chemiczne zachem plant in the province of kuyavia-pomerania, poland, which is dedicated to the manufacture of chemicals and chemicals, due to the closure of the production operations and the restructuring of the zachem corporation, as a result of the structural changes in world trade due to globalisation and the impact of the economic and financial crisis. the personalised services to be financed by the egf comprise recruitment incentives and intervention work for the 50 most disadvantaged workers. while this aid alone cannot alleviate the problem of unemployment in the european chemical sector due to the tendency to move chemical manufacturing to asia, it does constitute good assistance and training for the reintegration of the workers concerned.
in writing. the podemos delegation in the european parliament has voted in favour of the mobilisation of this fund, considering that there is an objective need and a legitimate expectation on the part of the workers made redundant to receive the associated series of grants. however, we consider the globalisation adjustment fund to be insufficient in the current economic climate. the processes of industrial conversion and labour flexibility make it more difficult to absorb a growing mass of workers and devalue the social rights of workers.
in writing. ‒ europe and the world are engaged in a profound process of globalisation which, while a source of trade and wealth creation, can also entail risks to which we must be very attentive. as a result of this process, there are sectors which are more exposed to international competition, and the eu must therefore respond to those citizens who lose their jobs as a result of globalisation. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) supports workers who lose their jobs as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns caused by globalisation (e.g. the closure of large companies or the relocation of production outside the eu) or by the global economic and financial crisis. i have therefore voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (application egf/2013/009 pl/zachem)

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to approve the mobilisation of eur 981 956 from the european globalisation adjustment fund for 708 workers who have lost their jobs at duferco and nlmk, companies located in la louvière, belgium, and engaged in steel production, as a result of the structural changes in world trade due to globalisation and the impact of the economic and financial crisis. the steelmaking sector has suffered from severe economic disruption, in particular a rapid decline in the eu market share, which has been exacerbated by other factors such as the decreased demand for steel in the automotive and construction sectors as a result of the economic crisis and a relative increase in production costs. the personalised services to be financed by the egf cover various needs in terms of training and retraining of workers. while this aid alone cannot alleviate the problem of unemployment in the european steel industry, it does provide good assistance and training for the reintegration of the workers concerned.
in writing. ‒ the podemos delegation in the european parliament has voted in favour of the mobilisation of this fund, considering that there is an objective need and a legitimate expectation on the part of the workers made redundant to receive the associated aid package. however, we consider the globalisation adjustment fund to be insufficient in the current economic climate. the processes of industrial conversion and labour flexibility make it more difficult to absorb a growing mass of workers and devalue the social rights of workers.
in writing. ‒ europe and the world are engaged in a profound process of globalisation which, while a source of trade and wealth creation, can also entail risks to which we must be very attentive. as a result of this process, there are sectors which are more exposed to international competition, and the eu must therefore respond to those citizens who lose their jobs as a result of globalisation. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) supports workers who lose their jobs as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns caused by globalisation (e.g. the closure of large companies or the relocation of production outside the eu) or by the global economic and financial crisis. i have therefore voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (application egf/2013/007 be/hainaut steel (duferco-nlmk))
in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns caused by globalisation or the financial crisis and to help them find new jobs. i voted in favour of this report because it gives the green light to the mobilization of the steel companies duferco belgium sa and nlmk la louvière sa (belgium). in this case, the egf funding amounts to eur 981 956 and the package includes measures such as individual jobsearch assistance, general information services, training and the promotion of entrepreneurship.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is about changing the regulations to limit pollution caused by trucks. in particular, it is proposed to extend the maximum length authorised in council directive 96/53/ec. technological developments make it possible to add retractable or folding devices to trucks, thus achieving significant energy savings. the maximum authorised dimensions and weights for these trucks operating within the eu have therefore been extended.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement which we have been negotiating for so long and i would like to thank the rapporteur for his impetus. the approval will allow manufacturers to use new technologies to improve the design of trucks, in particular from an environmental point of view. trucks will be safer, cleaner and more efficient.
in writing. ‒ this amendment to the directive setting maximum authorised weights and measures for the international carriage of certain goods and passenger vehicles closes the door to international travel by vehicles over 40 tonnes, in a decision that has benefits for both safety and environmental protection. the cabs of buses and lorries will also be made less aggressively designed to help avoid overtaking while improving driver visibility by improving the size and placement of the front and side windows. measures are also introduced to improve aerodynamics and thus reduce consumption and therefore co2 emissions. for the same purpose, weight exemptions will be allowed for buses with alternative propulsion systems to traditional combustion engines and which will help to reduce co2 emissions. and to encourage combined transport, excess weights will be allowed for the transport of sea containers when combined with sea or rail travel. i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. we voted in favour of this recommendation because it is an initiative to improve energy efficiency and reduce greenhouse gas (co2) emissions, to adapt transport legislation to technological advances and changing market needs and to facilitate intermodal transport operations, while ensuring undistorted competition and the protection of road infrastructure.
in writing. ‒ the maximum authorised dimensions and weights for certain vehicles on eu roads are a matter of great concern because of the need to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and the changing needs of the market, which require us to adapt in order not to lose competitiveness on the international market. this is a measure which is not against anyone, as it simply aims to increase the competitiveness and efficiency of european industry while taking into account the environmental aspect and the objectives of reducing greenhouse gases.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is about changing the regulations to limit pollution caused by trucks. in particular, it is proposed to extend the maximum length authorised in council directive 96/53/ec. technological developments make it possible to add retractable or folding devices to trucks, thus achieving significant energy savings. the maximum authorised dimensions and weights for these trucks operating within the eu territory have therefore been extended.
in writing. ‒ my support for the proposal put forward in the european parliament on the maximum dimensions and weights allowed in international traffic, which will allow truck manufacturers to build vehicles with greater weight and length than the current ones, but provided that they improve their environmental performance and safety measures. the commission is proposing to introduce measures to ensure that goods are transported more efficiently in the eu and that there is more scope for action against carriers who do not comply with the weight or safety limits.

in writing. ‒ heavy goods vehicles transporting goods in europe are needed and are fundamental for the european economy. the logistics sector is crucial and should be supported in an intelligent way. we do not need over-regulation but better regulation. we should push all actors to move as much as possible to greener ways of transport such as rail freight. however often the rail solution is not possible or is not a reliable option for the logistic sector for example because there is no guarantee when the trains will actually arrive. the 2011 white paper on transport provides that 30% of road freight carried over distances of more than 300 km should shift to other modes, such as rail or waterborne transport by 2030 and more than 50% by 2050, facilitated by efficient and green freight corridors. in order to meet this goal, appropriate infrastructure will need to be developed. before such an optimum goal can be achieve, we must be pragmatic and adopt realistic solutions.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it develops a type of financial product designed to enable large international capital to finance the construction of large infrastructures. this report is intended to give a boost to the real economy and employment when, in reality, it will only allow an increase in income for the large construction consortia which have proved unable to sustain a boost in job creation. this type of fund, in the context of the efsi negotiation, is another way of rewarding international speculative capital with legal guarantees to be able to invest in the infrastructure sector. private capital has proved to be the cause of the present crisis and therefore cannot be part of the solution; our bet to boost the real economy is public investment and that is why we have voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of a new regulation on european long-term investment funds. long-term financing is an essential instrument to put the european economy on a path of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, in line with the europe 2020 strategy. european long-term investment funds provide financing for different infrastructure projects, unlisted companies or listed smes of a lasting nature that issue equity or debt instruments for which there is no easily identifiable buyer. by financing such projects, the european long-term investment funds contribute to the financing of the union's real economy and the implementation of its policies.
in writing. we voted against this directive, the final result of the trilogue negotiations between the commission, parliament and the council. the idea of channelling scattered funds into investments of a lasting nature and of general interest is not in itself harmful, on the contrary. but this channelling should be carried out according to alternative criteria: through independent professional management, under public tender and management, with criteria which are compatible with the saving purpose and the activity in which it is invested, with a public regulation which guarantees and, of course, is open to improving these regulations and guarantees, and not putting any restrictions on the possibility for the member states to deepen and advance this regulation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this regulation because its purpose is to boost long-term european investment in the real economy by mobilising and channelling private savings, in line with the union's objective of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. this eltif regulation can be an important complement to the european fund for strategic investments (efsi), which should be conceived as a permanent countercyclical instrument of the european union, and therefore should have legal personality and indefinite duration, so that it can issue debt securities and reinvest its profits. the efsi should therefore be a lever to direct investments where they are needed most, and this task will remain relevant when the financial and economic crisis is over. the efsi should concentrate investment in those areas where there is a sudden drop in economic growth and employment rates. the so-called investment plan for europe must therefore be structural rather than cyclical. i also think it is important that the efsi should be able to issue government bonds with the inclusion of a retail tranche for purchase by citizens.
in writing. ‒ long-term financing is undoubtedly an essential instrument to be able to channel the european economy onto a path of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, in line with the horizon 2020 strategy, to ensure a high level of employment and to maintain and improve our competitiveness at international level. europe, especially some countries in the south of the continent, is facing the problem of lack of financing, an aspect in which european long-term investment funds can play a very important role in providing financing for infrastructure projects by unlisted companies or smes. we must not forget that by financing the projects of these companies we are helping to finance the real economy of the eu and thus helping to create jobs.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it represents a series of positive steps for card users in the european union. different types of card are one of the main means of payment in the different eu member states; however, the lack of uniform legislation has allowed numerous abuses by many financial companies to the detriment of their customers. the report aims to harmonise payment systems to prevent such abuse and to provide a stronger legal framework for payment transactions, whether national or international. as this is a proposal for a regulation which can considerably improve the protection of users of this type of payment instrument, i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it represents a considerable improvement in the rights of credit card users. in particular, it makes progress in removing obstacles to the efficient functioning of the card market, including in the area of card-based payments and card-based mobile and internet payments, determines that all debit and credit card-based payment transactions should be subject to a maximum exchange rate and clarifies the costs of transactions carried out with so-called 'universal cards', among others.
in writing. we voted in favour of this directive, which for the first time establishes a european regulation on the fees consumers pay for credit card transactions. in a context where payment systems are increasingly centralised under the control of an oligopoly of a few private companies, it was urgent to establish international regulation to put a stop to them. the directive sets a maximum ceiling for fees for credit card payments, with the possibility for member states to set lower ceilings, the lower of which must always be respected in the case of international transactions. while our position would have been to abolish these charges altogether, we still consider that this regulation is a positive step towards ending certain abusive practices and protecting small businesses and consumers.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this regulation because it seeks to fill an important gap that called into question both the unity of the internal market and the rights of consumers, by imposing different fees depending on whether the payment card transaction is carried out within the member state where it was contracted or in another member state. this is yet another example of the financial fragmentation which exists in our union and which must be thoroughly corrected by the so-called 'capital markets union' announced by the commission, and whose green paper we have just seen. this regulation introduces a cap on so-called 'interchange fees' of 0.2% per transaction for debit cards and 0.3% for credit cards, irrespective of whether these payment transactions are national or cross-border, which is certainly a major step forward. this regulation is also an important complement to directive 2014/92/eu of the european parliament and of the council of 23 july 2014 on the comparability of fees relating to payment accounts, the switching of payment accounts and access to payment accounts in basic form.
in writing. ‒ the establishment of maximum limits on interchange fees applied to card payment transactions is a positive step towards greater protection of the european consumer. as consumers are often unaware of the existence of these exchange rates, their amount costs retailers and ultimately consumers tens of billions of euros each year. although payment cards are the most commonly used electronic payment instrument for retail purchases in the eu, the internal market is still far from being integrated and the adopted measure represents a step forward in this respect.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because limiting the fees charged by banks for the use of credit and debit cards will help to increase consumption and will help smes in particular. there will be a cap on bank charges on these transactions of 0.2% for debit cards and 0.3% for credit cards. this limit will apply in all 28 member states and will affect all card payments, both cross-border and domestic. for too long, we have been subject to vague and unpredictable bank rates. that is why i support this legislation, which is fair and logical. in the current economic situation, we must promote consumption and reduce unnecessary barriers.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it allows the mobilisation of resources following the 257 redundancies linked to the closure of a plant of the saint-gobain sekurit (sgs) group, located in auvelais, which produced safety glass for the automotive industry. these redundancies took place during the period considered from 31 august 2013 to 31 december 2013 and thereafter and are related to the decrease in production of safety glass for the automotive industry in the union. this mobilization of funds is due to the disastrous consequences of the internationalisation of the productive sectors in the eu. these funds are not able to solve the problems of these workers in the context of unemployment in belgium, but at least they give the possibility of alleviating a small part of the human drama. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to approve the mobilisation of eur 1 339 928 from the european globalisation adjustment fund for 257 workers who have lost their jobs as a result of the closure of a saint-gobain sekurit (sgs) plant in auvelais (belgium) manufacturing safety glass for the automotive industry, as a result of the structural changes in world trade due to globalisation and the impact of the economic and financial crisis. in this case, and despite the fact that the part of the intervention criteria concerning the minimum number of redundancies (500) during the reference period has not been met, a derogation from the general rule has been approved because of the significant effects of the redundancies. the personalised services to be financed by the egf comprise activities to assist individuals in their search for employment, general information services, vocational training and retraining and the promotion of entrepreneurship. although these aids alone are not able to alleviate the unemployment problem in the walloon region, they do constitute good assistance and training for the reintegration of the workers concerned.
in writing. ‒ the podemos delegation in the european parliament has voted in favour of the mobilisation of this fund, considering that there is an objective need and a legitimate expectation on the part of the workers made redundant to receive the associated aid package. however, we consider the globalisation adjustment fund to be insufficient in the current economic climate. the processes of industrial conversion and labour flexibility make it more difficult to absorb a growing mass of workers and devalue workers' social rights.
in writing. ‒ europe and the world are engaged in a profound process of globalisation which, while a source of trade and wealth creation, can also entail risks to which we must be very attentive. as a result of this process, there are sectors which are more exposed to international competition, and the eu must therefore respond to those citizens who lose their jobs as a result of globalisation. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) supports workers who lose their jobs as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns caused by globalisation (e.g. the closure of large companies or the relocation of production outside the eu) or by the global economic and financial crisis. i have therefore voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (application egf/2013/011 be/saint-gobain sekurit)
in writing. ‒ the podemos delegation in the european parliament has voted in favour of the mobilisation of this fund for the saint gobain company in belgium, considering that there is an objective need and a legitimate expectation on the part of the 257 workers made redundant to receive the associated aid package. however, we consider the globalisation adjustment fund to be insufficient in the current economic climate. the processes of industrial conversion and labour flexibility make it more difficult to absorb a growing mass of workers and devalue workers' social rights.
in writing. the podemos delegation in the european parliament voted in favour of the mobilisation of this fund for the saint gobain company in belgium, considering that there is an objective need and a legitimate expectation on the part of the 257 workers made redundant to receive the associated aid package. however, we consider the globalisation adjustment fund to be insufficient in the current economic climate. the processes of industrial conversion and labour flexibility make it more difficult to absorb a growing mass of workers and devalue workers' social rights.
in writing. ‒ this report gives the green light to the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) in belgium. the application concerns 257 redundancies at sgs benelux, a company active in the manufacture of safety glazing for the automotive industry, before and during the reference period from 31 august 2013 to 31 december 2013. in this case, and despite the fact that the part of the intervention criteria concerning the minimum number of redundancies (500) during the reference period has not been met, a derogation from the general rule has been approved because of the significant effects of the redundancies. the egf financing of eur 1 339 928 will be used to help cover the costs of measures to reintegrate workers made redundant: assistance in finding an individual, general information services, vocational training and retraining and promotion of entrepreneurship.
in writing. ‒ with regard to the financial contribution from belgium on budgetary matters and sound financial management of the egf, i consider it positive that, in order to obtain rapid assistance for workers, actions have been carried out by belgium in advance of the decision and even before the submission of the application. there have been many redundancies at sgs benelux due to the fall in demand for automotive safety glass in western europe. this demand for glass has shifted mainly to eastern europe, and has seen an overall increase in the rest of the world. the context in which this occurs is difficult, since these unemployed workers will have to compete with many other unemployed in charleroi and namur who have the same experience and training. the egf therefore provides training and retraining measures to remedy this situation at regional level. this action follows coordination with other organisations to implement these measures and, in addition, the principle of equality and non-discrimination continues to apply in the measures carried out by the fund. i therefore consider that this proposal should be adopted.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to approve the mobilisation of eur 1 339 928 from the european globalisation adjustment fund for 257 workers who have lost their jobs as a result of the closure of a saint-gobain sekurit (sgs) group plant in auvelais, belgium, which manufactures safety glass for the automotive industry, as a result of the structural changes in world trade due to globalisation and the impact of the economic and financial crisis. in this case, and despite the fact that the part of the intervention criteria concerning the minimum number of redundancies (500) during the reference period has not been met, a derogation from the general rule has been approved because of the significant effects of the redundancies. the personalised services to be financed by the egf comprise activities to assist individuals in their search for employment, general information services, vocational training and retraining and the promotion of entrepreneurship. although these aids alone are not able to alleviate the unemployment problem in the walloon region, they do constitute good assistance and training for the reintegration of the workers concerned.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, as i did for the other reports which have called for the mobilisation of a fund which is essential for mitigating the impact of globalisation on the functioning of local economies and the future of regions affected by deindustrialisation processes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it allows the mobilisation of resources following the 257 redundancies linked to the closure of a plant of the saint-gobain sekurit (sgs) group, located in auvelais, which produced safety glass for the automotive industry. these redundancies took place during the period considered from 31 august 2013 to 31 december 2013 and thereafter and are related to the decrease in production of safety glass for the automotive industry in the union. this mobilization of funds is due to the disastrous consequences of the internationalisation of the productive sectors in the eu. these funds are not able to solve the problems of these workers in the context of unemployment in belgium, but at least they give the possibility of alleviating a small part of the human drama. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i consider myself a strong advocate of women's rights. progress towards equality between women and men is slow and it is therefore important to focus on such important issues as the fight against gender-based violence, which is the most widespread human rights violation in the world and affects all strata of society; the integration of women into the labour market on an equal footing, without discrimination of any kind; the wage gap, which remains stable at 16.4% on average in the eu and has even increased in some countries such as spain; sexual and reproductive health rights, including the right to abortion in legal and safe health conditions; the difficult reconciliation of family and work life, which prevents many women from working full-time in vulnerable jobs and even forces them to leave the labour market; the situation of vulnerable groups of women, such as women with disabilities or women in rural areas; the poor or poor representation of women in political and economic decision-making. the tarabellla report covers all these issues.

in writing. ‒ competition policy is itself a tool for safeguarding european democracy, insofar as it prevents excessive concentration of economic and financial power in a few hands, which would risk the independence of european political power from the big industrial and banking groups; it is also a cornerstone of the european social market economy to ensure the proper functioning of a dynamic, efficient, sustainable and innovative internal market. this annual report on eu competition policy, which i voted for, sets out the main priorities of the socialist group, including ensuring fair competition and combating social dumping in the labour market, fighting fragmentation in the eu digital market, ensuring an open internet and enshrining net neutrality, and putting an end to tax evasion and illegal practices in some member states in the area of tax agreements with companies. in addition, it is important to carry out a thorough analysis of the tax provisions specific to each member state in order to be able to put forward tax harmonisation measures which are advantageous to smes and guarantee the competitiveness of the member states.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this regulation, even though i disagree with the inclusion of paragraph 85 insofar as it affirms the importance of competition policy to ensure the efficient allocation of resources and to promote economic growth. in particular, i am pleased by the inclusion of two amendments that i have tabled: one on the promotion of competition and the fight against monopolies and oligopolies as a factor of safeguarding the independence of european political power from the large economic and financial conglomerates; and another on the need to monitor the unity of financial markets as regards the loss of payment card service when the cardholder moves to another member state, which is also contrary to article 15 of directive 2014/92/eu of the european parliament and of the council of 23 july 2014 on the comparability of fees relating to payment accounts, payment account switching and access to basic payment accounts, still in transposition period, in addition to the relevant articles of the treaties, namely articles 63 and 169 tfeu, among others.

in writing. ‒ the treaties state that, in the economic dimension, the eu is 'an open market economy with free competition'; however, a stronger focus on fostering competition is needed to achieve ambitious goals for employment, growth, investment and the global competitiveness of the european economy, as sustainable and effective competition encourages investment and benefits end-users and fuels the economy. the commission should also be able to provide the necessary information to the member states and the commission in order to ensure that the competition rules are applied in a transparent and non-discriminatory manner. the creation of such powers also entails the fight against social dumping and the implementation of european social and environmental legislation. i voted in favour of asking the commission to apply the competition rules, in the field of state aid and merger control, in order to achieve a properly functioning internal market and to promote social progress.
in writing. ‒ the higher efficiency of the market economy lies in and is dependent on the level of competition that actually exists. if it declines, so does not only efficiency but also any hint of social justice. i therefore vote in favour of this report in order to ensure maximum european competition and to draw attention to the elements which have been threatening it lately, such as covert state aids, tax privileges or social dumping.

in writing. ‒ this report includes a crucial aspect in terms of economic model: the necessary overcoming of the centralistic models of single and indivisible management, which does not leave room for another possible organization of logistics and transport activity in one state. on the contrary, we must propose appropriate models, preferably public ones, which have the subsidiarity principle as an ally. we must also take into account the municipalities when managing infrastructures such as ports and airports.
in writing. ‒ the commission really has a chance to make a difference in the fight against oligopolistic practices. in the google antitrust case a lot of people forget that, among the dozens of complainants, there are several us companies. some of them, like yelp, have no problem going public; others do not want to attack google openly, because they fear retaliation measures, such as demotion or exclusion by google. we met several us companies who are victims of these practices, which explained how they simply disappear from a google search for several days, which has a huge economic impact on them. i want to stress once again that this is not a european versus american company war! i am not ideologically against google or any other us company. i am against monopolies. google has a 90% market share in some european countries and is the ‘de facto’ gatekeeper of the internet for european smes and consumers. the preferential treatment of google’s own services is not fair practice: google does not always have the best and the most pertinent choices for consumers. i am convinced that google will only move with the threat of a fine, or with the threat of an unbundling regulation.

madam president, i voted against the report by the european central bank because i do not believe that its actions deserve the defence and democratic legitimacy of this parliament. the european central bank's mission should be to support the member states in their task of reviving the economy by supporting public debt issuance and the stability of savers' deposits on the markets. instead, mr draghi is feeding new financial bubbles with one hand while with the other he is shutting down the credit to those states whose governments are fighting for the social rights of the working majority. the method is more discreet than mr trichet's letters, in which he called for cuts or harsh labour reforms, but no less determined or brutal. with their votes today, the majority parties have once again shown that they prefer financial proximity to solidarity with the european people.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because i do not share its positive view of the activities of the european central bank, whose monetary policy is deepening the economic crisis and the disparities between the eu member states. the ecb is pursuing a policy which takes into account only the interests of large financial corporations and speculative capital, in the face of the unquestionable need for a truly expansionary monetary policy to give a boost to the european economy. the ecb continues to pursue, in a totally discretionary manner, a policy which increases disparities in the eu, without democratic control of which we will not be able to get out of the crisis. this report follows the line of the majority groups in the european parliament which approve of the management of the bank and that is why i have decided to vote against it.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this resolution because the final report contains the amendments tabled by the spanish socialist delegation which note the serious economic situation in europe, particularly concerning unemployment, and the support given by the european central bank to the shift towards a more expansionary monetary policy, which has helped to build confidence in the euro area and the single currency. the economic situation remains worrying, due to the combination of flat growth and very low inflation, even with signs of deflation, hence the need to create conditions for a rebound in investment in the euro area, both public and private, in order to cope with the lacerating unemployment figures, especially youth unemployment. in this regard, the ecb is encouraged to take into account in its balance sheet expansion policy the purchase of bonds for the financing of eib projects, which underwrite some of the most productive investments in the euro area, in particular those projects which, after undergoing a cost-benefit analysis, have been selected by the commission for providing european added value and projects related to the digital single market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the ecb's performance because it recognises the danger of deflation and supports the policy of monetary stimulus. in this respect, although the decision is post-periodic, i welcome the ecb's announcement of an expanded asset purchase programme, including government debt, on 22 january 2015. however, monetary union is not sound in the long term unless it is accompanied by an economic, fiscal and budgetary union capable of offsetting the macroeconomic shocks that occur within it, which in turn requires a federal political union. as mr draghi explained, integration based on common institutions, such as the currency, is more effective than integration structured through rules, such as the stability and growth pact. concrete steps are therefore needed to create a fiscal capacity for the euro area, fuelled by taxes such as the international financial transaction tax, and capable of sustaining a treasury issuing euro-denominated public debt, which in turn would contribute to increasing the liquidity and financial stability of the monetary union.
in writing. ‒ 2014 saw a great deal of activity by the ecb, which helped to stabilise the european economy and averted further evils. the european union must continue to help, more rapidly, to lay the foundations for sustainable and inclusive economic growth that will enable us to get back on the path of growth and job creation. the ecb's initiation of monetary buying and selling (mbo) operations must in my view be seen as an element aimed at consolidating the economic recovery. however, the member states should not regard this instrument as a means of avoiding the necessary structural reforms. the eu needs a balance between austerity policies and measures to boost economic activity and employment, and the ecb can play a key role in this.
in writing. ‒ in favour of the proposed stimulus measures because of their importance at european level.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the ecb's performance because it recognises the danger of deflation and supports the policy of monetary stimulus. although the decision is post-periodic, i welcome the ecb's announced on 22 january 2015 extended asset purchase programme of approximately eur 1.2 trillion, including government debt, which is already having positive effects by lowering the interest rates on sovereign debt securities of euro area member states. i am less enthusiastic about the fact that most of these assets will be acquired by the eurosystem and not by the ecb, i.e. by the national central banks themselves, which puts the credibility and solidarity of monetary union at risk. in any event, the ecb should estimate the benefit to the ecb and the eurosystem of this operation. the ecb should also explain the continued maintenance of the official interest rate at 0.05% given that there is scope for further reductions, which could provide an additional stimulus to economic growth and the fight against deflation.
in writing. ‒ as a full member of the committee on employment, i was an alternative rapporteur for the committee's opinion on the european central bank's annual report 2013. although not all our demands have been taken into account, the joint work with the committee on economic and monetary affairs has made it possible to put the difficult economic situation into figures and to soften the enthusiasm for so-called structural reforms as a factor of growth, which has been reflected in the final commitments of the resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because of its positive view of the activities of the european central bank, whose monetary policy is deepening the economic crisis and the disparities between the eu member states. the ecb is pursuing a policy which takes into account only the interests of large financial corporations and speculative capital, as opposed to the unquestionable need to support the financing of the states in order to give a boost to the european economy. the ecb continues to pursue, in a wholly discretionary manner and outside democratic control, a policy favouring financial bubbles while pushing for neoliberal reforms with the threat of closing the liquidity of the financial system and the public debt markets of those states which are reluctant to do so. this report follows the line of the majority groups in the european parliament which approve of the management of the bank and that is why i have decided to vote against it.
in writing. ‒ the 2013 annual report on the european central bank highlights the progress made towards improving stability in the euro area thanks to the ecb's swift reaction, but also points out some threats that still persist and that we in the european parliament consider necessary to tackle, such as the fact that economic activity is still too weak or the fall in the inflation rate, in addition to the high unemployment rate. i therefore support the report by mr pablo zalba, who also points out that monetary policy alone cannot stimulate aggregate demand unless it is complemented by appropriate fiscal policies and national structural reforms, which we must all work on.
in writing. ‒ the european central bank's annual report for 2013 recognises the ecb's work to achieve stability within the euro area and its response to the crisis. however, the report also highlights the lack of credit transfer to smes. the banks have seen a fall in lending of around 35% between 2008 and 2013, and are called upon to better align their policies with the real economy. the proposal, although it could be improved, seemed to me worthy of approval.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this resolution because the final report contains the amendments tabled by the spanish socialist delegation which note the serious economic situation in europe, particularly concerning unemployment, and the support given by the european central bank to the shift towards a more expansionary monetary policy, which has helped to build confidence in the euro area and the single currency. the economic situation remains worrying, due to the combination of flat growth and very low inflation, even with signs of deflation, hence the need to create conditions for a rebound in investment in the euro area, both public and private, in order to cope with the lacerating unemployment figures, especially youth unemployment. in this regard, the ecb is encouraged to take into account in its balance sheet expansion policy the purchase of bonds for the financing of eib projects, which underwrite some of the most productive investments in the euro area, in particular those projects which, after undergoing a cost-benefit analysis, have been selected by the commission for providing european added value and projects related to the digital single market.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because i do not share its positive view of the activities of the european central bank, whose monetary policy is deepening the economic crisis and the disparities between the eu member states. the ecb is pursuing a policy which takes into account only the interests of large financial corporations and speculative capital, in the face of the unquestionable need for a truly expansionary monetary policy to give a boost to the european economy. the ecb continues to pursue, in a totally discretionary manner, a policy which increases disparities in the eu, without democratic control of which we will not be able to get out of the crisis. this report follows the line of the majority groups in the european parliament which approve of the management of the bank and that is why i have decided to vote against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as i think it sets up a good analysis and guidelines for the action of the ecb. particularly, and taking into account that the ecb has started a program of quantitative easing, i hope that this institution will give more weight to buying bonds from the eib that have a direct relation with the real economy.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it seeks to enshrine the austerity + structural reforms cocktail as the only economic recipe for europe, despite the evidence that it is a failed model with serious social, environmental and economic consequences.

reinforcement of growth at home, we continue to be concerned about developments in our neighbourhoods, and therefore funding for actions we take on the external side must remain sound for countries facing humanitarian and civilian crises. we welcome very much the focus that the rapporteur has put on eu added valued and how our budget turns into an engine for growth and convergence. we are keen to reinforce – already in the 2016 draft budget – an approach that provides for measurable elements of results achieved, in other words, a strong focus on a budget oriented towards performance and results. in terms of payment appropriations, we all remember the negotiations on the 2015 budget that ensured that, at the end of last year, the level of payments remained at eur 24.7 billion of unpaid bills. i want to thank you for the efforts we have made together to prevent this level from going up even further and i can assure you that in the proposal for 2016 we will have a draft budget which allows us both to reduce the backlog and correct the pace of implementation for the new 2014—2020 programmes. we are fully committed to the interinstitutional dialogue on the payment plan. as we promised, it will be made available by the end of march. on 30 march we will have our first trilogue, and that should also provide analytical documents that explain the payments situation today, how we expect it to evolve over time and what measures we are taking, so we can have a rhythm of absorption of the backlogs that by the end of 2016 brings us to a sound position. we are committed to controlling administrative expenditure and staffing. our 5 % staff cut is on track and we really hope all institutions will stick to the same administrative restraints so that we can demonstrate to our taxpayers that our focus is on what we do for them. on timing, we intend to present the draft in late may so as to take into account the decision regarding reprogramming under shared management, the revisions of the mff (dab 2) and progress made on the european fund for strategic investment (dab 1), as well as actual implementation in 2015. i very much look forward to our strong collaboration in this process on the budget for 2016.

president-in-office of the council.– mr president, honourable members, the presidency would like to thank you for your continuing involvement and support in the response to the ebola virus disease crisis. following our debate, i would like to underline three aspects. firstly, clearly there is no room for complacency. we need to continue our efforts in the immediate response. getting down to, and staying at, zero is our objective. the question is how to prevent a similar crisis in the future. i believe that during last week’s conference it was stated by all participants that the world after ebola cannot remain the same if we do not want to be confronted with another epidemic of an even larger scale. first and foremost, advances realised in developing vaccines and effective treatment against ebola and other neglected diseases. the participants welcomed the encouraging results of treating ebola patients with favipiravir that is undergoing the final stage of testing. secondly, it is clear for us that, together with affected countries, we need to build resilience for the region. we need a comprehensive cross—border strategy encompassing health, education, public services and economic development. the council therefore welcomes the mano river union summit held in the capital of the ivory coast, abidjan, on 15 february, and the commitments made by the countries of the region: a reduction of ebola in 60 days, close cooperation, establishment of a regional centre for infections, preventions and control and the fostering of the economic recovery of affected countries. at the same time, the idea of creating a marshall plan for the affected countries or restructuring their foreign debt should be dealt with in appropriate fora, in the margins of the imf, world bank and other international financial institutions. the eu can use instruments that are at its disposal to strengthen the resilience and capacity of the affected countries while preparing for the world bank meeting in april and the un ebola donors’ conference in may 2015. thirdly, improved governance, accountability and transparency of national, regional and local systems will allow us to provide a more inclusive and effective result for citizens. lessons learned from this crisis should be incorporated in the recovery and development plans. the council will continue monitoring the situation. together with the european commission, we will continue to work with the countries of the region and international organisations in devising the most appropriate recovery and development strategies. in order to reinforce the eu and global preparedness and response to health threats in the light of the experience to fight the ebola epidemic, it is important that the commission and the eu member states take stock of lessons learned over the last month. there is a lot to do and we need to come to a zero—case situation.
in writing. four conclusions should be drawn from this international conference. firstly, that this parliament will continue to work to ensure a thorough monitoring of the situation until the virus is eradicated and we reach patient zero. secondly, that aid is still more than necessary as the countries concerned are faced with limited basic services, a devastated economy and almost non-existent health systems. yes, medical personnel are still needed, mobile hospitals, but above all, they need to be provided with the hope of seeing their children return to school or simply have access to clean water. the socialists therefore support the cancellation of the debts owed to the countries concerned. thirdly, we must help them in their regional drive to improve their prevention and response capacities to epidemics such as ebola and others that continue to cause thousands of deaths on the african continent (aids, tuberculosis, malaria, etc.) and to strengthen their health systems. finally, we ask that the decline in the number of cases does not mean a reduction in efforts to find a treatment and a vaccine against ebola. these will be the main lines of socialist policy in the report which this parliament will be issuing in the coming months.

in writing. the european parliament must strengthen the european commission's proposal on the european fund for strategic investments (efsi). the esi funds are an idea with great potential. there is general agreement that this instrument is essential to complement the eib's traditional activity, constrained by the need to maintain the highest credit rating. so why accept an ambiguous scheme, with no legal personality, no clarity on its duration beyond the planned investments until 2018, and no mandatory national contributions? is there not a need for a permanent, flexible, countercyclical instrument to concentrate investment in those states, regions or municipalities whose employment rate is deteriorating? we have a golden opportunity to draw up a good regulation from the outset, which is not at odds with a rapid adoption of it, provided that the council shows a degree of ambition comparable to that of parliament and the commission and closes forever these years of european myopia. this requires the efsi to be granted legal personality, to be explicitly stated as having an indefinite duration, to allow the issuance of debt securities, and to set out in the regulation mandatory national contributions and other stable sources of funding, as well as the reinvestment of profits.
