million european citizens who are asking us not to be complacent, to do everything we can to attract investment, to strengthen our industry and to change our production models, in order to guarantee their right to access decent work in the european union. and to that end, commissioners, we propose a number of things. first, his investments. we support their investment plan, but we remind them that it is a complement. a necessary addition, which, moreover, must be implemented quickly. they cannot replace investments already planned in advance. the commission has already taken a number of measures to improve the quality of the information provided by the member states. and develop into projects that provide value, an added value. we are asking for fiscal responsibility, mr rosati, which is compatible with economic growth and employment, which is compatible with the greater flexibility provided for in the stability and growth pact, because the fiscal multiplier effects in the european union are still too high to be compatible with job creation. but above all, we also ask them to incorporate fiscal and social responsibility into their community language. that we cannot make structural reforms a mantra that fits everything. that we need to do more. that the structural reforms we are promoting in the european union must first of all be compatible with economic growth and job creation, because some have had the same procyclical effects as excessive fiscal consolidation. but they must be compatible with a social model, which is the distinguishing feature of the european union. because some of the structural reforms that have been promoted so far, in the words of the commission itself, have, for example, excluded very many citizens from basic public services, for example, in the exercise of their right to universal health care or to quality education. and, above all, broad spectrum. the competitiveness of the european union is not dependent solely on labour reforms. that in addition to labour reforms which are compatible with the non-fragmentation of labour markets and the non-devaluation of wages, there are also other very necessary reforms which we are looking forward to you promoting within the european semester: energy reforms, internal market reforms, administrative reforms, tax reforms which can make - as i say - a smaller workload in the european union. and a report which is also constructive, commissioners, in order to put an end to inequality. i use their own data. the 50% of jobs created in the european union today are not enough to lift workers out of working poverty. we therefore ask that the commission, within its powers, should promote within the european union - as it has done in the past, by means of wage devaluation - the creation of a framework of sufficient, decent wages, which will allow something as basic as people to live with dignity in their work. you also say that you are concerned about the alarming reduction in the gross disposable income of families, and i say that this is mainly because we have cut social spending in a very significant way. that we need strong social indicators to assess this impact, precisely to avoid the increase in inequality due to an excessive increase in the reduction of public spending, mainly on basic social rights. and finally, you're concerned about the income gap. between the top ten percent and the bottom ten percent in the european union, which in some countries has increased sevenfold in recent years. and for that, i say to you, we have to ensure that there are sufficient and dignified automatic stabilizers at national level, especially in pensions and unemployment benefits, and much fairer and more equitable labour tax regimes.
on behalf of the green group, mr president, i too would like to thank mr rosati for his efforts and cooperation. however, we do not share the substance of the report, among other things, because there is an uncritical endorsement of the cocktail of the trio 'structural reforms, fiscal consolidation and investment', which we believe has failed in recent years as a method of getting europe out of the serious crisis in which it finds itself. in addition, some of the better data we have right now in some member states in relation to gdp and avoiding a third recession is simply due to the action of the european central bank and also to the fall in the price of oil; in any case, not to the cocktail that is presented to us in the annual growth survey as the only way out. i have to say that structural reforms in most member states have been socially very damaging and have been a key factor in the devaluation problem. the gains in competitiveness are being questioned very much; for example, in my country we are again running a trade deficit, so the strategy i had devised has not worked. on the other hand, fiscal consolidation has in some cases gone too fast and made things worse, and here, of course, we are going to have a lot of debate with the rapporteur, mrs berès, in the report on the evaluation of economic governance, about how this all fits together. because flexibility is always applied ex post when it is already unavoidable and it is not possible to do it ex ante to give member states room and margin to deal with a recession. and finally, the investment. the juncker plan is clearly not a serious plan to encourage investment. we have the european central bank doing quantitative expansion and a european investment bank that has to make an investment plan. and the two plans don't talk to each other. so we think that's bad news. i think there must be a change in economic policy and that is not the solution.
mr president, despite the work that i acknowledge has been done by the rapporteur and many others, unfortunately we are faced with a very lax, far-fetched, all-encompassing, unfocused text which leads to confusion rather than to strong recommendations. it certainly contains some excellent ideas, such as paragraph 8, which calls for the european fund not to be a substitute for investments already made but to go further; it is followed by paragraph 9, which has nothing to do with the european semester. i would also like to welcome paragraph 15, which says, in an economic context and in the short term - which is what we are talking about in a european semester - that in order to break imbalances, in a single monetary area and in a single market, it is also important that areas or countries with a surplus draw on the economy. and that's great advice. but, alongside this, we find a whole series of other concepts, a whole immense series of other debatable ideas, much more adapted to social policy. i am talking, for example, about the very respectable minimum income, which, of course, i will support in due course. i am talking, for example, about the ways in which deficits are calculated. this creates confusion which impoverishes our authority in the field of employment and impoverishes those important terms which will have to be dealt with in other legislative texts in due course. we also find here a red line which the alde group will not cross, namely when we turn this paper into an ideological debate on economic models or structural practices. on that, if that structural line is not passed, we will vote, although it is not the best text to present to our electors.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, let me begin by paying tribute today, on the european day of the victims of terrorism, to all the victims in europe, in spain and especially in my region, navarre. let the victims of terrorism know that they will always be in my memory. back to the semester. i would like to begin by thanking all the rapporteurs and the alternate rapporteurs for their work. in my opinion, they've done a more than reasonable job. the recent events in greece, with the arrival of the new government and the absence of any risk of economic contagion, show that we now have instruments that we did not have just a few months ago. so we have to be reasonably satisfied. because one of those instruments is the european semester. but that is not enough, ladies and gentlemen: we must continue to have instruments which enable or encourage governments to make further progress in the process of fiscal consolidation, but above all we must give governments incentives to make reforms. because reform, your honour, means growth. my country, spain, is an example. having been one of the most ambitious countries in terms of reforms, it is now the country that leads the euro area in growth. so, we know the recipe, we have to implement it. but that is not all, ladies and gentlemen, we must continue to give greater democratic legitimacy to the whole process of economic and, ultimately, political integration in which we are engaged, because without legitimacy we will not have the support of the citizens.
i am glad to see that employment continues to be the focal point of the commission's programme. i strongly support the three pillars on which the guidelines for this year focus, as they support each other. for growth, and above all job creation, to be the end result, the investment boost needs to be accompanied by the necessary structural reforms and long-term budgetary responsibility. it is essential today that parliament should speak out clearly and forcefully so that our citizens know that, despite the great difficulties they have faced in recent years, they are our main objective, because it is time to give priority to the social spheres. the data and forecasts that are coming to light in the last few months are clear. the recovery is beginning to take hold and not only is the union as a whole expected to grow and create jobs in the coming years, but the countries with the greatest problems, such as mine unfortunately, are expected to do so at an even higher rate, as the winter forecasts show. in fact, at the moment, one in two europeans in the euro area who leaves unemployment is in spain. however, it is not enough. we cannot be satisfied until unemployment is clearly reduced, citizens see the recovery, credit is facilitated for smes and labour mobility is improved.
the rapporteur. mr president, thank you all for participating in this debate. i will remind you of some data from the european commission itself: the annual growth rate in the european union as a whole last year was slightly above 0%, in 2014 long-term unemployment rose in the european union by 4 points. 75% of youth unemployment is now longterm unemployment. one in four households in europe is at risk of social exclusion. the question is whether we can be compliant with this data. if there is anyone who thinks that with this data we do not have to do more and faster to precisely reverse a social reality that is becoming unbearable for many european citizens. i agree with the change in the line of economic and social policy being pursued by the european commission, but we need it to be more ambitious and more fair. we say yes, we are in favour of investment, but that it should go to the regions, to the places where there are the greatest macroeconomic imbalances and where the highest unemployment rates occur. there must be fiscal responsibility, but, mr rosati, fiscal responsibility - we have been told this by the international monetary fund and the oecd - cannot be excessive austerity. it must be compatible with economic growth and job creation. that fiscal responsibility must be applied using the greater flexibility provided for in the stability and growth pact, so that we do not drown in recession. we need fiscal responsibility but above all, i remember, social responsibility. social responsibility because structural reforms cannot become a mantra in which everything is included. social responsibility to end the wage devaluation that has pushed millions of workers today to live below the poverty line because their wages do not allow them to live with dignity. the 50% of jobs created today, according to the european commission, are not jobs that can lift these workers out of active poverty or working poverty. so we have to change. change to make a more just society. we must change to make economic growth compatible with the european social model that we so much advocate.

in writing. ‒ with the entry into force of the lisbon treaty, an alignment exercise was carried out with omnibus i and ii to ensure that all previous comitology and ad hoc decision-making procedures relating to trade policy are in line with the new system of delegated and implementing acts. the commission's proposal is a continuation of this work, with the recasting of regulation (ec) no 625/2009 on common rules for imports from certain third countries. in this case, the main change is to remove from the annex countries which are already wto members such as armenia, russia, tajikistan and vietnam. since it is a technical report, i have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ in the interests of simplification and clarity of union law, so that it is more accessible and understandable to the citizen, i voted in favour of the codification and recasting of regulation (ec) no 625/2009 on the common rules for imports from certain third countries. that regulation, which currently applies only to a limited number of countries: azerbaijan, belarus, kazakhstan, north korea, turkmenistan and uzbekistan, has been substantially amended by various legislative acts in recent years and, in order to improve the clarity and easy comprehensibility of the legislative text, it is appropriate to recast all those provisions in a new regulation, respecting the content of the codified texts and making only the relevant formal amendments. as regards substance, the annex to the regulation is only updated to remove the reference to a number of third countries that have acceded to the world trade organisation, namely armenia, russia, tajikistan and vietnam.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the amended agreement establishing the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean, despite not being in favour of the provisions applicable to fisheries in the gfcm, as the agreement revises the structure and content of the current one by introducing a clearer explanation of the purpose of the gfcm agreement (defining a clear overall objective of ecological, social, economic and environmental sustainability of marine resources), better defines the functions of the gfcm and creates a well-defined dispute settlement mechanism.
in writing. ‒ the gfcm is one of the so-called regional fisheries management organisations (rfmos) whose purpose is to promote the development, conservation, rational management and better exploitation of living marine resources, as well as the sustainable development of aquaculture, in the mediterranean and the black sea. following a performance review completed in 2011, an amendment to the gfcm convention was submitted in 2013 to clarify its objectives and functions and to enhance its efficiency. the contracting parties adopted the amended version of the constitutive convention at its 38th annual session (19-24 may 2014), where it is aligned with the most up-to-date instruments of the rocs. the main changes include a clearer explanation of the purpose and underlying principles of the convention (biological, social, economic and environmental sustainability of living marine resources) and the definition of the gfcm's functions (promotion of common fisheries management through multiannual management plans, establishment of restricted fishing areas and collection and dissemination of data), as well as sanctioning measures and dispute resolution. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. we voted in favour of this recommendation because, although the proposed amendments do not ensure the best protection of the marine environment and its resources, they are the result of negotiations between the contracting parties following the recommendations of an evaluation completed in 2011, and it is preferable that the competences of the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean be clearly defined for the effective fulfilment of its objectives, which are: to promote the development, conservation, rational management and better use of living marine resources, as well as the sustainable development of aquaculture in the mediterranean and the black sea.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of clarifying the objectives and functions of the cgpm and strengthening its efficiency. the amendment to the convention will provide a clearer explanation of the purpose of the gfcm convention, namely the biological, social, economic and environmental sustainability of living marine resources, and will improve the definition of the functions of the gfcm, including the promotion of common fisheries management through multiannual management plans, the establishment of fishing restricted areas and the collection and dissemination of data, the imposition of sanctions to address cases of non-compliance by members/non-members and the resolution of disputes.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report of the committee on fisheries on the amendment of the convention establishing the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) following the decision adopted by that regional body at its last annual session in may 2013. the new version revises the structure and content of the current convention in order to bring it into line with the modern instruments of regional bodies. the main changes introduced, which i fully support, include a clearer explanation of the purpose and underlying principles of the gfcm convention. the new convention sets a clear global objective for the biological, social, economic and environmental sustainability of living marine resources. it also integrates new elements of the common fisheries policy, such as maximum sustainable yield, the application of the precautionary principle and the ecosystem-based approach, the reduction of discards and the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing. finally, it introduces provisions for the establishment of measures/sanctions to address cases of non-compliance by members/non-members.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the general guidelines for the preparation of the 2016 budget, section iii. this resolution sets out the main political priorities for the 2016 budget: job creation, business development and entrepreneurship for sustainable growth in the eu, the implementation of the investment plan and the fight against the payments crisis. the resolution stresses the importance of the union budget as a tool for creating smart jobs, ensuring inclusive and sustainable growth across the eu, economic, social and territorial cohesion, support for r & d, energy transition and interconnections, migration and asylum policy, external aid, as well as that of eu programmes such as horizon 2020, cosme or erasmus+. it also stresses the vital importance of continuing the fight against youth unemployment and the need to ensure the funding of the youth employment initiative from 2016 onwards. the resolution also calls for the full implementation of the joint declaration on a payment plan to end the payment crisis and the problem of outstanding invoices which undermine the eu's credibility.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the 2013 annual report on the protection of the eu's financial interests fight against fraud because it contains important criticisms of the current european policy on combating fraud and includes new proposals that are interesting and could contribute to ending this scourge, such as the harmonisation and improvement of the mechanisms for monitoring and collecting data on fraud in the different states, the assumption of responsibility by the commission for the recovery of european funds used fraudulently, the harmonisation of the definitions of the different crimes and applicable penalties, or transparency measures aimed at knowing details of the entities and projects receiving european funds. although i reject the proposal to set up a european public prosecutor's office and am critical of the work done by eurojust, i believe that these proposals can be an impetus to really punish in a proportionate and homogeneous way the many cases of fraud, many of which have been carried out with the complicity of administrations, if not directly by them.
in writing. ‒ the report contains encouraging data, such as the reduction in the financial impact of irregularities detected, both non-fraudulent (38% less than in 2012) and fraudulent (21% less), or that for the first time cohesion policy was not the area with the highest number of fraudulent irregularities, or that most of the irregularities detected were thanks to the control mechanisms provided for in eu law and not through criminal investigations. however, there has been no significant progress in the time taken to report cases of fraud. however, the implementation of the new legal and administrative measures to combat this scourge must be assessed. it is necessary to continue to fight against the misuse of public money and to continue to analyse and propose improvements in fraud detection, prevention and prosecution systems. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work is a very good one. i therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the fight against fraud, corruption, money laundering and other illegal activities affecting the financial interests of the union and its citizens must remain a priority for the eu and all member states. in view of the economic and fiscal situation in many eu countries, fraud is a scourge that shows the lack of solidarity and civility of the companies and citizens who defraud. we must therefore continue to fight with determination and constancy against illegal practices that harm the welfare of europe.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the report on the fight against fraud. we believe that it is very important to have strict control over the use of funds from the european union and that, as public money, it must be scrupulously controlled. we think it is a good report, which criticises the role of the member states and stresses that they should put in place more measures to detect fraud and toughen the penalties for fraudsters. among other things, it proposes to improve transparency both in the beneficiaries of the funds and in the use made of them. we attach great importance to the fight against fraud and transparency, especially when it comes to public money, and we therefore believe that this report sets a good path for further work.

i have supported this resolution on kosovo because the freely expressed will of the people, their possibilities for well-being and the integration of diversity as a basis for peace and stability are part of the union's founding values. the history of kosovo refutes the ideas of sovereignty, identity and fundamental rights that these old nation states have, which still do not understand that we need a true federal europe. a common space capable of jointly addressing global challenges. a space which must be based on the free adherence of all the identities that make it up, of all those that its citizens feel. a space in which the imposition of such sensitive issues as a national identity is the result of the blindness of those who continue to believe that their territorial integrity - another concept to be revised - is above the will of the people.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because it continues in line with parliament's positions on the candidate countries, in which a colonial relationship is reproduced between a rich and powerful centre and an impoverished and obedient periphery. in this case, a positive vote is equivalent to endorsing the policy of the atlantic alliance in the balkans, imposed through illegal wars in order to divide the peoples of the former yugoslavia and reposition the united states in europe. the motion for a resolution was an appeal to the authorities of the self-proclaimed republic of kosovo to consolidate the state attributes they have been acquiring in recent years, which is why i voted against it.
in writing. ‒ the text welcomes the end of the political impasse following the months of elections in kosovo, with the constitution of the assembly and the appointment of the new government, stressing the urgency of addressing the strengthening of the rule of law and the judicial system, the fight against corruption and organised crime, unemployment, as well as structural economic reforms and sustainable development. the socialist amendments, mostly included in the final text, concern the rule of law, the fight against terrorism and radicalisation; the lack of transparency in the media and the importance of media freedom and independence; the role of women in government and the fight against discrimination against lgbt people; the role of eulex and the need for a broad and in-depth analysis to assess the overall effectiveness of the mission; or, finally, the strengthening of relations with neighbours as an element of stabilisation in the region. we have abstained on what we consider to be an inappropriate call for the remaining member states, including spain, to recognise kosovo's independence.
in writing. ‒ on my own behalf and as the representative of the spanish delegation to the epp group in my capacity as secretary-general, we wish to state, in connection with the resolution on the process of european integration in kosovo, that the negative meaning of our vote is due to the fact that the resolution treats kosovo as if it were an ordinary independent state, recognised by the entire international community. this is not the case, to the extent that five member states of the european union, including spain, have not recognised it.
in writing. ‒ we must celebrate the progress made in kosovo, while being aware of the enormous challenges ahead. the consolidation of the rule of law in all its forms and dimensions must be one of the priorities of the government of kosovo. similarly, structural economic reforms and sustainable development should be promoted by creating a regulatory framework and incentives for economic development. the eu must support kosovo in fulfilling its obligations and overcoming its recent past, as well as in achieving results from the belgrade-pristina dialogue.
in writing. ‒ kosovo was militarily occupied by nato, under the pretext of a humanitarian alibi, in 1998. however, un security council resolution 1244 of 10 june 1999 states that kosovo is an autonomous province of serbia. in 2008, kosovo unilaterally declared its independence, thus violating international law. since then, there has been persecution and criminalization of serbs, the destruction of their historical monuments, major corruption scandals, and links to organ trafficking, drug trafficking and jihadism among senior leaders who were part of the kla (designated by international bodies as a terrorist organisation). the state can be said to be a kind of us-backed narco-state as there is a key military base for us interests in the region. the process of kosovo's integration into the eu would therefore amount to recognition of kosovo, which is contrary to international law, and would further undermine tensions in the region, making reconciliation and stability more difficult. that is why we voted against this resolution.

in writing. ‒ whereas 110 of the 193 member states of the united nations recognize kosovo’s independence, including 23 of the 28 member states of the eu and knowing that each candidate country will be judged on its own merits and that the speed and quality of the necessary reforms determines the timing of eu membership. i agree with this motion to encourage the new government to follow the european course and pursue firmly, even through a legal framework, a number of priority issues, including the consolidation and validation of the rule of law. i welcome the progress made on issues such as women’s rights and gender equality, the coalition against terrorism, the stabilisation and association agreement in july 2014, which provides for enhanced political dialogue, greater trade integration and new forms cooperation. finally, i think that the member states that still don not recognize kosovo, should act as soon as possible in order to establish diplomatic relations with this new european state.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it positively sanctions the neoliberal orientation of the economic governance framework. the annual prospective study is the european commission's economic study which sets the whole european semester process in motion. this study develops a very limited, monetarist analysis which takes no account of the social effects of austerity policies or the differences in the productive structures of the eu member states. on the basis of this limited analysis, austerity recommendations to member states will be justified, deepening the effects of the crisis. this report does not in any way condemn the way in which this study is being prepared and that is why i have decided to vote against it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the annual growth prospective study because it recognises that, alongside reforms to increase productivity and competitiveness, the pace of fiscal adjustment needs to be matched by the growth rate of the gross domestic product of the member states, and the investment plan for europe needs to be implemented. this is the first report by the european parliament on the so-called european semester for the coordination of economic policies which is being adopted after the election of the new commission, and it shows the change in european public policies which we socialists have been calling for for some time. however, i believe that the eu's economic policy should not rest solely on these three pillars (reforms, gradual fiscal consolidation and investment), but should be supplemented by the fiscal pillar (automatic exchange of information, harmonization of corporate tax) and the social pillar. in this sense, reforms cannot be synonymous with cuts to the welfare state, but must be conceived as instruments to improve workers' productivity, increase the accumulation of human capital, increase per capita income, and reduce social and territorial inequalities.
in writing. ‒ it is a fact that the eu's economic recovery is not consolidated and that in many member states the tax and labour market situation is very worrying. 2015 and 2016 may be the key years for europe's exit from the crisis, so we must continue to boost investment, accelerate structural reforms and pursue fiscal consolidation that fosters responsible growth. we must also continue to focus on the integration of the single market, on increasing the competitiveness of the european economy and on improving performance through innovation. smes must be a priority at both european and national level, as they are the backbone of the european economy and the source of employment for millions of citizens.
in writing. ‒ we voted against this report, which defends, with a heterodox monetary policy favourable to private finance, the return of financial bubbles, the socialisation of losses, a poorly conceived and meagre private investment policy, and the persistence of the austerity policy which will continue to curtail social rights and public services together with alleged structural reforms in labour markets (adaptation of the labour force to the market, flexibility of employment relations), while technological and energy innovation are left to the care of providence.

in writing. ‒ overall, the report has the following positive elements: (a) it recognises that the eu's economic problems are cyclical and structural; (b) it supports the commission's three-pillar strategy of increased investment, structural reforms and growth-friendly fiscal consolidation; (c) it supports the juncker plan; (d) it supports the commission's proposal on simplifying the european semester; (e) it supports increasing the degree of empowerment of states with regard to the country-specific recommendations and structural reforms; (f) it expresses concern about the eu's overall competitiveness; (h) it recognises the social and employment effects of structural reforms, which must be socially balanced and generate quality jobs; (i) it calls for the fight against tax fraud; (k) it recognises that it cannot be invested in research and education and which is growth-friendly; (d) it calls for the states to consider adjusting their tax burden and to protect consumers from tax competition; and (e) it calls for the states to consider investing in public services.

in writing. ‒ the european union must persevere in implementing a strategy to ensure growth and economic recovery in europe through investment, the implementation of structural reforms and also the consolidation of a growth-friendly fiscal model, as we have discussed and i fully share in this parliament. it is important, in order to advance all these objectives, that we achieve greater involvement of national parliaments in the debates on the european semester and greater national follow-up and autonomy in the country-specific recommendations. it is important, and we have discussed this here on numerous occasions, that member states follow the recommendations put forward by the commission, as only 9% were implemented in 2013. in addition, measures need to be put in place to move towards a more competitive and adaptable europe in the face of future crises, through working together towards the integration of capital markets, the fight against tax evasion and fraud, the creation of an internal eu energy market and the achievement of a more efficient labour market.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that the austerity policies implemented so far have prevented us from achieving the eu's growth, employment and social objectives. fiscal consolidation must be compatible with sustainable growth, decent employment and the maintenance of the welfare state, and i believe that we must make use of all possible flexibility. i also believe that a plan is needed for smes to facilitate their access to cheap credit, to the eu's innovation and research policies and to facilitate the restructuring of their debt to avoid their bankruptcy, as these are the backbone of job creation in the eu. the 50% of jobs created in europe today do not provide a decent life for families, so there is an unbearable bag of work poverty that must be reversed urgently, because decent wages are essential for social cohesion. finally, i voted in favour of this report because it calls on the european commission to take an initiative to promote and promote the minimum income in all the member states.

in writing. ‒ i believe that the new commission should make it clear from the beginning of its mandate that it has come to change the sign of the policies we have applied to date in the face of the crisis. the people are at the centre of political action. the objective of strategy 2020 and the means to grow in a smart, sustainable and cohesive way is people. that is why i support the call for a minimum income programme to be set up at european level. this is reflected in the juncker commission's programme. i have seen how it has served my country, the basque country, for 27 years to avoid exclusion. it is time to rescue people from poverty with more effort than is devoted to rescuing the financial system and certainly at a much lower cost. we need a commission with more resources and more power and capacity to lead productive investment and to mobilise private capital in favour of the real economy by penalizing speculation. that is what i call a social and federal europe. the europe of the people.

in writing. ‒ a report was presented based on 4 parts: 1) ambitious economic policies for growth, quality job creation and the fight against deflation; 2) labour market reforms to increase growth potential, human capital and productivity; 3) a decisive call for convergence and the social dimension of the eu; and 4) strengthening the democratic legitimacy of the european semester. the rapporteur from the spanish socialist delegation has managed to maintain most of his initial proposals, and group priorities such as: 1) that the austerity policy pursued so far by the eu has impeded the eu's growth, employment and social objectives; 2) that 50% of the jobs created today in europe do not serve to ensure a decent life for families; 3) that the juncker investment plan is not enough to stimulate growth; and 4) that decent and sufficient wages are essential for social cohesion.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the basis of the commitments made in the imco committee. these reflect the s&d group's priorities for the internal market pillar, highlighting the need to revitalise the european economy through a better and fairer functioning of the single market, capable of boosting sustainable growth and social cohesion, creating quality jobs and increasing competitiveness through investments in r&d, training and capacity building. it also recognises the need to target investments towards european reindustrialisation and strategic growth sectors such as the digital single market, emphasising the essential interconnection between high levels of network penetration and high levels of ict skills for citizens and businesses. the report includes a key point for the s&d group and calls for renewed efforts to combat tax fraud, evasion and avoidance, and to build good tax governance and improve tax coordination, in order to avoid unfair competition and market distortions and ensure equal opportunities in the single market.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it goes into more detail on the development of the single market through the economic governance framework. this report is aimed at integrating the implementation of the single market as a requirement within the objectives of the stability and growth pact. this is translated into direct attacks on the public sector, considering it a barrier to the single market, giving a political impetus to the implementation of the energy union and insisting on the elimination of public aid to avoid market distortions, etc. the report attempts to make the deficit targets of the economic governance framework conditional on the implementation of the internal market, which directly erodes the possibility of governing against neoliberal policies. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.

in writing. ‒ single market governance must be improved so that it is the engine of the eu, and not only so that it can promote and facilitate growth and jobs, but also so that it can serve as a benchmark for member states' commitment to the structural reforms that are needed. i voted in favour of this report which considers it necessary to re-establish political oversight at the highest level, avoiding artificial distinctions between what happens at eu level and what happens in the member states, while developing more efficient tools to ensure that citizens and businesses enjoy the benefits of the single market.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report on the basis of the commitments made in the imco committee. these reflect the s&d group's priorities for the internal market pillar, highlighting the need to revitalise the european economy through a better and fairer functioning of the single market, capable of boosting sustainable growth and social cohesion, creating quality jobs and increasing competitiveness through investments in r&d, training and capacity building. it also recognises the need to target investments towards european reindustrialisation and strategic growth sectors such as the digital single market, emphasising the essential interconnection between high levels of network penetration and high levels of ict skills for citizens and businesses. the report includes a key point for the s&d group and calls for renewed efforts to combat tax fraud, evasion and avoidance, and to build good tax governance and improve tax coordination, in order to avoid unfair competition and market distortions and ensure equal opportunities in the single market.
in writing. we have voted against this report. the report, among other things, reiterates support for ttip, the free trade agreement to which podemos is opposed. on the other hand, it makes no reference to the fight against unemployment and poverty, which are particularly serious problems in our country and require structural changes. as in ttip, it also calls for the removal of 'regulatory obstacles' (social, labour rights, etc.) to make certain services which are not yet 'well explored' competitive and profitable. it also mentions the need to further liberalise financial services and to remove any regulatory barriers that may cause harm. we therefore vote against this report, which seeks to introduce policies which are not in the interests of the people.

madam president, in recent years, while the european union has substantially improved its tools, its instruments in the field of foreign policy, our challenges and threats in the field of security have increased, they have come closer than ever, both in the eastern and southern neighbourhoods, and they have been aggravated by the emergence of new failed states around us. in the face of this reality, we must first improve our internal coordination, whether by the states, the intelligence services, the diplomatic services or the european external action service. and secondly, to strengthen cooperation with the outside world, gaining decisive influence. to do this, we need to develop a new, more practical and ambitious neighbourhood policy, but remembering that the european union has deliberately decided not to emphasise the use of force. we don't want to fight. we prefer to convince and cooperate. and that doesn't make us any weaker. it makes us stronger. so let us, with the help of parliament and federica mogherini, put our democratic legitimacy and our foreign policy instruments at the service of the conquest of reason.

member of the commission.– mr president, our debate this evening is very timely. we all know that discrimination is one of the scourges of our society. we are shocked when extreme violence hits our front pages and television screens. but we all know that the problem is far more widespread. ethnic and religious minorities, jews and muslims most obviously, are facing discrimination, harassment and violence and there are many reasons to believe this is getting worse. a 2013 study by the european union agency for fundamental rights showed that an overwhelming majority of jewish respondents felt that anti-semitism has increased over the past five years. countries like belgium, france and hungary were mentioned in particular. there is more than anecdotal evidence to suggest that european jews consider emigrating due to security concerns. this is wholly unacceptable. there is also growing evidence of discrimination and stigmatisation of muslims as well as an increase in the number of islamophobic incidents. in france a 53 % increase in individual attacks against muslims was registered in 2014 compared to 2012. since the paris attacks a further spike in incidents has been observed. violence seems more and more part of this extremism. in just a few years, we have seen fatal terrorist attacks in toulouse, brussels, paris and copenhagen. such trends are fundamentally contrary to the traditions and values which have made europe the society it is today. when negative stereotypes are fuelled in the media, in political rhetoric, in public rallies, those responsible are directly challenging the traditions of pluralism, inclusion and tolerance that lie at the heart of europe, and of the european project. the fundamental values of freedom, diversity and respect for the equal dignity of all individuals cannot be compromised. so how can the eu itself help? of course, our direct remit is limited, but we certainly need leadership and a clear message from its institutions. this parliament, the european council and the commission all gave a full and unconditional defence of our values in the wake of the paris attacks. but we must stay vigilant. we must show that we are for solidarity, to protect communities under pressure and to avoid stigmatisation. stepping up actions aimed at preventing and combating extreme forms of racism, prejudice and intolerance should be a priority. the eu has specific legislation on combating racism and xenophobia by means of criminal law. the commission acquired enforcement powers for this legislation in december last year. we have also adopted a directive to support the victims of crime, including all victims of hate crime, which will enter into effect as of november this year. the commission will prioritise the effective enforcement of both instruments. phenomena such as hate speech online will also be examined in this context. in order to prevent violence, extremism and radicalised behaviours we also need to strengthen measures promoting social inclusion and cohesion. a priority in this context is to fill existing gaps in eu law on protection from discrimination. in 2008, the commission proposed a directive on equal treatment, prohibiting discrimination outside the labour market, irrespective of disability, age, sexual orientation and religion or belief. it would extend this protection beyond employment, where eu legislation is already in force, to the areas of social protection, education and access to goods and services. this must now be taken forward into law. we must make the most of the programmes we have to help member states to address the root causes. for example, the europe for citizens programme brings together both the critical memory of the past and civic engagement firmly rooted in shared values as a defining feature of vibrant democracy in european union. particularly important is our work to address radicalisation. we need to better understand why some people are drawn down a path so much at odds not only with european values, but with the beliefs of their own communities. that takes time and effort, but there are grass-roots actions in schools, prisons and community centres across the european union, which are working to exactly this end. the commission offers support to such projects and helps others to learn from them. within the radicalisation awareness network local actors can exchange their experience and knowhow. over 1 000 practitioners have now been involved over the last three years, resulting in concrete recommendations and hands-on support. promoting better interfaith and intercultural understanding also plays a crucial role. in may and june this year the commission will organise high-level meetings with religious leaders and non-confessional organisations to discuss the issue of tolerance, respect and living together. finally, the commission decided to devote its first ever annual colloquium on fundamental rights, scheduled for this october, to fostering tolerance and respect, with a focus on preventing and combating anti-semitic and anti-muslim hatred. rising anti-semitism, islamophobia and extremism challenge the common values on which the european union is founded. we must stand up to safeguard these values. as policymakers, political leaders, community and religious leaders, as well as citizens, we must make sure that all our communities can feel at home together and share the hope of a future in europe, in order to give europe a future.

member of the commission.– mr president, the debate today on the challenges associated with land rights in tanzania is yet another testimony of the attention that parliament has devoted to this matter for years and for which i thank you. this complex topic rightfully deserves our attention as it touches on issues that the european union takes a keen interest in: human rights, rule of law and governance, and healthy and transparent business environment. the phenomenon termed ‘land grabbing’ has different manifestations. reports involving foreign investors or those threatening the livelihood of pastoralist communities have caused concerns. i refer to the most recent shocking case in loliondo, serengeti area, where park rangers and security forces burned the homes of masai villagers, which affected 3 000 people. this was the latest episode in a longstanding conflict where the government’s authority to manage land use collides with the exercise of the pastoralist communities acquired customary rights. the eu delegation and member statesʼ missions in tanzania have consulted with the representatives of the pastoralist communities and they await the outcome of the investigation launched by district authorities. land disputes are usually the result of complex and contrasting interests, weak legislation and administration, and poor dispute settlement mechanisms lead to conflicts that occasionally erupt with serious violations of human rights. tanzania has made commitments to improve land governance by signing up to the land transparency initiative launched by the g8 or by participating in the multilateral open government partnership. we support these efforts and advocate for efficient and corruption—free land administration and law enforcement. as we celebrated women’s day last sunday, let me conclude by mentioning a special form of land grabbing that is often overlooked. women in africa are often denied ownership of land and lose it if their husband dies. in tanzania, the eu supports a project promoting women’s ownership of land in densely populated areas. this contributes to a more equitable use of land and a more balanced growth, and ultimately to women’s empowerment.
in writing. we welcome the fact that the resolution calls for the rights of the indigenous people of tanzania and denounces cases of land grabbing. it also calls for coherence in development cooperation policies and for the responsibility and role of the eu and european companies in land grabbing actions. it also stresses the importance of transparency and accountability and emphasises the problem of food insecurity due to the increase in biofuels. however, we find the resolution somewhat vague in that it does not address fundamental points such as food sovereignty, the problem of corruption, the right to decide, the problem of privatisation of common goods such as water and other resources.

in writing. ‒ boris nemtsov, former deputy prime minister of the russian federation and former governor of nizhni novgorod, was one of the leaders of the liberal and democratic opposition in russia, and was killed near the kremlin two days before a demonstration planned for 1 march 2015 against the effects of the economic crisis and conflict in ukraine, which he was organizing. i strongly condemn the murder of boris nemtsov, as it is a very significant political crime and it is not surprising that he was shot dead near the kremlin, in an area with surveillance cameras and the presence of the police and security services. i take this opportunity to pay tribute to boris nemtsov as a leading opposition leader and a staunch fighter for a more democratic, prosperous and open russia. i also want to express my deepest condolences to his family and loved ones. i am voting in favour of this resolution in which the european parliament calls on the russian authorities, in the interests of democratic respect, to put an end to all forms of pressure, repression and intimidation, both political and judicial, against opposition leaders, representatives of civil society and the independent media.
in writing. ‒ i believe that it is necessary for this parliament to push for an independent international investigation to be carried out to clarify the murder of russian politician boris nemtsov. that is why i wholeheartedly support the resolution calling for this matter to be dealt with with with all the rigor, since we are facing the most important political murder in recent russian history. all europeans should be concerned about what is happening in russia, where there is increasing hate speech and fear, and there are situations like the murder of this russian opposition leader, who was gathering evidence of russian involvement in the war in eastern ukraine and who was killed just two days before the demonstration against that war he was going to lead. mr nemtsov, as this resolution points out, committed his life to a more prosperous and democratic russia and to a stronger friendly relationship between russia and its neighbours. i also deeply regret that some members of the european parliament and diplomats who wished to attend the funeral were refused entry to russia.
in writing. ‒ following the statements by the vice-president/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy on the assassination of russian opposition leader boris nemtsov and the situation of democracy in russia, the european parliament calls in a resolution for the circumstances of the death of opposition politician boris nemtsov to be clarified, for his brutal murder to be investigated and for the perpetrators to be brought to justice swiftly. the european institutions, the european parliament of course, and the european governments have condemned this crime and have insisted that a diligent investigation be carried out.
in writing. the text presented underlines the position of rejection of any kind of amnesty for the perpetrators of the downing of flight mh17. the minsk agreements provided that 'a pardon and amnesty will be granted, under a law prohibiting the prosecution and punishment of those who were connected with the events, in particular, in the donetsk and lugansk regions of ukraine'. this raised concern for the dutch government, as 196 dutch civilians were killed on a commercial flight over donetsk. however, the kiev government has already assured that no amnesty will be granted, so the amendment rains on the ground in that area. in any event, we believe that there is no direct link between the two cases and that the text should have been devoted to the murder of the opposition leader nemtsov in a monographic way, so we have voted against its adoption.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the text presented because, contrary to what it might seem, it does not represent a condemnation of the violation of human rights, but a further step in the strategy of certain actors of the european union, well coordinated with the americans, to isolate russia. the european parliament is not usually concerned about the harassment of political leaders. in reality, this is only a problem when such events take place in countries in which the eu has a special interest. in this particular case, the perpetrator of the crime is solved.

in writing. ‒ the annual report takes stock of the most important progress in the field of the cfsp and deals with human rights, non-proliferation of weapons and the spread of eu values. it also analyses geographical issues in the main areas of the cfsp: enlargement, transatlantic relations, relations with russia, the eu's neighbourhood, the middle east and asia. this report was agreed with broad agreement by the four political groups in parliament: epp, s&d, alde and greens. it takes a clear position on russia's actions in relation to ukraine, and in relation to the middle east it emphasises the two-state solution. it stresses the need to focus on the fight against isis and address the growing challenges stemming from the failure of the state in syria, iraq, libya and the sahel. the socialists and democrats have had a great deal of influence on the drafting of the report through the compromise amendments that have been agreed.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it insists on the militaristic drift of the european union, advocates closer cooperation between the eu and the atlantic alliance and supports the merger of internal and external security. the voting proposal lacked elements which i consider essential to support any initiative relating to the common security and defence policy, such as progress towards nuclear disarmament on a global scale, support for and strict application of international law in all eu military activities and the separation of civil and military actions.
in writing. ‒ the annual report takes stock of the most important progress in the field of the cfsp in the last year, in terms of its institutional structure and horizontal issues such as human rights, non-proliferation, the spread of eu values and its main geographical areas: enlargement, transatlantic relations, relations with russia, the eu's neighbourhood, the middle east and asia. the report, with broad agreement between the epp, s&d, alde and greens/efa groups, takes a hard line on russia's actions in relation to ukraine and a balanced approach to the middle east peace process, with an emphasis on the two-state solution. the need to focus on the fight against is and to address the growing challenges stemming from the failure of the state in syria, iraq, libya and the sahel is also highlighted. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ we voted against because the brok report insists that the political, economic, financial and defence resources of the european union and its member states must be combined in order to maximise the union's geostrategic influence to make it a key political player on the world stage. to this end, it provides for the subordination of all strategic policies under the cfsp/csdp and explicitly calls for increased resources for defence-related issues. we therefore vote against the report because it does not reflect the eu's negative position on the conflicts in the neighbouring countries (both southern and eastern); the report does not focus on the peaceful resolution of conflicts; it defends the geopolitical nature of the atc, it does not refer to the separation between eu policy and nato policy, nor does it refer to the separation of civilian and military actions in the area of the union's security and cooperation policy.

in writing. ‒ eh bildu has voted against report as it insists that political, economic, financial and defence resources of the eu and member states must be combined in order to maximise the eu’s geostrategic influence and unleash its full potential as a global player, at the same time that it promotes the subordination of all strategic policy areas under cfsp/csdp and demands increased resources for defence and military. furthermore the report advocates further militarisation of the eu, stronger eu-nato cooperation and supports the merge of internal and external security. eh bildu is an anti-militaristic coalition that strongly opposes the figure of nato, hence since that starting point we are unable to support it. moreover, we object it because it does not reflect eu’s negative and escalating role regarding the current conflict in the southern and eastern eu-neighbourhood. it speaks of peaceful conflict solution but focuses at the same time on boosting permanent structured cooperation and it promotes ttip and its geopolitical character. instead of these, we demand no military funding from eu-budget; all activities to be strictly within un charter and international law; a civilian eu with strict civil peaceful approaches to conflict solutions; and a strict separation of eu from nato.
in writing. ‒ in the face of the growing instability on the borders of the european union in recent years, i have stressed that the eu does not want to fight but prefers to cooperate and to persuade. europe is facing the greatest period of threats and challenges in its recent history: security, failed states and conflicts in both its eastern and southern neighbourhoods. we must therefore strengthen our internal cooperation between states, intelligence and diplomacy and extend our decisive influence abroad by renewing our neighbourhood policy.

in writing. ‒ for european socialists, the defence, promotion and respect of human rights is a central and backbone element of the eu's foreign policy. the annual report is one of parliament's main instruments for monitoring and guiding the union's action in this field. this year's text, written by a socialist rapporteur, provides an innovative perspective, focusing on cross-cutting and thematic issues, and contains specific recommendations on the main challenges facing human rights worldwide. among the most important elements that have been introduced - despite the vote against the pp group in many cases - are the strong defence of women's sexual and reproductive rights, the push for recognition of same-sex marriage and the concept of climate refugees. the report makes a strong case for the universality and indivisibility of human rights in the face of the rise of the discourse of cultural relativism and addresses very important areas where further progress is needed, such as the role of business, especially large multinationals, and the reinforcement of the coherence of eu policies.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because it completely ignores the deterioration of the human rights situation in western sahara. in recent years, the situation in the territory - pending decolonization - has worsened significantly in terms of freedom of association, freedom of expression and freedom of assembly. in this connection, there is no call for the release of political prisoners, nor is there any call for morocco to allow access to the occupied sahara for independent observers and members of the european parliament. the report mentions the situation in other specific cases, but in ignoring this particular one i was unable to vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because terrorism poses a direct threat to all countries and all people, regardless of their ethnic origin, religion or beliefs. it can only be countered by a global alliance, in full compliance with international law, fundamental values and international human rights standards. counter-terrorism measures should not be abused to repress legitimate dissent or violate the universal human rights of individuals. the resolution calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and for the eu to take action to combat terrorism. the resolution calls for action on the root causes of terrorism, including political and cultural issues and emphasising prevention and de-radicalisation. it also called for better cooperation between the parties to promote, protect and defend human rights. it also called on the arab countries and eu member states to work towards greater protection of religious minorities in the arab world and to give full effect to the eu guidelines on freedom of religion or belief.
in writing. ‒ the resolution put to the vote makes explicit reference to the human rights violations taking place in the member countries of the arab league, which, in my view, are an obstacle to considering that organization as an ally in the fight against terrorism. however, there is no explicit mention of the fact that some of the member states of that organization are actively financing and supporting the islamic state organization, which eludes the main problem that needs to be addressed at this time. i therefore abstained.

in writing. ‒ the threat posed by terrorism on a global scale requires a coordinated response involving national governments, international integration organisations and non-state actors. this integrated response, by a kind of international alliance, will only be effective if it is carried out in full accordance with the principles of international law and with full respect for human rights and the values on which international society is based. in this context, the eeas and the arab league secretariat signed last month the eu-arab league memorandum of understanding on counter-terrorism. the central idea of the agreement is that it is not only europe that is suffering from the terrorist threat but, very especially, the arab countries and with special emphasis iraq, libya and syria. the fight against terrorism cannot be limited to military or security matters, but must also include political and cultural aspects and the fundamental aspect of prevention.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution which addresses the problem facing the french, british and irish people as a result of indiscriminate fishing for sea bass, mainly recreational, in the english channel during spawning seasons. the european commission is asked to carry out a thorough analysis of the stocks of bass, and to draw up a multiannual plan for fisheries and the introduction of a quota system (tac) in order to deal with the current situation of over-exploitation.

in writing. ‒ according to various studies on the state of the sea bass stocks, this is worrying, despite the emergency measures already adopted by the commission, as the sea bass needs a long period of time to recover its stocks. the segment of the various sea bass fishing activities and the segment of the recreational fishery percentage of the catches should be precisely determined. we need to protect the sea bass.
in writing. ‒ we voted against this motion for a resolution because, although it is an initiative which aims to promote a protection plan for an overexploited species such as the sea bass, it has contradictory aspects. the fishermen are in a worrying situation, despite the measures taken by the commission. in addition, the lack of more precise scientific data, the definition of the types of sea bass stocks or the different regional incidence between commercial and recreational fisheries, among others, are aspects that can have a negative impact when proposing multiannual plans and establishing quotas, which could be regionally unbalanced.

in writing. ‒ the commission and the member states are asked to assess the state of the sea bass stocks and their demarcation, as well as the migration of the species and the exact breeding sites. it is considered that measures for the management of the fishery for sea bass at european level are necessary to protect sea bass and that these measures should take account of scientific knowledge and give priority to proximity management and the principle of regionalisation. i voted in favour of this proposal, which calls on the commission to propose a multiannual management plan for sea bass to bring stocks above maximum sustainable yield.

in writing. ‒ the united nations human rights council is a unique platform for the defence of universal human rights. that is why i regret that i was unable to vote in favour of the resolution on the eu's priorities for the meetings of the council this year. the european union insists on applying a double standard in its human rights policy. so, while i agree with the general framework and the issues that i consider fundamental are set out - such as the abolition of the death penalty, the defence of the rights of women, children and lgbti people or economic and social rights - in dealing with the specific cases parliament swept under the carpet the systematic violations of the human rights of the palestinian people perpetrated by the israeli regime or the moroccan repression against the saharawi people, which prevented me from voting in favour.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this resolution because it is a balanced and complete text and because it is of great value as a product of consensus between the parliamentary groups. however, this is a resolution that comes too late. it was adopted on 12 march, that is to say, we have submitted what parliament considers should be the eu's priorities to the un human rights council ten days after the first session began. the title of the resolution has, of course, been changed to cover the various sessions that will be held throughout the year. there is also a question of form which i think we should improve for future occasions: the internal character of many of its sections. i think that a text that is addressed to all stakeholders and is not so eu-centred would be of greater value.
in writing. ‒ we are dealing here, on the one hand, with cross-cutting issues such as political and social rights, women's rights, children's rights, lgbtqi, the fight against torture, the death penalty, etc. and then there is a geographical perspective with a review of the countries which are somehow on the agenda of the human rights council or the priorities expressed by the eu for this session, among others: ukraine, syria, libya, iraq, bahrain, south sudan, egypt, etc. special emphasis is placed on the need to counter the increasingly frequent attempts to undermine the universal, indivisible and interdependent status of human rights, while aiming for an eu that, speaking with one voice, will see its presence at the united nations strengthened, increasing its credibility, visibility and coherence. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the promotion, protection and universality of human rights are part of the eu's identity. human rights are inherent in all human beings, regardless of nationality, race, gender, ethnic origin or religion. the eu is firmly committed to the hrc and the multilateral human rights system. it is important that the un can defend human rights and freedoms worldwide in an independent manner, an objective for which it will always have the support of the eu.
in writing. ‒ we voted against, as the commitment signed by all the groups except the gue/ngl group does not cover what we consider to be key points in the field of human rights. while the resolution does condemn violations of rights in different countries, it does not address the root causes of such violations, nor does it reject the concept of the 'responsibility to protect'. the resolution is especially weak on issues related to gender, immigration, lgbt rights, debt, protection of personal rights, self-determination of peoples and the right of peoples to dispose of their natural resources, arms trade, the israeli occupation of the west bank and east jerusalem, and the situation of palestinian prisoners.

in writing. ‒ eh bildu abstained in the vote on the joint motion for a resolution on eu priorities for the united nations human rights council (unhrc) in 2015. the joint motion presented notes on country-related priorities for the eu for ukraine, dprk (the democratic people’s republic of korea), iran, myanmar, belarus, bahrain, egypt, mali, south sudan, sri lanka, syria, iraq and palestine / israel, but it omitted many countries with a complicated situation, including colombia, mexico, saudi arabia, turkey, burundi, nigeria, gambia, afghanistan, azerbaijan, uzbekistan and many others. indeed, it is sad to see that cases such as those of mexico, azerbaijan and uzbekistan, included in the group motions for resolutions, were omitted in order to achieve compromise. moreover, several inalienable rights are not mentioned or are barely addressed. there is nothing on cultural rights or on public services; the text does not go deeply into economic and social issues; and the situation of migrants and refugees is not well addressed. hence, supporting this proposal would be complicated for us. nevertheless, some positive points about it should be noted, such as the development of a section on climate change and human rights, and the paragraphs on women’s rights and children’s rights.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it sets out a clear position on what the priorities of the eu and its member states should be at the various sessions of the un human rights council in 2015. however, i want to express my specific disagreement with the final wording of the paragraph which deals with the situation in the gaza strip. the ppe group has tabled an amendment despite the fact that the text had already been negotiated by the various groups which signed the joint motion for a resolution. the original text tried to focus on the tragic humanitarian situation, without addressing, this time and for the sake of consensus, the degree of responsibility of the various actors involved in the conflict. the socialists strongly condemn the launching of rockets by hamas against the israeli civilian population, but the text, as amended by the people's group, makes clear the enormous degree of responsibility of the israeli army and government in the present situation of enormous humanitarian crisis, generated after the last offensive last july, and aggravated by the continuing and illegal blockade imposed on the strip.

my support for the resolution we passed today is much more than a vote. it is loud and clear enough! to make a people suffer who do not deserve to be made to go through what is happening. enough of killing students. it is enough to imprison politicians and businessmen with total impunity. it is enough that the opponents fear for their lives. enough with the invention of conspiracy theories to violate fundamental rights by means of enabling decrees. enough of hiding behind a dictatorship disguised as democracy. it is enough that the division of powers is not respected. it is enough that the venezuelan people live in fear. but it's also a "enough is enough" look away. anyone who does not condemn what is happening in venezuela is an accomplice, and here, unfortunately, we have seen some cases today. venezuela does not need compassion, it needs a determined action by all democrats; that is our challenge today.
mr president, ladies and gentlemen, podemos defends the fundamental principles of the rule of law and freedom of expression. we also believe that in a democracy, the way to resolve conflicts is through dialogue. we therefore think that this parliament should use its influence to promote democratic solutions which respect the sovereignty of the peoples, and not to support sanctions which only make matters worse or to interfere in the internal politics of other countries. we think it's obvious that there are a lot of problems in venezuela. but we also believe that the only way to solve these problems is to open up spaces of understanding and of peaceful and constructive dialogue between all parties. as ban ki-moon has said, as pope francis has said, as celac and unasur have said, in podemos we believe that the best way to defend democracy and human rights in venezuela is through dialogue. that is the objective we should pursue.
in writing. ‒ we have supported the joint resolution presented by the most important groups in parliament to send a respectful but forceful and clear message to the venezuelan authorities that they must respect the rules of the democratic game; they must release the detained politicians; they must not only not harass or arrest, but protect elected officials, and they must try to restore coexistence and dialogue with the opposition forces. we also demand that the instructions authorizing the security forces to shoot at protesters be withdrawn. the detention of the mayor of caracas and the worsening of the conditions of detention of other political leaders prompted a debate in the mini-plenary session of 25 february. in the resolution, we support the mediation efforts of unasur and some latin american leaders to return to dialogue and the creation of a democratic space free of tension where they can concentrate on strengthening their coexistence and the rule of law.
in writing. ‒ the resolution put to the vote is a direct attack on the will of a people, the venezuelan people, who decided years ago to live according to their own rules, carrying out their changes in line with the principles of international law and without interfering in the internal affairs of other states. this principle has not been reciprocated by the european union and the majority parties in parliament, which are once again attacking this south american country. energy independence and the sovereign will of the people are two principles against which the union acts with real force, both outside and within its borders. indirectly insisting on the application of sanctions is nothing more than following the policy of the united states, a country that recently declared venezuela "a threat to its national security". in this context, calls for respect for human rights are hypocritical, since the venezuelan state has mechanisms to defend its constitution, which is endangered by a handful of minority party leaders. i voted against this resolution because i believe in the principle of respect for the sovereignty of peoples to choose their own destiny.
in writing. ‒ i am voting in favour of this resolution, which deals with a matter of the utmost gravity and urgency. the latest actions of the venezuelan government represent a flagrant violation of human rights. the new resolution 8610, which allows the army to use firearms in the control of "public meetings and peaceful demonstrations" in contradiction with article 68 of the venezuelan constitution, on the use of firearms, the new political arrests, which do not comply with the minimum procedural and legal guarantees, and the torture in prisons force us to denounce and send a forceful response. we stress the agreement reached on the resolution on the sending of a delegation of members of the european parliament to venezuela.

in writing. ‒ the situation in venezuela is deteriorating by leaps and bounds. opposition is criminalized and imprisoned, protests are violently suppressed, the media are subjected to stifling control and intimidation, the separation of powers shines through in its absence, the population suffers from shortages of products... in view of this situation, the european union must speak out in favour of respect for democracy and human rights in venezuela and demand, in particular, fair treatment for antonio ledezma and leopoldo lópez. few votes are as easy as supporting this resolution.
in writing. ‒ we support all those parts of the resolution that favour dialogue and a democratic solution to venezuela's problems. there is one article in the resolution, however, which is not in line with european values and represents a way of looking at international relations which we do not share, either in this case or in any other, because instead of helping to resolve conflicts it makes it more difficult. paragraph 12 'urges the commission and the council to consider and adopt as many measures as are necessary to safeguard european interests' in venezuela, which opens the door to the adoption of sanctions, as the united states has already done recently. these policies, instead of encouraging dialogue, make it more difficult: the price of sanctions is not paid by governments but by citizens (as in the case of russia with spanish farmers), and sanctions would also be harmful to the interests of our companies. we want the eu to be a diplomatic tool to promote dialogue and a democratic solution to conflicts. we are for peace, democratic dialogue and human rights, and we condemn any violation of fundamental rights, wherever it occurs.
