in writing. ‒ the resolution put to the vote is a direct attack on the will of a people, the venezuelan people, who decided years ago to live according to their own rules, carrying out their changes in line with the principles of international law and without interfering in the internal affairs of other states. this principle has not been reciprocated by the european union and the majority parties in parliament, which are once again attacking this south american country. energy independence and the sovereign will of the people are two principles against which the union acts with real force, both outside and within its borders. indirectly insisting on the application of sanctions is nothing more than following the policy of the united states, a country that recently declared venezuela "a threat to its national security". in this context, calls for respect for human rights are hypocritical, since the venezuelan state has mechanisms to defend its constitution, which is endangered by a handful of minority party leaders. i voted against this resolution because i believe in the principle of respect for the sovereignty of peoples to choose their own destiny.

mr president, mr juncker, at the beginning of his speech, referred to the general economic context in which we are operating and pointed out that some elements are changing positively - the price of oil, the exchange rate of the euro, some macroeconomic variables - but we are far from having overcome the problems we have been suffering for a few years. as far as growth is concerned, we are going to grow by a little over 1 per cent this year. that's like a third of the united states, and that growth comes after two years of zero growth or recession. as far as unemployment is concerned, we have doubled the unemployment rate in the united states, we have very high longterm unemployment, and we have failed to reduce youth unemployment. investment is 20% below the pre-crisis level and divergences within the european union are continuing to grow, putting social cohesion at risk and also putting convergence at risk. the commission is responding to this situation. the commission has presented the investment programme, the investment plan; it has put forward a proposal for flexibility in the rules of the stability and growth pact; it has also put forward a political proposal on fiscal transparency and, today, it has referred to the need for us to use the new possibilities of oil and the exchange rate. however, the council is not responding with the same intensity. and i think that, while we recognize that there is a line of action in the commission's response to the crisis, the council's position on these problems remains timid - if not a little bit autistic. i therefore ask the council to make the same commitment with the same intensity as the commission is at least showing. let me end, mr sassoli, by saying that, unfortunately for me, i have not been able to grow as mr timmermans has since the commission presented itself at the beginning of july. unfortunately, my height is still equivalent.
mr president, i would first of all like to join the spanish delegation of the people's party in expressing solidarity with the victims of the plane crash in the alps yesterday - a tragedy in europe which affects us as europeans, which moves us as europeans and which should concern us as europeans - and also to take this opportunity to thank the french authorities for their efforts to collect the remains of the victims and to help in whatever way they can to ensure that the investigation into this accident is resolved in the best possible way. i would also like to congratulate the council on the agreement on the energy union for two reasons: firstly, because it will help us to fight climate change better from europe and to arrive at the paris summit more united, more firm and more coordinated - which is important - and, secondly, because it will help energy interconnections, which not only allow energy islands to cease to be energy islands but, through at least the iberian peninsula, gas from north africa to reach the rest of europe. i also welcome the fact that the european neighbourhood policy has been revised to take account of the danger posed by the establishment of terrorism in north africa, particularly in tunisia and libya, and i ask that the next summit on 'southern neighbourhood' to be held in barcelona on 13 april send a clear message to the terrorists: europe will be a wall, an impenetrable wall for terror and intolerance.
in writing. the directive on the automatic exchange of information between member states adopted in 2014 covers interest and dividends on accounts and profits from the sale of financial assets. however, it does not include the (mostly secret) tax rulings between member states and multinationals, which is what lux leaks has revealed. the commission proposes to amend directive 2011/12/eu to extend this automatic exchange of information to tax agreements. in this way, such decisions by tax administrations in favour of companies will have to be automatically communicated to all member states and the commission. the proposal has a retroactive period of 10 years and no commercial or professional secret may be invoked to prevent the provision of information. it is a positive and necessary measure, but the current proposal has some weaknesses: the information exchanged will not be accessible to the public; the obligation to exchange is conditional on a cross-border impact of tax agreements, which may be a loophole; the obligation only affects legal persons (natural persons such as actors or high-profile footballers could sign such agreements); no sanctions are specified in case of non-compliance with the obligation to exchange
madam president, i welcome the content of this annual report on taxation because it is what was needed after the luxleaks scandal. transparency on the functioning of the european treasury is needed, and more harmonisation and participation is needed so that taxpayers can contribute to initiatives that 'improve' tax and productive reality. taxation must be put at the service of the real economy, favour the honest taxpayer and punish financial plunder, tax evasion, tax avoidance and aggressive tax planning. we compete with taxation by supporting innovation, not evasion. those who practice such behaviour, i believe, should be excluded from recruitment and public aid, in addition to the tax penalties. we also need a financial transaction tax which will generate own resources for the common institutions, and an urgent reform of vat, which is old, unfair and facilitates evasion. finally, congratulations on the global approach, because that is what we, true europeanists, expect from our union.
member of the commission. madam president, ladies and gentlemen, i would first like to thank each and every one of you for your contributions. what i take away from this debate is, first of all, a very high degree of convergence of views on the objectives. we all, whatever our preferences, want to see a fairer and more efficient tax system in the union. we want to create a transparent and predictable framework for eu businesses, which enables them to compete on world markets. we want to give the tax administrations of the member states the means to exercise their prerogatives, which are now weakened. that is the message i will be conveying to the finance ministers and we must all convey to the national governments, who, as you know, have a vital role to play in this matter - the unanimity rule is a complicating rule - if we want europe to remain credible in this area. i'm going to make three brief remarks, in telegraphic style. firstly, in response to some comments, i can tell you that i believe that what we are proposing is substantial and that in terms of transparency in particular, the progress of the package i will present next week marks - i do not hesitate to say this - a kind of new era for the european union: never before has such an ambitious approach been proposed, which goes far beyond the arsenal we have had since 1977. i would add that this is, of course, a first step and not an end in itself. the commission will present before the summer a second package which will include both measures for competitiveness and which will include new steps towards transparency, which i am - i said - ready to study with you. i mentioned the country by country report. secondly, it is true that we do not act only for ourselves. we are doing this in a global context, in particular in the context of the oecd beps initiative, in the context of the g20 initiative and i would like to see collaboration opened up with other countries outside the european union. i would like to mention, for example, in a field other than that which we are dealing with today, the agreement on the automatic exchange of banking information, which was initialled last week with switzerland and will be concluded this summer. this is a real revolution, again, which marks the future end of banking secrecy in a great country which we know has a certain image in this case. thirdly, i want to assure you of my determination to make a difference, to rely without hesitation on the demands of a public opinion which today no longer tolerates certain injustices or practices, to hold the member states accountable. to do this, we need you, parliament, and us, the commission, to work together, almost hand in hand. that's why i'm willing to listen to your suggestions. that is why the work that your assembly is carrying out in the econ and taxe committees on this subject plays a vital role both in raising public awareness of the current situation of taxation in the union and in defining the solutions to be implemented. i look forward to the results of this joint work.
in writing. the directive on the automatic exchange of information between member states adopted in 2014 covers interest and dividends on accounts and profits from the sale of financial assets. however, it does not include the (mostly secret) tax rulings between member states and multinationals, which is what lux leaks has revealed. the commission proposes to amend directive 2011/12/eu to extend this automatic exchange of information to tax agreements. in this way, such decisions by tax administrations in favour of companies will have to be automatically communicated to all member states and the commission. the proposal has a retroactive period of 10 years and no commercial or professional secret may be invoked to prevent the provision of information. it is a positive and necessary measure, but the current proposal has some weaknesses: the information exchanged will not be accessible to citizens; the obligation to exchange is conditional on a cross-border impact of tax agreements, which may be a way out; the obligation only affects legal persons (natural persons such as actors or high-profile footballers could sign such agreements); no sanctions are specified in case of non-compliance with the obligation to exchange.

in writing. there can be no fair taxation without publicity. taxation needs transparency and in the 21st century there can be no opacity with social irresponsibility. in the light of these principles, i would like to make three suggestions to the european commission's proposal for amending the directive on the automatic and compulsory exchange of information in the field of taxation: 1. not just the states. depriving citizens of access to this information is unjustified and cannot be explained in the age of transparency. 2. the obligation to inform states should also extend to their agreements with natural persons and not only with legal persons. 3. states should publish a blacklist of companies that commit tax fraud or tax evasion so that the corporate reputation of companies is affected by tax irresponsibility.

in writing. the fiscal transparency package presented last week by the european commission in response to the luxleaks scandal, which aims to combat the secrecy of tax deals between large corporations and governments, is rather vague. first of all, despite including some improvements in the information received by the tax authorities of the states, it should not be called a transparency package, since it maintains opacity to the people by hiding the access of citizens to the information of these agreements. to achieve a decent level of transparency, it is the people who must have the possibility of accessing information. i hope that the corporate tax package that the commission will publish in june will go further and be ambitious in publicising the ultimate beneficiary of business structures, with public country-by-country reports on business activity, and that it will try to curb competition between states to reduce tax dumping.

in writing. transparency in the european union has become a pillar of the european parliament and the other european institutions in recent years. the fight against tax fraud must be a priority for the european institutions, as it is for the member states. companies must pay their taxes where their profits are generated. the initiatives currently being taken and those still to come within the european union, both in the field of corporate taxation and the fight against harmful tax practices, and in that of administrative cooperation, must fundamentally promote transparency and the exchange of information. the proposal for a directive to establish the exchange of information on tax agreements is of great importance, as it will allow member states to have access to agreements that the administrations of other countries grant to taxpayers, thus ensuring proper taxation. i would like to highlight the important work being done by the special committee on tax resolutions and other measures similar in nature or effect, chaired by our colleague alain lamassoure.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, madam high representative, ladies and gentlemen, as i predicted in the debate on the situation in libya at the previous plenary session, the decomposition of this country has already reached tunisia. i would remind you that the high representative stated in that same debate that the situation in libya and north africa is a priority for the european union alongside that of ukraine. however, this equality of priorities does not seem to be reflected either in economic or political terms. in particular, two thirds of the european neighbourhood instrument funds are allocated to the eastern region of europe, with a population of just over 12 million, while the southern region, with a population of 22 million, is not given the same attention. this highlights the imbalance of priorities. but the situation in the southern part of the union is extreme. the european neighbourhood policy needs to be urgently reviewed in order to ensure a balanced and permanent commitment of the union to its eastern and southern partners. in the specific case of tunisia, the terrorist attack last week, in addition to seeking to derail its fledgling democracy, has sought to harm its most important productive sector, tourism. we cannot forget that tunisia is the only country where the democratic transition has been genuine: in no other arab country is there an islamist government that has won and lost power in free elections; there is no other state on the southern shore of the mediterranean - the southern border of the european union - that is not today a religious or military autocracy, except tunisia; and the islamic state, which we are far from defeating, is knocking at its door. we must therefore respond to this situation, we must help tunisia with all the means at our disposal and initiate a comprehensive support plan, including loans, investments and security aid over the next few years. we cannot afford to lose a single more focus of tension and instability on europe's southern border, we cannot afford to lose tunisia.

mr president, the single markets are often used as a tool to devalue working conditions. the transport market, which is so important for economic and social development, is a fragile market which is being compromised by unfair practices such as the relocation of companies to countries with low operating costs. the legislation we have either does not serve or legitimises social dumping; the principle of freedom of choice in employment contracts, contained in the rome i regulation, is a lie: the worker can never choose his working conditions over the employer. the european union must promote the harmonization of living and working conditions, upwards and not downwards: a minimum wage cannot mean a 'lower minimum wage' in some countries of the union. and we must promote economic balance between the various countries of the european union, because this is, in the end, the ultimate cause of these inequalities and differences, and not impose on the rest of the countries, as has been done, the working conditions of the countries with the lowest conditions.
look, there are various requests, there are blue cards which, unfortunately, we will not be able to attend to because - i repeat - we have accumulated more than half an hour of delay, on the one hand, and, on the other, we have already granted the floor to those who previously made use of it, which is why, in this case, we cannot give them the turn to speak.
in writing. the internationalisation of the economy is a hard limit for the left in each state: policies to expand demand and public services, to raise wages or to improve working conditions, are at risk because of the ease with which capital moves its factories and its warehouses where taxation is lax and the exploitation of workers is greater. the fight against fiscal or labour dumping therefore increasingly requires negotiations and decisions at european level. but the present eu not only insists on replicating the logic of the market, but even accelerates the decomposition of the gains of the workers' movement in each state. instead of clearly defending the introduction of a minimum wage in transport, the commission maintains the ambiguity over the interpretation of its own directives, delaying a decision which would necessarily validate their legality. instead of helping to regulate a sector which has been badly affected by the liberalization of services and the lax implementation of labour legislation, the commission is unable to defend it, delving into the profound crisis of the european project.
in writing. over the last few years, both the commission and the european parliament have been calling for the administrative burden on businesses to be reduced wherever possible, so that they are not put in the way of their economic activity and make full use of the potential of the single market, which is based mainly on the free movement of people, goods and merchandise. road transport comprises a major part of the transport of goods in the european union and is the main element of the internal market. it is therefore necessary to remove the remaining technical and legal barriers. we do not believe that there is social dumping in countries where purchasing power is simply lower. if there are illegal practices, they must be controlled, but it makes little sense that a minimum wage rule should seek to equalise countries with such different per capita incomes. the european commission should act quickly and clearly on a matter which clearly transcends national borders and goes beyond the principle of subsidiarity, as well as being a regulatory precedent with clear consequences.
madam president, it is important to have this day of commemoration of the genocide of the roma people in the second world war, but in this case we have learned little from the horrors of the past: the persecution of the roma people continues today within the borders of the european union. in 2007, mr franco frattini, then vice-president of the european commission, said: "what you have to do is simple: go to a nomadic camp in rome and ask them: 'can you tell me where you live?' if they say they don't know, take them and send them to romania. and as juan de dios ramírez heredia, president of the spanish roma union, said at the time: 'cogedlos' brings back memories of europe's saddest history. "take us" dictators have always said; "take us" the nazis said to take us to the concentration camps and then to the gas chambers. and little has changed since 2007, except that the wave of racism and xenophobia has also been joined by social democracy. the current french prime minister, manuel valls, is known for trying to expel a 15-year-old girl while she was on a field trip, and besides, here in this parliament we also have a far right sitting who keeps shouting 'get them'.
madam president, i would not have stopped for anything in the world from asking to speak in a debate in this european parliament, which reflects on the international day of the roma people and which pays tribute to the victims of the holocaust against the roma in the second world war - which also took place. and i am proud of it because the socialist group had the first gypsy member of this parliament, juan de dios ramírez heredia, and now it has two distinguished and honourable members, soraya post and our colleague damian drăghici. but i am also proud that the socialist group is unwaveringly committed to combating discrimination, to equal rights and opportunities, and to combating the stigmatisation of any population, even a minority, in european society. and that is why i ask this parliament to monitor national strategies against discrimination against the roma people, including in a country like my own, spain, which boasts a successful experience of integration of the roma community and which, however, still perpetuates the anti-roma stereotype in a series of sayings and even jokes in spanish. we are extremely demanding against stigmatisation and especially against hate speech, and we deplore that in this parliament we have had to listen to manifestations of this negative stigmatisation of the roma, full of hatred, by representatives of the extreme right, which embarrass this parliament.
madam president, in 1928, years before the genocide of the gypsies, one of the greatest spanish poets, federico garcía lorca, published the romance of the gypsies. it made the gypsies visible in a positive for literature, visible and dignified, reflecting their fragile humanity. we need more 'garcías lorcas', and we need debates that are not held at invisible hours, because we have to compensate. gypsies are still being rejected. today too, even to bury a ten-month-old baby maria francesca on january 4, 2015, in france, in champlan, it was impossible to bury her there and they had to bury her somewhere else. look, in the romance of the moon, by garcía lorca, there is talk of the death of a gypsy child in these verses: "the moon goes through the sky / with a child in hand. / inside the forge crying, screaming, the gypsies. / the air sails, sails. / the air is watching her. i pray for the soul of maria francesca and for ours, because we have heard things today that are certainly inciting hatred.
madam president, first of all i would like to express my sympathy to the families and friends of the victims of the terrible plane crash which has shocked us. ladies and gentlemen, the report by the european network for linguistic equality on discrimination in spain is forceful. in the spanish state, the fundamental rights of those who speak co-official languages, such as catalan or valencian - as we call it - galician, basque, aragonese or asturian, are being violated in a way that is incompatible with democracy. the report includes hundreds of cases that go to aberrant limits, such as denying medical care or beating people for speaking these co-official languages. most of these attacks are caused by agents of the spanish administration, including security forces, who act with impunity. the spanish authorities are consenting to this violation of human rights, because living in one's own language is a fundamental right which every european state should guarantee. if we tolerate governments like the spanish one allowing this kind of practice we become accomplices. this report will soon reach the united nations commission on human rights and there it will embarrass all europeans who feel democratic.
madam president, please listen to these figures: 500 million euros invested in the construction of an undersea gas storage facility off the coast of castellón in eastern spain; 1 350 million euros in compensation to the concessionary company for the halting of the project - which we will pay all consumers for 30 years in the electricity bill -; more than 500 earthquakes recorded in the area during one month as a result of gas injections. these are the facts; and the facts are that the spanish government approved a decree-law compensation of more than 1 350 million euros for a plant which never became operational; and that the compensation was paid with unprecedented speed - in forty days - without justifying either the urgency or the amount. we therefore ask the commission to investigate whether this compensation is subject to a right.
madam president, a few months ago, the graphic humorist known as el roto published a cartoon in which it could be read: we must encourage young people to leave the country, lest they try to change it. hundreds of thousands of young people - and not so young - have been forced into exile in recent years because the spanish state denies them a future. they are expelled and, furthermore, afterwards, when they are already out, they are prevented from voting. in 2011, the popular party and the socialist party changed the electoral law and now spanish citizens living abroad have to beg for their vote to participate in the elections, a process with a thousand obstacles and a thousand difficulties that, practically, prevents them from exercising their right to vote. in fact, in the last european elections only 4.5% of the population resident abroad voted and in andalusia only 3.8%, which casts doubt on the legitimacy of the election result. it's perfect: first they get kicked out and then they don't get to vote. perfect for some to continue to sit on their seats serving those who have led us to the current situation of unemployment and exile. but whether they like it or not, and despite the denial of the vote to thousands of young people, we are going to change this country.
i want to return to the subject of the czech republic as a czech mep, namely the protection of consumer rights in the field of telecommunications services. i have already reported that the czech republic has adopted a law on electronic communications, which, according to most lawyers, is contrary to the content of the universal service directive and significantly reduces the rights of consumers in relation to significant, influential and economically powerful operators. i sent a question to the commission on this matter and was very pleased that the commission does not take this matter lightly, that it states that it is following the matter and that the commission has approached the czech republic with a request for clarification and ensuring compliance of czech legislation with eu law. i would ask and urge the commission to continue to monitor this issue and, if inconsistencies are found, to take all steps to remedy what i consider to be discriminatory czech legislation.
madam president, i would like to bring to the attention of this house the impact of the crisis on the fundamental rights of spaniards, after three years of popular party rule. the assessment i am about to make corresponds to the conclusions of a study published by this parliament. the study says: "the numerous austerity measures adopted in spain, with cuts in social, educational and health budgets, have led to a worrying increase in family poverty, negatively impacting fundamental rights. in education, the reforms adopted have led to a great inequality in the spanish education system; public health care is no longer universal and free; in pensions it is recognised that there is already a reduction in the amount of pensions with the consequent reduction in purchasing power. the report concludes that the austerity measures adopted by the rajoy government have led to growing inequality in spain. the first response of the citizens to these harsh policies is the results obtained by the popular party in my region, andalusia, last sunday, losing 14% of the votes, against the victory of the socialist party, which has pursued another policy in defence of fundamental rights.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal because the application of the greek authorities meets the eligibility criteria laid down by the egf regulation. the redundancies are in the sector of radio and television programming and broadcasting activities in the attica region which is linked to the global economic and financial crisis. a total of 928 redundancies were recorded in 16 enterprises operating in division 60 (radio and television broadcasting and programming activities) of nace rev. 2 in the nuts level 2 region (5) of the attica region (el 30), greece. at present, the attica region has the highest number of unemployed among the 12 greek regions; and also because the application will be for vocational guidance, training, retraining and vocational training, specialised training and education, job search and training and mobility grants, and all eligible displaced workers will participate in the measures financed by the egf.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to approve the mobilisation of eur 5 046 000 from the european globalisation adjustment fund for 928 workers who have lost their jobs in 16 companies operating in the sector of radio and television broadcasting and programming activities in the attica region of greece as a result of the economic and financial crisis in the country, which has significantly reduced the costs of daily information, despite its importance, and has drastically restricted loans to businesses and individuals as a result of the lack of liquidity in greek banks. the personalised services to be financed by the egf include career guidance, training, retraining and job search activities, as well as grants for the creation of new businesses and the promotion of entrepreneurship. although this aid alone is not sufficient to alleviate the problem of unemployment in the attica region, which already has the highest number of unemployed among the twelve greek regions, it does constitute good assistance and training for the reintegration of the workers concerned into employment.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report as it allows for mobilisation following a total of 424 redundancies at lufthansa technik airmotive ireland ltd (ltai) and at two of its suppliers in ireland. this mobilization of funds is due to the disastrous consequences of the internationalisation of the productive sectors in the eu. these funds are not able to solve the problems of these workers in the context of unemployment in ireland, but at least they give the possibility of alleviating a small part of the human drama. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i support the mobilisation of these funds for two reasons: they will affect a group of people who are very difficult to relocate because of their specific skills and an average age which is close to the average retirement age in ireland and because of the inclusion of about 200 ni-nis who will have a powerful tool to enter the labour market. it is an imaginative and practical use of the possibilities of the funds for adaptation to globalisation. the reason for the redundancies is that the major maintenance work on the largest european airplanes has been moved to asian countries. in this case, the philippines.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to approve the mobilisation of eur 2 490 758 from the globalisation adjustment fund for 424 workers who have lost their jobs at lufthansa technik airmotive ireland ltd and two of its suppliers in ireland, engaged in the repair and installation of machinery and equipment. these redundancies have occurred as a consequence of profound structural changes in international trade patterns brought about by globalisation, as a consequence of a major transformation of eu trade in goods and services due to a technological shift towards the production of new generation aircraft and components, a shift towards broader aircraft component production practices, and a shift in the location of global aircraft production; highlighting the trend of us and western european airlines to send their large capacity aircraft to china for heavy maintenance. the personalised services to be financed by the egf comprise training and retraining activities which constitute good assistance for the reintegration into employment of the workers concerned.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because its adoption will mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) to provide an amount of eur 2 490 758 in commitment and payment appropriations in relation to an application to mobilise the egf following the 250 redundancies at lufthansa technik airmotive ireland ltd and two of its suppliers in ireland.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report on the mobilisation of resources for adaptation to a globalised area. the report deals with a heading for the reintegration of 250 workers in ireland into the labour market and the economic benefits this budgetary mobilisation will have for the region.

in writing. - i vote in favour. the european globalisation adjustment fund was set up to provide additional support to workers suffering from the consequences of major structural changes in world trade patterns. in the light of the request submitted, i consider that it should be granted.
in writing. ‒ ireland submitted an application egf/2014/016 ie/lufthansa technik for a financial contribution from the egf, following a total of 424 redundancies at lufthansa technik airmotive ireland ltd (ltai) and at two of its suppliers in ireland. workers in this sector have very specific skills which are difficult to use in other sectors, and therefore it is not easy for them to find a new job. the importance of improving the employment prospects of all workers through appropriate training measures and the recognition of skills and competences acquired throughout the worker's career should therefore be recalled. i would like to ask the commissioner to give us a clear answer to this question.
in writing. ‒ my support for the proposal to mobilise the european globalisation adjustment fund to support ireland in the wake of the dismissal of 424 workers from lufthansa technik airmotive ireland ltd and two of its suppliers. in this case, ireland will not only support these workers with european funds, but also 200 young people who are neither studying nor working. the european parliament hopes that the support provided through this tool will enable all these people to return to the labour market soon.

i shall briefly explain my vote on the macro-economic assistance to ukraine. i very much welcome the fact that, in addition to the political assistance to ukraine which we are declaring here in parliament, we have today also accepted concrete macro-financial assistance in the form of eur 1.8 billion in the form of a medium-term loan. i am convinced that if we want ukraine to follow the path of democratisation, the development of the rule of law and a market economy in the long term, we must support it not only politically but also economically. we need to get this country back on its feet, just like america helped western europe after world war ii. that is why i supported this proposal and i hope that we will consider other forms of support in the future. it is necessary that this support be linked to the conditions of further reforms in ukraine, so that the money that will be provided to ukraine as loans does not end up in the pockets of the oligarchs, but really helps this country.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the granting of macrofinancial assistance to ukraine proposed by the european commission, firstly because of the urgent need to mobilise international public aid for the neighbouring country, which is in a serious crisis, aggravated by the armed conflict in the east of the country and the consequent instability that makes it impossible for it to access international debt financing markets. secondly, because the aid programme will serve as a support and impetus for the much needed internal reform process in ukraine, by being accompanied by a political programme agreed with the authorities of the country. this assistance will therefore contribute to the achievement of the eu's objective of promoting stability and economic development in ukraine and, more generally, in the associated countries of eastern europe.
in writing. ‒ macro-financial assistance is an exceptional crisis response instrument that the eu makes available to its partner countries with severe payment problems. the report proposes to grant ukraine financial aid of eur 1.8 billion, taking into account that this is in addition to the funds already given to it by the eu, the imf or the world bank. since this aid is conditional on the implementation of certain requirements, such as structural reforms in the economic field (privatisation, deregulation) and in the political field, i voted against.
in writing. ‒ europe is only credible when, as in this case, it is consistent. ukraine is facing an exceptional situation, perhaps never seen in the european framework before. to its internal problems of misgovernance, corruption and instability is added external aggression, russia's illegal annexation of crimea, and the economic and financial losses caused by that state of larval warfare and occupation. ukraine is also outside the international debt markets. i also believe in the two effects that this initiative can have. encourage new donors and promote other 'creative' financial avenues, as the report says, to stimulate good governance, the fight against fraud and corruption.

in writing. ‒ the ukrainian economy is in a severe and acute crisis, triggered by deep-rooted structural problems and exacerbated by the well-known armed conflict in the eastern regions. the ambitious macroeconomic adjustment and structural reform programme of the new government that took office in february 2014 has been supported by an imf financial assistance programme and two eu macro-financial assistance operations. however, ukraine's reform efforts have been seriously affected by the armed conflict. the additional macro-financial assistance proposed by the commission on 8 january 2015 can make a significant contribution to a new international assistance package for ukraine. it should also catalyse a gradual return of confidence and support reform efforts in the country through an accompanying political programme to be agreed with the ukrainian authorities. i voted in favour of the first reading, accepting the commission's proposal.
in writing. ‒ my strongest support for the proposal to grant a loan of eur 1.8 billion to ukraine, as i believe that we must undoubtedly help this country to contribute from the european union so that it can get out of the difficult economic situation it is going through as soon as possible. ukraine is a great ally of the european union and we must repay that friendship with all the support we can give at this time when the country is also facing a terrible armed conflict. i therefore express my full support for the ukrainian people and my hope that this situation will be overcome as soon as possible.

in writing. ‒ the ukrainian economy is going through an acute and severe crisis caused by structural problems and, mainly, by the ongoing armed conflict in the east of the country, which is causing trade restrictions with its russian neighbour and very serious problems around gas supply. the external financing deficit and ukraine's lack of access to international debt markets make additional official financial assistance one of the country's few resources. the european parliament has repeatedly supported the provision of assistance to ukraine and welcomes the commission's proposal to provide ukraine with an additional amount of eur 1,8 million in macro-financial assistance and considers it positive to approve at first reading this commission proposal based on the conclusions of the european council of 18 december 2014.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the annual report on taxation because it reiterates the need to fight against tax fraud and evasion as well as aggressive tax planning, and in particular supports the automatic exchange of information on tax agreements between member states and corporations. it is not possible for large multinationals to reduce their tax payments to a minimum. profits should be taxed where they are generated. it also reminds the council that it must adopt the directive on the harmonisation of the corporate tax base, blocked by some member states since 2011, and the directive on the financial transaction tax (ftt) through enhanced cooperation. in addition, the spanish socialists believe that derivatives should be included in the scope of the itf and that taxes on wealth are essential to combat the inequality arising from the growing accumulation of capital. we have also advocated that the commission should promote, through the country-specific recommendations in the framework of the european semester, the introduction of a wealth tax in the member states where it is not yet in place. in short, we socialists reiterate that tax competition is incompatible with the internal market.
in writing. ‒ given the importance of the problem of tax evasion in the eu and the urgency of addressing it, we expected a report proposing concrete measures to tackle the problem. in our view, the report lacks the social justice perspective and the importance of redistributive nature. moreover, it does not include as a key objective the taxation of large companies, multinationals and wealth. finally, the report is clearly in line with neoliberal policies and the dominant model, as it calls for a reinforcement of the european semester, and proposes a tax policy under the european semester.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the annual report on taxation because it reiterates the need to fight against tax fraud and evasion as well as aggressive tax planning, and in particular supports the automatic exchange of information on tax agreements between member states and corporations. it is not possible for large multinationals to reduce their tax payments to a minimum. profits should be taxed where they are generated. the report also reminds the council that it must adopt the directive on the harmonisation of the corporate tax base, blocked by some member states since 2011, and the directive on the financial transaction tax (ftt) through enhanced cooperation. in this sense, it is important to emphasise, as the report does not mention it, that derivatives should be included in the scope of the itf. in addition, there is no mention of the wealth tax, which is essential to combat the inequality resulting from the growing accumulation of capital. the commission is responsible for advising on the establishment of the wealth tax in member states where it is not yet in place through the country specific recommendations. in short, we socialists reiterate that tax competition is incompatible with the internal market.

on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, as has been said here, we are discussing a modification of the financial framework, which is essential in order to be able to take advantage of those 21 000 million euros, which for various reasons could not be programmed in 2014 and which we are transferring to 2015. i think that no one is opposed to this and we all agree that it must be adopted quickly and that the important thing is that these programmes are carried out. but i would like to focus a little on what will happen to payments, not only because of this modification of the financial framework but also because of the implications of the transfer of payments towards the end of the framework. because in this debate with the commission on payments and the situation of unpaid invoices, it is true that, with the information we have, it seems that the situation is stabilizing as regards the previous financial framework. but unfortunately we are delaying payments from the beginning of the financial framework to the end. basically, for two reasons: because of this modification of the financial framework and because of the delay in the start-up of the programmes, we will have more payments at the end of the period but also because we have had to use in 2014 payments that were planned for the end of the mandate, due to a lower scheduling of payments in 2014. so, in that review of the financial framework we were talking about earlier, let us hope that the european commission takes this into account and can put in enough payments so that we do not have a situation as regrettable as we have had so far.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, the reality of youth unemployment, which affects more than five million young people in europe, is even more stark and worrying in spain, where more than half of them are unemployed. and more than 300,000 young people have left our country since 2008, as both the tide granate and youth without a future have denounced in parliament. this is the terrible balance sheet of the precarious situation we are facing because of the austerity and adjustment policies implemented by both the socialist party and the people's party. the current amendment to the multiannual financial framework to transfer the resources foreseen in 2014 to the 2015 financial year under the so-called youth guarantee is good news, but it is an insufficient measure. ladies and gentlemen, do not be fooled. and most of all, don't be fooled. we are again faced with a make-up operation. we are again faced with a political gamble which does not move towards quality and equal employment for young people. we will continue to advocate a much greater increase in european and national funds, which are mainly directed at investment programmes in r & d & i, public infrastructure of social value and the creation of activities from the point of view of the social and solidarity economy.
mr president, in your day, in armenian, people spoke of the mec yelen, the great catastrophe. i don't want to discuss the appropriateness of the concept of genocide to what actually happened. it's probably the most appropriate. and we cannot forget or minimize. we must continue to work in all areas to face the truth, however harsh and painful it may be. and we must expect the present turkish authorities to face up to the horror of what happened a hundred years ago in the context of the first world war, without any subterfuge whatsoever. but for the same reason we must distinguish between the grave responsibility of the ottoman empire in the last stage of its existence and the demand we must make today to the present turkish state. let us therefore work to make compatible the knowledge of the truth, the recognition of the responsibilities which correspond to that empire and the concrete progress towards understanding between the peoples and the respective institutions. let us not turn this anniversary into a defenseless judgment on turkish society and citizenship, which today is hosting millions of refugees, which wants to look to the future in peaceful coexistence with its neighbours and which sees in europe the common framework of freedom, justice and prosperity to which it legitimately aspires. that is the european responsibility. our motto today is "reconciliation". that is the key word that should guide our thinking and our decision.
mr president, i would encourage turkey to accept that the extermination of over one and a half million armenians between 1915 and 1919 was genocide. taking that responsibility and disqualifying these behaviors produces truth, justice and reparation. and it facilitates non-repetition and facilitates reconciliation. the annual review of the health of turkish democracy is helping to bring about this change. in april last year, for the first time, president erdoğan acknowledged the armenian pain, called the deportations and mass crimes inhumane and conveyed his condolences to the families of the victims. we must encourage this development, which will accelerate if there is unanimous international recognition of this genocide, which is indisputable in the light of the definition in force since 1948. it was an honour for me to preside over the basque parliament when, in 2007, it took that step.
mr president, i am a citizen of the spanish state, one of those states which does not want to recognize the existence of the armenian genocide. and there are many within the european union, which i think we should be ashamed of. i do not think that concealing or disguising what a genocide entails will improve political relations. the european union must be courageous and make it clear that in a process of reconciliation, the same cannot be demanded of the executioners as of the victims, of turkey as of the armenian people. it must be courageous and recognize that many european powers knew and did nothing to prevent that genocide. madam commissioner, calling terror by its name, the armenian genocide, and demanding its recognition and condemnation is a sine qua non for a future of peace. and perhaps, on this basis, we will react and support as we should the freedom-seeking aspirations of the people of nagorno karabakh, another aspect of the armenian problem in which europe can still avoid a tragedy.
on behalf of the alde group. madam president, i support the start of a new phase in the european institutions in the recruitment of people with disabilities. this group needs positive discrimination in the european public employment market. it is an appropriate way to set an example, to apply here, in an extensive way, the provisions of the new directive 2014/24/eu on public procurement. the european institutions are thus joining the practice of some state and regional institutions which apply this criterion. in the basque country, this reserve in some bodies of the administration reaches up to 5%, and 93% of their colleagues believe that their performance is equal to the rest and their degree of acceptance in the work environment is 4.6 out of 5. this measure will also help raise awareness in society of the needs of these groups and encourage other attitudes in line with the 2020 strategy. a renewed commitment to a europe without barriers. and we are thus adding to the prominence that the social economy and the association of disabled people have throughout the union in the creation of jobs for people who have much to contribute. because many of these limitations force those who suffer from them to develop skills and expertise which are real sources of added value in the jobs they perform. something i learned when a blind person explained to me the usefulness of a keychain that he used to know if there was light in the place where he was. and he said, "well, some people need light". think of the extraordinary message conveyed by those words.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. madam president, one of europe's objectives in delivering on the 2020 strategy is that people with disabilities should participate in the economic and social life of the european union. but that full participation is not possible if they do not have the central element, which is employment. and unfortunately, people with disabilities -- and especially women with some disabilities -- have tremendously high unemployment rates. promoting employment through reserve quotas can be a good measure, provided it is respected. and unfortunately, we cannot have the same thing happening in spain, where these reserve quotas are replaced by other measures which provide economic benefits to companies. and so, in the end, the unemployment rate for people with disabilities does not go down. quotas should also be accompanied by positive measures and good practice, such as job adaptation and possible access to selection tests. and with that, the european institutions would set a good example and companies would also be encouraged to hire these people.
madam president, i have been working for many years with the disability sector and with the european fund and spanish organizations. there is no doubt, if we go to the sector, that quotas are necessary. i have heard many speeches here, perhaps because there is no link with the disabled sectors. quotas are not the solution, but they are one more thing. positive action measures must be developed, particularly to help groups of disabled people who are experiencing greater difficulties, such as those with intellectual or psychosocial disabilities. that can't be an isolated incident. it has to be done in an environment where there are hiring processes, where there are, as the un convention says, reasonable adjustments. today the commission is not a model. today we do not know how many are disabled and how many are not. we have no information. what reasonable adjustments have been made to the jobs, as the commission says? what's the budget for this? we don't know all that. and so i think that the european union, which is working on these issues, must be a model. and so, what i propose to the union.... there have been a lot of complaints about accessibility. for example, in the union there is a part of traineeships for disabled people, but in a format that is not accessible. what do i propose to the commission? positive measures. i propose budget, i propose reasonable adjustments, i propose follow-up, i propose accessible communication and i propose a plan. because in the end, if we want to achieve the goals of equality and non-discrimination, it has to start with us.
madam president, madam commissioner, you have said that the quota system is not allowed under the current regulations and i see that you have little intention of changing them, which i do not understand, because you will understand that your job, as well as ours, is precisely to analyse what is wrong in order to propose changes in the rules. to justify a political position simply on the grounds that the rule does not allow it seems to me to be a rather weak argument. i think quotas are necessary. i think it's also a demand of the sector. i think that since we signed the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities we have committed ourselves to empowering those rights to equal opportunity, and that we have to be more. we must be a model, we must set an example for the other institutions. and so, i think we should incorporate it. we cannot ask the private sector to incorporate, to incentivise, to create - in addition to public support - tax benefits or all kinds of incentives to promote disabled people in employment if we do not set an example. i think we need to increase it to at least 5%. introduce at least 5% of quotas in the european institutions reserved for disabled people. and i think all the other measures are not incompatible. i think that people who are trying to say today that necessary measures such as increasing technical services or improving accessibility are incompatible with quotas are twisting the debate, which does not deserve the rights of these people, who must be able to exercise equal opportunities.
vice-president of the commission. – mr president, i would like most sincerely to thank everybody who has taken the floor this evening. this is certainly an issue that is not just about people with disabilities but about the europe we want to live in. i want to start with something that flashed through my mind while thinking back to when my own country became a member of the european union in 2007. for me one of the joys of this membership was that my niece, who was born with dwarfism, would live in a union where people with disabilities enjoy equal opportunities. i want to believe that this is exactly the europe we want, a europe where that happens for her and for everybody else. but we cannot possibly dream of a good life for our children if we do not integrate everybody. we are an ageing region. we need everybody to contribute to our economy and to the well-being of the european people. so for me this is not just a matter of looking at one topic, rather it is the coherence of the values we live by. that takes me on to how we intend to approach the integration of people with disabilities. firstly, i strongly believe that we have to make recruitment a door through which everybody who wants to enter the institutions can enter. as i mentioned at the beginning, we have done a lot in this area. if you go to the ‘guide to open competitions’ you will find specific information for candidates with disabilities. in every application form there is an access requirements form that can be filled in so if you have disabilities and you need any type of assistance you can get it. dyslexia is also taken into account in epso competitions. as i mentioned, there exists all the elements to make sure that people can compete. what we have to do more of – and i recognise this – is to reach out to people with disabilities and encourage more of them to apply. on the topic of how many apply and what percentage are successful, we have quite accurate data. out of about 30 000 applicants in the last competition, around 300 made it. among them were seven people with disabilities. obviously, if we want more to apply we have to be more open in terms of how we reach out to people with disabilities to make sure they understand that a career in the european institutions is a good career for them. what worried me a lot in the staff survey when we got the results was that the staff engagement index for people who defined themselves as staff with disabilities was lower than the overall average for staff. in other words, people with disabilities do not feel that they are equally encouraged to engage in the institutions. that tells me that the institutions have to do more to engage with them. i very much agree with all those who spoke about making sure that we remove barriers for people with disabilities when making an application, but also then to ensure that they can get promoted and to encourage them to progress in terms of applying their skills. that will be an area that we will look into very carefully in the new strategy. i mentioned in the beginning that we do not have accurate data because of restrictions arising from the confidentiality of medical records. i am determined that we have to find a way to remove this restriction because we cannot rely only on self—identification if we want to be proactive and create conditions that allow people to work to their fullest ability and to grow within the commission. but this is a question for which i do not have an answer today; a question that we intend to answer as we put forward the new strategy. as regards the issue of the staff regulations, i heard loud and clear those who said that it is a very lousy excuse to state that the staff regulations do not allow you to have quotas. so i want to elaborate. i think there is a reason why the staff regulations do not allow us to have quotas; it can become a slippery slope. if we get quotas for people with disabilities, then there is pressure to have quotas on nationality and quotas on this and that. while each of these issues on their own may be very legitimate, once we go in the direction of creating a quota system on one criterion in an organisation where there is a very strong tendency to think of national quotas, i think we would see the merits, which has been a very strong factor in our decision-making, being undermined. now i am not saying that we should not think of maybe applying quotas to only one segment, but i do not want to go into that before i am convinced that we are not going to resolve one problem and create another. but what should our level of ambition be? well, many of you said what i believe should be our level of ambition. we have to be an example for the european union. the european institutions have a responsibility to lead by example. in some of our member states the quota system aims at between five and ten percent; i think the highest is in germany. so we need to look at what would be the appropriate level of ambition to target as regards people with disabilities. on self-identification, we are not in a very bad place because in the survey 5.7 % tell us that they have disabilities. therefore, we have reached a certain order of magnitude. but is this real? we count on people telling us that they have disabilities; but we do not know. so we have to improve the data collection and we have to be able to say where we are and where we are headed. where we are headed clearly has to be a good message to europe. it is not just about people with disabilities. if you walk around the institutions, we have a way to go in terms of the presence of minorities and in terms of women in management positions. there is scope for us to make ourselves more diverse than we currently are. how far are we going to go? obviously i do not want to promise a very rapid change with immediate effect, because a big organisation is a bit like the queen mary; you make a policy change and it takes time for this change to be reflected in the composition of our staff. we are determined and i would obviously support you. you will see me coming here again on this topic. i am sure you will bring me here again. it is an area where i very much value your encouragement for us to do something. we owe it not just to disabled people, but we owe it to europe to be the place of values that we have been embracing over the decades.
in writing. the socialists bring this debate to the european parliament's plenary in order to promote and ensure that the european institutions fulfil the commitment made in defence of equal opportunities for people with disabilities. as well as being a matter of fairness, it is a duty we undertook when we signed the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. currently, quota systems for persons with disabilities in the supply of employment in enterprises, public and private, and institutions exist in 21 of the 28 member states. it is ironic, however, that while we in europe call for these rights to be guaranteed, the institutions themselves put up barriers to access to employment and professional development for the most vulnerable. we believe that our social model is precisely what makes europe different: a model of fair, inclusive welfare that guarantees equal opportunities for all. these employment quotas are a further guarantee to allow real independence for these people, and we believe that from here we must set an example for society and the rest of the institutions. we cannot ask the private sector to do the same if we in the public sphere do not comply first.

in writing. the socialists bring this debate to the european parliament's plenary in order to promote and ensure that the european institutions fulfil the commitment made in defence of equal opportunities for people with disabilities. as well as being a matter of fairness, it is a duty we undertook when we signed the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities. currently, quota systems for persons with disabilities in the supply of employment in enterprises, public and private, and institutions exist in 21 of the 28 member states. it is ironic, however, that while we in europe call for these rights to be guaranteed, the institutions themselves put up barriers to access to employment and professional development for the most vulnerable. we believe that our social model is precisely what makes europe different: a model of fair, inclusive welfare that guarantees equal opportunities for all. these employment quotas are a further guarantee to allow real independence for these people, and we believe that from here we must set an example for society and the rest of the institutions. we cannot ask the private sector to do the same if we in the public sphere do not comply first.
in writing. people with disabilities represent 16% of the european population. participation and inclusion of persons with disabilities is a general principle of the united nations convention and a fundamental obligation of those who have signed it, including the european union. disabled people have the right to work. to ensure equality for people with disabilities, it is essential to promote non-discrimination, accessibility and positive measures to facilitate access to work. the european institutions have a good system of guaranteeing access for people with disabilities to posts within the organisational structure. however, there is currently no quota system as there is no definition of 'person with a disability' in the staff regulations. quota systems have proved effective as an integrating instrument. through quotas, we would make it easier for people with disabilities to access work. this is a positive measure which will make it possible to redress existing inequalities. the aim of quotas is to make them obsolete, but in the meantime access must be guaranteed.
mr president, we are faced with a sovereign decision by the government of the united mexican states. with extension. what's the way forward? the commissioner has already said that. the way forward is to ask for the negotiating mandate article 218, to start the negotiation and to conclude the negotiation. it's that simple. and that's complicated, considering the sentence. but, mr president, we have not even asked for a negotiating mandate. and the negotiating mandate must be requested at the jai council in june. this is the only way we can meet our obligations to start negotiations before 1 july. a bit of a clue. do you know what iberia does in my country? she flies to mexico twice a day. she flies seven days a week to mexico. he flies every day of the month. if the sanctions are applied, iberia will be costing 230 000 euros every week. do you realize what this means in the field of trade relations? something truly unthinkable. do you realize that if there is no community response, each member state will be able to use its sovereign power to transfer pnr data to another sovereign state which requests it in the area of security and with due regard to the preservation of privacy? in any case, mr president, what i am asking mr avramopoulos now - and i have here the press release from the mexican authorities from the last days of march - is that, since they have put their trust in him, he should start the request for the opening of negotiations as soon as possible, that is, at the jha council in june.
mr president, i think we have to be clear and here, in the end, what we are talking about is to give in, to lower our data protection standards because the airlines are asking for it, because these big companies are asking for it. i think it is important to remember that in 2013 the committee on civil liberties of this european parliament already rejected the proposal for a directive on the use of travellers' data. and i understand that this is, or should be, above the wishes and demands of the airlines. neither should airlines dictate our data protection policy nor is blackmail by the mexican government acceptable. we are obviously concerned that our data may be in the hands of a state with institutions penetrated by drug trafficking, a state where human rights are violated and with high rates of impunity. and by the way, one question: what will happen to our personal data if this agreement is finally signed? you're going to trade our data? because, no doubt, data is now big business. will our data also end up in the hands of multinational corporations in the united states and canada to use it for their benefit?
mr president, mexico, a priority partner of the european union, has a very advanced pnr system and has been asking european citizens for pnr data for a very long time. failing agreement, a moratorium was established. later, another one. and another, which expired on april 1, when mexico decided to sanction airlines for not providing this data. thanks to the constructive attitude of the mexican authorities in the negotiations with the commission, an agreement was reached to postpone this mandatory data provision until 1 july. those are the facts. what we have been given is a respite, but the problem is not solved, and everyone in this house knows what it is. we urgently need a european pnr, because it is a necessary instrument for protecting our citizens against terrorist attacks. proof of this is that many other countries have it. as chair of the delegation to the eu-mexico joint parliamentary committee, i am particularly concerned about this issue. and i say to those who opposed and oppose the pnr, you must know that actions have consequences. and when, a year ago, they applauded the failure to adopt this valid instrument, they did not think that today we would be putting at risk not only the safety of our citizens but also the normal operation of our airlines. ladies and gentlemen, irresponsibility pays off. and i think in europe we've had time. what not everyone has is a desire to have a european pnr. mr president, on 2 april last 149 people were killed at garissa university in kenya. most were students, and, according to survivors, the al-shabab terrorists, who attacked and shot the victims, went after the christian students. the reports of this massacre are terrible and should make us all, governments and international organizations, but also society as a whole, reflect on whether we are doing enough to contain the religious persecution that christians are suffering in many parts of the world. a few months ago, we received pope francis in this chamber. he himself warned of this situation and called on the international community not to remain silent, not to look the other way in the face of these murders. i ask you not to remain indifferent to this injustice. we all call for decisive action by the european union, greater involvement and leadership at international level, which shows that we in europe are determined to fight relentlessly for human rights.
mr president, on 15 june 2011 there was a large demonstration in barcelona, which surrounded the parliament of catalonia, and members were insulted, threatened and some attacked. the police didn't arrest anyone. eight youths were subsequently charged, but they were not charged with any violent or aggressive act, because the culprits could not really be found. after three years, the national court acquitted the accused. but recently, the supreme court of spain has reviewed the sentence, and, despite accepting the non-violent, non-aggressive acts, has sentenced them all to three years in prison. this sentence is literally scandalous, because it criminalizes freedom of expression, demonstration and social protest, however vigorous. i would like to make a statement here about the shame that we democrats feel at the continuing and increasing degradation of the spanish judiciary in favour of certain political and ideological positions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it allows the mobilisation of eur 6 052 200 following the dismissal of 2 804 workers in france following the bankruptcy and closure of the road transport company mory-ducros. this mobilization of funds is aimed at mitigating the disastrous social consequences of the economic crisis of the capitalist system. while these funds are not able to solve the problems of these workers in the context of unemployment in france, they at least offer the possibility of alleviating a small part of the human drama. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because the application made by france to access the globalisation fund following the 2 513 redundancies at mory-ducros sas in 84 different areas of france belonging to the land and pipeline transport sector meets the criteria required by the egf regulation. these redundancies have been the result of the global economic and financial crisis and 17% of those made redundant are people aged between 55 and 64 who need to receive training in order to be able to join new jobs and avoid remaining unemployed with a clear risk of exclusion.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report to approve the mobilisation of eur 6 052 200 from the european globalisation adjustment fund for 2513 workers who have lost their jobs at mory-ducros sas, which operates in the land transport sector; redundancies spread over 84 locations throughout mainland france. bankruptcies in the road transport sector have increased by 35% per year between 2013 and 2007 mainly as a result of the global financial and economic crisis, which between 2007 and 2012 caused a decrease in the transport of goods by road in vehicles weighing more than 3,5 tonnes by 13,7% in the eu and by 21% in france. the personalised services to be financed by the egf comprise a single action: advice and guidance for redundant workers provided by a team of expert advisers (reclassification unit). the aid, which is administered by three contractors, is designed to ensure that as many workers as possible are reintegrated into the workforce and covers as much of the french mainland as possible.

in writing. ‒ europe and the world are engaged in a profound process of globalisation which, while a source of trade and wealth creation, can also entail risks to which we must be very attentive. as a result of this process, there are sectors which are more exposed to international competition, and the eu must therefore respond to those citizens who lose their jobs as a result of globalisation. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) supports workers who lose their jobs as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns caused by globalisation (e.g. the closure of large companies or the relocation of production outside the eu) or by the global economic and financial crisis. i have therefore voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (application egf/2014/017 fr/mory-ducros).
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it gives the green light to the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) for france to facilitate the reintegration into the labour market of 2 513 workers made redundant at mory-ducros, a company operating in the land transport sector. the total amount mobilised is eur 6 052 200. the european globalisation adjustment fund was established to provide additional support for workers made redundant as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns caused by globalisation or the financial crisis and to help them find new jobs.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund. as is customary with the mobilisation of this fund, we are not opposed to it since it consists of the provision of direct aid (grants) and indirect aid (training) to workers dismissed by companies that go bankrupt because of the adjustments for industrial conversion and the volatility of certain markets, both characteristic factors of globalisation. however, in the justification we need to see these aids as simply palliatives or corrective measures applied to structurally favour the unfair and unsustainable current economic model, to the extent that they justify the continuation of the spiral of deindustrialization which has been undermining the economies of the member states.

in writing. ‒ the social protection committee is a body within the meaning of article 160 tfeu. it has an advisory role and contributes to the evaluation and monitoring of the social protection policies of the union and the member states. in practice, the role of the social protection committee is closely linked to the functions of the european semester, through which the european institutions coordinate and impose tough reforms of social protection systems on the member states, with the complicity of a majority of neoliberal governments. i cannot accept that the social protection committee serves to legitimize the erosion of democratic sovereignty, the loss of social rights and the dismantling of social services for the benefit of private capital. i have therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i believe that these types of mechanisms are necessary to advance social cohesion and a european social model that is a benchmark in the world. the competent authorities of the member states should include in their political and budgetary priorities the improvement and consolidation of social protection systems. i share the four priorities for progress at european level, but among them i would have liked to see the reference to the need to move towards a european middle-income system, which juncker has already included in his plan at our request, included in the objective of promoting social inclusion. it is the system that the basque country launched 26 years ago as the guaranteed income income, and that has made it possible to avoid social exclusion and achieve a great social cohesion, leading us to occupy the third place, after iceland and denmark, in sustainable human development. but above all, the council must make it clear whether it will respect parliament's position or what changes it will make to it if it proposes them.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the technical amendment proposed to allow the president of the social protection committee to stand for a second and final term of office. this gives greater stability to the work of this body set up to promote cooperation on social protection policies between the member states and the commission, with particular attention to promoting social inclusion and ensuring high quality and sustainable healthcare.

in writing. ‒ the social protection committee, set up by council decision 2000/436/ec - repealed and replaced by decision 2004/689/ec - has clearly demonstrated its usefulness as an advisory body for both the council and the commission. the current proposal for a council decision aims to establish a social protection committee, with an advisory role, to promote cooperation on social protection between the member states and the ec. the tasks of the committee shall be to monitor the social situation and the development of social protection policies in the member states and the union; to promote the exchange of information and good practice between the member states and the commission; and to draw up reports, deliver opinions or undertake activities in its fields of competence at the request of the council or the commission or on its own initiative. the committee will also cooperate with the social partners and inform the ep. the committee shall be composed of two representatives appointed by each member state and two representatives of the commission. the committee shall elect its chairman from among the members nominated by the member states for a term of two years, renewable once. that is why i voted in favour.
