the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' in the context of the directive. the employment committee is constituted in accordance with the mandate of article 150 tfeu. it has an advisory role and contributes to the evaluation and monitoring of the social protection policies of the union and the member states. in practice, the role of the employment committee is closely linked to the functions of the european semester, with which the european institutions coordinate and impose tough reforms of social protection systems on the member states, with the complicity of a majority of neoliberal governments. i cannot accept that the employment committee serves to legitimize the erosion of democratic sovereignty, the loss of social rights and the dismantling of social services for the benefit of private capital. i have therefore voted against.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because at this time of economic crisis and with more than 25 million unemployed in the european union, the council must say whether it will respect the position and the text adopted by parliament. and if, on the other hand, he intends to propose a new text amending the text approved by this house, he should consult the relevant bodies again. institutional respect, transparency and the need to strengthen credibility and confidence in the european institutions oblige them to do so.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the technical amendment proposed to allow the chair of the employment committee to stand for a second and final term. this gives greater stability to the work of this body, which was set up to promote coordination between member states on employment and labour market policies and to contribute to the adoption of the broad guidelines of the eu's economic policies.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the legislative resolution on the draft council decision setting up the employment committee and repealing decision 2000/98/ec as it represents a step forward in the area covered by the treaty on the functioning of the european union which provides that the union is to take the necessary measures to ensure coordination of the employment policies of the member states, to reinforce their effectiveness by developing a coordinated strategy for employment, and in particular to promote a skilled, educated and adaptable citizenry to changing productive needs, as well as to ensure the adaptability of labour markets to economic changes.
in writing. we have voted against this council proposal to extend the chairmanship of the employment committee from two to four years. the committee's main task is to adapt the proposals of the european semester to the employment policies in the member states. we have already taken a position against the european semester for proposing measures such as promoting the mobility of workers as a way of fighting unemployment, raising the retirement age, further deepening structural reforms or adjusting wages to productivity.

in writing. ‒ the tfeu provides for the establishment of an advisory committee on employment which should help ensure that the european employment strategy, the coordination of macroeconomic policies and the economic reform process are formulated and implemented in a coherent and mutually supportive manner. the proposal for a council decision aims to establish an advisory employment committee to promote coordination between member states on employment and labour market policies. the task of the committee shall be to verify the employment situation and employment policies in the member states and the union. in fulfilling its mandate, the committee shall consult the social partners and work in cooperation with other relevant bodies and committees dealing with social and economic policy issues. each member state and the commission shall appoint two members of the committee for its composition. the committee shall elect its chairman from among the members nominated by the member states for a term of two years, renewable once. the president shall be assisted by four vice-presidents. i believe that this measure can bring benefits to the implementation of the european employment strategy, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ my support for the european parliament's report on the creation of the employment committee. it is important that we put in place all the mechanisms to ensure full effectiveness and maximum coordination in the development of community employment policies, in order to help in the fight against unemployment which affects so many citizens of the european union.
in writing. ‒ as with the previous standard, i supported the proposal to set up an employment committee. it is employment that must be one of the priorities of any policy and that is why i welcome the establishment of this committee and have supported the amendment of the rules. in the previous point i already highlighted coordination between member states as an appropriate method of working in this field.

in writing. ‒ council regulation (eu) no 1311/2013 establishing the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 (mff regulation) provides for a review of that framework in the event of delays in the adoption of shared management rules or programmes. as at 31 december 2014, and due to the delay in reaching an agreement on the multiannual financial framework 2014-2020, around 300 operational programmes had not been adopted. as a result, more than €21 billion of funding for programmes such as the youth employment initiative, the european regional development fund, the european social fund, the cohesion fund, the european agricultural fund for rural development, the european maritime and fisheries fund, the asylum, migration and integration fund and the internal security fund (isf) would have been lost without this review. the revision of the multiannual financial framework in accordance with article 19 of the mff regulation allows for the transfer of appropriations not used in 2014 or extended due to the non-adoption of programmes. the report proposes to transfer these appropriations to subsequent years. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this revision.
in writing. ‒ the delayed implementation of several eu programmes (some as important as the fisheries, cohesion, social or asylum funds) has meant that many of the budgetary transfers allocated for 2014 could not be used. in this project these amounts are carried over to subsequent years, to ensure that programmes adopted in the multiannual budget can be effectively financed despite the accumulated delays. because of its technical nature and despite the limitations of the european budget, i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of amending the current multiannual financial framework to transfer the resources foreseen in 2014 to the 2015 financial year under the so-called youth guarantee. but again, this is not enough. first, let us consider that if there is this availability of funds it is because the member states spent in 2014 barely 3% of the amount available. the commission has also proposed that the commission should be able to provide the commission with a report on the implementation of the guarantee fund. finally, let us ask ourselves: what will happen to our young people after december 2015, when this modest provision of funds is over? we will be vigilant to prevent, at least in spain, the application under this guarantee of subsidies or loans which have only proved effective in reducing labour costs. we will continue to advocate a much greater increase in european and national funds, focused mainly on investment programmes in r & d & i, on socially useful public infrastructure and on generating activity from the perspective of the social and solidarity economy.

in writing. ‒ the european structural and investment funds are the most important investment policy of the european union, so it is essential that all resources are used as timely and efficiently as possible to create growth and jobs. the late adoption of the cohesion policy regulations for the period 2014-2020 prevented the timely adoption of all operational programmes, and this proposal therefore aims to transfer to 2015 virtually all the appropriations not used in 2014 that were earmarked for heading 1b, 'economic, social and territorial cohesion', with the exception of the erdf contributions to cross-border programmes under the instrument for pre-accession assistance (ipa) and the european neighbourhood instrument (evi), which were transferred to 2017. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ this amendment to the regulation establishing the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 is a purely technical amendment following the delay in the implementation of the operational programmes in 2014. however, a critical comment needs to be made. the programmes concerned are key to jobs, growth, innovation and research and have a direct impact on the development of the regions. we are talking about the european social fund, the youth employment initiative, the cohesion fund, the european regional development fund, the asylum, migration and integration fund, and others. we cannot afford such a huge loss of resources at a time of crisis like the present one; the credibility of the institutions has been affected, first by the rigidity of the old system and now by the slowness to change the procedure. and it is still a patch.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution to commemorate the centenary of the death of one and a half million innocent armenian victims, caused by the ottoman empire in 1915, because we socialists condemn all crimes against humanity. the resolution also recognises the steps taken by the current turkish government to improve the treatment of the present-day armenian minority, in the context of a freer debate on the country's past. turkey and armenia are called upon to ratify and implement the 2009 zurich protocols, to take all necessary measures to normalise their bilateral relations without preconditions and to promote educational, academic and cultural exchanges in order to foster better mutual understanding. the resolution welcomes the statements by turkish president tayyip erdogan offering his condolences and acknowledging the atrocities against the ottoman armenians, and encourages turkey to use this commemoration as an opportunity to continue its efforts to establish an objective version of what happened and thus move towards a genuine reconciliation between the peoples of turkey and armenia.
in writing. ‒ the genocide suffered by the armenian people took place exactly one hundred years ago and deserves to be commemorated. it's important to honor his victims to remember that events of this nature cannot be repeated. it is therefore necessary to stress the importance of recognizing the historical truth. the proposed resolution is not only a commemorative one but also of importance for the future of relations between armenia and turkey. in this connection, although turkey has not yet recognised this genocide, parliament welcomes the recognition of these atrocities by the president and prime minister of turkey, hoping that this will be only the first step towards the recognition of the genocide and the subsequent reconciliation between the two peoples. i have therefore voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution considering that 2015 marks the centenary of a tragic event which entails great suffering for the armenian people. today we pay tribute to the one and a half million innocent armenian victims who lost their lives amid the senselessness and barbarity of war. armenia and turkey still have a long way to go and must continue to move towards reconciliation and overcoming the terrible events that have occurred, always keeping in mind the memory of the victims based on truth and mutual respect. there will be no reconciliation without truth, and without truth neither turkey nor armenia will ever be able to overcome the terrible past they have in common.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution to commemorate the centenary of the death of one and a half million innocent armenian victims, caused by the ottoman empire in 1915, because we socialists condemn all crimes against humanity. the resolution also recognises the steps taken by the current turkish government to improve the treatment of the present-day armenian minority, in the context of a freer debate on the country's past. turkey and armenia are called upon to ratify and implement the 2009 zurich protocols, to take all necessary measures to normalise their bilateral relations without preconditions and to promote educational, academic and cultural exchanges in order to foster better mutual understanding. the resolution welcomes the statements by turkish president tayyip erdogan offering his condolences and acknowledging the atrocities against the ottoman armenians, and encourages turkey to use this commemoration as an opportunity to continue its efforts to establish an objective version of what happened and thus move towards a genuine reconciliation between the peoples of turkey and armenia.

in writing. ‒ the socialist group has always been at the forefront of the fight for roma integration and against anti-gypsyism in europe. all too often, roma people, the largest ethnic minority in the eu, live in conditions of extreme poverty and social exclusion, with limited access to employment and social services. i voted in favour of this resolution because it strongly condemns the racist and violent attacks which are still being inflicted on them. we therefore call on the european commission to monitor the respect of the fundamental rights of all eu citizens and to respond to any violations that may occur. we also call for the implementation of the european framework of national roma integration strategies to consider children and women as a priority and to develop specific measures to guarantee and improve their access to education and housing. i also believe that the recognition of the genocide suffered by the roma during the nazi regime and the establishment of a european day of remembrance of the roma holocaust are fundamental to recognising the place that this people has in our common history.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution calling for the establishment of a european day of remembrance of the gypsy holocaust, commemorating the genocide of the roma people in the nazi concentration camps on the anniversary of the murder of 2 789 roma in the auschwitz-birkenau camp in a single night, in a camp for roma and roma women known as zigeunerlager where 23 000 people were imprisoned, of whom 20 000 were killed by fascism. the roma people have so far been treated as secondary victims of fascism despite the extermination they have suffered, and this resolution seeks to put an end to this historic injustice. the resolution does not only refer to this particular period, but to the historical discrimination which this people has suffered up to the present day, and we hope that the resolution will shed some light on this. we would have liked it to be accompanied by specific measures to tackle the situation of a people with high rates of unemployment and marginalisation throughout the european union, but we agree with it because of its symbolic value and the support it brings from the gypsy social fabric.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution because it is necessary to take a stronger position in the face of the worrying rise in anti-gypsyism, which is accompanied by acts of violence, by applying framework decision 2008/913 on combating certain forms of racism and xenophobia. their situation requires more active policies by member states, with plans and strategies at national, regional and local level in which children are a priority and the special discriminatory situation of women is taken into account, in line with the european framework of national roma integration strategies. i voted against my group's position on amendments nos 1 and 2, which sought to remove the reference to the holocaust; i voted in favour of recital n and paragraph 14 of the resolution which refer to the gypsy holocaust. the reason is that this was the definition given by the united nations when they declared january 27, the day of the liberation of the auschwitz-birkenau concentration camp, as international holocaust remembrance day.

in writing. ‒ the roma people, who number between 10 and 12 million in europe, have been discriminated against for centuries in europe, because of anti-gypsyism which has manifested itself in acts of violence, exploitation and stigmatisation. the terrible stigmatization of this group is shown by the fact that, according to estimates, at least 500,000 roma were exterminated during the second world war by the nazis and other allied regimes. we must therefore acknowledge the historical fact of the genocide of the roma people that took place during the second world war. it is essential that member states effectively implement directive 2000/43/ec on the implementation of the principle of equal treatment of persons irrespective of racial or ethnic origin, in order to prevent and eliminate discrimination against the roma community, in particular in matters of employment, education and access to housing, and to actively combat manifestations of racism and xenophobia.

mr president, i will try to separate the issue of the persecution of christians from the specific issue of the terrorist attack in kenya. it is an undeniable fact that in many parts of the world, particularly in that area of the middle east, christians are subject to continuous persecution, which is dramatic for two fundamental reasons: firstly, because of the number of lives that are lost and, secondly, because it is a planned action, carried out to banish those christians from the area and to wipe out those communities. i therefore share the view that this is a dramatic matter, which requires a sensible, calm debate in this parliament. my group is prepared to have a debate on the persecution of christians in the world on the agenda of the next partsession as soon as possible. on the specific issue of the attack in kenya - as the president is well aware - we in the conference of presidents removed the term 'islamic' from the original title, so as not to present it as a religious confrontation, and it was in fact the epp group which then proposed that the subject be the persecution of christians. i think it is not appropriate to discuss this subject in this particular debate because many or some of the dead caused by that bombing were not christians. so my group proposes that we hold a debate on the persecution of christians in the world at the next partsession and not change the title of the debate on the terrorist attack in kenya.
madam president, it is obvious that we need a strategy against alcohol abuse when 25% of our young people's deaths are caused by it: at least 60 chronic diseases are recorded as being caused by it and hundreds of billions of euros are borne by the public coffers as a result. and we need -- as who says -- a roadmap where we start with clearly early action. i therefore have no doubt about the need for a strategy against alcohol abuse. but i want to stress that, the excessive consumption of alcohol, and therefore i also want to express, perhaps, the doubt i have about the inclusion in this resolution of the issue of ingredients on the labelling, or of calories. i am not against it; i think it is in favour of quality and consumer guarantees, but perhaps it is not the best time, the best document or the best solution, because it may even call into question the quality of the product itself. i would, however, ask for support for amendment no 27 on campaigns to promote alcoholic beverages, so that they respect the regulations we have in place.
madam president, i will not be the first to say that alcohol abuse is not a problem in some member states, but let us not confuse responsible drinking with abuse. ending abuse is not a matter of laws, labels, or prices, even if that is the most convenient way to ease some consciences. the best solution is education and example to minors starting with the family, but that requires more work, more dedication and more effort. in the european union we have some first-class economic sectors which grow raw materials and produce and market drinks with a higher or lower alcohol content, and they are the first to be interested in responsible consumption. we already have regulations on promotion and labelling, and wine is the most regulated agricultural product, let us not forget that. no matter how many labels and price increases there are, we are not going to prevent many young people and fewer young people from abusing alcohol, if no one has educated them in responsible consumption. pregnant women have their gynecologists, who tell them what they can and can't eat. drivers have the traffic codes. that's all i know.

member of the commission.– madam president, the landing obligation is a vital element of the reformed cfp. it aims to end the wasteful practice of discarding fish back into the sea. discarding casts a negative image on the industry, has a harmful impact on sustainable stock exploitation and marine ecosystems and affects the financial viability of fisheries. the omnibus proposal you are discussing today, and voting for on monday, is an important step and will bring legal clarity and create a level playing field for the industry in implementing the landing obligation. i want to specifically thank mr alain cadec and the shadow-rapporteurs for their very hard work and their commitment to find compromises. i am delighted that we have, in the end, reached an agreement that is acceptable to all parties. the compromise text agreed fully respects the basic elements and underlying principles of our initial proposal: to ensure legal clarity, to remove inconsistencies with the landing obligation from existing legal instruments, and to enable proper implementation of the landing obligation. but the next phase regarding demersal fisheries in the north-western waters, the south-western waters and the north sea is approaching fast, so we absolutely need the kind of legal certainty that the omnibus will now provide. i am happy to report that the development of discard plans for these fisheries is progressing very well. member states’ cooperation has evolved, learning from the first experiences with the pelagic discard plans for the 2015 landing obligation. work with the advisory councils has intensified along the way and the member state groups are now bringing them more on board in the preparation of joint recommendations. interaction between the commission and member states is also smooth and we are well on track to having plans in place before the start of next year. what about implementation so far? this is a very important element and here i have to say that we are in close contact with industry and national authorities and stand ready to assist with the policy instruments already available in our toolbox. we have also been in discussion with the pelagic advisory council to set up a committee with a hands-on assignment to closely monitor the introduction of the landing obligation. even in the absence of the omnibus regulation entering into law, we have not heard of any major problems since the start of the year. we have received and replied to a few requests for clarification from member states and the advisory councils, but these have all been relatively minor issues. cooperation seems to be good between the inspectors of the different member states regionally, and by and large our information suggests that fishermen are complying with the rules. in conclusion let me say that we are very appreciative of the responsible attitude shown by the member states and the industry so far. we hope that this will continue to be the case in the future.

madam president, commissioner, the ban on discards is a major change in the management of fisheries in europe. as has already been said, fishermen will have to make a substantial effort to adapt technically to this new arrangement, an effort which will be greater in the case of the small-scale fleet. the 'bus' regulation which we shall be voting on tomorrow aims to eliminate the contradictions between the new discard ban and the regulation on technical measures and control. after intensive negotiation, we have reached an agreement which gives some flexibility to the obligation to land all the fish caught. it must be borne in mind that the commercial outlets for fish that were previously discarded will be very limited and i believe that this parliament has made every effort to introduce into the commission's initial proposal a number of essential amendments to make it easier for the european fishing fleet to apply the new community requirement. the fisheries sector needs time to adapt. we know this well in a region like galicia, where i come from, the first fishing region in europe; the next item is the debate on the recommendation for second reading, on behalf of the committee on the environment, public health and food safety, on the council position at first reading with a view to the adoption of a directive of the european parliament and of the council amending directive 94/62/ec on packaging and packaging waste to reduce the consumption of plastic bags (05094/1/2015 - c8-0064/2015 - 2013/0371 ((cod)) (rapporteur: margrete auken) (a8-0130/2015).
madam president, commissioner, the directive we are going to adopt in parliament today is much more than an effective instrument to erase from our environmental memory the terrible picture of the sea flooded by plastic. it is true that the image is shocking at sea, but so is it on land, where each bag that is spilled takes no more and no less than 150 years to disappear. if plastic revolutionised our production and consumption model years ago, now the model change we have in store is the circular economy. and so we have a new challenge, a new revolution to do. that is why we said that this directive is more than just an instrument, it is an emblematic example of how to achieve the transition to more sustainable production, in which - from design to waste - more environmentally friendly materials are chosen, alternatives are sought, pollution is paid for and reuse and responsible collection are encouraged. we think it is a good idea to classify the bags according to their weight and use. the temporary permanence of such bags will help to achieve the desired transition, but the commission will have to ensure that alternative materials can be developed on a large scale. we are aiming to increase the number of bags per person from 200 to 40 by 2025. if it is achieved, it will mean that we have also succeeded in turning the system around and in opting for a new production model. it will be an effort for countries and consumers, but the benefits will be extensive to the entire planet.
madam president, commissioner, plastic bags - as has already been said here - are the source of many environmental problems, especially at sea. in recent years, member states and the companies concerned have made considerable efforts to reduce the consumption of handbags and many of them have taken measures to reduce their consumption. the directive aims to give the eu countries certain tools to prevent the generation of this type of waste, including a ban on free delivery of shopping bags. in my country, they are already charged in most supermarkets, and i assure you that this is an effective measure. i am also pleased that exceptions are allowed for thinner bags. these bags are indispensable for the wholesale sale of perishable food products, so it is a good decision for reasons of hygiene and food safety, and they also avoid the dispersion of food waste. their replacement, if so decided, should be done by carefully calibrating the advantages and disadvantages, in addition to the replacement materials. i would like to congratulate the rapporteur very warmly on the work she has done, and all the rapporteurs on the great fruit they have obtained from the negotiations with the council, and for ensuring that we can vote on this directive here today with a broad consensus.
madam president, commissioner, when we talk about reducing the consumption of plastic bags we are talking about improving our environment, about legislating to leave a better planet for our children. it may not seem like an interesting debate at first glance, but it is, because it affects millions of europeans every day and will have a direct impact on our daily lives. after years of struggle, we are on the verge of an agreement to reduce plastic bags, an important and necessary agreement to make progress in improving our environment, because - as the commission's own information campaign says and as has also been said here today - it takes five minutes to produce a plastic bag that will be used for five minutes, but it will take 500 years to disappear. given the disparity in situations across member states, i think it is important that they have been given the possibility to decide whether to reduce this consumption to 40 bags per person per year by 2025 or to pay for the consumption of these bags, which should come into force before the end of 2018. however, we must be vigilant to achieve real changes in habits that will get us to the goal. and i agree with mr flanagan that our grandmothers could teach us some great lessons without so much talk. in catalonia we have been working to achieve this goal since 2007, with really hopeful results, because in 2012 we already achieved a reduction of 54% and we have proposed to reach the reduction of 33 grants per person per year by the next 2020. i would not like to end without first congratulating the rapporteur, mrs auken, and the alternative rapporteurs on the excellent work they have done. i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. madam president, the gue/ngl group tabled several amendments seeking a wider development of this monitoring system; we understand that this position has been taken into account in the proposal and would like to congratulate the rapporteur on his work. in this sense, the establishment of a european monitoring system for co2 emissions from ships is therefore a first step towards reducing these and other emissions with much more determination and ambition. the collection and exchange of information must therefore be really effective, because it must be stressed - as has already been said - that greenhouse gas emissions from shipping are expected to increase at such a rate that they will counteract the effects of other measures - too timid in my view - to slow down or reduce global warming. the ultimate objective of this system is of course to help reduce marine emissions and the consumption of fossil fuels. it must therefore be, as the rapporteur points out, a first step. we must be more ambitious in regulation and objectives, and i would also like to ask the commission how it plans to accelerate or influence these negotiations in the international maritime organisation. we must also be aware that any measure will be insufficient if it is not accompanied by a thorough reflection on the global system of production, distribution and consumption.
in writing. ‒ the international convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for personnel on fishing vessels was adopted on 7 july 1995 at an international conference in london attended by more than 74 governments, including 22 of the current member states of the european union. the objective of the convention is to ensure that personnel on board fishing vessels are suitably qualified and in good health. the international convention contradicts certain points of directive 2005/36/ec, which provides for the mutual recognition of professional qualifications in the member states, by limiting such recognition to the states signatory to the convention. ratification of this convention therefore requires prior authorisation by the eu and a written commitment by the member states that, in the event of conflict, community law will prevail. this report allows the ratification of this convention by member states which have not signed it and clarifies the situation of those which have already ratified it. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution authorising member states to accede to the international maritime organisation's international convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for fishing vessel personnel, after having seen the positive recommendation of the committee on employment and social affairs. this accession will enable the groups concerned to have access to better and more harmonized training at european level.
in writing. ‒ endorsed this recommendation for a first reading and an abbreviated procedure by parliament to approve the council decision authorising member states to ratify the international convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for personnel on fishing vessels (stcw-f convention) by virtue of the eu's exclusive competence to recognise the regulated professions exercised by eu nationals on board fishing vessels. the purpose of the convention is to ensure that personnel on board fishing vessels are qualified and fit for duty so that threats to the safety of life, property at sea or the marine environment are minimised during operations on board. the provisions are mandatory for ships over 24 metres in length and with engine power of 750 kw or more and concern masters, officers, engine officers and radio operators. spain had already ratified it. parliament is recommending that a minimum level of training be set at eu level and we believe that the scope of the convention should be extended or at least that regulations should be adopted for vessels of less than 24 metres in length, and we are therefore asking the commission to legislate on this matter.

in writing. ‒ the vote on the recommendation at first reading and the shortened procedure by which parliament gives its assent to the council decision authorising the member states to ratify the stcw-f convention under the exclusive competence of the european union to recognise the regulated professions exercised by eu nationals on board fishing vessels. the objective of the stcw-f convention is to ensure that personnel on board fishing vessels are qualified (as evidenced by an official certificate) and fit for duty (after medical examination) so that potential threats to the safety of life or property at sea or to the marine environment are minimised during operations on board. the provisions are only binding on ships over 24 metres in length and with an engine power of 750 kw or more and concern masters, officers, engine officers and radio operators. the european parliament uses its co-legislative powers to recommend the establishment of a minimum level of training at eu level.

in writing. ‒ in view of the draft council decision authorising eu member states to accede to the international convention on standards of training, certification and watchkeeping for personnel on fishing vessels (stcw-f convention), i give my approval to the draft decision. this decision is based on the great importance of this convention in the field of maritime organisation. it imposes a general safety requirement, since fishing is an activity in which many deaths occur every year. measures such as monitoring the qualifications of fishermen or a minimum period of compulsory prior training for vessels over 24 metres in length are some examples of what this convention requires to improve the conditions of fishing personnel. the aim of the decision is to have the member states ratify this convention in order to have a minimum level of training and fisheries security at european level, taking into account that such training costs would not entail an increase in expenditure for the states, since the eu finances such training expenditure.

in writing. ‒ the implementation of this system may conflict with some individual rights and freedoms. for this reason, we welcome the proposed amendment which suggests that manufacturers should ensure that users of the ecall system can easily and manually deactivate the system on board their vehicles if they wish. it is necessary to create conditions for reducing road accidents by building safe roads, improving existing traffic and safety conditions and jointly promoting actions with the competent authorities to help victims. these are indispensable measures for accident prevention and assistance, and ecall is a good mechanism to help with this. that is why i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ this regulation calls for the introduction of an ecall system in cars and light commercial vehicles from 31 march 2018. it will be directly connected to the 112 emergency service in the event of a serious accident by transmitting the exact location of the vehicle, so that the number of road accidents and fatalities is expected to be significantly reduced. we have decided to vote in favour of this initiative provided that the data protection provisions are respected and users are not subject to permanent tracking.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the outcome and agreement on the development of the ecall system that we voted on today after months of work and negotiations. the protection of driver data, which is guaranteed by this agreement, is as important as the system itself, which will allow timely arrival in many accident cases. safety is first on the road.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council on type-approval requirements for the deployment of the ecall in-vehicle system and amending directive 2007/46/ec. under this proposal, by the end of march 2018 all cars and light commercial vehicles will have to be equipped with ecall devices that will automatically connect to the 112 emergency services in the event of an accident. this will improve road safety and significantly reduce the time taken for emergency services to arrive in the event of a serious accident. it is estimated that this system could save 2,500 lives each year and reduce the severity of injuries.

in writing. ‒ an agreement has finally been reached between the european parliament and the council for vehicles to be fitted as standard with a device which, in the event of an accident, automatically calls the emergency services. this will reduce the time taken to rescue and care for the injured and will reduce car crash deaths by 10%. it is therefore a major step forward in the fight against road accidents. allowing users to easily deactivate the system would render ineffective the obligation we are imposing on manufacturers. i therefore voted against the amendment which made this point. i understand the reservations raised by some colleagues about the privacy of data, but the text adopted prevents the tracing of the vehicle before the accident, prohibits the emergency services from passing on the information received to a third party and requires that data be automatically deleted from the internal memory of the device.

in writing. ‒ several of the amendments in this report significantly improve the council's position by underlining the importance of reducing energy consumption to meet the objectives of overall energy sustainability or of monitoring and monitoring the impact on ecosystems and fuelling the development of biofuels. we also value the protection of land to prevent the cultivation of biofuels from displacing local and indigenous communities. this report does not have a final vote, as it is a second reading within the tripartite dialogue process.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the adoption of the report because of the importance of the quality of fuels and renewable energies, especially in their impact on the common agricultural policy. there are four important points that will need to be negotiated with the council, namely the limitations of conventional biofuels, the factors of land use change, the target for advanced biofuels and the pursuit of a policy beyond 2020. our stance on the whole will be crucial.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of ratifying the agreement reached with the council at second reading on the amendment of the directive on the quality of petrol and diesel and the directive on the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources. the revision of those two directives was necessary to bring them into line with the new climate change objectives, in particular the mandatory target of achieving a 10% share of renewable energy in the transport sector by 2020 and a 6% reduction in the greenhouse gas intensity of road transport fuels. the agreement caps conventional (food) biofuel production at 7%, including energy crops. a binding target for advanced or second generation biofuels has not been achieved, but a recommended target of 0,5% has been achieved. in addition, the text recognises the impact on climate change of land use change for biofuels (iluc factors). although further progress could have been made in terms of the mandatory nature of iluc factors, the concept of 'low iluc biofuels' in the ep is reflected.
in writing. ‒ several of the amendments in this report significantly improve the council's position by underlining the importance of reducing energy consumption to meet the objectives of overall energy sustainability or of monitoring and monitoring the impact on ecosystems and fuelling the development of biofuels. we also value the protection of land to prevent the cultivation of biofuels from displacing local and indigenous communities. this report does not have a final vote, as it is a second reading within the tripartite dialogue process.
in writing. ‒ the aim of the proposal is to initiate the transition to a biofuels policy that will allow for significant greenhouse gas emission savings, also taking into account indirect land-use change emissions. the contribution of biofuels to the achievement of the 2020 targets is expected to be significant.
in writing. ‒ over the past decade, the eu has promoted the use of biofuels to reduce co2 emissions in transport. the result has been the development of a sector, both in agriculture and in business, capable of producing them to meet european guidelines. however, over time, it has been found that first generation biofuels have a number of environmental problems that make them less attractive. that is why i support the agreement reached by the european parliament and the council to specify that the biofuels that deserve european support are second generation biofuels, which do not have the drawbacks attributed to first generation biofuels.
in writing. ‒ we voted no to the proposal to amend certain directives because the proposals put forward by parliament, such as setting a limit of 6.5% for first generation biofuels or a binding target for the limitation of advanced biofuels, have been rejected by the council. the member states are coincidentally following the lead of the industrial lobbies, which reject any initiative aimed at reducing energy consumption in the interests of efficiency.
in writing. ‒ we voted no to the proposal to amend certain directives because the proposals put forward by parliament, such as setting a limit of 6.5% for first generation biofuels or a binding target for the limitation of advanced biofuels, have been rejected by the council. the member states are coincidentally following the lead of the industrial lobbies, which reject any initiative aimed at reducing energy consumption in the interests of efficiency.
in writing. ‒ the iluc directive has come under fire over the last five years from business-oriented industry lobbies who claim that its methodology of accounting and calculation is not adequate to meet the objective. the truth is that industry sectors do not want to endorse any political responsibilities in safeguarding soil and food crops or support a reliable improvement in reducing energy consumption. the new rapporteur assigned to the report supported parliament in demanding more ambitious targets regarding second and third generation sustainable low-ghg emission fuels. the council’s approach of a non-binding target of 0.5 % was not satisfactory, nor were other positions expressed by the council that systematically refused to negotiate or look for viable solutions within the coreper mandate. even though the provisions on low-iluc fuels have been improved to prevent loopholes and the commission can review the legislation, member states who wish to apply a cap on land-based fuels in order to comply with the fqd target will be able to do so. energy crops have been made part of the iluc legislation, correcting an omission in the original commission proposal. appropriate references to the waste framework directive have been incorporated. the result is so deceiving, that the proposed deal is not acceptable and therefore eh bildu has voted against.
in writing. ‒ the three institutions agree to put a limit on the production of conventional (food) biofuels. the commission has also proposed that the eu should be able to use the eu's own resources to support the development of the eu's energy sector. the first reading commitment agreed in the ep stated that by 2016, at least 1,25% of the total fuel had to be sourced from advanced or second generation biofuels (biomass, etc.) and that by 2020 the target was to be 2,5%. the commitment does not include a binding target for advanced countries, but does include a recommended target of 0.5%. since land use change for biofuels has an indirect impact on climate change, the commission proposed to count them in the co2 emissions calculations. the undertaking does not impose iluc factors, but does include in the above-mentioned review clause that iluc factors are taken into account when determining sustainability criteria and, in addition, the concept of 'low iluc biofuels' in the mou is included.
in writing. ‒ several of the amendments in this report significantly improve the council's position by underlining the importance of reducing energy consumption to meet the objectives of overall energy sustainability or of monitoring and monitoring the impact on ecosystems and fuelling the development of biofuels. we also value the protection of land to prevent the cultivation of biofuels from displacing local and indigenous communities. this report does not have a final vote, as it is a second reading within the tripartite dialogue process.
in writing. ‒ i support the resolution we adopted in the european parliament on the directives on the quality of petrol and diesel and the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources. we must move europe towards a biofuel policy that will allow for significant greenhouse gas emission savings, taking into account also indirect land use change emissions. as the rapporteur has said, if we do not move in this direction, europe's future in the fields of the environment, employment and investment may be threatened.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of ratifying the agreement reached with the council at second reading on the amendment of the directive on the quality of petrol and diesel and the directive on the promotion of the use of energy from renewable sources. the revision of those two directives was necessary to bring them into line with the new climate change objectives, in particular the mandatory target of achieving a 10% share of renewable energy in the transport sector by 2020 and a 6% reduction in the greenhouse gas intensity of road transport fuels. the agreement puts a 7% limit on the production of conventional (food) biofuels, including energy crops. a binding target for advanced or second generation biofuels has not been achieved, but a recommended target of 0,5% has been achieved. in addition, the text recognises the impact on climate change of land use change for biofuels (iluc factors). although further progress could have been made in terms of the mandatory nature of iluc factors, the concept of 'low iluc biofuels' in the ep is reflected.

in writing. ‒ the spanish socialists are very positive about the adoption of this new directive to reduce the consumption of plastic bags, not only to combat the high incidence and persistence of this waste in the environment, but also because the text adopted with the council is also a first and innovative step in the way of understanding our production model. for the first time, the three european institutions have been able to push forward a legal text based entirely on preventive criteria. in the case of plastic bags, our much-requested strict application of the waste hierarchy is now a reality. preventing waste is the first link in the circular economy model that we believe in and that has to be our new industrial revolution. given the wide disparities in the consumption of plastic bags between member states, measures such as the distinction of ultra-light bags, the promotion of new alternative materials, labelling to identify certain types of bags and the recommendation of a unit price at the point of sale will be, in addition to the binding targets, essential steps to achieve the minimisation of waste that the circular economy challenge imposes on us.

in writing. ‒ the average plastic bag that a european citizen throws away every year, often after only one use, is around 180 bags. these bags end up in the wild and in the seas, creating an environmental problem which the legislation i am voting for today is intended to put an end to. it is not a question of avoiding its use, but of rationalizing it. one measure that has proved effective is to charge for their use, so that consumers have a greater incentive to reuse them. in any event, if member states prefer not to apply this measure, they may apply other measures which they consider more appropriate, provided that they achieve the objective of reducing their use set out in the directive.
in writing. ‒ we voted against the proposal because the commission's position does not imply the necessary commitment to solve this serious environmental problem. measures such as reducing the average annual consumption of non-biodegradable lightweight plastic bags to 90 per capita by the end of 2019 and 40 per capita by the end of 2025, and not ensuring that the bags are not given to buyers free of charge until 2018 are seen as a lack of real commitment to the problem.

in writing. ‒ greenhouse gas emissions from shipping are expected to increase at a rate that will offset the effects of other measures to slow or reduce global warming. according to the agreed text, the regulation will establish a community system for the monitoring, reporting and verification of co2 emissions from maritime transport, in order to improve information on the efficiency of ships and emissions from the sector, and to promote the reduction of emissions and fuel consumption. this is just a first step towards reducing these and other greenhouse gas emissions from shipping. we must be much more ambitious in regulation and objectives, and the commission must negotiate in the international maritime organisation with that approach. this is the mandate which the european parliament has given to the commission and that is why we voted in favour of adopting the regulation.

in writing. ‒ this report concludes the tripartite dialogue process on improving the quality of european statistics. the changes introduced will improve the quality of statistics provided by the ine and other state statistical authorities participating in eurostat, ensure their compatibility with those developed by the banco de españa and allow the commission to monitor and inspect infringements or manipulations committed by political interference in the definition and measurement of socioeconomic variables. we appreciate the final agreement on an issue which is of particular relevance to the spanish state, because of the infringements committed in measuring the public deficit or unemployment and the dubious adjustments in indicators such as poverty or inequality, with the aim of hiding the serious consequences of the neoliberal economic model.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the parliament's recommendation for the adoption of a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 223/2009 on european statistics. the commitments made will ensure that statistics are more credible and harmonised in europe, increase transparency and prevent member states from interfering in the production of statistics. the role of the european commission and the european parliament in monitoring the appointment and functioning of the president of eurostat is also increased and the methodology for collecting information is improved. in addition, field missions will be authorised to avoid manipulation situations such as those which have occurred in the past.
in writing. ‒ this report concludes the tripartite dialogue process on improving the quality of european statistics. the changes introduced will improve the quality of statistics provided by the ine and other state statistical authorities participating in eurostat, ensure their compatibility with those developed by the banco de españa and allow the commission to monitor and inspect infringements or manipulations committed by political interference in the definition and measurement of socioeconomic variables. we appreciate the final agreement on an issue which is of particular relevance to the spanish state, because of the infringements committed in measuring the public deficit or unemployment and the dubious adjustments in indicators such as poverty or inequality, with the aim of hiding the serious consequences of the neoliberal economic model.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this regulation to improve the transparency and quality of the statistics provided to eurostat by the national and subnational agencies. the availability of high-quality statistical information, a public good in itself, is essential for economic research, financial stability and informed decision-making in the field of european public policies. this is particularly important in view of cases such as the manipulation of statistics by a member state, but also by regions, as allegedly happened in spain with the comunidad valenciana, governed by the pp since 1995, which prompted the opening of an investigation by the commission in 2014, an investigation not yet concluded. for this reason, it is essential to strengthen the independence of the state statistical agencies and to introduce the possibility of on-the-spot inspections by the commission in the member states. parliamentary control of eurostat and its coordination with the european system of central banks is also improved. i therefore believe that this regulation deserves our full support and i congratulate the rapporteur, mr hughes bayet, on the excellent work he has done.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the amendment of the regulation in accordance with the provisions of protocol no 2 on the application of the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality.
in writing. ‒ our position is in favour of this proposal, which was adopted without a vote. this is the final stage of a legislative process to ensure the independence and reliability of the statistical agencies of the various countries.

in writing. ‒ this report concerns the multiannual fisheries management plan for the baltic sea which applies to the stocks of cod, herring and sprat. this management plan replaces the previous one for cod stocks. cod, herring and sprat are important fisheries in the baltic sea. until now, there was no management plan for herring and sprat, which made it difficult to maintain sustainable stocks and stable fishing opportunities for herring fishermen. however, this plan does not sufficiently guarantee the protection of various marine species. the lower limit of the maximum sustainable yield for the adoption of delegated acts concerning specific conservation measures for the conservation of plaice, sole, turbot and whiting and to minimise incidental catch of birds, mammals or marine reptiles is not guaranteed, as the scientific opinion of ices has indicated that the current exploitation rates of some of these stocks are not consistent with the achievement of the maximum sustainable yield. however, the amendments were not adopted. that is why i voted against.
in writing. ‒ this multiannual plan is the first we have voted on since the adoption of the reform of the common fisheries policy and will set a precedent for all plans to come. i have not followed the line of my group in amendment no 30, which referred to fishing mortality and the establishment of a percentage. i agree that scientific studies should establish the situation in each fishery, but at each moment, and not by establishing a double clause. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. ‒ one of the main elements of the new common fisheries policy (cfp) is the multiannual management plans, which will allow for long-term programming and the application of the specificities of each eu region to fisheries, an essential element of the cfp's new regionalisation strategy. the multiannual plan adopted today aims to establish a single management for the cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea, through sustainable exploitation and stable fishing opportunities, ensuring management based on the latest scientific information. spain has no direct interest in this multiannual plan, but it is important because it will serve as a basis for those who will come after and for the sake of consistency in the way eu waters are managed. in this vote, the spanish socialists are advocating the establishment of a range from 0 to fmsy (maximum sustainable yield) according to the most recent scientific data.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the objective of the proposal, which is to establish a multi-species management framework for the cod, herring and sprat stocks in the baltic sea, where fishing is mainly focused on the three species mentioned. cod, herring and sprat have accounted for more than 94% of the baltic catches in recent years. it is of the utmost importance to develop regulations which take into account the interactions between the species concerned. it is necessary to monitor the rates and patterns of exploitation of these stocks in the light of advances in scientific knowledge of interactions and changes in environmental conditions.
in writing. ‒ cod, herring and sprat are important fisheries in the baltic sea. the aim of the proposal is to establish a single management plan for the baltic sea cod, herring and sprat stocks. this plan will promote the sustainable exploitation of the stocks concerned and offer stable fishing opportunities, while ensuring management based on the latest scientific information. spain has no direct interests in the baltic sea; however, this process is being followed to ensure that there is consistency in the way stocks in eu waters are managed regardless of their location. in fact, there is a widespread view that this plan is important, in that it will serve as a 'template' for those who will come after.

in writing. ‒ one of the central objectives of the reform of the current common fisheries policy is the progressive elimination of discards in all eu fisheries by introducing the landing obligation. this is designed to make better use of available resources and responds to public expectations of an end to the practice of dumping marketable fish into the sea. in addition, high levels of discards are recognised as a key point in the lack of environmental sustainability of the cfp in the impact assessment itself carried out for the cfp basic regulation. after the vote in the committee on fisheries of the european parliament and the negotiations in the tripartite dialogue, it was possible to include in the final document points which i consider very important, such as the obligation for the commission to draw up annual reports on the measures taken by the member states and producer organisations to comply with the landing obligation, on their socioeconomic impact, on safety at work on board vessels, etc., as well as other measures to make it easier for fishermen, especially small fishermen, to implement this obligation while avoiding excessive bureaucratization. i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i am pleased that the landing obligation regulation was adopted after a difficult negotiation with the council. this regulation comes from the last legislature and will only affect the landing obligation of the fisheries concerned on 1 january 2015, and the legal harmonisation of the fisheries subject to this obligation will have to be carried out subsequently in connection with the new technical measures framework that the commission has to propose in a few months.
in writing. ‒ the landing obligation is one of the cornerstones of the new common fisheries policy (cfp), which came into force at the beginning of the year and which prohibits any return of catches to sea (discharges). thus, from january 2015, and progressively according to an annual schedule established by species, fishermen are obliged to land all their catches. in order to implement this measure, it was necessary to amend certain provisions in the existing regulations on technical measures, management and control measures which are contrary to the landing obligation and oblige fishermen to discard fish. the commission has therefore put forward a proposal for a regulation which will remove, on a transitional basis, all legal and practical obstacles to its application while a new regulatory framework for technical measures is being developed. this is the omnibus regulation which we have adopted today with my vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ article 15 of the basic regulation of the common fisheries policy imposes an obligation to land all catches. this obligation will be phased in between 2015 and 2019. consequently, fishermen should land all unintended catches which are not marketable because there are no quotas or because the catches are below the minimum conservation reference size. the current rules oblige fishermen to discard non-marketable catches. this contradiction with the landing obligation should therefore be eliminated.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report, which amends the existing rules to bring them into line with the common fisheries policy. the prohibition of discard, or 'landing obligation', is a key objective of the reformed cfp, approved by the european parliament in december 2013. discards are catches that are thrown back into the sea because they are of an unacceptable/undesirable species or size. most of the fish that are thrown away die. at the same time, mechanisms are being introduced to prevent the development of a black market in illegal catches. the ultimate objective is to move towards a sustainable fisheries model compatible with the protection of the marine environment.

in writing. ‒ the new cfp prohibits all discards (returns to sea of catches that are either below the minimum size or below the quota allocated to the fisher). instead, from january 2015, and progressively according to an annual schedule established by species, fishermen are obliged to land such catches in port. however, this principle of the cfp creates certain inconsistencies arising from the fact that there is a large number of secondary regulations which directly conflict with this landing obligation. the commission has also proposed that the fishing fleet be given a licence to fish in the waters of the member states.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the implementation of the bologna process as i reject the measures being taken in its implementation, as well as strategy 2020, which leads to the commercialisation and privatisation of higher education and competition between universities. i also reject the involvement of companies in the development of educational programmes and the submission of education to the dogma of free competition and market interests. i believe that the responsibility for the education system should lie with the state and that it is the member states which should ensure genuine recognition of diplomas. the budget for education and research must be increased, as must the number and amount of grants. i am also convinced that educational diversity, including linguistic diversity, must be respected in europe. i therefore, as a supporter of universal, free, quality public education, which meets the needs of society and not the needs of the market, had no choice but to vote against this report on the bologna process.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the follow-up report on the implementation of the bologna process, as the lybacka report reflects the current situation and the development of the process which at one time generated much criticism and tension in the european education sector. the future of europe lies in young people who must have access to the best quality higher education systems.
in writing. ‒ the bologna process was born with the aim of ensuring a coherent, transparent and high quality higher education, guaranteeing high common standards to facilitate student mobility. although 47 countries are now involved and some of the objectives have been achieved, there is still a long way to go in achieving these objectives, while new challenges have emerged, such as the very high level of youth unemployment, economic constraints and demographic changes, which call for further developments. the report, which was initiated by the s&d group, calls for an objective and critical review of progress and setbacks in the achievement of the priorities set for the period 2012-2015 in order to further consolidate the european higher education area, to boost the bologna process in the face of new challenges such as those described and to encourage higher targets, with the involvement and commitment of all stakeholders, including social partners. i have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ the bologna process aimed to create a european higher education area by 2010. the aim is to provide students with a wider and more transparent offer of quality educational opportunities, as well as to create a simplified process of recognition, both internal and external, in all national higher education systems. it is necessary to continue the implementation of bologna to create the conditions for greater mobility, to adapt education systems to labour market needs and to improve overall employability and competitiveness.
in writing. ‒ we voted out of this report, which seeks to give impetus to the bologna process, and we oppose it because its 'major objectives' - the establishment of a european higher education area which harmonises its administrative and curricular procedures, facilitates mobility and adapts the training criteria to the new global challenges - mask a change in priorities: from being a knowledge-generating entity at the service of society to being, as in all areas likely to generate profit, at the service of economic profitability as defined by the markets, disregarding the effect of this criterion in increasing social inequality.
in writing. ‒ the bologna process is a joint effort to make it possible to compare the quality of higher education qualifications in the 29 participating countries. since its creation in 1999, it has contributed to the launch of the european higher education area, the recognition of diplomas and thus to student mobility within the eu and the participating countries. despite these achievements, much remains to be done. in particular, education systems need to be adapted to the labour market, young people's skills for employment need to be improved and the attractiveness of higher education in europe needs to be increased. since some five million young people under 25 are unemployed in the eu, one of the main priorities of the bologna process should be to develop the highest possible level of knowledge for citizens through broad access to education that addresses youth unemployment and the skills supply/demand mismatch.
in writing. ‒ we voted out of this report, which seeks to give impetus to the bologna process, which we oppose, because its 'major objectives' - the establishment of a european higher education area that harmonises its administrative and curricular procedures, facilitates mobility and adapts the training criteria to the new global challenges - mask a change in priorities: from a knowledge-generating entity at the service of society to being, as in all areas likely to generate profit, at the service of economic profitability as defined by the markets, disregarding the effect of this criterion on the increase of social inequality.

in writing. ‒ in the vote on the follow-up to the implementation of the bologna process, i voted against the european parliament resolution, as the text supports or feeds the trend towards a higher education system marked by cuts and privatisations, obsessed with competitiveness, which results in young people trapped by full-time and drowned by fees that many and many can no longer afford. eh bildu advocates a truly unique educational model, of quality, inclusive, non-exclusive and participatory, capable of creating critical students; a model where the right to study fully in basque in all cycles of education is fully guaranteed. i therefore voted in favour of the alternative text proposed by the gue/ngl group, a full amendment to the whole of the resolution adopted.
in writing. ‒ the s&d group decided to draw up this own-initiative report in order to give the ep a clear position before the next ministerial conference on the bologna process in yerevan, armenia, in may 2015, as it is important to carry out an objective and critical review of the progress and setbacks in the achievement of the priorities set for the period 2012-2015 in order to further consolidate the european higher education area (ehea) and to boost the bologna process in the face of new challenges (such as high youth unemployment, economic constraints and demographic changes). the report focuses on assessing the process and identifying key priorities for the coming years, building on appropriate political commitment and cooperation from the eees, strengthening the bottom-up approach, developing new tools and methods, as clusters to help countries facing challenges, and encouraging others to reach higher targets, with the involvement and commitment of all stakeholders, including social partners.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the implementation of the bologna process as i reject the measures being taken in its implementation, as well as strategy 2020, which leads to the commercialisation and privatisation of higher education and competition between universities. i also reject the involvement of companies in the development of educational programmes and the submission of education to the dogma of free competition and market interests. i believe that the responsibility for the education system should lie with the state and that it is the member states which should ensure genuine recognition of diplomas. the budget for education and research must be increased, as must the number and amount of grants. i am also convinced that educational diversity, including linguistic diversity, must be respected in europe. i therefore, as a supporter of universal, free, quality public education, which meets the needs of society and not the needs of the market, had no choice but to vote against this report on the bologna process.
in writing. ‒ in june 1999, 29 european countries signed the bologna declaration, which set the goal of creating a european higher education area (ehea) by 2010. this proposal calls on the member states, the eees countries and the eu as a whole to foster public understanding and support for the bologna process, including the core measures, in order to achieve a more effective and dynamic participation in the achievement of its objectives. i voted in favour of this proposal because i believe that increased investment in education is essential to effectively combat poverty, social inequalities and unemployment, particularly youth unemployment, and to promote social integration.
in writing. ‒ the bologna declaration and the creation of a european higher education area have made it possible to provide students with a wider and more transparent offer of quality educational opportunities, as well as to create a simplified process of recognition, both internal and external, of all existing national higher education systems. however, i agree with the report we adopted in the european parliament's plenary that the achievements of this process have been uneven in the participating countries and that there is a need to improve in this respect, as well as to establish new instruments and working methods to further improve. it is also essential to move towards more student-centred learning and to ensure that adequate funding is in place to achieve all the bologna objectives. i think that the report we have adopted, which i also supported, gives a magnificent overview of the achievements and the challenges still to be met, and i hope that its conclusions will be taken into account.
in writing. ‒ in june 1999, a total of 29 european countries signed the bologna declaration. the aim was to establish a european higher education area (ehea) with a wider and more transparent offer of quality educational opportunities and to foster labour and citizen mobility. however, in countries like spain, bologna has served as a pretext for policies that have damaged equal opportunities. university fees are much higher and postgraduate or master's scholarships have been abolished, while the list of european accreditations is very short and it is as difficult as ever to homologate degrees between eu countries. only talent can bring prosperity and bring the countries of the union out of the crisis with dignity, and that is why we must denounce the fact that we have not been efficient so far.
in writing. ‒ i support the report assessing the bologna process in the field of education, as i consider the trans-parency of education systems and european cooperation in education to be one of the key areas of european integration. i am personally reluctant to try to make all subjects compulsory for bachelor's and subsequent master's studies, but in general i consider the progress in the bologna process to be positive and worthy of further support.
in writing. ‒ the bologna process was born with the aim of ensuring a coherent, transparent and high quality higher education, guaranteeing high common standards to facilitate student mobility. although 47 countries are now involved and some of the objectives have been achieved, there is still a long way to go in achieving these objectives, while new challenges have emerged, such as the very high level of youth unemployment, economic constraints and demographic changes, which call for further developments. the report, which was initiated by the s&d group, calls for an objective and critical review of progress and setbacks in the achievement of the priorities set for the period 2012-2015 in order to further consolidate the european higher education area, to boost the bologna process in the face of new challenges such as those described and to encourage higher targets, with the involvement and commitment of all stakeholders, including social partners. i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ we voted out of this report, which seeks to give impetus to the bologna process, and we oppose it because its 'major objectives' - the establishment of a european higher education area that harmonises its administrative and curricular procedures, facilitates mobility and updates the training criteria to meet new global challenges - mask a change in priorities: from a knowledge-generating entity at the service of society to being, as in all areas likely to generate profit, at the service of economic profitability as defined by the markets, disregarding the effect of this criterion on the increase of social inequality.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the implementation of the bologna process as i reject the measures being taken in its implementation, as well as strategy 2020, which leads to the commercialisation and privatisation of higher education and competition between universities. i also reject the involvement of companies in the development of educational programmes and the submission of education to the dogma of free competition and market interests. i believe that the responsibility for the education system should lie with the state (or the level of government that has the competence depending on the member state) and that it is the member states that should ensure genuine recognition of diplomas. the budget for education and research must be increased, as must the number and amount of grants. i am also convinced that educational diversity, including linguistic diversity, must be respected in europe. i therefore, as a supporter of universal, free, quality public education, which meets the needs of society and not the needs of the market, have had no choice but to vote against this report on the bologna process.

in writing. ‒ access to education should not only be universal but it must be good in order to be more competitive as a society and avoid the high rates of unemployment that exists in some european countries. the bologna process and the europe 2020 strategy must face the inadequacy of current occupational qualifications, as one of three employers find cannot find skilled workers in some sectors. mobility, internationalization, and support to university education between eu countries should give the same equal opportunities for european citizens. needed reforms must be taken as soon as possible so that will be a benefit to us all, that is why i supported this resolution. i encourage all institutions and governments involved in making this possible.
