in writing. ‒ this report responds to a european commission communication entitled 'european cinema in the digital age: building bridges between cultural diversity and competitiveness'. while i reject the approach of commodification of culture, i have supported this report from parliament which, unlike the european commission's communication, which emphasises the competitiveness aspects of the film industry, stresses the importance of the cultural aspect and calls for increased public funding for this sector. i am also convinced of the importance of preserving europe's cultural heritage by digitising its cinema, promoting the cultural and linguistic diversity of films. i therefore decided to vote in favour of the report, since it improves the approach of the european commission by moving away from the logic of consumerism and emphasizing the importance of promoting cultural education in schools and non-formal institutions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on european cinema in the digital age because of the importance of this industry in economic activity. the european film industry needs to continue developing innovative services, new business models and distribution channels to improve the cross-border availability of european films in the union and to allow viewers across the union to access an ever-growing catalogue of films through an increasing number of platforms. it also proposes that the european film industry should learn from best practice outside the union.
in writing. ‒ the european film industry is diverse and creative and has great potential, as it is a successful and inspiring film heritage worldwide, and as it has the capacity to generate growth and jobs. however, the industry faces new opportunities and challenges in the face of the digital revolution, which requires adaptability to develop innovative services, new business models and better distribution channels to reach new and wider audiences. the resolution recognises the impact of illegal content use on the creative cycle and on creators' rights, and highlights the need to combat such use, while calling for the development of more quality legal offerings and greater awareness, especially among young people, of illegal use. it also called on the member states to promote initiatives to facilitate the production, distribution, availability and attractiveness of european films, and considered that the application of reduced vat rates to cultural audiovisual works could promote the growth of new services and new platforms. i have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report by the european parliament's culture committee, which is being presented in the context of a debate on the promotion of european cinema initiated by a commission communication. the debate is framed by the increased distribution of american films and the dilemmas that new distribution methods create for filmmakers. the european commission's position placed a strong emphasis on promoting a model favourable to large industry and focused on co-financing film production. this resolution avoids the most controversial points as far as the business model is concerned. however, it promotes public support for the distribution and promotion of films and encourages the access of all citizens to culture through subtitling, the creation of public archives, etc.

in writing. ‒ forests cover more than 40% of the eu's surface and are an essential resource for improving quality of life and creating jobs, particularly in rural areas, while maintaining ecosystems and combating climate change. the amendments reflected the need to put social and environmental improvement criteria above the logic of financial gain, agroforestry activities, biodiversity and the multifunctional nature of forests, the creation of specific support measures to prevent and combat fires that allow early intervention, avoiding soil erosion, and the recovery of vegetation cover. in the end, the vast majority of our amendments were rejected by the committee, although some improvements were made to the original document, and we therefore abstained in the final vote.
in writing. ‒ the european forestry strategy highlights the importance of forests and forestry not only from an environmental point of view but also from an economic and social point of view. it also proposes to improve the coordination of the various european policies involved (energy, research and development, employment, climate, etc.) so as to encourage the creation of a more coherent approach. we have therefore decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ in september 2013, the european commission published a communication entitled 'sustaining forests and the forestry sector: a new approach for a new eu forestry strategy', which revises and updates the 1998 strategy. the european forest strategy sets targets for 2020, including the sustainable management of forests and the reduction of deforested or degraded land, and sets out a number of priority areas for action, such as coordination and communication on forest-related issues, support for rural and urban society from the forestry sector, improving the competitiveness of goods and services generated by forests, the relationship between forest area and climate change, and the development of innovative initiatives in the sector. the resolution on a new eu strategy for forests and the forestry sector calls for a new strategy focused on coordination, so that forestry and forests fit better into the different european policies (energy, environment and climate protection, and r & d) and a more coherent approach can be defined, for which it calls for the strengthening of the standing forestry committee. that is why i voted in favour.

mr president, as regards the document, i agree with the substance, but not with the form. it is not just a matter of being able to listen, mr vice-president and commissioner, but of being able to read. and i cannot argue that the commission approved it three minutes ago, at this very moment, half an hour ago. no, no, because the media is summoned for immediately after. we want to read the document in depth. so, after a cursory reading, what can i say? i can say that i agree with what are called the 'threat priorities', that is terror, organised crime and cybercrime. i also agree with the five lines underlying the philosophical principles, of course: fundamental rights, democratic control and transparency, making the most of existing instruments, coordination of internal and external policies, and strengthening the control and cooperation of the european agencies, which are too many in the field of security and not all of them are well coordinated. i approve the budget, but i think it is insufficient. not enough for what? insufficient because we have to present, mr commissioner, mr vice-president, as soon as possible, the internal security strategy 2015-2019. it is a commitment which must be fulfilled as soon as possible, as a complement to the agenda. and to conclude, a curiosity. look, in the 25 pages, the words "fundamental rights" are mentioned 27 times - that's very good - "border control" once, "migration" three times, "human trafficking" eight times, and "pnr" 14 times. that is a very hasty analysis. the machine - the machine - has given me this answer. but in any case, as soon as possible, mr vice-president and commissioner, the internal security strategy 2015-2019.
madam president, i would like to express our support for the creation of this european prosecutor's office because it will help to prosecute corruption offences that harm the european union better, more independently and more effectively. i propose and will support that the prosecution of crossborder crimes committed by international terrorism be incorporated into its functions. i am in favour of the collegiate structure proposed by the commission if we really want independence: i believe it will encourage police coordination by avoiding incomprehensible vetoes in investigations of terrorism and fraud affecting the union. i hope that there will be no more embarrassing spectacles at european level, such as those in spain, and that this will provide a contrast which will help to improve the situation. there, the proximity of the accused to the party of the government generates scandalous favourable deals and even leads to the possibility of erasing, in full judicial instruction, the files of the computers in which the treasurers of the popular party presumably kept all their accounting. it's our responsibility to address these issues.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used effectively. mr president, i would first like to say that i am pleased to note that this year the budget implementation rate for the erasmus+ and creative europe programmes 2007-2013 was 100%. but on the other hand, in relation to other programmes of the committee on culture and education, i note that unfortunately europe for citizens, which is a direct link between the european union and the citizens in supporting actions, petitions and civil rights, has an excessively low level of funding at present. i am also concerned that, as mentioned in a eurobarometer report on access to culture, public budgets for the safeguarding and promotion of cultural heritage are falling significantly at european level. i therefore believe that it is necessary to strengthen the union's instruments to support the european agenda for culture.

mr president, commissioner, i am of course in favour of this reform of the european social fund regulation to speed up the implementation of the european plan to promote youth employment: that is our priority. i am, however, missing a more rigorous analysis by the commission of the reasons why the member states with the most difficulties have not succeeded in presenting more operational programmes, and i repeat here that, on many occasions, the problem is that some states are tempted to centralize these programmes and to distance them from the regional institutions which have the competence, which are closer to the real economy and have the greater capacity to drive it forward, which have more practice and which have a better scale to achieve public-private partnerships, which work better and have better results. so, advance funds, yes, but auditing these kinds of problems and encouraging them to be corrected, too. i would therefore like to ask you whether you intend to carry out any analysis of these characteristics.
mr president, i want to make it clear in my speech that we are not against the youth guarantee programme, but we do not share the way it is being implemented in certain countries, including spain. we value prefinancing, but this is not the main problem, nor are active policies in the evolution of youth unemployment. the problems are correlated with the decline in economic activity, which hinders the integration of young people into the labour market. the problems of youth unemployment are not solved by lowering social security contributions or subsidizing entrepreneurs. these measures do not guarantee continuity in employment or on-the-job training; in short, they do not guarantee quality employment. the commission itself has already warned certain countries that this programme has had only a marginal effect and the court of auditors' own report warns of the risks of a bad implementation of the programme. if we are to create quality employment, it will have to be, among other things, through productive investment and increased wages and social benefits.

is the youth employment initiative budget alone enough to create all those jobs and put young people in the driver's seat? is the youth employment policy we have in europe sufficient? no, of course that's not enough. we will not get there with the youth employment initiative alone. that is why we have other funds at our disposal. in many countries and regions, however, there was a financial barrier to getting projects off the ground. the increase in prefinancing removes this financial obstacle and they can really get going. so this should help. but beyond that, we have resources from the esf, resources from the european regional fund, resources to invest in people - including young people - in the employment and social innovation (easi) programme and resources in erasmus+ and a number of other programmes. nor is the policy itself enough. employment is a question of supply and demand. we need to work on both fronts. that is why this commission is devoting all its policies to creating sustainable growth and job creation. that is why we will be working on initiatives to help the longterm unemployed get back to work, to better match skills to needs, to ensure that there is more respect for vocational training, that there is better vocational training available to young people, that there is a good labour market policy in the member states and things like that. our investment package must also be seen in that light. if everyone in the field takes responsibility, then we can do something and give those young people a new perspective. i'm sure you will. the proposal you have so broadly supported here today will enable us to make a major contribution to this. i would like to thank you again for that and congratulate you again on the speed with which you have moved this through parliament.

in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the commission's discharge for 2013 because, in trying to approve the management of the barroso commission which no longer exists before the incoming commission, the reasonable thing was to limit ourselves to taking stock, expressing our concerns, acknowledging progress and making the necessary recommendations. but the rapporteur, who was the chairwoman of the committee on transport and tourism, did not see it that way. although the socialist amendments have improved the text as much as possible, we regret that we were unable to prevent by 37 votes, including those of the spanish people's delegation, the biased and partisan use of an obsolete olaf report to criticise the aid to the tindouf camp on which more than 90,000 lives depend. it is intolerable that a closed inquiry, ten years later, should be resurrected with a hidden political will, an inquiry which concluded that there was no need for administrative or budgetary measures and which, on the contrary, helped to strengthen the real demands of the population of the sahrawi refugee camps. the olaf in 2007, the commission itself and the un have now repeatedly recognised both the emergency and the need for the aid and the proper management of it.

in writing. ‒ the spanish socialist delegation voted in favour of the adoption of this legislative report, as the measure proposed by the commission involves increasing the resources that the european institutions advance to the member states to implement the youth employment initiative. this will increase the money coming to the emn in 2015 by 1 billion, helping to tackle the problems of financing the start of operational programmes, which many of the countries with the worst youth unemployment problems have had so far, including spain. in the spanish case, it will go from receiving just €9.5 million to receiving almost €285 million during 2015, which should also increase the number of young people benefiting from the measure. the european institutions have worked with agility to accelerate this flow of resources, now it is the turn of the emn to take advantage of these measures. however, funds are still insufficient and the substance of the macroeconomic policies pursued so far by the european institutions must be changed if we are to tackle one of the worst tragedies of the economic crisis, namely youth unemployment.
in writing. ‒ the european union youth employment initiative acts as an umbrella for a range of policies aimed at ensuring young people's access to employment and training. however, its implementation is being highly controversial due to the slow and lack of coherence in the implementation of the programs associated with it. the use of the funds as a business subsidy for recruitment, as in spain, is also controversial, both for reasons of distribution and for its ineffectiveness in creating youth employment. it should not be forgotten that without a policy of productive transformation based on public investment, youth unemployment will retain its structural character. however, training and learning policies can help to mitigate some of their effects, and i have therefore voted in favour of the funding for these programmes, as proposed in the report. in any case, it is necessary for the european commission to carry out an impact study of this initiative, assessing and recommending best practice in the field of training and learning and ensuring the involvement of trade unions in its implementation.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of this legislative report, as the measure proposed by the commission involves increasing the resources that the european institutions advance to the member states to implement the youth employment initiative. this will increase the money coming to the emn in 2015 by 1 billion, helping to tackle the problems of financing the start of operational programmes, which many of the countries with the worst youth unemployment problems have had so far, including spain. in the spanish case, the amount will increase from a meagre €9.5 million to almost €285 million in 2015, which should translate into an increase in the number of young people benefiting from the measure. the european institutions have worked with agility to accelerate this flow of resources, now it is the turn of the emn to take advantage of these measures. however, funds are still insufficient and a change of perspective is needed on the underlying policies being implemented by the european institutions and some member states in relation to youth unemployment.
in writing. ‒ decisive action is needed to combat youth unemployment, especially as the rate of youth unemployment has been dramatic for years. the youth employment initiative is one of the eu's tools for implementing the objectives of the youth guarantee in those states most affected by the crisis. unfortunately, it has not been used sufficiently by the member states so far, since the member states most affected by youth unemployment are also those which have the greatest difficulty in finding co-financing. the commission has decided to make progress in unlocking this situation by €1 billion, an amount which must now be used by the member states to help youth employment.

in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the release of eur 1 billion for prefinancing the operational programmes of the youth employment initiative, from 10% to 30% of prefinancing. we believe that the youth employment initiative is not the right plan to tackle the problem of youth unemployment because the diagnosis it starts with is wrong, as it starts from the basis that young people are not active enough in finding jobs or are not sufficiently trained, thus blaming young people for not having jobs. even though we do not agree with the plan, we have voted in favour of it because the release of funds can help the concrete operational programmes to work and help young people to find quality employment.

in writing. ‒ this is a first reading report by the european parliament, which was dealt with under the urgency procedure. it aims to increase imminently the disbursement of money committed by the european social fund to member states under the youth employment initiative during the current financial year 2015. the commission has proposed from the outset special measures to implement the advance commitments in the first two years of the programming period (2014-2020) in order to accelerate their implementation, by requiring these programmes to be implemented in 2018 instead of 2023, due to the urgency of the youth unemployment situation. the shorter implementation timeframe of the yei implies that the process of implementation on the ground in the first few years is crucial to the overall success of the initiative. after the first year of implementation, the european commission has found that, despite these special implementation measures, implementation is not proceeding at the expected rate.
in writing. ‒ the european union youth employment initiative acts as an umbrella for a range of policies aimed at ensuring young people's access to employment and training. however, its implementation is being highly controversial due to the slow and lack of coherence in the implementation of the programs associated with it. the use of the funds as a business subsidy for recruitment, as in spain, is also controversial, both for reasons of distribution and for its ineffectiveness in creating youth employment. it should not be forgotten that without a policy of productive transformation based on public investment, youth unemployment will retain its structural character. however, training and learning policies can help to mitigate some of their effects, and i have therefore voted in favour of the funding for these programmes, as proposed in the report. in any case, it is necessary for the european commission to carry out an impact study of this initiative, assessing and recommending best practice in the field of training and learning and ensuring the involvement of trade unions in its implementation.
in writing. ‒ an increase in the amount of initial funding for programmes implemented under the youth employment initiative means that more funds are allocated to these programmes, as they are particularly needed to tackle the problem of high youth unemployment in those member states with a youth unemployment rate of over 25%. the measures to be taken will focus on the most vulnerable groups of young people and those most at risk of being disadvantaged in terms of employment. not only are follow-up actions carried out by these programmes, but also great importance is attached to the receipt of effective training by young people to try to have a good future employment situation. it is true that various measures have already been taken at european level to try to improve the situation in this area, but there is still a need for further measures which could be achieved by this 30% increase in the initial pre-financing of programmes supported by the employment initiative. i therefore approve the proposal for that regulation.

in writing. ‒ regulation 3030/93 defined rules applicable to imports of certain textile products originating in third countries with which the european union has concluded agreements. the provisions of the regulation had finally become obsolete as a result of russia's accession to the wto, the signing of the association agreement with serbia and the expiry of the safeguard clause on textile imports from china. european trade policy is to blame for the aggressive tariff dismantling of the textile sector. the internationalisation of the production chain has dealt a severe blow to the european industrial fabric, while leaving many developing countries dependent on a sector known for its aggressive and even slave-like practices towards workers. however, as this is a purely technical report, i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report by which the commission proposes to repeal regulation (eec) no 3030/93 on the common rules for imports of certain textile products from third countries, which applies to imports of textile products originating in third countries with which the eu has concluded bilateral agreements, signed protocols or established other arrangements. in recent years, the european union has maintained bilateral agreements on trade in textile products only with russia and serbia. after russia's accession to the wto and the entry into force of the stabilisation and association agreement with serbia, the regulation has lost its main purpose. in order to enhance legal certainty and to simplify and clarify european legislation, so that it is more accessible and understandable to the citizen, this regulation should be repealed.

in writing. ‒ under the treaties, the european parliament has the right to scrutinise the legality and regularity of the implementation of the expenditure of the european institutions and agencies each year. the main objective of exercising this right is to ensure that public funds are used in the best possible way. this scrutiny is based on the report of the european court of auditors, a written question and answer procedure and, finally, the public hearings of the institutions and agencies before the european parliament. this report refers to 26 special reports of the court of auditors on the implementation of the funds and assesses some heterogeneous programmes and cross-cutting issues. parliament has not detected any irregularities in the implementation of the budget of any of them, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the commission's discharge for 2013 because, in trying to approve the management of the barroso commission which no longer exists before the incoming commission, the reasonable thing was to limit ourselves to taking stock, expressing our concerns, acknowledging progress and making the necessary recommendations. but the rapporteur, who was the chairwoman of the committee on transport and tourism, did not see it that way. although the socialist amendments have improved the text as much as possible, we regret that we were unable to prevent by 37 votes, including those of the spanish people's delegation, the biased and partisan use of an obsolete olaf report to criticise the aid to the tindouf camp on which more than 90,000 lives depend. it is intolerable that a closed inquiry, ten years later, should be resurrected with a hidden political will, an inquiry which concluded that there was no need for administrative or budgetary measures and which, on the contrary, helped to strengthen the real demands of the population of the sahrawi refugee camps. the olaf in 2007, the commission itself and the un have now repeatedly recognised both the emergency and the need for the aid and the proper management of it.

in writing. ‒ the report proposes discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the eighth, ninth and tenth european development funds for the financial year 2013. the court of auditors' report shows that the annual accounts are true, legal and regular in all material respects and that there is continuing improvement in the monitoring and supervision of management, with an estimated low error rate. from a purely technical point of view, the report deserves our approval. however, the report contains political assessments which we do not share. in particular, it insists on strengthening the conditionality of aid according to macroeconomic criteria which force governments to adopt neoliberal policies contrary to the interests of their populations or by reinforcing bureaucratic decision-making and monitoring processes which may prove unacceptable to the resources or sovereignty of the recipient states. on the contrary, it hardly touches on the necessary duty of solidarity in development aid or on the eu's shortcomings in this regard. for all these reasons, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour as the court of auditors has found that the final annual accounts of the 8th, 9th and 10th edfs for the financial year 2013 present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the edfs as at 31 december 2013 and that their operating results, cash flows for the year and changes in net assets at the end of the year are in accordance with the provisions of the edf financial regulation and with internationally accepted accounting standards for the public sector. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any information on the amount of the aid granted to the beneficiary.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the approval of parliament's accounts because, through this procedure, we seek to improve its internal functioning and efficiency year after year, and to ensure that the budget allocated to this institution is used in the most correct way. this time we showed the citizens that in 2013 we saved 5% on the travel expenses of the deputies, we managed the audiovisual media better as well as an improvement in the interpretation and translation budget without sacrificing quality and multilingualism. it has also enabled us to identify areas where urgent changes are needed, such as the underrepresentation of women in management positions. we particularly welcome the fact that for the first time there is a new mandate to manage the allowances for members' general expenses with greater transparency, a mandate to which the pp and many delegations had always shown enormous resistance. it has been achieved thanks to an initiative led by our group which for the first time, beyond vague promises of greater transparency, gives a mandate with broad support from all the groups for the bureau to present more precise rules for the accountability of these diets.
in writing. ‒ under the treaties, the european parliament has the right to scrutinise the legality and regularity of the implementation of the expenditure of the european institutions and agencies each year. the main objective of exercising this right is to ensure that public funds are used in the best possible way. this scrutiny is based on the report of the european court of auditors, a written question and answer procedure and, finally, the public hearings of the institutions and agencies before the european parliament. parliament has not detected any irregularities in the implementation of the european parliament's budget, which is why i voted in favour of giving discharge.

in writing. ‒ the report proposes discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the european external action service for the financial year 2013. however, there are serious doubts about staff qualifications, liability and pay - which had already been highlighted in previous years - and delays in the implementation of internal or anti-fraud rules. some of the report's assessments, such as the simplification and flexibility of the eeas' administrative and financial obligations in its missions, will not only not solve these problems, but will aggravate the opacity of the functioning of european foreign policy. nor do we agree with the specific references to the lines of intervention of the eeas, because they set political objectives outside the budgetary review; and it is particularly worrying that the independence of european foreign policy is being strengthened outside any effective democratic scrutiny. i therefore voted against the report.
in writing. ‒ i support the report for its timely observations on staff structure, transparency measures, excessive number of senior officials and geographical balance of service components. i think it is very important to call for an effective equality policy because the current ratios are very bad, especially at the top management level (42 men and 4 women). i reiterate my concern about the real estate policy of this service and the procurement of security systems and services.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report because the european external action service has continued to implement its budget without the court of auditors having detected any major errors; progress has been made in correcting errors found in previous years, which were mainly the result of the creation of the service. the report also welcomes the suggestions made by the court of auditors on improvements which are expected to be implemented as soon as possible.

in writing. ‒ under the treaties, the european parliament has the right to scrutinise the legality and regularity of the implementation of the expenditure of the european institutions and agencies each year. the main objective of exercising this right is to ensure that public funds are used in the best possible way. this scrutiny is based on the report of the european court of auditors, a written question and answer procedure and, finally, the public hearings of the institutions and agencies before the european parliament. during the proceedings, parliament detected irregularities, in particular with regard to aspects such as the external activities of judges and the case of two retired translators who were subsequently awarded contracts. since the court of justice was unable to clarify these points, i have voted against giving the consent.
in writing. ‒ i share the observations made on the external activities of the court's judges and, in particular, the call to activate the entire digitisation project of the administrative and technical services of this institution. it is very important that the recommendation on respect for multilingualism, which is fundamental to guaranteeing equal opportunities for actors, is supported and respected. i share the call for spending on staff working outside the office to be limited, giving priority to the use of in-house facilities or the use of telematic means. i hope that the gender imbalance in this institution (70-30%) will be addressed once and for all.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report as the court of auditors has noted that no significant deficiencies have been identified in the human resources and tendering cases examined by the court of justice of the european union and that the total payments for the year ended 31 december 2013 for administrative and other expenditure of the institutions and bodies are free from material error. in addition, the court of justice has committed itself to further improving its system for the timely supervision and control of staff selection and public procurement procedures. it is also worth noting that the court of justice has prepared a detailed and comprehensive annual activity report and has included full information on its human resources management, in response to parliament's request.

in writing. ‒ i have supported this report as the court of auditors observed in its annual report for the financial year 2013 that no significant deficiencies were identified with regard to the issues examined concerning human resources and public procurement of the committee of the regions and concluded that the payments for the financial year ended 31 december 2013 for administrative and other expenditure of the institutions and bodies are free from significant errors. however, given the delay in adopting the internal rules on the procedures for reporting irregularities, it called on the committee to apply these rules without further delay.

in writing. ‒ i have supported this report as the court of auditors observed in its annual report for the financial year 2013 that the total payments for the administrative and other expenditure of the european data protection supervisor for the financial year ended 31 december 2013 were free from material error and that the control and monitoring systems for administrative and other expenditure were effective, and concluded that no significant deficiencies had been identified with regard to the issues examined concerning the human resources and public procurement of the supervisor. in addition, it is appreciated that the supervisor followed the observations included in the resolutions of the parliament on discharge in the financial years 2010 and 2012 in order to develop its strategy 2013-2014. however, it should be noted that the supervisor should pay more attention to the principle of sound financial management in relation to the principle of annuality in budgetary programming, that is, as regards economy, efficiency and effectiveness in using the appropriations at its disposal to carry out the tasks assigned to it.

in writing. ‒ i have supported this report because the court of auditors has observed how improvements have been implemented on observations made in previous years. the budget monitoring efforts throughout the financial year 2013 resulted in a budget implementation rate of 98,80%, representing a slight decrease compared to the previous year (99,30%), while the payment appropriations execution rate was high at 90,80%. according to the authority's annual report, the budget was fully implemented in titles i (personnel) and ii (infrastructure), while in title iii (operations) the implementation rate reached 96,99%.

in writing. ‒ under the treaties, the european parliament has the right to scrutinise the legality and regularity of the implementation of the expenditure of the european institutions and agencies each year. the main objective of exercising this right is to ensure that public funds are used in the best possible way. this scrutiny is based on the report of the european court of auditors, a written question and answer procedure and, finally, the public hearings of the institutions and agencies before the european parliament. parliament has not detected any irregularities in the implementation of the budget of the european railway agency (era), which is why i voted in favour of approving the management of the budget.

in writing. ‒ the report proposes a new regulation for money market funds. the review was necessary in view of the risks identified for the financial stability of the marketing of these products and in particular of funds with constant liquidity. traded in tax havens such as luxembourg or ireland, they are sometimes perceived as quasi-deposits despite their exposure to the financial markets and the lack of state guarantees for their return. this lack of definition can not only be a vehicle for fraud, but can also contribute to amplifying the effects of a financial crisis by inducing massive sales of funds in an attempt to limit losses incurred. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the financial instruments are not used for the purpose of financing the community's activities. i voted against the report because it not only maintains them, but also increases their diversification to facilitate their penetration into markets such as public debt or the savings of charitable institutions - objectives to which we are radically opposed.
in writing. ‒ i support this report by my socialist colleague neena gill because it is a first attempt to regulate so-called money market funds, which provide liquidity to companies but at the same time present a major systemic risk by being perceived as banks when in reality they are investment funds. this proposal for a regulation increases transparency in the sector, while introducing requirements for diversification of assets, which helps to reduce the volatility of these funds and thus helps to stabilise financial markets. a termination clause is also included for most so-called constant value funds which present double the risk of variable value funds. in short, this is another step on the road taken since 2009 to strictly regulate the financial sector of the economy, after many years of deregulation promoted by the neoliberal right in europe and the united states.

in writing. ‒ money market funds (mmfs) provide short-term funding to financial institutions, companies or governments, and in doing so contribute to the financing of the european economy. the events of the financial crisis have exposed several features of mmfs that make them vulnerable in the event of difficulties in financial markets. in order to preserve the integrity and stability of the internal market, it is necessary to lay down rules on the functioning of mmfs, in particular on the composition of the portfolio of mmfs. similarly, uniform rules on mmfs are essential.
in writing. ‒ we voted against this report. money market asset investment funds (mmafs) are considered one of the elements of the 'shadow banking' which has been a major factor of instability and volatility in financial markets. in particular, fiamms offering constant net worth, considered to be virtually money deposits, have been a source of problems by triggering massive redemption requests, which in the us led to a public bailout of these funds. this type of fund is not authorised by the cnmv in spain and is marketed mainly in ireland and luxembourg. the commission proposal proposes stricter regulations for fiamms. however, we think that they are insufficient and we in the gue/ngl have proposed amendments which prohibit the establishment of these funds in tax havens and their progressive disappearance within ten years. since the amendments have been rejected, we have voted against.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report. there is one worrying element: the proposal contains a provision allowing certain mmfs with constant net worth to continue to operate funds with variable net worth without conversion, which is irresponsible and a privilege for this type of fund. these funds act like banks but without having to comply with banking regulations. in addition to opacity, there is risk of contagion and insecurity for investors. the commission, together with the socialist and liberal group, is continuing to support the privileges of the financial institutions, even though they are responsible for the crisis.

in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to adapt regulation 517/94 of 7 march to the new rules on delegated and implementing acts adopted following the adoption of the treaty of lisbon. this regulation lays down limits on imports of textiles from third countries not covered by specific import arrangements and on supervision and surveillance against the risks which such imports may pose to european textile production. this is a sensitive area, but one on which this resolution has a limited impact, since it currently affects only imports from two states with a small presence in the sector. the adaptation of this text contributes to its clarity without introducing fundamental changes with respect to the original wording. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the regulation on common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries not covered by agreements, as it concerns the codification and recasting of council regulation 517/94. the proposal is part of an adaptation exercise following the entry into force of the treaty of lisbon to ensure that the previous decision-making procedures in trade policy are adapted to the new regime of delegated and implementing acts.
in writing. ‒ in the interests of simplification and clarity of union law, so that it is more accessible and understandable to the citizen, i voted in favour of this report which codifies and recasts regulation 517/94 on the common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols, other agreements or by other specific import arrangements of the union. at present, belarus and north korea are the only countries not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols, other agreements or other specific import arrangements of the union - including the gsp and the everything but arms agreement - from which the eu imports textile products. the proposal is limited to a codification and recasting of existing acts, without any substantial amendments.

in writing. ‒ purely technical report by which the commission proposes to codify and consolidate regulation (ec) no 517/94 on the common rules for imports of textile products from certain third countries not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols, other agreements or by other specific import arrangements of the union. at present, belarus and north korea are the only countries not covered by bilateral agreements, protocols, other agreements or other specific import arrangements of the union - including the gsp and the everything but arms agreement - from which the eu imports textile products. the regulation has been substantially amended by various legislative acts over the last 20 years and, in the interests of clarity and simplification of european legislation, it is appropriate to consolidate all these provisions in a new regulation, while respecting the content of the codified texts.

in writing. ‒ this report on the estimates of revenue and expenditure of the european parliament reflects the administrative and financial needs of the european parliament for the coming year. there are new operational priorities that require an increase in certain items, such as cybersecurity. in other areas, such as those concerning european political parties and foundations and fees, we believe that more austerity is needed, especially at a time when many states, and therefore their citizens, are forced to endure budgetary rigors. exemplarity is not a whim, but a duty. otherwise we will never regain the trust we lost.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this decision, which reflects the administrative and financial needs of the european parliament for 2016, based on the first estimates presented by the secretary-general of the parliament. it is true that the spanish socialists would have liked the budget to be frozen at the level of 2015 and that the expenditure on parliamentary assistance should not be increased, as we have voted. however, the decision adopted sets the level of current expenditure at eur 1 823 648 600, a moderate increase compared to the 2015 budget - by 1.6% compared to the 3.09% initially planned, thanks to the negotiations of the s&d group with the other political groups - while an exceptional item of eur 15 million is allocated to improving the security of the parliament buildings in brussels and cybersecurity.

in writing. ‒ this is the first full budgetary procedure to be held in the new legislature. the bureau endorsed the general guidelines for the 2016 budget proposed by the secretary-general, which focus on strengthening the capacity of parliamentary committees to monitor the executive. in the current context of high public debt and budgetary consolidation, parliament must demonstrate budgetary responsibility, while ensuring sufficient resources to enable it to exercise all its powers and function properly.
in writing. ‒ while we consider the proposal for a total increase of 2.4% in parliament's operating budget to be satisfactory in the current crisis context, we vote against the text, considering firstly that there has been no real conciliation agreement between parliament's bureau and the committee on budgets, nor any willingness to negotiate on the part of the former, which has imposed its own criteria. secondly, there are budgetary increases which we consider absolutely inappropriate in the present economic context (such as those relating to the increase in expenditure on parliamentary assistance and the renovation of furniture) and, at the same time, there are also unjustified cuts proposed, such as those relating to general staffing changes and specifically to interpretation services. in general, it is desirable that there should be more debate on ways of properly optimising and making transparent the investment of parliament's public resources, and this resolution (not yet final, as the final stage will be developed at the end of the year) does not help to resolve this central issue.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this regulation to improve the transparency and quality of statistics provided to eurostat by national and subnational agencies. the availability of high-quality statistical information, a public good in itself, is essential for economic research, financial stability and informed decision-making in the field of european public policies. this is particularly important in view of cases such as the alleged manipulation of statistics by a member state, but also by regions, as allegedly happened in spain with the comunidad valenciana, governed by the pp since 1995, which prompted the opening of an investigation by the commission in 2014 pending the results. for this reason, it is essential to strengthen the independence of the state statistical agencies and to introduce the possibility of on-the-spot inspections by the commission in the member states. parliamentary control of eurostat and its coordination with the european system of central banks is also improved. i therefore believe that this regulation deserves our full support and i congratulate the rapporteur, mr hughes bayet, on the excellent work he has done.
in writing. ‒ despite the serious problems of corruption that plunder the coffers of the spanish state, we have had to vote against the proposal as we did not have enough information from the commission to properly analyse its proposal. in addition, we believe that there is already a european anti-fraud office with powers similar to those of the proposed prosecutor's office, which is not performing its duties sufficiently. our priority is to strengthen this office so that it can really act against tax fraud which every year causes the spanish state to lose around 59.515 million euros every year. we also do not know in detail the relationship between this supranational body and the justice systems of the various member states, which seems to us to be a deliberate omission of details on the part of the commission and which could lead to the creation of a two-speed justice system within the union.
in writing. ‒ the creation of a european public prosecutor's office (eppo) was voted out. there is a marked lack of effectiveness and coordination of taxation between eu member states, which justifies the necessary improvement and revision of the system. however, the creation of a new body does not seem to be the solution, as before tackling it it would be necessary to gather more information about 1) the competences that the eppo would have under the current framework with olaf and eurojust, 2) its relationship with the national courts of the ms, 3) the actual functioning of the bodies that already exist. the idea of focusing on the creation of a new entity to combat tax fraud distracts the discourse from the necessary evaluation of the activities of olaf itself and from the improvement of the structures already present in the eu framework.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the added value of the european public prosecutor's office, which will consist in a single and independent prosecutor's office being responsible, at european level, for the investigations and criminal prosecutions in cases of fraud involving eu funds and in increasing criminal prosecutions, the recovery of funds and taxpayers' confidence in the eu institutions. the current system, while functioning properly in some member states, has proven to be rather ineffective within the union in terms of initiating criminal proceedings and recovering funds.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the creation of the european public prosecutor's office, bearing in mind that the european public prosecutor's office will be a single and independent office which will be responsible, at european level, for the investigation and prosecution of criminal cases of fraud involving eu funds.
in writing. ‒ the european public prosecutor's office will be responsible, in accordance with article 86 tfeu, for investigating, prosecuting and bringing to justice offences relating to fraud against the financial interests of the european union. this report, the second interim report drawn up by parliament, sets out the main concerns of the s&d group, with specifics on the selection procedures for independent european prosecutors; the division of competences between the european public prosecutor's office and national prosecutors; the involvement of the european public prosecutor's office in the prosecution of ancillary offences (fraud-related offences which are not in themselves fraud offences); the rationalisation of investigative measures carried out by a european public prosecutor's office; the need for rules on admissibility of evidence to properly respect existing eu legislation in this area; the strengthening of the procedural rights of suspects; judicial review of the actions of the european public prosecutor's office; and the clarity of data protection provisions. i have therefore voted in favour.

mr president, since 2011, the spaces for political and democratic participation have been closing in burundi. little by little, the ruling party and the president have intimidated, harassed, detained and broken any possibility of installing a democratic system. we have little to celebrate so far, but the announcement of president nkurunziza's decision has made the situation completely worse. this decision to stand for a third term - as my colleagues and the commissioner himself have said - violates the arusha accords and violates the spirit of the burundian constitution; and in a country with such a dramatic past and in a region with such fragile stability, president nkurunziza's decision is a very serious risk for everyone. it's very simple: ask the president to reconsider his decision. we must ask the government to reopen the spaces of political participation, to reopen the radio stations it has closed, to release the political prisoners, to open the way to democratic participation. and if that is not the case, mr commissioner, if the president does not re-train and if the political, civil and fundamental freedoms that are necessary for an electoral process are not given, then the european union and the european parliament should not support the electoral process in burundi, because it will be a false, rigged process, and because nkurunziza will need a lot of repression to sustain that campaign.
member of the commission, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– mr president, this has been a very useful exchange, and i thank the honourable members for the clarity and purpose of their interventions. regarding our election observation and coordination, i would like to point out that we coordinate extensively both on the ground and at headquarters. in burundi we liaise closely with the un election observation mission and maintain close contacts with the african union, and we shall continue to do so. from this debate i draw three main conclusions. firstly, that we have the support of this house in reviewing all the options available to us under the cotonou agreement and other instruments if the situation is not resolved, with particular attention required to the respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms. secondly, that we have a responsibility to burundians to protect them from increased economic and humanitarian risks in an already fragile country, and that we must keep this in mind. thirdly, that while we retain our desire to support elections with the instruments at our disposal, we ought clearly to present to the burundian authorities what the conditions of open electoral and political space mean to us and then closely monitor this in the days ahead. i look forward to maintaining dialogue with you, and again i signal my appreciation of parliament’s role in keeping this important issue on the international agenda.
member of the commission, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– mr president, i fully share your concerns on the plight of christians worldwide. recent events such as the bombing of two churches in pakistan, killings in nigeria, beheadings in libya, constant persecution by isil/daesh in syria and iraq, and the most recent massacre in the garissa university college in kenya give the impression of a besieged community. such attacks targeting christians are deeply worrying and, this goes without saying, completely unacceptable. the barbaric violence and inhuman methods used by, for instance, al-shabaab, daesh and boko haram, are frontal attacks against international human rights values and principles, and against the very nature of what makes us human beings, regardless of our religion or belief. the eu condemned unreservedly the indiscriminate attacks, atrocities, killings and abuses of human rights which are perpetrated by these terrorist organisations, against christians but also against other religious and ethnic groups that we should not forget in the course of this debate. as recalled in the eu guidelines on freedom of religion or belief adopted in june 2013, all persons belonging to religious communities or minorities should be able to live, practise their religion and worship freely, individually or in community with others, without fear of intolerance and attacks. we can never allow these values and fundamental principles to be challenged or compromised. this applies to people of all faiths or none, and this definitely applies to christians. we must not forget either that the first victims of terrorism and terrorist acts are muslims and arab countries. we need to avoid falling into the logic and perception of a clash and religious confrontation. the king of jordan reminded us all of this very fact during his remarkable speech to this chamber. he said that ‘the recent attacks in some countries against christian and minority communities are an offence against humanity as well as against islam. arab christians are an integral part of our region’s past, present and future’, said the king. today, on its southern flank, the european union is facing an arc of conflicts and crises, with spillover effects throughout the region and cooperation with our partners in the arab world is essential if we are to address the regional challenges and threats which they, and we, face. security threats, of course, include jihadist terrorism and transnational crime. we need to work together, including on the protection of minorities, both on open conflicts and on the root causes of some of these crises – including the economic and social situation of the younger generation in many of these countries. the very inclusive council conclusions of 9 february on counter-terrorism list precisely a full set of actions in order to address radicalisation and counter violent extremism. further engaging with third countries on all fronts is key: this includes bilateral, regional and multilateral cooperation with governments on security, education and human rights issues, but also with local communities, including through supporting inter- and intra-faith dialogues. but let me come back to the latest attack in kenya. this gruesome attack is the latest and most deadly in the string of terrorist attacks perpetrated by al—shabaab in kenya over the last 18 months. acts of terrorism have unfortunately become a recurrent feature in kenya; and terrorism is a threat that is gradually increasing in the greater horn of africa region. the garissa attack was crueler than previous attacks, probably being inspired by the methods used by islamic state or boko haram. the specific targeting of christians and the executions were noted also from previous attacks, as in mandera by the end of last year. this ‘trend’ is extremely worrying. despite the fact that representatives from the kenyan muslim community came out stronger than before condemning the attack, there is a considerable risk that it also will lead to further division and antagonism between religious communities, which is clearly the aim of the perpetrators. this is what high representative/vice-president mogherini referred to in her statement of 3 april when she said: ‘by attacking students in the college near garissa, killing 147 young people and injuring many more, the terrorists showed their determination to undermine education, to provoke division between different faiths, to deprive the country of a future of economic and cultural growth, of stability and dignity for all its citizens’. radicalisation and violent extremism is a global problem and cannot be dealt with in isolation. thus, while the global terrorist threat requires a global approach, solutions have to be specific and tailor-made. apart from addressing the issue at the international level, reconsidering global and regional strategies, the european union is pursuing work in mapping and better understanding how radicalisation operates concretely in individual countries, such as kenya, and in communities in order to improve our response and counter it.
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, while many of us were able to attend mass freely on holy thursday, at the same time, at a university in kenya, the terrorist group al shabab was selecting christian students to murder them. can you imagine the terror felt by these young people when they were separated from their peers to die for the simple fact of being christians? or the anguish felt by the parents of the girls kidnapped in nigeria from a christian school? or the helplessness of christians in the middle east who have to leave their homes if they do not want to die? that is why the people's party has made and continues to make a resolution in which we wanted and succeeded in including, alongside these atrocious acts in kenya, the reference to christians and their persecution. that's where the problem started, because the other groups didn't want and didn't want to negotiate with me, they wanted me to remove all reference to christians, all mention of christians. by refusing me, they have made another resolution, where, of 39 paragraphs, only two mention christians, whereas our resolution speaks of all the persecutions suffered by christians throughout the world. i think we owe him. i'm told we'll do one more in the future the other groups tell me. no, sir, a christian is dying every hour. we don't have time to waste. this is a good opportunity. that's why we have to talk about christians. the people's party has no complexes, it does not distinguish between first and second class victims, and that is why i ask for support for the people's party resolution, because that is the support for all persecuted christians in the world.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, we condemn all violence and all discrimination based on religion, in any religion. but education is the best antidote to extremism and that's why al shabab attacked a university. and it's true that one college student who survived said, "this is not going to have an impact on the world because they haven't killed any white people". and it is true that the western media has dealt with the issue of the killing in kenya in a very tangential way. in fact, the students themselves had to launch a campaign, which was called 147 is not just a number, and remember the names of all those who had died. i am afraid that, among all of us, there is a great deal of ignorance of what is really happening in that country. even after kenya's independence, there was a serious conflict between the north and the rest of the country. nairobi and garissa have always been very far apart and surely the relationship with somalia has made it all much more dangerous. now the al shabab terrorists are saying, they are claiming, that this is a war against kenya. and that is why the european union must support kenya in its security, to monitor its systems and its security problems. we must help them control their relationship with somalia. we are talking about helping them with means and with political determination, because, without a doubt, this is a war against kenya and, in short, it is a war against all.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president i am very sensitive to the persecution of christians all over the world and they deserve it and i will do everything i can and will have all my support for those who want to put that flag forward in a resolution of this parliament. but, having said that, it is our intention and that of the alde group to focus on the killing of students in kenya, in garissa, a killing that was undoubtedly due to religious motives as well - as is happening in syria, as, there are persecutions even in china - but also to ethnic motives, also to the old and very old war that exists in that part of the world between the shifta, who are those who live in southern somalia, who have what is called in spain "african hatred" towards their neighbours and very much towards the enlightenment, towards western values, towards a number of westernized students; in the end, towards democratic values. and we absolutely wanted in our resolution, while respecting all these intolerable discriminations, to put our finger on the wound of this concrete and appalling fact to say that europe cannot be inhibited, as it is not already in other areas such as mali or somalia itself. we must protect here and now, regardless of whether we speak after the persecution against any minority - and the roma are equally worthy - we must involve the european union and we must involve it on the spot, including with trainers, trainers, with our specialists who, with the help of the african troops on the spot, control them, help them, but also prevent in the short term this kind of killing and this kind of persecution of the western democratic values that we defend. and that is the purpose of our resolution, which we shall be voting on tomorrow.
on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, first of all, i would like to express our strongest condemnation of the attacks and murders committed by al shabab at the university of garissa and our full solidarity with the victims and their families. the european union must act with all the means at its disposal to attack the deep roots behind the conflicts and which create the conditions which favour the development of groups such as al shabab. we also believe that solutions based on a military approach are not the right answer: the us military intervention in somalia in 1992, with disastrous implications that the peoples of the region are still paying for today; the responsibility of the former colonial powers in promoting conflict and plundering the natural resources of the horn of africa; land grabbing, poverty - we cannot forget that the majority of the kenyan population lives below the poverty line - the hundreds of thousands of refugees, child mortality, hunger and malnutrition. the solution does not require further military operations by either the eu or the united states in the region. the western powers and multinationals must stop plundering africa, take their claws out of the region and respect the sovereignty of the peoples so that they are the masters of their destinies and their resources.
the question of the 'blue card'. i wanted to ask mr. corrao something. ignazio, i wanted to remind you - as you have referred to my words - that i am not counting when i say that in a resolution christians are mentioned only twice. no, this does not mean in any case an ideological war or anything like that. i am simply saying that in the resolution before us the title, apart from kenya, is 'persecution of christians'. if you do not mention christians twice in that resolution, then something is wrong. if we pass a resolution on the persecution of the roma, as has been done in this house, and the roma are not mentioned in it, and they are not mentioned in this house, then something is wrong. that's all i've pointed out.
president-in-office of the council.– madam president, let me start by saying that it is our common responsibility to preserve and safeguard the cultural heritage of the ancient civilisations upon whose shoulders the rich cultural heritage of europe stands. here i mean any kinds of destruction – those that occur due to natural disasters and those that are shamefully caused by human malicious actions. the presidency strongly condemns the deliberate and brutal destruction of ancient artefacts and the burning of over a hundred thousand rare manuscripts and documents in iraq’s northern city of mosul by da’esh militants. precious cultural heritage of ancient civilisations has irreversibly vanished and continues to be under threat of illicit trafficking. acts of destruction of the sculptures, manuscripts and sites that isis/da’esh have seized from the countries it occupies are not just a tragedy for the syrian and the iraqi people, it is a loss for civilisations of the entire world. the council is aware of the gravity of the situation. i would like to recall in this regard the two regulations the council adopted regarding restrictive measures against iraq in 2003 and syria in 2013. the regulations prohibit the import, export and transfer of cultural goods which have been illegally removed from these two countries. the aim of these measures is precisely to prevent the illicit trafficking of cultural heritage and the use of it for the purposes of financing terrorist activities. as the honourable members certainly know, the export of cultural goods to third countries is subject to uniform controls at eu external borders. however, such uniform rules do not exist for import. with this concern in mind, last year the council asked the commission to prepare a study on the issue of illicit trafficking of cultural objects, including the import to the eu of cultural goods illegally exported from third countries. the study is due to be completed by 2016. the council supports un resolution 2199 of 2015 that also condemns the destruction of cultural heritage in iraq and syria, particularly by isis/da’esh and the al-nusra front, and urges all member states to take steps, in cooperation with interpol and unesco and other international organisations, to prevent the trade in items of cultural, scientific and religious importance illegally removed from either country during periods of conflict. cooperation with unesco is essential to strengthen the protection of global cultural heritage. i would like to use this opportunity to call on those member states who have not done so yet to ratify the unesco convention of 1970 on the means of prohibiting and preventing the illicit import, export and transfer of ownership of cultural property. the council also called on member states to cooperate with unesco by taking common actions in order to prevent crimes against cultural goods. cooperation with interpol and europol is on-going to strengthen the effectiveness of combating this type of crime. finally, in 2012 the council set up an informal network of law enforcement authorities and expertise competent in the field of cultural goods called eu cultnet. the aim of this network is to strengthen coordination at national level to combat crime against cultural goods. during the next culture ministers’ council meeting that will take place in just three weeks, the commission will give an update on culture and cultural heritage aspects. this update will be an important contribution to the eu regional strategy for syria and iraq as well as the da’esh threat. it is a well-known fact that illicit trafficking of cultural and archaeological artefacts is one of the financial sources for isil/da’esh and other terrorist organisations. therefore, addressing the issue is also important in the wider context of countering terrorism. the fight against terrorism is an issue of particular importance to the presidency. particular attention is being paid to the swift implementation of the eu counter-terrorism measures, including on countering the financing of terrorism. i would like to conclude by saying that the world’s cultural heritage is a source of inspiration and immense knowledge, as well as a resource to facilitate peaceful co-existence by promoting trust and mutual understanding with a view to the resolution and prevention of conflicts. this patrimony has a universal value and it belongs to all of humanity, irrespective of ownership or territory. there is no reason which could justify any attempt to destroy it, and europe must stay vigilant in protecting it.
member of the commission.– madam president, we have all been horrified by the tragic loss of so many lives and the human suffering in syria and iraq. we are also appalled by the terrible images of destruction of cultural sites both in iraq and syria, which we are debating today. this is a horrible attack against not only the culture of those countries but also against the values and the memories of several centuries of history. we cannot remain silent in the face of such events. we therefore welcome this opportunity to speak here and join the european parliament in the condemnation of such barbaric behaviour. as you know, the european union is committed to the preservation of cultural heritage as an essential element to maintain the liveliness of national identities and to nurture the awareness of the role each community of people plays in the global society. the responsible behaviour of individuals is also based on the sense of belonging that cultural heritage inspires and on the connections it maintains with our past. the european union has repeatedly condemned isil/da’esh’s deliberate destruction of archaeological and cultural heritage in syria and iraq and the extremist ideology behind it, most recently in its foreign affairs council conclusions of march 2015 and in the eu regional strategy for syria and iraq. in those conclusions the european union also noted that such actions could even be qualified as war crimes under international humanitarian law. also, iraq called upon the un security council to adopt an ad hoc resolution on the destruction of cultural heritage which would label those acts as crimes against humanity. the european union and its member states support and commend the efforts of both international and local partners to safeguard as much cultural heritage as possible from the territories occupied by isil/da’esh. the european union is taking appropriate steps in accordance with un security council resolution 2199 to prevent the illegal trade in cultural property, as this also directly contributes to the financing of isil/da’esh and other terrorist organisations. the council has adopted regulations banning imports of cultural goods coming from the two countries. now we must ensure that they will be appropriately enforced by the member state authorities. more generally, the fight against the trafficking of cultural property is a part of the eu’s fight against organised crime. the framework decision on the fight against organised crime establishes the definitions of offences for participating in a criminal organisation and provides for corresponding penalties on natural or legal persons. europol too plays a role in this, providing support to ongoing investigations and facilitating the exchange of information about offences committed, and stolen and sought-after cultural property. member states are also encouraged to use interpol’s dedicated database on stolen works of art and to cooperate with its special unit dedicated to the fight against illicit trafficking in cultural goods. moreover, the european union funds the international observatory on illicit traffic in cultural goods, a collaborative platform designed by the international council of museums. in the context of the european agenda on security that was adopted yesterday, the commission is also exploring the need to take measures in the area of terrorism financing, including measures relating to illicit trade in cultural goods. since 2014 the european union has also financially supported, with eur 2.7 million, the unesco-run action plan for cultural heritage in syria. the project aims at the emergency safeguarding of syrian cultural heritage implemented by unesco. cultural heritage is also a powerful antidote against intolerance, xenophobia and fanaticism of all sorts. the remains of past civilisations remind us that cultures are the product of a never-ending process of elaboration and transformation where there is no definite truth but just countless attempts to find a meaning to human life. for all these reasons, the european union will do whatever is in its power to protect cultural heritage from pillage and destruction and to prosecute the perpetrators of such crimes. in that regard, the european union is ready to upscale any form of cooperation with all international organisations engaged in
