president-in-office of the council.– mr president, establishing an exception to copyright in favour of the blind and visually impaired has always been a matter of great importance. in this regard, we are grateful to parliament for actively promoting ratification by the european union of the marrakesh treaty, which is specifically dedicated to this matter. the marrakesh treaty enhances opportunities for millions of visually-impaired persons to participate fully in public life, to enjoy the arts and to share scientific progress and its benefits. it does so by establishing a set of international rules, which ensure the cross-border exchange of published works, books and printed materials in a format accessible for the persons concerned. to ensure the benefits to visually-impaired persons, the marrakesh treaty imposes the introduction of a limitation or exception to the right of reproduction, distribution and making available to the public of right holders. it is an important instrument to further improve the everyday lives of persons with disabilities. the european union signed the treaty on 30 april 2014. throughout the negotiations, all european union member states, without exception, have remained fully committed to the union’s accession to the marrakesh treaty without delay. despite that, the process has been overshadowed by a deep division of views over the legal basis and the nature of the competence of the european union. this disagreement of principle has up until now delayed the decision on ratification by the european union of the marrakesh treaty. the commission considers that the marrakesh treaty falls under exclusive european union competence. on the other hand, the majority of member states are of the view that the treaty falls under shared eu/national competence. i must admit that discussions on the division of competences between the european union and its member states is a very complex legal and political matter, as it touches upon the core principles of the functioning of the european union. this discussion goes far beyond the specific treaty. the latvian presidency has been working hard to reconcile the views, working actively with member states and the commission to find a pragmatic solution – be it a horizontal or a specific one. to achieve this, flexibility on the part of everyone involved is required. unfortunately, no agreement has been found so far. i assure you that the council will continue to make every possible effort to reach a solution that would allow the marrakesh treaty to have the required impact and grant the benefits to the people in need. this is a matter of the utmost priority and importance. in any event, i must draw your attention to the fact that the european union, even without formal accession to the treaty, may already give practical application to its provisions by making the respective changes to the eu legislation and thus benefiting the people in need.
member of the commission.– mr president, let me be brief and clear. the commission regrets the council’s decision to delay the ratification of the marrakesh treaty to facilitate access to published works for persons who are blind, visually impaired, or otherwise print disabled. the commission presented its proposal for a council decision to conclude the marrakesh treaty on behalf of the union on 21 october 2014. now it is up to the council to find an agreement on it. this is a very important treaty that would help millions of visually-impaired people around the world to have better access to culture and education. the european union could have a key role in providing books in formats that are accessible to them. the commission also intends to present a legislative proposal to implement the marrakesh treaty in union law. however, neither the legislative proposal nor the adoption of eu legislation is a precondition for the discussion of the commission’s proposal on the conclusion of the marrakesh treaty. on the latter, the commission now considers seeking the opinion of the court of justice of the european union.
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities is very clear in article 21 on equal opportunities and the rights of persons with disabilities to education, social participation, employment and culture. it is the first human rights treaty signed and ratified by the european union. the marrakesh treaty was signed on 27 june 2013 by wipo and, as of now, it is the first treaty also related to copyright in which consumers participated. it was made from the point of view of consumers and not from that of the rights holders, as was the custom. it is a tool - the marrakesh treaty - that is being demanded by the whole disability sector at the global level and at the european level: the european forum, all the entities, because it is an instrument, an international human rights tool for access to culture for 30 million people who are blind or who have some problems in accessing printed reading. it is therefore a compromise, and i agree with the commission on this point; and if it is a priority, the council must find a solution. we are two years behind schedule and you have to find an immediate solution so that 30 million people can have access to what we call the 'hunger for reading', as well as to education, culture, equal opportunities and social participation. it is not a necessity: it is a fundamental human right and therefore must be a priority. i ask the council to tell us and to give us a timetable for ratification now. i also ask the council not to mix up the debate which is about to begin with the issue of copyright, because they are two different debates and if we mix it up we will end the legislature without having ratified the marrakesh treaty. so we cannot be filling our mouths in this parliament all day long with equal opportunities, non-discrimination... we have a treaty that has been signed for two years and we are not doing everything in our power to ratify it and thus fulfill the main commitment, which is equality for all.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president the marrakesh treaty, agreed two years ago, seeks to secure the right of the visually impaired - 30 million of whom live in europe alone - to access culture by way of exceptions to the restrictive intellectual property laws that exist today. it is therefore a matter of extending a right and that is why my group, which i represent, will always be in favour of this. the european union and the member states must ensure that these intellectual property rules are non-discriminatory and that they are amended, because they are clearly within the european union's sphere of competence. but if all this is so clear, i don't understand what we're waiting for. it is unacceptable that only 1% of books or magazines are available to these groups, hindering their right to education, participation and, ultimately, effective social inclusion. for us, the most important thing is that this ratification should be carried out as soon as possible and that we can support it in parliament. rights cannot be frozen, whatever the reason - including the economic one, which is always behind it - because article 30 of the un convention on the rights of persons with disabilities says that states must ensure that people with disabilities have equal access to cultural life. we therefore call for and demand that the deadline be lifted so that the agreement can be reached as quickly as possible and the treaty can be ratified as soon as possible.

president-in-office of the council.– mr president, the presidency welcomes the strong support of parliament for its attempts to have the marrakesh treaty produce its effects without any unnecessary delay. i understand your criticism towards the council as it is the institution taking the final decision on ratification by the european union of any international treaty. however, the quality of the council decision depends to a large extent on the quality of the proposal submitted to it. as i have said, any discussion on competence is a very difficult and sensitive one. we have had several rounds of discussion in an attempt to find a solution. to find one, flexibility needs to be shown by everyone – and i will repeat that – by everyone. many of you have referred to the need for a timetable. i will transmit this proposal to my colleagues in the council. a measure that could significantly facilitate unblocking the situation is a legislative proposal by the commission to adapt the euʼs legal framework to the marrakesh treaty ahead of the council decision on the conclusion of the marrakesh treaty. such a proposal would ensure clarity and legal certainty as regards the necessary steps for the implementation of the marrakesh treaty. what would not be helpful or productive is to suspend our discussions to start lengthy court procedures. i will repeat that the council fully recognises the importance of the ratification by the european union of the marrakesh treaty. the council is in no way interested in creating unnecessary hurdles in the process, but what must be done must be done. i will conclude by saying that the marrakesh treaty has been included on the agenda of the foreign affairs council that takes place on monday next week. let us see what next week will bring.
in writing. although the marrakesh treaty was signed on 27 june 2013, almost two years have passed and it has not yet been implemented. the ratification of the marrakesh treaty is an essential step towards ensuring that almost 30 million blind, visually impaired or otherwise difficult people have access to printed text and are guaranteed access to culture. it is estimated that less than 5% of books published in europe are available in accessible formats for blind or partially sighted people, and that available books cannot be shared across borders in europe and the rest of the world where less than 1% of published books are available for blind or partially sighted people. this lack also deprives these people of access to literature in their mother tongue and in a foreign language and limits their right to education, information and social participation.

the rapporteur. madam president, i would like to thank mr hoyer for his presence, the european investment bank for its collaboration in the drafting of this report and the alternative rapporteurs, who are also here today, for their constructive attitude and the good work done with their proposals. the bank is destined, in our view, to play a much more important role in the future of the european union because of the need to urgently abandon recession and austerity and move towards investment and higher welfare quotas. the role of the eib will therefore be essential and this makes this year's report special, also because we are on the verge of the start of the so-called juncker plan. i will divide my speech into four blocks, which are basically the blocks that the report deals with, the first being investment. the fact that this report was drawn up in parallel - as i said - with the juncker plan has obviously drawn our attention to this. as you know, my group and i are sceptical that there will be a leverage of private capital of the proportions proposed, 1 to 15, because, as far as we have seen, we have no precedent with such a high factor. in the report we emphasize that the guarantees for the efsi are not new funds but allocated resources, and we would like to see an assessment of the reallocation of these resources to see whether this is indeed better than having them put to other uses. we also point out that the project selection process should aim to avoid foreclosure effects of private capital from projects that are already being done or would have been done the same. we also hope that the house will support our reference to the fight against unemployment as a central activity of the european investment bank and we also support - because i believe it is necessary - the european central bank being able to buy the bonds that the eib will issue under the esi fund. the second set of issues we deal with in the report is the evaluation of the project bond initiative, which has been a good part of our work. i would like to start, of course, with the first pilot project, which was, of course, the castor project. on 26 january you yourself, mr hoyer, said in the european parliament that the castor project had become a tragedy and i share your assessment. we are also joined today by representatives of the platform in defence of the sénia lands, whom i would like to pay tribute to for their tireless struggle to stop the project and for compensation. this was clearly not a project in the public interest. it was paralysed by more than a thousand earthquakes and a bad environmental assessment which ignored the reports of the experts and ended with the intention of compensating a private company for paralysing the work with 1 300 million, compensation which the spanish government now intends to be paid by the spanish citizens on their gas bill for 30 years. we believe - and this is one of the issues addressed in the report - that the european commission and the european investment bank must act to prevent this waste. i would also like to express to you, mr hoyer, a certain unease on the part of the citizens who are here with us today because of the lack of response to the complaint lodged with the bank's complaints mechanism office. the third block i would like to mention is the energy policy block. in this section we acknowledge the steps taken by the eib in its new policy, with the gradual phasing out of aid to coal projects, and we stress in this connection the need to present a plan to end such projects. finally, the climate assessment you are about to launch also seems to us to be a good initiative. and the fourth and final block is transparency and accountability. we welcome efforts to improve transparency, but we are a little disappointed with the results of the transparency policy review. we believe that the old culture of secrecy of the european investment bank should be left behind - and this is usually pointed out - and that we should start publishing on the basis of the principle of publication, that is to say that confidentiality should be the exception and not the rule. finally, we would like to point out that the issue of the use of tax havens in financial intermediation and also the new tax policy should be an important element of the work of the european investment bank, and we ask - and i end with this - that the bank refrain from cooperating with financial intermediaries which have a negative record in terms of transparency, tax evasion or aggressive tax planning practices, fraud, corruption or environmental and social impact. i would therefore like to thank you, mr hoyer, for your cooperation and hope that you will take account of the recommendations that the european parliament will make to you.
the question of the 'blue card'. mr. lucke, thank you so much for accepting the card. you said germany has no investment problems. i wonder what the situation is in a country with a current account surplus of 7%? is it too much savings? how can you say that germany has no investment problem when the country's own potential for growth is very limited and the excess of savings is overwhelming, which complicates the management of the current account of the other countries, the countries of the south?

member of the commission.– madam president, i would like to thank you for this interesting debate here today. the current economic and financial situation requires decisive policy action, and we believe that the european investment bank’s activities are a crucial component of the eu’s efforts to bring back sustainable growth and employment to europe, especially with the eib and the commission partnering in the challenging delivery of the investment plan for europe. i am confident that parliament’s assessment of the eib’s activities in the year ahead will be as supportive as its opinion on the 2013 annual report, and i look forward to continuing our close and successful cooperation between the commission and the bank.
president of the european investment bank.– madam president, thank you very much for this interesting debate. it would take a lot of courage and endurance on your side if, in view of the diversity and variety of the questions and comments raised, i were to go into each and every detail, but i promise that i will come back to each and every one of you on the questions you have raised. let me concentrate on a few points. let me begin with the notion that maybe we are a little bit too satisfied with what we have done and that we might even be complacent. we are satisfied but we are definitely not complacent because, in view of the challenges in europe, the situation of the labour markets and the lack of growth, in view of the investment gap and the innovation gap, there is no reason for complacency in the european union for anybody and certainly not for the eib. on the other hand, in 2012 the eib turned anti—cyclical. until then it was clear that, according to all decisions taken, the bank would have to reduce lending volume after the huge positive impact it had had on the mastering of the first wave of the crisis, but then we had to go down again. this is the reason why i then turned to the european council and said that we needed either capital increase or we would behave procyclically, out of necessity. so the european council, with your support, decided in favour of the capital increase and we delivered on that. that turned the bank anti-cyclical and we are proud of that achievement. the analysis last year was clear. the investment gap has been there since 2007, but in addition – and this should not be overlooked – we have had an innovation gap and an education expenditure gap in europe for almost 18 years. these together are leading to a dangerous reduction in the competitiveness of european industry in the globalising economy. sometimes we should look a little more outside europe to see what is happening in this world. we have been in crisis mode for seven years and we are now finding out that, during those seven years, others around the world have done their homework and have advanced considerably. therefore we need to address the questions of competitiveness and this is the basic idea of the juncker plan. the juncker plan certainly does not only mean the european fund for strategic investments (efsi). it also means regulation, continuation of sound fiscal policies and cutting red tape. we addressed that issue in detail at the european finance ministers meeting last week in riga. on efsi, there is the continuous question of additionality and i want to address it very clearly. efsi, the shift of budgetary means from subsidies to guarantees, if you so decide – it is your decision – means that we will be able to address risk dimensions which until now the bank would not have been able to address in that volume. it is not true that we do not do very risky things. we have, under ‘special activities’, a window of between eur 4 and 5 billion per year for these activities and we do them. with the juncker plan we will be able to do business in this field of far more than eur 20 billion per year. so it is a qualitative and quantitative change and that is what is meant by additionality. additionality does not mean that each individual project is necessarily higher in risk than the portfolio will be. the portfolio will certainly be considerably higher in that respect so there is no reason to believe that this is going to be business as usual. the second point in this context is that we have to make sure that the huge investment and innovation gap in europe is addressed by attracting private funds. otherwise it is never going to work. we conducted a study last year to identify the differences between the targets set by the european council, and discussed in this very parliament, and the means provided, privately and in public budgets, in order to achieve these goals. these differences are so huge it would never be possible to level them out with public money. so we need to crowd in private money. the eib is the crowding-in bank and there are the huge volumes that we get from the capital markets every year and the quality stamp that we put on projects which then leads to confidence among private investors that it makes sense to invest in these projects as well. we have been addressing the differences in economic development in the member states. look at the per capita figures we had in recent years for the bankʼs activities. cyprus per capita showed eur 306 per person for activities of the bank in cyprus. in spain it was eur 258. these are the strongest countries. in germany it is well over eur 100 and that is quite justified because the economic situation in spain is one thing and in germany it is another. so we have to address the differences and i believe that we are doing this. in conclusion, you can be sure that we will use the funds provided by the european union and the member states with care and diligence and that we will try to preserve our strong position in the market. of course triple a is not a fetish; triple a is a business necessity in order to be able to crowd in huge amounts of private capital at reasonable rates. we are trying to do this in an effective way and also in an efficient way because the eib is the leanest bank of its size in the world. not only are we by far the biggest one – two and a half times the size of the world bank – but we are also the leanest one. if you compare the employment figures of the eib and, let us say, the ebrd or the world bank, it is dramatic. from that point of view, you can be sure that we are trying not only to be effective and have an impact on improving the situation in europe, but we are also trying to be efficient.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. four points very fast, mr hoyer. the first one is on the efsi. i want to insist on a point that my colleague mentioned, which is that we should respect procedures. we did not think it was right for the bank to announce projects when we have not yet completed the trilogues and it would therefore be important for us to respect the rhythms in the institutional dynamic. secondly, we are very concerned in this parliament - and i think many of my colleagues have mentioned this - about the question of transparency. i have not been able to mention the glencore case before, but it is an important case, even one in which the european ombudsman showed interest. the conclusions of the transparency policy review we already know how they came out. we would therefore like you to pay more attention to this matter. thirdly, i would like to say that in your two speeches you have not mentioned the question of project bonds at any point and the first two have not gone well. my italian colleague also mentioned the passante di mestre, the motorway, which i could not mention at the beginning because of lack of time, but i would like to stress once again the issue of the castor project. i do not think you can let the castor project end as the spanish government intends, by bailing out and making the spanish citizens pay for it. the bank must be more involved in the kind of projects it finances and i think - and we hope - that you in this parliament can intervene to prevent this from happening. and finally, i would like to say that i think it would be a good exercise if, after parliament's report has been adopted, we could have a dialogue to see how the recommendations we will be adopting this morning can be implemented at the bank. i think it would be good if that were to become a tradition and, in any case, i thank you for coming.

member of the commission.– madam president, i welcome this opportunity to discuss with you the outbreak of a new plant disease which poses a very serious threat to the whole of our agricultural sector. xylella fastidiosa is a bacterial disease which, following its first introduction into the european union, is now heavily affecting olive oil production in southern italy. the commission is very concerned about this situation because there is no effective treatment to cure the plants once they become infected. it is the first time such a bacterium has been found in the eu and it affects a very large number of plant species, with devastating effects. the occurrence of this disease, regulated as a quarantine organism, was notified by the italian authorities on 21 october 2013. the area affected is almost the entire province of lecce, in the apulia region. emergency measures were first taken in february 2014 and further strengthened in july 2014. these measures lay down strict requirements for import and movement of host plants in the eu, timely identification and control in the affected areas in italy and the removal of all infected host plants. the commission’s food and veterinary office carried out two audits in 2014. the second audit, conducted in november 2014, concluded that the situation had dramatically deteriorated since the first one conducted in february of the same year. a new outbreak has been confirmed recently in the province of brindisi. this shows that the disease has already moved outside the originally affected area. clearly, there is a high risk of a further spread if decisive measures are not taken as a matter of immediate urgency. in addition, the european food safety authority published in january this year a pest risk assessment with a list of potential host plants, including main agricultural crops such as citrus and grapevine. this list contains approximately 200 species – a much larger number than that covered by the previous eu emergency measures. although not yet found in citrus and grapevine plants, the range of host plants affected by the bacterium found in apulia is gradually increasing as investigations continue to unfold. italy has, in the meantime, declared a state of emergency, nominated a special commissioner in charge of this file and announced a series of measures to be taken, including significant financial funding. in parallel, the commission has reviewed the current eu emergency measures with great care in line with the precautionary principle. i can assure the honourable members that the list of potential host plants to be covered, including citrus and grapevine, as well as restrictions on movements outside the infected zone and from infected third countries, has been considered from a strong precautionary perspective. the new measures proposed by the commission and endorsed by the member states on 28 april this year foresee the following: for the heavily infected province of lecce, it was finally agreed to restrict the measures to the felling of infected trees and intensive testing of the surrounding trees. for any outbreaks outside lecce, including the one in the province of brindisi, a more precautionary approach is being taken by preventable felling, not only of the infected trees but also other host plants within 100 metres. this is essential to prevent the further spread of this bacterium in the european union. i want to be clear on one thing: the strict conditions applied on movements out of the demarcated areas in italy are also applied to imports from affected third countries. furthermore, given that recently coffee plants imported from costa rica and honduras were intercepted in the european union with xylella fastidiosa, the commission is now banning such imports. lastly, let me reassure you that the commission is in permanent contact with the italian authorities to explore all possible tools available to support financially implementation of the eradication measures foreseen in our legislation. compensation can be granted for eradication measures such as removal and destruction of plants, phytosanitary treatments, including for sampling and testing, on condition that all proposed eradication measures are fully implemented. at the same time, we are exploring any possibility of further support with the rural development programmes and horizon 2020. let me conclude by saying that maximum vigilance is essential now to preserve the agricultural economy in the area concerned and to prevent further spread in the rest of the european union.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution from the committee on the environment, public health and food safety because i share its concern that europe has the highest rates of alcohol consumption in the world, with excessive or harmful drinking being the third leading cause of preventable diseases and a risk factor for over 60 chronic diseases, including cancer and cardiovascular disease. the eu published a strategy in 2006 to cooperate with member states and other actors to coordinate actions to reduce alcohol-related harm. however, little action has been taken. this report calls on the new european commission to work towards this. since many of my group's requests for information and correct labelling of alcoholic products, as well as for greater regulation of advertising and the promotion of prevention campaigns among young people, were included in the text, i have decided to vote in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour because the proposal is based mainly on information campaigns, the promotion of healthy lifestyles, the long-term harmful effects of alcohol, age limits for alcohol consumption, etc. we believe that this raises the need for more information on labelling and for more regulation of advertising relating to alcohol and its derivatives. we do not, however, share the radical position of eliminating public aid without specifying specific cases to be taken into account, such as aid for agriculture.
in writing. ‒ i welcome this alcohol strategy. as a liberal i am in favour of better regulation and not over-regulation. i also want to stress that i am in favour of and support the wine and spirits industry. in my constituency back home there is a vibrant and very well-performing wine production, for example. i am also in favour of and welcome better transparency and better information for consumers. like with other products, displaying nutritional information on the bottle is a good thing, to make sure consumers can make informed choices. providing a list of ingredients and nutritional information can facilitate comparison and choice between alcoholic drinks. the wine and spirits industry already does a lot to advocate responsible drinking and correct behaviour. moreover, let me stress that it is already forbidden to advertise near schools or to target children. let me conclude by stressing that, as with other products, education and information is key. prohibition only creates a black market and does not solve binge-drinking problems, for example; on the contrary, it aggravates it.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution to ensure that the eu effectively combats alcoholism, with a social, economic and health approach.

in writing. ‒ i supported the resolution on the second anniversary of the rana plaza building collapse, firstly, to remember the more than 1 200 victims, the vast majority of whom were women, of accidents in the bangladeshi textile industry, in which more than 1 200 people were killed and injured; workshops that supplied companies such as adler modemarkte, ascena retail, carrefour, grabalok, j.c. penney, manifattura corona, nkd, pwt and yeszee; to demand that companies linked to rana plaza and the tazreen factory, which was burned down shortly before, provide the aid they owe to the victims, many of whom are unable to return to work and in need of medical care; to remind the importance of the bangladeshi government undertaking legislative reforms to ensure effective protection of the right to freedom of association and to freedom of labour for working people in their country, by pointing out the good will of the workers and by calling on the ilo and the eu to ensure that companies are held accountable for their actions and to provide compensation for the victims, because they fear that the ilo and the eu will not be able to provide adequate evidence of their good behaviour and to the victims.
in writing. ‒ as recalled in the resolution, on 24 april 2013 more than 1 100 people were killed and more than 2 500 injured in the collapse of rana plaza, a building housing several garment companies. the text clearly sets out the seriousness of these facts and the situation of labour rights in the clothing industry in developing and least developed countries. in the case of bangladesh, the restrictions on the right to strike and to join trade unions, especially in the export-free zones, the lack of labour inspections and the insufficiency of the minimum wage to cover the basic needs of the population are the main issues. it also focuses on the hypocrisy of multinationals such as adler modemarkte, ascena retail, carrefour, grabalok, j.c. penney, manifattura corona, nkd, pwt and yeszee, which have not yet contributed anything to the voluntary fund for compensation to victims and relatives despite their link with the accident. i have voted in favour of this resolution, which i share in a clear way.
in writing. ‒ i supported this resolution on the second anniversary of the rana plaza building collapse in bangladesh. i supported the amendment which detailed the names of the companies which have not yet assumed their responsibility towards the victims and, for this, it was also very important to approve the amendment which refers to the inclusion of a mandatory and enforceable clause on corporate social responsibility in the bilateral trade and investment agreements signed by the union.

in writing. ‒ the 2013 collapse of the rana plaza building housing several garment companies caused more than 1 100 deaths and some 2 500 injuries. positive steps have been taken to improve the situation of workers in bangladesh, such as the eu-led initiative to launch the pact, in order to ensure a new start in terms of occupational health and safety, working conditions, respect for labour rights and the promotion of responsible business behaviour in the bangladeshi garment industry. similarly, the authorities in bangladesh have made good progress, but there is still a long way to go in this field. the eu must be vigilant in fulfilling its obligations towards the bangladeshi workers.

in writing. ‒ our group has requested a statement from the commission, followed by a parliamentary resolution, on the second anniversary of the collapse of the rana plaza building in bangladesh, the fire at the tazreen complex in bangladesh and other consecutive tragedies which claimed the lives of over 1 200 workers in the textile industry in south-east asia - the vast majority of them women - who were producing for european and other western companies. the most prominent examples are spanish companies such as inditex, mango and el corte inglés, and others operating in spain such as h&d, benetton and primark. the disasters highlighted the terrible working conditions, health and safety conditions for people who produce the clothing of many of our major brands, as well as the lack of transparency in the supply chain. it took some of the companies weeks to find out if they had subcontractors with the workshops affected by these tragedies, and the compensation paid to the victims or their relatives arrived very late. in fact, to this day, the companies responsible still owe some nine million u.s. dollars to the compensation fund set up to assist the victims.

in writing. ‒ it is already two years since the collapse of the rana plaza building in savar, bangladesh, in which 1 134 people died and 2 500 were injured, many of whom were temporarily or permanently disabled. although working conditions and wages remain low, currently 200 fashion brands and retailers have signed the legally-binding agreement on security and fire protection of buildings. we welcome this first major milestone while issuing an urgent appeal to those who have not yet signed the appeal, especially those based in the eu. gradually there will be better working conditions worldwide.

in writing. ‒ the spanish socialists welcome the resolution adopted by parliament on the humanitarian drama of immigration in the mediterranean. it was the horror of the tragedy that moved the political groups to adopt a resolution which advanced european positions that had never been taken before: - the recognition that the abandonment of the mare nostrum mission and its replacement by the joint operation triton, with a smaller budget, was a serious mistake; - the commitment made by the member states to promote joint operations and increase naval resources with the aim of preventing further deaths at sea; - the consideration of the migration issue in north africa as an international humanitarian crisis which calls for a comprehensive policy, from the pacification and stability of those countries to the fight against mafias, from political development cooperation to a common asylum policy including the extension of the mandate of the easo; - the effective implementation of the solidarity of the member states for asylum seekers and refugees and their integration into our countries as a vital, legal, moral and democratic duty of our beliefs.
in writing. ‒ we understand that the tragedies and deaths in the mediterranean are a consequence of the 'europe fortress' that has been defended by the european institutions. that is why we voted against this resolution, which we regard as an attempt by the majority groups to wash their image. apart from failing to acknowledge the direct responsibility of european policies, the text speaks of the need to strengthen cooperation with third countries to combat immigration (which seems to be a veiled reference to the creation of detention centres in the countries on the southern shore of the mediterranean) and calls on the states to increase their contributions to frontex, an agency whose mission is not rescue but to combat the entry of people, despite the fact that many of these people may be asylum seekers. instead of strengthening these mechanisms, we should instead focus on guaranteeing humanitarian corridors and visas in the countries of origin for those fleeing violence, and on an international policy not based on warmongering or destabilising third countries, and on passing regulations to prevent the plundering of the natural resources of the south.

in writing. ‒ the horror of the tragedy has moved the political groups to adopt a resolution which advances european positions. i would like to highlight the following:- the recognition that the abandonment of the mare nostrum mission and its replacement by the joint operation triton, with a smaller budget, was a serious mistake; - the commitment made by the member states to promote joint operations and increase naval resources with the aim of preventing further deaths at sea;- the consideration of the migratory phenomenon in north africa as an international humanitarian crisis which calls for a comprehensive policy, from the pacification and stability of those countries to the fight against the mafias, from development cooperation to a common asylum policy including the extension of the mandate of easo;- the effective application of the solidarity of the member states to welcome asylum seekers and refugees and to integrate them into our countries as a vital moral, legal and democratic duty.
in writing. ‒ the terrible loss of human lives in the mediterranean by migrants trying to reach europe has deeply shocked us all. according to the international organisation for migration, more than 1,500 people have lost their lives in the mediterranean sea since the beginning of this year. smugglers and traffickers exploit irregular migration by showing a total disregard for human life. the eu and the member states must put the necessary resources into ensuring that their search and rescue obligations are fulfilled. the member states must also show solidarity with those states most exposed to the phenomenon of irregular immigration, since it is a serious problem affecting the whole union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the humanitarian tragedy of migration in the mediterranean because, in the face of the horror of the tragedy suffered, we have put forward european positions that have never been given before: - the recognition that the abandonment of the mare nostrum mission and its replacement by the joint operation triton, with a smaller budget, was a serious mistake; - the commitment made by the member states to promote joint operations and increase naval resources with the aim of avoiding further deaths at sea; - the consideration of the migration issue in north africa as an international humanitarian crisis that calls for a comprehensive policy, from pacification and stability of those countries to the fight against mafias, from development cooperation to a common asylum policy including the extension of the mandate of easo; - the effective implementation of the solidarity of the member states for asylum seekers and refugees and their integration into our countries as a vital, moral and democratic duty, as we believe.
in writing. ‒ the spanish socialists welcome the resolution adopted by parliament on the humanitarian drama of immigration in the mediterranean. it was the horror of the tragedy that moved the political groups to adopt a resolution which advanced european positions that had never been taken before: - the recognition that the abandonment of the mare nostrum mission and its replacement by the joint operation triton, with a smaller budget, was a serious mistake; - the commitment made by the member states to promote joint operations and increase naval resources with the aim of preventing further deaths at sea; - the consideration of the migration issue in north africa as an international humanitarian crisis which calls for a comprehensive policy, from the pacification and stability of those countries to the fight against mafias, from political development cooperation to a common asylum policy including the extension of the mandate of the easo; - the effective implementation of the solidarity of the member states for asylum seekers and refugees and their integration into our countries as a vital, legal, moral and democratic duty of our beliefs.
in writing. ‒ the recent deaths of migrants drowned in the mediterranean must serve as a stepping stone to the development of a genuine european migration policy. there are various dimensions in which we must act, and it is imperative to point out that a fundamental pillar of this policy must be the establishment of a european search and rescue fund covering the performance of these functions by the member states, both when they act individually and when they do so under the coordination of frontex. we cannot leave italy alone in the task of preventing the hundreds of deaths that have occurred in recent weeks. europe must also pursue the mafias that exploit vulnerable migrants, strengthen cooperation with countries of origin and transit, work towards the stabilisation of libya, promote voluntary return policies, implement the common european asylum system, and address, through its common foreign and security policy and its development cooperation policy, the root causes of migration.
in writing. ‒ after the tragedy in the mediterranean last week, the european union has reacted. the joint motion for a resolution negotiated by the epp, s&d, alde and greens/efa has several problems. it calls for the strengthening of frontex's activities and funding (including search and rescue operations), focuses on the issue of human trafficking, calls for the strengthening of cooperation with libya's neighbouring countries to combat criminal networks and is unable to make a single criticism of the european union's structural policy. it does not even criticise the limited mandate of triton, which operates no more than 30 nautical miles from the italian coast, which prevents assistance being provided to vessels that sink near libya. he talks about asylum protection as a voluntary matter. asylum protection cannot be a voluntary matter. it is an obligation the eu has assumed through a wide variety of international treaties. when the question of asylum is a voluntary one, we already know that many countries will not take it on, as is the case in spain (130 resettlements for the whole year). we abstained.
in writing. ‒ the spanish socialists welcome the resolution adopted by parliament on the humanitarian drama of immigration in the mediterranean. it was the horror of the tragedy that moved the political groups to adopt a resolution which advanced european positions that had never been taken before: - the recognition that the abandonment of the mare nostrum mission and its replacement by the joint operation triton, with a smaller budget, was a serious mistake; - the commitment made by the member states to promote joint operations and increase naval resources with the aim of preventing further deaths at sea; - the consideration of the migration issue in north africa as an international humanitarian crisis which calls for a comprehensive policy, from the pacification and stability of those countries to the fight against mafias, from political development cooperation to a common asylum policy including the extension of the mandate of the easo; - the effective implementation of the solidarity of the member states for asylum seekers and refugees and their integration into our countries as a vital, legal, moral and democratic duty of our beliefs.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this document relating to the recent tragedies in the mediterranean and the migration and asylum policies of the european union.
in writing. ‒ this is a debate with a resolution with representatives of the council and the commission to pay tribute to the victims of the tragedies and to analyse the results of the european council meeting of 23 april. on 19 april a shipwreck off the coast of libya shocked the whole of european public opinion. this is the greatest tragedy in the mediterranean to date, with between 700 and 900 people on board, of whom only 28 have been rescued, but unfortunately this is not an isolated incident. days later, two other barges with about 450 people on board were found adrift in the mediterranean. according to the unhcr, more than 1,600 people have died attempting this crossing so far this year. to deal with this situation, the european council held an extraordinary meeting on 23 april. they have made a commitment that combines solidarity measures with others to support the control work of countries that are on the migration route of these migrants to the mediterranean.
in writing. ‒ we understand that the tragedies and deaths in the mediterranean are a consequence of the 'europe fortress' that has been defended by the european institutions. that is why we voted against this resolution, which we regard as an attempt by the majority groups to wash their image. apart from failing to acknowledge the direct responsibility of european policies, the text speaks of the need to strengthen cooperation with third countries to combat immigration (which seems to be a veiled reference to the creation of detention centres in the countries on the southern shore of the mediterranean) and calls on the states to increase their contributions to frontex, an agency whose mission is not rescue but to combat the entry of people, despite the fact that many of these people may be asylum seekers. instead of strengthening these mechanisms, we should instead focus on guaranteeing humanitarian corridors and visas in the countries of origin for those fleeing violence, and on an international policy not based on warmongering or destabilising third countries, and on passing regulations to prevent the plundering of the natural resources of the south.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution calling on the european union and the member states to do everything possible to prevent further deaths at sea; i call on the eu and the member states to provide the necessary resources to ensure that search and rescue obligations are effectively met and to this end to receive the necessary funding and personnel in the short, medium and long term, under the coordination of frontex. in addition, the eu's border and security policy must be strengthened immediately and the functioning of frontex and the european asylum support office (easo) improved. the resolution also calls on the member states to work closely with europol, frontex, easo and eurojust to combat human traffickers and criminal networks for the illegal crossing of borders, and to detect and trace their funding.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the amendments to the suspension of the exceptional trade measures applied to bosnia and herzegovina because i consider that bosnia deserves special treatment in trade terms following the enlargement of the eu to croatia, which has significantly damaged the bosnian economy. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report amending regulation (ec) no 1215/2009 on exceptional trade measures for the balkan countries. the period of application of the regulation is extended until 2020 to extend the exceptional trade measures until that date, thus giving the western balkan countries and the eu sufficient time to adapt the preferences granted under the regulation to those provided for under the various ratified stabilisation and association agreements. in addition, it is envisaged that the preferences granted to bosnia and herzegovina will be suspended as from 1 january 2016 if bosnia and herzegovina fails to reach an agreement with the eu on the adaptation of trade concessions under the interim agreement to take account of the accession of croatia to the eu. the commission has also adopted a proposal for a regulation on the protection of the european union's financial interests against counterfeiting and for a regulation on the protection of the financial interests of the european union against counterfeiting and for a regulation on the protection of the financial interests of the european union against counterfeiting. on a socialist proposal, it was also possible to include a serious and systematic violation of labour rights as a reason for suspending preferences.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the amendments to the suspension of the exceptional trade measures applied to bosnia and herzegovina because i consider that bosnia deserves special treatment in trade terms following the enlargement of the eu to croatia, which has significantly damaged the bosnian economy. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environmentally friendly use of energy.
in writing. ‒ trade between the eu and the western balkan countries is liberalised through a series of stabilisation and association agreements and an interim agreement in the case of bosnia and herzegovina. following the accession of croatia to the eu, bosnia and herzegovina has not yet agreed to adapt the interim agreement to take account of its traditional preferential trade with that country under the central european free trade agreement, which had bound both countries since before 1 july 2013. after three rounds of negotiations with bosnia and herzegovina, it was not possible to reach an agreement. in view of the impasse in the negotiations and the damage to the eu's trade interests, the commission proposes that the extension of the autonomous trade measures for bosnia and herzegovina should not be automatic but should be conditional on the acceptance by bosnia and herzegovina of the eu methodology for the adaptation of the interim agreement.
in writing. ‒ we voted against, as it envisages the suspension of trade preferences (applicable in eight months) for access to the european market for products coming from bosnia. these are very sensitive agricultural products for bosnia. the bosnian economy is in tatters. bosnia suffers from a chronic large trade deficit and is under the imf programme. unemployment, and particularly youth unemployment, is at an outrageous rate. exactly one year ago, bosnia experienced its most violent social unrest since the war of the 1990s, and this is due to the economic situation. most of these problems - for which the eu is also responsible - are due to the post-war constitutional configuration. other balkan countries have accepted the 'technical adaptation' of their stabilisation and association agreement, but we must not forget that bosnia is not like any other balkan country and that, moreover, its prospect of accession is long term, unlike the rest of the balkan countries. we believe that three rounds of negotiations are not enough. we believe that in this case a more flexible solution can be found which is not based on traditional trade.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of postponing the vote so that an agreement can be reached in the tripartite dialogue.
in writing. ‒ in 2003, bosnia and herzegovina was granted the status of potential candidate country for eu membership, and in 2008 signed a stabilisation and association agreement committing itself to meeting the eu's conditions for membership. an interim agreement on trade and trade-related matters has since been applied to bosnia and herzegovina, pending the completion of the ratification process of the stabilisation and association agreement. the inta report highlights the progress made by the western balkan countries towards closer integration with the eu and calls on the eu and bosnia and herzegovina to seek agreement on the adaptation of the interim agreement with the eu in order to avoid the suspension of preferences. in addition, it was agreed in the inta committee that the commission's decision to suspend preferences, in case of non-compliance with the conditions laid down in the regulation, should be made by delegated act and not by implementing act.

in writing. ‒ we abstained from voting on the report on developments in bosnia and herzegovina in 2014, as we believe that its approach does not correspond to our perspective on the balkan countries. one reason is the insistence of the various parliamentary groups (which are opposed to our position) on increasing pressure on these countries to carry out structural reforms in the economic, social and political spheres. we reject these reforms as a precondition for their future accession to the european union. however, and despite this, the report includes a commitment to intensify regional cooperation, particularly in the face of natural disasters and catastrophes affecting bosnia and herzegovina.

in writing. ‒ the resolution condemns in the strongest terms the deliberate terrorist attack perpetrated by al shabab on 2 april 2015 in garissa, in which 147 university students were killed and 79 others were injured. we condemn all violations of human rights, in particular when people are killed on the basis of their religion, beliefs and ethnic origin. freedom of religion is a fundamental right and we strongly condemn any violence or discrimination on religious grounds. i voted in favour of the resolution adopted because the violence in nigeria and kenya reveals that terrorism is a threat that requires a global solution. we socialists believe that the eu should promote religious freedom and inter-religious tolerance, and support kenya and nigeria in addressing the root causes of radicalisation. bombings, suicide bombings, sexual slavery and other forms of violence, as well as kidnappings by terrorist sects in africa, constitute crimes against humanity.
in writing. ‒ i share the unequivocal condemnation by this resolution of the massacre committed on 2 april by the terrorist group al shabab in the attack on the university campus in the kenyan city of garissa, near the border with somalia, a massacre in which 148 people, mainly students, were killed. i have voted against this text because it does not address the underlying problem in the region and does not take account of fundamental factors such as the united states' military intervention in somalia in 1992 with disastrous consequences for the peoples of the region, the responsibility of the former colonial powers for promoting conflict and plundering the natural resources of the horn of africa, land grabbing, high rates of poverty, hundreds of thousands of refugees, infant mortality, hunger and malnutrition. the eu is also committed to the protection of the rights of the palestinian people, and to the protection of the rights of the palestinian people.

in writing. ‒ in recent months we have witnessed too many times the barbarity of jihadist terrorism in syria, iraq, libya and kenya, a barbarity which often focuses on the persecution of religious minorities, especially christians. the murder of students in kenya is but a drop in the ocean of crimes against christians. christians are one of the groups most affected by the violence of jihadist terrorist groups, and this community, with centuries of history in iraq and syria, is forced to flee their countries to save their lives. the question we must ask ourselves is how long will we look the other way, how long will we raise our voices for those who do not have it and are persecuted in their home countries because of their religious status. peaceful coexistence is not only desirable, but possible in view of the centuries of common history. we must fight with all the tools at our disposal to eradicate the scourge of jihadist terrorism and guarantee to all people the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion.

in writing. ‒ the resolution put to the vote contained positive elements, such as condemnation of the destruction of cultural, archaeological and religious sites by the militias of the islamic state (is) organisation in syria and iraq, the countries most punished for their activities. the eu authorities are also called upon to tackle the illicit trafficking of such goods, which is a source of funding for the is. however, i could not vote in favour of this resolution, as it appeals to the eu's security and defence policy without acknowledging or even mentioning the responsibility of the eu states in promoting the breeding ground for the situation, promoting conflict and war in iraq and syria, and facilitating the funding and access to arms that have given rise to is.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this parliament resolution because it strongly condemns the deliberate destruction of cultural, archaeological and religious sites by the islamic state in syria and iraq, which the director-general of unesco has defined as 'cultural cleansing'. the resolution calls for a focus on preventing and combating the illicit trafficking of cultural property, in particular cultural heritage objects illegally exported from iraq since 6 august 1990 and from syria since 15 march 2011, as, as unesco itself has warned, the looting and smuggling of objects and places of cultural and religious interest in syria and iraq, in particular by is/daesh, is being used to help finance the terrorist activities of that group. it is therefore urgent to take the necessary measures to curb the destruction and looting of heritage and to extend the category of crimes against humanity to include acts which deliberately damage or destroy on a large scale the cultural heritage of mankind.

in writing. ‒ the terrorist group is/daesh is not only committing crimes against humanity in the territories it dominates, it also aims to erase the history of civilization by destroying priceless cultural sites in syria and iraq. this cultural cleansing aims to erase all cultural signs of civilizations before the rise of islam, thus ending the cultural identity of many communities. as unesco states, the proceeds of looting and smuggling of objects and places of cultural and religious interest in syria and iraq in particular are being used to help finance the terrorist activities of this group. the illegal trafficking of cultural goods must be combated to put an end to the smuggling and plundering of the heritage of syria and iraq and to end a major source of funding for jihadist terrorism. we must also fight to bring the members of this terrorist group to international justice.
in writing. ‒ the destruction of the common heritage of humanity is not only a war crime, but also a crime against humanity. the eu must urgently take action to prevent terrorist groups such as the islamic state from using the destruction of museums, civil and religious buildings and archaeological sites to destabilise the population and destroy their identity, as is currently happening in iraq or syria. in addition, terrorists sometimes use the looting of archaeological sites and the illegal trafficking of cultural objects - which have one of the main destinations on the european market - to finance their activities in conflict zones. to combat this phenomenon, coordinated action is needed by the eu, international institutions such as unesco, the world customs organization, interpol or europol, and the member states.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this joint resolution as we believe it is an important issue, not only because of the issue of the destruction of cultural heritage, but also because of the artifacts that have been looted and subsequently used to finance the terrorist operations of isis/daesh, among others. in this sense, cultural artefacts have been turned into weapons of war. in fact, the illicit trafficking of cultural goods is the third largest illegal trade in the world - after drug and arms trafficking - and therefore requires a strong political stance from the european parliament. we believe that the joint resolution is along those lines and we therefore support it.

in writing. ‒ numerous archaeological, religious and cultural sites in syria, iraq and tunisia have recently been the subject of deliberate destruction by extremist groups linked, in particular, to the islamic state of iraq and syria (is/daesh). it is true that the fight against illegal trade in cultural goods is not a specific competence of the eu, as it is not enshrined as such in the treaties, but nevertheless the fight against this illegal trade is included in several areas of eu competence, such as the internal market, the area of freedom, security and justice, culture and the common foreign and security policy. i therefore voted in favour of this resolution, calling for a rapid and secure exchange of information and sharing of best practice among member states with a view to effectively combating the illegal trade in cultural property; and calling on the eu to take action, in collaboration with unesco and the international criminal court, to extend the category of crimes against humanity recognised by international law to include acts that deliberately destroy the cultural heritage of mankind on a large scale.

in writing. ‒ the resolution adopted condemns the human rights situation in the maldives, especially as regards the media and civil society. it also highlights the situation of former president mohamed nasheed, who is in prison under the anti-terrorism law. i could not vote in favour of this resolution because it seeks to protect the political process in that country, including the balance of forces which must prevail. europe's experience in this field is extensive, and its results are poor.
in writing. ‒ the political situation in the maldives has deteriorated over the past few months, with constant protests, clashes between protesters and police, and dozens of arrests by the authorities - which organizations such as amnesty international have denounced - are trying to muzzle peaceful protesters and silence critical media and civil society. abuses are also being recorded in the judicial system, such as the case of former president mohamed nasheed, whose trial began the day after his arrest and whose conviction was handed down after nineteen days of trial. the united nations high commissioner for human rights has not hesitated to criticize that this process contravenes maldivian laws and international standards for a fair trial. in view of this situation, it is urgent that the parties involved avoid any action that could aggravate the situation, that violence against peaceful protests be brought to an end and that those who have perpetrated violent attacks against them be prosecuted. it also urges the political forces to behave in accordance with democratic standards and to cease any attempts to intimidate the political opposition in order to return the maldives to the path of transition to democracy.

in writing. ‒ on 13 march 2015, the former president of the maldives, mohamed nasheed, was sentenced to 13 years in prison on terrorism charges for ordering the arrest of the then chief judge of the criminal court in january 2012. it is also highly worrying that opposition politicians continue to be routinely intimidated. to these disturbing developments must be added that at least 140 peaceful protesters have been arrested since february. we must demand the immediate release of former president mohamed nasheed. the european parliament must express its concern at the growing trend towards an authoritarian regime in the maldives and the repression of the political opposition.
in writing. ‒ on april 23, a report by amnesty international was published that says human rights in the maldives are in free fall and accuses the authorities of muzzling peaceful protesters, silencing critical media and civil society, while abusing the judicial system to imprison opposition politicians. the rise of religious vigilante groups allegedly in collusion with the police is mentioned, which has brought with it an increase in kidnappings and attacks on social gatherings in recent years, particularly against those accused of promoting atheism. the current situation may also have implications for the country's economy, which is heavily dependent on foreign tourists. the tourism sector is the backbone of the maldivian economy, as it represents a significant part of the national income and its foreign exchange reserves.
in writing. the maldives is a symbol of holiday comfort for most of my countrymen, but now there is a real political drama taking place there with many aspects of human rights violations. i am therefore concerned about the current proceedings with the representatives of the former maldivian government, which emerged from a democratic election and whose end is still shrouded in uncertainty. the very fact that former president nasheed was sentenced to 13 years in prison for terrorism, and is accused of wrongfully dismissing the chief justice, confirms doubts about the rule of law in this asian country. that is why i support the resolution before us today.

in writing. ‒ this resolution reiterates the eu's unequivocal commitment to bosnia and herzegovina and to the country's territorial integrity, sovereignty and unity, while stressing that this country will not be a candidate for eu membership until appropriate institutional conditions have been established. the european union is also calling for the establishment of a european union-wide network of information and communication networks. it also urges political leaders to refrain from the divisive nationalist and secessionist rhetoric that has polarized society, stressing that the socioeconomic needs of citizens must be the priority. for all these reasons, i support this resolution and the eu's renewed approach to bosnia and herzegovina, which i see as a new opportunity to resume its reform process and improve the country's social and economic situation. this opportunity must not be missed. ensuring a better life for its citizens must be bosnia and herzegovina's political priority in the context of its european integration process.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe it contains important positive elements, such as the need to strengthen credit support to small and medium-sized enterprises; to strengthen the governance and administrative resources of the eib to avoid a repeat of the financial and tax scandals it has been the protagonist of in the past; to channel funds towards initiatives to create jobs, improve energy efficiency or research and development. however, there are still significant risks in the eib's activities, in particular its association with the juncker plan (a public guarantee which seems designed to encourage private speculation in large transport or energy projects, as was the case with the eib's activity in castor) or its lack of transparency in relation to cohesion and development policies, which will require greater scrutiny of its activities by parliament.
in writing. ‒ the castor project was approved in 2008 as a natural gas reservoir. the project never came to fruition because of the earthquakes, and the spanish government approved compensation of 1 350 million to the company and the termination of the concession to operate the warehouse. the eib, through the pbce (project bond credit enhancement) programme, supported the project by upgrading its credit rating and thus enabling it to obtain capital market financing. we consider that the eib and the commission did not take into account the risk of increased seismic activity linked to the injection of gas, despite the existence of studies which clearly warn of the potential dangers of this operation. we therefore urge the commission and the eib to take steps to prevent the spanish people from having to pay, either through a higher public deficit or through higher energy costs, eur 1 300 million in compensation for a project that has been preceded by a disastrous evaluation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which highlights the increase in eib financing activities by 37%, but also concerns about economic stagnation in the eu and, in particular, the significant decline in public and private investment and the dizzying 35% fall in lending to smes between 2008 and 2013, which is hampering economic recovery, job creation and the reduction of inequality and poverty. the report makes recommendations on how the eib can play a key role in stimulating investment in europe. it noted that the european fund for strategic investments gives priority to projects with european added value, with positive cost-benefit analyses and with the greatest possible impact on job creation. it also urged the eib to look at the fall in sme financing and to continue to increase its lending capacity for innovative smes and start-ups. it also regretted the poor risk assessment of the eib and the commission in the castor project and urged both to take steps to avoid the spanish citizens having to pay eur 1.3 billion for this failed project. finally, greater transparency is required.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe it contains important positive elements, such as the need to strengthen credit support to small and medium-sized enterprises; to strengthen the governance and administrative resources of the eib to avoid a repeat of the financial and tax scandals it has been the protagonist of in the past; to channel funds towards initiatives to create jobs, improve energy efficiency or research and development. however, there are still significant risks in the eib's activities, in particular its association with the juncker plan (a public guarantee which seems designed to encourage private speculation in large transport or energy projects, as was the case with the eib's activity in castor) or its lack of transparency in relation to cohesion and development policies, which will require greater scrutiny of its activities by parliament.
in writing. ‒ the european investment bank (eib) is a key european institution, particularly in this context of low private investment, and for its role in the investment plan for europe. the eib cannot operate under the logic of a private investment bank, which means that its main objective must not be to maintain the triple a, but to act as a real development bank, investing in the most deprived areas, providing capital and reinforced technical assistance. it is also important to monitor and evaluate more thoroughly the impact of the projects financed so that we can identify their contribution to the member states' macroeconomic picture. i would also like to point out that the eib's debt issues are the only example to date of european public debt, but, nevertheless, citizens cannot directly purchase the eib's bonds. it would be very positive if the eib were to issue government bonds with retail tranches, particularly under the european fund for strategic investments (efsi). finally, it is important that the culture of greater risk-taking that is attributed to the efsi permeates the eib, and not the other way around.
in writing. ‒ in the face of the severe economic crisis affecting many eu countries, it is essential that all possible eu and member state resources, including those of the eib, are effectively mobilised to promote and strengthen public and private investment and boost competitiveness. the eib is an instrument designed to strengthen social cohesion and provide valuable support to member states. the eib should continue to play its role as a catalyst for financing secure long-term public and private investments. more efforts should also be made to finance smes. we must remember that the eib is called upon to play a decisive role in financing the investment plan for europe, with the allocation of eur 5 billion for the creation of the new european fund for strategic investments. the european parliament adopted the report on spain, with a clear criticism of the government for the cost of the failed castor project, and called on the commission and the eib to take steps to avoid the spanish citizens having to pay eur 1.3 billion in compensation.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report, which critically examines the role played by the eib in financing projects which have been beneficial to a majority and harmful to the social majorities. in particular, he mentions the castor project and the compensation approved by the congress of deputies to acs (florentino pérez) for over-costs arising from poor technical and business management, which will make citizens pay, dangerously increasing energy poverty.

in writing. ‒ the report proposes a number of recommendations on the eib's operational methodology, in relation to how the eib can play an important role in stimulating investment in europe. the importance of the eib's ability to finance smes is also stressed, and the importance of investments in strategic infrastructure and in projects aimed at sustainable energy and the fight against climate change is emphasised. finally, from spain's point of view, it should be noted that the report includes a criticism of the unsuccessful castor project, the first project to be carried out with the so-called "project bonds" which resulted in multi-million-dollar compensation from the spanish treasury to the successful bidder. i agree with these considerations and have therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the eib is not a commercial bank and must continue to play its essential role as a catalyst for financing secure public and private long-term investments, while continuing to apply best banking prudential practices in order to maintain its strong capital position, with the consequent positive impact on borrowing conditions. i voted in favour of this proposal, which calls on the eib to engage, together with parliaments, governments and the social partners, in a structured communication process to identify on a regular basis specific job creation initiatives which will make it possible to increase european competitiveness in a sustainable way and contribute to growth and employment, and in particular youth employment.
in writing. ‒ my vote in favour of a critical report on the european investment bank, even after the 'scrubbing' of the margins of parliamentary logic. without such a 'chaplain', the question would be whether the eib is fulfilling its founding mission when, on the basis of risk-free thinking, it fails to properly assess projects and ends up giving money to those who do not need it or to those who assume the possible losses in the event of failure. we fear that the castor project is not the exception, but the rule for the eib.
in writing. ‒ the annual report on the european investment bank highlights the importance of this institution and its decisive role in facilitating access to finance for european companies, as well as the need for an increase in the case of smes. upyd demands an urgent review of the rules on the evaluation and control mechanisms of projects so that failures as resounding as the castor project are not repeated. we also ask the european commission to investigate the aid granted by the spanish government to the castor project.

in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution is the result of an oral question to the european commission on behalf of the committee on agriculture. the facts concern the holding of the 2015 expo in milan under the title of "feeding the planet, energy for life". the resolution focuses on different aspects of this expo related to the idea of improving food production and distribution, tackling food waste and promoting new approaches to tackling the challenge of malnutrition. but it does not include such important issues as the human right to water, to food sovereignty or the right to land. i therefore voted against, because i cannot hold events which are organised and run by a large number of multinationals, such as the barilla foundation or nestlé, which, far from fighting to 'feed the planet', are fighting to feed their economic profits. so the expo is presented as the catwalk of the multinational food companies, but only of those who own control of food worldwide, who produce globalized junk food simultaneously creating millions of hungry and millions of obese.
in writing. ‒ i have voted in favour of this resolution on the 2015 world expo 'feeding the planet, energy for life', which will open its doors in milan in may 2015. the eu will have a significant presence under its flag and, through this resolution, the commission is asked about the measures envisaged to improve food production and security of supply, combating the scarcity of natural resources and promoting research and sustainable forms of agriculture; combating food waste throughout the agri-food supply chain, with ambitious, clear and binding targets, and promoting healthy food and quality standards in the field of nutrition, both in terms of research and education incentivizing responsible and healthy lifestyles and through the development of policies to eradicate malnutrition and prevent obesity.
