in writing. ‒ this resolution strongly condemning the violence perpetrated by the terrorist group boko haram in nigeria emphasises the social and economic causes of the conflict in the country with the largest economy in the african continent which, however, is one of the most unequal in the world, where less than 10% of the population controls 90% of the wealth. it therefore calls for the fight against poverty, inequality, lack of educational opportunities and lack of access to health care by promoting an equitable distribution of oil revenues. it also congratulated the nigerian people on the holding of their last elections, called for the release of those kidnapped by boko haram, in particular more than 2 000 women and girls, condemned the recruitment of child soldiers and called for women victims of sexual violence to have access to adequate sexual and reproductive health services and for the necessary medical assistance to be provided to the sick and injured without distinction. it also reiterated its call for the repeal of the law criminalising homosexuality and the death penalty. i have therefore voted in favour of this text.
in writing. ‒ april 14 marks the first anniversary of the kidnapping of 276 chibok schoolgirls for whom little progress has been made in their release. the brutal actions of boko haram have made it a real regional threat, leading to increased cooperation between nigeria, cameroon, chad and niger. the numbers are alarming, with more than 10,000 deaths since 2009, more than half of them in 2014. in the recent presidential elections there has been a change in power and former general muhammadu buhari has been elected, who has as a priority the fight against violence. the eu is committed to supporting regional efforts to combat this threat, which has led to large movements of refugees and internally displaced persons. the fundamental issue of the fight against barbarism has led me to support this resolution which, among other issues, calls on the nigerian government to promote the participation of women in the public sphere and political life and reiterates the call of the european parliament for the repeal of the law against homosexuality and the death penalty.

in writing. ‒ nigeria is undoubtedly a country of contrasts: the most populous country in africa, with huge oil reserves, but whose wealth is not enjoyed by a large part of the population. it is also a country with great ethnic and religious diversity, which suffers from the horrors of terrorism in the north of the country due to the actions of the terrorist group boko haram, a serious threat to the security of the entire region. the new president of nigeria must firmly fight terrorism, as well as work for the social and economic development of the northern and southern states in order to address the problems of poverty, inequality, educational opportunities and access to healthcare, which are one of the causes of the spiral of violence. for our part, the eu must provide political, humanitarian and development aid in all areas to nigeria, as well as in the fight against boko haram.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the resolution on the situation in nigeria, condemning the rising tide of violence in the country caused by the actions of boko haram, which are causing a large number of civilian casualties. the resolution also recognises the importance of mobilising domestic resources through fair tax systems that enable the redistribution of wealth and the benefit of natural resources as a key element in eliminating inequality and ensuring good governance and reducing the violence that inequality itself generates. the resolution also recognises the importance of defending the rights of women and lgbt groups threatened by the growing situation of violence.

on behalf of the alde group. mr president, commissioner, i would like to thank you for your reply. nadiya savchenko was the only ukrainian soldier on a peacekeeping mission in iraq, the first pilot of the armed forces of ukraine, an example of determination and progress for her country. nadiya is a member of the ukrainian parliament and a member of the parliamentary assembly of the council of europe: she is entitled to immunity and diplomatic privileges. nadiya is the victim of a purely political detention which violates the european convention on human rights, signed by russia, in particular the right to liberty and security and the right to a fair trial. implementing the minsk agreements implies the release of all hostages and persons detained in connection with the conflict in ukraine. what are international protocols and agreements for? we cannot give in to blackmail from anyone or we will lose credibility and reason for being. the european union and the member states must immediately demand that the russian federation fully comply with all its international commitments, including the minsk agreements, and immediately release ms savchenko and return her to her homeland. nadiya means hope. let's give him a reason to have it.
author. mr president, solidarity is not a schizophrenic concept - it depends on where it occurs - but the same. the syrian government has been bombing yarmouk for three years, and the siege has been very severe, with a partial blockade, which has caused hundreds of deaths: 160 000 palestinians, as a result of the ethnic cleansing of northern palestine. for more than ten years gaza has been under a total blockade, with relentless bombardments that have killed thousands. the difference is that in one case it is a criminal regime and a terrorist organization, and in the other, a regime that acts in a similar way, but which we call democratic. blockading and bombing civilians is the same crime, whoever does it, and solidarity must be the same: in yarmouk and in gaza. i hope - and i despair - that we in this parliament will have the same sensitivity to gaza as we have to yarmouk, a solidarity which i welcome.
i would just like to say, mr president, that i welcome the motion for a resolution that is being debated here. i think the proposal is well balanced. of course, it is necessary to write in the introduction and call on the parties to the civil war in syria to stop attacking the yarmouk camp, which is objectively one of the darkest, saddest places on the planet today and a huge humanitarian disaster is taking place there. but i'm afraid he's going to stick to words. what is important, and what i consider to be concrete support and assistance, is that the european union, specifically the european commission, is releasing eur 2.5 million and that this money will be used to support people suffering from the civil war in syria and specifically in the yarmouk camp. the question is how much is enough, i think there should be a debate in the future whether this amount should not be increased, and we should also be very strongly calling and calling - and this is also in this document - for the mainly hostile parties to allow the international humanitarian organizations the money that is thus freed to use it for concrete humanitarian aid and to deliver it to those who need this humanitarian aid. otherwise, it will be just words, there will be money, but no concrete help will be provided. i therefore welcome and support the motion for a resolution.
i am not going to go into the details of the commission's proposals. the population of yarmouk has been under siege for more than two years by the forces of bashar al-assad and, since april, by the so-called islamic state. a humanitarian catastrophe that shows the inability of the international community to stop the killing and to get through the siege of yarmouk. yarmuk symbolizes the absence of international support for democratic processes in syria and the rest of the region, which has strengthened both dictatorships and extremist groups. it also symbolises the lack of a solution to the occupation of palestine, which would require, among other things, compliance with the un resolution calling on israel to accept the return of palestinian refugees. any solution must begin with the lifting of the blockade imposed by the regime, the entry of humanitarian aid and dialogue between the palestinian militias. the international community and the united nations must meet their responsibilities. in this sense, the european union must assume its responsibility towards the refugees arriving on our shores from syria.

member of the commission.– mr president, benchmarks may sound like a minor technical issue, but in fact they go to the heart of the financial services sector and to the economy more widely. they are the basis on which financial contracts are priced. they determine the value of great numbers of financial products, including the interest rates paid on many mortgages. the investment and pension funds in which citizens save for their future use benchmarks to determine their value or their performance. so it follows that we need to be able to trust benchmarks, but a sequence of scandals has badly undermined confidence – and let us not forget that this is not a victimless crime. for me, manipulating benchmarks is the same as stealing. so that is why, to rebuild trust, we proposed that benchmark providers should be properly regulated and supervised; that they should put governance controls in place and manage conflicts of interest; that they should make benchmark setting more transparent and ensure that contributors to benchmark setting are appropriately overseen. for critical benchmarks with cross-border impacts, we also propose setting up colleges of national supervisors, involving the european securities and markets authority (esma). this will ensure appropriate oversight and the continuous availability of these benchmarks by requiring contributions from firms if needed. this has not been an easy file, but it is a critical one, and i would very much like to congratulate ms van nieuwenhuizen on the skill with which she has taken it forward. i look forward to discussing some issues further in trilogue. the broad scope of the legislation means that it needs to be appropriate both for big and for small benchmarks, and although our proposal had elements of proportionality, the committee on economic and monetary control has proposed a more risk-based approach for non-critical benchmarks. i am grateful for your thinking on this and look forward to helping to strike the right balance. as the eu will be the first jurisdiction to establish such a wide-ranging benchmark regulation, we must also address the question of access for third-country benchmarks, and while we want to keep our borders open, we must avoid importing risks linked to benchmarks that are not robust. here again i look forward to discussing how we can achieve those objectives. overall, i think that this is another important step in making sure that we have the building blocks for a strong financial system in place. now we need to put these measures into effect.
on behalf of the s&d group. mr president, first of all i would like to congratulate the rapporteur and all the alternative rapporteurs who have been negotiating this regulation over the last few months, which i believe substantially improves the commission's initial proposal. the position of my group - the socialist group - has been to improve the monitoring and regulation of critical indices and, in this respect, in the text to be voted on tomorrow we have achieved a definition of a qualitative critical index which allows the definition of national critical indices. in addition, since these critical indices are a 'public good' - as our colleague mrs matias said - they will be able to be subject to a reasonable price controlled by the supervisor and, in addition, these critical indices will have a college of competent authorities chaired by esma thanks to the text which this parliament will approve. we are therefore very pleased with the regulation we have achieved so that critical indices (euribor, libor - the big indices that put financial stability at risk) can be subject to stricter regulation and so that, in addition, commodity indices can also be defined as critical. in return, it is true that the negotiations have been complicated and we have had to make concessions in some respects. the proportionality of which the rapporteur and others before me have spoken implies that non-critical indices will be somewhat less restrictive in their regulation. but it is true that, thanks to our group, the national competent authorities will have the capacity to monitor how the managers of these non-critical indices perform their work with a subsequent analysis in the reports of the way in which these indices are compiled. finally, we have reached an agreement to make the indices produced in third countries comply with ioc rules. it is more than what we had before, it is not all that we would have liked, but we believe that it is a great agreement that will allow consumers, european citizens, to have much more robust and much more serious indices.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, mr hill, you mentioned that manipulating is the same as stealing. i want to talk to you about the irph and this regulation, which should be designed precisely with the specific aim of reducing the risk of manipulation of benchmarks. however, the minimum requirements laid down by the new rules are very basic and even then the irph would not meet them. for example, it is required to make public the data used to compile the index, which is not the case with the irph, on the grounds that it is secret data. moreover, the irph is not representative of the market and is not subject to the law of supply and demand, which would not meet two other minimum requirements. this parliament must prevent families with fewer resources from being forced to pay up to 300 euros more than mortgages using the euribor as a benchmark. the irph is clearly abusive. it's driving affected families first into misery and then into eviction. this regulation cannot leave any loophole which would allow this abusive index to continue to be applied by banks.

vice-president of the commission. – mr president, i would like to thank parliament for the invitation to deliver a commission statement on the tobacco agreements. these agreements have been introduced with the support of this house as an instrument in our fight against cigarette smuggling, with the first one signed in 2004. then, and now, parliament has been our key ally in the fight against cigarette smuggling, a criminal act that siphons away money from our budgets. we know the data: around eur 10 billion are lost every year as a result of smuggling, which impacts primarily on our member states but also on the eu budget. just to put this in perspective, our 28 member states in 2013 had fiscal income from legal cigarette sales of over eur 90 billion. that means that because of this criminal activity they have lost more than 10% of income that would have benefited their citizens, and that makes fighting cigarette smuggling financially very important. we also recognise the negative impact on our public health policies. legislative restrictions in the eu and national level prices are designed to deter smoking, and to protect citizens, especially youngsters. in contrast, illicit tobacco products are available, including to young people, at a substantial illegal discount. there is also a security dimension, since cigarette smuggling is one of the main sources of revenue for organised crime, and on 28 april we adopted a new european agenda for security, disrupting the access of organised crime to revenue from various smuggling activities, including the cigarette trade, which is part of this fight. parliament has strongly supported lifting this fight to a global level. why? because cigarette smuggling is a global phenomenon and therefore it requires a global solution. what we now have is the protocol to the who framework convention on tobacco control and i am very pleased to inform you that on 4 may the commission adopted a decision proposing that the council ratify it. we do recognise, however, that ratification will take time. so far, out of the minimum requirement of 40 ratifications for the protocol to enter into force we only have seven. in addition, even if we are to reach the 40 ratification requirement, we do not yet know whether the key sources and transit countries will actually sign up to the protocol. i can assure you that we in the commission take very seriously our role of encouraging exactly those countries to be amongst those ratifying in a timely manner. we are also advancing a timely implementation of the tobacco products directive. however, this directive cannot play an effective role in controlling cigarette smuggling from outside the eu. it is in this context of the limitations, at this moment in time, on what we would like to pursue as the long-term solution that we are looking at other instruments at our disposal. one such instrument can also be the anti-fraud agreements with the major tobacco companies. as i mentioned, the first was signed in 2004. it was with philip morris international (pmi). it will expire in july 2016. this agreement introduced innovative concepts like track and trace, due diligence – you need to know to whom you sell, you also have to make that information accessible – and anti-money laundering provisions. pmi agreed to pay usd 1.25 billion, of which slightly more than 90 % – 90.3 % – went to our member states. the agreement is legally binding and enforceable. its contractual nature allows for elements to be included which would not have been easily available by legislative means, and in particular seizure payments without proof of fault. they offer an additional financial incentive to compliance. my predecessor, former commissioner šemeta, has already informed parliament that we had brief exploratory meetings with pmi as required by the agreement, at which point pmi expressed interest in discussing a prolongation. we are also analysing the situation in light of evolving trends in illicit trade. we know that the cheap whites are our biggest threat now, not those that come from these big companies, and we are also looking at how the development in the regulatory landscape which i have already mentioned would impact our judgement on how to approach the future of this agreement. we are going to finalise an assessment in a couple of weeks and, of course, we will make it available to parliament and the public. there are some facts that are very clear: that the main objective of the pmi agreement – to reduce the presence of smuggled pmi products on the eu black market – has been achieved. between 2006 and 2014 the volume of illegal pmi products seized by member states under the agreement dropped by 85% and that substantially exceeds the overall downward trend in seizures. this drop applies equally to both genuine and counterfeit pmi products. we are currently considering the next steps forward in this dossier, guided by our commitment to fight the illicit trade and serve the interests of our citizens. i want to state very clearly that we are very open on how we are going to end this, and in this sense my being here with you this evening is very important as an input that you will provide in our deliberations. i will keep you duly informed as we progress on this very important and very sensitive topic. i would like to end by thanking the greens for their initiative, including mr geier, who i know is very interested in this matter. actually, i realise he is not a green but would like to thank him for his interest, for which i am very grateful.

in writing. the court of justice of the eu distinguishes between printed books, which are goods, and electronic books, which it considers a service. the court of justice has therefore reminded france and luxembourg in a judgment of 5 march that they cannot unilaterally impose a reduced vat rate on e-books, thus failing to comply with the relevant directive and their obligation as member states. however, as a reader, writer and politician, i believe that a book is a book. and it is so regardless of its format, the material it is composed of and the way it is reproduced to reach the reader while serving to carry out its essential cultural task: the dissemination of human knowledge. the alde group has asked for this matter to be placed on the agenda for the plenary. for years parliament has been asking the commission to correct this error, this absurd misunderstanding which prevents member states from truly harmonizing the vat legislation on digital and printed books. this must continue, not only in line with the requirements of the european digital single market, but also because the publishing industry in europe is in serious danger.

in writing. ‒ this report concerns the codification of regulation (eec) no 2481/72 of 19 december 1972 on the safeguard measures provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the swiss confederation. a new regulation is intended to bring together a number of events held between the two parties over the years. although it is presented as a question relating, rather than to the content, to the legal certainty of the union's acts on relations between the signatory parties, i have chosen to abstain in the vote because, in essence, these agreements are concluded to satisfy the interests of the large multinationals and always harm the majority of people on both sides.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the codification of regulation (eec) no 2481/72 of 19 december 1972 on the safeguard measures provided for in the agreement between the european economic community and the swiss confederation. a new regulation is intended to bring together a number of events held between the two parties over the years. as this is a question of the legal certainty of the union's acts on relations between the signatory parties, rather than of their content, i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because it is an authorisation for the council to conclude, on behalf of the union, the european convention on the legal protection of services based on conditional access or conditional access. the convention, initiated by the council of europe, refers to audiovisual and information society services which are subject to a fee or conditional access, particularly in terms of illegal reception for commercial purposes, which can also cause problems for public television and broadcasting services. these public services are of particular interest to us and we believe they should be given special protection, and we therefore feel that the convention does not adequately address this aspect. however, its celebration is a positive step towards ending illegal access to audiovisual services. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the eu ratifying the european convention on the legal protection of services based on conditional access or access-based services, which will allow the scope of the legal framework established by directive 98/84/ec to be extended and thus effectively combat infringements of protected services. the need for extensive and effective protection of these services is particularly relevant, as many non-eu european states can be safe havens for the development and dissemination of conditional access-based service piracy devices, as their legal systems do not provide for any sanctions for this very specific type of piracy activity. it was therefore appropriate to extend the scope of the provisions of directive 98/84/ec by this convention and to create a common and effective framework at european level for the protection of those services. this directive created a common eu-wide framework to combat illicit devices that enable unauthorised access to pay-tv services and to effectively protect these services. this protection covers both traditional television and radio broadcasting and transmission via the internet.

in writing. ‒ the spanish socialist delegation voted in favour of this report because it calls for strict regulation of the benchmarks used in financial contracts. we welcome the inclusion of the following socialist priorities:- to extend the consideration of critical indices, allowing indices below the nominal value proposed by the commission and the council to be declared critical;- to include raw material indices in the articulation, thus strengthening their regulation and allowing them to also be declared critical;- to ensure that national supervisors can enforce compliance with the requirements laid down in the regulation also for non-critical indices; - to improve the transparency and robustness of the methodology used for its compilation; and- to strengthen the role of esma in the monitoring of critical indices. our group is committed to the complete elimination of any doubts about the integrity of the benchmarks. in the negotiations now beginning with the council and the commission, we will therefore ensure that no index susceptible to manipulation is exempt from the application of this regulation, and we will keep a special eye on mortgage indices so that situations such as those which occurred in the past with the euribor are not repeated.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because, as adopted, parliament's position allows the european system of central banks (escb) to be exempted from the provisions of the regulation. this report seeks to regulate the economic benchmarks, following the very serious libor and euribor scandals which have allowed a real transfer of income to the banking sector for years and which have led to the execution of hundreds of thousands of evictions both in spain and throughout europe. we have called for separate votes to cancel the escb exemption which, in practice, leaves this legislation without effect. the majority groups in the european parliament have opposed our request and prefer to maintain this exemption, which will allow the ecb to continue to operate without transparency in this area. i have therefore decided to vote against this report.
in writing. the commission proposal seeks to create a regulatory framework at eu level to prevent manipulation of benchmarks such as the euribor or libor. the supervisory role will now be exercised by a board of national authorities chaired by the european securities and markets authority. financial scandals uncovered in the wake of the crisis showed manipulation by some of the major banks to influence indices such as the euribor. the european commission itself accused a large number of banks of breaching competition rules and imposed sanctions on them, including j.p. morgan, hsbc, crédit agricole, deutsche bank, société générale, the royal bank of scotland and citigroup, some of which had been involved in a cartel to influence the prices of euro interest rate derivatives, such as mortgages. upyd has always stressed the impact and importance of these indices for european citizens and the urgency of creating more transparent standards. we have voted in favour of the proposal, although we regret that it has been delayed so long because of the blockade of some political groups.

in writing. ‒ this regulation was adopted without a vote, as it has reached its final stage after being negotiated and adopted by the council. the aim is to tighten the regulation of indices used as benchmarks in investment products, such as libor, following the scandal of manipulation of this index by british banks. the text remains excessively lax for indices which are not considered critical. that is why we would have voted against it.

in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it contains positive aspects such as the requirement that the commitment to allocate 0.7% of gdp to development cooperation be fulfilled, it advocates the strengthening of the public-private partnership in financing for development. the report calls for the implementation of the same neoliberal policies as those applied in the eu in development cooperation, i.e. making public resources available to the private sector for its benefit, protecting its investments and demanding reforms consistent with liberalisation. i believe that the pursuit of profit by multinationals is incompatible with sustainable development based on social justice, a development which requires that the basic pillars for the well-being of populations, such as education, health or the right to housing, be public services guaranteed by the states, which are the only actors capable of ensuring their universality, quality and free of charge.
in writing. ‒ this report provides the eu's position for the third international conference on financing for development from 13 to 16 july in addis ababa. we call for the greatest degree of political and economic ambition for the construction of the new development framework, aiming to create the necessary conditions for the financing and implementation of the post-2015 agenda. 2015 is a pivotal year, with the adoption of the sustainable development goals and the agreement on global action against climate change. the main objective is to eradicate the poverty of 1.5 billion people, reduce inequalities and promote sustainable development. this can only be achieved by mobilising sufficient and appropriate resources. we call on the eu and its member states to re-commit to the 0.7% gni target for oda, reserving at least 50% of their oda and 0.2% of gni for ldcs, and to adopt multiannual budgetary timetables for increasing oda by 2020. for these main reasons, and for other reasons raised in the report, i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ the resolution on financing for development contains numerous initiatives to achieve a global partnership so that those countries with higher incomes commit to establishing actions that promote the development of those countries with the least. official development assistance (oda) is a mechanism with an important role in this area as it sets effective guidelines for financing development. among other measures, i stress the importance of promoting initiatives in areas such as health, education or energy, which are a priority for the eu, all through coordinated action between member states. at the same time, fiscal issues must be taken into account, avoiding financial crimes that impede the development of emerging countries. the importance of human rights should not be forgotten in these projects, taking into account the particularly vulnerable situation of women and girls in these countries. finally, i agree with the need to increase investment in research and measures to promote access to finance for smes and micro-enterprises in developing countries, all on the basis of principles of transparency and effective supervision and control of accounts. i therefore support the resolution with my vote in favour.

madam president, we voted in favour of the report on safer health care in europe because it calls for the protection of citizens against health cuts by ensuring the sufficient number of professionals. let me draw your attention to the state of health care in my country, spain, which until recently had one of the most efficient health systems in the world. the policies pursued in my country by the people's party have contributed to the degradation of health care through privatizations in the management of health services and through cuts. degradation has been particularly aggressive in regions such as the valencian community or the community of madrid. let me remind you, ladies and gentlemen, that the european project was based on an idea of democracy linked to social rights and public services. those who degrade health do not only degrade democracy, they also degrade the european project.
in writing. ‒ the report aims to ensure improved patient safety by identifying and correcting those factors in healthcare that may pose an added risk to the health of the population. the report expresses particular concern about the misuse of certain medicines, such as antibiotics, whether due to commercial pressure, insufficient public funding, lack of training or bad practices, against which it calls for greater collaboration between states and greater legislative activity. it also criticises abuses in livestock farming, where indiscriminate use of antibiotics is a threat to public health. it also stressed the importance of prevention and the proper training of medical staff, as well as the good hygiene conditions in hospitals. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the european union. since i share many of the conclusions and recommendations of the report, i have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ according to the eurobarometer, 50% of europeans believe that healthcare can be harmful to patients. 25% said they or their family members had experienced adverse events, and in 46% of these cases patients had made complaints in the period 2009-2014. moreover, between 8% and 12% of patients in hospitals in the eu, some three million people, suffer harm or adverse events (healthcare-associated infections, whether in-patient or out-patient). this report is a response to the commission's second assessment report on patient safety, which shows that there is an increased level of awareness but that important differences persist between member states in relation to patient safety strategies, patient empowerment, training of professionals and, in general, prevention and control of hospital-acquired infections. member states are called upon to act in the sustainability of quality health systems, the development of patient safety strategies, training in the control and prevention of hospital-acquired infections or the promotion of research into new antimicrobials. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ european health systems are the envy of those outside europe. this doesn't mean we shouldn't try to improve them. the report on which i am voting today contains many points with which i fully identify: ensuring that health systems and health facilities are professionally managed by administrators appointed on the basis of merit and not political affiliation; exchanging best practice among health professionals so that they are up to date with the latest technology and best practices in hospital hygiene; ensuring equal access to health services; and, in the face of increasing antibiotic resistance, stimulating the development of new effective antibiotics. we must continue to work to ensure that our health systems continue to be the flagship of our welfare state.

in writing. ‒ according to available figures, between 8% and 12% of patients in hospitals in the eu (around 3 million people) suffer harm or adverse events (healthcare-associated infections, hospital-acquired or not (haci)). the report calls on member states to take action in the following areas: sustainability of quality health systems; development of patient safety strategies; training for healthcare professionals in the control and prevention of hospital-acquired infections; collection of patient and iras data; monitoring and isolation of cross-border patients to prevent contagion. it also stressed the importance of the responsible use of antibiotics to avoid the development of antibiotic resistance and the promotion of research into new antimicrobials. finally, remember the principle of 'one health', the link between human and animal health. i agree with these considerations and have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ this resolution emphasises the main function of health system regulation at european level, which is to ensure patient safety. in view of this and in the wake of the economic crisis, which has often left this priority unattended, the resolution proposes measures to improve european health care in the various member states. aspects such as a commitment to e-health or greater investment in health research and development are some of the measures that are established. all these actions must be carried out in a coordinated and cooperative manner between the states. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of the health of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. as this resolution sets out measures to guarantee safe health care in the eu, i give my approval.

in writing. ‒ the report aims to ensure improved patient safety by identifying and correcting those factors in healthcare that may pose an added risk to the health of the population. the report expresses particular concern about the misuse of certain medicines, such as antibiotics, whether due to commercial pressure, insufficient public funding, lack of training or bad practices, against which it calls for greater collaboration between states and greater legislative activity. it also criticises abuses in livestock farming, where indiscriminate use of antibiotics is a threat to public health. it also stressed the importance of prevention and the proper training of medical staff, as well as the good hygiene conditions in hospitals. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the european union. since i share many of the conclusions and recommendations of the report, i have voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ this report correctly identifies eco- and environmental efficiency as one of the main challenges for smes in the coming years. it stressed that investment in research and development and adequate funding for smes should be given priority in order to facilitate the transition to an environmentally sustainable economy, and that both objectives should be integrated into the commission's programmes. however, the report is hostage to neoliberal assumptions, as it focuses more on entrepreneurship, foreign investment or deregulation than on public planning and the protection of workers and consumers as central axes of the transition to an environmentally and socially sustainable economy. it is also ambiguous in that it does not specify how 'green' growth can be reconciled with the proposed 'circular' economy. i therefore abstained.
in writing. the green economy holds great potential for the growth opportunities it offers smes. these companies face many difficulties at all levels, whether in production, business practices or access to finance. according to the central directory of enterprises (dirce), there are more than three million enterprises in spain, of which 99.88% are smes. the rest of europe is in a similar situation, with smes generating two out of every three private sector jobs and more than half of the total value added created by businesses in the eu. the european commission's green action plan for smes aims to improve the use of resources, support green entrepreneurship, exploit opportunities and facilitate market access. an excellent initiative, properly implemented, will be of great value to our companies.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which underlines the economic and employment potential of green growth and the circular economy for smes, in particular in the exploitation of sectors such as renewable energy sources (in particular wind, solar, hydro and geothermal), energy efficiency, resource efficiency, waste management, emission reduction, electrification and 'cradle to cradle' design. this will require improving the resource efficiency of smes; supporting green entrepreneurship; exploiting the opportunities presented by greener value chains and the promotion of the circular economy; and facilitating market access for green smes to achieve a greener internal market. this report complements the commission's green action plan for smes: enabling smes to turn environmental challenges into business opportunities, which sets out a guideline and framework for how the eu, in cooperation with member states and regions, will help smes to seize the business opportunities offered by the transition to a green economy.

prime minister of hungary. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i have come here today because you are talking about my country, hungary. i am always honoured when members of the european parliament debate the situation in hungary. and it is my imperative duty to speak out on behalf of my country, hungary and the hungarian people. i would like to remind you that the hungarians voted in a referendum to join the european union, and we are proud of our decision. mr president, we could also think that it would be logical that we are here today because europe is curious about the successes of hungarians, curious about what and how hungary has achieved over the past five years. i have a lot to talk about. in 2010, hungary was 21st out of 28 member states in terms of the growth rate of gross national product, and last year it was already in 2nd place. while elsewhere public debts are rising, in hungary we have reduced them from 85% to 77%. and in 2010, we had unemployment well over 11 percent, and now it's under 7 percent, and in three years, i hope, we'll have full employment. however, ladies and gentlemen, you have called this debate because i know that under the heading of the 'hungarian situation' you want to talk about political issues, especially the issue of immigration. as far as political issues are concerned, i would like to inform you that hungary is the most thoroughly examined member state of the european union with regard to the rule of law. at the same time, i welcome the fact that you are putting on the agenda important issues that really concern european citizens: law and order, public security, immigration. these issues are the questions of our common future. the answers to these questions may determine the kind of union we leave to our children. but these problems are not hungarian problems, they are european problems. and yet, my country is being discussed today for one reason, and that is that hungarians generally like to talk straight about difficult things. we're like that, we don't like gossip or gossip. we like to talk straight or not at all. so we talk directly about the death penalty, about immigration, and we also feel that the discourse that many people have been using to say that the "c.p.c.a". is politically correct has not brought us europeans any closer to a solution. therefore, we speak directly and openly about it, we express our opinion that we hungarians want europe to remain european and we want to preserve hungary as a hungarian country. both of our objectives are legitimate and, i believe, fully in line with the fundamental values of europe and the intentions of the founding fathers of the union. ladies and gentlemen, i propose that we make a clear distinction between free movement within europe, the free flow of labour, and migration from outside europe. and within the latter, we must distinguish the case of refugees from the case of immigrants who come here solely because they want to live in a higher standard of living, a higher level of well-being than their home countries can offer. the situation in hungary is such that we cannot give jobs to immigrants. it's better to be honest and straightforward about this. ladies and gentlemen, we are primarily concerned with the issue of immigration for a living in our own way. there is good reason for hungary and the european union to address the issue of livelihood immigration. ladies and gentlemen, i am convinced that what we now know as the european commission's proposal is absurd in our own language, close to what we might call madness. i believe it's a dangerous attitude to say that there's no problem here, that we open the gates wide and let whoever wants to come in. the facts speak clearly: europe is under immense migratory pressure today. compared to 2010, illegal immigration in europe has tripled. in a short time, the number of illegal border crossers in hungary has increased twenty-fold. we are openly arguing that the existing conventions should be revised and re-examined and that the right of the eu member states to defend their own borders should be returned to the national authorities. we think that would be the sane, humane and practical approach. with all due respect, i think it's crazy to suggest that we allow refugees into europe and distribute them around some artificially-designed quota. ladies and gentlemen, i am convinced that the quota will only encourage smugglers, will entice more people to europe and encourage them to attempt dangerous sea crossings to reach eu territory. i therefore believe that it would be better to transfer the regulation of immigration to the member states. my view is, and i am glad that the debate has started on this, that instead of quotas, individual member states should be allowed to decide this issue themselves. we hungarians want to decide for ourselves whether we want immigrants in hungary or not. we are a christian, national government, we have compassion in our hearts, and we have always welcomed refugees, genuine refugees, and we will continue to do so in the future. but the immigrants did not run away. they want a better life, and that's why they come. we understand that, but we can't accept it. illegal border crossing is a crime that must be dealt with. hungary must protect its legal order and its borders. we don't want hungary to be a target country for illegal immigrants. there are countries that have decided that they want to live with this problem. they decided they wanted an immigration policy. we respect that decision. that's why we started the immigration consultation. we believe it is only fair and proper to ask our citizens about this. i would like to tell one of the speakers that there is no consultation on the death penalty in hungary at the moment, there could be some fatal misunderstanding. ladies and gentlemen, i would like to remind you that hungary has not signed any agreements or conventions with anyone about what cannot be discussed in hungary or what can be discussed. we didn't sign an agreement on what we could and couldn't consult on. what topics we can and can't bring up. our association treaty with the european union does not contain any clause that states that certain things should not be discussed or certain questions should not be raised in the member states of the european union. that is why we consider it a violation of the eu treaty if anyone tries to interfere with what we, hungarians, can and cannot express an opinion on. ladies and gentlemen, if we look at the number of asylum seekers as a proportion of the gross national product per capita, hungary is the second most affected member state after germany. if you look at the number of asylum seekers per thousand people, we're also second only to sweden. i would like to draw your attention to the fact that the european commission's migration agency is not paying enough attention to the western balkans. in the first quarter of 2015, 24,000 of the 43 000 asylum applications lodged in hungary were from kosovo. this appropriation is intended to cover the financing of the european schools in the member states and the european schools in the union. and the ukrainian crisis, i ask you, do not ignore, because this is the test that lies ahead. ladies and gentlemen, on the question of the death penalty, i think that europe should not bury its head in the sand. i don't want to go back to the middle ages and have questions that are forbidden to talk about. this debate is not really about the death penalty, but about the freedom of thought, opinion and speech. i insist that we talk about the death penalty. we are on constitutional grounds, and the rules can only be changed in our country in accordance with the european union. ladies and gentlemen, the principles, conventions and rules of the european union are not set in stone, nor are they the product of gods or inspired by gods. they're made by humans, which is why humans can change them at any time. this is freedom and this is democracy. ladies and gentlemen, on these issues, everyone's opinion is a man's opinion and no more, no matter who the man is. whether philosopher, european commissioner, prime minister or party leader. his opinion is that of a european citizen. it's not a sacrament, it's not a dogma, it's not a higher truth. therefore, hungary continues to stand for freedom, stands for the idea of free expression, for the european value. thank you for your attention.

the financial sphere. besides that, it is to combat organised crime such as money laundering, tax evasion and other related crimes, but also – many times mentioned here – terrorism. it is not here only to save money and to prevent money from going into a black hole somewhere, but to use the money for much better purposes, which was said several times. it is not only about saving money, it is, i may say, about saving human lives, because financial transactions are usually, or very often, the first signs that a terrorist attack or some terrorist action is being prepared, so this has an essential role for strengthening security in europe. i would like to thank parliament once again for its support. i hope tomorrow’s vote will push us forward.
in writing. the importance of domestic resource mobilisation has become a recurring theme in development cooperation discussions and a stated objective of the eu. the positive role of taxes in increasing government revenues to finance sustainable and equitable development that reduces poverty and inequality is increasingly recognised. however, the use of anonymous legal entities to launder illicit proceeds is common practice. it is estimated that up to 2.7% of global gdp is money laundered from criminal activities. the world bank estimates that more than 70% of large-scale corruption cases involve anonymous companies. decent people will no longer be satisfied with mere harsh words against money laundering that are not accompanied by concrete actions. the current system and the rules imposed so far by the legislators are failing to stop these illicit flows. it is time for a change, it is time for concrete and effective measures against money laundering.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, europe was conceived as a project for peace and prosperity, for freedom and quality of life. today, that means we have to put as much determination and urgency into rescuing people as we have into rescuing financial institutions. many banks were victims of their own greed. that greed has driven many business ventures and life projects of individuals and families, the vast majority of whom acted in good faith. that's why it's imperative to give them a second chance. because it's a matter of justice. but it is also another tool in the service of the real economy and employment. this review of insolvency proceedings and the commission's recommendations set out very clear principles which all member states must respect and which must also apply to individual debtors. the inequality of legal instruments between creditor and debtor, the time limits for appeals designed to serve the powerful, and the inhuman vetoes on payment, which condemn individuals and families caught in unjust mortgage procedures, are not acceptable. they are the faces and eyes of the crisis. and in 90 percent of cases, we can alleviate their situation with consistency and determination. i therefore call for a european guarantee for this second chance principle and for the decisive use of infringement procedures for states such as spain, which have been singled out by the european courts for their resistance to changing their laws in this direction.

mr president, i welcome this amendment to the regulation which regulates bankruptcy law. i myself, as minister of justice in the czech republic, was responsible for the new insolvency law and i know how important this is to society. this is not just a technical professional standard, but the quality of insolvency law has a very significant impact not only on the business sector but also on the functioning of the company as such. we have been dealing with the question of the length of insolvency proceedings in the czech republic, but now we are more concerned with how to strengthen non-liquidation forms of resolution of the debtor's situation. however, this proposal, which is here, concerns cross-border insolvency proceedings. i am convinced from my own experience in the czech republic that this is a very good regulation and it is good that after ten years you are carrying out a revision that removes some problems, such as clarifying the jurisdiction of the insolvency court in question so that the aforementioned insolvency tourism cannot take place, where the place where insolvency law is somehow best for the debtor is chosen for a purpose, not for the creditors. it is also very good that you are extending the scope of this proposal and that in future not only liquidated forms of insolvency but also non-liquidated forms of insolvency will fall within the scope of this regulation. and the third thing i want to mention is the issue of compulsory insolvency registration. i think this is absolutely crucial and if we want to have an efficient european insolvency procedure in the future, we need to have one public register.
as has been said, mr president, today we are also dealing with the request of my group and myself that we may extend the reference framework we have from the insolvency of companies to a reference framework for personal insolvency, which is absolutely necessary in order to guarantee a minimum of protection for individuals. something that is economically efficient and absolutely socially just. why is this framework for people's insolvency necessary? firstly, because we have very different legislation within europe on this matter, from the insolvency commissions in france to the rehabilitation model in britain, which allow hundreds of thousands of people - £150,000 a year in britain or £50,000 in france - to have a well-deserved second chance. but, unfortunately, in some countries we do not have this necessary legal door, this escape from a situation which has caused a social disaster. spain is a paradigm in this. we have had 570,000 foreclosures during the economic crisis, hundreds of thousands of first-time evictions; a social disaster, as i said, but also a moral collapse, the one we see on the tv news when the police force drives old women out of their homes. that is why it is necessary - because no one stops paying debts because he wants to - to find a european legal door by extending this insolvency to families, because honest citizens also deserve a second chance.

in writing. in the eu, about 8% of people aged 16 and over report a severe disability and about 18% a moderate disability. the eu and most member states have signed the convention, and many member states have ratified it in their national legislation. the convention establishes an international monitoring system by designating government bodies responsible for matters relating to its implementation, and also provides that civil society will be integrated and involved in the monitoring process. as a result, the eu disability unit was set up, which produced a report on the implementation of the convention, on which the un presented a 'list of issues' to which the commission now has to respond. as one of the european parliament's commissioners responsible for the implementation and monitoring of the convention, i felt that a resolution was urgently needed, highlighting the need for coordination between the various european institutions, the need to adopt the european accessibility act and parliament's support for the commission in preparing the response, and in which parliament also expresses some displeasure that the commission has not relied more on it in the preparation of the report.

member of the commission.– mr president, please allow me to start by expressing my thanks to the members of this house for their mainly positive reactions, encouragement and support of the overall agenda. i have taken note of all their remarks and concerns. we all know that addressing migratory challenges means making some bold decisions. starting from the very beginning of the life of this commission, commitment on this issue has been shown by the commission itself, president juncker and myself – you will remember my commitment before the committee on civil liberties, justice and home affairs (libe) during the hearing – and we have delivered results in a very short period. in the beginning some of you might have believed that we would not be in a position to do so. well, here we are before you today after the public announcement of the new european agenda on migration. the time for decisions has come. do we want to honour our responsibilities? do we want to face the new reality throughout europe? the european agenda on migration is not only an emergency response, it is a strategy that will lead europe – that will lead us – forward in the next five, or even ten, years. during this period a lot of things will change but we have to strive towards our destination: to adopt and implement a comprehensive european policy on migration. this is why the agenda outlines a broader set of initiatives in the medium term in order to manage migration better. but we all know that any action alone will not be enough to solve the situation. this agenda requires political will and commitment, and this commission has both. solidarity shall not only be a slogan, as many of you have said. we need member states to participate. we need their support. the important thing is to make a difference and to show that we are able to address the situation together. this agenda is based on the conviction that the european union migration policy is not about opening or closing borders. both of those options are unrealistic. the european agenda on migration is about managing migration better so that migration can take place in an orderly, safe and regular manner. the commission is already mobilising all its resources to implement these actions and will adopt a package implementing measures next week. triggering this emergency mechanism means that more needs to be done together for those who are in need of protection. let me say here that it is not a free ticket to another european country. it has become indispensable. this package will include, among other things: firstly, a proposal for a decision, based on article 78(3) of the treaty, establishing an emergency relocation scheme. this proposal will also give details on how the regulation will work, including necessary safeguards. secondly, we will present a recommendation on the establishment of a european resettlement scheme. thirdly, an action plan on smuggling. fourthly, guidance on fingerprinting. finally, a public consultation on the future of the blue card. the commission’s european agenda on migration completes and deepens the commitments of the european council and it is a response to the call by parliament. migration is a critical issue for the future of our societies and for the future of europe. we need to regain people’s trust by proving that europe is able to manage migration in an effective way. that means going beyond words and putting good intentions into practice. the european agenda on migration offers a comprehensive approach to address the migratory challenges. as i said before, it must be seen as a package, and all the measures proposed have to be implemented in parallel. no member state can address this challenge alone. thank you for this very fruitful debate. as i said earlier, i count on your support more than ever, knowing that parliament shares our ambition finally to prevent and plan instead of only reacting to dramatic events. i hope that you can also help me to get support from member states and citizens. we need this european agenda on migration. i am even more convinced of this after today’s debate.
president-in-office of the council.– mr president, i would like to thank you very much for this very important debate today. parliament’s contribution is instrumental in finding the most appropriate answers to the challenges we have. this is one more step in the continued dialogue between our two institutions on the very important issue of migration, which we intend to pursue. given the seriousness of the migratory pressure on the eu, all contributions to this debate are welcome, in particular if they can contribute to finding a solution to the challenges we are facing. i can therefore promise you that we will take duly into account parliament’s views on the different aspects of the european agenda on migration. in any case, this is just the first phase of a long debate. i am sure that the next presidencies will also pursue this cooperation with parliament on this very complex issue of migration. as i have already said, at the beginning of this debate, as a result of swift action and cooperation between institutions we can already talk about substantial steps taken in the direction of addressing the humanitarian challenge the eu is facing due to migration flows. i started my speech today by underlining that it is no longer time for words. it is time for deeds. this is the approach of the council. the council has already delivered concrete results and decisions. we have prepared the roadmap and have welcomed the presentation of the agenda by the commission. we also took the decision to prioritise the tripling of the resources allocated for frontex and we have decided to establish an eu naval operation. more steps will follow when preparing for the june european council. some of you, in your comments, criticised the council for its lack of support for the emergency mechanisms under article 78(3) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. such criticism is premature as the commission’s communication was adopted just one week ago. even if some member states have already expressed their preliminary views concerning the emergency relocation mechanism, the council has not yet defined its position. we are still waiting for the commission’s concrete proposals. once tabled, the council will immediately activate its preparatory bodies. we will certainly have another opportunity to discuss the mechanism as decisions on provisional measures may be taken only after consulting parliament. i will be honest. it will not be easy to find an agreement in the council on such a major and sensitive issue as migration policies, just as it is also not easy to find an agreement in this house. what is important at this moment is that the presidency and the council stand ready to respond to the commission’s proposal. this house has today also shown a lot of interest in knowing more about the eu naval operation. eunavfor med will be conducted in sequential phases and in accordance with the requirements of international law. it will start by surveilling and assessing human smuggling and trafficking networks in the southern-central mediterranean and will be conducted as soon as possible. the second and third phases of the operation will work to search, seize and disrupt the assets of smugglers, based on international law and in partnership with the libyan authorities. the eu csdp operation is part of a set of comprehensive measures aimed at responding to the immediate need to save lives, address emergency situations and tackle the root causes of irregular migration, as requested by the european council on 23 april. the council agrees with the need to have a european solution. it is important to have a comprehensive approach with a view to providing asylum for those in genuine need, as well as at the same time ensuring the effective return of those who do not have a right to stay. but the most urgent priority is to stop further loss of life. we look forward to working together with you to find the best and most effective solutions to the crisis we are facing.
in writing. with the new european agenda on migration the eu is responding to the migratory pressure on europe and in general in the right direction. priorities are identified, given the urgency of acting on the humanitarian emergency caused by the incessant and unacceptable deaths in the mediterranean. the aim is to improve the european asylum system by activating the emergency mechanism provided for in the eu treaty, in order to distribute refugees fairly among the member states. the aim is to strengthen the frontex agency so that it can also carry out rescue and salvage operations at sea. new legal and safe avenues for legal immigration will be explored. it also strengthens the fight against irregular immigration by cooperating with the countries of origin and transit and by combating organised networks of trafficking in human beings. the agenda is positive but the reactions of governments are not. the agenda will not be effective if states start resisting to take in the rescued. the eu must achieve a common migration and asylum policy. the member states must be aware that we are facing a serious emergency and we have a responsibility to act with 'internal solidarity'.

in writing. the european agenda on migration is the eu's response in the right direction to the migratory pressure on europe. the urgent priorities for action in the face of the humanitarian emergency caused by the incessant and unacceptable deaths in the mediterranean are identified. the aim is to improve the european asylum system by activating the emergency mechanism provided for in the eu treaty, in order to distribute refugees fairly among the member states. the aim is to strengthen the frontex agency so that it can also carry out rescue and salvage operations at sea. new legal and safe avenues for legal immigration will be explored. strengthen the fight against irregular immigration by cooperating with source and transit countries, and the fight against organised networks of trafficking in human beings. i think the agenda is positive but not so the reactions of the governments. the agenda will not be effective if the states start by refusing to take in the rescued. the eu must adopt a common immigration and asylum policy. the member states must be aware that we are facing a serious emergency and we have a responsibility to act with 'internal solidarity'.
in writing. the european union is finally taking responsibility for a phenomenon, immigration, which affects certain states in particular but which must be managed by all. the commission's comprehensive and holistic approach is welcomed, addressing both immediate measures - such as tripling the capacity of joint frontex operations and activating the emergency mechanism to assist member states facing a sudden influx of migrants - and longer-term measures, combining respect for the rule of law with the protection of human rights. in order to implement this plan as soon as possible, it is necessary that the member states agree to overcome as soon as possible the discrepancies on the quotas for the distribution of asylum seekers.

in writing. ‒ this recommendation gives the european parliament's consent to add croatia to the eu's trade and cooperation agreement with south africa, given that this country acceded to the eu in july 2013 and the agreement in question was signed in 1999 and entered into force in 2004. so, although it is a technical amendment which does not affect the substance of the trade and cooperation agreement, i abstained because i am opposed in principle to such agreements, which benefit multinationals and the political and financial elites to the detriment of the peoples of the parties concerned.
in writing. ‒ the eu and south africa signed an agreement on trade, development and cooperation on 11 october 1999, which entered into force on 1 may 2004, with the objectives of strengthening bilateral dialogue, supporting south africa in its economic and social transition process, promoting regional cooperation and the economic integration of the country into southern africa and the world economy, and expanding and liberalising bilateral trade in goods, services and capital. the agreement also established a regular political dialogue on issues of common interest, both bilaterally and regionally. the agreement was revised in 2009 to introduce in the context of development the requirement of respect for democratic principles, human rights and the rule of law, cooperation on disarmament and non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, and cooperation in new areas such as the fight against terrorism and money laundering. the participation of croatia in the agreement with south africa is a natural consequence of its accession to the eu and therefore the conclusion of this additional protocol to the agreement with south africa should be approved.

in writing. ‒ the agreement on trade, development and cooperation (tdca) between the eu and its member states, of the one part, and the republic of south africa, of the other part, was signed in pretoria on 11 october 1999 and entered into force on 1 may 2004. it was revised in kleinmond, south africa on 11 september 2009. the signature of this additional protocol is necessary to enable the republic of croatia to become a contracting party to the gcca, as the republic of croatia's accession to the eu took place on 1 july 2013. the purpose of the additional protocol is simply to formulate in the acdc the few technical and linguistic adaptations required by croatia's accession to the eu, so i vote in favour of this draft.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal for a directive because the soundness, integrity and stability of financial and credit institutions, as well as confidence in the financial system as a whole, could be seriously jeopardised by the efforts of criminals and their accomplices, whether by covering up the origin of the proceeds of crime or by channelling the proceeds of legitimate or illegitimate activities for terrorist purposes. money launderers and terrorist financiers could take advantage of the free movement of capital and the free provision of financial services that an integrated financial area brings to facilitate their criminal activities, and coordination measures at union level are therefore necessary. i also welcome the fact that the socialist and democratic group has succeeded in including in the future regulation the establishment of a public register of beneficial owners of financial assets, at the level of the member states, and to which anyone with a 'legitimate interest' can have access. it is necessary to identify any natural person who owns or controls a legal person. this is a fundamental tool in the fight against the interposed societies.
in writing. ‒ the european council has repeatedly refused to lift the ban on many tax practices that facilitate money laundering. the commission has also taken into account the fact that the tax authorities of the member states have not yet taken the necessary measures to ensure that the tax authorities of the member states are able to exercise their discretion in the assessment of the taxable profit of luxopco. the final compromise, although insufficient, represents a step forward from previous negotiating positions. this report does not have a final vote, as it is a second reading within the trilogue process.

in writing. ‒ i have given my support to this regulation amending and updating a 2006 rule which sets out the information that must appear on the payer and the recipient of bank and financial transfers for the purpose of preventing money laundering. it is particularly important that, thanks to the work of the socialist and democratic group, all transactions outside the eu are marked in the same way as those of an intra-community nature, with the exception of those with an amount of less than eur 1000, so as not to affect the remittances of immigrants. penalties for non-compliance and monitoring mechanisms have also been strengthened. european harmonisation of information on bank transfers is essential to combat money laundering from illicit operations such as drug trafficking, terrorism or organised crime, but also to bridge the processes of the banking union and the so-called capital markets union, so that users of financial services do not have to face disparate conditions depending on the member state in which they are resident.

in writing. ‒ the objective of this report (which does not have a final vote, as it is a second reading within the trilogue process) is to implement control measures on transfers of funds in the context of the fight against financial fraud and money laundering. the existence of this regulatory framework, although clearly insufficient, is a small step in the international fight against financial crime and tax evasion.

in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the revision of this regulation, which lays down common rules on the court with jurisdiction to open insolvency proceedings, the applicable law and the recognition of decisions where a debtor - whether a company, a business or an individual - is insolvent, because some of its provisions could be improved upon after ten years of its entry into force. the main innovation is to prevent the debtor from moving his assets or the court proceedings from one country to another in order to improve his legal situation, thus avoiding that some companies or debtors suddenly change their seat before the opening of insolvency proceedings. it provides greater legal certainty and allows consideration to be given to whether the change of seat is due to objective reasons or not. it has also been possible to include a recital on the rights of workers in respect of the establishment of a preferential right for them, taking into account that they are the weakest when insolvency proceedings are opened.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to review the existing european regulation on transnational insolvency proceedings. from the point of view of workers, the final outcome of the negotiations is still insufficient: insolvency proceedings continue to overprotect the interests of debtors with regard to the preservation of employment or the choice of the national framework within which the procedure should be opened. however, positive aspects such as better judicial and administrative control of insolvency proceedings and the facilitation of the maintenance of the activity while the company restructures its activities and accounts should be acknowledged. this report does not have a final vote, as it is a second reading within the trilogue process.

in writing. ‒ figures provided by the european commission indicate that some 200 000 businesses are affected by crossborder insolvency proceedings in the european union each year, meaning that 1.7 million jobs are at stake. the fourth part of these insolvency proceedings has a crossborder element. the purpose of this proposal for a regulation is to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of these proceedings, for the benefit of debtors and creditors, thus facilitating the survival of companies and offering entrepreneurs a second chance. it also adapts the current insolvency regulation to the developments in national insolvency legislation since the entry into force of the regulation in 2002.

in writing. ‒ the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council amending regulation (ec) no 1346/2000 on insolvency proceedings is a technical report. the scope of the regulation has been extended to cover hybrid procedures and company restructuring. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a decision on the proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos at work. the regulation now also allows for the coordination of procedures for corporate groups. the s&d group also managed to include a recital on workers' rights: 'the additional harmonisation measures should also introduce privileges for workers'. i agree with these considerations and have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ my support for parliament's position on the establishment of new rules on crossborder insolvency proceedings. it is important to adopt rules that give more leeway to companies that operate in several countries and are in trouble, because that is how we are going to prevent them from going bankrupt. we are talking about some 50,000 companies facing crossborder insolvency proceedings each year, and up to 40,000 people losing their jobs because of this, which makes it urgent to act to bring this initiative forward.
in writing. ‒ we consider that this regulation does not sufficiently reflect the eu's priorities and current national practices in insolvency law. the current crisis and high levels of unemployment, which affect more than 25% of the working population in spain, have led hundreds of thousands of families to reach a critical situation which, in many cases, does not allow them to meet their most basic needs. the consequences have been that many families have lost their homes because they could not cope with their debts. in this regulation we have also tried to put the emphasis on improving the deteriorated rescue mechanisms for firms in difficulty, which are often the sole economic livelihood of thousands of people.
