madam president, commissioner, it is said that the belgian colonial forces used to refer to the territory of burundi as 'urundi ruanda', that is to say 'the other rwanda'. the similarities are striking: the bloody civil war, which left 300,000 dead in burundi until 2005, as a result of ethnic tensions between hutus and tutsis; poverty, impunity and the exodus of hundreds of thousands. is burundi the other rwanda? the crisis that burundi is currently experiencing is marked by an eminently political feature: it is the intention of its president to perpetuate himself in power, contrary to what the burundian constitution and the arusha peace accords establish, which has generated this conflict. and does europe have anything to say about this? do you have something to do? the rwandan genocide was not only ethnic but also political. ten years ago, kofi annan bitterly lamented the international inaction, his inability to stop the genocide, which claimed the lives of 800 000 men, women and children. ban ki-moon has urged the security council to act and to mobilise its instruments to safeguard peace in burundi: does that seem enough? failure to act once is a mistake, a terrible and irreparable mistake, but failure to act a second time is simply a crime.
president-in-office of the council. – madam president, sport is universal. it is said to be the only truly international language. sport opens doors, brings people and communities together and bridges divides. for us europeans, any discussion of sport is first and foremost associated with discussion about football. albert camus used to say: ‘what i know about morals, i owe to football.’ for that reason it is all the more unfortunate to hear that sport is being used for criminal purposes. fifa, born in europe a little over 100 years ago, has not only gone global, but the events it organises are watched by millions, and sometimes billions, of people. as we speak, the fifa women’s world cup is ongoing in canada. these events are a source of hope for boys and girls around the world. such events cannot be undermined by continual suspicions of criminal activities. illegal betting and match fixing have been making the headlines in recent years. but who could have imagined that the scale of organised crime was so massive. football is not only a game; it is also an economic activity, creating jobs and attracting investments. as in every economic sector, a sound and transparent basis is needed. for all these reasons, it is important that trust be re—established. the council and its presidency have been following the recent developments within football’s governing body, fifa, with great attention and concern. the context in which we must address this issue is important. the responsibility for good governance and the proper functioning of sporting organisations lies with the international sports bodies themselves and not with governments or eu institutions. however, given the importance of sport to citizens, and of football in particular, it is clear that standards of governance in international sporting organisations are an area of legitimate concern. as far as the eu is concerned, the lisbon treaty introduced a new specific competence in the field of sport. it is noteworthy that article 165 of the treaty mentions the moral integrity of sport in particular. the council has paid specific attention to the issue of how sporting organisations are governed and run. in may 2011, the council adopted a first eu work plan for sport. it established an expert group to address the issue of good governance, which agreed a set of ‘principles of good governance in sport’. these principles identify the key elements necessary to ensure public and stakeholder confidence in the organisations responsible for sport. even if the role of the eu is limited to facilitating exchanges of good practice, transfers of knowledge and networking of stakeholders at national and international level, the eu institutions have a role to play in ensuring that good governance principles adopted at eu level are recognised and implemented in all eu member states. the eu can also facilitate the promotion of principles of good governance in sport beyond its borders, with both the sporting bodies and the public authorities of third countries. honourable members, i would like to quote european council president tusk. in the context of the recent g7 meeting in germany, he said: ‘i am really satisfied that some leaders want to use the summit to discuss corruption, including the recent fifa scandal. we do not need empty declarations against corruption but we have to be ready to fight against those who were corrupted and those who corrupt. we need to fight corruption in all its dimensions, no matter how powerful the authors of these disgraceful practices are.’ i would like to highlight the work done by the eu on corruption in recent months. the latvian presidency made this a priority, as early as the trio presidency programme. we highlighted, in particular, cooperation with the group of states against corruption (greco), as well as progress on the anti-money laundering directive. indeed, following an agreement between our two institutions, we strengthened rules to prevent money laundering. the anti-money laundering directive will strengthen eu rules and ensure consistency with the approach followed at international level, based on the recommendations of the financial action task force. and the funds transfer regulation introduces further requirements regarding the information accompanying transfers of funds. i signed these pieces of legislation with president schulz at the time of the european parliament part-session in may. of course, the global fight against corruption requires much more action and many more steps, as illustrated by the recent revelations on fifa. but we have made a contribution, at eu level, to the priority that the fight against corruption represents. with regard to the recent developments at fifa, there is now an opportunity for major reform of that organisation. however, as i said, no matter how many laws we pass, they will not be effective if there is no true will on the part of the organisation to self-regulate and observe these standards. the council will follow this debate closely and pay due attention to the views that are expressed.
member of the commission.– madam president, i want to thank the european parliament for putting this item on today’s agenda. i usually enjoy talking about sport, but today’s subject troubles me deeply. football often dominates the news and conversations all over the globe. it is the most popular game in the world, and european clubs and our national teams are at its heart. but the last two weeks have revealed an uglier side of the beautiful game. we see an international governance system in football that is broken and has lost all trust and credibility. european fans and our own football associations have shown clearly what they think. fifa as an organisation in its current form is no longer fit to run international football. small change will not be enough – but big change may not be enough either. fifa needs a fresh start, a complete overhaul of the organisation’s culture and institutions. it needs to take responsibility to become a new transparent organisation that meets the highest ethical and moral standards. fans across europe and around the world demand nothing less. what role should the european union play in this process? clearly this is not an area where we should be legislating or creating new instruments. our job in the eu is not to organise sport, but we will support and encourage those who are serious about reform. the commission has already been working for some time with a group of experts on good governance, which developed recommendations looking at transparency and accountability in decision-making, democratic structures and processes, inclusive representation and effective auditing. the expert group is now working on ways to take these recommendations and principles forward. we are looking at how the rights to organise major sporting events are awarded across the single market and taking into account the realities of the digital age. building on this, i now want to look at how to promote the implementation of principles of good governance by all the sports organisations, including football. of course, it is not for the european commission or the european union to run sports organisations. they have to take responsibility and implement good governance standards themselves. but we can help to develop those standards and encourage federations to put them in place. we can signal to those sport bodies which want to play ball that we are ready to help them. the autonomy of sport, free from government interference, is fundamental; but, like other organisations that play a public role and which fail to respect the highest ethical standards, our sporting federations must face greater scrutiny. competition in our single market must follow the rules. at the commission, we work closely with member states and sports organisations to achieve a real change in sport governance. we will not stand by silently when sports federations fail to do their job. we must be ready to share the thinking we have done in europe with others who now face the challenge of reform. we owe it to the millions of sports fans in europe and beyond.

mr president, the identification of fifa as corrupt is an example of what happens when we accept that a matter of such obvious public interest as professional sport is dominated and managed from private structures without effective democratic and judicial control. it is a world without external control mechanisms and without the proper separation of powers in its internal functioning and decision-making processes. any reform that does not include these issues is doomed to failure, by the many references we make to good governance. how is it possible that we have had to wait for legal action from non-eu countries such as switzerland and the united states? the enormous economic impact of football creates the ideal scenario for the worst vices of individual or, as in the case of fifa, structural and institutional corruption to grow: the relationship between corrupt and corrupters becomes quite evident. but if you want to get to the bottom of it, let's do it by targeting three very clearly identified economic sectors: audiovisual communication; advertising and sponsorship of athletes and teams; private sports betting, especially in its digital version. we talk about the world cups in france, south africa, russia and qatar, but we do not include any reference to the 2006 world cup and the recent revelations about the saudi vote and the supply of arms to this country from germany itself. we should send a message of apology, from the recorded vote, for the incomprehensible re-election of mr blatter as fifa president just a week ago. did you know that france and spain were the only european countries to vote in favour of mr blatter? horror and shame.
author. mr president, is there a link between sport and respect for human rights? the olympic movement is based on three fundamental values: excellence to give our best, friendship above all differences and respect - respect for others, respect for fundamental ethical principles. this oral question to the council, which i am submitting on behalf of the subcommittee on human rights and the committee on foreign affairs, is intended to make us reflect, to make us reflect on the growing discrepancy between the values that inspire sport and what many major sporting events have become in reality: a huge accumulation of interests, both economic and political; a tool for the shampooing of regimes that are far from being democratic; a missed opportunity to really move towards greater respect for human rights. sport, such a powerful tool, cannot live without the defence of human rights and the commitment to freedom of expression. sport cannot be blind to what happens where it celebrates its great events, because that blindness makes us all accomplices. these are the first ever european games, promoted by the european olympic committee, and it is therefore europe's responsibility not to be an accomplice of a country, of a regime which systematically violates the values which we claim to defend. we cannot ignore what is happening in azerbaijan, and this is the baku 2015 games. europe cannot come to baku to applaud, while we know the level of repression in that country against those who dare to speak out against the government. we are not only being told this by the major human rights organisations - and i have to report that amnesty international has been prevented from entering azerbaijan today - but we are also being told this by the council of europe, the united nations and the osce. there is a clear consensus on this situation. azerbaijan is engaged in a relentless persecution of human rights defenders and the preparation of these games has only served to increase that repression. civil society has been systematically eradicated in that country, suppressed, silenced, and the european union and its member states say nothing. there are no longer any organizations working on human rights; the ones that were there - about twenty - have been closed. in azerbaijan, sports can certainly be practiced freely in large, top-class facilities; but if you criticize the government or defend human rights, you have two options: jail or exile. because if you criticize electoral processes, like anar mammadli and elnur mammadov, you go to jail; if you document the cases of political prisoners, like intigam aliyev or khadija ismayilova did, you go to jail. if you don't resign yourself to remain silent, just raise your voice, as leyla yunus and her husband arif yunus did, you are doomed to the worst treatment. you see, mr president, leyla yunus was a finalist for the sakharov prize and this parliament has made a commitment to her. he's about to serve a year in prison. all this time in pretrial detention, without being tried, in prison, in very poor health. her husband was also imprisoned: we know nothing about him. their daughter dinara, who is here right now, in this house, and who has only them in the world, is wondering why we are not doing anything. perhaps the council can give us some answers today, it can give some answers to dinara yunus. what is the position of the council and the high representative on this relationship between sport and respect for human rights and democracy? should the council not take advantage of the forthcoming baku games as a unique opportunity for the european union and its member states to collectively and forcefully defend human rights and universal values? should not respect for the most basic of human rights be a prerequisite for deciding where to hold major sporting events? there are less than 48 hours until the opening of these european games. i want to call for the release of all prisoners of conscience who are suffering from the lack of freedom in azerbaijan today. it is a task we can all push for - european governments, this parliament, sportsmen, fans. what better occasion than when all of europe and the world are looking to azerbaijan to demonstrate our commitment to the universal values we share! what better than to allow all the human rights defenders, journalists, activists in prison, to enjoy this great occasion for azerbaijan in freedom!
president-in-office of the council.– mr president, i share your concerns regarding the situation of human rights in azerbaijan and particularly the detention of human rights defenders. the european partnership is a space in which respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms must be guaranteed. i will inform commissioner hahn and the high representative of this discussion and will also convey your concerns to them. i would like to recall that respect for human rights and democracy is a core value of the eu, and we do not hesitate to promote it. the eu, through the european external action service, is raising its concerns with the azerbaijani authorities directly and publicly, irrespective of the european games. the eu special representative for human rights, stavros lambrinidis, and commissioner hahn also raised the eu’s concerns on human rights issues during their recent visits to baku in february and april respectively. in particular, they called for the fair treatment and release of detained individuals. the eu delegation in baku, working closely with the embassies of eu member states, is supporting local human rights defenders, including by applying the eu guidelines on human rights defenders. together with like-minded partners, the eu is carefully monitoring the cases – including the court cases – of those in detention. we are also working with the council of europe and are hopeful that the joint committee drawn from azerbaijan’s government and civil society, mediated by the council of europe, will deliver positive results. we continue to look actively for other ways in which we can support civil society in azerbaijan, including those activists and independent journalists currently in detention. as i said at the beginning of the debate, the baku games are an excellent opportunity for the azerbaijani authorities to demonstrate their progressive commitment to democratic values and human rights. we hope this opportunity will not be missed.
in writing. major sporting events take on a dimension that goes far beyond the sporting arena. the purpose of this oral question is to highlight the importance and potential that these events can and should have in making a substantial contribution to the defence of human rights. the baku european games (azerbaijan) - the first of its kind - are taking place from 12 to 28 june. the united nations warns of the relentless persecution of opponents, human rights defenders and journalists in the country, whose civil society has been eradicated, silenced. this repression has been increased as the date of the games approached. sport cannot live without the defence of human rights, and europe cannot appear in baku to applaud while we are aware of the suffering that the aliyev government inflicts on anyone who dares to speak out against it. we call for the release of all prisoners of conscience in azerbaijan and hope that, with the cooperation of governments and sports federations, respect for human rights will finally become a key element in deciding the venues of major sporting events in the future.

president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– madam president, on behalf of the eu’s high representative, i would like to thank you for again adding syria to this week’s plenary agenda and for giving us an opportunity to follow up on the plenary debates that we conducted on the same issue in february and april this year. although terrorist groups in syria and iraq have been seriously weakened in many respects over the past weeks, the challenges ahead remain huge, as illustrated by the fall of ramadi and tadmor/palmyra at the hands of daesh. as was the case in all cities that have fallen to daesh, the inhabitants of tadmor have been and are still exposed to arbitrary killings and violence. the ancient site of palmyra, right next to tadmor, is also a symbol of syria’s rich cultural heritage and identity. it has been a crossroad of civilisation throughout history. the threat of deliberate destruction that daesh is exerting in archaeological and cultural sites such as palmyra may amount to a war crime, according to the rome statute of the international criminal court. the eu has taken all the appropriate steps in accordance with un security council resolution 2199 to prevent the illegal trade in cultural property that contributes directly to the financing of terrorist groups. but the occupation of palmyra/tadmor by terrorists is only one of the latest military developments in syria. it is first and foremost a strong reminder of the urgency to achieve a lasting political solution to the crisis. to contribute to that effort, we must remember that firstly, while daesh is a single organisation and that a regional approach is needed to tackle it, the circumstances in syria and iraq are different. secondly, from the eu perspective, an inclusive political transition in syria and inclusive political governance in iraq are crucial to sustainable peace and stability: the fight against daesh and other terrorist groups must be conducted in parallel with the search for lasting political solutions. thirdly, military, political, counter-terrorism and stabilisation efforts need to go hand in hand to be effective both in syria and iraq. this approach is at the heart of the eu regional strategy for syria and iraq as well as the daesh threat, which was adopted in march 2015 and is currently being pursued and implemented. this is also the position presented by high representative mogherini on behalf of the eu at last week’s meeting of the small group of the global coalition to counter daesh. the fight against daesh and other terrorist groups is not only a military endeavour. it must be conducted in parallel with efforts to address the root causes of the political crisis in syria and iraq. an inclusive political transition in syria and inclusive political governance in iraq are crucial. this is the key policy objective of the eu regional strategy for syria and iraq as well as the isil/daesh threat, adopted by the foreign affairs council on 16 march. the fight against daesh and other terrorist groups will require sustained engagement and efficient coordination, and more than ever the eu is determined to continue to use all relevant means to contribute to this effort alongside other regional and international partners. on syria, our position is clear: it is the assad regime’s brutal war against its own people, massive human rights violations and systematic obstruction against democratic reforms that have contributed to the flourishing of daesh in syria. as a consequence of its policies and actions, the assad regime cannot be a partner in the fight against daesh. the eu continues to fully support the efforts of un special envoy de mistura to achieve a reduction in violence that may create an environment conducive to a political process. the eu has participated in the geneva consultations on the political and security developments since the adoption of the geneva communiqué of 2012, and we hope that this will help reignite an inclusive political process on the basis of this communiqué. efforts to reignite a political process must be inclusive, involving women and civil society, and must be accompanied by confidence-building measures such as the end of indiscriminate bombing and arbitrary arrest or detention, as reported by the united nations commission of inquiry. the eu reiterates its call for the immediate and unconditional release of all political prisoners and activists, including human rights defender and free speech advocate mazen darwish, who has been arbitrarily detained since 16 february 2012. we condemned this arrest and called for his immediate release. if mazen were tried today, his alleged crime would fall under the provision of existing amnesties, but the legal process appears to have been deliberately stalled and mazen has never been tried. there are undeniable reports of thousands of cases of arbitrary detention throughout syria. it is a vital report and documents such crimes to ensure that perpetrators are held accountable. our ultimate objective is to help build a democratic and pluralist syria where all minorities and vulnerable groups have a place. the magnitude of the syrian crisis is testing the capacities of the entire international aid system. the needs are overwhelming, and an extraordinary effort is needed to mobilise significant funding, ensure access to the people in need, and aid efficiency. we are also determined to continue supporting the syrians and the neighbours of syria affected by the crisis. humanitarian aid and longer-term assistance are, and will remain, important pillars of the eu’s response to the crisis in syria and in the neighbouring countries. at the kuwait iii conference of 31 march, the commission and member states pledged close to eur 1.1 billion – double the eu pledge at the 2014 conference. of this, eur 500 million in humanitarian aid, early recovery and long-term stabilisation assistance come from the eu budget. so humanitarian and non-humanitarian aid is delivered both inside syria and in neighbouring lebanon, jordan, iraq and turkey to refugees and host communities. those countries have played a considerable part in the international communitiesʼ humanitarian response to the syria crisis, hosting well over 3.5 million refugees. the political and humanitarian crisis in syria remains, therefore, at the heart of our internal debate on migration in the mediterranean and an important part of our dialogue with all our regional partners in this region. this highlights our will to sustain the level of our humanitarian and non-humanitarian engagement in response to the crisis in syria and its regional consequences.
in writing. in recent months, the idea has been spreading that europe is more concerned about the 'palmira stones' than its people. the number of victims, after the takeover of the city of palmyra by isis on may 22, exceeds four hundred. no archaeological ruin, ancient temple or architectural monument can be worth more than one of these lives. however, the heritage of a country is an integral part of the identity of its people and therefore i believe that the eu should cooperate with unesco to protect it. moreover, as a result of the threat to the archaeological site of palmyra, public awareness of the human tragedy that is taking place has increased. the eu calls on the syrian authorities to stop the destruction of heritage and to release journalist and human rights activist mazen darwish, who has been unjustly imprisoned since 2012.

author. - madam president, does it make sense that we are talking today in the european parliament about a ten-year-old girl, who is not yet 1.40 metres tall, who has been raped by her stepfather and whose pregnancy is discovered by her mother after five months? i think it does make sense. and it has because this girl is the embodiment and symbol of thousands of girls who suffer rape and pregnancy every year and not everywhere receive the same attention and care. denying these children, victims of sexual violence and abuse, a humanitarian abortion not only violates international law, as the un itself denounces, but also violates our obligation as an international community to provide them with access to comprehensive healthcare guaranteed by the convention on the rights of the child, whose 25th anniversary we celebrated recently. she's a girl who could live anywhere in the world, yes, but she lives in latin america and she lives in paraguay. and i don't think this girl is left or right, but she lives in paraguay; a girl whom, like all the children of the world, we have committed ourselves to protecting, and she is the only real living link between our european agendas today between brussels and strasbourg. this girl is that link that exists because there are international laws which, in this case, clearly state that a humanitarian abortion is required. the best interests of the child must take precedence over any other consideration.

in writing. ‒ the black sea basin is a strategic region for the eu. the resolution urges member states to continue not to recognise the annexation of crimea and condemns russia's support for ukrainian separatists. the european union is also calling for the establishment of a european union-wide network of experts in the field of human rights, including the european union's special representative for human rights, mr barroso. the resolution stresses that nato has a moral obligation to strengthen the defence capabilities of georgia and ukraine, while urging the commission to update its strategy for the region. beyond the purely military, member states are encouraged to diversify their energy sources, and the commission is encouraged to continue negotiations on the gas pipeline linking the eu with turkey. the report also calls for an inquiry into human rights violations during the conflict and expresses concern about the environmental impact that the conflict may be having on the region. i have therefore voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. the measures proposed by the five presidents' report are in the right direction, although the report is less ambitious than the european parliament's on the economic governance framework. beyond what the document contains, we must also take into account what is not yet being discussed. in particular, the absence of key psoe proposals is noteworthy: mutualisation of the public debt of the member states (eurobonds); launching the debt amortization fund on the basis of the esm, a particularly important element in solving the greek public debt crisis once and for all; issuing european public debt; european unemployment insurance. nor is it defined how the proposed euro area/european treasury fiscal capacity would be financed. finally, in the debate on the future of economic and monetary union, there is no reference to the need to strengthen the euro area horizontally, i.e. to extend it to the member states which are legally obliged to adopt the single currency. in this way, economic and monetary union would be strengthened politically while reducing the democratic deficit, because the european parliament would truly be the parliament of the euro.

opinion of the committee on transport and tourism. mr president, i would like to express my deep gratitude and appreciation to the two rapporteurs, mr fernandes and mr bullmann, for their patience, as well as to the entire team of the european parliament and to the other players in this agreement. the feie offers us two general virtues which are, in my view, essential for our discourse to the citizens. firstly, it has restored the words to the european anthem, so that it can once again be the 'hymn to joy', after these terrible seven years of weakness, suffering, poverty and backwardness in europe. the virtue of the juncker plan is that it has restored the original impetus of a common europe. after a crisis like a war, it's time to grow again: to jobs, to jobs, to jobs. the second virtue is more complex - and a two-sided coin - and opens up the debate on the coexistence of regulatory framework and growth. the surplus side is calling for more flexibility in the state aid rules. the other part, the deficit part, is seeking to ensure that investments in european programmes, clearly and explicitly european, such as the efsi, do not penalise the public debt. if the first virtue must be attributed to the commission, to president juncker, supported from the minute minus zero by this parliament, the second is that of a very intense negotiation, through the night, in a trilogue that was somewhat strange at the beginning, because in parliament we started off facing the council and the commission as an adversarial bloc, and i must especially thank vice-president georgieva - and she is present - for opening the door to a solution by restoring to the commission its interinstitutional role of helping us and therefore helping the citizens to find the solution. and that solution, after hours and hours of intensive negotiation, has borne fruit in the case of the transport sector, with 500 million euros coming out of the council's mouth or pocket, and going back to the erm, and we have even been able to advance another 500 million in the form of direct subsidies, which is what our transport sector needs most. we have also managed to bring the leverage effect of the 1 x 15 guarantee of the efsi in line with the principles and values of the ten-t programme, thus making it complementary and placing emphasis precisely on the sectors where the commission was finding the greatest difficulties: urban mobility, accessibility, safety, reduction of pollution, accidents, etc. and also extending the core and comprehensive networks through possible new nodes, but always with reference to the connecting europe facility, its principles and its objectives and values, and ensuring the presence of experts from the transport sector in all the necessary areas of programme governance. we in parliament have now fulfilled our task of improving the agreement. it is now up to the commission and the european investment bank, together with the private sector, the member states, the regions, civil society, etc., to put it into action so that it has the effect of creating jobs and growth in this sector as employment intensive as ours. the representatives of the sector were equally satisfied and hopeful yesterday in riga.
the fact that we are here today, mr president, debating an investment plan, shows that things are changing in the european union. we are finally abandoning the passion for austerity which is so damaging to europe. because austerity policies neither create growth nor jobs nor, of course, help european citizens. but in the last few months we've been seeing changes in economic policy. perhaps it is not yet too obvious in our daily lives, but that change is the change that society has demanded and that this group has asked the european commission to make. we have seen first of all how this commission has revised the pact for flexibility, stability and growth, giving more flexibility and more room for manoeuvre to implement growth-oriented policies. we have also seen a change in fiscal policy, with a firm pursuit of fraud and evasion and, moreover, a new approach to european corporate taxation; and we have also just seen, a few days ago, the report by the five presidents on strengthening economic and monetary union. and today we are talking about this juncker plan, an investment plan that wants to mobilise 315 billion euros to be invested in the real economy, which is what really matters to people. the commission, the council and parliament have been negotiating morning, afternoon and night - literally - to reach an agreement which can be adopted today, because the need to give an urgent boost to investment in europe has made us work against the clock, but the urgency has not prevented us from working on the important things, because we tabled more than 1 400 amendments to this plan, because we believed that the proposal could be improved, and the result of the agreement shows that. our work has improved funding. we have gotten another billion euros. and so we are not so much affecting existing programmes that also invest in the future of the european union, such as horizon 2020 and the connecting europe facility. our financing proposal was more appropriate and more ambitious, but it was a pity that the council did not have the courage to give the necessary financial support to such an important project. in fact, it is a pity that the council is not even in this debate today. but in any case, the final word on financing has not been said. in september we will negotiate the 2016 budget and we are also on the eve of negotiating a revision of the financial framework and we hope to obtain more resources for the plan. but not only has the financing been changed, but there has not been a single article of the rules of procedure which we have not improved. and that's it. i would like to thank the rapporteurs, mr josé manuel fernandes and mr udo bullmann, because they have managed to manage and negotiate a good agreement for europe. and now we should probably start working on a second juncker plan.
mr president, i think that the agreement reached during the trilogues was the best possible one, taking into account the position of the council and the commission. at many moments they were completely united against parliament. i do not think that the juncker plan is the cure for all our economic problems, but i do think it can be useful and that it goes in the right direction. the juncker plan can help to build the european infrastructure still needed to enhance our growth and deepen the single market. in particular, the efsi can be of great help in those countries which face more problems raising private capital in the financial markets. moreover, a personal objective was – from the beginning – to include provisions that ensure that the efsi will not be used to build ‘ghost airports’ without planes or high-speed trains without passengers. only projects with the capacity to attract private investors will be able to be part of the fund. the inclusion of the ten-t corridors is a very good piece of news too, as is the inclusion of regional promotional banks in the plan. in barcelona (where i come from), the catalan finance institute – a historic collaborator with the european investment bank – has been for years a key institution for reaching many innovative smes.
mr president, we are witnessing a certain ceremony of exaltation today, a certain self-referential triumphalism which is understandable. how can we dissent from a proposal which is finally geared to growth and not to the obsession with austerity which is already in force in other areas? that's why it's more necessary, i think, the critical counterpoint that i'm going to try. we have a new investment fund, but we don't have an investment plan. we have a powerful financial instrument, with some very interesting project management and selection elements, but we have no clear and verifiable objectives beyond the wishful thinking of perhaps mobilising eur 315 million. we do have some negative consolidated realities, such as the allocation to the best european programmes under horizon 2020. perhaps the best expression of the real ambition of the efsi is the famous phrase 'in particular through', used to avoid any real commitment to the coherence of the selected projects with the explicit objectives of the european strategies. mr katainen said that the market failure that characterizes the present situation had to be addressed, a much larger private investment gap, by the way, than the fund wants to create. once again, all in the service of the market and only in the service of the market. the general interest, at best, will be a desirable second derivative. okay, we'll work to get reality to disprove our critical concerns. we will try - and i will try - from our social and economic reality, from my own country, to see that the projects which justify the decision which this parliament will adopt today are put forward. but as we will see in the votes, this debate is absolutely overcoming geographical or ideological boundaries. i shall vote against, as the best demonstration of my commitment to a real policy, aimed at sustainable growth and reducing inequalities, objectives which this plan does not even claim to assume.
mr president, commissioner, the approval of the juncker plan is undoubtedly proof that with political will europe advances and the citizens win. i would therefore like to congratulate the rapporteurs, mr fernandes and mr bullmann, and of course vice-president katainen, on the enormous work they have done. because, without a doubt, this plan will contribute to the objective that we all have in this room: growth and job creation. but let us not forget that this will not solve the great problem europe has. it is certainly part of the solution, but it is not the solution. as vice-president katainen said, we need to continue to make progress on reforms at national level, but also, at european level, we need to encourage the single capital market, the single energy market and the digital single market to boost growth and job creation. but, without a doubt, what we're about to approve today is great news.
in writing. the juncker plan is not an investment plan, however much it is insisted upon. it is an insurance plan for large private investors, who see their speculative projects as subsidized by the state, which guarantees their losses in case of bankruptcy. once again, the neoliberal framework is imposed in the definition of public policies. where criteria of cohesion and the spine of the european economy, of productive convergence of its less developed regions, were needed, we find the deepening of the liberalizing trends of the last decades: in infrastructure, in energy; even in public services, since governance itself pushes the states to cut back and resort to this type of plans. there is a need for a public investment programme, in which the state takes care of technological development and economic diversification, especially in foreign trade. and there is also budgetary scope for this, if the eib supports the states directly and the ecb acts on the secondary market, if genuine fiscal harmonization is carried out: all proposals that your commission rejects, deepening the crisis of the project and the european economy.
blue card question. what is it? thank you very much, comrade lucke, for accepting the question. in your speech you have contrasted national sovereignty, the ability of states to direct their economic policy, and i would like to ask you whether you do not think that you are worthy of representing the sovereignty of your fellow citizens, of the german citizens, as we all are in this house, worthy of representing european citizenship and sovereignty.
on behalf of the green group, good afternoon. thank you very much, colleagues. first of all, i would like to thank the rapporteur, who has made it possible for us to have a good working relationship. however, i have to say that my group's vote will be negative, not least because i think the right wing of this parliament has wanted to impose a report that is timid, that is not ambitious and that is extremely conservative, and a clear and unambiguous support for what the current governance framework is. i think that is a mistake, and i regret that the socialist group has given in to this pressure. look, the framework has failed. the objectives pursued by the framework we have adopted are exactly contrary to the rules we have set ourselves, not least because, with the rules we have set ourselves, we now have more deficits, more indebtedness and more recession and it is therefore clear that this does not allow the european union to achieve the path of well-being. so let's assume that the framework has failed and let's assume that we need legal reform. many groups have been calling for parliament to call for a legal reform of the framework which would open up the prospects for a great many things which are essential at the moment, whether it is having our own budgetary capacity, a sufficiently strong taxation system, a review of the rules of the stability and growth pact, what kind of reforms we are making and the question of debt. the reference to the debt issue in the report is very timid and we know that we have a serious problem, even though there are many groups that have made amendments in this respect so that there would be a reference. and i would like to say that in some of these areas this report is a step backwards, because in the area of debt and other matters we had, for example, in the troika report of the previous term, much more advanced references. i therefore believe that my group cannot support this report at the moment and i would also like to say - and i am making this appeal to all the members of the left in this parliament - that we must not go forward by putting a couple of commas in a completely ideologized neoliberal framework, which is not ours. we must put forward a real alternative to reform the euro area, which is the urgent thing right now.
mr president, i have heard many critical voices in this debate and i would like to point out that the merit of this report and of the report by the chairmen is that it provides us with an opportunity to open a debate on the reforms that our economic and monetary organization needs. this is the value of this report. it's not perfect, obviously. it's a necessary pact. it is an opportunity to work on the necessary reforms in the fiscal union, in the social union, in labour mobility, in political organisation, in the political reforms that have to be made in the treaty, including for better governance. it's very easy to say no. i understand many who say no, but today i want to reclaim the importance of the pact, the importance of agreeing. because europe, for the most part, does that by agreeing and tackling problems as we're going to do this afternoon.
the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. obviously, there's a problem here. i know that many groups are raising this question because they want much stricter application of the rules of the pact, but the problem is that in many circumstances the rules are contrary to the objectives themselves and are often unenforceable. i therefore believe that there is also a lot of reflection to be done here on the extent to which the flexibility itself incorporated in the stability and growth pact is sufficient or not, because in recent years what has happened is that flexibility has simply been used to be able to legalise de facto situations; that is to say, when a state no longer complied with the rules, flexibility made it possible to fill that legal gap. but that is clearly not the case and, in any case, with the commission's communication on flexibility, we hope that this will improve. we must also, of course, make the rules clear. the commission must explain exactly how it applies these criteria and we are therefore also interested in asking it some questions, for example, what methodology is used to draw up its economic analyses within the framework of the pact itself. that is a very important question. and if the commission can also explain its choice between a bottom-up or a top-down economic analysis when assessing the reform efforts of the member states. we'd like to know that too. thirdly, what kind of analysis has been the basis for the council's recommendations since the six-pack of governance measures came into force? also, that they clarify that. finally, my last question - and i will end with this - is when the commission will make public its legal opinion on the consistency of communication 12/2015 with the provisions of the stability and growth pact, in accordance with regulation (ec) no 1049/2001 itself on public access to documents, which is a question that has been repeated in many debates and which we believe is also important.
commissioner, with the reform of corporate taxation you have opened up one of the crucial issues of the present european union, an institutional framework designed to favour the interests of big business, with a tax structure that is regressive both in the member states and in the union as a whole. the proposals you are putting forward are clearly insufficient, they lack clear commitments and dates that would allow us to have confidence that progress will be made in the fight against tax evasion. in the meantime, the greek government has presented to the institutions viable plans to increase revenue through the fight against tax evasion in its country. instead of welcoming these proposals, mr juncker and mr dijsselbloem, the architects of tax havens like luxembourg and the netherlands, have preferred to impose a reform of indirect taxes which criminally increases the burden on the working classes. commissioner, with your commission's policy we are today closer than ever to a system that robs the poor to give to the rich. this is the tale of robon hood.
member of the commission: i think that this debate tonight shows once again that, particularly when it comes to tax reforms, corporate tax reforms, these reforms are often controversial. i think it is clear that there is a consensus that action must be taken, and i think that is also clear from the work of the special tax committee here in this parliament, mr lamassoure. some colleagues think we are going too fast, too far and exaggerating, and others regret that we are not more courageous, that we do not prescribe more than we program. i would like to reply to this double criticism that this plan is well thought out in the commission, that it is solid and balanced, balanced and also that it is realistic. colleagues, i want to thank you. most of you have supported the commission's approach and i would like to thank you for your broad support for that action programme. in reply to some of your interventions, i should like to make the following comments. first of all, i would like to say something about consolidation. i can assure you that in the form we will give to the common base for corporation tax, consolidation will remain an important, firm objective that the commission has in mind and that we will not lose our ambition in that regard. as regards the tariffs, some of my colleagues have also advocated uniformity or harmonization of these tariffs. i'm afraid i'm going to have to disappoint those people, because it's not going to be about rates. the proposal concerns only the corporate tax base, not the rates. thirdly, i should like to say something about the reporting by country. i can assure you - and this was also a question from one of the members - that the whole commission is determined to take this seriously and to extend the rules to this end as far as necessary. finally, i would like to point out that the commission is cooperating constructively with the oecd. i said that in my introduction. but of course we do not do this without taking account of the special features of the systems which are specific to the european union. you know that tax systems are very sensitive to sudden shocks, that they have little resistance to them. that means that all reforms must be very well documented, thoroughly prepared and also implemented correctly. the approach presented today is the right one, an ambitious but realistic approach. a solid but also flexible approach. we also need this flexibility to adapt to future developments. i am convinced that the commission, with the proposal which i have had the honour of presenting here today on behalf of the commission, will ensure that there is more justice, that there can be more effective taxation and that we can and will move to a tax system which is a much stronger stimulus to employment and growth. that's what people expect from us. that is what the citizens of europe can expect from us. and that is what is being asked of us by the business community, by large companies, but especially by small ones. it is now up to the member states to take action, to take control of this dossier. i am counting on your support, ladies and gentlemen, to support us in your capitals and here in this european parliament. i think we have a common goal and if we work together to achieve it and put our energy into it and do everything we can to get there, then i am sure we will be able to make serious steps forward. we look forward to discussing this matter with you and i thank you very much for this exchange of views.
in writing. the commission will relaunch its proposal for a common consolidated corporate tax base (ccctb) as a comprehensive solution to corporate tax reform. negotiations on the biccis proposal submitted by the commission in 2011 are currently at a standstill. the commission will immediately start work on a new proposal to introduce a biccis on a compulsory basis in accordance with a progressive approach. this will enable member states to move more rapidly towards the implementation of the common tax base. consolidation would be introduced in a second stage, as this has so far been the most complex element in the negotiations. the action plan also addresses the issue of effective taxation in the eu, which is summed up in the idea that companies should pay their fair share of tax in the country where they make their profits. according to the commission, this can be achieved without harmonising corporate tax rates across the eu. in this respect, we must be more ambitious in the legislative field, launch a more comprehensive transparency strategy and aim to include all 28 member states in the initiative.

madam president, the spanish supreme court ruled last may that the extension of the port of valencia, one of the most important in the mediterranean, was illegal. the construction work began on july 1, 2002, soon to be 13 years since the disaster. he expropriated over a thousand landlords in the la punta area, the best productive orchard in all of europe. sixty people were evicted from their homes and hundreds of years old farms and barracks were destroyed, a unique heritage that has been lost forever. the people of la punta were harassed, left homeless and without land, and all this was done to build a logistics zone of 680 000 m2, which is completely empty, in which not a single company has settled. and the european union funded that illegal, failed and unsustainable project. it is therefore responsible. that is why i am asking that the culprits be found and that the same funds that were used to destroy it be used now to rehabilitate this unique neighbourhood in europe, to return it to the situation it was in before. it's a matter of elementary justice.
madam president, i would like to refer to the latest report by the international monetary fund, which recalled the growing inequalities that are affecting europe and the world today and warned us that inequality is not only a social problem today, but is a serious obstacle to economic growth. the international monetary fund has done so and the oecd did so recently in may. to recall some facts from my country, spain. during the economic crisis, the rich in my country have grown by 40%, but at the same time today we have 29% of people 29% at risk of social exclusion or poverty. we must remember that inequalities are the great challenge of our time, that they are hindering economic growth, that they are a social disaster, but above all they are eroding our democracy, european democracy and that of our states, because without a socially just model it is impossible to have economic growth and a sustainable democracy in the long term.
madam president, we live in turbulent times, times of external and internal tensions. tensions arising from the failure of a global order that sought the surrender of all sovereignty. tensions arising from the emerging multipolarity of the emerging countries. tension over a design that punishes our nations in the south and east for indebtedness, deindustrialization and inequality. it is in this context that the european union will define its future. it can remain the pawn and the board on which other atlantic interests are played and defended. he can continue to push free trade agreements that only guarantee the freedom of big corporations. it can continue to support regional inequality, the destruction of secular states and the support of ethnic and religious apartheid regimes, or it can turn the corner and ensure its presence with sovereignty and independence, with respect for our neighbours and with justice for our peoples and nations.

in writing. i supported the waiver of immunity in the case of member of parliament ud voigt because i believe that the german courts should be able to decide whether he, as chairman of the npd political party, did not violate the law by publishing a publication at the time of the world cup which could have contained racist attacks on players of the german national team. these activities and the initiation of the investigation took place long before his election to the european parliament and cannot therefore in any way be considered as a political obstruction of his mandate as a member of the european parliament. i believe that freedom of speech is a fundamental value, but it is not possible to think that this freedom has no limits or that it can be used to spread racist or class hatred.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) because i believe that the result achieved by the european parliament after tough negotiations with the council marks the concrete achievement of our priority of reorienting european economic policy towards growth and investment. we have managed to make the efsi an investment tool that promotes projects in line with our political priorities. the agreement reached ensures the financing of quality investments, facilitates additional co-financing for all member states, strengthens the governance of the efsi within the european framework and proposes a more appropriate and ambitious alternative financing of the guarantee fund to safeguard the european r & d & i and transport programmes, horizon 2020 and the connecting europe facility with an additional eur 1 billion. it is a good agreement which will give an urgent boost to much needed investment in the union.
in writing. ‒ the european fund for strategic investments (efsi), the cornerstone of the juncker plan, aims to increase investment in the european union and foster economic recovery by providing support for economically viable projects that are currently not being developed because private investors are hesitant about financing them. the creation of this fund gives us a unique opportunity to revive the union's economy. however, we believe that this funding should not be at the expense of the budgets of other key european research projects such as horizon 2020 or the connecting europe facility. upyd considers it a great step forward that the board of directors of the efsi is composed of representatives of the commission and the european investment bank, and not of the states themselves. the selection of projects by an investment committee of independent experts will also ensure that projects are selected on the basis of objective criteria and sound financial management, avoiding political opportunism, cronyism and misuse of the money of all europeans. that is why we have decided to vote in favour of this regulation.

in writing. ‒ the european fund for strategic investments is a leveraged fund: with a capital of eur 21 billion, supplemented by the european investment bank (eur 5 billion) and the european union (eur 16 billion), this envelope will be used to raise more resources in the form of bond loans. the expected leverage is eur 315 billion (x15), but the sincerity of these claims can be doubted. on the one hand, the previous similar package, the growth and jobs pact of 2012-2013, which was supposed to create €60 billion, with a leverage of 6, actually resulted in €20 billion, with a leverage of 2. the fund will also have a positive effect. it will mainly benefit companies that would have invested with other means of financing anyway. finally, this plan will be subject to structural reforms (labour market reforms and fiscal consolidation), i.e. an austerity policy which is already hampering growth. this is why the steering committee is composed of only commission and eib members, supposedly to guarantee its independence. the states have been excluded, and that does not bode well for the future.
in writing. ‒ we voted against the commission's proposal because, although the result of the tripartite dialogue improved the commission's intolerable proposal, this fund is by no means - by its size or its forms of administration - the countercyclical gamble that europe needs. the efsi is intended to support the development of the union's financial markets by supporting the development of the union's financial markets and the union's financial markets.

in writing. ‒ the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) aims to provide assistance to workers made redundant and to self-employed persons whose activity has ceased as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns caused by globalisation, the continuation of the global financial and economic crisis or a new global financial and economic crisis, and to assist them with their reintegration into the labour market. i voted in favour of this report to approve the mobilisation of eur 630 000 from the egf for technical assistance to improve the functioning and implementation of the fund. this technical assistance will improve the tracking and data collection of applications, the general knowledge, information and visibility of the egf through the improvement of its website, create a knowledge base/application interface to standardise, simplify and accelerate the processing of application and management procedures, strengthen the administrative and technical support to the egf member states and finance a mid-term evaluation with a view to finalising the evaluation by 30 june 2017, as required by article 20 (1) (a) of the egf regulation.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report. the report approves the mobilisation of a small part of the commission's budget (eur 630 000) to help implement the european globalisation adjustment fund. this fund was used, for example, in the case of the closure of the delphi company in the bay of cadiz, although the management of this item by the junta de andalucía did not give the promised results. the report includes an amendment tabled by the rapporteur, mrs liadh, which suggests that the number of workers made redundant needed to mobilise the fund may be revised downwards. this is an important point in view of the future review of the egf.

in writing. ‒ this is a technical report on the mobilisation of eur 630 000 from the fund to cover technical assistance at the initiative of the commission. the technical assistance shall be aimed at financing monitoring and information, creating a knowledge base/application interface and advising member states on the use, monitoring and evaluation of the egf. in accordance with article 11 (1) of the egf regulation, up to 0,5% of the maximum available resources of the egf (i.e. eur 750 000 in 2011 prices) may be used each year for technical assistance at the initiative of the commission. i agree with these considerations and have therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because the european globalisation adjustment fund supports people who lose their jobs as a result of the changes in world trade brought about by globalisation. the fund is intended to help, for example, workers in companies that relocate production outside the eu or in companies that have to close as a result of a global economic crisis.
in writing. ‒ we are talking about a fund which is responsible for processing transfers of funds to cover maximum redundancy payments for the cessation of different business activities in the member states. in this case, we are dealing with a technical adjustment by the commission on the basis of the content of the proposal which has already been approved by the council. it is therefore appropriate to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the review of the economic governance framework because it is urgent and necessary to complete the turnaround of european economic policy, and in particular to close the gaps in economic and monetary union (emu). the report suggests ways of making better use of the flexibility provided by the existing rules, strengthening economic coordination and simplifying procedures, and improving democratic control of structural reforms. in particular, the following elements should be highlighted:- approval of common structural or convergence policy objectives by co-decision (i.e. with the involvement of the european parliament). - interinstitutional agreement on the participation of the european parliament in a simplified european semester. - fiscal capacity of the euro area to cope with asymmetric shocks. - convergence of tax policies. - the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion at european level. - initiatives to reduce the stock of public debt in the euro area. - strengthening the social dimension, including the establishment of a european minimum wage. i also believe it is important to complement the vertical strengthening of emu with its horizontal consolidation so that, by 2020, the member states which already meet the economic conditions will join emu.
in writing. ‒ the report on the economic governance framework seeks to set out the european parliament's position in the debate on economic and monetary union with a view to further integration and cooperation in economic matters. what could have been a unique opportunity for the european parliament to take an ambitious stance in establishing a sound framework for crisis management and for advancing the economic and political governance of the union has been left in a decaffeinated text that does not even consider the basis of the european commission's own proposal. upyd regrets that fundamental aspects such as the revision of country-specific recommendations, the revision of macroeconomic imbalances or an insolvency mechanism for states are not included. the text also makes no reference to the role of the european court of justice or the need for an external representative of the euro area. in short, the report lacks analysis, concrete proposals and effective solutions. we have therefore decided to vote against the report.

in writing. ‒ the report focuses on the strengthening of the euro area's economic governance framework since the start of the crisis. in this context, and given the slow growth, the wide disparities in the situation between member states, high unemployment, low inflation and low levels of investment, the report considers that decisive action is urgently needed. the report highlights the following issues: support for the commission communication on flexibility in the interpretation of the stability and growth pact; adoption of the common structural or convergence policy objectives by co-decision (i.e. with the involvement of the european parliament); adoption of an interinstitutional agreement on the european parliament's participation in a simplified european semester; elimination of the troika; convergence of tax policies; the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion at european level; and strengthening the social dimension, including the minimum wage. i agree with these considerations and have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the role of co-legislator condemns the european parliament to fall far behind the commission, which could only be a positive thing if parliament took advantage of the review of the past to guide the future. this is not the case with the berès report, which we are voting against, where instead of a critical look the policies with which the eu has faced the economic crisis are praised, ignoring the fact that they have divided the continent between creditors and debtors, and have generated colossal unemployment and poverty. the european parliament has voted in favour of the commission's proposal to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover all the activities of the european union's institutions. it is not only a mistake, but it is a failure on the part of this parliament to go ahead and propose solutions for the future.
in writing. ‒ the governance of the euro area, always difficult, has been particularly complex during the period of economic crisis, with decisions that may not have always been the right ones, but which i believe have been the right ones overall to deal with this difficult situation. however, there is a need to reflect on economic governance and that is why i support the european parliament's resolution, in which we call for issues such as taking greater account of national circumstances when implementing measures or ensuring control over the indirect effects that are caused.

in writing. i consider it crucial in this report on the review of the economic governance framework that there be no attempts to relax existing economic governance rules, such as the excessive deficit procedure or the macroeconomic imbalances procedure, and to weaken the emphasis on budgetary discipline and structural reforms in favour of public investment. the maintenance of budgetary discipline is one of the main tasks of the state in the economic field and its implementation has a key economic impact on the state of the economy. on the other hand, i consider the idea that public investment is more important than budgetary discipline to be wrong and, i am not afraid to say, harmful.
