member of the commission.– mr president, this is an important moment for the capital markets union (cmu), and i would like to thank mr gualtieri and mr balz for setting out the issues facing us so clearly. this is a classic single market project for all 28 member states: for those without developed capital markets, as well as for those with. indeed, i would argue that it is member states without strong capital markets which could stand to gain the most, because cmu will help create the conditions for capital to flow across borders and to smes, no matter where they are. to help this flow, we will look at venture capital, at angel investing, at crowd-funding and at private placement. it is, as we have already heard, a major priority of the cmu to broaden the range of financing options for smes, to complement banking, and to improve the funding conveyor belt. we have all seen examples of european ideas and european businesses going to the united states for their funding. i want those businesses to stay and grow here in europe. we will review our venture capital regulation; we will strengthen our venture capital industry; we will review the prospectus directive to make it easier for larger smes to raise money on the public markets; we will seek to free up bank balance sheets by reviving the eu market for securitisation through the identification of simple, transparent and standardised securitisations. that will help banks to lend more, including to smes. we are also looking at how we could improve sme credit information to make it easier for smes to attract investment. i think that members of this committee know better than anyone about the steps taken over the last five years to improve the regulation of capital markets. your resolution also rightly argues that we should take stock of the overall impact of financial regulation and be proportionate in our measures, and i agree with that. on supervision, respondents to the consultation argued that the esa’s existing set of powers are sufficient, but some also called for greater supervisory convergence to ensure a level playing field. we also need to consider our overall macro-prudential framework. in terms of next steps, we are on track to publish our action plan in september. concrete proposals will follow shortly afterwards. they will include a comprehensive package on securitisation, with updated calibrations for solvency ii and crr, the definition of infrastructure and revised calibrations for solvency ii, and these proposals to review the prospectus directive. this is an ambitious programme. it will require sustained effort over a number of years, but we need to make quick progress, so i hope that these first proposals can be fast-tracked by the co-legislators. i look forward to developing this project with you, but most of all, i look forward to helping more european businesses, especially smes, get the funding they want, in order to increase choices for savers, to strengthen cross-border investment and also, i believe, to increase financial stability.
on behalf of the ppe group the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the single capital market is precisely one of the instruments for achieving and reconciling both objectives. because the single capital market will improve the allocation of financial resources between the various countries of the european union. and also because, as commissioner hill has said, it will improve the financing of small and mediumsized enterprises, the real engine of economic growth and job creation. this is the way, your honours. let us not deceive the european citizens. the cancellation of a sovereign debt that has an average default of sixteen years will not boost growth. with growth, sovereign debt will be sustainable. without growth, it's hardly going to be. and for growth, to drive economic growth, we know what we have to do: reforms at the national level - my country, spain, is an example - and more europe, more economic integration, i insist. and the capital markets union is a first and a big step in moving in that direction. (the speaker agrees to answer a question put under the 'blue card' procedure (rule 162 (8) of the rules of procedure))
the answer is 'blue card'. your honor, i disagree. the single capital market is an important instrument for improving the competitiveness of our economy and for boosting growth and job creation. and the basis for its success will undoubtedly be that it covers the whole of the european union; not just the euro area, but the whole of the european union.
mr president, the european commission considers that its proposal for a single capital market is the solution to the financing problems of the european economy, but this is not the case. during the early years of the euro, banks and others used their credit to fuel the huge financial bubbles, the consequences of which we are still suffering. despite the billions of euros dedicated to the bank bailout, which we will never get back, the flow of credit to the real economy continues to be stopped. opening this flow to the major international investment funds will only increase speculation and instability in funding. the problems of the european economy are different and stem from the profound stagnation of demand due to austerity policies, not from a lack of capital. the idea that smes should be financed through complex financial products rather than credit seems cynical. the financial markets have failed the european union and now it is the public's turn. if no one was afraid to bail out the banks with public money, no one should be afraid to boost the economy from the state. what can save the economy is public investment and public banking to finance smes and create jobs.
mr president, thank you very much, commissioner. i think that the document which has been discussed and adopted by the committee on economic and monetary affairs on the future of the capital market is well-targeted. i congratulate mr gualtieri and mr balz on their agreement, on their wording, but there are three things that concern me about the green paper that the commission has presented. the first is the absence of any proper reflection on the euro area's relationship with the rest of the union. forgetting that a substantial part of europe is based in the euro area, that the euro can be a key element in organising a real capital market, i think it would require additional reflection, a public debt issue that would allow a risk-free asset. in any case, beyond this, the capital market wants or should regularize shadow banking, which is non-bank financing after all. and i would like to ask the commissioner what legislative initiatives he expects us to take to ensure that this non-banking market is regulated efficiently, including taxation, in addition to insolvency proceedings. there is a very important financial regulation agenda to try to get these non-bank markets in a clear and efficient order, and in the last few months we have learned that the commission is not keen to push through many legislative initiatives, but in this area it is essential, in taxation, in any of the points to get that market to work. (the speaker agrees to answer a question put under the 'blue card' procedure (rule 162 (8) of the rules of procedure))
the answer is 'blue card'. mr woolfe, i obviously do not share your view that europe is not growing because there is too much regulation. i believe that europe needs a clear regulatory framework. that in this case, to get that capital market unit going we need a legal environment. and i simply recommend or urge you to defend your constituency, your representatives, clearly, because i think the united kingdom would have a lot to gain if we were able to organise a common european market.
mr president, commissioners, there are several reasons for this commission proposal on the circular economy. the first is the growing demand for resources due to economic growth in third countries. secondly, the scarcity of raw materials on our continent, especially the most valuable ones, since we only have exceptional and difficult-to-access deposits. the third reason is our desire to minimize environmental impacts in the exploitation of natural resources and also in waste management. the aim is to reintroduce waste into the production cycle, thus creating a virtuous circle of efficiency, waste management, emission reduction and, in general, environmental protection. a very commendable task, but a very difficult one. i therefore thank and congratulate the rapporteur on her work, which has not been easy. we must be aware that in this matter a large part of the effort has to be made and paid for, of course, by the companies and, ultimately, by the consumers and the citizen. i am in favour of the new legislation the commission is working on being ambitious, but at the same time realistic. the important thing is that member states, on the basis of the waste hierarchy, continuously improve the quality of waste management. in this way we can achieve our real objective, which is to reintroduce as much waste as possible into the economic cycle and to ensure that the waste disposed of without recycling is as little as possible and, if possible, not disposed of at all.
mr president, this is a report with good criteria and objectives, such as energy efficiency, sustainable product life cycle and zero waste. in my view, it rightly calls for binding targets where they are needed, such as reducing waste generation, and with whom it is needed, involving local and regional authorities in the development of the circular economy package. the report fully supports separate collection and calls for mandatory targets, and proposes to limit incineration strictly to non-recyclable and non-biodegradable waste. in a large part of gipuzkoa, a territory of euskal herria, we have been following this path for several years, and we have fulfilled, in 2015, the objectives that are set here for 2020. gipuzkoa shows that it is feasible to double recycling rates in four years and to make the transition to 70% in ten years, that is to say that the binding objectives required by the approach advocated in this report are perfectly possible.
member of the commission.– mr president, i am very pleased to have the opportunity to participate in this evening’s debate. i welcome the fact that this is a full debate which reflects the importance of the european milk sector. it is a critical element of the eu agricultural sector, which is in itself a key driver of jobs and growth, contributing significantly to the commission’s jobs and growth agenda. i want to convey my particular thanks to the rapporteur, mr nicholson, who has used his long experience in the sector to draft a report that is a very useful contribution to the debate that has surrounded the long-awaited and historic expiry of milk quotas just three months ago. but as he has said, this particular issue is not confined to that period of time. i read the report with interest, and i share most of the report’s assessment of the challenges and opportunities that lie ahead of the sector. before commenting on some of the specifics of the report, i would like to say something about the current market situation. perhaps not surprisingly, maybe even inevitably, there has been some price volatility following the end of quotas. this volatility, which has been contributed to by a global oversupply of milk, has led to downward pressure on milk prices, with the effects being felt most acutely in some member states more than others. the eu average price in may was 30.48 cents per kilo. in absolute terms, and if applied consistently across the eu, this would represent a reasonable return for most farmers. however, i acknowledge that the variation in prices paid to farmers in different member states can be quite significant. i am concerned about these developments, and i therefore instructed my services to assess the market situation more closely in terms of the member states that have a very low price presently. in the union, in 2014, we produced 4.5% more milk than in the previous year, while the other main world suppliers increased their output in the area of 2%. in 2015, and in spite of the limited reduction in deliveries during the first quarter, we are already on par with last year, and projections indicate that, in spite of moderate prices, we will end the year with an overall increase of 0.9%. outlets have to be found for these quantities of milk. while we have some challenges to face, we are fortunate that we can count on a complete toolkit of measures available to the cap to address these challenges, thanks to the work on the cap reform by paolo de castro, michel dantin, jim nicholson and others. these are available, and these measures include the safety net tools, including the public buying-in of butter and skimmed milk powder as well as private storage aid schemes; the possibility to intervene in exceptional circumstances, as in the case of the russian import ban; direct payments to support farmers’ income, including coupled support up to 13% of the national envelope; rural development policy, which allows farmers to finance investments, be better trained or receive compensation for being located in areas of natural constraint; the possibility to implement risk management tools; the milk package, which is yet to be fully exploited, and which can strengthen the integration of the producers in the supply chain; and the strengthening of the milk market observatory board, with more timely meetings and more time data available now, providing signals in the marketplace on a monthly basis. dairy farmers can also benefit from the quality policy and from research and innovation, which are particularly relevant for producers oriented to niche products. we have more money in the promotion policy budget to accompany dairy operators in their search for new customers, and the identification of new markets is a personal priority for me. i have heard some suggestions recently that the commission is doing very little to support dairy farmers. any objective analysis of this matter certainly does not stand up to scrutiny. let me illustrate the reality: the safety net measures – intervention in private storage, both for butter and skimmed milk powder – have been available to eu operators since last summer. by its rapid action, the commission has provided economic actors with certainty and security. special targeted support, for a total amount of eur 40 million, was granted to dairy farmers from those member states most directly hit by the russian ban – the baltic states and finland in particular. after beef and veal, dairy is the second—largest recipient of voluntary coupled support, with 20% of the total amount, amounting to eur 820 million in 19 member states. as regards the milk package, which i said earlier has yet to achieve its full potential, we should not underestimate the huge progress that has been made. 13 member states have provided for compulsory contracts. the number of recognised producer organisations is growing. what is more relevant is their impact on jointly-negotiated volumes of milk deliveries. in germany and the czech republic, more than one-third of deliveries are negotiated by these organisations. in france, this figure is some 17%, and in spain – 12%. other member states are following this welcome trend. the commission recently approved 41 new programmes to promote agricultural products in the eu and in third country markets, worth eur 130 million over three years. some eur 24 million are devoted to specific programmes on dairying. school milk schemes: last school year, 19 million children participated, with more than 300 000 tonnes of milk and milk products distributed for a total eu expenditure of eur 66 million. as i mentioned, they have strengthened the role of the milk market observatory. the economic board meets on a regular basis so that all actors can benefit from more timely and complete market information than ever. some voices claim that increasing intervention prices is the solution. it is one of the options that are certainly mentioned in mr nicholson's report. in my view, this could be counterproductive, because this product has to be put out on the market in the future, and it is apparent that farmers and economic operators follow market signals. let me also be very clear about proposals to increase intervention prices. this would do nothing but delay the inevitable – a necessary adjustment – and make it even more painful in the future, in our view. and as we move towards a market-orientated policy, which is the policy agreed by the legislators, such a move would give the wrong signal. there is a need to change our mindset. the goal is not to produce as much as we can, but as much as we can find a market for. while i accept that there is a short-term difficulty (being experienced in the milk sector – and i hope my words will not come back to haunt me, mr nicholson, in relation to that statement), i believe that we should concentrate our energy on helping the european dairy sector reap the full benefit of the long-term positive prospects in terms of world consumption. this is a sector with enormous potential. there is an increased global demand of 2% and an increased middle class in the far east. we must all work together to ensure that we get our main share of this particular market and achieve our full potential.
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, commissioner, i am speaking on behalf of mrs herranz to stress something that you know very well. the milk sector is going through very difficult times and is very nervous about the fall in market prices. the abolition of the quota system last april was recently supplemented by russia's announcement that it would extend the embargo on european exports of milk and other agricultural products. the sector has already been struggling for years to cope with production costs and increasing price volatility. the situation is now very uncertain and therefore needs the support of the european institutions. i think that the european commission and the member states should listen to the demands made by parliament in the report we are voting on this week, which has tried to find solutions for the future. the european union should have more appropriate and operational instruments than those offered by the current common organization of the market to deal with the problems of the sector. first of all, the current safety net should be improved, as it is totally inoperative. there should be an update of intervention prices to take account of market realities. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of animals used for scientific purposes. it is no use having a european press observatory if it is not used in real time to alert the public to the arrival of critical situations. in order to make efficient use of this observatory, it would be necessary to define crisis levels in accordance with the indicators established for the whole of the european union, which should include the loss of economic margins by dairy farms. i also believe that producer organizations should be given greater bargaining power in relation to the links in the food chain in order to reduce the level of great helplessness in which farmers often find themselves. in many countries, like mine, the market is dominated by raw milk, so there is also a need to encourage the improvement of the added value of production and innovation measures. the commission has already taken steps to prevent the use of milk madam president, i am speaking as the alternative rapporteur for the s&d group and i would first of all like to thank the rapporteur for his collaborative and participatory approach to this report. but we socialists are in favour of a reform of the legal system which would precisely minimise the risks that public-private partnerships, or ppps, as they are known, can pose. we believe that a ppp should never be chosen because it is a method that accounts for the benefit of the administration by not running a deficit, but because it is the best way of providing a public service in the most efficient and cheapest way possible, and for this it is essential that the transfer of risks is redefined very well. we will never support a public-private partnership model which allows economic benefits to be privatized and losses to be socialized through the public purse. app should never be the first step towards the privatisation of a public service, and that is why we want a very clear, very transparent legal framework which also provides the administrations with technical and financial resources.

member of the commission.– mr president, ttip is a broad negotiation. it covers traditional trade issues but also many other issues, from medical devices regulation and financial services to sustainable development. to get it right, we need the engagement of the whole of this parliament, and this resolution is proving that engagement. the fact that 14 committees in addition to the committee on international trade were all active, proves that members are very engaged in this and has enabled the whole parliament to take part in discussions, in deliberations and in getting to know all the details of this agreement. when president juncker came here to present the agenda for his commission last july, he made clear that ttip was one of his core priorities, and this house at that time voted very strongly for his agenda. why? because ttip is an essential part of the commission’s strategy to open markets around the world. we are doing that not to benefit a small few, but in order to create opportunities for the whole of europe: the people of europe, the consumers of europe, the entrepreneurs of europe. one in seven people in europe have a job thanks to exports around the world. those jobs are highly skilled and better paid than average. 4.7 million of those jobs are linked to exports to the us. ttip would help increase that number. it would also make goods cheaper and more varied for consumers, and it would help to make our small and medium-sized companies more competitive. they would find it easier to export and to get their imported components and raw materials more cheaply. those are solid economic advantages. we cannot afford to turn our backs on them now or in the future. second, ttip is also a strategic alliance with the country that most closely shares europe’s commitment to core values and to a high level of protection of people and of the environment in our regulation. we need an ally like this to shape the globalisation we see deepening before our eyes every day. we are more affected by economic and political decisions made in other countries than ever before. we particularly need an ally, because we know that the strength of our voice in the world is, in relative terms, decreasing. ttip guarantees that partnership with america for the future, and we cannot afford to turn our backs on that either. there is, honourable members, as you know, an unprecedented debate about this agreement. that is a good thing. i respect people who have doubts and questions, across the continent and within this house. i take those concerns very seriously and have engaged a lot with national parliaments, with this parliament, with ngos, with civil society and other stakeholders to listen and to try to understand their concerns. i hope that all these people see the changes that we have made in order to take account of their views. since last november, i have opened up these negotiations to unprecedented public scrutiny. i have put eu negotiating proposals on the internet and increased the access of members of this parliament and representatives of the member states to the process. i have visited 14 national parliaments so far to exchange and open channels. i am happy to say that ttip is the world’s most transparent bilateral free trade negotiation. we have also made clear where we stand on public services such as public health and water concessions. this is a concern i have heard very frequently. i have, together with ambassador froman, the us trade representative, made a joint statement: the eu and the us are fully united around a crystal-clear vision that nothing in ttip will change the fact that only member states choose how their public services should be organised. we have also made it very clear where we stand on regulation. i have put the proposal on cooperating with the us online, and it says that there will be no limitations on the power of this parliament or any national parliament or of european governments. we want the benefits of shared expertise and we want opportunities for our people. that is all. i have made proposals for a deep reform of investment protection. the result is a completely new approach. we still want to foster job-creating investment but we are proposing a new system that sets down the right to regulate in black and white: a new system that takes us away from the private arbitration tribunals of the past. instead, we want a future in which disputes are decided in an international investment court, by judges and with a right of appeal. ttip will be a step towards that goal, not the final result. it is an essential step, given the role of the us as a global investor. parliament’s resolution is a vital step in those negotiations, but it is certainly not the end of our conversation. the commission will continue to be flexible and to take account of members’ views. beyond investment, we also have important proposals to discuss how best to protect labour and environmental rights and digital commerce. there will be many more issues to debate over the course of these talks, which are far from over. these negotiations are far reaching, and a lot of work is still needed. i will continue to push the us on our offensive interests, including on public procurement, where we expect an ambitious proposal, but also on services, energy and geographical indications, to mention just a few examples. parliament’s resolution will provide a vital basis for that conversation. it will also be vital for the negotiations themselves. having parliament’s priorities so clearly established helps the commission explain why we need to tackle them in the final agreement. so allow me to thank you for the work done, to look forward to the debate that we are about to have, and to pledge my full cooperation with parliament as we jointly push for the results that europeans need: a ttip that leads to jobs, growth and investment while protecting our values and our democracies.
the committee on foreign affairs and security has adopted a number of amendments. mr president, the negotiations on the att are taking place at a crucial moment from the point of view of foreign policy. the united states is paying increasing political and military attention to the asia-pacific region, while negotiating the association agreement with eleven countries in the region. atci will rebalance this situation. it will be an anchor in our relations with the united states in the face of its drift towards the pacific. it is therefore of great political importance, beyond its economic and commercial dimension. the challenges we face in our eastern and mediterranean neighbourhood are another reason for strengthening our ties with the united states, our natural ally. moreover, since the european and american economies still occupy an important place in the world, the rules of the atci will have many possibilities to be projected globally, to become world-wide. if we do not do it now, it will be the so-called emerging powers who will soon be making it, according to their values and interests. but atci should not be an end point. in the future, we must conclude a political agreement with the united states, which will strengthen our ties and establish the bilateral frameworks for consultation and concertation that are so necessary in the context of a globalised, multipolar and very complex world.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of giving approval to the council decision granting fishing opportunities in eu waters to fishing vessels flying the flag of venezuela off the coast of french guiana because it establishes a legislative framework appropriate to the fisheries that were already de facto taking place in that area. venezuelan vessels have been allowed to fish off french guiana for decades on the condition that some of the catch is landed in local ports. however, there is no international fisheries agreement between the eu and venezuela. that is why this new framework is necessary, which obliges venezuela to respect the compensations associated with this proposal and to respect european regulations in relation to, for example, the fish stocks that can be fished, the type of fishing gear, vessel tracking devices, reporting of catches, maximum number of authorized fishing vessels and proportion of catches landed in french guiana ports.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal to grant fishing opportunities in eu waters to fishing vessels flying the flag of venezuela in the exclusive economic zone off french guiana because the processing industry in this zone depends in part on the continuity of the fishing vessels and, although cooperation with venezuela does not conform to the legal framework of the union, the vessels have authority and activity. the legal solution to the declarations of commitment to the principles of the cfp therefore seems appropriate.
in writing. ‒ venezuelan fishing vessels have been operating in eu waters off the coast of french guiana for decades. in practice, fishing was authorised but without an international fisheries agreement within the meaning of council regulation (ec) no 1006/2008. in this case, the council opted for a unilateral declaration, with binding legal effects under international law, which it specified in council decision 2012/19/eu of 16 december 2011 approving, on behalf of the european union, the declaration on the granting of fishing opportunities in eu waters to fishing vessels flying the flag of the bolivarian republic of venezuela in the exclusive economic zone off the coast of french guiana. however, in the absence of co-decision, the commission and parliament denounced this declaration before the court of justice of the eu, which would annul it, but would maintain it until the entry into force of a new decision, which is the one now being considered and which i voted in favour of.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of giving approval to the council decision granting fishing opportunities in eu waters to fishing vessels flying the flag of venezuela off the coast of french guiana because it establishes a legislative framework appropriate to the fisheries that were already de facto taking place in that area. venezuelan vessels have been allowed to fish off french guiana for decades on the condition that some of the catch is landed in local ports. however, there is no international fisheries agreement between the eu and venezuela. that is why this new framework is necessary, which obliges venezuela to respect the compensations associated with this proposal and to respect european regulations in relation to, for example, the fish stocks that can be fished, the type of fishing gear, vessel tracking devices, reporting of catches, maximum number of authorized fishing vessels and proportion of catches landed in french guiana ports.
in writing. ‒ i voted for this text which confirms an old practice between venezuelan fishermen and french canneries in french guiana. this is to allow venezuelan fishing vessels access to french guiana waters, 12 miles off the coast. in return, fish processing is carried out in french guiana (representing 75% of the fish caught by venezuelan vessels) and french vessels from martinique have the possibility of fishing for hake or tuna off venezuela. guyana has a significant fishery potential, with various species of shrimp and 200 species of fish. it is regrettable that this potential is currently under-exploited, but the compensation provided by venezuela is sufficient to justify the fisheries agreement concluded with that country, especially since this agreement also limits illegal fishing in our maritime space.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this recommendation, which calls for authorization to fish for venezuelan vessels in the same way as it has been done so far: in compliance with the compensatory measures and european legislation in this field (species, fishing gear, vessel tracking devices, notifications, number of vessels, volume of fish and proportion of catch to be landed in french guiana). the processing industry based in french guiana is partly dependent on the exploitation of the natural resources of the exclusive economic zone (eez) by venezuelan fishing vessels. given the socioeconomic importance of this activity in the region, these vessels have been allowed to fish for decades, with part of the catch being landed in local ports. the landing and processing of fishery products therefore represent an important source of resources and employment for french guiana.

in writing. ‒ this draft amending budget no 3/2015 (dar no 3/2015) concerns the budgeting of the surplus of the previous financial year in accordance with the provisions of the financial regulation. the implementation of the 2014 budget year shows a surplus of eur 1 435 million. this surplus will correspondingly reduce the member states' contribution to the financing of the eu budget for 2015. in this context, it was important to support this ppr no 3/2015 as it introduces a general critique of the council's attitude of not fulfilling its commitments to countries in need by mobilizing additional resources but taking money from existing programmes. the commission has therefore linked ppr no 3/2105 and ppr no 4/2015 on the mobilisation of the european solidarity fund for romania, bulgaria and italy. we have thus ensured that both reports are subject to a common timetable for adoption and are closely linked from a political point of view.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this budgetary correction consisting of transfers between surpluses existing in certain budget headings of one year which can be reallocated to the next year, as a means of not losing that money (since if it is not reallocated, the budget of the next year is reduced by the same amount).
in writing. ‒ this report takes account of the eu budget surplus in the 2014 financial year and enters it into the 2015 budget, reducing the contributions of member states' gross national income to the union budget by eur 1 435 million. the budgetary correction is an eminently technical matter which, however, has acquired a political dimension in view of the criticism we socialists have made of the council's frequent attitude of not fulfilling its commitments to countries in need by mobilising additional resources, taking the money from existing programmes. in order to avoid this, this report has been linked to the report on draft amending budget no 4/2015 by linking the deadlines of both and calling for the new budgetary needs of the eusf in 2015 to be covered by contributions from the surplus of the previous year.

in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund aims to enable the union to respond quickly, effectively and flexibly to emergency situations and to show its solidarity with the population of regions affected by disasters up to a maximum annual amount of eur 500 million. the adoption of this report represents parliament's decision to mobilise the european union solidarity fund for the first time this year, due to the floods in romania, bulgaria and italy, and specifically concerns the mobilisation of the eu solidarity fund (eusf) for an amount of eur 66 505 850 in commitment and payment appropriations in relation to two floods in romania in spring and summer 2014, the floods in bulgaria in july and august 2014 and the floods in italy in october and november 2014.

in writing. ‒ in 2002, following the severe floods in central europe, the eu decided to create the solidarity fund to respond to major natural disasters, the basis of which was laid down in regulation (ec) no 2012/2002. the priority for the mobilisation of the solidarity fund shall be to minimise the immediate and direct impact of natural disasters. the reform of the regulation establishing the fund, with the aim of ensuring a rapid and efficient mobilisation, entered into force on 28 june 2014, ensuring a more effective and timely mobilisation of funds and simplifying the criteria for applying for aid. achieving the objectives of speed and efficiency is crucial to minimize the impact of natural disasters. the speed with which these funds can be made available to cover part of the rescue effort and to start the reconstruction and recovery of strategic infrastructure and services will be a major factor in the economic and social recovery of regions affected by natural disasters.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report as it proposes to mobilise the european union solidarity fund in relation to the floods in romania (spring and summer 2014), bulgaria (summer 2014) and italy (autumn 2014) on the basis of paragraph 11 of the interinstitutional agreement of 2 december 2013. this is the first mobilisation decision in 2015 and the total amount of the proposed aid, eur 66,5 million, complies with the provisions on the ceiling of the eu solidarity fund, as set out in the mff regulation, of eur 541,2 million (i.e. eur 500 million in 2011 prices). in parallel to this proposal to mobilise the eu solidarity fund, the commission has presented a draft amending budget (oj no 4/2015, of 15 april 2015) with a view to entering the corresponding commitment and payment appropriations in the 2015 budget, as provided for in paragraph 11 of the interinstitutional agreement.

in writing. ‒ the aspiration of all europeans is to have a european metro where all modes of transport are interconnected. creating a truly single transport space is a challenge and a challenge that is full of opportunities for smes, innovation and quality job creation. it is the only guarantee of sustainable, efficient and cost-effective european transport. an essential element in this system to which we aspire is the single ticket which allows and encourages the mobility of all citizens in a multimodal way. to achieve this objective, it will be necessary to have local and regional administrations and, in this sense, the basque country has embarked on this path with a pilot project that will allow moving across the territory in a multimodal way with a single ticket.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which aims to promote the creation of integrated tickets for different modes of transnational transport and to put an end to the added difficulties users encounter when trying to book such a journey. the report also calls on the commission to draw up a charter of rights for passengers on all modes of transport by the end of 2017, including a section on multimodal travel with clear and transparent protection of passenger rights in the multimodal context taking into account the specificities of each mode of transport and integrated multimodal ticketing. in view of the demographic change facing europe, it stresses the need to ensure accessibility to transport, in particular for vulnerable people, calling for much greater consideration to be given to the needs of people with disabilities or reduced mobility, as well as the special needs of the elderly.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this legislative initiative because it proposes to promote the development of information, planning and ticketing services for journeys throughout the union that respond to the challenges of energy efficiency, environmental sustainability and economic viability. the aim is to provide comprehensive information on travel offers by public and private companies related to air, rail, sea or road traffic and thus to facilitate seamless, multimodal and cross-border door-to-door mobility for travellers. on the basis of comprehensive information, travellers should be able to search for the most sustainable, fastest or cheapest alternative transport that best suits their individual requirements, book and pay for it online, and start their journey with a single ticket, no matter how many different modes of transport are used during the journey.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the extension of the special committee on tax resolutions as it deals with a crucial problem for the european union, which is the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion, as well as unfair tax competition within the internal market. this committee needs more time to complete its work so that a full report incorporating an ambitious package of recommendations can be produced. the luxleaks revelations have highlighted the fact that certain member states are eroding the tax bases of others through confidential tax rulings with private individuals (known as 'tax rulings'). the european commission has proposed an automatic and compulsory system for the exchange of information between member states, which we european socialists strongly support, and the revival of the initiative for the harmonization of the corporate tax base. taxation should not be a closed area where some states commit all kinds of abuses and bad practices, under the pretext of being part of sovereign powers. the union is a community of law in which the member states must act in accordance with the principle of loyalty and cooperation.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this extension because of the fundamental importance of this committee of the european parliament in clarifying the agreements reached with the european multinationals in the luxleaks case. this special committee was set up in response to the leak of the aforementioned information, which directly targeted european multinationals and governments that signed anti-competition agreements. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this extension.

in writing. ‒ it was important to support this draft amending budget no 1 for 2015 (ppr no 1/2015) as it is linked to the agreement on the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) which was approved last week by this same assembly. the purpose of the new regulation is to technically integrate the agreement on the efsi into the eu budget for 2015 in order to provide the efsi guarantee fund with the necessary eur 1 360 million for 2015. the content of ppr no 1/2015 fully translates the agreement on the efsi reached by parliament and the council.
in writing. ‒ the juncker plan is a necessary proposal to boost investment in strategic sectors such as digital, research and energy. the commission and council wanted to finance the plan with money already budgeted for such important programmes as the connecting europe facility or horizon 2020, but parliament argued for the need to find additional funds and succeeded in reducing cuts in these programmes by €1 billion. we therefore vote today in favour of a budgetary adjustment which we would have preferred differently but which we accept as the lowest common denominator between the three institutions and which allows the launch of the european fund for strategic investments, which should serve to stimulate the eu's competitiveness and contribute to the union's strategy for smart, sustainable and inclusive growth.
in writing. ‒ i abstained from this vote because, despite our disagreement with the juncker plan and despite the fact that we have already opposed the efsi itself on previous occasions, we believe that this rectifying does not alter the nature of the fund, neither to improve it nor to make it worse.
in writing. ‒ we socialists have fought during the last legislatures to turn the tide of european economic policy 180 degrees, against austerity and in favour of investment as a way of boosting the economy and returning to growth without undermining the european social model. now we are glad that this work is bearing fruit and the outlook is beginning to change with a commission that is finally taking the european parliament's demands into account and is committed to including investment as one of the pillars of its economic strategy. the report technically integrates the agreement on the efsi reached with the council into the eu budget for 2015, providing the efsi guarantee fund with the necessary eur 1 360 million for 2015. the efsi is the first of the major initiatives in this legislature along this new line. it aims, through public funding that supports projects in line with union standards, to attract private capital and revitalise the eu economy, leading to smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, as well as the creation of quality jobs and the enhancement of economic, social and territorial cohesion. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it involves approving cuts in key research and infrastructure programmes to allow the european fund for strategic investments to be developed. this appropriation is intended to cover the financing of the purchase, hire, maintenance and repair of equipment and installations, as well as the purchase, hire and maintenance of equipment and installations for the construction, maintenance, repair and overhaul of buildings, installations and equipment for the construction of buildings, and the purchase of equipment and installations for the construction of buildings. in order to boost this juncker plan, the commission has decided to cut significant public programmes such as the connecting europe facility. my opposition to this plan which will support european speculators rather than the real economy and the european industrial structure has been frontal, and that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ on 26 november 2014, the commission proposed an investment plan for europe with the aim of mobilising at least €315 billion over the next three years. to this end, the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) established an agreement between the commission and the european investment bank. such initiatives support the mobilisation of both public and private capital and at the same time help to remove cross-border barriers in energy, environment or transport infrastructure issues. that is why, and because this type of project shows the strong correlation between european funds and the efsi, i am voting in favour, since investments in research and transport are also key to strengthening and securing the objectives set within the union's budgets, and thus encouraging the growth expected under the europe 2020 strategy.
in writing. ‒ the european fund for strategic investments is of great importance in enabling projects to be carried out that contribute to sustainable growth and job creation in the eu. i support the proposal to increase the budget allocated to this fund and i am confident that the commitment to implement it as quickly and effectively as possible will be fulfilled, thus helping to achieve the objectives that europe has set itself for the coming years.

in writing. ‒ the european institutions have decided that the only way to solve the tragedies we have seen in recent months in the mediterranean is to move forward with the 'fortress europe' model that has brought us here. i reject this amendment which is only intended to provide more resources for frontex and europol for their border control work, which do not have rescue among their missions and yet prevent the entry of human beings within our borders. i therefore believe that if there really was political will to solve the problem, it would be invested in non-police and non-militarised rescue missions and then in cooperation policies to help the economic emancipation of the countries of the south. however, in line with the plans of high representative mogherini, it has been decided to spend money on the militarization of the mediterranean, something i cannot agree with.
in writing. ‒ i have given my support to this report on draft amending budget no 5/2015, which aims to strengthen the eu's resources to manage the increasingly large flows of migration and refugees. the report welcomes the intention of all the institutions to increase the budgetary appropriations relating to migration and asylum in view of the indisputable and urgent needs and recalls that parliament had already requested a considerable increase in the appropriations under these budget lines and additional staff for the agencies concerned. it regrets, however, the limited nature of the proposed increases in draft amending budget no 5/2015, which do not correspond to the real needs in view of the existing crisis in the mediterranean 'which is likely to worsen', the growing risk of an increase in refugees from ukraine and the need to address the challenges posed by migration in general.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it involves an increase in the financial resources devoted to the european agency frontex which is in practice militarizing the mediterranean. this amending budget represents an increase of eur 75 million for this agency and for europol, increasing the logic of criminalising migrants and the military reaction instead of addressing the necessary respect for the human rights of these people. frontex has been accused of not having mechanisms to monitor the respect of human rights in its internal workings and that is why it is an organisation whose development we cannot support. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ draft amending budget no 5/2015 (ppr 5/2015) aims to strengthen the eu's resources to manage the increasingly high levels of migration and refugee flows. the increase in commitments totalled eur 75 million, while the increase in payment appropriations amounted to eur 69.6 million. the increase in payment appropriations will be financed through the reallocation of the galileo programme, leaving the overall level of payment appropriations in the 2015 budget unchanged. the following aspects are strengthened:• asylum, migration and integration fund (amif) • internal security fund (isf). • agencies: frontex, easo and europolpr 5/2015 represents a first step in responding to the new challenges posed by the real needs arising from the current crisis in the mediterranean and the increase in migratory challenges. for all these reasons it was important to support it.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on this amending budget proposal because i consider that the current european border policy is currently guided by an absolutely security concept and contrary to the humanitarian budgets which should guide the eu (operations triton in italy and poseidon in greece). but voting against would mean cutting funds that are partly intended to save lives. my position is that there must be a fundamental change in european policies on migration, trade and development, without which everything that is being implemented and approved at european level will lack sustainability and coherence.
in writing. ‒ the tragedy of millions of people living in regions bordering our continent today because of war, poverty, hunger or lack of freedom means that an increasing number of those affected are putting their lives at risk every day in their attempt to reach europe or seek a future within the union, trying to participate and join our way of life and social model. europe cannot turn its back on these people and, in the present situation with increasing migratory pressure, must be able to articulate a collective, solidarity-based, fair and effective response. i voted in favour of this report because it represents a first step in that direction, 'mainly in connection with the current crisis in the mediterranean', but also knowing that much more needs to be done; that is the commitment of the european socialists. the draft amending budget should be the first sign of the eu's increased resources to deal with the increasing flows of migrants and refugees. the total increase in commitment appropriations is eur 75 million and the increase in payment appropriations is eur 69.6 million.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it encourages the expansion of large-scale dairy industry and large-scale intensive farming, at the expense of the destruction of small and medium-sized farms and of a sustainable extensive production mode. the report also focuses on an export-based economy and market expansion through the conquest of new markets, which i believe is not only unrealistic but can lead to serious problems both for eu dairy farms, already in a very serious crisis due to the disappearance of dairy quotas, and for third countries.
in writing. ‒ the report to evaluate the 'milk package' is of particular importance for the sector as it coincides with the end of milk quotas. the package contains a number of measures to better regulate the sector, promoting an improvement in the bargaining power of producers and strengthening their bargaining position. the global dairy market is increasingly volatile and reached its highest ever prices in january 2014, following which there were considerable price falls for the remainder of 2014. in order to ensure a fair and balanced free market, certain of its defects and imperfections must be corrected, and this is more evident than ever in the case before us. it is true that the different degree of development and size of livestock holdings in the different countries gives a different reading of the situation, but in the vast majority of countries the problems of imbalances persist and need to be addressed. given the specific problems of this sector, a number of measures and mechanisms are justified to ensure transparency and the development of a genuine free market, and the report contributes to this.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this proposal because it calls on the commission to deal with the crisis in the national milk market for a number of reasons, including the russian embargo. i therefore believe that the council should also consider the re-establishment of aid to producers who are going out of business and the maintenance of the previous decisions on milk quotas. we therefore need regulatory instruments to prevent and manage crises in the dairy sector.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution which points out the particularly difficult situation facing dairy farms, with high price volatility and recurrent crises hampering investment in farms, as well as the serious problems of the functioning of the single milk market. the resolution also expresses disappointment at the measures implemented after the adoption of the 'milk package', with a low level of implementation of the compulsory contracts and the fact that in some member states they contain abusive clauses that neutralize the initial objective of stability of deliveries, as is happening in spain and, in particular, in galicia. it is therefore necessary to strengthen the role of producer organisations in order to preserve their bargaining power and influence in the supply chain and to strengthen the milk market observatory.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it represents a boost to the investment model promoted by international capital to guarantee its investments at the expense of the public purse. public-private partnerships aim to attract private investors by protecting their resources from any risk of losing funds. the report advocates this model of speculative investment as a form of economic and commercial intervention in third countries. this investment model is directly opposed to a genuine development project in third countries which would improve the quality of life of the working classes; on the contrary, it is only intended to guarantee the big capitalists. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which highlights the need for a strong and clear regulatory framework, which prevents any kind of conflict of interest in eu companies' access to public-private partnerships (ppps) abroad. as the report shows, the risk transfer model needs to be very carefully designed to ensure that the private partner does not gain without taking on responsibilities. moreover, a ppp should not be the first step towards privatisation of a service. it is essential to ensure that administrations retain the right to decide on the management model of services of general interest at any time in the interest of the public. finally, the eu should commit itself to supporting the financial and technical capacity of the administrations responsible for ppps in partner countries where required, to ensure the sound design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of projects, applying the principles of good governance, transparency, involvement of civil society actors, and the fight against corruption and fraud.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it represents a boost to the investment model promoted by international capital to guarantee its investments at the expense of the public purse. public-private partnerships aim to attract private investors by protecting their resources from any risk of losing funds. the report advocates this model of speculative investment as a form of economic and commercial intervention in third countries. this investment model is directly opposed to a genuine development project in third countries which would improve the quality of life of the working classes; on the contrary, it is only intended to guarantee the big capitalists. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, which in particular promotes public-private partnerships, which are presented as beneficial for the european economy. in fact, i myself saw the futility of these public-private partnerships when i was regional councillor for nord-pas-de-calais, with, for example, the grand stade de lille, which eiffage was commissioned to build. this project has put the city of lille in a lot of debt and will probably never be paid off. public-private partnerships have proved so disastrous financially for the public authorities that the original financing plan for the seine-nord canal was abandoned in order to limit the cost of the project! the question of the development of such partnerships in third countries is therefore a matter of concern, particularly for emerging countries which could soon be victims of the same exploitation as our own public authorities. in addition, the access of foreign companies to our own markets, in the framework of these partnerships, is also questionable. companies from 'protectionist' countries will be able to win our own public contracts, which are easily accessible, without necessarily being reciprocal: no one will be surprised, of course, that such distortions of competition are tolerated by the europeans, who are not far from a contradiction.
in writing. ‒ i voted against because i reject the public-private partnership (ppp) strategy as a mechanism designed and used primarily as an instrument for market access, deregulation and liberalisation of public services and public procurement in third countries, especially developing countries, and as a means of diverting development funds to private enterprises. furthermore, we consider that there is a link between ppas and the risk of debt unsustainability; ppas are often a way of transferring risk from private companies to taxpayers.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which stresses the importance of public-private partnerships and calls on the eu institutions to take the necessary measures to promote the participation of eu companies, in particular smes, in ppp projects, which would bring considerable benefits in terms of job creation, productivity, competitiveness and technology and innovation that would translate into benefits and economic growth throughout the eu and in host countries.
in writing. ‒ the report makes numerous references to the need for a strong and clear regulatory framework that prevents any kind of conflict of interest, as well as the need to design the risk transfer model very carefully, to ensure that the private partner will not gain benefits without assuming responsibilities. reference is also made to the importance of ensuring that administrations retain the right to decide on the management model of services of general interest, at any time, in the interest of the citizenry. finally, reference is made to the need to create 'decent work' and to the need to mainstream gender in eu policies. i agree with these considerations and have voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ public-private partnerships (ppps) enable interaction between the two sectors, which also means that they are part of the structure that allows for economic growth, innovation and competitiveness. since the 2007 crisis, which affected all countries, funds for projects of all types require a high capital, which would be much more supported if the synergies between these two sectors are favourable. i voted in favour of the measures taken and the european parliament's motion for a resolution because, in addition to the reasons mentioned above, the european union has also considered the creation of rules which support fair competition within the single market, making it possible for international investors to negotiate on a level playing field.
in writing. ‒ public-private partnerships have proven to be highly effective in many sectors, so an extension of such initiatives could be very beneficial for europe in terms of achieving higher economic growth and more jobs. that is why i support this report, in which the european parliament calls for measures to promote greater participation by companies, including smes, in these partnerships, and the establishment of instruments to enable eu companies to participate in public-private partnerships outside the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which highlights the need for a strong and clear regulatory framework, which prevents any kind of conflict of interest in eu companies' access to public-private partnerships (ppps) abroad. as the report shows, the risk transfer model needs to be very carefully designed to ensure that the private partner does not gain without taking on responsibilities. moreover, a ppp should not be the first step towards privatisation of a service. it is essential to ensure that administrations retain the right to decide on the management model of services of general interest at any time in the interest of the public. finally, the eu should commit itself to supporting the financial and technical capacity of the administrations responsible for ppps in partner countries where required, to ensure the sound design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of projects, applying the principles of good governance, transparency, involvement of civil society actors, and the fight against corruption and fraud.

in writing. ‒ european farmers and livestock farmers work to obtain high quality products but nevertheless sometimes suffer the consequences of circumstances affecting the sector, such as the russian veto, which modify product prices and their stocks in ways that make them particularly vulnerable. they therefore need to have the right tools to react and grow the sector. we must therefore help them to seek new opportunities through internationalisation processes in order to guarantee them a fair income and create a profitable sector. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the commission published last year a report on the implementation of the reform of the fruit and vegetables regime agreed in 2007, which contains some valid analyses such as the persisting diversity between member states, the degree of organisation of the sector and the low bargaining power of producers in the value chain. in view of commissioner hogan's commitment to simplify the fruit and vegetable regime during his term of office, i have voted in favour of this motion for a resolution as parliament's first position on the next reform. the reform should confirm the validity of the basic organisational structure of this sector around producer organisations, its market orientation and the improvement of the quality and environmental aspects of production, achieved through the operational programmes. in addition, european legislation on the recognition of producer organisations, the audit of operational programmes and the measures taken in each member state will need to be simplified; crisis management instruments that have proved ineffective in major cases such as the russian veto will need to be improved; the creation of producer organisations will need to be encouraged; and unfair practices in the value chain will need to be tackled, among other issues.
