in writing. ‒ this report constitutes parliament's first formal response to the draft budget for the financial year 2016 presented by the commission on 27 may 2015. it will serve as a mandate for parliament's delegation in the tripartite negotiations with the council and the commission scheduled for 14 july and prior to the reading in the council of the draft budget. the report includes many positive elements: the effect of the inclusion of the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) in the 2016 draft budget in horizon 2020 and the connecting europe facility will be minimised; funding for the youth employment initiative is secured and increased from the 2016 budget as a key tool to fight youth unemployment in the european union; the reinforcement of external aid programmes, in particular assistance to palestine and unrwa and humanitarian aid, has also been achieved. i agree with these considerations and have therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report for several reasons, including the fact that it represents a new ratification of the previous agreement on the multiannual financial framework. we insist that in order to cope with the current economic crisis we need a boost to the economy from the public sector, and ratifying the cuts in the european budget means endorsing the logic of austerity that is sinking the european economy. the report also welcomes highly controversial headings that will be used against human rights both in europe and abroad, such as those on 'security and citizenship' and a 'global europe'. the need to change the logic of austerity is what has led me to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which is parliament's first response to the draft budget for 2016 and which provides for parliament's mandate to negotiate with the commission and the council a draft budget amounting to eur 153 500 million in commitment appropriations (+2.4%) and eur 143 500 million in payment appropriations (+1.6%). with this mandate, parliament expresses its position in favour of minimising the impact on horizon 2020 and the connecting europe facility of the inclusion of the european fund for strategic investments in the draft budget, securing and increasing funding for the youth employment initiative, as well as increasing funding to address the migration challenges.
in writing. ‒ we abstain in this vote and reaffirm our general criticism of this draft budget. the draft presented by mr fernandes has improved on the unacceptable proposals of the council and the commission and has sought to bring the positions of the groups closer together. our group has tabled a number of amendments which have been introduced and which, in our view, at least partially improve the document: mainly the need to increase funding for cohesion policies and thereby contribute to reducing inequalities between states, regions and localities, and the need to support with special emphasis those countries which are experiencing social, economic and financial difficulties. however, we believe that the budget is clearly too rigid and insufficient, and that it is not up to the challenges that the crisis of the economic model applied by the political currents that have hitherto dominated the economy has left us, and that the policies of austerity, financial and trade deregulation and cuts have only aggravated.

in writing. ‒ my abstention from voting is justified because the budget is not the tool the eu needs to get out of the crisis and, moreover, sensitive items such as erasmus or asylum policy are being maintained and increased.
in writing. ‒ the report assesses the commission's draft budget for 2016 in the light of the guidelines adopted by the european parliament in march 2014 and makes some key recommendations. i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report for several reasons, including the fact that it represents a new ratification of the previous agreement on the multiannual financial framework. we insist that in order to cope with the current economic crisis we need a boost to the economy from the public sector, and ratifying the cuts in the european budget means endorsing the logic of austerity that is sinking the european economy. the report also welcomes highly controversial headings that will be used against human rights both in europe and abroad, such as those on 'security and citizenship' and a 'global europe'. the need to change the logic of austerity is what has led me to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of this report because 'green jobs', while not the only solution needed for economic recovery in europe, have the potential to create jobs that are essential for the transition of our economies towards more sustainable models. this economic sector, despite the risks of its indefiniteness, is an umbrella for a great many activities necessary for an environmentally sustainable economic recovery. the report also calls for the development of quality jobs in the sector, so that it becomes a strategic axis of economic development on the continent.
in writing. ‒ the commission's green jobs initiative was published in july 2014, together with the green action plan for smes and the communication on the circular economy. this initiative underlined the challenges and opportunities for employment in the current transition to environmentally friendly, low-carbon energy sources and a resource-efficient economy. this own-initiative report, on which i voted in favour, is parliament's first position supporting the commission's approach to the transition to sustainable societies and economies. this transition, with equally sustainable consumption and production patterns, can generate opportunities for quality job creation and transform existing employment into green jobs in virtually all sectors and along the entire value chain. to make the most of these opportunities, it is necessary, among other things, to establish an integrated framework of labour policies and of promoting competence and skills among workers so that they play an active role. finally, i welcome the fact that the report recognises the need to introduce environmental and social criteria into public procurement policies.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of this report because 'green jobs', while not the only solution needed for economic recovery in europe, have the potential to create jobs that are essential for the transition of our economies towards more sustainable models. this economic sector, despite the risks of its indefiniteness, is an umbrella for a great many activities necessary for an environmentally sustainable economic recovery. the report also calls for the development of quality jobs in the sector, so that it becomes a strategic axis of economic development on the continent.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour, convinced that the green economy is a sector with a strong potential for job creation and that it should be harnessed and promoted at european level. our decision is based on three ideas in the report: 1) guarantees for a just transition and that this principle should serve as a basis for negotiation at the paris climate conference cop 21; 2) the ultimate goal of promoting the creation of quality and sustainable jobs, integrating displaced and low-skilled workers into the strategy; 3) the transition must not have a negative impact on social security systems or on low-income people. i would like to list some of the positive proposals contained in the initiative: the creation of new job opportunities in the green economy; the promotion of the acquisition of vocational skills, specific to green employment, oriented, free of charge and accessible to unskilled workers; public investment to create sustainable employment; the role of social partners (trade union representatives green) and the participation of workers; environmental and social clauses in public procurement; the reduction of insecurity resulting from the displacement of workers; and support for smes in this green transition.

in writing. ‒ the initiative in question is a successful convergence of the employment and environment agendas. while it is true that this objective presents a number of difficulties, i think that adapting to a green economy is practically an imperative if we are to reinvent ourselves and prosper. i think we need to concentrate on the strategic development of the environmental tax for businesses, provided that this does not impose an excessive burden that hinders the growth of smes. voting in favour of this proposal is voting in favour of the horizon 2020 programme, and as such i support the initiative.

in writing. ‒ we voted for more national and international responsibility in the fight against tax evasion and tax fraud, as well as against corruption, which in developing countries means a trillion dollars less annually for the fight against poverty. the eu must lead by example, by fighting tax havens and corruption and by imposing sanctions on companies that make non-transparent contracts in third countries, as well as by giving priority to financial and technical assistance for the establishment of national and local tax administrations in developing countries. our support for the mobilisation of national resources in the countries most in need is key to overcoming their dependence on external aid and reducing their levels of poverty and inequality.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i regarded as positive the call for a concrete action plan to combat tax evasion and avoidance in the impoverished countries, which would help their governments to redistribute and control resources better. tax havens, banking secrecy and the designation of 'tax-free zones' to supposedly attract foreign capital and investment are detrimental to the achievement of sustainable, inclusive development based on social justice and respect for the sovereignty of peoples, which requires fair progressive tax systems to address inequality. although there are areas where improvements can be made and the approach is not as ambitious as it should be, it is positive that a call is made for the launch of assessments of the impact of european fiscal policies on the impoverished countries, pointing out the need to monitor, on an annual basis and country by country, the activities of multinationals and their possible direct or indirect contribution to tax evasion and capital flight.

in writing. ‒ we vote in favour of the report, which calls for an effective action plan to combat tax evasion and, in particular, tax avoidance in developing countries: a plan that will facilitate a better mobilisation of national resources for equitable and sustainable development. the report also calls on the eu and its member states to ensure that, in the negotiation of tax and investment agreements with developing countries, income or profits from cross-border activities are taxed in the country of origin where the value is extracted or created, and urges the eu and the member states to go beyond the oecd framework and ensure the creation of a genuine intergovernmental body for taxation issues within the united nations.

in writing. ‒ the report underlines the importance of improving the mobilisation of national resources to tackle the problems faced by developing countries in the fight against tax evasion and avoidance. it proposes a list of recommendations for the addis ababa conference on financing for development aimed at reforming the global tax system. the commission is asked to come up with a communication to help developing countries establish fair, balanced, efficient and transparent tax systems by strengthening financial and technical assistance to these countries; to adopt effective solutions to improve transparency and cooperation in the fight against tax evasion, such as an automatic country-by-country information exchange mechanism, taking into account the needs and constraints of each country; to assess the impact of eu tax policies on developing countries; and to create a truly intergovernmental body for taxation issues, in which developing countries can participate on an equal footing in the overall reform of existing international tax rules. i agree with these considerations and have therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ in a globalised context such as we live in, we must develop convergence programmes between the different regions of the world to fight together against illicit tax flows. we need more transparency and more efficiency in both national and international tax systems in the fight against tax evasion and avoidance. the proposals in the report offer alternatives to reshape our institutions as agents of change. among other things, it suggests an incentive system, publishing a list of companies whose managers are genuinely committed to eradicating tax fraud in an open database. in addition, this resolution would force us to reach a final agreement on the universal definition of what constitutes a tax haven and would set global sanctions in cooperation with the united nations for those who violate the established rules. i support this project as an alternative to an outdated model that urgently needed to be changed.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report. the third international conference on financing for development will be held in addis ababa (ethiopia) from 13 to 16 july 2015. it should constitute an important contribution to and support the implementation of the sustainable development goals (sdgs). considering that revenue mobilization of domestic resources in developing countries represents another key issue at stake to implement sdgs, this specific and complementary report fixes the ep position on the addis ababa conference.
in writing. ‒ this report forms part of the position to be taken by the european parliament at the third international conference on financing for development to be held in addis ababa in july 2015. we are talking about a report which contains important recommendations for the european commission and the member states in view of this conference and which has had unanimous support in the committee on development, so i think it is necessary to vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of this report because it represents a major step forward in the consideration and treatment of waste as a resource for the european economy. this proposal is fundamental to the reshaping of the european economy, it seeks to promote an activity based on greater economic sustainability, and it even calls for sanctions in cases of planned obsolescence. the debate on waste generation and waste management is necessary to put an end to the environmental madness that has been the result of the capitalist industrial development of european countries. since the report puts this issue on the table in such a forceful and comprehensive way, i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the commission presented in july 2014 its communication 'towards a circular economy: a zero waste agenda for europe', which contained ideas to contribute, through existing legislation and new initiatives, to creating a circular economy by optimising all processes in the life of a product and minimising waste. this own-initiative report, which i voted in favour of, sets out parliament's first position on the priorities to be set for moving towards this circular economy, namely the need to set mandatory targets for the reduction of different types of waste by 2025, a specific target for organic waste by 2020, the gradual reduction of waste dumping, the adoption of the cascading principle for biomass in particular, the increase of recycling and reuse targets to at least 70% for urs and 80% for packaging by 2030, the strict limitation of incineration by 2020, an indicative target of 50% reduction of marine litter by 2025, a binding target of 30% resource efficiency by 2025 and the strengthening of ecodesign measures for all types of products.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of this report because it represents a major step forward in the consideration and treatment of waste as a resource for the european economy. this proposal is fundamental to the reshaping of the european economy, it seeks to promote an activity based on greater economic sustainability, and it even calls for sanctions in cases of planned obsolescence. the debate on waste generation and waste management is necessary to put an end to the environmental madness that has been the result of the capitalist industrial development of european countries. since the report puts this issue on the table in such a forceful and comprehensive way, i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the unsustainable use of resources is causing environmental damage and also poses an economic risk, both for the eu and for the rest of the world, as the world economy uses the equivalent of a planet and a half in terms of resources to generate global output and absorb waste. there is no doubt that if we continue along this path we will end up in an ecological and economic dead end, so we must use fewer resources and use them more efficiently. resource efficiency is a solution to the ecological dilemma we face and to the economic challenges europe is grappling with. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report on the supposedly efficient use of resources, calling for a move towards a 'circular economy'. as always, the principles and intentions behind the commission's proposals and the envi report are commendable: to re-examine our modes of consumption and production which have led us to this globalisation which is destroying our jobs and our environment. however, the paths being considered do not even claim to tackle the real cause: the uprooting of our economy and industries, their relocation to less social and environmental concerns. the circular economy is therefore a cautery on a wooden leg. as usual, the european union is using high principles to impose constraints on our territory, without compensating for these by protecting our markets. it thus puts our economy in a global competitive position. the jobs announced for the recycling of products which we will therefore continue to import are far from compensating for those destroyed by relocations and, worse, they make us even more dependent on these imports. for more responsible consumption and production, let's produce and buy locally and sustainably, let's give ourselves the means to re-industrialize.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour as we consider it necessary to extend the scope of the ecodesign directive, update the waste rules and give visibility to certain areas such as the construction of sustainable buildings. we are facing a paradigm shift and it is necessary to set binding waste reduction targets and to gradually reduce all types of waste disposal. to tackle the problem of resource scarcity, we believe it is necessary to reduce resource extraction and use and to break the direct link between growth and use of natural resources. parliament called on the commission to promote a life-cycle approach to products and to present an 'ambitious work plan' in this area. this should include the review of the ecodesign legislation by the end of 2016 to extend its scope to cover all product categories. it also called on the commission to set out requirements for the durability criteria of products and for their repair, reuse and recycling, and to propose measures to end planned obsolescence. the commission is also invited to propose these targets before the end of 2015.

in writing. ‒ the unsustainable use of resources causes significant environmental damage, while also posing an economic risk. the world economy today uses the equivalent of 1.5 planets, and if we continue at this rate, we will reach a dead end, with large and irreversible implications such as climate change, deforestation, desertification, land degradation or the weakening of ecosystems. this report sets out good criteria for tackling this situation, with a focus on the life cycle of products, eco-design policy and zero waste. despite the amendments made to the text after the plenary, eh bildu very much welcomes the proposals included in the resolution, in particular: the binding nature of the waste reduction targets; the implementation of mandatory separate collection for paper, metal, plastic and glass, together with the introduction of mandatory separate collection for biological waste by 2020; the recycling and reuse target of 70% of municipal solid waste and 80% of packaging; and that by 2020 incineration is strictly limited to non-recyclable and non-biodegradable waste. eh bildu has been committed to these objectives since its foundation, which is why we voted in favour of this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the report includes a number of positive proposals, such as the need to set mandatory targets for the reduction of different types of waste by 2025, a specific target for organic waste by 2020, the gradual reduction of waste dumping, the adoption of the cascading principle for biomass in particular, the increase of recycling and reuse targets to at least 70% for urs and 80% for packaging by 2030, the strict limitation of incineration by 2020, an indicative target of 50% reduction of marine litter by 2025, a binding target of 30% resource efficiency by 2025 and the reinforcement of ecodesign measures in all product types. i agree with this approach and have therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ i have decided to vote in favour of this report because it represents a major step forward in the consideration and treatment of waste as a resource for the european economy. this proposal is fundamental to the reshaping of the european economy, it seeks to promote an activity based on greater economic sustainability, and it even calls for sanctions in cases of planned obsolescence. the debate on waste generation and waste management is necessary to put an end to the environmental madness that has been the result of the capitalist industrial development of european countries. since the report puts this issue on the table in such a forceful and comprehensive way, i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the commission presented in july 2014 its communication 'towards a circular economy: a zero waste agenda for europe', which contained ideas to contribute, through existing legislation and new initiatives, to creating a circular economy by optimising all processes in the life of a product and minimising waste. this own-initiative report, which i voted in favour of, sets out parliament's first position on the priorities to be set for moving towards this circular economy, namely the need to set mandatory targets for the reduction of different types of waste by 2025, a specific target for organic waste by 2020, the gradual reduction of waste dumping, the adoption of the cascading principle for biomass in particular, the increase of recycling and reuse targets to at least 70% for urs and 80% for packaging by 2030, the strict limitation of incineration by 2020, an indicative target of 50% reduction of marine litter by 2025, a binding target of 30% resource efficiency by 2025 and the strengthening of ecodesign measures for all types of products.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of a call for a truly more ambitious proposal on the circular economy from the commission by the end of 2015. to summarise, the report calls for an inclusion of binding targets on waste reduction, increased targets for recycling, separate collection of biowaste, and ending the burning of recyclable and biodegradable waste. and for product policies it calls for binding an absolute reduction in the consumption of resources to sustainable levels and the phasing out of toxic substances.
in writing. ‒ we want an energy model based on renewables and without nuclear, but the report adopted today is about setting safe limits for food in the event of a nuclear accident. parliament has asked for the legal basis to be changed to articles 168 and 114 tfeu, as i think is appropriate. however, for the moment, we are being reduced to the role of mere consultants. we have to be practical. without going into any war of experts, the limits set by euratom may be insufficient, but those of any other body (fao, codex or independent) are not bound to eu legislation and are therefore indicative. i am not against stricter limits, but under the euratom procedure the only way we have to influence the setting and application of those limits is by a regulation on which we can hold the commission to account. european experts will again be deciding on the appropriate boundaries for our continent. the most sensible thing is to revise the euratom limits on the basis of our needs, to make them into law, european legislation, and to be able to intervene in the event of any breach. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of the herranz garcía report on maximum tolerances for radioactive contamination because the proposed levels and guarantees for food safety are clearly insufficient. this has been denounced by many experts, who have nevertheless never been summoned to a meeting by the rapporteur, despite the initiative of my group. i am convinced that legal instruments are needed to prevent accidents like those at chernobyl and fukushima on eu territory, and for this reason the closure of obsolete nuclear power stations such as garoña is urgent. it is also essential to establish, on the basis of strict scientific criteria, controls which will enable us to discard contaminated food from places where there has been a nuclear leak. the advocates of nuclear energy have not been unable to find a minimally reasonable solution to this problem, which is mortgaging the future of our descendants. i therefore call for strict controls on radioactive contamination while nuclear power stations are being decommissioned. since this report neither ensures rigorous controls nor advocates the closure of nuclear power stations, i could not vote in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report on the proposal for a regulation setting maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination of foodstuffs following a nuclear accident. despite greater transparency for the public, the regulation does not go back to the essential point: the maximum permissible limit of radioactive contamination. the proposed limits are therefore still those of 1987! this is all the more scandalous because other countries, such as japan, have more protective limits of 8 to 20 and the union applies these more protective limits to products imported from japan. in the face of this absurdity, i have therefore proposed that each member state should be able to set its own limits and suspend imports of foodstuffs which do not comply with them. i also supported a proposal to drastically reduce the limits. these protective measures were not, however, followed by those elected officials who were more committed to free trade than to the protection of the population, especially the french elected officials who were called republicans and centrists. the french socialist elected representatives have done no better by supporting a final text of which they know the ineffectiveness. as is often the case with public health matters, i could not give the commission a free hand, whose priority is not to protect us.
in writing. ‒ we abstained from the vote because we believe that in order to determine the permissible concentrations of toxic products in the diets of more than 500 million europeans, including millions of children, we must be very rigorous and listen to the best experts in the field. however, in this case many recommendations were either not taken into account or were rejected because the amendments containing them were not adopted. we believe that radioactive materials are carcinogenic and mutagenic substances for which there is no defined safety threshold. we support the amendments which establish maximum safety tolerances, but we cannot support a report which we do not consider to have been sufficiently worked out.

in writing. ‒ the report on ‘maximum permitted levels of radioactive contamination of food and feed following a nuclear accident’ is a report to the effect that, in the case that a nuclear accident happens, the europeans citizens would not be protected. this file will allow europeans to consume food with radioactive contamination levels higher than what is recommended by most of the international agencies and experts. moreover, the report doesn’t take on board many isotopes, and thus the legislation is poor. eh bildu strongly criticises the procedure by which the file was compromised, as the rapporteur clearly stated from the beginning that the maximum permitted shall not be modified, and as the agreed expert meeting never happened. the result of the plenary vote on amendments posed a situation in which important committee amendments 1-3 on the legal basis of the text were carried, but amendment 56 (rcv) on the levels of contamination and isotope types was rejected. facing that situation, towards the final vote eh bildu has abstained. for us it is unacceptable to have a legislation that doesn’t provide safety guarantees for the citizens, and since amendment 56 was not carried, we were unable to vote in favour. nevertheless, as committee amendments 1-3 were accepted which enables improved juridical instruments, we have considered the option of abstention.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this draft resolution on the council regulation laying down maximum tolerances for radioactive contamination of food and feed following a nuclear accident or any radiological emergency. the proposal for a regulation aims to bring the legislation into line with the new eu provisions on food safety. to this end, the same maximum accident tolerances as those laid down in article 31 of the euratom treaty are adopted in the annexes. these levels were confirmed in 2012 by the group of experts established under article 31 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the levels are also incorporated into the european commission's radiation protection 105 publication. the resolution also calls for the legal basis to be replaced by article 168 tfeu, so that the regulation, as well as subsequent revisions of the annexes to the limits, are adopted by codecision.
in writing. ‒ we abstained from the vote because we believe that in order to determine the permissible concentrations of toxic products in the diets of more than 500 million europeans, including millions of children, we must be very rigorous and listen to the best experts in the field. however, in this case many recommendations were either not taken into account or were rejected because the amendments containing them were not adopted. we believe that radioactive materials are carcinogenic and mutagenic substances for which there is no defined safety threshold. we support the amendments which establish maximum safety tolerances, but we cannot support a report which we do not consider to have been sufficiently worked out.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, firstly, because we demand to work towards zero tolerance. secondly, it is important to note that during the debate we learned that when the report was discussed in parliament's committee on the environment, the european commission refused to provide the identity of the experts who make up the euratom expert group. furthermore, a public debate on the limits could not be organised either because these same euratom scientists said they were not 'available' to participate. although some (pp) members said that they had no need to know who the scientists were, we do need to know, because science is not neutral and often the results depend on who pays for them and, moreover, revolving doors are, unfortunately, becoming more and more frequent. this regulation does not provide any guarantees for health after an accident, but is a text that aligns with the interests of the nuclear lobby, and i think that the commission must put our right to health and to food that does not make us sick above the interests of any business.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the so-called capital markets union (cmu) because it is essential to increase financial integration in the union. in particular, non-bank financing opportunities for smes need to be expanded and barriers to access to financial services across borders, including at all levels, need to be removed. a single european capital market will promote investment, economic growth and employment. the european commission's green paper on this subject is not sufficiently comprehensive. there is not a single reference to the single currency, which, by simplifying intra-european financial transactions, has been the traditional engine of integration, nor to the need for public debt of the union to play the role of a risk-free asset in the european economy. we also know that non-bank financing is largely shadow banking. the creation of the cmu must be accompanied by appropriate regulation so that this sector does not act as a trapdoor for bad practice. the socialists will be very vigilant so that the umc does not become an excuse to deregulate and increase systemic risk.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution because it seeks to promote the capital markets union, an instrument which will be used to avoid the regulation of the banking sector and facilitate the speculative plundering of the real economy in the european union. this proposal is not in the interests of industrial enterprises or small and mediumsized enterprises, which are the ones that create jobs, but it responds to the demands of speculative capital, which aspires to have easier access to the real economy and thus be able to generate new financial bubbles and greater speculation in the face of the scarcity of markets on a global scale. the very idea of forcing smes to finance themselves through the issuance of shares means that they are prevented from having normal access to credit and from being able to speculate on their income.
in writing. ‒ the existence in the eu of a well-integrated financial system resulting from a capital markets union can increase the resilience of economic and monetary union (emu) to sudden shocks, as well as being an effective instrument for generating jobs, growth and investment. progress in this area will contribute to the smooth functioning of emu in the short term. however, it remains necessary to define a long-term perspective of the necessary evolution of emu and in which areas further work is needed to develop stronger common governance. it is important to implement a coherent strategy around the triangle of structural reforms, investment and fiscal responsibility and, in this context, to move towards more effective commitments to the introduction of growth-friendly reforms in the euro area. the functioning of the single market must also be improved. i therefore voted in favour of this motion for a resolution on the construction of a capital markets union.

in writing. ‒ it is a fact that investment in the real economy in europe has declined relatively for several decades, despite a large increase in the size of the financial sector, both european and global, over the same period. it is necessary to continue working towards improving the long-term financing of the european economy and improving access to capital markets through new sources of financing geared to the needs of the real economy, as the lack of access to finance for smes is one of the main obstacles to growth in the eu. for these reasons i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ we voted against this resolution. the capital markets union is one of the key initiatives of the new commission and in particular of jonathan hill, commissioner for financial stability, financial services and capital markets union. the idea is that companies are too dependent on bank financing, so capital markets are being stimulated. the resolution of the parliament is the product, once again, of the grand coalition between the s&d and epp groups. the resolution is critical of capital markets and some of the instruments (e.g. securitisation) that have led to financial crises, and fails to identify the root causes of the shortage of bank credit linked to austerity measures. the commission's proposal is to encourage the development of capital markets and the diversification of the financial system, and to praise rather than question the financial legislation already adopted.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on the so-called capital markets union (cmu) because it is essential to increase financial integration in the union. in particular, non-bank financing opportunities for smes need to be expanded and barriers to access to financial services across borders, including at all levels, need to be removed. a single european capital market will promote investment, economic growth and employment. the european commission's green paper on this subject is not sufficiently comprehensive. there is not a single reference to the single currency, which, by simplifying intra-european financial transactions, has been the traditional engine of integration, nor to the need for public debt of the union to play the role of a risk-free asset in the european economy. we also know that non-bank financing is largely shadow banking. the creation of the cmu must be accompanied by appropriate regulation so that this sector does not act as a trapdoor for bad practice. the socialists will be very vigilant so that the umc does not become an excuse to deregulate and increase systemic risk.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution because it seeks to promote the capital markets union, an instrument which will be used to avoid the regulation of the banking sector and facilitate the speculative plundering of the real economy in the european union. this proposal is not in the interests of industrial enterprises or small and mediumsized enterprises, which are the ones that create jobs, but it responds to the demands of speculative capital, which aspires to have easier access to the real economy and thus be able to generate new financial bubbles and greater speculation in the face of the scarcity of markets on a global scale. the very idea of forcing smes to finance themselves through the issuance of shares means that they are prevented from having normal access to credit and from being able to speculate on their income.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution on the european agenda on security as it goes into the cuts in rights and freedoms being carried out by both member state and european authorities. the solution to security problems cannot be found in mass spying on citizens or in targeting entire groups of the population. at a time when espionage scandals and illegal files of social activists have become public, this resolution aims to give a veneer of legality to these policies and to the discrimination of population groups under the pretext of fighting against radicalisation.
in writing. ‒ the european agenda on security aims to set out the key priorities and actions for the period 2015-2020 in the field of eu internal security, replacing the current eu internal security strategy 2010-2015. the three main priorities are the fight against terrorism and radicalisation, the fight against organised crime and the fight against cybercrime. this agenda lays the foundations for cooperation and joint actions to be undertaken by the european institutions and agencies, member states and civil society and international partners. for all these reasons, and in view of the importance of these challenges, i have voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.

in writing. ‒ it is of great importance to support the measures contained in the agency to combat terrorism and prevent radicalisation. responding to the threat posed by foreign fighters and terrorism in general requires a multidimensional approach that addresses in a comprehensive manner the factors underlying radicalisation as well as the commission of terrorist acts of all kinds. the eu must work urgently to properly assess the security threat and focus on areas of immediate priority for counter-terrorism. the eu must act more forcefully and urgently in the fight against terrorism. for these reasons i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ we voted against the european agenda on security. we believe that the way the agenda is constructed reflects a militaristic conception of the term security which does not correspond to the project of european union as a union for peace and social issues as the key elements of the project. we also understand that there is no preliminary work in defining the term security, or national security, necessary preliminary work in order to be able to establish a sound agenda. the mention of human rights as a fundamental element of a european agenda for security cannot be a secondary element in it either, which makes it necessary to review the subordination of terms to one another and of the contingent to the necessary, that is, the law in the social sense of the term.

in writing. ‒ the conflict in yemen is causing terrible suffering to the yemeni population (more than 20 million people urgently need humanitarian aid), but it also exemplifies the chaos in the area, chaos that came with the proxy war and unilateral interventions. a coalition led by saudi arabia, a theocratic dictatorship very friendly to the eu, is bombing with banned weapons and has imposed a naval blockade that affects civilians. we are convinced that there is no military solution to this situation and we call for an inclusive political solution, the lifting of the naval blockade, a ceasefire, the cessation of bombing, the cessation of arms supplies and an investigation into whether the united kingdom, france, germany and spain have failed to comply with the european union's code of conduct on arms exports. since the resolution adopted insists on the need for a political solution to the conflict and condemns the airstrikes by the saudi-led coalition and the naval blockade imposed on yemen, pointing to the coalition as the cause of thousands of deaths and further destabilisation of the country, i have voted in favour of the text.
in writing. ‒ yemen is the poorest country in the arab world. 47% of its population live on less than two dollars a day and four million yemenis are malnourished or lack access to food. the military offensives and coalition bombings have plunged the country into political instability and an unprecedented economic collapse. the yemeni government faces many challenges. the peace agreement and national association is not supported by a large part of civil society. the government has been met by the houthis, who have seized power in half the country. saudi arabia has formed a coalition to restore the president to power, turning yemen into a battleground between the two rival regional powers, saudi arabia and iran. parliament called for a ceasefire, access for humanitarian aid and humanitarian workers and a political solution to the crisis, urged all parties to implement un security council resolutions and insisted that all necessary measures be taken to ensure respect for human rights.

in writing. ‒ the current crisis in yemen is the result of an unfair distribution of power and the inability to realise a fair distribution of power, systematically ignoring the many tribal tensions in the country. on 26 march 2015, a saudi-led coalition together with various arab states launched a military operation in yemen against houthi rebels at the request of yemeni president abd rabu mansur hadi. the eu should urge all parties in yemen to seek to resolve their differences through dialogue and consultation and call on all regional actors to engage constructively with the yemeni parties. it is essential that all parties respect international humanitarian law and international human rights law to ensure the protection of civilians. for these reasons i voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because, from a security, interventionist and neo-colonial point of view, i believe that the european union must increase its influence in the countries of the middle east and north africa by all available means, including military means, in order to extend 'european values' and safeguard their values and interests, such as, among other things, the defence of their energy security. this report by a french socialist mep insists on the military approach to conflict resolution, even celebrating the bombing of the military coalition against is. it is also totally interventionist in the countries of the region, since it advocates pressuring these countries to implement liberal economic reforms and accept new free trade agreements with the eu. i am convinced that the relationship with our neighbours cannot be centred on the repression of migrants with aberrant instruments such as frontex or on the promotion of asymmetric economic relations. on the contrary, we shall only have real security if we do not interfere, if we do not destabilise and, above all, if we do not have an unequal economy and trade. this is the exact opposite of what is contained in this report, which is why i did not hesitate to vote against it.
in writing. ‒ the absence of democracy is one of the fundamental causes of instability in this region. the answer is a multidimensional approach. the european parliament also called on the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu's citizens are able to access the information they need to make their decisions. poverty and inequality are other causes of the present instability. the report calls for greater emphasis to be given to them and encourages the eu to establish free trade areas and streamline the procedures for sending financial aid. the report also calls for the eu to take action to combat terrorism and to ensure that the eu's external borders are not encroached upon. egypt is called upon to respect human rights and political freedoms. the european council welcomed the progress made in the negotiations on the nuclear programme with iran. parliament also called on the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu's external relations were not jeopardised by the conflict.

in writing. ‒ the conflicts in syria, iraq, yemen and libya, as well as the rising tensions in the middle east and north africa region, are major causes of destabilisation in this region and for the security of the entire region. stabilisation of the region is not only a matter of security, but also has economic, political and social consequences. the european union was unable to anticipate the problems arising in the region and to deal with the complexity of the situation. the eu must address the causes of the rapid deterioration of the situation in the middle east and north africa region through an ambitious approach, as well as support the international campaign against isil. for these reasons i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the rise of radical islam, and more particularly of the islamic state, in the middle east and north africa, is the direct, predictable and catastrophic consequence of western interventionism over the last 15 years. under atlanticist leadership, the european union has helped to overthrow stable - though undeniably authoritarian - regimes, leaving people systematically to be prey to tribalism and the emergence of terrorist movements. the peillon report, in its security aspects, makes no mention of the causes of a situation whose consequences are now being felt by all the citizens of the member states of the european union and draws no lessons from what has clearly unleashed the terrorist threat in recent years. far from giving the member states the means to defend themselves against this threat, this report once again intends to entrust this role to the european union, without any strategic, diplomatic, moral or ideological challenge. for all these reasons, i opposed this text.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the review of the european neighbourhood policy (enp), launched by the european commission, which sets out the eu's relations with the countries closest to it, to the south and to the east. the enp needs to be adapted to new contexts, such as the conflict in ukraine and instability in syria and libya. the central role of respect for and promotion of human rights in the new enp, which must be more flexible and coherent, is underlined. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of the environment and the environment from harmful substances. priorities must be agreed with each country, but specifically mention promoting the rights of women and the lgbti community, and fighting poverty, exclusion and unemployment. this more social dimension has been introduced by our socialist group. on migration, support is given to the signing of agreements to facilitate and liberalize visas and the opening of legal immigration channels. the council also called for the establishment of a european union-wide network of national authorities responsible for the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms.
in writing. ‒ i agree that a review of the neighbourhood policy was necessary in view of its obvious failure. the eu, however, continues to pursue its eurocentric and asymmetrical vision, believing that its model of democracy must be imposed and maintaining an absence of self-criticism on the role of the european union. not to mention the incentive approach, the rewarding of effective partners, with neo-colonial inspiration. the european union continues to seek stability based on relations with the political elites. we have a common european security policy subordinated to the policies of the united states and nato. moreover, this report consciously avoids mentioning the western sahara conflict and refers to morocco as an ally. the alawite regime is the main recipient of european union neighbourhood policy funds, while maintaining the occupation of western sahara. no state in the world recognizes morocco's sovereignty over western sahara and the european union, unfortunately, remains de facto an accomplice and collaborator of the moroccan occupation. that is one of the reasons why i voted against this report.

in writing. ‒ the report is the european parliament's response to the consultation launched by the european commission to review the european neighbourhood policy (enp). the current revision process responds to the need to adapt the enp to the new context, marked by the conflict in ukraine in the eastern neighbourhood and by the instability in syria and libya in the southern neighbourhood. the report underlines the strategic importance of the enp and the central place that respect for and promotion of human rights must continue to occupy in the new enp. the report talks about reforming the new policy with the aim of making it more flexible, focused and coherent. one of the key points of the report is also the defence of the principle of conditionality and 'more for more', whereby those countries which are making the most progress with what has been agreed in the action plan should receive more support from the eu. the importance of promoting the rights of women and minorities, including lgbti people, and of fighting poverty and exclusion is also mentioned. i agree with these considerations and have therefore voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ socialists have always defended the need to guarantee a fair remuneration to authors because without it there is no sustainable cultural creation. europe has a thriving cultural industry which is able to continue to create jobs in the midst of the crisis. and copyright is the foundation on which the cultural industries are built. europe needs to review its legislation to adapt it to the digital environment and to be able to harness its potential to create new jobs and innovative industries. but it is important to avoid framing copyright reform as a clash between authors and users. the report also calls for the creation of a european union-wide network of information and communication networks, including the european information and communication network, which will be used to support the development of the european union's information society. i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i abstained because the most negative aspects initially raised by the rapporteur were removed during the vote on the report, namely the possibility that the use of photographs, videos and other images which are permanently in public places should be subject to prior authorisation by the authors, which would have constituted an intolerable restriction on the dissemination of culture and knowledge. however, i could not vote in favour of the final text, because it essentially reinforces the idea of copyright as a model which aims to seek the greatest possible economic benefit for large companies rather than making a proposal aimed at a profound change in the current model of intellectual property; one which gives priority to the dissemination of culture and knowledge and which gives relevance to the social and collective aspects of works and works.

in writing. ‒ a copyright reform should contribute to further development of technologies, cultural exchange and enhance legal certainty in the creative sector. any reform of copyright legislation must provide a high level of protection of intellectual property in order to encourage investment in creativity and innovation and to safeguard employment and encourage job creation. this position represents the right balance between user access and fair remuneration for creators, taking also into account the interests of small and medium-sized enterprises. the report adopted in committee reflects the balance of rights indicated in the commitments which led to a positive vote in this report. the commission will continue to support investment in the creative industries, while at the same time giving the industry an opportunity to integrate digital technologies and providing end-users with better access.
in writing. ‒ the commission intends to modernise the copyright framework through the proposal for a revision of the directive. this is a reform which should contribute to further development of technologies and cultural exchange, while improving legal certainty in the creative sector, which should provide a high level of protection of intellectual property, by encouraging investment in creativity and innovation and by safeguarding employment and fostering job creation. the modernisation of the legislative framework cannot in any way lead to the abolition of freedom of panorama. we must be able to strike the right balance between copyright protection and access to knowledge for european citizens. i therefore voted in favour of the report and against the amendment on freedom of panorama.

in writing. ‒ we need to adapt the intellectual property regime currently applied in the eu to a constantly changing digital environment in order to ensure that creators are remunerated, meet citizens' expectations and promote innovation in the digital domain. we also need further harmonisation of exceptions and the implementation of a solution to tackle geo-blocking so that we can move towards a true european digital market where consumers can access europe's cultural diversity, regardless of where they live. i strongly support the existence of exceptions to support research and education, as well as freedom of panorama. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be consulted on the proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment by the placing on the market of products containing or consisting of certain substances or preparations which may be used for the protection of human health or the environment. the debate on copyright should not be tilted towards the criminalisation of consumers. the development of new online services has allowed the multiplication of legal offers on the internet, which should be promoted for the benefit of artists and creators, whose contractual position should be strengthened, but also for the benefit of smes and users.
in writing. ‒ i abstained on the report on the harmonisation of specific aspects of copyright. we believe that there must be a tendency towards the homogenisation of the different intra-community legislation. however, this homogenization must take account of the different pillars on which the so-called knowledge society is based, it must ensure equal opportunities and access to the content produced and it must also protect the authors of such content by guaranteeing legal spaces for dissemination that do not prejudice access for consumers. the idea of a digital single market has its good points, but it also has its bad points. with a digital single market, copyright enforcement can be pursued throughout the european union, so specificities would be lost. these specificities are criticized for limiting access, but in some cases they are necessary for fair remuneration of creators (emphasis on several paragraphs of the document (25, 26 and 27). they are also necessary to facilitate management by each country according to the needs linked to its own conditions.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because i am convinced that 'democratization' cannot be a pretext for interference, regime change and interventions in favour of geostrategic and imperialist interests of the eu in third countries. convinced that the european endowment for democracy is in breach of international law and treaties and of the principle of non-interference enshrined in the charter of the united nations, i have tabled an alternative motion for a resolution through my group in this parliament calling for the abolition of the edd, since neither this mechanism nor the european neighbourhood policy have ever contributed to the consolidation of democracy for the benefit of the people, but to a general regression of social and economic rights through the imposition of free trade agreements and the consolidation and strengthening of the power of oligarchies and authoritarian regimes. i therefore voted against this report and called for the creation of a new cooperation policy based on equality, solidarity and mutual development, which would replace the current eu policies based on xenophobia and warmongering.
in writing. ‒ the european endowment for democracy (edd) is an independent private law foundation, based in brussels and co-financed by the eu and the member states. after two years of existence, we are now making a positive assessment of the edd, which was set up to promote the european values of freedom and democracy, and which i supported in the vote in the house. the edd offers fast and flexible funding, based on policy analysis and efficiency of applications, complementing other eu funds, with low administrative burdens and simple procedures. at the same time, the edf regularly consults the institutions and other actors in order to ensure synergies, complementarity and added value with eu financial instruments and member states' bilateral activities, and thus avoid possible duplication. the report stresses that in order to maintain and further develop the effectiveness of the edd, stable and transparent funding needs to be ensured in the long term. there are still 12 member states which do not contribute.

in writing. ‒ under the guise of promoting and supporting 'democracy, the rule of law and respect for the universality and indivisibility of human rights and fundamental freedoms', andrzej grzyb's report on the emff proposes a number of measures to strengthen the emff, with obvious ideological and geostrategic underpinnings. thus, russia is specifically targeted by this text, which, not only gives moral lessons and interferes in the relations of two sovereign states, but also makes itself very clear as a defender of communitarianism (ethnic, religious, lgbt). democracy needs sovereign states and free peoples to exist, concepts which are foreign to the european union. for these reasons i opposed this report which uses universal values in a perfectly self-interested way.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this assessment. the activities of the european endowment for democracy are based on the 'democratization scheme' of the eastern countries on terms chosen and decided by the eu. this means it can be all or nothing. this means a clear interference in the internal politics of foreign countries and the will to implement a political, economic and social system according to the parameters dictated by the eu. in international law, the principle of non-interference is recognised by article 2 (4) of the charter of the united nations. i therefore consider that the aim of this organisation is to see the neighbourhood policy as a violation of international laws and treaties. in podemos we defend the right of peoples to decide their future and to decide their model of political, economic and social development.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because i am convinced that 'democratization' cannot be a pretext for interference, regime change and interventions in favour of geostrategic and imperialist interests of the eu in third countries. convinced that the european endowment for democracy is in breach of international law and treaties and of the principle of non-interference enshrined in the charter of the united nations, i have tabled an alternative motion for a resolution through my group in this parliament calling for the abolition of the edd, since neither this mechanism nor the european neighbourhood policy have ever contributed to the consolidation of democracy for the benefit of the people, but to a general regression of social and economic rights through the imposition of free trade agreements and the consolidation and strengthening of the power of oligarchies and authoritarian regimes. i therefore voted against this report and called for the creation of a new cooperation policy based on equality, solidarity and mutual development, which would replace the current eu policies based on xenophobia and warmongering.
in writing. ‒ the european endowment for democracy (edd) is an independent private law foundation, based in brussels and co-financed by the eu and the member states. after two years of existence, we are now making a positive assessment of the edd, which was set up to promote the european values of freedom and democracy, and which i supported in the vote in the house. the edd offers fast and flexible funding, based on policy analysis and efficiency of applications, complementing other eu funds, with low administrative burdens and simple procedures. at the same time, the edf regularly consults the institutions and other actors in order to ensure synergies, complementarity and added value with eu financial instruments and member states' bilateral activities, and thus avoid possible duplication. the report stresses that in order to maintain and further develop the effectiveness of the edd, stable and transparent funding needs to be ensured in the long term. there are still 12 member states which do not contribute.

in writing. ‒ the situation in burundi continues to deteriorate as president nkurunziza has turned a deaf ear to the international community and continues with his electoral plans. on 29 june, legislative and local elections were held in the country, despite the continuing climate of violence, the total absence of conditions for the development of an electoral campaign, the lack of impartial media and the increasing number of citizens who decide to leave the country for fear of the outbreak of an open civil conflict. this joint motion for a resolution, which i voted for, calls for action against those responsible for the current situation and the violence against civilians, including possible targeted sanctions and asset freezes. the council also called on the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu's financial assistance to the country is not used to further the current political crisis. the resolution also calls for more emergency aid to meet the needs of the growing number of refugees in neighbouring countries.

in writing. ‒ the motion for a resolution put to the vote is the result of the european parliament's intention to commemorate the anniversary of the tragic events that took place in the town of srebrenica in july 1995, when it was occupied by the army of the republika srpska. however, i could not vote in favour of the motion for a resolution because, unfortunately, such statements are a clear manipulation of the victims of those atrocities, who were later evoked to commit other crimes no less atrocious by the western powers in the region. moreover, the commemoration of srebrenica is a reminder of other no less tragic events that took place in the same context, such as the mass expulsion of serbs from krajina in august 1995. for these reasons, therefore, i have finally abstained.
in writing. ‒ the council has been unanimous and consistent in calling the events in srebrenica a genocide, of which 11 july 2015 marks the 20th anniversary. this act of ethnic cleansing took place during the bosnian war. the crimes were committed by the army of republika srpska, under the command of general mladic and the president of republika srpska, radovan karadzic. the victims were about eight thousand people, practically all bosnian muslims. that killing has left deep emotional scars on the surviving society and persistent obstacles to reconciliation between the ethnic groups of bosnia and herzegovina. the srebrenica massacre was declared an act of genocide by the international criminal tribunal for the former yugoslavia, occurred in a un-designated safe haven, and is a symbol of the international community's impotence to intervene in a conflict and effectively protect innocent civilians. the ep adopted resolutions on this killing in 2005 and 2009. the eu currently maintains a stabilisation agreement with bosnia and herzegovina, signed in 2008, which entered into force last month. i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution.

author. - mr president, as is obvious, we defend and support this resolution. we do so, i think, by also sharing with the other authors, and i hope with all the groups, a certain uneasiness. because it is a question of 'we are already used to it: a certain repetition, a certain expression of concern or of denunciation in the face of certain realities' of facts which have already been the subject of consideration and treatment in this parliament. in this case, the cambodian case, it's not even a year and a half old. more specifically, in january 2014. there seems to be an insurmountable contradiction - we should be thinking about it - between economic development, the production of prosperity and respect for human rights, the rule of law, the establishment of basic standards of social and labour regulation, etc. we are now concerned about the cambodian government's triple legislative initiative which does not seem to respect our minimum criteria for what should be a process of participation, of social debate, precisely because it also affects groups such as non-governmental organisations or trade unions, which are protagonists, which should be protagonists of these basic rights. and this is happening at the same time as the country is repeating the classic issues of the past few years, especially the policies aimed at, for example, the eviction of small farmers from large areas of land, usually owned by the state itself, to convert them into concessions and pre-industrial farms, etc. or it coincides with the proliferation of small workshops, which are also protagonists of a more than doubtful respect for human rights. part of that reality, let's be clear, has to do with ourselves, with our incentives, with our industrial demand, with our consumption habits. there is a connection between the large sugar cane plantations and our soft drink industry; there is a connection between the workers in the garment factories and our large retail chains. it is therefore worth asking whether this positive initiative of 'everything but arms' should not be supplemented by another slogan. all right, everything except weapons, but nothing without rights. i think it would be necessary and timely.
the european parliament, which is demanding that the commission sign aggressive trade agreements with developing countries, which facilitate the penetration of the large multinationals into their economies, pretends to be surprised by the tragic consequences, which are nothing more than the expulsion of farmers from their land and the exploitation of workers in exporting factories. we want to call on the cambodian government to ensure that the international labour organisation conventions on trade unions and labour are respected, allowing workers to organise themselves against multinationals, and to stop and reverse the terrible land grabbing by the big agro-exporting companies. but europe's responsibility goes beyond recalling these fundamental principles: europe must act to ensure that full recognition of labour and land rights is included in its association and cooperation agreements, especially with the least developed countries. only then can he avoid collaborating in the exploitation of workers he now denounces.

first vice-president of the commission.– madam president, i welcome this annual debate on the situation of fundamental rights in the european union and i appreciate the huge amount of work done by ms ferrara. the european parliament’s call to all eu institutions and all member states to protect and promote fundamental rights is loud and clear. the european commission fully supports this call. allow me to start by addressing some of the substantive questions raised in your report, before turning to more institutional aspects pertaining to the mechanisms at our disposal for the protection of fundamental rights. equality is a central issue in your report, and indeed this principle is at the heart of the european project. yet discrimination all too often continues to occur in every single member state. take the recent case concerning a town district inhabited primarily by roma citizens, in which the electricity meters were placed on poles six metres high, whereas in all other parts of town they were placed at a height where they could easily be monitored. i am glad that the european court of justice clarified that such practices are not acceptable under eu law. much remains to be done to secure equal treatment everywhere, regardless of religion or belief, race or ethnic origin, gender, age, disability or sexual orientation – and eu law has a crucial role to play in this respect. i therefore welcome the call in your report for the rapid adoption of the equal treatment directive, which remains a priority for this commission. it is highly regrettable that it has not yet been agreed. another issue that worries me is the rise of intolerance and hatred in our societies: you can see it on a day-to-day basis now, certainly linked with the refugee crisis. we are going through a period of crisis right now which is not just social and economic. it is political and moral. in times such as these, we see again the old tendencies of trying to identify scapegoats – of always looking for somebody else to blame – and minorities are always at the receiving end of the blame. therefore, combating prejudice, racism and xenophobia has to be a focus of action. this is also the reason why the commission will devote its first annual fundamental rights colloquium at the start of october to issues related to hate crime and discrimination, and in particular the fight against anti-semitism and islamophobia, which are distinct but related phenomena. another important set of challenges raised in your report concerns the protection of personal data, the right to privacy, and the maintenance of security. in this respect, let me first of all stress that getting the data protection reform agreed by the end of the year remains a top priority for the commission. both the data protection regulation and the proposed directive for criminal-law enforcement authorities are crucial pieces of legislation to ensure that citizens across the eu continue to benefit from solid, up-to-date rules safeguarding their right to the protection of personal data. i am confident that we will succeed in adopting a meaningful and strong reform package by the end of this year, and i count on your continued support in this respect. we will also continue to insist on the full observance of data protection standards in our relations with third countries, including the united states of america. i am pleased to note that we are on the point of finalising negotiations for an umbrella agreement with the united states, setting out ambitious and comprehensive standards for the protection of personal data when such data are exchanged between law enforcement authorities in the united states and in the european union. let me also stress that there should be no doubt that personal-data processing – for any purpose, including the enforcement of criminal law – must comply with the charter of fundamental rights, and in particular be necessary and proportionate. this being said, we also need to take into account the fact that there can be duly justified situations requiring – for legitimate reasons of criminal-law enforcement and in order to ensure public security – that the personal data of persons not immediately suspected of criminal activity also be processed. let me now turn to the more institutional questions in your report, in particular the question of whether we need new mechanisms for the protection of fundamental rights, including a new strategy for fundamental rights. at this stage, today, i am not convinced that we do. mainstreaming the charter of fundamental rights should be a reflex for all eu institutions throughout the policy cycle. we have the existing 2010 strategy on the application of the charter of fundamental rights and, before considering new mechanisms, we should continue to implement it. this means a systematic screening of all relevant legislative and policy measures to ensure their compatibility with the eu charter of fundamental rights. the adoption of the better regulation package is a further step in this direction: it provides for fundamental rights to be taken into account systematically in the assessment of all significant policy initiatives. of course, this also is a shared responsibility of all the eu institutions. therefore, as outlined in the commission’s proposal for an interinstitutional agreement on better law-making, a similar assessment should also occur when significant amendments are made to commission proposals during the legislative process. the commission, as guardian of the treaties, is also committed to ensuring that the member states respect the charter – including, if need be, by means of infringement proceedings. in 2014, the commission launched 11 infringement procedures against member states specifically to ensure that charter rights are respected. the main areas of concern are asylum and immigration, in conjunction with the lack of free legal assistance, the right to an effective remedy, detention conditions and the situation of children. your report also calls for a strengthening of the framework for the protection of the rule of law in the european union. i fully agree that ensuring full respect for the rule of law is crucial to the protection of fundamental rights throughout the union. without the protection afforded by independent courts, and without effective judicial redress mechanisms, fundamental rights will remain on paper only. that is why the commission, two years ago, adopted a rule of law framework setting out a structured process according to which the commission will react when there are specific indications that there is a systemic threat to the rule of law. i can assure you that we remain vigilant as regards any threats to the rule of law, wherever they may occur, and that we will not hesitate to activate the framework when necessary. i can also assure you that the commission’s approach will remain objective and impartial, and based on the law and the facts on the ground and not on political speeches. let me also stress that the commission remains fully committed to eu accession to the european convention on human rights. accession to the convention will serve to strengthen our fundamental values. it will improve the effectiveness of eu law and the coherence of fundamental rights protection across europe. december last year. let me conclude as you did, ms ferrara, in your opening statement, with a few words about migration. i fully agree that our reaction to this crisis must also be about protecting fundamental rights: the fundamental right to asylum for those in need of refuge; their right to be protected from risking their lives in the hands of ruthless traffickers; and also their right to be conflict with a feeling of being overrun or flooded. we need to get out of that contradiction. there is no need to fear being flooded, and certainly not if we can apply asylum policy as it was intended. and there is certainly no need to take leave of our fundamental values. that means that people who flee from war and persecution have a place in our society. let me conclude by stressing that it is a joint responsibility of the european parliament, the commission and other institutions to ensure respect for, and the promotion of, our common values. democracy, fundamental rights and the rule of law must be, and continue to be, a reality for every single citizen and anybody else who is in europe. all institutions and bodies, including the commission and the european parliament,
