the fisheries agreement between the european union and guinea-bissau can be considered one of the most important agreements currently in force. it is one of the few fisheries agreements in the european union that allows access to mixed fisheries. the country has enormous resources, but it is considered one of the least developed countries. it is estimated that two thirds of the families live below the poverty line. its gross domestic product per capita is one of the lowest in the world. its economy is heavily dependent on agriculture, particularly cashew. small-scale fishing, including subsistence fishing, ensures the survival of thousands of fishermen. despite the signing 35 years ago of the first fisheries agreement between the european union and the republic of guinea-bissau, the results achieved so far, in comparison with the sector, are shockingly meagre. three quarters of the approximately 1 500 boats surveyed in 2009 were canoe-type, made from tree trunks. we believe that a more detailed assessment and consideration of this agreement, its history and its future prospects is necessary. given the role and powers of the european parliament in this area, we believe it is appropriate and necessary to adopt a non-legislative resolution on this agreement. the agreement should promote a more effective and sustainable development of the guinean fisheries sector and related industries and activities, in particular small-scale fishing, which contribute significantly to food security and food sovereignty and to local livelihoods, increasing the added value that remains in the country and contributing to the improvement of the quality of life of the population as a result of the exploitation of its natural resources. mechanisms should be established to enhance transparency, accountability and participation of local people, in particular small-scale fishing communities, including the possible revision and increase of the sectoral support component of the agreement, while creating other and better conditions to increase and ensure that the positive impact of the agreement preferably falls on local communities. persistent and lasting efforts are needed to produce positive results and, finally, as examples of areas to be supported, institutional capacity building, vocational training, small-scale fishing, a greater focus on gender policies with a recognition and appreciation of the role of women, distribution, marketing of fish, conservation, first processing. as in other countries in the region, it is considered necessary to improve the quantity and reliability of information on catches in general and on the state of conservation of fishery resources, as well as support for capacity building by guinea-bissau. finally, we stress that parliament must be immediately and fully informed at all stages of the procedures relating to the protocol or its renewal. it is proposed that a report be submitted annually to parliament and the council on the results of the multiannual sectoral programme referred to in article 3 of the protocol and on compliance with the catch declaration requirement.
member of the commission.– madam president, it is a pleasure to be here for this joint debate on the sustainable fisheries partnership agreements and the associated protocols with madagascar, guinea-bissau and cape verde. i welcome this opportunity to discuss these protocols with you, and i would like to thank, first and foremost, the rapporteurs – mr serrão santos, mr ferreira, who was represented by ms senra rodríguez, and mr van dalen – for their reports. i am also pleased to note that the reports adopted in the committee on fisheries recommend that parliament give its assent to the three protocols we will be discussing today. i can assure you that i have taken careful note of your suggestions for improvement. our strategy underlying fisheries agreements is to consolidate and possibly extend the network of agreements, in particular tuna agreements. these agreements will allow our fleet to rely on a real continuum of agreements in the three main regions concerned – basically the atlantic, the indian ocean and the pacific – bringing stable and consistent rules for its fishing operations. at the same time, they will ensure the sustainable use of fisheries resources. they will support effective fisheries management and they will contribute to the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing, and they will help the development of local industries and guarantee good value for eu taxpayers’ money. let me now say a few words on each of these protocols. the biggest of the three fisheries agreement, as has been mentioned, is the one with guinea- bissau. it is essential for the eu fleet and it is also vital for the economy of guinea-bissau, which is highly dependent on fisheries. under the new protocol, the eu fleet has been able to resume its fishing activities in guinea-bissau after an interruption of over two years, and these fishing activities are sustainable: the stocks are considered to be in a good state and fisheries indicators such as catch levels and fishing effort have remained stable over the past years. fishing opportunities were, in fact, slightly reduced and we took specific conservation measures. having said this, it is clear that the situation needs to be monitored very closely. scientific cooperation with guinea-bissau should also be intensified, as well as scientific cooperation at regional level. sectoral support to guinea-bissau has been programmed mainly to improve the management of fisheries resources, to further reinforce control and surveillance capacities, to improve sanitary conditions and to promote artisanal fisheries. allow me to turn now to another partner in the region, cape verde. although this fisheries agreement is the smallest in financial terms, it is of strategic importance for the eu fleet because of high catch volumes and its position in the regional network of tuna agreements. as mr van dalen mentioned, the sustainability of shark fishing was a concern under the previous protocol. several measures are therefore included in the new protocol to regulate shark catches by eu vessels more effectively. firstly, the reduction in fishing opportunities for longliners is expected to reduce or at least ‘freeze’ the number of shark catches. secondly, the protocol provides for a monitoring mechanism for shark catches and a study on the situation of sharks in cape verde and the wider region. we will monitor closely the implementation of these measures, which should also be seen in the wider framework of the international commission for the conservation of atlantic tunas (iccat). the new sectoral support programme will focus on reinforcing cape verde’s monitoring, control and surveillance capacity through the installation of a new vessel monitoring system (vms) and the introduction of electronic catch reporting. let me now turn to the eu-madagascar protocol. this protocol is an important part of a broader network of fisheries agreements with coastal states in the south-western part of the indian ocean. let me highlight just two of its key elements: first, its contribution to the development of the malagasy domestic fishing sector, in particular its small-scale component; and, second, its provisions on sharks and the protection of the most vulnerable species. in terms of sectoral support, the protocol aims to strengthen the monitoring and control capacities of the malagasy authorities nationally and also at the level of the south-western indian ocean. this should help make madagascar one of the major regional players in the fight against iuu fishing. here too mr serrão santos raised the concern about sharks. on shark fishing, the protocol very clearly defines the scope of authorised shark fisheries. allowable species show either stable abundance indices or slight positive trends. in addition, through its catch limits, the protocol will clearly constrain fishing mortality on sharks in malagasy waters. with regard to protection of the most vulnerable species – and i am referring here to sharks, sea-turtles, marine mammals and seabirds – the measures in the protocol go beyond management conservation measures adopted by regional fisheries management organisations. the protocol specifically defines prohibited species in relation to capture and retention on board. on top of this, eu ship-owners have put in place best practices to decrease incidental catches and to handle vulnerable species caught incidentally in fishing gear. let me thank you again for today’s opportunity to debate three of our fisheries agreements. i look forward to hearing your views.

on behalf of the alde group. madam president, i want to support the signing of these third generation fisheries agreements with madagascar, cape verde and guinea-bissau because the almost 20 million euros that will be provided to these countries will help to develop the local fishing industry and to maintain european industry, both in the extractive and processing sectors. they also promote more sustainable and controlled fishing practices and are a key instrument in the fight against unregulated and unreported fishing. they also propose realistic alternatives to well-intentioned but unworkable proposals, such as those on shark fishing. these agreements also improve the monitoring of the impact of the funds provided on local development and contribute to the stability of these countries. the clearest example - as the commissioner has already said - is the agreement with guinea-bissau, whose negotiation was resumed after the elections in may last year, which ended the situation opened up by the coup d'état of 2012. the partnership with this country dates back to 1980. in total, the agreements provide fishing grounds and opportunities for 265 vessels, which also help to sustain the shipbuilding industry. european shipyards are innovating to improve the efficiency and sustainability of ships and are incorporating technical means to avoid discards. for these reasons, i ask you to support these proposals and i encourage you to banish some stereotypes which do not correspond at all to the responsibility with which our fishing industry works in the world.

member of the commission.– mr president, i would like to thank all the honourable members who actively participated in this debate. it is good to note that there is substantial support from the european parliament for these agreements. the european union’s fisheries partnership agreements (fpas) promote sustainability and the development of the partner countries’ fisheries sector, particularly in these developing countries, and they are not simply a transfer of money in exchange for access to fishery resources. here i would like to make three points. firstly, the sustainable fisheries partnership agreements are a regulated and transparent tool which allows us to frame the activity of the eu fleet in partner-country waters in full observance of the principles of sustainability, good governance and fairness. they are now being recognised as such by most of the stakeholders, including many ngos. secondly, our bilateral fisheries agreements are true partnerships, and the sectoral support provided to the partner countries is tailored to the individual needs of each country. sectoral support has, for example, been used to support artisanal fisheries, to reinforce partner countries’ monitoring, control and surveillance capacity and to improve the availability and quality of scientific data. thirdly, as implementation can sometimes be challenging, as a result of the limited administrative capacities of some of our partner countries, the commission monitors the implementation of sectoral support closely and also provides technical support and training. some members had reservations in relation to guinea-bissau, and the commission takes note of the nomination of a new government in that country. we remain concerned about the political and institutional situation there and we encourage all political leaders and institutions to work together to overcome the existing divergences and to find a stable solution allowing a peaceful continuation of the reconstruction and reform process. for the time being, the situation has no direct consequences for the fisheries agreement between the european union and guinea-bissau. nevertheless, it is being followed closely in order to ensure that appropriate measures are taken if necessary and, as ms garcia mentioned, the common fisheries policy can only contribute to economic and political stability. i would like to conclude by confirming that these agreements are beneficial to the eu fishing sector and to the partner countries, and also in terms of promoting more sustainable fishing outside the eu and strengthening the fight against illegal, unreported and unregulated (iuu) fishing through the introduction of better controls, monitoring, supervision, scientific research and evaluation. i would like to thank once again the rapporteurs and all of today’s speakers for this interesting debate and for parliament’s generally positive approach to these three protocols. i am looking forward to tomorrow’s vote.
in 2010, the european union's fisheries agreement with guinea-bissau accounted for a quarter of the total economic transfers made by the union. the fisheries agreements are intended to improve the quality of life of the population, as reflected in their texts. in fact, the data show that the objectives were not achieved. unfortunately, this is no different from what we see in other countries with which the european union has fisheries agreements. the economic supremacy of the european union should not be used to get the governments of these countries to give up their natural resources, but to contribute to improving the quality of life of the people. we therefore insist that these agreements should help to improve the living conditions of the local population and support the development of small-scale fishing and related industry and activities. at the same time we call on the commission to recover, promote and strengthen small-scale fishing in the european union itself.

mr president, road transport is in a transitional phase and is awaiting the commission's strategy. the demands for interoperability, environmental efficiency and the need to link production and distribution together, among other things, force a rethinking of a model that is too dependent on large infrastructures and large transport companies. in this transition it is important to place the rights and demands of workers, both employed and selfemployed, at the centre of the debate. rest periods and wages must be guaranteed, there must be no extra loading and unloading work and, above all, social dumping must be combated. the abuse of cabotage and posted workers rules is a matter which requires more stringent inspections and clear responsibility on the part of the employer or subcontractor. it is unacceptable that the sector should be liberalised for the sole purpose of removing the protection of national conventions and regulations. transport operators are not mere service providers and therefore cannot be exempt from labour standards.
mr president, commissioner, i thank the rapporteur for the effort he has made. europe needs an integrated interoperable mobility system that improves the environmental and economic sustainability of transport. the saturation of the market today costs us 1% of european gdp, and the closure of many states or the defence of their particular interests are the cause of the failure to comply with many european standards which, if applied, would radically improve the competitiveness of our economy, that of everyone. investment commitments must be met in accordance with priorities agreed and approved by all because they add value to the whole system. we must think of all users, including those with reduced mobility, when we talk about passenger rights. we will maintain the global leadership of european industry in transport technology, the future of our economy and the quality of service that will improve our lives and our options in the face of climate change.
mr president, i would also like to thank the rapporteur for getting off his bike and offering us a global convention of good ideas for the future of transport. some concerns: firstly, road safety. this year we lost the battle, as the casualties have increased. the crisis has aged the fleet of vehicles and ruined the infrastructure, so we look forward to your proposals, madam commissioner. i would remind you that both the eff and the efsi instruments are useful for maintaining infrastructure. the other is safety, the safety of passengers and workers from terrorists. we have already had to deal with this in madrid, unfortunately, in the vicinity and in the stations of london and paris, and we wish him every success in the next working group with the council and we support him in the proposals he has to make in this regard to deal with it. transport workers, their training, their working conditions and even, imperatively, their health are all essential. we wonder what has happened to the young europeans who are unemployed while our railways, airplanes, ships and lorries cannot find a generational replacement. we look forward to your proposals, commissioner, to make the transport professions an attractive sector for so many young unemployed people. sustainability, essentially in urban mobility, i see it. that is why we support the use of bicycles and also their pacification. we also point to aspects such as the tram. finally, we need a budget, and for those who have not been able to see in the efsi a fundamental complement to the cef, i ask you, madam commissioner, to show us from your responsibility that both instruments are fundamental to getting all our projects off the ground.
mr president, i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work she has done and to point out - as this report indicates - that the academic and scientific fields are no exception to the inequality that exists in europe in terms of the opportunities for promotion for men and women. in this case, the situation is even more cruel because the number of women who successfully start in these fields is very large - in some areas it is greater than that of men - but the invisible glass ceiling prevents them from progressing. we are facing another scenario, one more european challenge for real equality, without which there will never be social justice. our amendments, which have been accepted by the rapporteur and the committee, simply wanted to emphasize that, in order to avoid such discrimination, measures must be taken, especially educational measures, to involve men in tasks considered 'feminine', and especially in the education of children, which are the ones that end up - as has been said - by preventing women from continuing their professional development. if the woman bears all the responsibility of family life, it is absolutely impossible for that glass ceiling to disappear by any more quotas or measures we take. i am therefore very grateful that this view has been included in this report and i hope that it will permeate all the measures for equality which are advocated here.

member of the commission.– mr president, the commission welcomes the report on empowering women and girls through education. this report underlines that education policies and practices are crucial in order to sensitise young people to gender equality and to combat gender stereotypes, sexism and gender-based violence from an early stage. for all these reasons, the commission is pleased to see parliament’s report in line with its work in this field. there are important achievements. there is now much greater awareness of gender equality as an educational issue. women have greatly increased their participation in tertiary education; almost 60% of university graduates in the eu are women. in addition, women’s participation in previously male-dominated study subjects is now significantly higher. yet despite important progress in recent years gender inequalities still persist in european education systems. for example, while women are more likely to have a higher education degree, they are still under-represented in science, mathematics and engineering studies and careers in research. women are not making labour market gains commensurate with their educational achievements. while there are many more women graduates, men still have a higher employment rate than women among recent graduates, leading to a 4% gap at eu level. there are also strong gender imbalances in the teaching profession. women are being under-represented in management positions, including in higher education, and men under-represented in the teaching force. right now schools, universities and teachers are rarely assessed in terms of their gender equality policies and practices. the gender equality dimension is mainstreamed into the strategic framework for european cooperation with member states in the field of education and training. last march, the education ministers met in paris, in the aftermath of the terrorist attacks in france and denmark, and adopted the paris declaration on promoting citizenship and the common values of freedom, tolerance and non-discrimination through education. gender equality was clearly and obviously identified as one of our core eu values that education ministers committed to strengthen and promote. the gender equality dimension is also mainstreamed into erasmus+, our current funding programme, which offers substantial opportunities for gender-related work. the commission shares the view that gender equality must go beyond the level of political intentions and become a reality. the commission also welcomes the strong emphasis on teachers. the attitudes of teachers and teacher educators are crucial in facilitating change. the commission will continue to promote gender equality through its policies and programmes. this is reflected in the new priorities proposed for cooperation with the member states in the context of the et 2020 strategy framework. faster progress is possible. we need to move from the identification of challenges to solutions. we need active policy intervention that is sufficiently resourced, guided by evidence, with concrete and measurable targets and with tools to monitor progress. the commission is looking forward to seeing the impact of this report and of the resolution on policy debates and on policy action around europe.
in writing. education is a fundamental instrument for empowering women, improving their economic and social status and promoting the shift towards a more equal society. factors such as poverty, social norms or gender stereotypes negatively influence the educational outcomes of women and girls and contribute to segregation in the labour market. on the other hand, teachers' attitudes, classroom environments or learning approaches can reproduce gender stereotypes that unconsciously influence students' personal development and educational choices. we therefore need to carry out studies and campaigns to raise awareness and train teachers on the influence of these stereotypes, so that we can better identify and combat inequalities. we must also insist on the need to introduce sexual education and health subjects in schools, with special emphasis on equality and respect. it is also important that we facilitate the continuing training of women so that they can grow professionally and avoid stagnation or abandonment of the labour market. to achieve this, it is essential to promote measures that facilitate work-life balance where men and women cooperate and share the responsibilities of work and private life.

mr president, headlines from june 2015: 'the european union fails to agree on the distribution of 40 000 refugees', 'spain rejects the quota proposed by the european commission'. it is true that it is national selfishness that has been standing in the way of this longed-for european solution to the greatest refugee crisis in recent years. but to assess the commission's present situation, it is necessary to discuss other fundamental issues and policies. europe will not emerge from the crisis and create jobs unless we put in place policies for growth and investment, and in this respect we welcome the first steps taken under the juncker plan. but there is another fundamental question: where is the social europe? where are the struggles against inequalities? where are the initiatives on the minimum wage and the european minimum income? where are the initiatives for equality between men and women? mr juncker, time is running out and europe is not waiting.

president of the council. mr president, mr president of the commission, ladies and gentlemen, we have just heard from president juncker and we all know that the situation, which was already very difficult before the summer, has taken on dramatic proportions with record numbers of refugees entering on the three main routes: the central mediterranean, the eastern mediterranean and the western balkans. the current situation is different from previous ones in its scale, the very rapid sequence of developments on the ground and the confusion in which they occur. the pressures on our reception capacities, our linguistic and administrative capacities are considerable, but beyond the figures and institutional considerations, it is essential to remember in this debate that the situation is, above all, indicative of human tragedies, all of them different, which affect individuals and affect families. faced with a situation of such complexity, there is no simple answer. the situation requires a firm and coherent response from europe, combining responsibility on the one hand and solidarity on the other. in addition, we need to implement a sustainable common migration policy. we must act with urgency, while preserving the future and preparing comprehensive and lasting solutions. given the external dimension of the problem we are facing and its impact on europe, the member states and relations between them, it is essential that we recognise that we cannot manage the situation by moving in a dispersed manner. i can only repeat what i said in the previous debate. our first concern will be people and their safety. it's a moral obligation to do so. this obligation also lies with us under international law and with all other state actors in conflict zones from which migration movements originate or through which they pass. secondly, we must ensure that all those who might benefit from the international protection system are given a dignified welcome. i would simply like to recall briefly what the president of the commission said about the thousands, tens of thousands of europeans, european citizens who have shown a tremendous spirit of solidarity. i believe that this illustrates europe's capacity for solidarity and it also shows, to use a beautiful phrase of the german president of the enlightened europe, ein helles europa, wie ein helles deutschland. i believe that this is the europe we support, love and must move forward. of course, we will also need to set up reception facilities that are up to the challenge, both within the union and in third countries. it will require a joint effort, which will not be without budgetary implications and this concerns you, of course, in the first place. it should be remembered that on the balkan route the vast majority of people are eligible for international protection. on two occasions in recent months, heads of state or government have addressed the complex challenges of migration and refugees. they rightly called for the development of a comprehensive approach, focusing on three key dimensions that need to be advanced in parallel: relocation and resettlement, return, readmission and reintegration, and cooperation with countries of origin and transit. during the month of july, the council made progress on relocation and resettlement and since we are already talking about emergency tools, i would like to take this opportunity to thank your parliament for adopting the keller report today. this adoption enables the council to adopt the relocation decision next monday and, above all, and this is the most important thing, to start relocating the people who have arrived since 15 august. but let us be clear, this is not enough in the face of the scale of the crisis and the human tragedies we are experiencing. and that is why i welcome the presentation by the commission of these new proposals which take account of these developments and the scale of the phenomenon. i can assure you that in the weeks and months ahead the presidency will do everything possible to move forward with all the proposals. that is why the presidency has called an extraordinary justice and home affairs council meeting for next monday, 14 september, to review all the measures to be taken. i will not go into detail here, but there are immediate priorities: the implementation of the hotspots, the strengthening of the effectiveness of our return policy and our readmission instruments and above all the fight against the smuggling of migrants by smugglers. at international level, we need to work to strengthen cooperation with our partners in managing migration flows, including africa, the western balkans and turkey. in this effort, each member state and the union must make their contribution in a spirit of responsibility and sharing, because europe must find a solution that touches all questions and all problems, a solution that really responds to the challenges we face. i don't hide the differences. we have different histories, we have different situations, we have different traditions between member states, but today we have a duty to overcome the obstacles and to focus on what we have in common. what we have in common is stronger than the differences that separate us. (applause) i would like to thank in this context we also count on the active contribution of the european parliament and i am pleased to be able to listen to your debate which will be reflected in the council's discussions.
first vice-president of the commission.– mr president, i do not have to speak for a long time, because president juncker has given you the full explanation of the plans of proposal of the commission. i just want to use this opportunity, when three institutions are coming together to talk about this issue, to call upon the european parliament to strongly support the commission’s proposals today. that would be a clear signal in the preparation for the council on monday, where we know that some member states still have a number of steps to take before they can agree with the commission’s proposal. the stronger parliament can be today in coming out with its position, the better we are prepared for the council on monday. there are those who sell the illusion that simply by closing all the borders and sending everybody back we could solve this problem. there are also those who maintain that by simply opening all the borders and letting everybody in we could solve the problem. these are illusions. they have the advantage of being clear in terms of proposals, but the disadvantage of being completely impossible in terms of practicality. closing the borders and sending everyone back would mean that we take leave of our most fundamental values as europeans. it would also mean acting in clear violation of our legal obligations. opening the borders and letting everyone in would mean that we would put an end to the european social model as we know it, because it could not support people coming from all over the world in great, endless numbers. for that reason, we need to make a clear distinction between those who deserve our solidarity because they flee from war and persecution, and those who might have genuine feelings about seeking a better future but should not abuse the asylum system to attain that goal. to do that, we need a combination of solidarity and responsibility: solidarity with those who need refuge, solidarity with the states who are now burdened to excess because they are the states of first arrival, notably greece, italy and hungary. there needs to be european solidarity with these states – solidarity with the refugees and solidarity with the states in europe who need it today. that is the basis of our proposals, but also a call on responsibility: the responsibility to better guard our borders; the responsibility to make a swift registration of those who arrive at the borders so we can distinguish between those who have the right to asylum and those who do not; responsibility to create a list of safe third countries so that we can be swifter in returning people who have no right to stay; responsibility to organise the reception of refugees in a way that respects their human dignity. the combination of all these things is what the commission proposes. let me end on this, before handing the floor to federica: what we do today, and what we will be doing next monday, is closely linked to the destiny of europe – not just of the european union – but to the destiny of europe as a community of values, where we need to respect what we see is being done by countless european citizens today. we need to respect the basic humanity that makes me so proud of being european. (applause)
vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– mr president, frans timmermans said quite rightly that this is a defining moment for our union. words are important, i believe, and the refugee crisis we are facing – not only us, but the region and the world – puts our deepest values, and indeed our identity, to the test. it is a moment of truth, to see if we are really europeans and if we are really a union. that is what it is about: our responsibility to protect the lives of human beings, and human rights and solidarity among member states and towards those in need. but this is also a test for our international credibility. do not think that we can go around the word promoting human rights if we do not guarantee the highest asylum standards inside the union. do not even imagine that we can promote peace and cooperation among parties currently at war if we do not accept the others inside our own communities, and if we do not manage to find unity among ourselves. our external credibility depends largely on our internal coherence and consistency. we have to be aware of that. do not imagine that there is only an external response to the crisis, just as there cannot be only an internal response to the crisis. the two dimensions of our action – and of our identity and our response – reinforce one another or weaken one another. this is the truth, like it or not, and we have to face it. to be credible, preaching well is not enough. we must act well, we must act fast, and we must act unitedly. today, we are presenting a communication setting out the way forward for all the external action needed to address this crisis. we all know there is no magic fix to the crisis around us, and most of the external action we can take – and we are taking – will give results in the medium and long term. still, it is important that we do act now. i know it is difficult for politicians to explain the reason for taking actions that will pay back, in some cases, in years, but if we do not do that responsibly, generations coming after ours will face the same problem again and again. let me say that our external action finds us united for once. while this is not enough, because we also have to find internal unity on domestic policies, it is crucial for our action. the first priority is saving lives. commission president juncker outlined how much we have stepped up our work in this respect, noting the many lives that it has thus been possible to save. the second task is addressing the root causes, and i will come back to that. the third, and it is just as important, is to fight smugglers and traffickers of human beings, not only at sea but all along the routes, because this is a security issue too. the financial flow around the criminal organisations and networks can finance all kinds of activities potentially relevant in terms of european and international security. our strategy has been clear and consistent since the beginning of our mandate. we cannot focus only on the last mile of the tragedy: we must also consider all the steps of the refugees’ odyssey. most of the people we see today coming to europe are fleeing from conflict and persecution. this is the first issue we need to address. four million have fled syria. between syria and iraq, more than 10 million have left their homes and are internally displaced. let me say one thing: we have rightly focused in recent months on minorities in need of protection in the middle east – christians, kurds or yazidis – supporting their right to stay on the land, and go back to the communities, where they have been living for centuries. but let me also say clearly that it is not sufficient to protect them only when they are far away from us. we also have a duty to protect them – and all their fellow countrymen – when they become close to us. the long-term answer obviously is putting an end to the conflicts and the wars, facing the threat of daesh, starting processes of national reconciliation. the deal we reached with iran, although primarily a non-proliferation deal, can open the way to new possibilities, and the work in this direction, with all our international and regional partners and all the international and regional powers, has already started. secondly, we are working with the international community – mainly with the un agencies, with the countries of origin and transit and those who host an impressive number of refugees. we have mobilised almost eur 4 million in humanitarian and development aid to assist displaced syrians within syria itself and in jordan, lebanon, turkey and iraq. there is a very specific case, which is libya: not a country of origin, but a country of transit, and, more than that, an open corridor. that is why, as you know very well because we have debated it several times in this chamber, so much daily and nightly effort is being invested, with the un and special representative bernardino león gross, in trying to achieve a national unity government in libya that could allow us to partner the libyan authorities in the management of this corridor. let me say too that it is going to be very important – and we are looking very much in this direction – to work to the south of libya. if we focus only on the libyan sea border, forgetting about the libyan land border, we will never manage to solve the issue of the corridor. that is why i have started an unprecedented dialogue with the countries of the sahel, and in particular – although not exclusively – with niger. today, as you know, we are putting forward a proposal for a trust fund for africa to promote economic opportunities, development, security and better management of migration in a context of equal partnership with the african countries and our partners. the institutions will provide eur 1.8 million to this fund and i expect the member states – all of them – to do their fair share. you cannot ask for international cooperation at european level and then not put up the money for it. remember this when we come to discuss the budget. (applause) we have to show coherence in our decisions. a regional trust fund for syria has already started in recent months, and the first contract opened through the fund deals with schools and education. let me stress this, because i believe that – as we see syria losing an entire generation to war and exile – we have to invest in syrian children. that is an investment not only for the future of the country and the region but also for our security, because it is the best investment we can make against terrorism and radicalisation. thirdly – and i shall finish – we are fighting those who trade in human life: the smugglers’ and traffickers’ networks. we are doing this in partnership with countries of transit and we are doing this in the mediterranean. our naval operation in the mediterranean sea has now fulfilled the objectives of the first phase. we gathered intelligence and information on the smugglers’ routes, assets and strategies. in this first phase alone, and in the space of just five weeks, we identified 16 cases in which we would have been able to go after the smugglers, bring them to justice and capture the vessels. that is why i proposed last weekend in luxembourg, where the defence and foreign ministers were meeting, that we move to phase 2 on the high seas, in full observance of international law, and i asked member states to contribute to the mission, because this is also an opportunity for us to show that, when we have political will and a sense of urgency and unity, we can use the military and security tools that we already have to hand. but there is something else of which i am proud: that in these very first weeks of common action in the mediterranean we have saved the lives of 1 500 men and women at sea through our operation. this is not the main purpose of the operation but it is an important component of it. with regard to the way forward, we will have the valletta summit on migration in november, bringing together leaders of the european and key african countries – those that are part of the khartoum and rabat processes as well as the african union commission and the economic community of west african states commission. we will also have the high-level conference on the western balkan route, bringing together eu member states, western balkan countries and turkey. both have to be addressed with the same degree of attention and urgency. to conclude, we need to realise as europeans that this is not just a time for emotion: that is the easy part. let me be cynical: as politicians we are not asked to express our emotions; we are asked to take decisions that are consistent and coherent with our emotions, and to be strong in so doing. emotions are not enough. we need to act and this is the time. i hope that all the eu institutions, the member states, citizens and public opinion – because this wave of emotion in public opinion can change, and we have to be aware of that – will finally take responsibility for, and live up to, our values, the values of our history, the challenges of the most difficult times our history has recently faced, and the potential of our regional and global role. what is at stake, as frans timmermans said very well, is not only the lives of human beings – though a single life is enough – but also the state of our union. (applause)
member of the commission.– mr president, as you noticed, the state of the union speech was mostly on migration and shows what our priorities are. the president of the commission was clear, and i want to be clear, too. the management of migration is a crash test for europe and for the union’s credibility. i want to express my thanks to both first vice-president frans timmermans and federica mogherini for their opening remarks and for the excellent cooperation we had throughout the last month in putting together this ambitious and much-needed package. today’s package is our response to an unprecedented refugee crisis happening right in front of our eyes. as the refugee crisis around europe becomes bigger, our answers need to become bolder, more comprehensive and more ambitious. this is the europe we want. this is the europe we must have. so today we are putting forward four very concrete measures that in the short- and medium-term can help tackle all the major challenges we are confronted with. the significant increase in arrivals over the summer cannot be managed by the member states of entry alone. to address this migration we need a coordinated european approach. that is why we are now proposing to relocate 120 000 people fleeing war, persecution, oppression and chaos from italy, greece and hungary according to a distribution scheme. this new proposal comes in addition to the measures tabled before the summer to relocate 40 000 persons from italy and greece. i expect that a vast majority of the members of this house will vote in favour of this proposal later today and will also support in the future the new temporary relocation scheme. at the same time we have to learn the lesson that the current crisis is teaching us. europe is not well-equipped to manage sudden and extraordinary surges of refugee inflows. we need structural solutions to face such events in the future so that we can systematically support member states and guarantee protection for those who are really in need. that is why we propose establishing a permanent crisis relocation mechanism by amending the dublin regulation. in parallel with increasing our support to guarantee shelter for those in need of protection, we have to make sure that those who do not have the right to stay in the european union are promptly returned. as a first step, member states shall be in a position to steadily process unfounded or unlawful requests so they can devote their human and financial resources to legitimate requests, filed by those who urgently require international protection. that is why we are putting forward today the introduction of an eu list of safe countries, including the balkan countries and turkey. in 2014, nationals from these countries submitted over 17% of the total of 562 000 applications filed in the european union. these requests put a heavy burden on the european union’s national asylum systems, while the vast majority of them were clearly unfounded. by including these countries in the list of safe countries of origin, the examination of the applications for international protection will be fast-tracked. this will increase the efficiency of asylum systems, and will allow member states to devote greater resources to protect those in need and to return the applicants of unfounded requests faster. currently europe has a very low rate of return: around 40% of third-country nationals. this undermines the credibility of our migration policy. we therefore also present here today a european return programme aiming at fostering a clean-cut return policy. this communication is the occasion for the commission to set out a list of actions to support greater operational cooperation among member states and to stress the need to find leverage in our relations with third countries so that they readmit their nationals. i really count a lot on your support to implement this package as you have done, and i have to commend once again this house for being very supportive from the very beginning of our efforts to adopt a common european migration policy. i count on you and i thank you very much for the support you have provided thus far.

in writing. ‒ the fisheries agreements that the european union signs with third countries, although they are disguised as sustainable and mutually beneficial for both parties, are still the cover for continuing to exploit the resources, in this case fisheries, of the countries with which they sign these agreements. guinea-bissau, after 35 years of agreements, is still mired in poverty and its fisheries sector remains undeveloped. the european union is using its economic supremacy to impose agreements which actually benefit industrial fisheries. these agreements, if they are to be implemented on equal terms, must be based on justice, equity and sustainability and, in the case of agreements such as this, must be geared towards achieving food sovereignty for the people, so that no state or group of states will squander the resources of third parties. in considering that this is not the case and for the reasons set out here, i have not been able to give my consent to this agreement.
in writing. ‒ this renewal is made possible by the eu's decision to normalise its relations with guinea-bissau, following the holding of democratic elections in 2014. i welcome this renewal, which ensures the sustainability of fishing activities in line with the principles of the new cfp, allowing the galician cephalopod fleet access to this fishery, which means its return to the european agreements after its expulsion from mauritania in 2012. up to 16 vessels will be able to operate in guinean waters, thus alleviating their situation. it will also ensure the activity of 20 shellfish vessels from huelva, 14 freezer-freezer vessels and 9 pipe vessels with berth in bermeo, all of which are affected by the suspension of the agreement with mauritania. france, italy, greece and portugal also have fishing opportunities. the protocol will provide an annual disbursement of eur 9.2 million, of which eur 3 million will be used to strengthen the fisheries sector and the fisheries administration in guinea-bissau. i am grateful to the commission for speeding up the procedure for approving this agreement, which is also a sign of support for the new democratic government and will provide a significant injection of liquidity for the administration of guinea-bissau. i have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ given the latest political turmoil in guinea-bissau, it is more important than ever to support this fisheries partnership agreement. this three year agreement contains a financial contribution of eur 9.2 million per year in support for the overall development of guinea-bissau's fishing sector. a vital aspect of this agreement is that, while eu vessels will achieve greater fishing opportunities, stronger efforts will also be made to reinforce measures to prevent illegal and unreported fishing, which is of course positive progress.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement which will allow eu fishing vessels to fish in guinea-bissau's waters. this is an important agreement, since it concerns 28 surface tuna seiners, 12 tuna seiners and a number of shrimp trawlers and freezer trawlers. france will benefit directly from this convention, since it will be able to send 12 tuna seiners and surface longliners and 3 tuna seiners to the area. the agreement also benefits guinea-bissau, which will receive eur 9 200 000 per year, including eur 3 000 000 under the sectoral policy, which will help develop port infrastructure. in addition, each eu trawler will have to take on board seamen from guinea-bissau. finally, since guinea-bissau does not have the means to combat illegal fishing, its fishing zone will be monitored by european vessels, which will also collect scientific data to monitor the evolution of fish stocks. the agreement thus plays the role of a development agreement, since it contributes to the political and economic stability of guinea-bissau.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament approves the fisheries agreement between the european union and guinea-bissau as it is for the benefit of both parties. the eu is in charge of the socioeconomic status of the african country, which is at the tail end of the countries of the world, and which lives basically on agriculture and, to a large extent, on so-called international donors such as the european union. following the suspension of negotiations with mauritania, the eu-guinea-bissau fisheries agreement is becoming even more important, to the point of being one of the most important agreements currently in force. that is why i am in favour of this agreement, which is undoubtedly for the benefit of all.
in writing. ‒ my support for the european parliament's recommendation on the new eu fisheries protocol with guinea-bissau. we are facing an agreement which is not only good for the community fleet, which will have new opportunities for activity, but also for this country, since the eu is currently making agreements which go beyond the economic, and which provide a real framework for collaboration for the improvement of the signatory countries, in this case guinea bissau.
in writing. ‒ this renewal is made possible by the eu's decision to normalise its relations with guinea bissau, following the holding of democratic elections in 2014. i welcome this renewal, which ensures the sustainability of fishing activities in line with the principles of the new cfp, allowing the galician cephalopod fleet access to this fishery, which means its return to the european agreements after its expulsion from mauritania in 2012. up to 16 vessels will be able to operate in guinean waters, thus alleviating their situation. it will also ensure the activity of 20 shellfish vessels from huelva, 14 freezer-freezer vessels and 9 pipe vessels with berth in bermeo, all of which are affected by the suspension of the agreement with mauritania. france, italy, greece and portugal also have fishing opportunities. the protocol will provide an annual disbursement of eur 9.2 million, of which eur 3 million will be used to strengthen the guinea-bissau fisheries sector and fisheries management. i am grateful to the commission for speeding up the procedure for approving this agreement, which is also a sign of support for the new democratic government and will provide a significant injection of liquidity for the administration of guinea-bissau. i have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement which will allow eu fishing vessels to fish in guinea-bissau's waters. this is an important agreement, since it concerns 28 surface tuna seiners, 12 tuna seiners and a number of shrimp trawlers and freezer trawlers. france will benefit directly from this convention, since it will be able to send 12 tuna seiners and surface longliners and 3 tuna seiners to the area. the agreement also benefits guinea-bissau, which will receive eur 9 200 000 per year, including eur 3 000 000 under the sectoral policy, which will help develop port infrastructure. in addition, each eu trawler will have to take on board seamen from guinea-bissau. finally, since guinea-bissau does not have the means to combat illegal fishing, its fishing zone will be monitored by european vessels, which will also collect scientific data to monitor the evolution of fish stocks. the agreement thus plays the role of a development agreement, since it contributes to the political and economic stability of guinea-bissau.

in writing. ‒ the fisheries agreements that the european union signs with third countries, although they are disguised as sustainable and mutually beneficial for both parties, are still the cover for continuing to exploit the resources, in this case fisheries, of the countries with which they sign these agreements. these agreements are not intended to support the development of the fisheries sectors of third countries, but to buy governments to keep things as they are. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fisheries sector is not affected by the crisis. in the meantime, the eu's artisanal and shallow-sea fisheries are being progressively dismantled by the policies of the european union and our governments. these agreements, to be on an equal footing, must be based on justice, equity, sustainability and, in the case of agreements such as this, be geared towards achieving food sovereignty for the people, so that no state or group of states will squander the resources of third parties. it is important to have a thorough social debate on what these agreements really mean, both for the people of third countries and for the european productive sectors. for the reasons stated, i have voted to abstain.
in writing. ‒ i welcome the signing of this protocol, which will benefit 30 longliners, 28 freezer tuna-fishing vessels and 13 tuna-fishing vessels from france, portugal and spain. in particular, it will benefit 22 galician longliners, 16 freezer tuna seiners with home ports in the basque country and galicia, and 7 tuna seiners with home ports in the basque country. this is therefore good news for the spanish and european fishing fleets, as it ensures the sustainability of fishing activities in line with the principles of the new cfp. this new protocol covers a period of four years and offers fishing opportunities to 71 eu vessels in the tuna sector for a reference catch of 5 000 tonnes/year under a financial contribution of around half a million euro per year, half of which is earmarked for the promotion of sustainable fisheries, including the strengthening of cape verde's surveillance and control capacities and support for its local fishing communities. it is regrettable that the activity was interrupted between 31 august and 1 january, with particular damage to the spanish long-line fleet. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement which allows european vessels to fish in cape verdean waters. the agreement covers 28 tuna seiners (16 spanish and 12 french), 30 surface longliners (23 spanish and 7 portuguese) and 13 tuna seiners (7 spanish, 4 french and 2 portuguese). in return, the republic of cape verde will receive eur 550 000 for the first two years and eur 500 000 for the following two years. half of this will go to sectoral policy, which will include the development of local fishing communities. as is often the case in fisheries agreements with developing countries, the europeans will be involved in the fight against illegal fishing, which the republic of cape verde does not have the means to combat at the moment. i note, however, that there are legitimate concerns about shark catches. the european commission said that longliners traditionally caught a lot of sharks in this area but that it had reduced their numbers to limit bycatch. further studies, made possible by the existence of a fisheries agreement, will determine whether further measures are needed to protect the shark species concerned.

in writing. the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and the republic of cape verde dates from 24 july 1990 and six protocols have been applied since then. the main objective of the agreement is to enable european union vessels to fish in the waters of the african country and to intensify cooperation between the parties with a view to establishing a partnership framework towards a sustainable fisheries policy. the european union and the republic of cape verde have also committed themselves to strict monitoring in order to ensure the sustainable exploitation of the fishery resources. it is clear that this agreement is mutually beneficial and i therefore vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ the fisheries agreements that the european union signs with third countries, although they are disguised as sustainable and mutually beneficial for both parties, are still the cover for continuing to exploit the resources, in this case fisheries, of the countries with which they sign these agreements. these agreements are not intended to support the development of the fisheries sectors of third countries, but to buy governments to keep things as they are. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the fisheries sector is not affected by the crisis. in the meantime, the eu's artisanal and shallow-sea fisheries are being progressively dismantled by the policies of the european union and our governments. these agreements, to be on an equal footing, must be based on justice, equity, sustainability and, in the case of agreements such as this, be geared towards achieving food sovereignty for the people, so that no state or group of states will squander the resources of third parties. it is important to have a thorough social debate on what these agreements really mean, both for the people of third countries and for the european productive sectors. for the reasons stated, i have voted to abstain.
in writing. ‒ this protocol is part of the eu's network of tuna fisheries agreements in the indian ocean and mainly benefits vessels from france, italy and portugal and some 40 spanish vessels, several of them from my community. the commission has also decided to extend the period of validity of the financial contribution to the fishing activities of the malagasy fleet in the area of the malagasy fishing zone. this is to be added to the expenditure of european shipowners, which may amount to up to 4 million. the agreement is in line with the principles of the new cfp, ensuring the sustainability of fishing activities and improving fleet control standards. among the improvements achieved is a 25% increase in the quota allocated to the european long-line fleet for shark catches, of which almost all of the 18 spanish long-line vessels are galician. it also allows the european fleet to be stable in the indian ocean for a longer period of time, from 2 to 4 years.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the fisheries partnership agreement between the eu and madagascar as through these agreements a responsible fishing scheme can be achieved. this four year protocol grants fishing opportunities to eu vessels in the fishing waters of madagascar in line with internationally accepted rules, develops the local fishing sector and encourages concrete measures to safeguard vulnerable species.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement allowing european vessels to fish in malagasy waters. the agreement covers 40 tuna seiners and 54 longliners. the republic of madagascar will receive eur 1 566 250 per year for the first two years and eur 1 487 500 for the following two years. this includes sectoral policy support of eur 700 000 per year. this aid will help to develop local fisheries. the rapporteur, mr ricardo serrão santos, said that the recruitment of malagasy seamen would increase and that processing activities on the island of madagascar would be developed. whether these laudable goals will be achieved remains to be seen. finally, i note that madagascar has concluded fisheries agreements with other countries, so the presence of european fleets will also make it possible to monitor the evolution of fish stocks in the region and, of course, to combat illegal fishing.
in writing. ‒ we voted against this report for both ecological and social reasons, including the following: the plan allows for the fishing of endangered species, as well as a significant number of species classified as threatened (bluefin tuna, bluefin tuna, spanish mackerel, striped bass, blue shark). the plan also makes no provision for the preservation of seabirds, turtles and marine mammals, which often die horribly. in addition, the population of madagascar is one of the poorest in the world. under the scheme, european subsidised vessels consume the fish on which they depend for their nutrition and survival. the population of madagascar is not distributed fairly, less money is provided (decreasing by more than 100,000 euros per year) while the eu benefits more ((the reference tonnage increased by 750 tons). this is no accident: european union payments to madagascar have been declining steadily since the 1980s. these contributions do not benefit the development of the country as the plan lacks measurable objectives on this.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of approving the council decision on the conclusion of the protocol amending the marrakesh agreement establishing the world trade organisation. the agreement on trade facilitation is a historic milestone, as it is the first multilateral agreement to be reached since the creation of the wto in 1995, and it is a boost to the doha round negotiations to set the rules for international trade in the 21st century. the agreement is part of the so-called 'bali package', which covers two other groups of trade policies: proposals on trade in agricultural goods and a development chapter specifically for the least developed countries. the agreement, which aims to simplify customs procedures and reduce export costs by reducing unnecessary bureaucratic burdens and ensuring fewer delays at customs, will have an economic impact of some eur 60 billion per year on global gdp. it also includes transparency rules, special attention to smes and differentiated treatment for developing countries, for which transitional periods are provided, as well as technical assistance to facilitate their implementation.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this trade facilitation agreement because it aims to speed up 'the movement of goods by further reducing customs controls'. the agreement is to 'offer' developing countries the possibility of categorizing their commitments and determining the timetable for their implementation. it is in fact a question of adapting to the difficulties of these countries in complying with international agreements, when they do not have the necessary infrastructure and means, particularly in customs matters. the agreement therefore allows them to prioritise their actions until they can meet all their obligations. this mechanism is based, once again, on the unproven idea that ever greater free trade would enable these countries to develop. this type of agreement shows that the europeans still do not take into account the social and environmental disasters caused by the increased globalization of trade. they are therefore pursuing their objective of gradually abolishing all customs controls in order to facilitate the transit and movement of goods.

in writing. ‒ the trade facilitation agreement (tfa) is a very positive and innovative agreement for several reasons. the agreement, which was concluded at the ninth wto ministerial conference, is the first multilateral agreement since the wto was set up in 1995. the agreement aims to harmonise and simplify procedures relating to trade, thus creating a more favourable environment for businesses. it will also have a major impact on developing countries, as they will receive differential treatment, allowing them to decide when to apply the various provisions and for which they will need technical assistance. the emphasis on greater transparency will also help to fight against border corruption and provide greater security, which in turn will be a strong incentive for trade intensification. so, since the agreement is a source of benefit for both parties, i am in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ the purpose of this report is to regularise and enable the accession of austria, belgium and poland to the budapest convention on the contract for the carriage of goods by inland waterways. this convention provides legal certainty in this area by laying down general rules on the obligations of the contracting parties, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the budapest convention on the contract for the carriage of goods by inland waterways aims to promote inland navigation and harmonise its contracts and rules throughout europe. only those member states which have inland waterways falling within its scope are contracting parties to it. although the convention is an agreement which falls partly within the exclusive competence of the european union, it nevertheless provides for the possibility of the union becoming a party, and member states cannot ratify or accede to it without the union's authorisation (article 2 (1) of the treaty on the functioning of the european union). eleven member states are already parties to the convention, while fifteen member states have indicated that they have no inland waterways regulated by the convention. belgium, austria and poland have expressed their interest in becoming parties to the convention. their participation will promote the wide application of this legal instrument for the benefit of citizens and businesses, and the decision to authorise belgium and poland to ratify and austria to accede to the budapest convention should therefore be approved.

in writing. ‒ the budapest convention on the contract for the carriage of goods by inland waterways contributes to the internal market in transport by harmonising inland waterway contracts and rules across europe. the ratification of the convention by belgium, austria and poland will encourage the wide application of this legal instrument to the benefit of citizens and businesses. parliament is right to recommend such ratification.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the budapest convention. the convention covers contracts for the carriage of goods by inland waterway, mainly on the rhine, the danube and their tributaries. it is essentially a matter of harmonizing these contracts and standards for inland navigation in europe. the report adopted endorses the draft council decision authorising the kingdom of belgium and the republic of poland respectively to ratify the budapest convention and the republic of austria to accede to it. this approval is necessary because member states cannot ratify or accede to the convention without a mandate from the union. while this limitation of their sovereignty is regrettable, it does not justify preventing those states which wish to accept it from accepting the budapest convention.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it allows for the activation of an emergency mechanism so that 40,000 asylum seekers can be relocated from the member states which are experiencing increased pressure at their borders due to the refugee crisis (greece and italy) to third eu countries. the report also lays the foundations for developing a permanent system of emergency redistribution so that we can act with agility in case of emergency. the report we have voted on should serve as a model for the new emergency redistribution system. the commission has incorporated our proposals so that the interests of refugees are taken into account. i think that's the way it should be. to achieve a positive outcome for everyone, that is, for refugees and for society as a whole, it is important that we focus on refugees, where their families are, their language skills and their qualifications to improve integration opportunities.
in writing. ‒ although this report contains aspects that we reject outright, such as the identification of migrants by their fingerprints as if they were criminals, we voted in favour of this report because we believe that it is going in the right direction in terms of asylum policies by going beyond the dublin regulation and proposing a policy based on solidarity between states but taking into account the will of asylum seekers. the main positive points are a broader definition of family reunification than we have had up to now and a system of placement of applicants based on their preferences. it also includes reference to a periodic assessment of the use of the funds received by the member states for their asylum policy and the need to take into account the specificities of women and lgbti people.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it allows for the activation of an emergency mechanism so that 40,000 asylum seekers can be relocated from the member states which are experiencing increased pressure at their borders due to the refugee crisis (greece and italy) to third eu countries. the report also lays the foundations for developing a permanent system of emergency redistribution so that we can act with agility in case of emergency. the report we have voted on should serve as a model for the new emergency redistribution system. the commission has incorporated our proposals so that the interests of refugees are taken into account. i think that's the way it should be. to achieve a positive outcome for everyone, that is, for refugees and for society as a whole, it is important that we focus on refugees, where their families are, their language skills and their qualifications to improve integration opportunities.

in writing. ‒ this summer's events have shown that member states need to work together to respond to the refugee crisis. the report i am voting for today contains interim measures for italy and greece to enable them to deal effectively with the significant influx of third country nationals on their territory, which is putting a great deal of pressure on their asylum systems. these measures are a step in the right direction but we must not forget that they are only part of the overall approach that the eu must develop on migration.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this proposal to introduce provisional measures to distribute 'migrants', i.e. illegal immigrants, in all european countries. this project is in line with the lax policy advocated by the european commission. it is a sign of encouragement for those seeking to emigrate, which will lead to new waves of departures and new tragedies in the mediterranean. these newcomers, motivated in most cases by economic reasons, will compete directly with the poorest europeans in terms of access to work, health and housing. finally, by doing so, the commission and the european parliament demonstrate how dangerous it was to give the european union powers in the field of immigration and asylum. this power, as we had foreseen, is being used to open our borders even further, against the wishes of the majority of french and european citizens.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report which directly addresses the refugee crisis in europe, and in particular the relocation of asylum seekers arriving in italy and greece. while we consider the number of refugees considered in this text (40000) to be clearly insufficient given the scale of human displacement that is taking place, the text speaks of this number as a start. the commission is also proposing an automatic system of relocation, which takes into account the preferences of refugees. the mechanism thus approved can serve as a test bed for developing an effective system that can be applied on a larger scale in the months and years to come.

in writing. ‒ my vote was positive to this ska keller’s report. it establishes an emergency mechanism for the relocation of 40 000 refugees with high recognition rates (syrians, eritrean, iraqis) from italy and greece to other member states is adopted. the parliament insists on a binding distribution key for the relocation of refugees. in addition, it is in favour of significantly stronger solidarity measures and increases the number of refugees to be relocated to 110 000. a large majority of the ep also suggests that the preferences of refugees for a member state, based on family, social and cultural ties, should be taken into account to the extent possible.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which seeks, within the limits set by the treaties (such as through the principle of subsidiarity), to increase the participation of subnational entities in the decision-making process on european policies. the text adopted therefore supports, among other things, the creation of a european urban agenda, which considers the objectives of territorial cohesion taking into account the potential and threats of densely populated areas. i should like to remind you, however, that priority must be given to rural areas, where unemployment is generally high, public services are more difficult to access and the population is increasingly depopulated. however, i voted in favour of the need to promote, through the many financial instruments (such as integrated territorial investments, community-led local development, etc.) and the participatory instruments, a more rational model of sustainable development in the urban areas of the european union, which create synergies not only with each other but also with their rural environments.
in writing. ‒ more than 72% of the eu population lives in urban areas, where two-thirds of gdp is produced. in addition, the impact of european policies themselves is enormous at the local level. in view of the importance of urban areas in europe, the eu has begun to engage in local affairs, mainly through regional and urban development policies. this report, by german socialist kerstin westphal, examines the challenges of eu urban policy and makes recommendations for a future common policy on sustainable urban development. the lack of coherence and coordination between the various eu standards and programmes and between the local level and the other levels of government seems to be evident. to enhance this interaction, the role of the eu urban special representative is suggested, among other measures, to coordinate eu policies and initiatives and optimise decision-making work between different levels of administration, while adapting the urban programme to the objectives of the 2020 strategy and the challenges of social inclusion, demographic change and sustainability.

in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this own-initiative report by the committee on regional development, which is devoted to analysing and proposing ideas for eu urban policies. given that 78% of the union's population lives in urban areas, a coordinated approach is considered necessary for policies that directly affect them. while we believe that there is a need to be careful with certain formulations on 'multi-level governance' that could open the door to privatisation of essential aspects of urban management, we believe that overall the text is a positive step.

in writing. ‒ this own-initiative report analyses urban policy issues arising from eu policies. the document develops guidelines and limits for a future sustainable common policy. the present and the future of europe and the rest of the world are going to be purely urban. this is why, as this report stresses, it is crucial to improve the coordination of urban development policies and objectives within the eu. in this sense, the urban dimension needs to become a basic element of all relevant eu policies. in addition, union legislation should be simplified in order to facilitate its application and reduce costs. as the report says, it would also be interesting to propose a new model of governance in which cities can contribute their experiences and their views to the legislative process of the european union. the figures for the urban population are strikingly clear and will be even clearer in the coming years. that is why i am voting in favour of a report which stresses the inevitability of designing and implementing a truly sustainable and efficient urban model.
in writing. ‒ more and more people, both in europe and the rest of the world, live in cities. and we have to take that into account when designing policies of all kinds. that is why i think it is so timely that the report on the urban dimension of eu policies which we have supported, which makes it very clear from parliament that the eu must take this reality into account and act and legislate accordingly. we must be able to adopt an efficient and clear urban policy to ensure that its inhabitants have adequate living conditions and that cities become the driving force of the european economy and society.
in writing. ‒ i am aware, even as a citizen of pilsen the fourth largest city in the czech republic of the importance of the urban dimension of eu policies. i support its further development. i'd just be careful about setting up new entities within it. i do not need to say that support for the urban dimension cannot and does not conflict with rural development. as a local councillor and long-time mp, i know how important it is to contribute to maintaining the quality of life in rural areas today. the report on the urban dimension has my support.
