in writing. ‒ the ilo estimates that 880,000 people are in forced labour in the eu, many of them women victims of sexual exploitation; therefore, a greater effort is needed by eu states and institutions, including within their own economies. i voted in favour of the report because it facilitates the fight against trafficking and the protection and compensation of victims of forced labour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a council decision because eighty-six years after the adoption of the convention, which states that forced labour is prohibited and criminalized, 20.9 million people are still suffering from it. this is a systematic violation of human rights which must be avoided. this protocol can help in this respect, as it sets out requirements for member states to adopt national plans to eliminate this scourge and, more interestingly, the obligation to protect victims, including those who fall into human trafficking networks. the adoption of this protocol and its measures will improve the fundamental rights of individuals and give us more democratic legitimacy.
in writing. ‒ the forced or compulsory labour convention is one of the eight core ilo conventions. yet, more than 80 years after its adoption, it is estimated that at least 20.9 million people worldwide are victims of forced labor. the protocol aims to address existing gaps and to make progress in the prevention of trafficking for the purpose of labour exploitation, as well as in the protection and compensation of victims of forced labour. it also sets out measures to be taken by ilo member states to prevent forced labour: education and information; protection of persons, in particular migrant workers, against possible abusive and fraudulent practices in the recruitment and placement process; and actions to address root causes that increase the risk of forced labour. the ratification of this protocol is an important step in the fight against trafficking in human beings and in guaranteeing the rights of victims of crime throughout europe. it is very unfortunate that millions of people are still subjected to this kind of work today all over the world. that is why i voted to give it its approval.
in writing. ‒ the ilo estimates that 880,000 people are in forced labour in the eu, many of them women victims of sexual exploitation; therefore, a greater effort is needed by eu states and institutions, including within their own economies. i voted in favour of the report because it facilitates the fight against trafficking and the protection and compensation of victims of forced labour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the protocol in view of the need to address the gaps in its implementation and to make progress in the prevention of trafficking for the purpose of labour exploitation and in the protection and compensation of victims of forced labour. we must continue to fight for the total eradication of forced labour, because we cannot allow millions of people to be subjected to this kind of work all over the world.
in writing. ‒ the fact that approximately 20.9 million people globally still endure forced labour means that this proposal for a council decision fully merits to be supported. this shocking statistic means that basic fundamental human rights of so many remain violated. the protocol outlines the criteria necessary for members states to adopt national strategies to combat forced labour and apply the protocol’s provisions through consultation with employers’ and workers’ organisations. another vital part of this protocol is the emphasis placed on protecting victims of human trafficking and the fight against traffickers. therefore, i was very pleased to vote in favour today.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this draft for the ratification by the member states of the 2014 protocol on the forced labour convention, a convention drawn up within the international labour organisation. i am of course opposed to this form of modern slavery which still affects almost 1 million people in the european union. the 2014 protocol has the positive side that it expands the possibilities of redress and compensation for victims of forced labour. it also allows for better cooperation between states. however, care must be taken that this text is not diverted from its purpose to encourage illegal immigration. i do not want to see additional rights, in the form of facilitating entry or residence in our countries, granted to illegal immigrants under the pretext of fighting forced labour.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the recommendation as the 2014 protocol aims to address existing gaps in the implementation of the convention and to make progress in the prevention of trafficking for the purpose of labour exploitation, as well as in the protection and compensation of victims of forced labour. in 1930, when adopting the convention to which this recommendation refers, the ilo urged states to end the use of forced labour and to criminalise it. it is regrettable that more than 80 years later some 21 million people in the world are still victims of forced labour and with this protocol we are still moving in the direction of preventing these situations of human rights violations from continuing. the ratification of this protocol is an important step in the fight against trafficking in human beings and in guaranteeing the rights of victims of crime throughout europe. we support the vote by parliament to give its consent so that the member states can ratify the protocol as soon as possible and thus maintain their commitment to combating forced labour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the council decision calling on the member states to take control measures on the substance known as 4-methylamphetamine. it has been distributed illegally without consumers being properly informed of the health risks it poses, as it has been associated with several deaths in several member states due to its high toxicity.
in writing. ‒ there have been 21 deaths in four member states, where 4-methylamphetamine has been detected in autopsies, either alone or in combination with one or more substances, especially amphetamine. although the available information does not allow the role of 4-methylamphetamine in these deaths to be established with certainty, in some cases the substance was the main drug detected, with levels comparable to those found in certain cases of death caused by amphetamine use. i voted in favour of subjecting 4-methylamphetamine to control measures throughout the union. this substance carries significant health risks, as evidenced by its detection in several reported fatalities, especially when used in combination with other substances. also due to its strong similarity in appearance and effects to amphetamine, the fact that it can be consumed inadvertently, as well as its limited medical value and use, the decision to subject 4-methylamphetamine to control measures throughout the union is justified. the adoption of control measures at union level can also help to prevent 4-methylamphetamine from becoming an alternative to amphetamine in the illicit drug markets.

in writing. ‒ the scientific committee of the european monitoring centre for drugs and drug addiction (emcdda) has concluded that the psychotropic substance 4-methylamphetamine poses health risks. i therefore support the introduction of control measures for this new psychotropic substance.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the council's draft given the clear risk to public health arising from the illegal sale of 4,4'-dmar and mt-45. the first is a derivative of two substances that are already banned, and the second, it has a toxicity much higher than morphine. furthermore, there is no evidence that any of the substances have any medical or other legitimate use. although there is no extensive scientific basis for the harmful effects of these substances, we use the precautionary principle to support their immediate ban.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the council decision calling on the member states to take control measures on the substance known as 5-[2-aminopropyl]indole. according to a scientific risk assessment report this substance can cause tachycardia, hyperthermia, midriasis, agitation and tremors. other than that, it has no known medical value either. the decision also facilitates the exchange of information between member states on these new psychoactive substances and their potential health risks within the eu framework.
in writing. ‒ between april and august 2012, four member states recorded 24 fatalities in which 5-[2-aminopropyl]indole was detected either alone or in combination with other substances in samples taken for autopsy. although it is impossible to determine with certainty the role of 5- ((2-aminopropyl) indole in all fatalities, in some cases it has been recorded as a specific cause of death. if the availability and use of this new psychotropic substance were to become widespread, the consequences for individual and public health could be significant. the available evidence and information is sufficient to justify the subjecting of 5-[2-aminopropyl]indole to control measures across the union. in view of the health risks it poses, as evidenced by its detection in several of the notified fatalities, the fact that it could be inadvertently consumed and the absence of any medical value or use, 5-[2-aminopropyl]indole should be subject to control measures across the union. for all these reasons, i have decided to vote in favour of this decision.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the council decision calling on the member states to subject to control measures substances known as 25i nbome, ah-7921, mdpv and methoxetamine. these substances are being sold illegally as drugs or substitutes for other more well-known drugs without consumers being properly informed of the health risks they pose, as they have been associated with several deaths in several member states. many member states have already taken control measures on this substance. the decision also makes it easier for them to exchange information on these new psychoactive substances and their potential health risks within the eu.
in writing. ‒ four deaths associated with 25i-nbome have been recorded in three member states, with 32 cases of non-fatal poisoning reported. if the availability and use of this new psychotropic substance were to increase, the consequences for individual and public health could be significant. there are no data on the prevalence of consumption of this substance, but the limited information available suggests that it may be consumed in a wide range of settings, including the home, bars, nightclubs and music festivals. 25i-nbome is openly marketed and sold online as a 'research chemical', and information from seizures, samples collected, consumer websites and online retailers suggests that it is sold as a medicine itself, and that it is also marketed as an 'illicit' substitute for lsd. the emcdda has identified more than 15 online retailers selling this substance that may be based in the union and in china. i believe that the evidence and information available are sufficient grounds to subject it to control measures throughout the union, and i have therefore voted in favour of this decision.

in writing. ‒ between june 2013 and june 2014, 31 deaths related to 4,4'-dmar were recorded in three member states, 28 deaths related to the presence of mt-45 in biological samples. the risk assessment report reveals that there is little scientific evidence available on 4,4'-dmar and notes that further research is required to determine the health and social risks posed by it. the available information on mt-45 suggests that it is consumed mainly in private, either by users willing to try a new substance or by opioid dependent users who do not have access to heroin or other opioids. the evidence and information currently available are sufficient to subject 4,4'-dmar and mt-45 to control measures across the union. as a consequence of the health risks posed by their use, as evidenced by their detection in several deaths, their possible inadvertent use and the lack of medical value of these substances, 4,4-dmar and mt-45 should be subject to control measures. for these reasons, i have voted in favour of this decision.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the mobilisation of the eu solidarity fund in support of the requests of bulgaria and greece due to the major floods in both countries. in the case of bulgaria, it affected most of the south-east in late january and early february 2015. in greece, evros and central and western regions in february 2015. this aid will enable urgent relief and recovery operations to be carried out. both cases were classified as 'regional disasters' and therefore need this contribution to carry out the operations indicated.
in writing. ‒ the commission proposes to mobilise the eusf to provide financial assistance in relation to one natural disaster in bulgaria (severe winter weather conditions and classified as 'serious natural disaster' according to the eusf) and two in greece (floods in evros and central greece, both classified as 'regional disasters' according to the eusf). all of them from early 2015. i support the adoption of the commission's proposal for a decision because in both cases they meet the eusf criteria because of the nature of the disasters, their enormous scope and their profound impact on local communities and economies; and because the damage has deeply affected the regions, not only public infrastructure but also private property, businesses, farmland and forests. for the general budget of the eu for the financial year 2015, the eusf shall be mobilised to the amount of eur 16 274 765 in commitment and payment appropriations. after deduction of the advances paid equivalent to 10% (eur 637,782 for bulgaria and eur 989,695 for greece), the amount outstanding is eur 14 647,288 (eur 5 740,033 for bulgaria and eur 8 907,255 for greece).

madam president, the european parliament has today called on the european commission to legislate strongly to protect trademarks, especially craft trademarks. the name of products such as albacete knives or talavera de la reina ceramics needs the european commission, its legislative initiative, precisely to not disappear. thousands of jobs and thousands of inhabitants need the european commission's legislative action, precisely to maintain the rural population, jobs and production. the 'made in' is blocked in the council and another of the instruments of protection we have at european level is the geographical indications which are also protected for non-agricultural products. i call on the european commission to take seriously the almost unanimous message sent today by the european parliament and to protect these products, to protect citizens, to protect small businesses, to protect artisans, and to protect them precisely from unfair competition from other parts of the world, which hits them where it hurts the most: in the quality of their products and also in their local and artisanal production.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the rozière report because the extension of the system of protected geographical indications to non-agricultural products would have a great deal of positive repercussions both for the eu as a whole and for spain. firstly, it would create a quality guarantee to protect traditional and artisanal products which are crucial to the economy of certain regions from illegitimate copies which reduce their added value. it would ensure the economic viability of thousands of smes and the maintenance of the jobs they create. it would also provide consumers with additional assurance of the quality and traceability of the products they consume. spain is a testament to the success of the current system of protected geographical indications for agri-food products, and i believe that extending it to non-food products will bring similar benefits at european level in terms of sustainability for smes in these products, employment and consumer protection.
in writing. ‒ i believe that the system of geographical indications for agricultural products has proved to be a positive mechanism for protecting small local producers in certain nations and states currently belonging to the eu. i therefore believe that it is a good thing to extend this system to other types of products than agricultural products, taking into account the experience and lessons learned during this time with agricultural products.

in writing. ‒ the report on the extension of geographical indications in the eu, in which i have personally participated as rapporteur for the epp group and which has been adopted, aims to extend the protection of geographical indications throughout the eu to agricultural products of a clearly defined geographical origin and manufactured using traditional methods, and to extend this protection to the category of non-agricultural products by establishing rules applicable throughout the european single market. in the context of the european single market, it is necessary to harmonise national laws in this area. it is also necessary for public administrations to protect traditional products in order to fight against fraud in these products, and also to incorporate a system of management, inspection, infringement and sanction that controls geographical indications in products marketed in europe. this push for geographical indications is key because it can bring important benefits to the consumer and also to the companies producing these non-agricultural products, which are generally smes.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of an eu protection system based on geographical indications for non-agricultural products. non-agricultural products are an important part of our cultural heritage and an essential part of the economic and social life of many regions of europe. it must be borne in mind that the reputation of a geographical indication is a collective, intangible good which, if not protected, can be used freely and without restriction, leading to a decrease in value and even leading to the loss of the product itself. similarly, it should be borne in mind that harmonised european legislation in this area will always be beneficial for the european union in international trade negotiations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the rozière report because the extension of the system of protected geographical indications to non-agricultural products would have a great deal of positive repercussions both for the eu as a whole and for spain. firstly, it would create a quality guarantee which would protect traditional and craft production types which are crucial to the economy of certain regions from illegitimate copies which reduce their added value, strengthen the economic viability of thousands of smes and ensure the maintenance of the jobs associated with them. it would also provide consumers with additional assurance of the quality and traceability of the products they consume. spain is a testament to the success of the current system of protected geographical indications for agri-food products, and i believe that extending it to non-food products will bring similar benefits at european level in terms of sustainability for smes in these products, employment and consumer protection.

in writing. ‒ i voted today in favour of this initiative which calls on the european commission to implement a european system for the protection of local know-how by creating geographical indications for non-agricultural products. such protection would not only help to recognise and make more visible local crafts by recalling the link between production and territory, but also protect these traditions against imitation and counterfeiting. the report also stresses the importance of preserving traditional skills and know-how, which contribute to the attractiveness of the territories and their cultural impact.
in writing. ‒ this report on protected geographical indications concerns non-agricultural products, such as laguiole knives, calais lace, etc. these indications promote traditional and local know-how, offering the consumer guarantees of quality. at present, these indications exist, but as the report states, they are fragmented: 'some member states do not offer any specific protection, others have established different definitions, procedures and different levels of protection ...'. it is therefore necessary to remain vigilant as to the real intentions of the promoters of this report, who, when they refer to the present system, accuse it of causing distortions and hindering the 'unified development of the common market'. the report put to the vote calls on the commission to present a single system for the protection of these geographical indications, accompanied by a single european register, which could, in the long run, mean that it would be impossible for the states to create new non-agricultural geographical indications without the consent of the european union. in the end, we will judge the tree by its fruit: either the commission develops these geographical indications to protect jobs in europe, or it sacrifices to american requirements, in the framework of the transatlantic treaty, and limits this protection.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the possible extension of the protection of geographical indications of the european union to non-agricultural products. this type of indication has historically existed for agricultural products, thus attempting to satisfy the protection of products of priority interest to the primary sectors of the respective countries. the extension to other types of products is interesting, taking as a basis the experience gained in agricultural products. we still believe that this requires detailed analyses of each sector for which geographical indications could be created.

in writing. ‒ greece has been hit by the consequences of the financial crisis in a unique way. this has led to an exceptional situation which has been deemed necessary to address by specific measures so that the lack of liquidity and of public funds does not hamper investments under the erdf, the esf, the cohesion fund and the emff. i support amending the common provisions regulation to, inter alia, provide for additional pre-financing for the 2014-2020 cohesion policy operational programmes under the investment for growth and jobs goal, as well as to allow the ceiling of the cumulative total of pre-financing and interim payments to be 100% and to increase to 100% the co-financing rate of the 2007-2013 operational programmes under the convergence and regional competitiveness and employment objectives. this will allow greece to advance the distribution of over €2 billion and possible savings of around another €2 billion, to finish the projects in progress and to reimburse the beneficiaries of the funds so that they can make the planned investments and be reimbursed immediately after submitting their payment applications.
in writing. ‒ this is a european parliament position adopted at first reading so that the greek state can obtain short-term advantages in its financing by advancing part of the payments budgeted in the 2014-2020 structural and cohesion funds, increasing the co-financing ceiling and implementing the outstanding payments of the 2007-2013 framework. it is estimated that these measures will have a positive impact on greek public finances of some eur 2 billion, a tiny fraction compared to the eur 260 billion that greece has had to borrow from the troika institutions (imf, european central bank, and european commission) in exchange for measures that have deepened the impoverishment of greek society. moreover, they do not represent an extra disbursement by the european institutions but an advance on the budget for the years 2018 and 2020 respectively. despite this necessary general criticism of european economic policy, the proposal allows the greek government to receive an extra liquidity in the short term and, as it is not a solution in itself to the economic problems arising from the contraction of public spending, i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ greece has been hit by the consequences of the financial crisis in a unique way. this has led to an exceptional situation which has been deemed necessary to address by specific measures so that the lack of liquidity and of public funds does not hamper investments under the erdf, the esf, the cohesion fund and the emff. i support amending the common provisions regulation to, inter alia, provide for additional pre-financing for the 2014-2020 cohesion policy operational programmes under the investment for growth and jobs goal, as well as to allow the ceiling of the cumulative total of pre-financing and interim payments to be 100% and to increase to 100% the co-financing rate of the 2007-2013 operational programmes under the convergence and regional competitiveness and employment objectives. this will allow greece to advance the distribution of over €2 billion and possible savings of around another €2 billion, to finish the projects in progress and to reimburse the beneficiaries of the funds so that they can make the planned investments and be reimbursed immediately after submitting their payment applications.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the european structural and investment funds in the case of greece, because we have thereby supported a €35 billion investment plan to improve greece's competitiveness, including €20 billion from the structural and investment funds and €15 billion from the agricultural funds. support for this initiative will allow for the swift adoption of the measures by the council of the union and their immediate entry into force. the decision ensures that these extraordinary funds for greece from the 2007-2013 programming period are made available in time, before it expires in 2017, and will also help greece to meet the necessary requirements to access the community funds allocated in the current 2014-2020 period.

in writing. ‒ this is a european parliament position adopted at first reading so that the greek state can obtain short-term advantages in its financing by advancing part of the payments budgeted in the 2014-2020 structural and cohesion funds, increasing the co-financing ceiling and implementing the outstanding payments of the 2007-2013 framework. it is estimated that these measures will have a positive impact on greek public finances of some eur 2 billion, a tiny fraction compared to the eur 260 billion that greece has had to borrow from the troika institutions (imf, european central bank, and european commission) in exchange for measures that have deepened the impoverishment of greek society. moreover, they do not represent an extra disbursement by the european institutions but an advance on the budget for the years 2018 and 2020 respectively. despite this necessary general criticism of european economic policy, the proposal allows the greek government to receive an extra liquidity in the short term and, as it is not a solution in itself to the economic problems arising from the contraction of public spending, i have decided to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report because of the urgent need for public investment in the greek economy to boost a sustainable recovery. however, given the difficult financial situation of greece, it is essential that the eu ensures that the lack of liquidity and public funds in greece does not hamper investments under programmes financed by the european regional development fund, the european social fund (esf) and the cohesion fund, and by the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff).
in writing. ‒ greece has been hit by the consequences of the financial crisis in a unique way. this has led to an exceptional situation which has required specific measures to prevent the lack of liquidity and public funds from hindering investment under the erdf, the esf, the cohesion fund and the emff. i voted in favour of amending the structural funds regulation to allow for additional pre-financing to be granted to cohesion policy operational programmes in the period 2014-2020 under the investment for growth and jobs goal, to allow the ceiling for the cumulative total of pre-financing and interim payments to be 100%, and to increase to 100% the co-financing rate for the 2007-2013 operational programmes under the convergence and regional competitiveness and employment objectives. this will allow greece to advance the distribution of over €2 billion and possible savings of around another €2 billion, to finish the projects in progress and to reimburse the beneficiaries of the funds so that they can make the planned investments and be reimbursed immediately after submitting their payment applications.

in writing. ‒ the liquidity problems of the athens government put at risk the financing of all projects for the period 2014-2020. that is why i voted in favour of this report, which provides in particular for a derogation concerning the prefinancing and cofinancing of projects financed by the european cohesion and structural funds for the benefit of greece, in order to support it in its economic and social situation.
in writing. ‒ the specific measures for greece consist of prefinancing and co-financing the greek operational programmes, so that the country can benefit from the european structural and investment funds without having to advance sums that are not available to it. for example, co-financing will reach 100% for the 2007-2013 programmes. at this level of co-financing, it is more appropriate to speak of a 'donation' to greece than of co-financing. it is clear that this particular scheme is at the expense of the other member states which contribute to the eu budget. it may also encourage other member states to apply similar measures. in particular, the discussions in committee have highlighted the risk that these funds will be allocated to programmes aimed at facilitating the reception and integration of illegal migrants on greek territory. in that case, far from promoting the development of greece, these funds will serve to impoverish it and, at the same time, all of europe.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this legislative act, which will free up european structural and investment funds for greece, modify the provisions of the cohesion policies and increase eu funding to 100% in the period 2007-2013 (eliminating the need for co-financing), disburse 5% of the budget immediately and improve the conditions for pre-financing for projects in 2015 and 2016, thus providing liquidity to the greek government. these funds are not given under the memoranda, although the negotiation process and questions about the government's solvency had blocked some items.

in writing. ‒ the exceptional situation facing greece in recent years has made it necessary to address the problems of lack of liquidity and public funds by the greek government with specific measures, so that they do not hamper investments under programmes financed by the erdf, the european social fund (esf), the cohesion fund and the european maritime and fisheries fund (emff). the commission therefore proposes that the regulation on common provisions for these funds be amended to approve various financial measures which make the conditions for implementing operational programmes and projects linked to these structural funds in greece more flexible. we have voted in favour of this measure.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mobilising the european globalisation adjustment fund in the case of adam opel in germany. the german authorities declared the complete closure of the production plant in bochum due to the global economic and financial crisis explaining the decrease by 25% in the registration of vehicles registered between 2007-2015. this is the 13th application under examination under the 2015 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 6 958 623 and concerns 2 692 workers out of the 2 881 workers made redundant at adam opel and supplier.
in writing. ‒ the report refers to the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 6 958 623 from the egf for germany for the 2 881 redundancies at adam opel ag (bochum, north rhine-westphalia), which operates in the motor vehicle, trailer and semi-trailer manufacturing sector. the measures for redundant workers covered by this application include vocational training measures, career guidance, workshops, business creation advisory service, job search, job fairs, mentoring services and post-employment advice and training allowance. i therefore support this ep report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund: application egf/2015/002 de/adam opel. europe and the world are engaged in a profound process of globalisation which, while a source of trade and wealth creation, can also entail risks to which we must be very attentive. as a result of this process, there are sectors which are more exposed to international competition, and the eu must therefore respond to those citizens who lose their jobs as a result of globalisation. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) provides support for workers who lose their jobs as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns caused by globalisation or the global economic and financial crisis.
in writing. ‒ i gave my support to this european globalisation adjustment fund application in favour of germany. the funding application of automobile manufacturer adam opel ag is well merited given the difficult conditions created by the financial crisis in terms of a twenty record drop in car sales. this was compounded by a decision by its parent company, general motors, to disallow the export of their vehicles to any market outside europe. therefore, i fully support this approval of this financial instrument which gives redundant workers the tools to be once again reintegrated into the workforce.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the mobilisation of this new part of the egf, following our traditional position: we cannot oppose the financial implementation of commitments that have already been made and which ultimately help to alleviate a situation of lack of protection for workers affected by the closure of companies, but we do not for that reason consider that this fund not only does not solve at all the impacts of the policies of deindustrialisation and massive labour flexibility imposed by the neoliberal model applied in europe today, but legitimises it, by alleviating its direct and immediate effects.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of mobilising the european globalisation adjustment fund in the case of ford genk in belgium. the belgian authorities claim that the closure of the plant in genk is the reason for the redundancies and link this to profound structural changes in international trade patterns caused by globalisation and the loss of market share by the european automotive industry. this is the 14th application examined under the 2015 budget and concerns the mobilisation of a total amount of eur 6 268 564 and concerns 4 500 workers out of the 5 111 workers made redundant at ford genk and 11 suppliers or converters.
in writing. ‒ this report relates to a financial contribution of eur 6 268 564 from the egf following the 5 111 redundancies at ford genk (belgium) and at 11 suppliers or converters in the motor vehicle, trailer and semi-trailer manufacturing sector. with this application, and to date, this sector has been the subject of 22 egf applications, 11 of them based on the globalisation of trade and 10 on the global financial and economic crisis. this application covers three types of measures for covered redundant workers: individual assistance in job search, case management and general information services, training and retraining, and compensation and incentives. in 2013, a first wave of redundancies at ford genk resulted in a first application to the egf and the second application concerns the redundancies carried out by the ford genk plant in 2014 until the final closure of the plant in december 2014. i therefore support this ep report.

madam president, i have supported this report. i'm from the czech republic, which supports and is active in supporting developing countries. it should be noted that for the next period 2014-2020 the contribution of the czech republic to the european development fund is being doubled. we are naturally concerned and concerned about the efficiency of the money we give to third countries. this report can certainly contribute to this, since it clearly states that more cooperation is needed with local authorities, not just central governments, in the allocation and use of this money, because in certain cases, as we have discussed in the plenary on several occasions, the use of the money is often controversial and the question is how much of it ends up with the final recipients, those who need it and who are to be helped. so, greater involvement of local authorities, which is the philosophy of this report, is the right thing to do. i welcome it, and that's why i supported the report.
in writing. ‒ i did not vote in favour of this report because it promotes the development of public-private partnerships as a central part of the role of local authorities in the poorest countries. we reject this type of consortium because we understand that this investment model makes it impossible to carry out a real project to improve the living conditions of the majority of the population in the impoverished countries in the medium and long term and seeks to secure the profits of large corporations at the cost of transferring the risk of their investments to the public sector. however, i abstained on the grounds that the report includes positive aspects on the need to develop public services at local level, the strengthening of the role of local authorities to achieve greater gender equality quotas or the promotion of social organisations to achieve truly inclusive development.
in writing. ‒ local authorities are the key state actor in achieving the sustainable development goals which have just been adopted in new york and which will form the new global development agenda for the next 15 years. its role in protecting vulnerable populations in middle-income countries, and especially in fragile states in crisis, is essential. the report proposes to strengthen the decentralisation of development cooperation and to set up innovative partnerships to ensure positive results in the implementation of the new development agenda, the conclusions of the climate change summit. the urgent need to integrate local authorities as full agents in the implementation of the european development fund and the development cooperation instrument should be emphasized. it also includes the establishment of a partnership between the european union and local authorities, and encourages collaboration agreements between local authorities in the member states and local authorities in developing countries in areas such as training and human capacity. i therefore support this report.

in writing. ‒ local authorities play a key role in achieving the millennium development goals, in particular in the fight against poverty and in the delivery of community services such as water sanitation, healthcare and education. they should be at the centre of the implementation of the international development policy. i welcome this report that recalls the importance of the local dimension for development and that encourages the spread of decentralised development cooperation initiatives and the use of mechanisms for cooperation among cities in order to achieve these goals.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report on the role of local authorities in developing countries in cooperation. the report assumes that governance improvement requires encouraging governments in developing countries to transfer part of their national budgetary resources to regional and local authorities. the rapporteur considers that decentralisation is an effective means of combating corruption, including that of multinational companies, and would contribute to the modernisation of public administration. there is reason to doubt that this is the case, given the experience of european countries, which shows that decentralisation does not really limit corruption. it has also led to a drift in public finances and an administrative maze that is incomprehensible to citizens. finally, it is undeniable that this project constitutes an interference in the way in which states are organized.
in writing. ‒ we abstained because although the report includes positive language on public services, the role of civil society and gender issues, the report identifies the private sector as an essential partner - through instruments such as blending and public-private partnerships - for development. we believe that this may open the door to the privatization of development cooperation policy. furthermore, we believe that the report will have little or no impact on cooperation policy coming at a time when the regulatory and financial aspects of the new 2030 development framework have already been internationally agreed and approved.

the question of the 'blue card'. i would like to ask our colleague on what basis he says that other car manufacturers have done the same. do you have any information about that? how can he make such claims, which generate a shadow of doubt and a general distrust in the whole european automobile industry, without 'in principle' having any evidence or data? i'd like to know how you can make that assessment.
ladies and gentlemen, it seems that the european commission has known since 2011 that the emissions controls of volkswagen cars were not showing reliable figures and no one has acted to prevent it. ladies and gentlemen, we are facing a new and shameful scandal, already known as dieselgate, which cannot be left as a mere corrective or a sanction to the irresponsible automobile industry, its lobbies, and also - why not say it - to its institutional backers. the volkswagen fraud case is yet another example of the crisis in the production, energy and transport models which undermine the ecological basis of our survival, violate our rights as consumers, cost hundreds of thousands of jobs and - why hide it - also the lives of hundreds of europeans through pollution. we will demand accountability for this and for all the corruption cases that have shaken and shake this predatory capitalism that most of you continue to support in this house.
mr president, 'at volkswagen we are not content to build cars with less co2, we have developed a global attitude towards ecological sustainability'. this is what volkswagen's website says today. not only have they been violating european legislation on polluting emissions since at least 2008, but they also boast the opposite, sell sustainability and respect for the environment and, now that the scandal threatens to reduce the profits of their managers, they act with blackmail and threats about their production in europe. the question at stake is whether the european commission will take strong action or whether, on the contrary, the european commission will continue to act as it is told by the lobbyists of the car industry, putting its interests above our health and that of the planet. let us not be mistaken: the european commission was aware of what was happening and has been covering it up. today, a committee of inquiry must be sent to all the companies because it may not be just volkswagen. on the contrary, if such a committee of inquiry is not set up, the message is that the big, the powerful, the german multinationals do not have to comply with the law.
mr president, commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the european union has set itself the ambitious target of having 20% of our gross domestic product come from industry by the year 2020. we also have the objective - as it could not be otherwise - of reducing co2 emissions. to achieve these objectives, we need to improve our competitiveness. and to improve our competitiveness, reforms are key, both at national and european level. there is no doubt that the automobile industry is key to achieving this ambitious 20% target, and i believe that no one in this house doubts that volkswagen is key within the automobile industry. because volkswagen has almost 500,000 workers in the european union, many of them in spain, many of them in my region, in navarre. so it's key to keep looking. we must investigate and go as far as necessary, we must go as far as we have to go, but it is also important, ladies and gentlemen, not to prejudge. it is also key not to jump to any preconceived or hasty conclusions. it's key to be cautious with unsubstantiated speculation. the prestige and reputation of european industry, which is the key to achieving the desired 20% target, is at stake. i therefore appeal to everyone's responsibility. there's a lot at stake. the answer is 'blue card'. mr urban, no one has said otherwise. if you had read the press, you would have seen that the minister for industry, mr soria, has demanded accountability and has asked to see this matter through to the end. but i would also encourage you, mr urbán, to take care of the 500 000 workers in europe, many of whom - as i said - are in spain, many of whom are in catalonia and many of whom are in navarre, and we all have to take care of them here.

member of the commission, on behalf of the vice—president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy. – mr president, libya is at a critical juncture. the situation on the ground has continued to deteriorate. the number of internally displaced civilians has increased. in several areas – notably in a number of benghazi neighbourhoods – we are facing a serious humanitarian crisis. health and educational services have been disrupted: many hospitals and schools are now barely functioning. oil production is at its lowest, cash reserves are fast being depleted and the government is cutting subsidies. the libyan dinar has tragically devalued. as a result, there have been shortages of basic goods such as flour, and the price of bread and other staples has climbed. the security situation has also deteriorated. the ceasefires established locally are welcome but are not enough. there is little law or order. in many cities crime takes place with impunity. this has also facilitated the continued trafficking of migrants by criminal gangs. libya’s southern border is essentially open. too many lives are put at risk at sea in unsafe boats. more and more libyans themselves are trying to move abroad. both tunisia and egypt have been very welcoming and supportive but many libyan families there, having used up most of their savings, find it impossible to make ends meet. the majority of libyans are sick of the conflict. the war has only benefited terrorist groups like daesh. they represent a threat that cannot be ignored. they prosper thanks to the war and the divisions of libyan society. when they do not manage to ally with local militias, they struggle to keep control on the ground. last summer they lost derna but they managed to put down a rebellion in sirte, a key city on the motorway connecting tripoli and benghazi, and the terrorist threat extends not just to libya but to neighbouring countries. this is yet another reason to push for a national unity government – a government that can put the greatest number of militias under the authority of the state institutions. there has been progress in the political process. the un special envoy, bernardino león, with our full and active support, is doing all he can to bring together the government of the national assembly in tobruk and the rival gnc in tripoli. last week, in new york at the un general assembly, the international community showed its unanimous support for leon’s efforts, in front of representatives of both factions and of civil society. we urged both sides to sign the negotiated agreements. in new york we witnessed something new and encouraging, finally. the whole international community, including all libya’s neighbours, shared the same views on the way forward. this is in part a result of the active lobbying by the european union and its member states. the european union has played an important role in getting the process this far. we have worked day and night – literally – to support the perspective of a government of national accord. now the international community is united on this: it is the libyans who have to take responsibility now and form a government to put an end to their country’s collapse. we know very well that even if a government of national accord were formed, change in libya would not happen overnight. it might take time for the situation to improve, even if we get all the main parties to sign this agreement. but it would create an opportunity for improvement. it will not be a conclusion, but a starting point. let me set out what the european union’s strategic objectives are and the action we are currently taking – and preparing to take – to achieve them. we want security, stability, accountable government and the rule of law in libya. the people there deserve to live in peace and have their human rights respected. we want the libyan economy to flourish once again, and also their commerce with the european union, and we want the traffickers who prey on the desperate to be finally brought to book. our initial efforts to help libya establish control of its borders and build stronger institutions can only start once we have a deal and we have a new government to work with. but we stand ready, as we pledged to all parties in new york last week, to launch a support package worth eur 100 million as soon as a political agreement is reached. this would include a range of measures funded from the european union’s programme budget for libya as well as the instrument contributing to stability and peace (icsp). this money will help rebuild libya’s institutions. it will encourage dialogue between the country’s different groups, support local governance, civil society and of course the media. it will help allow people to get their lives back to normal, helping with the delivery of basic services, including health. we will assist the ministries most concerned with helping to manage migration. we will support smes and employment opportunities to give a chance to libya’s youth and put the country back on track. this will be in addition to the humanitarian aid we are already providing for the most urgent needs of the most vulnerable people. we are undertaking planning work to help provide a secure environment for a government of national accord and the european union is assisting the united nations support mission in libya (unsmil) with a planning cell based in tunis. we are also working with the un on longer term planning to assist the new government in other sectors and we intend to play a prominent role in all the joint working groups. working groups from both the international community and the libyan government are being set up right now. but now it is up to the libyan parties to make a move: the decisive one. no—one can take this decision in their place. i know how much this house has always been supportive of a political agreement. i am sure it will continue to play a key role to help the parties reach a stable solution. it is now high time that parties show leadership, take on their responsibilities and sign the agreement. it is time for libya to get back on its feet.
on behalf of the alde group. mr president, mr commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, the proposal for an agreement which we now have on the table is probably the last chance for the two factions to lay the foundations for a ceasefire and for the formation of a government of national unity which will make it possible to move forward with the pacification of the country and the stabilization of the region. and i'm not saying that, bernardino leon is. to do that, october 20 is the deadline. if a government of national unity is not formed by then, we will have to start negotiations from scratch, and what is worse, a lack of agreement will not only be negative for the libyan population, as it will have regional consequences in the continuation of the process of balkanization of the country, but will also favour the growth of the islamic state. as we speak, daesh is advancing and already controls a coastal strip in libya the size of switzerland. it is militarily organized in both iraq and syria and has access to warplanes and warships. and we are still failing to act, failing to reach agreements vital to the viability of the region, which lies on the southern border of the european union. we can't keep dodging our responsibilities. we must support and exert all possible pressure to bring the negotiations to a successful conclusion and, subsequently, we must offer all possible assistance to the libyan authorities to intervene militarily against the islamic state and prevent its expansion. only then can we lay the foundations for a stable future in the region.

author. mr president, next 10 december is the world day against the death penalty. it is a good time for the european union to reaffirm its international leadership in efforts to abolish the death penalty and in favour of a universal moratorium on executions. where are we at? well, there's a little good news and a lot of bad news. i'll start with the bad ones. fifty-eight countries in the world still retain the death penalty in their legal systems. twenty-two of them carried out executions in 2014. some states apply the death penalty to an alarmingly high number of people. the information, by the way, is very difficult to add, because some countries do not provide data on their executions. this is the case with china and vietnam, very important countries, practically partners of the european union. they hide information that we should be demanding in a very strong way, because, furthermore, the lack of data on china destroys any statistics we need to make a true assessment of the application of the death penalty in the world. so my first conclusion is that the european union must demand from the countries with which it has important relations certain data on the number of executions carried out in accordance with their civil and military laws. the commission also notes that the data on the number of executions in the member states is not available. however, in some specific countries executions have not only not decreased, but have increased in this same period of time. the dishonor chart in terms of executions is led by iran, with 289 executions announced in 2014, and saudi arabia, with 130 executions that same year. by the way, our most precious ally, the united states of america, is very high on the death penalty implementation chart 35 executions in 2014. of the 607 people executed in 2014, 70 percent were executed in just three countries: iraq, iran and saudi arabia. the united states of america, indonesia, japan, malaysia and pakistan executed people with mental, physical and intellectual disabilities in 2014. the second part of my speech is devoted to what we call the 'world death row', that is to say, those sentenced but not yet executed: the condemned who are waiting. in 2014, almost 30% more people were sentenced to death than in 2013. so the global death corridor is not just not decreasing, it's increasing. and we also think that the actual data is far superior to what we know. egypt, with 509; nigeria, with 659; pakistan, with 231; and bangladesh, with 142, lead the ranking of convictions in 2014. egypt and nigeria are seeing a huge increase in the number of such convictions. our ally, the united states of america, is once again at the top of the condemnation list, with 72 death sentences in 2014. in the world, more than 19 000 people were on death row at the end of 2014, of which 8 500 were in pakistan alone, a country which, as you know, has lifted the moratorium it had committed to. this afternoon's debate was prompted by the political groups in the subcommittee on human rights of this parliament. we want to know what measures the european union has taken to move towards the abolition of the death penalty and, in particular, in its bilateral relations with the countries that still apply it, especially those where the number of death sentences is increasing. i would also like to know how far we are prepared to push the institutions of the european union. are we prepared to sacrifice even our negotiating agreements with some countries in order to demand moratorium and abolition? are we ready? some countries are very different from us and it will be very difficult to reach agreements with them, but some are very similar. some share our vision: the united states of america, for example. i think we are legitimate to add - and we can afford to add - to the difficulty of the atci negotiation the moratorium and abolition of the death penalty. you see, this is about saving lives. it is about the european union helping to save lives, fulfilling its commitment to save lives. it also has relations with third countries.

mr president of the european parliament, mr president of the european commission, ladies and gentlemen, i should like to begin my speech in this house by thanking the president of the european parliament for his kind invitation to address me, as king of spain, to your majesty, the legitimate representatives of the european citizens. and thank you, mr. president, for your words and for your generous introduction. i do so as a spaniard who also feels deeply european; i do so in the spirit of the historical heritage that has gone before us and in the conviction that our future lies in the continuation of our great common project of the european union. (applause) for men and women of my generation, europe has always been present in our intellectual and vital development. this presence, this closeness, has given rise to affection, hope and illusions; it has generated a feeling of belonging to the european project whose very being coexists constructively and naturally with our identity as nationals of the member states of the union. this conviction in europe is also born of the clear awareness that the union is the story of an undoubted collective success which, despite its difficulties, has succeeded in an outstanding way in achieving its main and highest objectives. the objectives of peace, harmony and coexistence between nations which, only decades ago, were the protagonists of one of the most devastating and brutal conflicts in world history. the objectives of prosperity and economic growth have made it possible for millions of men and women - and families - on our continent to live and to enjoy levels of material and social well-being unknown in the past. the european union is a great example of the kind of europe that can be built on the foundations of the european union. the faith in europe with which i began my speech is born of the profound european identity of my country. spain and the spanish people are europeans - and you know it - in culture and geography, in history and also in political vocation. it is not possible to conceive of spain without europe, nor europe without spain. and therefore i am european, because i am spanish. (applause) the political, economic and social achievements and the extraordinary projection of spain in recent decades and in all fields could not be understood without the democratic and progressive will of the spanish people and without our firm commitment to european integration. the democratic spain of recent decades has been solidly based on a firm and sincere will to understand one another among the spanish people, a generous and fraternal will. and it is based on our constitution, which is the great pact that defends, preserves and protects the rights and freedoms of citizens, protects the peoples of spain in the exercise of their various cultures and traditions, languages and institutions, and enshrines freedom, justice, equality and political pluralism as essential values of our coexistence. europe was built on the will to add, not to subtract; to unite and not to divide; to share and be in solidarity. so, ladies and gentlemen, you can be sure that you can count on a spain that is loyal and responsible to the european project; a spain that is united and proud of its diversity; a spain that is solidary and respectful of the rule of law. i therefore regard our contribution to the prosperity of the european union and to this union as one of the most important political achievements in recent human history. on the other hand, spain's membership of the european union has made a decisive contribution to the further economic and social development of our country. this year we are celebrating the 30th anniversary of spain's accession to the european communities. the 'return of spain to europe' - if i may use this expression - is seen as the culmination of a great collective project that began with the enlightenment of the 18th century and was felt intensely from the end of the 19th century. the ideas of regeneration and modernisation across europe - very present in the last century in ortega y gasset and madariaga - were linked in the 1960s to the path towards the democratization of my country. europe has thus been one of the great basic consensus of spanish society. it has been the horizon of democracy and also of economic modernisation and social and political regeneration of our country; and it continues to be so today. europe is where we spaniards wanted to be, where we deserved to be and where we will always remain. spaniards have always had a trusting attitude towards the idea of europe. my country has received a great deal from the union, that is certain, but it has also made a significant contribution to the community project and to the construction of europe. spain has always shown its european vocation, with crucial contributions in areas as diverse as european citizenship, cohesion policy, the ladies and gentlemen, the european project, which was born more than 60 years ago, is in fact creating an area of peace, prosperity, freedom, justice and solidarity of which we can all be rightly proud. however, what has been done so far cannot lead to complacency or conformity. nothing is won forever. we cannot lose sight of the future, nor allow ourselves to stand still or to retreat in the face of difficulties or challenges which are great and which therefore require a new political impetus. it is true that at the end of the 20th century europe embodied the utopia inspired by the ideals of reconciliation, peace and shared prosperity, which were put into practice by the founding fathers in the 1950s. but today europeans must identify - beyond the preservation of what has been achieved and the overcoming of everyday challenges - new and lofty objectives, new and great goals which will give strength and enthusiasm to the european project, both from within, the result of the convergence between the leadership of the leadership and the drive and sensitivity of all our fellow citizens, and from outside, in our common external projection. for the european union to regain its prominence in the world, it is necessary to formulate a new ideal, a new european purpose that mobilizes citizens in favour of integration and the project of unity. in this sense, the consequences of the economic and financial crisis on our societies and the social and political challenges it has generated should make us reflect and lead us to decisive and effective action to strengthen the european project, an irreplaceable and vital project for all. the strengthening of the democratic legitimacy of the community project is therefore a fundamental element and a fundamental necessity. out in 1943: 'the countries of europe are too small to ensure their peoples the prosperity and social advances they need.' in this respect, and from an institutional perspective, it is worth noting that the european parliament has assumed a decisive leadership and offers a powerful political impetus towards community integration. it would be impossible to understand this project of political and democratic integration, as a union of states and citizens, without the european parliament. but everyone - member states and community institutions - has a role to play in strengthening good governance in the union, respecting independence and the separation of powers, ensuring transparency and accountability and, ultimately, bringing citizens closer to decision-making. the identification seems clear that we must go further in strengthening economic and monetary union. in this context, the institutional framework we have established must be supplemented by mechanisms which strengthen financial solidarity and make it possible, through control and surveillance, to prevent past excesses. in the near future, we must continue to push for a rigorous framework for budgetary coordination and supervision; move forward with the introduction of euro area-specific budgetary mechanisms; deepen the banking union to overcome the effective fragmentation of financial markets; and, above all, in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which establishes a european small claims procedure and aims to simplify and speed up litigation in small claims cases in crossborder cases and to reduce costs. it was specifically designed to help consumers and small and medium-sized enterprises to recover debts, thereby ensuring access to justice.
in writing. ‒ the european small claims procedure is designed to simplify and speed up small claims litigation in civil and commercial matters and to reduce costs. this is a reform of particular importance for smes, which will be able to use the mechanism to solve their problems in the transnational arena more quickly and at lower cost, but it is also relevant for citizens, in matters such as consumer disputes. thanks to the socialist leadership, this agreement was concluded during the latvian presidency, and included particularly positive aspects such as, among others, the increase in the threshold to €5 000 with a five-year review clause to analyse the possibility of a further increase in the future; the promotion of the use of telecommunications and videoconferencing for hearings and free assistance for the use of the procedure. i have therefore voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ the approximately 150,000 medium combustion plants in the eu are a major source of sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter emissions, with serious consequences for human health and the environment. the objective of this directive is to control and reduce emissions of sulphur, nitrogen and particulate matter. the agreement reached with the council sets a ceiling for emissions of sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter from existing combustion plants with a thermal output of more than 5 mw, which will come into force from 2025. the commission will also consider the possibility of extending the scope of the directive to include the use of renewable energy sources. the legislation does not prevent member states from tightening the standards required by the directive. the agreement reached with the council is good for further improving the quality of the air we breathe in europe and that is why i have voted in favour of it.

mr president, i voted in favour of this regulation. at first sight, it may seem that this is a complex administrative regulation that will complicate the lives of citizens and businesses. but the opposite is true. i am convinced that the unification of standards for caseins, the establishment of clear conditions for their moisture content and composition will, on the contrary, lead to uniform rules for the food industry throughout the european union. these are standards drawn up and accepted by international specialized organizations. i think it's going to help the industry, it's going to help the individual consumer, because they're going to have confidence that the caseins and the caseinates are meeting the quality that they're putting on them, say, these very technical standards. overall, it is another way of breaking down internal barriers in the internal market of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the directive of the european parliament and of the council on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption. i think it introduces more regulation on these substances and positive progress on the original proposal in terms of providing consumers with the right information. the products covered by the proposal (caseins and caseinates) are not intended for sale to the final consumer but only between food processing undertakings, but it is important that citizens have all the information they need on the labelling of the final products. the proposal therefore includes provisions on the labelling of caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption. where the required information is not provided on the packaging, containers or labels, these products may not be placed on the market as food caseins or caseinates or used in the preparation of food.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this legislative resolution repealing council directive 83/417/eec and adopting a new directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to caseins and caseinates intended for human consumption. parliament's work has enabled it to improve the commission's text, focusing on providing sufficient food information for the final consumer in business-to-business relationships; to update the definition of 'casein' through a technical update; to introduce a specific label for caseinates exceeding the minimum composition requirements for milk proteins set out in the annex to the directive; to propose that the power to adopt delegated acts to adapt the annexes to international standards be conferred on the commission not for an unlimited period of time but for up to five years or to propose an ambitious, albeit realistic, date for the implementation of this directive in the member states (12 months after the entry into force of this directive).

in writing. ‒ council directive 83/417/eec calls for the approximation of the laws of the member states concerning certain lactoproteins (caseins and caseinates) intended for human consumption. since the entry into force of the directive, several changes have taken place, in particular the development of a comprehensive legal framework in the field of food law and the adoption of an international standard by the food code for edible casein. in the interests of clarity, directive 83/417/eec should be repealed and replaced by a new directive. the proposal seeks to empower the commission in the new legal context created by the lisbon treaty. it also takes account of the development of legislation in recent years. i voted in favour of the proposal.
in writing. ‒ among other objectives, this report seeks to bring the compositional requirements for food caseins into line with international standards. this is very important, since it will ensure a level playing field for food business operators on the world market. on the other hand, food shall be correctly labelled indicating the casein and caseinates content so that consumers, and in particular those suffering from food intolerances or allergies, can make informed choices. i therefore consider that to be a positive proposal and have voted accordingly.

in writing. ‒ this report proposes to adapt the financial regulation to the provisions of the new directives on public procurement and on the award of concession contracts. a number of changes are introduced, such as the new innovation partnership procedure, the introduction of compliance with labour, social and environmental legislation as a core requirement and the award methodology based on the most economically advantageous tender. it is important to note that works and service concessions are added to this financial regulation, which are subject to the same types of procedures as public contracts. the articles on exclusion have also been amended. the grounds for exclusion are clarified and brought into line with the directive, as well as the possibility for the economic operator concerned to take corrective action. in order to avoid confusion, exclusion is clearly separated from the dismissal of a given procedure. a number of provisions have also been introduced to respond to clarifications and simplifications in the text. the provisions on public procurement have been revised in order to ensure consistency in the terminology used in the title and to clarify certain rules. i therefore support this ep report.

in writing. ‒ the proposed european small claims procedure aims to simplify and speed up litigation in small claims proceedings in crossborder cases and to reduce costs. in particular, it is designed to help consumers and small and medium-sized enterprises (smes) to recover their debts and thus ensure access to justice. several surveys have shown that a high percentage of companies involved in crossborder litigation do not go to court, either because of the disproportionate costs of legal proceedings in relation to the amount of the claim or because the process would take too long. the report therefore aims to further reduce the costs and duration of proceedings and to facilitate the procedures for the parties involved. i therefore support this report and have voted in favour of it, in view of the benefits that such measures will have in resolving such disputes.
