in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a technical change which will ensure the proper functioning of the different funds managed by the european commission. the report seeks to adjust the changes in revenue in the eu budget generated by the agreements with the united kingdom, in addition to the increase in own resources raised by the commission to improve the allocations of certain items. these include various funds for development cooperation through external action and funds for the functioning of the office of the body of european regulators for electronic communications. as this is a technical change to ensure the proper functioning of the funds, i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report taking note of amending budget no 6/2015 presented by the commission and of the council's position. compared to the initial 2015 budget, national gni-based budget contributions can be reduced by eur 2 260 million thanks to traditional own resources revenues exceeding the forecasts by eur 1 133,5 million. this technical adjustment of the revenue of the union budget is based on recent statistical developments and is in line with the agreed distribution among the member states.
in writing. ‒ draft amending budget no 6/2015 includes a revision of the provisions on traditional own resources, vat and gni bases, the budgeting of the relevant uk corrections and their financing, all of which involve a change in the distribution of member states' contributions to the eu budget. it also includes the creation of two new budget lines for the expenditure supporting the trust funds managed by the european commission in the fields of development and cooperation and enlargement respectively, and introduces a change in the staff of the berec office, without affecting the total number of posts and its budget. as stated in the report, none of the elements of the draft amending budget has an impact on the expenditure of the 2015 budget, while in terms of revenue it only implies a change in the distribution of contributions between member states. i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the revision of the revenue from traditional own resources financing the budget resulted in revenue exceeding the forecast of eur 2 600 million (mainly from sugar taxes and customs duties). it also provides for corrections of errors in the united kingdom's calculation of its own internal national income (which meant that it contributed less than it should have) and for compensation. this means that almost all member states will have to contribute less resources, since it is stipulated that an increase in these revenues leads to a lower need for contribution. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ the amendment to the budget aims to mobilise european funds to meet the urgent needs of migrants in the european union. although i share the concern about the situation of these people and support the idea of giving more resources to the office for refugee support, it seems to me to be a huge hypocrisy that, at the same time, more resources are approved for frontex and europol. i believe that the policies of the european union and the action of its frontex agency have a lot to do with the humanitarian emergency we are currently witnessing, and reinforcing the instruments of a strong europe can in no way help to improve the situation. i abstained in order not to give my tacit support to the criminal policies of the european union on migration and asylum.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this motion for a resolution to support the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument for an amount of eur 66.1 million in commitment appropriations as the 2015 ceiling for heading 3 does not allow adequate funding for important and urgent political priorities of the union, such as the refugee crisis.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it gives the green light to the mobilisation of eur 66.1 million from the flexibility instrument for immediate measures to respond to refugee crises. the funds will be used to provide emergency assistance to the member states most affected, to increase the staff of eu agencies on the front line and to provide humanitarian assistance and assistance in third countries. on the eve of the eu summit of heads of state and government which will deal with this issue, the spanish socialist delegation reminds us that large agreements on the resettlement of refugees are useless unless they are accompanied by money to finance immediate measures. the current crisis management by the twenty-eight has been totally inadequate and its ineffectiveness has affected the eu's credibility on our ability to deal with the number of refugees coming to europe. we must show the public what the eu can do and we therefore welcome the broad support in this house for the gardiazabal rubial report. parliament has shown that there is the political will and the resources to respond to this crisis.
in writing. ‒ council regulation (eu) no 1311/2013 of 2 december 2013 establishing the multiannual financial framework for the period 2014-2020 allows the flexibility instrument to be used to finance clearly defined expenditure which cannot be financed within the available ceilings under one or more headings of the multiannual financial framework. having examined all possibilities for reallocating appropriations and having exhausted any unallocated margin under the heading of expenditure on security and citizenship (heading 3), the commission proposes to mobilise the flexibility instrument for an amount of eur 66,1 million above the ceiling of heading 3 of the multiannual financial framework. the payment appropriations corresponding to the proposal to mobilise the flexibility instrument amount to eur 52,9 million in 2016 and eur 13,2 million in 2017 and are intended to finance support for measures to manage the refugee crisis, which is why, as rapporteur, i have proposed to the european parliament to proceed with the utmost urgency to allow the funds to be released as soon as possible.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour and this should be read in conjunction with the following draft amending budget (no 7/2015). the flexibility instrument allows for the redistribution of resources, which in this case address the refugee crisis.

in writing. ‒ draft amending budget no 7/2015, together with the request for mobilisation of the flexibility instrument, are combined requirements operating within an urgent and exceptional procedure to transfer resources to the emergency aid reserve in response to humanitarian aid needs expressed by unhcr, the world food programme and other relevant organisations to help refugees and migrants immediately. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the union's macro-financial assistance in the context of the union's macro-financial assistance. it should be borne in mind that i voted in favour because the overall balance is that most of the resources are allocated to urgently needed and immediate humanitarian aid, although some will be allocated to security, border control and return initiatives. the place where the functions of frontex or europol should be changed is in other committees, in particular in the libe committee, where further work will have to be done to change the non-humanitarian functions they perform.

in writing. ‒ these proposals foresee the reinforcement of the emergency assistance provided under the asylum, integration and migration fund (amif) by eur 80 million and the internal security fund (isf) borders by eur 20 million. furthermore the proposals provide for 120 additional posts to increase the capacity of three agencies: 60 posts for frontex, 30 for easo and 30 for europol for 2015. further reinforcement is foreseen for a number of external measures as well (additional funding in commitments for the european neighbourhood instrument and additional payments for humanitarian aid). eh bildu opposes the additional staff for frontex, easo and europol; indeed, our coalition opposes the nature of those agencies. nevertheless for the time being, the main issue with this vote is to try to get the necessary funding available in time to provide nurturing and healthcare for migrants and refugees before the end of the month. hence, eh bildu voted in favour of the immediate budgetary measures under the european agenda on migration.
in writing. ‒ on 23 september 2015, member states adopted the decision to relocate 120 000 refugees from italy, greece and other member states directly affected by the refugee crisis. on 30 september, the commission presented a set of priority measures to be taken over the next six months to deal with the refugee crisis. this is the first of a series of concrete proposals to be funded in 2015 and 2016 with €1.7 billion of eu funds to tackle the refugee crisis. the proposals submitted for 2015 amount to eur 801,3 million to support priority actions. the second group of proposals for the remaining eur 900 million for 2016 will be included in a letter of amendment to the draft budget for 2016 in the month of october. both parliament and the council have dealt with this matter with the utmost urgency to enable the funds to be released as soon as possible. i agree with the measures and the urgency, so i voted for it.

in writing. ‒ the increase in the number of refugees and migrants was not foreseeable when the multiannual financial framework for 2014-2020 was adopted. i am satisfied with the speed with which the commission has reacted to the current refugee crisis. this report reaffirms the willingness of the european parliament to act expeditiously in accordance with its budgetary responsibilities. i hope that member states honour their commitments. i challenge the competent authorities to work to help stabilise the countries of origin and assist countries of transit – for surely the proposed measures will not be enough given the total number of people seeking protection in the union.

in writing. ‒ following the latest developments in the field of migration, commitment appropriations of eur 401.3 million are intended to be allocated to the following measures: reinforcement of asylum and migration and internal security funds for the most affected member states (eur 100 million), staff increase in the three agencies managing this area: frontex, easo and europol (eur 1.3 million) and increase of the european neighbourhood instrument for the syrian crisis (eur 300 million). because of the crisis situation we are facing and the urgency of the situation, it is necessary to vote in favour of this measure in order to be able to show in this way the commitment of this house to the current migration crisis.

in writing. ‒ the eu is experiencing a huge influx of refugees, undoubtedly driven mainly by the situation in syria. this situation has generated a movement of people towards our borders that exceeds any expectation of immigration hitherto envisaged by the european union. this has created major difficulties in several member states, especially those which are the entry and transit zones for refugees. the measures put in place so far are insufficient. i therefore fully support the adoption of new exceptional measures, especially those relating to the increase in the budget in this area, which will be very positive in helping all the member states (especially greece, hungary and italy) to manage this influx of refugees.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of the waiver of immunity of béla kovács as it is clearly a case of political persecution. the suspension of the immunity of an elected official in order to enable him to face legal proceedings cannot be used as a political weapon against members of the european parliament. this is a clear case of exploitation of it, which is why i did not vote to waive his immunity.
in writing. ‒ the committee on legal affairs has been debating the case of mep béla kovács for several months. the stages of the procedure laid down in the regulation (exchange of views, hearing and consideration of the draft report) were strictly followed and there was also a hearing with the hungarian authorities to look into the case. the committee on legal affairs voted overwhelmingly in favour of the suspension of immunity after rejecting the possibility of such a request being part of an open procedure intended to cause political damage to the member. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i could not vote for the candidate for deputy director-general of the european fund for strategic investments, because her career is closely linked to infrastructure investment projects. this path is giving a clear signal of the potential direction of the efsi investments, which will seek to replace public investments in infrastructure with public-private consortia that in the long run prove much more costly for taxpayers. in addition, he was the only candidate put forward by the council, which is a procedure that leaves much to be desired for the democratic will expressed by the european parliament. it is because of all this that i have not been able to vote in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal to appoint iliyana tsanova as deputy director-general of the european fund for strategic investments. mrs tsanova has already passed the hearing of the committee on budgets and the committee on economic affairs of parliament and has answered the questions put to her satisfactorily, showing her worth for the post assigned to her. i wish you a good career in your new job.
in writing. ‒ at a joint hearing of the committee on economic and monetary affairs and the committee on budgets, ms tsanova was able to demonstrate that she was qualified for the post and clearly show her competence for the post of deputy director-general of the efsi. i therefore voted in favour of your appointment.
in writing. ‒ the only candidate proposed was the bulgarian economist iliyana tsanova and, despite her extensive experience, i voted against her because of her link with the development and infrastructure sector (european bank for reconstruction and development), an area in which the efsi will be active, and because of the risks of conflict of interest that could arise.

madam president, i would like to address the point concerning the preparation of the mandate for the negotiation of a new global climate agreement. i endorsed the mandate, even though some of the key amendments, in my view, that my group supported, were not passed. i believe that a new treaty, which would be in force in 2020, is a necessity. on the other hand, i am saying in advance that the treaty which will be adopted and binding should first set limits which are attainable, which are not to be met by certain countries alone and which do not lead to european industry becoming uncompetitive, or uncompetitive, with industry in other developing or developed countries. this is, in my view, a very key criterion by which i will assess the final form of the contract. it is also important that as many countries as possible sign the treaty, especially third world countries that are major polluters.
madam president, i voted in favour of this report so that parliament can be firm in demanding legal obligations to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. the european union's position is not without its paradoxes, however. how can we think that the market, and especially the financial market, can be the way to a sustainable society? how can we imagine that the same instrument that encourages endless consumption and irresponsible investment can replace the state in the ecological transition? i cannot deny that i have doubts about the ability of the european union to implement the recommendations of this report in the face of the interests of the most savage capitalism. i hope that this report will not be reduced to mere words. other policies, yes, but also another economic model, another way of life. otherwise, the fight against climate change is lost in the first place.
in writing. ‒ my vote in favour of the pargneaux report is a strong endorsement of the negotiating mandate of the european parliament delegation to the united nations conference on climate change (cp21) in paris from 30 november to 11 december. the socialists strongly support an active eu role at the paris summit with the aim of reaching an ambitious and legally binding agreement on emissions reductions, as well as sound financial instruments for achieving this objective. as the date of the paris summit approaches, there is a need to step up climate diplomacy. world leaders must understand that limiting global warming to a maximum of two degrees will not only help prevent climate change and the associated natural disasters, but will also prevent a dramatic increase in the number of refugees as a result of climate change. on the other hand, the eu's 20/20/20 targets for emissions, renewable energy and energy savings demonstrate that there is no contradiction between growth and sustainability, as evidenced by the fact that the european economy has grown by 45% since 1990.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it calls for legal obligations to reduce greenhouse gas emissions rather than the non-binding commitments which unfortunately are the usual norm in this area. however, i believe that giving priority to implementation through market instruments and, in particular, financial market instruments is incompatible with the commitment to reduce emissions effectively. on the contrary, they will accelerate the breakdown of the traditional productive fabric, without in any case ensuring a transition to an environmentally and socially sustainable economy. that is why i doubt the european union's ability to implement the recommendations of this report or to combine them with its commitment to neoliberal policies.
in writing. ‒ my vote in favour of the pargneaux report is a strong endorsement of the negotiating mandate of the european parliament delegation to the united nations conference on climate change (cp21) in paris from 30 november to 11 december. the socialists strongly support an active eu role at the paris summit with the aim of reaching an ambitious and legally binding agreement on emissions reductions, as well as sound financial instruments for achieving this objective. as the date of the paris summit approaches, there is a need to step up climate diplomacy. world leaders must understand that limiting global warming to a maximum of two degrees will not only help prevent climate change and the associated natural disasters, but will also prevent a dramatic increase in the number of refugees as a result of climate change. on the other hand, the eu's 20/20/20 targets for emissions, renewable energy and energy savings demonstrate that there is no contradiction between growth and sustainability, as evidenced by the fact that the european economy has grown by 45% since 1990.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on a new international climate agreement in paris drawn up by the associated committees in parliament. i have voted against my group's line on two amendments. the first is amendment no 5 to paragraph 10 where i have supported the epp group amendment which stresses the importance of reaching an effective and binding global agreement at the paris conference and points out that the continued absence of such an agreement will further jeopardise the competitiveness of the union's economy and expose it to the risk of carbon leakage. i also abstained on amendment no 4 by the epp group because i did not agree with its content, nor with the content of the original text of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the text because it raises the need for the eu to devote more economic and technological resources to the fight against climate change and to establish and strengthen legally binding commitments in paris to reduce emissions of co2 and other gases that contribute to the greenhouse effect. however, while the report addresses the problem that co2 emissions from transport have continued to rise, it does not introduce any criticism of free trade or the atci and leaves everything to the development of clean transport technologies. as regards the defence of co2 emissions trading, this is a system which in my view creates a new economic bubble through the buying and selling of emission allowances and which is proving ineffective in meeting the objectives for which it was theoretically conceived, which is why we have spoken out against this system.

in writing. ‒ the 21st conference of the parties (cp21) to the united nations framework convention on climate change (unfccc) and the kyoto protocol will be held in paris from 30 november to 11 december 2015. the european parliament decided to draw up this own-initiative report following the publication of the commission communication of 25 february 2015 as part of the energy union package entitled 'the paris protocol, a roadmap to combat climate change beyond 2020'. the report, which is the mandate of the european parliament delegation for the december meeting of cp21, is consistent with the positions of our political group and i have therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ my vote in favour of the pargneaux report is a strong endorsement of the negotiating mandate of the european parliament delegation to the united nations conference on climate change (cp21) in paris from 30 november to 11 december. the socialists strongly support an active eu role at the paris summit with the aim of reaching an ambitious and legally binding agreement on emissions reductions, as well as sound financial instruments for achieving this objective. as the date of the paris summit approaches, there is a need to step up climate diplomacy. world leaders must understand that limiting global warming to a maximum of two degrees will not only help prevent climate change and the associated natural disasters, but will also prevent a dramatic increase in the number of refugees as a result of climate change. on the other hand, the eu's 20/20/20 targets for emissions, renewable energy and energy savings demonstrate that there is no contradiction between growth and sustainability, as evidenced by the fact that the european economy has grown by 45% since 1990.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it calls for legal obligations to reduce greenhouse gas emissions rather than the non-binding commitments which unfortunately are the usual norm in this area. however, i believe that giving priority to implementation through market instruments and, in particular, financial market instruments is incompatible with the commitment to reduce emissions effectively. on the contrary, they will accelerate the breakdown of the traditional productive fabric, without in any case ensuring a transition to an environmentally and socially sustainable economy. that is why i doubt the european union's ability to implement the recommendations of this report or to combine them with its commitment to neoliberal policies.

in writing. ‒ i strongly support such a resolution because climate change is now recognized worldwide as a top urgency. the future of our kids and future generations depends on our strong actions today. the 2015 protocol must be legally binding and ambitious from the outset when adopted in paris, and should aim at phasing out global carbon emissions by 2050 or shortly thereafter so as to keep the world on a cost-effective emission trajectory compatible with the below 2°c target, and that a global ghg emissions peak will be reached as soon as possible. i call on the eu to work with its international partners to that end, showing examples of good practices. the agreement must provide a predictable framework which encourages investments and scaling by business of efficient carbon reductions and adaptation technologies;only an ambitious and legally binding international agreement would help to address the carbon leakage and competitiveness concerns of the relevant sectors and in particular the energy intensive sector. i call for a general reinvigoration of the eu’s climate policy, which would help build momentum in international climate discussions and would be in line with the upper limit of the eu’s commitment to reducing its ghg emissions to 80-95 % below 1990 levels by 2050.

in writing. the ferber report is aimed at improving transparency in the exchange of information in the tax field, which is why we voted in favour. it is a text that would not have seen the light of day if it were not for the courage of mr deltour to let europe know of the complicity of juncker and european governments in large-scale tax evasion. however, this proposal should not be confused with the possibility of genuine public scrutiny or an automatic check on tax evasion. the mechanisms by which large multinationals avoid their taxes, including the tax agreements to which this proposal refers, are still in force and are known and protected by the various governments. clear and transparent rules are not enough: we also need to commit ourselves to a fair and progressive tax system. in this respect, we lack the political confidence in the juncker commission to expect it to use the new instruments at its disposal to effectively control and regulate tax avoidance. europe is still a long way from responding to the luxleaks scandal.
member of the commission.– mr president, i want to start by thanking the rapporteur, mrs schaake, for the excellent work that she has done on this, of course with input from other colleagues as well. as was said, we will be discussing some very technical elements, but let us not forget that we are talking about highly politically—sensitive issues such as ending the death penalty, torture and ill-treatment, which are key priorities for all the work of the european union. it is in fact an anomaly that so many countries still have the death penalty and that so many thousands of people are still waiting in death row all over the world, but the fact is that it has actually decreased. one hundred and forty countries do not apply the death penalty today and 98 have legally abolished it, compared to 59 twenty years ago, so this is going in the right direction, but that does not mean that we should rest – there is so much to do. we have different tools at our disposal in foreign policy, but trade also can play a very important role and that is why this report is so important. trade can be a leverage to promote, around the world, european values such as human rights, sustainable development, fair and ethical trade and the fight against corruption, and those values are the pillars of the newly proposed trade strategy by the commission. the regulation we are talking about, regulation (ec) no 1236/2005, takes account of this – the role of trade – to restrict foreign trade in goods that could be used for executions, torture or ill-treatment, and we welcome very much the effort done by the european parliament to amend the regulation. we largely share the spirit and the approach taken by the committee on international trade (inta), the rapporteur and parliament, although some of the amendments in the report call for measures without precedent in export-control legislation and could be a bit difficult to implement in practice. we support several amendments, such as amendment 6 extending the proposed definition of ‘broker’ to cover nationals from member states not resident or established in the union. this is acceptable in principle, but it could be difficult to enforce, so the inclusion of foreign subsidiaries of legal persons incorporated in the eu should of course not go beyond what is compatible with international law. amendments 9 and 10 on the transport of transiting goods whose export and import is prohibited by the regulation are also acceptable for the commission if amendment 10 does not cover more than non-union goods. it is related to amendment 15, and that can also be accepted; we just have to make sure that it is formulated in compatibility with wto requirements. amendment 21 referring to the transmission of information to human rights oversight bodies is also acceptable. of course, here, companies requesting an export authorisation that submit information to competent authority have a legitimate interest in not giving certain data and making them public, so we need to make sure how the text is drafted here. furthermore, we can accept amendments 18 on best practices for technical assistance, 19 on guidelines and 26 on the report published by the commission on the implementation, if you can agree that this is not an obligation for the commission. we can also accept amendment 2 adding human dignity and then several other more technical amendments that i will not go into now. i mentioned that some of the proposed measures are without precedent in export-control legislation. last spring, members approved here in parliament regulation 479 on common rules for exports, which confirmed the basic rule of trade policy: that exports are to be free unless trade restrictions are necessary to achieve an accepted objective, such as the protection of public morals. torture, ill treatment and the death penalty are, of course, never acceptable, but we just make need to make sure that trade restrictions to promote respect for human rights meet the necessary trust. in this regard, while we fully understand the rationale of a view to propose an end-use or catch-all clause, we think it could lead to the introduction of restrictions going beyond what is necessary and preventing a level playing field for exporters. this could present a challenge to the uniformity of the union’s trade policy, and for this reason the commission had instead proposed the urgency procedure, which would help us to deal with most of the cases that could be addressed in a more proportionate manner. but we are willing to see if those objectives, which are basically the same, can be reconciled in a formula that we can agree upon. regarding the amendment on the definition of brokering services, number 5, it would make the regulation cover a range of activities, financial services and insurance related to goods that are outside the union, and that would be very difficult to monitor and control. but rather than amending the definition, we could identify which restrictions on which services need the necessity test and then use of specific drafting to regulate those activities. we recognise the usefulness of the coordination group and we share the objective behind that amendment. we just need to be very careful to make sure that that article is not at odds with the agreed arrangement for delegated powers in the treaty. we would need to find an appropriate formula to create a forum for consultations between member states, stakeholders, civil society and the commission.as you know, the eu works towards the abolition of the death penalty in all countries. the countries that are included in the proposal, in the authorisation of the annex, have ratified the second optional protocol to the international covenant on civil and political rights without reservation, so they agreed to abolish the death penalty. when controlling exports to prevent eu involvement in executions in third countries, we should focus our efforts on countries that have not abolished it, and therefore we disagree with amendments 33, 35 and 37 because there is nothing to show that these countries concerned would have applied the death penalty, despite the ratification of the protocol. let me conclude – it has become rather technical – by expressing my conviction that this report, by the rapporteur and many of you, is a very good basis for further work to make the regulation into a more robust export—control regime that promotes respect for fundamental rights without unduly restricting foreign rights. i express here the full commitment by the commission and me, personally, to work with you and with the council to achieve that objective and a good final product.
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, commissioner, the european union, through this regulation, reaffirms its policy towards the abolition of the death penalty in the world, as required by article 2 of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union. the abolition of the death penalty and of inhuman and degrading treatment is one of the major priorities of the union's human rights policy, and the european union is the leading institutional actor in the fight against the death penalty. the european people's party is firmly opposed to the death penalty and any form of torture and we do not want to be complicit in these practices. we therefore stress the importance of controlling exports of products which could be used to impose capital punishment or torture. and this regulation is an instrument which makes it possible to ensure respect for and protection of human dignity, the right to life and the prohibition of torture. it also allows, under strict supervision, these products to be used for legitimate purposes, such as medical purposes. we shall therefore vote in favour of this report tomorrow, as a group, because we think it is a balanced proposal which contributes to the protection of human rights and makes the european union a pioneer in the regulation of trade in these products.
the european union is committed to the eradication of the death penalty and torture in the world, but that commitment would be worthless if it were not accompanied by firm and rigorous action, such as the one we are debating today in the plenary. the european union took a big step in 2005 when it adopted the first regulation, but unfortunately it quickly became obsolete in the face of the dynamism of the market and the sophistication of the capacity of companies to manufacture and design instruments for the death penalty and torture. in 2010, therefore, the council, then chaired by the socialist government of josé luis rodríguez zapatero, urged the commission to reform the regulation. five years later we can be here today debating; a long time has passed. but fortunately we are here now, we have the regulation we asked for, and i really think it has been improved in the committee on international trade, thanks to the amendments by the groups and, of course, to the excellent work and consensus effort of the rapporteur, whom i congratulate from here. we welcome this proposal because it extends controls to legal products which could be handled at destination; because it also extends the list of products which can be used to inflict the death penalty; and, of course, because it introduces more agile and effective mechanisms for reviewing the list of controlled and prohibited products. we believe that this proposal will ensure that no national, no european company or its subsidiaries abroad can profit from this trade. as i said at the beginning, and as the commissioner and all those who have gone before me have rightly pointed out, europe needs to show that it is committed to human rights, that it will not allow trade to be a profit-making instrument for inflicting the death penalty and torture, and, of course, that trade policy is a fundamental instrument to help defend human rights. and finally, mr president, i would like to congratulate and thank all the non-governmental organizations for human rights for their invaluable work and cooperation.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, it is common sense that we should not allow our companies to trade with third countries with materials which we have banned in europe because they are related to inhuman or torturous practices. we cannot sell to others what we ourselves have outlawed. in this respect, we think that the regulation is positive and that it is on the right track. but it is necessary for the european commission to set up an effective monitoring system to ensure that all member states comply with this regulation. and we must also ensure that the transit of these goods through the european union is prohibited. however, i think we should be more ambitious. we are making an inefficient use, for example, of our official development aid, with which schools and hospitals are being built in palestine, if, at the same time, we are selling arms to israel with which they will destroy those very schools and hospitals. we must also review our economic association agreements with states which systematically violate human rights and therefore ban military armaments and arms sales.
member of the commission.– mr president, it is good to see that there is such strong unity on these important issues. it sends a strong signal to the rest of the world, and shows that we are determined to use all possible tools that we have at our disposal – today we are talking about trade – to abolish the death penalty along with torture and ill—treatment. let me thank again the rapporteur and all the shadow rapporteurs and the committee on foreign affairs, which has been involved as well, and reiterate the commission’s determination to have an ambitious regulation in place to restrict foreign trade in goods that could be used for executions or ill—treatment or torture. we will, as many of you said, make sure with this amendment that we close the loopholes and also, in response to some of your questions on the catch-all clause, we have an open position so let us see how we can find a solution to this. on the implementation and monitoring, i think that the coordination group – or whatever we call it in the end – can have a very important role there. also, the commission has, via delegated acts, the powers to regularly modify the annex to make sure that it is kept up to date. we will also present next year a review of the export control system for dual use – many of you have referred to this, this evening, as well – in order to make sure that we have an even better regulation on items that can be misused in violation of human rights, which would be another very important milestone. i am sure that with such a strong agreement to really have a good regulation updated here, we can find a way to overcome the remaining difficulties and find a way to amend them in the right way so that we have a workable and efficient system that is proven for the future and equipped to ensure rapid reaction when a risk arises. this commission will certainly play its part in this.
first vice-president of the commission.– i very much welcome today’s discussion on the european citizens’ initiative (eci) and i welcome györgy schöpflin’s report, which i think is an excellent contribution. this is a good basis for me to discuss something that already came up during my hearing and that is something we really want to build on. we, the juncker commission, have said that we would act on big things and concentrate our efforts there. that is what we do, but we also need to change how we do it. in that context, i believe the eci can be a valuable contribution. it is a tool with which citizens can directly try to influence policy. it allows citizens to influence the agenda at european level and to bring to the fore the concrete issues which most concern them. it is therefore a tool to initiate political dialogue. as a member of the european convention, when i represented the dutch parliament, i was myself involved in the design of the citizens’ initiative. today, it is part of my responsibilities to ensure that it works properly and thus works better. it is still a young tool, but we already have some experience. last march the commission reported on the initiative’s first three years. it has started to show its potential. some 33 initiatives were registered, and collected signatures. three successfully gathered over one million signatures each. overall, about 6 million citizens gave their signatures – impressive numbers of people. all these efforts have succeeded in forging links among like—minded people across the continent. they helped spark genuine pan—european debates and brought new ideas into the european public space. this is promising for european participatory democracy and the emergence of a european demos. but, at the same time, we need to work to make the citizens’ initiative more user—friendly. i note that several points put forward in your report, mr schöpflin, converge with our report’s conclusions. we are already implementing a number of these measures. let me just mention a few. the commission has established a dedicated point of contact, which has already replied to around 1 200 questions in all eu languages on rules and procedures. we are also providing more specific support directly to organisers once their eci has been registered, including on legal requirements and logistical or technical aspects. going beyond our obligations on the regulation, we also provide ad hoc online hosting on commission servers free of charge. data requirements have sometimes been flagged as an issue. here we will continue our efforts to encourage member states to simplify their data requirements so that all citizens can actually exercise the right to sign an eci, should they wish to do so. we should also be open to do more if that is needed. i am therefore here today to listen very carefully to members’ assessment of how the instrument is working and discuss their ideas on how to improve it. the commission takes very seriously indeed parliament’s call for a legislative revision of the eci regulation. we are currently in the process of assessing the need, scope and objective for such a revision. we are collecting factual evidence and are listening widely to stakeholders. the commission would like to thank parliament for its constructive approach towards improving this important tool. i would like to personally thank and congratulate mr schöpflin for a job very well done in analysing the implementation of the eci, reflecting on possible improvements and building consensus across political groups and committees. he is not trying to make party political work with us; he is trying to help citizens reconnect – or, sometimes, connect for the first time – with our european level of political dialogue. i think the commission should be prepared to do whatever is needed to make that easier, more accessible and more successful.
the committee on petitions has already adopted a number of amendments. mr president, mr vice-president, the european citizens' initiative the first instrument of transnational participatory democracy was created to enable european citizens to engage directly with the institutions and to influence the governance of the union with their proposals. three years after it was launched, what the data tells us is that it hasn't worked as it should. and since what is not working must be fixed, we ask the commission to review it immediately. tools must serve the purpose for which they were designed. users must have all the facilities and support to use them. we need to harmonize the various national requirements and simplify the required documentation, including by proposing a common identification system. and we must certainly establish a one-stop shop by taking advantage of the existing headquarters and staff of the european institutions in each member state. but, moreover, my group, the alde group, believes that the european citizens' initiative should serve to change aspects of primary law. a thorough review is needed as soon as possible and problems must be addressed, because by improving the european citizens' initiative we will improve democracy.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, i think there are three conclusions to be drawn from this debate: firstly, citizens' initiative is very important for democratic participation; secondly, the current law does not work; thirdly, we have to improve it. that much we agree on. i wanted to suggest to mr timmermans a solution which i think is politically interesting for what may be the reform of the initiative, which is to provide that those initiatives which reach one million signatures but which are not accepted for competition or other legal reasons, will be given an institutional response. i believe that we cannot ignore an initiative which has such a capacity to be convened and which, for formal or legal reasons, cannot be followed up. my proposal is that there should be a response from the commission, whether by referring to other initiatives or by waiting for other legal reforms, but that there should be an institutional response.
member of the commission.– mr president, the commission very much welcomes charles goerens’ report. i want to commend and thank mr goerens for his great work and, of course, for his dedication to the fight against ebola. during this period we have had excellent and productive cooperation for which i am truly thankful to him. the european union has a special responsibility when it comes to promoting universal health coverage, supporting countries to achieve health–related sustainable development goals and to build resilient health systems better able to control outbreaks so we are better prepared when the next big epidemic strikes. the report remains very topical as this epidemic is not over. we have again been getting some new cases, unfortunately, in guinea in recent weeks. we must remain engaged until we reach a resilient zero, until the affected countries fully recover. the european union and member states have pledged over eur 2 billion. from this amount eur 900 million comes from the commission alone for response, recovery and research. we are also fully engaged in learning vital lessons from the ebola crisis: for example, the october luxembourg conference on lessons learned, which commissioner andriukaitis and i attended, came forward with important recommendations. these will fit into the health council conclusions in december. as the eu ebola coordinator i will also report on the overall lessons learnt to the european council at the end of this year. we have also been fully engaged in the g7 health ministers discussions on ebola earlier this month, in which commissioner andriukaitis participated. we are pleased that the g7 declaration expresses commitment to, and i quote, ‘strengthening health systems to enable the provision of basic healthcare [...] as well as water, sanitation and hygiene. the aim is to progressively achieve universal health coverage’. this is very important. as mr goerens’ report clearly emphasises, basic healthcare and clean water for all are essential. we can all agree that building and reconstructing a resilient health system is also essential – health systems able to detect, monitor and contain a health crisis. what have been the main lessons for the eu from this crisis? there are many things we could write in our response at eu level. our rapid and substantial ebola funding for the emergency response, for recovery, for research; our role in organising the transport of assistance to west africa; the very positive role of the european centre for disease prevention and control in deploying epidemiologists; also the crucial role of the four eu mobile laboratories or the eu medivac system that we deployed for all international health workers. but at the same time there are also lessons from what did not go as well. the first lesson: the international community was and still is ill–prepared for a global health emergency. global emergency and health governance need strengthening. this includes support to the who, the reform of the who and the review and implementation of international health regulations. here our help plays a key role. we also had difficulties in rapidly deploying medical teams. hence we are now working with member states to establish a european medical corps using the voluntary pool system of the european union’s civil protection mechanism. secondly, weak health systems in partner countries are a particular concern. the european union has committed to comprehensive health systems’ strengthening; however, we learned from ebola that we may not have been comprehensive enough. so we need to do more to strengthen national capacity, as i said, to provide health care for all and for outbreak control in particular. thirdly, the weakest health systems are severely underfunded. domestic resource mobilisation will not fill the gap soon. to have good preparedness and to achieve the health sdgs we need a minimum level of public health financing. forty countries spend even less than usd 30 per capita per year. that is the real figure. fourthly, the commission and member states have to programme health aid more strategically, leaving no one behind. we have to counteract any tendency to withdraw collectively from the health sector, focusing on those countries falling below minimum public financing. we need to think about how we can deploy our collective eu health aid more effectively and more predictably. last, but not least, the commission and member states should support a globally coordinated research effort to identify, make priorities and address recent gaps against future emergency epidemics. capacity building through research has an important role to play in strengthening local health systems. we are therefore supporting the global research collaboration for infectious diseases preparedness, an important tool for coordinating research funding.
the commission has also proposed that the council adopt a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a fire. mr president, as with the refugee crisis, the european response to the ebola epidemic was, in my view, late and bad. a few states reacted well, but the response of others was lamentable. the union as a whole has no reason to be complacent. i believe that the lessons we must draw must come from an honest and rigorous analysis of the european reaction during the first months, those following the alert issued by médecins sans frontières. and the global inaction in those first few months is partly why the scale of the epidemic was so great, and why it spread so unchecked. the ebola outbreak, an exceptional event, has brought to light how inefficient and slow the health and humanitarian aid systems are in responding to emergencies. we need a global strategy to support research and development for vaccines and treatments, and a global and fair strategy for development and international support and response.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, commissioner, mr goerens, first of all i would like to congratulate you and your whole team on the excellent work you have done on this report. the lessons to be learned from the ebola crisis, which has killed almost 12,000 people, are these: first, austerity kills. structural adjustment programs, imposed by the imf and the world bank in the 1980s and 1990s in africa, have eroded the health systems of these countries, rendering them powerless to deal with an epidemic of the caliber of ebola. the cuts and privatizations that have been taking place in european countries such as spain have also weakened health systems and are responsible for the poor management of treated ebola cases, such as that of nurse teresa romero, who contracted it due to lack of means and resources, and for no other reason. two, the pharmaceutical industry is driven solely by profit and does not research the diseases of the poor, as ebola has shown. in short, there is an urgent need to end austerity and develop robust health systems, and there is also an urgent need to look at alternatives to the current model of drug research. only then can we cope with future health crises on a global scale. i just want to end by saying that these 12,000 deaths serve to ensure that this does not happen again.

the rapporteur. mr president, vice-president ansip, ladies and gentlemen, the procedure on the regulation of the single market in telecommunications is coming to an end. after a long period of negotiations with the council, during which parliament has shown great determination, we have achieved the objectives we set ourselves from the outset. first, the abolition of the extra costs that consumers face when accessing the internet or trying to communicate by telephone when they are outside their country. secondly, we have managed to establish the necessary safeguards so that all - i insist - internet traffic is treated equally and that access to an open internet is made on equal terms, thus ensuring net neutral behaviour. these two objectives are fully reflected in the agreement with the council of 30 june last, which was signed by the majority of the political groups involved in the negotiations. as regards roaming charges, they will be abolished from june 2017 and, in addition, from april 2016 there will be a very significant reduction in both data and voice charges. it must be said that the disappearance of roaming charges is a long-awaited measure. it is expected by all: by individuals, small and medium-sized enterprises, start-ups and organisations of all kinds, who can now see in a tangible way that the european union, the european project, has a clear added value. we have certainly taken another step towards the removal of internal barriers, towards the free movement of people, towards a digital single market. as regards equal access to the internet, i have to say that with this agreement, europe will be the only region in the world which guarantees, by law, an open internet and net neutrality. the principle of net neutrality will be applied directly in all 28 member states and will ensure that all traffic is treated equally, without discrimination, without restriction or interference. the agreement also ensures that there will be no dual-track internet, prohibiting payment to prioritize one or the other. this is also, in my view, extremely important. for this reason, where traffic management intervention is necessary, such intervention may only occur when it is linked to the solution of temporary or exceptional congestion problems, to the protection of users against cyber attacks or in cases where there is an obligation, a resolution that requires it; and furthermore, when such management occurs 'where necessary', it will have to be transparent, non-discriminatory and proportionate. i would also like to mention the various measures that have been taken in relation to consumer protection in relation to all these provisions. finally, i would like to express my gratitude to the latvian presidency, during which the agreement was negotiated and concluded, and to the luxembourg presidency, which is now managing it, and to the commission, which has for its part been making great efforts for a long time to achieve the objectives now achieved. let me make a special mention of commissioner reding, commissioner kroes, commissioner oettinger and vice-president ansip, who at different times have helped to make this moment a reality. i would like to conclude by thanking all the alternative rapporteurs, and i do not forget the rapporteurs who are not here today but who had those responsibilities in the last legislature. the efforts of all have made it possible for us today to guarantee an open, non-discriminatory internet and to take a step towards a connected europe and a single market without digital customs.
mr president, we appreciate parliament's positions in defence of net neutrality and the end of roaming. we are not unaware, however, of the concessions made to the council which show that some parties have negotiated very differently from parliament and from the government. we hope that these ambiguities will be resolved in the vote and in the application of the rules of procedure. as far as roaming is concerned, we cannot tolerate the large telecommunications groups charging double for the same service. today we can correct this situation. let's not miss this opportunity. as for net neutrality, this is a basic and fundamental requirement, not only for respecting freedoms, but also for productive innovation and equal access in an increasingly digitalised world, both in leisure and in work. beyond today's debate, the union's digital strategy must consider the future not only of consumer rights but also the place and rights of the producer and worker in this digital world. i hope that in this debate we will be able to maintain the same consensus that we are trying to achieve today.
mr president, i would like to thank pilar del castillo vera, as well as the shadow rapporteurs, for achieving this deal with the council. this new regulation is an example of how the european union can bring concrete benefits to its citizens. parliament had called for the abolition of roaming surcharges and we will have this. as of june 2017, european union citizens will be able to travel across the eu without paying extra communication surcharges. this will also bring significant benefits to european companies. i regret that the council refused to accept the definition of net neutrality called for by parliament. nevertheless, we managed to include in the regulation minimum provisions to ensure non—discrimination and equal treatment on the internet. i deplore, however, that the council rejected negotiation on spectrum and end-user rights as this would have been a concrete step towards full realisation of the digital single market.

in writing. in order to deal with this dramatic influx of refugees into the eu, the european parliament has mobilised all its resources to manage the situation effectively and as quickly as possible. however, we are beginning to get tired and - why not say it - also frustrated at seeing a whole series of council meetings in recent months go by as 'urgent' and the implementation of the decisions taken is constantly delayed. the most important of these is the financial contribution by the member states to help manage this crisis. the european parliament is fulfilling its responsibility, now it is up to the countries to do their part and provide the €2.3 billion for refugees and humanitarian aid they promised. we cannot afford to remain in this impasse because of the unwillingness of certain countries; the lives of thousands of men, women and children are at stake.

the rapporteur. madam president, i would like to say that today's vote puts an end to the legislative process for the single telecommunications market. and because parliament has shown leadership throughout the process of communication and negotiation with the extraordinary council, we have achieved the main objectives we set ourselves. first, the end of roaming charges. we can also say that it is the removal of a kind of tax on the free movement of persons in the european union, and that barriers are being removed so that small businesses, start-ups and all kinds of organisations and institutions can make their way into the european single market. it is a tangible proof of the european union's added value. and secondly, a little respect, please, a little respect, be so kind, and secondly, the internet. the internet, there's no doubt about it, is a gem. it is a precious asset that technology has brought to us; that is full of opportunities, that is full of opportunities for everyone; that we have to care for gently and that we even have to pamper. this regulation provides the necessary guarantees for the internet to provide equal access for all, without discrimination, without interference, without restrictions, in a clear and unambiguous way. and, also, (the president cut off the member's speech to allow her to speak) no, no; i shall continue and i shall finish, because i have the right to speak in this house. and if there are people who lack respect for the intervention of any parliamentarian, let them wait and listen to who is speaking. and i have to say... there is very little to be done with noise, ladies and gentlemen, other than to try to create confusion. and i have to say that, in addition to creating a level playing field in access to the internet and establishing the guarantees of the principles of net neutrality, this legislation allows creativity, that talent, that innovation for innovative services on the internet can also flourish. ladies and gentlemen, we are... thank you, thank you very much, to the efforts of the alternative rapporteurs and to all those who have contributed to making this moment today a reality.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because this proposal aims to repeal certain acts adopted in recent decades which are no longer applicable, either because their content has been incorporated into successive acts or because of their temporary nature. the commission proposal does not allow the commission to declare acts adopted by the council obsolete. the acts contained in the proposal should therefore be repealed by the council and the european parliament in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure. the aim and content of the proposal for a regulation is a pure derogation from council directive 76/621/eec and council regulation (ec) no 320/2006. in particular, the two acts have become obsolete as the content of council directive 76/621/eec has been incorporated into the subsequent regulation 1881/2006, and council regulation (ec) no 320/2006 only established a temporary regime, which is no longer applicable.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal for a regulation of the european parliament and of the council repealing council directive 76/621/eec on the fixing of the maximum percentage of erucic acid in oils and fats and council regulation (ec) no 320/2006 establishing a temporary scheme for the restructuring of the sugar sector, given that both acts have become obsolete as the content of council directive 76/621/eec has been taken over by the subsequent regulation (ec) no 1881/2006, whereas council regulation (ec) no 320/2006 was limited to establishing a temporary scheme which is no longer applicable.

in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of repealing directive 76/621/eec on the determination of the maximum percentage of erucic acid in oils and fats and regulation (ec) no 320/2006 establishing a temporary scheme for the restructuring of the sugar sector, as the content of these rules had become outdated by the new cap regulation and therefore there was no point in their continuing to be in force.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because this proposal aims to repeal certain acts adopted in recent decades which are no longer applicable, either because their content has been incorporated into successive acts or because of their temporary nature. according to the commission's proposal, it is not within the commission's power to declare obsolete acts which have been adopted by the council. the acts contained in the proposal should therefore be repealed by the council and the european parliament in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure. the aim and content of the proposal for a regulation is a mere derogation from council directive 76/621/eec and council regulation (ec) no 320/2006. in particular, the two acts have become obsolete as the content of council directive 76/621 / eec has been taken over by the later regulation 1881/2006, which council regulation 320/2006 only established a temporary regime, which is no longer applicable.
in writing. ‒ the text adopted was intended to repeal two earlier texts, one by the commission on the maximum percentage of erucic acid in oils and fats and another by the council, which established a temporary scheme for the restructuring of the sugar sector. although both legal acts had become obsolete, they formally remained in force. in accordance with one of the principles of the european union, which aims to improve the transparency of union law and to better legislate, it is essential to repeal legal acts which no longer have any real effect. i therefore support this report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this international agreement with switzerland on the automatic exchange of tax information because it is a major step forward in the fight against tax evasion and avoidance, particularly in third countries. the eu and switzerland have agreed to establish a system for the automatic exchange of information on financial accounts opened by their residents as of 2018.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this report because, although it implies a necessary requirement for financial information, it implies a position in favour of the use of tax havens for europeans. the report implies an improvement in the systems for the exchange of financial information between the competent authorities of switzerland and the european union. however, this is not a sufficient commitment to ensure that european companies and citizens tax their funds in europe, as in many states, despite the availability of information, no action is taken. we need to abolish the use of tax havens for europeans, who must contribute to the financing of the member states like any other citizen. that is why i abstained from voting on this report.

in writing. ‒ the fight against tax avoidance and the need for fair taxation are major concerns at both european and global level. while great progress has been made at international level, it is still important to proceed with caution when repealing an existing directive that has been observed for several years. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the information provided by the member states is not used in the same way as the information provided by the member states.
in writing. ‒ the 2003 savings income tax directive was designed to collect information on savings of non-resident individuals. in the meantime, a directive on administrative cooperation covering the automatic exchange of tax information, in a general sense, was adopted in 2011 and revised in 2014 to bring it into line with global oecd standards. this directive shall enter into force on 1 january 2016. the result is that there is a great deal of overlap between the two directives, and so, in order to avoid confusion and having to comply with two different information systems, i have not opposed the repeal. however, the scope of the two directives does not coincide in their entirety, and therefore, by repealing the 2003 directive, they are exempted from the obligation to report certain types of low-risk savings deposits, as well as any paying agent (broker, insurance, etc.), since the 2011 directive imposes the obligations on financial institutions. the directive, which is more ambitious in general, also imposes fewer disclosure requirements on foundations and trusts. the commission should take measures to correct these gaps, thus achieving adequate coverage of all financial accounts.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a derogation from council directive 2003/48/ec, which seeks to fill any gaps in the current legislation in the area of taxation of income from savings. the current directive leaves it up to national bilateral agreements to tax savings located in five european countries outside the union (switzerland, liechtenstein, san marino, monaco and andorra), as well as in island and overseas territories with special tax regimes. this has created numerous situations of tax competition in the field of savings, which is what this derogation seeks to correct. that is why i have decided to vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report, in favour of repealing the 2003 directive on taxation of savings income, given that there is a more recent directive on the same subject. the rapporteur expressed her concern that this repeal might open up a legal loophole and has therefore included several amendments to that effect which we have supported.
in writing. the 2003 savings income tax directive was designed to collect information on savings of non-resident individuals. in the meantime, a directive on administrative cooperation covering the automatic exchange of tax information, in a general sense, was adopted in 2011 and revised in 2014 to bring it into line with global oecd standards. this directive shall enter into force on 1 january 2016. the result is that there is a great deal of overlap between the two directives, and so, in order to avoid confusion and having to comply with two different information systems, i have not opposed the repeal. however, the scope of the two directives does not coincide in their entirety, and therefore the repeal of the 2003 directive excludes certain types of low-risk savings deposits as well as any paying agents (broker, insurance, etc.), as the 2011 directive imposes the obligations on financial institutions. the directive, which is more ambitious in general, also imposes fewer disclosure requirements on foundations and trusts. the commission should take measures to correct these gaps, thus achieving adequate coverage of all financial accounts.
in writing. the 2003 savings income tax directive was designed to collect information on savings of non-resident individuals. in the meantime, a directive on administrative cooperation covering the automatic exchange of tax information, in a general sense, was adopted in 2011 and revised in 2014 to bring it into line with global oecd standards. this directive shall enter into force on 1 january 2016. the result is that there is a great deal of overlap between the two directives, and so, in order to avoid confusion and having to comply with two different information systems, i have not opposed the repeal. however, the scope of the two directives does not coincide in their entirety, and therefore, by repealing the 2003 directive, they are exempted from the obligation to report certain types of low-risk savings deposits, as well as any paying agent (broker, insurance, etc.), since the 2011 directive imposes the obligations on financial institutions. the directive, which is more ambitious in general, also imposes fewer disclosure requirements on foundations and trusts. the commission should take measures to correct these gaps, thus achieving adequate coverage of all financial accounts.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a derogation from council directive 2003/48/ec, which seeks to fill any gaps in the current legislation in the area of taxation of income from savings. the current directive leaves it up to national bilateral agreements to tax savings located in five european countries outside the union (switzerland, liechtenstein, san marino, monaco and andorra), as well as in island and overseas territories with special tax regimes. this has created numerous situations of tax competition in the field of savings, which is what this derogation seeks to correct. that is why i have decided to vote in favour.

in writing. ‒ the proposal aims to repeal the savings tax directive. in this case, the repeal of this directive must be coordinated with the amendment of the directive on administrative cooperation. the main reason for proposing such a derogation is that the administrative cooperation directive is of a much more comprehensive nature than the savings taxation directive. in view of this, i think it is necessary to vote in favour of this proposal.

in writing. ‒ in 2003, the council adopted a directive on taxation of savings income in the form of interest payments, known as the saving tax directive. the aim of the directive was to avoid distortions in capital movements and to enable the effective taxation of interest paid by paying agents established in one member state to natural persons resident in another member state. in order to ensure that there is a single rule applicable to the automatic exchange of information in the eu, to avoid situations where two different rules apply in parallel and with the aim of avoiding any interruption of the reporting, the savings tax directive should be repealed.
in writing. ‒ this report on the exchange of fingerprint data in sweden responds to decision 2008/615/jha, according to which the exchange of data to combat crossborder crime and terrorism should be subject to compliance in national legislation with european data protection provisions. in this case, sweden has fulfilled all the relevant requirements. we have always opposed the decision on crossborder police cooperation, because we believe that it does not guarantee effective protection but can be used to criminalise migrants or to store personal data without control. however, this particular report refers to compliance with data protection requirements, with which we do agree. we therefore abstained from voting.
in writing. ‒ in accordance with article 25 (2) of decision 2008/615/jha, the transfer of personal data pursuant to that decision may only be initiated when the general provisions on data protection set out in chapter 6 of that decision have been transposed into national law in the territory of the member states participating in that transfer. on 13 july 2015, the council concluded that sweden has fully implemented the general provisions on data protection set out in chapter 6 of decision 2008/615/jha. therefore, for the purposes of automated searching of dactyloscopic data, sweden should be entitled to receive and supply personal data pursuant to article 9 of decision 2008/615/jha. i have therefore voted in favour of this report, which is necessary to approve the exchange of fingerprint data with sweden.
