in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this directive because, given the changes in the tourism market and the increasing tendency of consumers to book their holidays online, it was necessary to modernise and adapt the legislation to the digital age. the adoption of this directive strengthens the rights of consumers: firstly, by covering new booking models - linked pages - combined travel comprising several travel services (flight, hotel or car rental) and purchased online will enjoy the same protection as packages purchased from travel agencies, as such linked offers in which the customer's name, payment details and email address are transferred from one provider to another and a second contract is concluded less than 24 hours after the service purchase is considered to be a combined travel for the purposes of the legislation. and secondly, by receiving detailed information on their rights, travellers will have more options to cancel the contract, and will have clear information in advance on who is responsible in the event of problems. they will also enjoy greater protection in the event of the insolvency of the entrepreneur.
in writing. ‒ this report is part of the process of adopting the directive of the european parliament and of the council on package travel and package-related services, amending regulation (ec) no 2006/2004 and directive 2011/83/eu of the european parliament and of the council and repealing council directive 90/314/eec. the council's proposal reflects parliament's concerns about the upward harmonisation of consumer rights in the field of tourism regulation. our position is therefore favourable.
in writing. ‒ the legal framework governing package travel contracts needed to be revised. the proposal aims to clarify and modernise the scope of protection and information for travellers when purchasing these services, improving their rights in line with the changes brought about by the internet. the new rules will increase transparency and strengthen consumer protection on online travel services. the european parliament has been able to ensure that travellers' protection against the insolvency of the entrepreneur covers all reasonably foreseeable expenses and all payments made by the traveller in connection with the package. the rights of travellers have been clarified, in particular on price reductions, compensation (including non-material damage) and poor contract performance. the burden of proof has been shifted to the organizers. in addition, the deadline for lodging a complaint has been extended by two years. in 2018, it will be verified whether an adjustment of the definition of 'package travel' is necessary. for all these reasons, and for other reasons, i voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this directive because, given the changes in the tourism market and the increasing tendency of consumers to book their holidays online, it was necessary to modernise and adapt the legislation to the digital age. the adoption of this directive strengthens the rights of consumers: firstly, by covering new booking models - linked pages - combined travel comprising several travel services (flight, hotel or car rental) and purchased online will enjoy the same protection as packages purchased from travel agencies, as such linked offers in which the customer's name, payment details and email address are transferred from one provider to another and a second contract is concluded within 24 hours of the purchase of the service will be considered a combined travel for the purposes of the legislation. and secondly, by receiving detailed information on their rights, travellers will have more options to cancel the contract, and will have clear information in advance on who is responsible in the event of problems. they will also enjoy greater protection in the event of the insolvency of the entrepreneur.
in writing. ‒ this report is part of the process of adopting the directive of the european parliament and of the council on package travel and package-related services, amending regulation (ec) no 2006/2004 and directive 2011/83/eu of the european parliament and of the council and repealing council directive 90/314/eec. the council's proposal reflects parliament's concerns about the upward harmonisation of consumer rights in the field of tourism regulation. we are therefore in favour of the
in writing. ‒ the new package holiday rules will apply to two types of contract: combined offers offered by operators or designed by the traveller and a new booking method, called 'linked trips', in which the buyer is guided, for example after booking an airline ticket, to contract a new service, such as a rental car, through a link. this better regulation of package tours will give travellers more options for cancellation, and they should have clear information in advance about who is responsible in the event of problems. before the traveller assumes any contractual liability, the seller must make it clear that he is contracting a package and inform the user of his rights and of the entity responsible in the event of a failure. in addition, consumers will be able to cancel their package and get their money back if the total price goes up by more than 8% or due to exceptional and unavoidable circumstances at the destination. the new rules strengthen consumer rights by covering new reservation models and providing detailed information on their rights, while also taking account of the interests of industry.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive because, given the changes in the tourism market and the increasing tendency of consumers to book their holidays online, it was necessary to modernise and adapt the legislation to the digital age. the adoption of this directive strengthens the rights of consumers: firstly, by covering new booking models - linked pages - combined travel comprising several travel services (flight, hotel or car rental) and purchased online will enjoy the same protection as packages purchased from travel agencies, as such linked offers in which the customer's name, payment details and email address are transferred from one provider to another and a second contract is concluded within 24 hours of the purchase of the service will be considered a combined travel for the purposes of the legislation. and secondly, by receiving detailed information on their rights, travellers will have more options to cancel the contract, and will have clear information in advance on who is responsible in the event of problems. they will also enjoy greater protection in the event of the insolvency of the entrepreneur.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this directive on package travel and linked travel services because it was necessary to modernise and adapt the legislation to the digital age. the adoption of this directive strengthens the rights of consumers. first, new booking models of linked pages and combined trips comprising several travel services (flight, hotel or car rental) and purchased online will enjoy the same protection as packages contracted through travel agencies; such linked offers where the customer's name, payment details and email address are transferred from one provider to another and a second contract is concluded within 24 hours of the service being purchased will be considered a combined trip for the purposes of the legislation. and secondly, consumers will be given detailed information on their rights: they will have more options to cancel the contract and will have clear information in advance on who is responsible in the event of problems. they will also enjoy greater protection in the event of the insolvency of the entrepreneur.
in writing. ‒ the directive regulating package tours was from 1990. it was time to update european legislation to take account of the growing role of the internet in shaping the travel of citizens, who no longer go to a travel agency but prefer to personalise their trips by booking transport and accommodation on different websites. the new directive we are adopting today clarifies and modernises the scope of protection for travellers who purchase combinations of travel services for the same trip or holiday, ensuring that they are better informed about the services they purchase and offering clearer solutions if something goes wrong.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the amendment rejecting the proposal on package travel and linked travel arrangements as a whole. the text presented is part of the digital single market and aims to harmonise legislation in the field of travel service providers who market their services online. the main aim is to combat hidden, unclear or ambiguous additional services, which are intended, for example, to conceal from consumers the fact that it is possible not to book certain services. however, the text presented misses the main problem. it does not oppose the abuses of dominant positions which have been progressively introduced by the most powerful digital operators. these abuses take the form of the following: the consumer who searches for a travel service on the internet is offered "targeted" choices, i.e. the search engines give him as answers the companies that are contractually linked to them. sometimes the companies that are promoted are themselves part of the same group of companies as the search engine. the result is that the largest economic players are obviously favoured at the expense of small and mediumsized enterprises.
in writing. ‒we voted against the ukip amendment which prevented this legislative resolution from passing to second reading. as this amendment was not adopted, and in accordance with the legislative procedure, there was no vote on the report, but it automatically went to second reading. this resolution contains positive aspects such as consumer protection, more information and solutions in relation to the contracting of travel and holiday packages. however, there are aspects which need to be improved, and which through the imco commission, such as extending the scope of this legislation, resolving ambiguities in cases of tariff change, economic compensation, etc.
in writing. i voted in favour of this directive because, given the changes in the tourism market and the increasing tendency of consumers to book their holidays online, it was necessary to modernise and adapt the legislation to the digital age. the adoption of this directive strengthens the rights of consumers: firstly, by covering new booking models - linked pages - combined travel comprising several travel services (flight, hotel or car rental) and purchased online will enjoy the same protection as packages purchased from travel agencies, as such linked offers in which the customer's name, payment details and email address are transferred from one provider to another and a second contract is concluded within 24 hours of the purchase of the service will be considered a combined travel for the purposes of the legislation. and secondly, by receiving detailed information on their rights, travellers will have more options to cancel the contract, and will have clear information in advance on who is responsible in the event of problems. they will also enjoy greater protection in the event of the insolvency of the entrepreneur.

in writing. ‒ this report is part of the process of adopting the directive of the european parliament and of the council on package travel and package-related services, amending regulation (ec) no 2006/2004 and directive 2011/83/eu of the european parliament and of the council and repealing council directive 90/314/eec. the council's proposal reflects parliament's concerns about the upward harmonisation of consumer rights in the field of tourism regulation. our position is therefore favourable.
in writing. ‒ the text presented to adapt combined travel - those with several elements, such as flight and car rental - and assisted travel services to the digital age has had strong support from my political group for several reasons. firstly, the current legislation dates back to 1990, when the tourism market has changed enormously with the internet and online bookings. the new rules will guarantee travellers the same protection as if they had bought their package tours from a travel agency. in addition, consumers will benefit from the coverage of new booking models, will have more information about their rights and will be able to change or cancel their trips for exceptional reasons at the place of destination such as natural disasters, and still get their money back. it is estimated that up to 120 million package holiday buyers will benefit from the new rules and that their losses will be reduced by up to eur 430 million per year. i therefore consider that this recommendation fully meets the objective of modernising the previous directive and have therefore voted in favour of it.
in writing. ‒ the legal framework governing package travel contracts needed to be revised. the proposal aims to clarify and modernise the scope of protection and information for travellers when purchasing these services, improving their rights in line with the changes brought about by the internet. the new rules will increase transparency and strengthen consumer protection on online travel services. the european parliament has been able to ensure that travellers' protection against the insolvency of the entrepreneur covers all reasonably foreseeable expenses and all payments made by the traveller in connection with the package. the rights of travellers have been clarified, in particular on price reductions, compensation (including non-material damage) and poor contract performance. the burden of proof has been shifted to the organizers. in addition, the deadline for lodging a complaint has been extended by two years. in 2018, it will be verified whether an adjustment of the definition of 'package travel' is necessary. for all these reasons, and for other reasons, i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i agree with this report, because the internet is indeed a tool with a great impact today and has led to many business areas having to restructure their offer and even their activities to adapt to this new digital age. in particular, this impact is felt in the travel sector, as more and more people are organizing and booking their trips through this tool. the type of travel has also changed, as the internet offers a much wider range of travel possibilities, resulting in fully personalised packages. the problem is that until now there were no laws that fully covered this customer profile and this put them in a delicate situation. i therefore think it is very positive that the eu has decided to update its legislation, as it will be very positive for european citizens because it benefits them and provides them with security.
madam president, i have supported this report, which deals with the question of a single european market for electronic communications. we often have a debate in our national states about what the european union does for citizens, what specific benefits it brings to them. this is precisely an example of how the creation of a single market within the european union, in this case the electronic market, is a benefit for individual citizens. citizens will not have to pay roaming charges from mid-2017. these charges have already been reduced quite substantially, there will be none, and this is evidence that the internal market brings positive benefits to citizens, to consumers. among other things, studies show that when a citizen in a foreign country uses the internet, uses a mobile phone, then uses these services much less because of roaming charges. so the end of the charges will also lead to more use of mobile networks.
madam president, the agreement i voted for and which we have just approved enshrines an idea of europe, a europe which eliminates the barriers to communication between citizens, a united europe. thanks to this agreement, we'll say goodbye to roaming. this will benefit citizens on their journeys through europe, but it also opens doors for our businesses to develop applications and services. this agreement also enshrines net neutrality. i wish the concept had been picked up. however, if we have to choose between words and principles, i choose to enshrine the principle of net neutrality, equal and non-discriminatory treatment, which is precisely what the report covers. we are therefore facing a step forward in a commitment to the digital leadership of the european union.
in writing. ‒ this regulation is of the utmost importance because it is the unequivocal expression of the benefits of the european project. the s&d group has been calling for the abolition of roaming surcharges for years. with this agreement, which i have supported, that wish will come true on june 15, 2017. it is true that the abolition has not been achieved by the end of this year, but we have managed to overcome the resistance of some member states who did not want the abolition of roaming before 2018 or a significant reduction of prices for the transitional period, as has been achieved since april 2016. this will benefit citizens travelling across the union, but also businesses, especially smes. but this agreement also enshrines the principle of net neutrality for the first time in all 28 member states. we would have wished the council had not made it impossible to include the concept in the agreement. but the definition adopted by parliament has been enshrined to ensure equal and non-discriminatory treatment of all internet traffic. the agreement is a step, but much work remains to be done to move towards the digital single market.
in writing. ‒ this report constitutes the final adoption at first reading of the council's position on the single european market for electronic communications. the proposal authorises the final adoption of an act which will have a major impact on the member states of the union by harmonising the rules on electronic communications. however, this harmonisation is carried out without sufficient guarantees to allow for net neutrality and by allowing for abuses by operators, such as roaming charges. that is why our position is against this approval.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the creation of a single european market for electronic communications because, in the context of digital globalisation as we are living in, it is necessary to urge legislative harmonisation and move towards the progressive abolition of 'digital customs'. the reduction in roaming charges will demonstrate the effectiveness of these measures at an early stage. once the transition period, which will end in june 2017, is over, the aim is to completely eliminate these roaming charges, to eliminate existing differences between member states and provide greater fluidity to the european digital market. moreover, it is essential to protect consumers in this process by ensuring firstly the principle of fair and non-discriminatory treatment and secondly the protection of personal information of end-users.

in writing. ‒ i supported this regulation that will put an end to roaming charges in the eu as of june 2017, allowing european union citizens to travel across the eu without paying extra communication surcharges. the parliament has fought for it and we will have it. this is an example of how the european union can bring concrete benefits to its citizens.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the motion to reject the commission's proposal. we are therefore against the castle pillar report because, although it puts an end to roaming within the eu (which is desirable), the european parliament has also voted on a much more worrying but less public issue: net neutrality within the community's borders. in this connection, and following the initial draft agreement published by the commission in june this year, the european parliament voted against all the amendments to a draft law which was precisely intended to ensure a single market guaranteeing electronic communications and, above all, to prevent operators from being able to prioritise traffic on their own terms, thus undermining the free and equal network we now know.

in writing. ‒ the proposal accepted in 2014 by the ep stated that roaming would disappear on 15/12/2015. unfortunately, legislation is not decided in parliament but in so-called 'trilogues' (negotiations between the council, the commission and parliament). in this case, the big parties have given the council and the big companies the opportunity to delay the end of roaming until june 2017. in addition, carriers will be able to continue to charge in exceptional cases in principle, leaving some doors open to roaming. on the other hand, as regards the principle of net neutrality, the situation is similar: many loopholes and open doors for, for example, large companies/providers to maintain a certain margin of decision according to their interests, even to alter the speed of the internet. eh bildu has tried today to get the agreement in the trilogue not accepted, so that roaming disappears in 2015 as european citizenship has long demanded and was approved in the house. the attempt by the greens/efa group has not succeeded, which is why we have voted for 12 more amendments to try to improve the council's proposal.

in writing. ‒ the report adopted aims to introduce harmonised rules that will guarantee free access to the internet, protect users' rights and eliminate the additional costs of roaming surcharges. on the first point, access to the internet must be equitable and non-discriminatory for all users. the traffic cannot be based on commercial considerations but must be subject to the technical quality of the service. the regulation also deals with consumer protection only in respect of such free access and roaming services and additional costs. consumers will now be warned that they may be falling victim to these costs when sending a message and/or making or receiving calls. finally, it was agreed to definitively eliminate roaming surcharges by 15 june 2017, although a transitional period was introduced to facilitate the transition from one phase to the other. once again, we are faced with one of those giant steps by the european union to bring it closer to its citizens. for all the above reasons and the benefits that the agreement will bring, i am in favour.
in writing. ‒ the agreement we have agreed after tough negotiations is an important step in building the digital single market. citizens will finally stop paying more for mobile roaming. in addition, despite initial opposition from the council, the european parliament has succeeded in having the principle of net neutrality mentioned for the first time. despite all this, upyd considers the two-year delay in the timetable to eliminate roaming unfair and intolerable. we live in a union without physical or economic frontiers, so it is not acceptable that the economic interests of the operators should take precedence over the interests of the citizens and the very idea of european integration. as for the mention of neutrality, it is a step forward but insufficient if what we want is to guarantee the full protection of rights and freedoms on the net. we will continue to defend the internet in the european parliament as a global public good that must be managed in the common interest and will therefore work towards a better and more complete definition of net neutrality.

in writing. ‒ first of all, i am pleased that the report has been adopted. in a world governed by globalisation, or what is the same thing, by the integration of the various international societies into a single world market, it was necessary for the european union to update itself to identify with this concept. until now, there were significant barriers between member states in relation to the online marketplace, which made online commercial activities very difficult and impeded them. i therefore believe that the creation of a digital single market in the eu will be a great step forward in its evolution, because it will not only facilitate the buying and selling of goods and services online, but will also bring significant benefits and, with it, new jobs.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to incorporate parliament's position into the commission's proposal on trade in products which can be used to apply the death penalty or to inflict torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. parliament's position reinforces the prohibition of this type of trade, including with regard to transit and export rules and services associated with this type of trade. that is why i voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ in 2006 the regulation was adopted which prohibits the export of a number of products which have no practical use other than to carry out the death penalty, torture or other ill-treatment, and requires a prior authorisation for the export of another list of products, which are in principle lawful but could also be used for unwanted purposes. however, due to the emergence of new risk products, such as anaesthetics used in third countries for lethal injection, and the rapid technological changes that have taken place, it is necessary to improve their effectiveness and to include instruments that could be used as instruments of torture and the death penalty at their destination, even if they were not originally manufactured or marketed in the eu for that purpose. the socialists have also succeeded in getting the proposal to prohibit technical assistance and commercial intermediation services and to include a generic clause allowing member states to prevent the export of other goods not covered by the regulation, which there is a reasonable suspicion could be used for torture or capital punishment in the country of destination. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal.

in writing. ‒ regulation (ec) no 1236/2005 establishes an export control regime aimed at preventing products exported from the eu from being used for the purpose of torture or other cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment. in order to provide clarity on the purpose and modalities of such controls, a specific chapter on export controls should be inserted to prevent controlled products from being used for the purpose of capital punishment. we also voted in favour of extending this control system to products in transit. we are thus improving a regulation which is consistent with the values of the charter of fundamental rights of the european union.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the report because we consider it common sense not to allow our companies to trade in third countries with materials which we have banned in europe because they are linked to inhuman or torture practices. in this report, the european parliament calls for a ban on the sale, marketing and advertising (including online) of such goods, and a ban on the transit of such goods across the union.

in writing. ‒ i would like to express my gratitude to mrs schaake and all the rapporteurs of this report. the commission's proposal is entirely relevant, we cannot allow european companies to export goods which could be used to carry out capital punishment or torture, but they cannot pay the just for the sinners, and i therefore believe that the global authorisation system will ensure that this does not happen. the award of an annual quality label to european companies will speed up the administrative procedures they are subjected to, while controlling the export of goods that could be used to apply the death penalty or inflict torture or inhuman treatment. it is very important to control the exports of goods which may be used for these purposes, but it is also important not to put obstacles and barriers in the way of european exporting companies, and a fair balance must be struck. that is why i support this proposal.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report setting out the european parliament's position on the proposal to amend directive 2011/16/eu on administrative cooperation, which aims to include the automatic exchange of information on secret tax agreements in its scope. the adopted text contains the following main elements: (a) the automatic exchange of information is not limited to resolutions considered to be 'cross-border'. (b) full retroactivity with opaque pacts still in force, irrespective of when they were signed. (c) the possibility of sanctioning states in the event of non-compliance. (d) storage of all resolutions in a database to which the commission has full access. (e) publication of summaries of the main tax rulings. i hope the council will take this into account. it is also important to extend and revise those aspects of the directive not related to the so-called tax rulings that have become outdated (unjustified exceptions to not giving the information, consideration of official secret for what should be only confidential information according to data protection regulations, etc.).
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it represents an objective improvement in the obligations to exchange information in the tax field. although this report continues to allow european tax evaders to resort to tax havens, it is an undeniable improvement. the report recognises the damage done to smes by large companies locating their profits in such havens. in our view, the exchange of information is a necessary but not sufficient condition for correcting the tax abuses that are taking place in europe. however, we recognize the value of this small step forward and that is why i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report setting out the european parliament's position on the proposal to amend directive 2011/16/eu on administrative cooperation, which aims to include the automatic exchange of information on secret tax agreements in its scope. the adopted text contains the following main elements: (a) the automatic exchange of information is not limited to resolutions considered to be 'cross-border'. (b) full retroactivity with opaque pacts still in force, irrespective of when they were signed. (c) the possibility of sanctioning states in the event of non-compliance. (d) storage of all resolutions in a database to which the commission has full access. (e) publication of summaries of the main tax rulings. i hope the council will take this into account. it is also important to extend and revise those aspects of the directive not related to the so-called tax rulings that have become outdated (unjustified exceptions to not giving the information, consideration of official secret for what should be only confidential information according to data protection regulations, etc.).

in writing. ‒ after failing to obtain approval for the management of its accounts in april, artemis has obtained it in this plenary session following the new information provided and the appearance of its director before the committee on budgetary control. on this occasion, however, as stated in the report adopted in parliament, which i have supported, the court of auditors has stipulated that the 2013 annual accounts of the joint undertaking present faithfully its financial position as at 31 december 2013 and the results of its operations and cash flows at the end of the year. it also notes improvements in audit systems, with the court receiving additional information directly from the national financial authorities from which 95% of the grants to the company originate, and progress in the implementation of the action plan to address the deficiencies identified by the court. it also points out that the company developed a new methodology for calculating the residual error rate, similar to that used by the commission services responsible for the jointly managed financing, with a residual error rate of less than 1%.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of not giving discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the council and the european council for the financial year 2013. this is not the first time that this has happened, since the council refuses to submit to the european parliament the necessary elements for us to exercise our right of scrutiny. because of this lack of cooperation, which is contrary to the principle of transparency, i have voted in favour of parliament's position, namely that we should not give discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the council and the european council for the financial year 2013.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report and therefore against granting discharge to the european council and the council, since, as the report of the committee on budgetary control once again shows, parliament does not have the information necessary to do so. the continuing difficulties which have arisen in the discharge procedures to date, due to a lack of cooperation on the part of the council, are to be deplored. in this respect, it should be recalled that parliament refused to give a discharge to the secretary-general of the council in respect of the implementation of the budgets for 2009, 2010, 2011 and 2012. the expenditure of the council is to be monitored in the same way as that of the other institutions, as a prerogative of parliament, in accordance with articles 316, 317 and 319 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union. the failure to submit the documents requested by parliament affects first of all the right to information and transparency of european citizens and, as the report points out, is a worrying symptom of a certain lack of democracy in the union's institutions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of not giving discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the council and the european council for the financial year 2013. this is not the first time that this has happened, since the council refuses to submit to the european parliament the necessary elements for us to exercise our right of scrutiny. because of this lack of cooperation, which is contrary to the principle of transparency, i have voted in favour of parliament's position, namely that we should not give discharge in respect of the implementation of the budget of the council and the european council for the financial year 2013.
in writing. ‒ today i joined many colleagues in voting against granting the 2013 european council and council discharge due to a lack of transparency, namely given that the council has refused since 2009 to give information regarding its finances. the best example of good practices have to be set at institutional level in order to earn citizens’ trust and confidence. moreover, we need to see a more open dialogue between parliament and the council, which this report also urges.
in writing. ‒ we have decided to vote in favour of not approving the management of the council and the eu council. the council refuses to provide the necessary information to enable it to examine properly the council's expenditure. there have been systematic difficulties encountered in the council's discharge procedure to date, due to lack of cooperation; parliament refused discharge in financial years 2009, 2010, 2011 and 2012, and postponed it in financial year 2013. without reliable information, the ep is unable to take an informed decision to approve the accounts.

in writing. ‒ for the seventh consecutive year, the april plenary postponed discharge. in the report, the rapporteur proposes to refuse again discharge to the european council and the council in respect of the implementation of the budget, as parliament has not received a reply to the questions put to the council in this and previous years. it is therefore necessary to vote in favour of this report, which refuses discharge on the grounds stated.

in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this resolution on the impact of ebola in the impoverished countries because we believe that it introduces a number of elements which make it possible to identify the cause of the problem and how to prevent such tragedies from occurring in the future. firstly, it values the work of non-governmental organisations positively and the response of governments and international institutions negatively. secondly, the effect of the international monetary fund's adjustment plans and the illegitimate debts to the southern countries on their health systems is recognized. the report also condemns the monopoly of large pharmaceutical companies over patents which prevent universal access to medicines and the importance of universal access to health care, calling for a new model of research and development based on principles of equality and solidarity. for all these reasons, we have supported a resolution which includes the right to public health and the need for fair trade that makes access to medicines available to all.
in writing. ‒ the ebola crisis mainly affects countries living in extreme poverty and vulnerability, with almost non-existent health systems. the european union, as a world leader in developing countries, has a responsibility and a duty to promote the right to universal health care. the key pillars of this cooperation are to secure financial support from who, to promote effective and fair r&d funding and to decouple these costs from the final price of medicines, to strengthen national health systems and facilitate universal access to health and medicines, and to support the establishment of a regional centre for infectious disease research in west africa. we must stress the vital importance for the countries most affected by this crisis - sierra leone, liberia and guinea - of receiving aid to get their economies moving. the report also calls for the funding gap for humanitarian action to be addressed, particularly in the area of health, and thus to strengthen the resilience of the countries concerned. i have therefore supported this report.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this resolution on the impact of ebola in the impoverished countries because we believe that it introduces a number of elements which make it possible to identify the cause of the problem and how to prevent such tragedies from occurring in the future. firstly, it values the work of non-governmental organisations positively and the response of governments and international institutions negatively. secondly, the effect of the international monetary fund's adjustment plans and the illegitimate debts to the southern countries on their health systems is recognized. the report also condemns the monopoly of large pharmaceutical companies over patents which prevent universal access to medicines and the importance of universal access to health care, calling for a new model of research and development based on principles of equality and solidarity. for all these reasons, we have supported a resolution which includes the right to public health and the need for fair trade that makes access to medicines available to all.
in writing. ‒ the ebola crisis has demonstrated the need to strengthen cooperation with developing countries, beyond the emergency aid that can be provided at the height of the health crises in these countries. the european union's action must therefore be in the field of development cooperation, to strengthen local health systems, which is also a necessary condition for contributing to poverty reduction. i therefore voted in favour of the report, convinced that the basis must be laid for long-term cooperation capable of preventing future crises, with emphasis on strengthening local health systems, to help give these countries a greater degree of autonomy in managing such crises.
in writing. ‒ today i voted in favour of this report on the ebola crisis. without doubt, the ebola outbreak presented an enormous challenge to medical authorities in affected countries. i am pleased to see that a vital aspect of the report is quick access to proven vaccines. the populations of liberia and sierra leone should be guaranteed access to new vaccines which have proven to be completely effective in guinea. in order to minimise and even prevent further outbreaks in developing countries, we simply must strengthen their health systems and learn from the mistakes of the past.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the report because it contains key elements for understanding the ebola epidemic of 2014 and 2015, which has killed nearly 12 000 people worldwide. the report, for example, stresses the importance of robust public health systems to deal with such epidemics, denounces the austerity in health followed by african countries under the mandate of the world bank and international monetary fund adjustment programs in the 80s and 90s and calls for exploring alternatives to the current model of research and development of medicines to make it go beyond the logic of the search for profit and respond to the demands of global health as a fundamental human right.

in writing. ‒ the text presented welcomes the new vaccine tested with 100% effectiveness in guinea in march this year and urges facilitating access to liberia and sierra leone. however, the guard should not be lowered with regard to some new cases that have appeared and their mode of transmission, which is still unclear. the report calls on the international community to develop educational and information campaigns in the affected countries. it is important to stress and support the reform announced by the who in may this year, which aims to establish a new emergency programme with a new reserve fund of 100 million dollars and a number of reservists worldwide to be deployed on the ground. it is also very important to work on conflict prevention, as this increases the fragility and vulnerability of health systems, and to fight against the social stigmatisation of patients and their environment in the face of future and possible new crises. the response to the ebola crisis was slow in the first few months, so anything that can be learned from it will deserve my support.

in writing. ‒ we are talking about a report that draws on lessons learned from the ebola crisis that took place in sierra leone, liberia and guinea. the report calls for the establishment of a european rapid response mechanism including experts in the field who can be deployed quickly. it also stressed the importance of investing in the health sector for economic development and poverty reduction in developing countries and called for the european development fund to be reviewed so that investments in health and good governance become priority areas for all countries with weak public infrastructure. we are therefore talking about a positive report and i think we must vote in favour of it.

in writing. ‒ the 2014-2015 ebola epidemic has been the largest epidemic outbreak of the disease to date. it originated in december 2013 in guinea and has since spread to several countries, including some in the eu. although it was eventually brought under control, it caused a period of great unrest among the eu population, a considerable number of infections and even deaths. i therefore believe that we do not need any more evidence to ensure that investment is needed in the development of health crisis prevention and assistance programmes, which will enable the eu to react quickly and effectively to any new cases that may occur in the future. this would create a framework for cooperation between member states, which would speed up all the processes. thank you very much, mr. president.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution on emission measurement in the automotive sector because it strongly condemns the fraud committed by volkswagen, which installed deactivation devices in at least eleven million diesel vehicles to circumvent eu environmental legislation. as a socialist, i regret that millions of consumers have been misled by false information about the emissions of their vehicles, emissions which cause damage to human health and environmental damage, and i have demanded in this resolution that workers should not have to pay the price for the manipulations, bearing in mind at the same time that the automobile industry is one of the sectors which contributes most to growth, innovation and employment. we call for legislative changes to improve the measurement of emissions in the car sector through the introduction of real driving tests and for consideration to be given to the creation of an eu-wide monitoring authority to detect breaches of emission limits, to prevent this from happening again.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it condemns the multinational company volkswagen for the emissions scandal, demanding guarantees on the measures to be taken to correct the situation it has caused. the resolution calls for the protection of jobs in the motor vehicle sector, which can under no circumstances be put at risk by the practices of a counterfeiting directive. it also draws attention to the role played by the european commission, which had information on the problem since 2011. although it is not the best possible resolution, i have decided to vote in favour of it because it is a wake-up call to the multinational and the authorities involved in the scandal.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it strongly condemns the fraud in the measurement of polluting emissions from cars, fraud committed by volkswagen by installing deactivation devices in at least eleven million diesel vehicles to circumvent eu environmental legislation. as a socialist, i regret that millions of consumers have been misled by false information about the emissions of their vehicles, emissions which cause damage to human health and damage to the environment, and i have called in this resolution for workers not to pay the price for the manipulations, bearing in mind at the same time that the car industry is one of the sectors which contributes most to growth, innovation and employment. we call for legislative changes to improve the measurement of emissions through the introduction of real driving tests and for consideration to be given to the creation of an eu-wide monitoring authority to detect breaches of emission limits, to prevent this situation from recurring.
in writing. ‒ following the research of an ngo, volkswagen admitted to having installed illegal software to cheat emission tests in the laboratory in at least 11 million vehicles worldwide, thus admitting a fraud affecting millions of consumers. the same test results were also made available to the eu and national authorities, but no action was taken at the time. a further revelation showed that a 2011 report by the joint research centre, a body of the eu, already pointed out discrepancies between emissions measured in the laboratory and on-road performance. it suggested that this gap could be due to the inadequacy of the test procedure in the eu and to the use of defeat devices. in the light of such fraud, i welcome this resolution that condemns this fraud, asks for transparency and appropriate sanctions to be taken and urges the commission to implement real driving emission tests. i also voted in favour of the establishment of a european parliament committee of inquiry in order to conduct an investigation on the responsibility of the commission and of member states in the lack of implementation and enforcement of the eu law.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of the resolution because, according to the european commission's research centre, in 2013 car emissions testing was problematic because it could enable the use of rigged devices that activate or modify the emissions control systems with the aim of improving their effectiveness during the checks. the volkswagen scandal is the tip of the iceberg of a fraudulent system but it is not an isolated case; they have rigged the engines of millions of diesel cars worldwide, polluting up to 40 times more than is permitted, and we consider it vital that the emission control mechanisms be modified to be carried out in real driving circumstances and that this situation is not repeated. the resolution also stresses the importance of ensuring that employees are not the ones who ultimately pay for the consequences of company breaches.

in writing. ‒ the figures for air pollution are alarming and the car industry has a lot to do with it. in the european union up to 430 000 people die prematurely each year from the effects of such pollution. the costs of the effects on the health of citizens are as high as eur 940 billion. it is estimated that up to one third of the urban population in the eu is exposed to levels exceeding the limit values and targets set by the eu. these figures are more than illustrative of the need to do something about it, especially after the scandal we have heard about volkswagen, which has violated pollution regulations. the report therefore seeks to move towards an increasingly sustainable and resource-efficient system for land transport and other modes. in addition, it is absolutely necessary to investigate in depth the manipulation of emission test results in several member states and other countries around the world. i have therefore supported this report.

mr president, madam vice-president, mr minister, since the commission presented its budget proposal to us, we have been working in this parliament to see whether the priorities of the european union were in line with the resources of the union, and i think that no one will be surprised if we say that we do not think that there are enough resources. so what our proposal implies is an increase of 3.6 billion euros for 2016, which, on the surface, may seem like a large figure, but which, if we look at it with the budget, is only a 2.34% increase. a small increment, a small gesture, but one that would allow for a big impact. because with these extra 3.6 billion we could offset, for example, the cuts we were forced to make under the juncker plan, and thus be able to meet the research and infrastructure objectives we set ourselves. or we could also renew the commitment to combat youth unemployment by funding the youth guarantee for another year. or we could compensate our farmers and cattle farmers, who are being affected by the russian veto or the milk crisis. and yes, with these 3.6 billion we could finance measures to provide care in a minimum of dignity to those thousands of people who have had to leave their homes. but, madam commissioner and mr minister, today, beyond this short-term debate about whether more money is needed here or there, we must go a step further. the rapporteur. mr president, during the last parliamentary term one of the most controversial aspects of the negotiation process for the regulation on common provisions for the structural and investment funds was the so-called 'macroeconomic conditionality' of article 23. i would like to begin by thanking all the alternative rapporteurs and their political groups for their availability and cooperation throughout the broad negotiating process which has made the agreement contained in this report possible. we are all concerned about the practical implications of the reprogramming and suspension of funds that may result from macro-conditionality. in a time of crisis such as the present, which has led to a sharp fall in investment, cohesion policy is key to maintaining the level of investment in member states and their regions, in particular for the improvement of employment. we therefore believe that macroeconomic conditionality should be considered as a last resort, with the sole aim of contributing to a more efficient use of the funds. that is, any decision under article 23 is only appropriate in exceptional contexts and must be well considered and fully justified in order to ensure its transparency, verification and review. and so it is reflected in this report. as enshrined in the treaty, the achievement of the objectives of the structural and investment funds should not be hampered by economic governance mechanisms, which prevents recognition of their importance in contributing to a stable macroeconomic environment and to an efficient and results-oriented cohesion policy. and in this report i also wanted to highlight something that was not the subject of the commission's communication: the role that parliament had to play in making this decision much more democratic. and so good institutional coordination is essential to ensure complementarity in the interaction between cohesion and good economic governance. in this connection, i have paid particular attention to the involvement of the european parliament in the event of the activation of macro-conditionality, regretting the commission's guidelines, which contain no reference to it. the commission, council and parliament must establish a structured dialogue at interinstitutional level, which ensures constant and clear cooperation and an adequate flow of information throughout the process. parliament must be informed immediately of any request for rescheduling and suspension of payments so that it can express its position in a timely manner and so that it can be taken into account by the commission, which we will hold to account. and we also call for an early warning approach to the member states affected by rescheduling, while asking the commission to carry out, in close cooperation with the member state concerned, a thorough analysis of all the options other than the application of article 23, which has to be applied only as an exception and at the last moment. these are some of the principles and aspects and demands i want to highlight in this first speech. it is therefore a report which i consider to be balanced and which is also aimed - and i have made a special effort in this respect - at the fairest and most democratic application of article 23. i was against article 23. now is not the time for that discussion. the discussion now is how article 23 can be applied so that its application is as fair and as democratic as possible.
the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the social partners are able to take part in the negotiations. mr president, commissioner creţu, macro-conditionality, i.e. the possibility of imposing sanctions for non-compliance with deficit or debt targets, has been introduced into the stability and growth pact since its signing, but transferring it to cohesion policy is the biggest mistake and the biggest mistake the european commission has made in its crisis policies in recent years. firstly, because social and cohesion policy is the only policy of strong solidarity, of sharing, of redistribution of income that the european union has. as i said, the introduction of macro-conditionality in cohesion policy is not only a clever idea, but it is a mistake because it is not applicable. you have shown this yourself with the recent decisions taken in the case of greece. secondly, because withdrawing funds is contrary to social cohesion, it is further detrimental to territorial convergence and it is also counter-cyclical in that it imposes a counter-cyclical element of economic growth on the member states that are doing the worst. we in the committee on employment therefore fully support mr blanco's report, we thank him for his work and we are absolutely convinced that the objective of mitigating the effects of article 23 is the right way to a better european union, a better social union. the rapporteur. madam president, thank you very much for your thoughts. i repeat, this is a balanced report and it is aimed at a fair and balanced application of the possible article 23 mechanism. throughout my political life, if i have worked for anything, it has been for social and territorial cohesion, for the cohesion of people and territories, and this report is precisely moving in that direction. it is precisely because of a broad consensus that it is moving forward, since even those groups which, like the gue/ngl, have tabled amendments to the report itself, have abstained in committee, which shows that this report is quite balanced, quite fair and quite advanced. i would also like to say, from my point of view, and this is reflected in the document, that article 23 cannot be used to exclude from the funds - mr juaristi referred to this - those who are unable to invest or attract investment, as their situation is deteriorating. this means that those facing socioeconomic difficulties and counting on the funds as a significant part of their investment should not suffer any additional losses. i therefore reject, and i want to say this very clearly, that regions or local authorities - as well as the citizens themselves who receive funds - can be paralysed as a result of the macroeconomic failure of a central level of administration. that is why, ladies and gentlemen, there is no doubt that frequent rescheduling would be counterproductive. it should therefore be avoided in order not to disrupt the management of the funds, undermine the stability and predictability of the multiannual investment strategy and to avoid any negative impact on the absorption of the funds. the penalising nature of any suspension of payments should also be emphasised and the commission should be requested to exercise its discretion with the utmost caution, having considered all the elements arising from the structured dialogue and the views expressed therein. finally, i welcome the intention expressed by the commission to limit to the maximum the reprogramming and suspensions which are unnecessary in the medium term, since the programmes and cooperation agreements adopted in the current period take account of the country-specific recommendation and the relevant council recommendations.

mr president, commissioner, you are right in what you have said in your speech, but whatever the feelings that gmos arouse, apart, of course, from sound scientific arguments, it is logical that the commission's proposal should be rejected simply because it is contrary to the principles of the single market. i would like to point out the contradictory attitude of many countries which, while prohibiting their farmers from growing genetically modified crops, allow their farmers to feed their livestock with imported and genetically modified proteins from third countries. all this distorts the debate, and it is understandable, to a certain extent, that the commission intends to delegate responsibility to the member states. however, the solution proposed by the commission is not the most appropriate, since it would leave the authorization of cultivation to national policies which are not concerned with scientific and food safety considerations most of the time. the european union has already lost the train of biotechnology and has left the vanguard to third countries which sell their production to us for our consumption. the new proposal to renationalize gmo crops could, in addition to breaking up the single market, have the unintended effect of exacerbating the shortage of feed and increasing the high price our farmers already pay for having to import these products that we cannot grow within the european union. the authorization of gmos is not a question of democracy; it is a question of food safety and science, but of independent science, such as that of the european food safety authority.
mr president, the debate on genetically modified organisms has been a very contentious one for years, and i personally believe that the opponents have not yet put forward any sound scientific reasons justifying any ban, either on the cultivation or on the marketing of these products for food, while, surprisingly, gmos are fully accepted in the pharmaceutical industry without any problem, and for years, for treatments such as diabetes or cancer. fifty-eight gmos have been authorised by the european union after undergoing very rigorous health and quality controls. behind these 58 gmos are, of course, years and years of research and progress which make it possible, for example, to supply fodder for livestock and thus compensate for the shortage of feed production in the european union. the european union today needs to import genetically modified soya from third countries to meet this shortage of feed for livestock. and this is a fact that no one can deny, not even those countries which are banning the cultivation of gmos on their territory, because they are at the same time committing an inconsistency by allowing gmos to enter into that same territory. so above all, i think that today we must forget about value judgments about gmos and that our aim should be to legislate consistently. if we want a market which favours the free movement of people, goods and capital, and in line with that policy, i think we must reject this commission proposal because it breaks up the single market. i therefore want to express my absolute, total support for the rapporteur, mr la via, in rejecting this proposal from the european commission.

member of the commission.– mr president, first let me thank the rapporteur, james nicholson, and the shadow rapporteurs, pilar ayuso, pavel poc, marit paulsen, lynn boylan, bart staes and eleonora evi, for the compromise text on novel foods we have in front of us today. i very much appreciate their hard work and commitment which has led to a good outcome. the right balance has been reached in ensuring that only safe foods may be placed on the market, while allowing for innovation in the agri-food sector. the current regulation on novel foods dates back to 1997. over the last 18 years, scientific innovation in the food sector has progressed, giving rise to the creation of new types of food products. in parallel, consumption patterns among citizens have also changed. the commission considers it necessary to adopt and improve an up-to-date legislative framework on novel foods to ensure food safety and to protect human health, while also facilitating the functioning of the internal market. this approach will ensure that innovation in the food sector can lead to the placing on the market of new scientifically—assessed safe foods. with a view to updating the current rules, the commission proposes to streamline the authorisation procedure, through a centralised procedure at commission level, by granting general authorisation and by ensuring a centralised safety assessment by the european food safety authority. to improve efficiency, deadlines would be established for the evaluation and authorisation procedure, thus reducing the overall time spent on approvals. to improve transparency, the commission would also make available on its website a summary of applications, as well as a list of applications that did not result in authorisation. this is in line with a request from this house. the safety of novel foods remains the main criterion for authorisation. the european food safety authority will be systematically consulted on all questions relating to the safety of novel foods. in conclusion, innovation will be facilitated without compromising on food safety. over the years, third countries have criticised our current rules, claiming that some foods that are traditional in their diets are considered to be novel foods in the european union. this agreement will help us to simplify the authorisation procedure of so-called traditional foods from third countries with a history of safe use, and facilitate their placing on the market. at the same time, safety must not be compromised. to this end, if safety concerns are raised, we will ask the opinion of the european food safety authority. the proposed new regulation on novel foods would contribute to innovation and facilitate market access on the agri-food sector by bringing clarity to the authorisation procedure. it would allow support for true innovators through its data protection provisions. applicants who are able to present safety studies based on their own protected data would benefit from an individual authorisation for five years. let me finish by again expressing my satisfaction regarding the compromise that parliament and the council have reached on this proposal, to which the commission can offer its full support.
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, first of all i would like to thank mr nicholson, the alternative rapporteurs and also the commission and the council for the exercise of flexibility that we all made in reaching this agreement after many hours of work. this regulation is necessary, as the commissioner has said, because since 1997 food technology has advanced so much that we cannot continue, 18 years later, without amending outdated legislation. we have already aborted an agreement in this parliament in 2011. and today the whole agri-food sector is waiting for us to be responsible and support this agreement, which is good and balanced. it should be made very clear that this is not a regulation on animal cloning or on nanotechnology. it is a legislation which only sets out rules for the classification, scientific evaluation and authorisation of new foods which strictly meet food safety requirements. that is why efsa will be responsible for scientifically evaluating them, and all with absolute transparency. the amendments tabled - which, by the way, are taken from the agreement with some additions - are apparently only intended to boycott an agreement which, i repeat, is very good and balanced. on behalf of my group, and of course on behalf of my own, i ask the house to support what has been agreed in the tripartite dialogues, by making a gesture of responsibility and support for the many smes that are waiting for us.
madam president, i would first of all like to congratulate mr nicholson, the rapporteur, and the other rapporteurs on a great job. the current legislation is from 1997, as mentioned, almost 19 years ago. there have undoubtedly been technological changes which must be taken into account and our legislation must therefore be adapted to strengthen our food sectors. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. this is a regulation which, as other colleagues have said, is very much in demand. today we are here in the final stage, after a very controversial start in 2011, and until now; and i want to express my explicit support for these commitments contained in the agreement. i trust in the european guarantee systems and i believe that the approval of this very reasonable agreement should not be jeopardised.
madam president, we must be tough on greenhouse gas emissions. the european union must also regulate as soon as possible the emission of methane, which causes respiratory and cardiovascular diseases and seriously damages crops in the mediterranean countries, if it is to be credible at the paris summit. what is at stake is the health of the planet, of people and, let us not forget, the bread of many farmers and fishermen. it is not enough that this report is approved, either. its implementation must be monitored. i therefore call on the european commission to fulfil its duties, not as it did in the volkswagen case. because it will also be of no use for governments like the pp to come here to brussels and tell you to make an olympic decision on the commitments you have made so that diesel can pollute 43% more. so, therefore, let's stop patting each other on the back. let's be demanding with accountability and responsibility, whoever it is and whoever falls. what's in the future is the health of our planet, which is the only home we have.
member of the commission.– madam president, i would like also to thank the honourable members for their valid comments and for their valid arguments. we keep reminding each other that we need to be more realistic and that we need to look more at reality, and i could not agree more. that is exactly what we should be doing and the biggest reality is that we have almost half a million european citizens dying every year from poor air quality, plus a bigger number with chronic respiratory diseases. the reality is that we need to stop this. as several of you have stressed in your statements, our citizens increasingly demand action to address the health impacts of air pollution. efforts are needed from all sectors, including agri-industry. it is important to keep the level of ambition for ammonia in line with the overall objective and to retain methane in the proposal. this will not have any negative effect on animal welfare and will not require keeping them inside, as some of members have tried to suggest. on the overall ambition, i share the rapporteur’s concern that if the position of this house is too far from that of the council, this will jeopardise the chances of agreement. i would therefore encourage your support for a plenary position close to the original proposal of the commission for all pollutants. it was also encouraging to note that we all agree on the objectives and it would be a big pity not to agree on how we can achieve these same objectives. a number of members referred to the supplementary impact assessment done by the european parliament’s own services. while this shows that with the climate and energy package we can deliver greater air pollution reduction for broadly the same cost, it also shows that we can deliver the same reduction at a lower cost. given that the assessment does not fully reflect the latest state of play, i feel the latter message should carry more weight. with regard to a number of other proposed amendments, many improve the original proposal. however, i would make two last comments. on the interim targets for 2025, it is important to ensure steady progress towards the 2030 reductions. but if the interim targets become binding, this could in some cases lead to disproportionate costs. hence i would support a solution based around the original commission proposal. with regard to reduction commitments for mercury, as emissions from all major sources are regulated under the industrial emissions directive, reduction commitments under the nec directive would not further reduce emissions. furthermore exposure of eu citizens to mercury is largely due to emissions from third countries. the commission is preparing the ratification of the minamata convention on mercury which is expected to curb those emissions and thereby reduce exposure of eu citizens to this toxic substance. as i said earlier on, every month that passes delays the implementation of policies that could alleviate the problems with bad air quality. i call on your support today to pave the way for a viable agreement between the co-legislators during the first reading. let me conclude by making some final remarks. first, this is not just about a better environment, it is about avoiding and reducing further deaths as a result of our non-action. polluted air kills; non-action does the same. eu citizens deserve, expect and have a right to action. we all acknowledge that we have a serious, lethal problem, so let us all come together towards a much-needed responsible solution. finally, let me assure everyone here that we are not after less agriculture, we are not after less economic growth, what we are after is better and healthier agriculture, what we are after is better economic growth that will contribute to better living and not to premature deaths.
in writing. this proposal is a further step towards reducing pollutant emissions and avoiding their cross-border spread. as with any proposal, the aim must be to achieve the best possible cost-benefit ratio and the best possible result. the exclusion of the outermost regions and the safeguards contained in the text for livestock farms as regards ammonia from manure and methane are consistent. we cannot and must not have the luxury of undermining our agriculture. we need to keep the methane and mercury out until we have an impact assessment. it is necessary to ensure that vehicle test methods are compatible with real driving conditions, because cars are the biggest polluter in urban areas. objectives for 2025 are also not necessary, as the proposal already includes them for 2020 and 2030.
in writing. ‒ our position on the 2016 eu budget has been to increase spending on all those budget lines aimed at improving the functioning of the european union. we have refused to finance european programmes which have an impact on the interests of the military industry or which support institutions such as frontex, with little profit for european citizens. we have also proposed and supported programmes of aid to the countries subject to the troika, to the occupied palestinian territories and various programmes aimed at creating jobs and supporting different sectors, and we have tried to avoid cuts in the items most important to the european economy. we believe that the union's budget should avoid austerity policies in order to boost the economy and we have voted in favour of this.

in writing. ‒ in this report i followed my political group line in almost every area, except in such articles referring to the implementation of austerity plans. for in these articles i therefore abstained, as the debate cannot be reduced to a ‘pro’ or ‘contra’ one. moreover, i did not support any increase in parliamentary assistance allowances, or funding to political parties and foundations, as i believe that the funding today is more than enough, and should not be increased any more. in the case of the free vote on using cap funding for bull fighting, i voted along my personal conviction, which is in favour, however i accept that it is a divisive and emotive issue for many.
in writing. ‒ we abstained in the vote on this document which determines parliament's negotiating position with the commission and the council. firstly, because the budget is slightly better than in previous years (very slight increase), with its lights (increase in humanitarian spending on refugees, improvement of educational aspects, research, youth employment initiative and support for smes) and its shadows (diversion of resources to an insufficient and problematic investment model - the efsi - and a significant percentage of additional resources for europe - strength and increased competitiveness). secondly, and mainly, because it is a matter of countering the council's regressive proposal, which would be much worse. the resolution is critical of the council's approach and includes several calls for extraordinary measures, the revision of the multiannual financial framework to achieve more flexibility or the promotion of quality employment. since the resulting budgets will presumably help to perpetuate a neoliberal eu, with a ridiculous and non-redistributive budget, we shall vote against them later.
in writing. ‒ overall satisfactory assessment of the result reached in committee reflecting the overall agreement for the 2016 budget between s&d, epp and alde, which has also been mostly followed by the greens. the position adopted by the committee on budgets: replaces all the cuts proposed by the council in the draft budget presented by the commission for 2016 in respect of commitment appropriations; proposes a substantial increase in the draft commission budget for political priorities, in particular. the ep's proposal now amounts to eur 157 427 547 086 in commitment appropriations, i.e. eur 2 520 million more than the draft budget (+1.63 per cent). i would like to stress in particular my individual vote in favour of the amendment prohibiting the allocation of resources from the european budget to bullfighting activities, which was adopted. for all these reasons, i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the 2016 eu general budget because it proposes an increase to finance our political priorities, and more specifically to offset the cuts in the agreement on the european fund for strategic investments (efsi) to meet the r & d & i and infrastructure objectives we have set ourselves, to secure the additional resources needed for the internal and external dimension of the refugee crisis, to renew our commitment against youth unemployment by funding the youth employment initiative for another year and to compensate our farmers and livestock farmers, who are being affected by the russian veto or the milk crisis. our proposal amounts to eur 157 427 547 086 in commitment appropriations, an increase of eur 3 600 million for 2016 which in reality represents only a 2.34% increase. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of the term 'competent authority' to cover the whole of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this resolution on the budget of the european union because it does not recognise the political importance of this instrument for boosting the economy of the 28 member states. the resolution contains positive points; in fact it is a much better position than that of the council, for example it condemns the cuts caused by the reallocation of funds which has resulted from the establishment of the efsi. however, we do not think that it covers all the needs of the union in the budgetary field, which needs an economic policy tool that increases public spending in the absence of any improvement in the international economy. that is why i could not vote in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because, despite its limitations, it responds to the urgent need to speed up the functioning of european justice. doubling the number of judges in the general court was not the first choice of the s&d group or of parliament as a whole; however, it would be worse than not reaching our maximum programme to allow the situation to remain as it is. the delays currently experienced by judicial processes harm citizens and unjustifiably increase the cost of the whole system. the economic costs of these delays far exceed the cost of the proposed reform; moreover, their costs in terms of trust and legitimacy are incalculable. it is no coincidence that this reform has its origin in a request from the court of justice of the eu itself. this reform also opens the door to gender parity in the european justice system, where it has been sorely lacking. it is an achievement that we should not underestimate, because it is the first step towards fulfilling a long-awaited commitment to equality in this field.
in writing. ‒ the court of justice of the european union requested in 2011 a legislative initiative to amend its statute with the aim of allowing an increase in the number of judges for the general court, based on an increase in its workload. the number of judges has varied, not so much because of this but because the member states have maintained the criterion of appointing their own judge. in 2014, the cj proposed to double the number of judges in three phases (28 more judges), to reach two judges per member state by 2019, and to abolish the civil service tribunal, a proposal supported by the council. however, i consider that the request of the cj to double the number of judges is not appropriate, since the data provided on the accumulation of pending cases and the duration of proceedings do not agree. nor does its proposal promote transparency in the appointment of judges. the court of justice is asking for a drastic increase in its budget without any justification, and it is also not justifying its request to abolish the cfp adequately, so i have voted against this proposal for a regulation at second reading.
