in writing. ‒ there are currently 28 judges at the general court, one from each member state. in addition, there are 7 judges working for the civil service tribunal. the fact is that the general court is absolutely saturated. the current time to reach a decision in sensitive cases is four to five years and there is a risk of a non-contractual liability claim against the union for undue delays of the order of millions of dollars. in june this year, the council informed parliament that it had already adopted its position at first reading on the matter, including the amendments to the statute allowing the increase of 28 judges in three distinct phases: 12 judges in 2015, 7 judges on 1 september 2016 and 9 judges on 1 september 2019. with the adoption of this report by parliament and the negotiating mandate, we support the council's position to increase the number of judges by one per member state. it's a matter that's been stuck for too long. the present situation calls for practical and rapid action to improve the work of the general court.

in writing. ‒ due to the delay in the settlement of cases and the accumulation of pending cases, the cjeu requested in 2011 that twelve new judges be added. this is the enlargement which i have supported today with my vote. furthermore, i have supported that those 12 new judges be chosen on the basis of their knowledge and experience. what i have not been able to do is to vote in favour of the council's position, which, unable to agree on how to elect these 12 judges - since there would then be 40 judges in total and the 28 member states would not be represented at the court by the same number of judges - proposes to include more judges than the court itself requested, with the resulting charge for the european public purse. i also did not support the proposal not to add any additional judges, because the ecj has an essential function 'to ensure uniform enforcement of european law in the member states' and must be provided with the necessary resources to enforce it without delay or delay.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of a large part of the article on the number of judges. the increase in the number of judges is necessary to increase the time taken in the large-scale general court proceedings in the union. the dossier includes a number of important amendments such as the gender balance and the insistence on transparent opposition systems. we believe that without these measures the dossier would be meaningless and the increase in the number of judges would simply mean the creation of more power in a system which is already far from the citizens of the union. it is these kinds of improvements that enable the court of justice to begin its approach to european citizens.

in writing. ‒ the court of justice of the european union requested in 2011 a legislative initiative to amend its statute with the aim of allowing an increase in the number of judges for the general court, based on an increase in its workload. the number of judges has varied, not so much because of this but because the member states have maintained the criterion of appointing their own judge. in 2014, the cj proposed to double the number of judges in three phases (28 more judges), to reach two judges per member state by 2019, and to abolish the civil service tribunal, a proposal supported by the council. however, i consider that the request of the cj to double the number of judges is not appropriate, since the data provided on the accumulation of pending cases and the duration of proceedings do not agree. nor does its proposal promote transparency in the appointment of judges. the court of justice is asking for a drastic increase in its budget without any justification, and it is also not justifying its request to abolish the cfp adequately, so i have voted against this proposal for a regulation at second reading.
in writing. ‒ the european parliament already voted by majority two years ago on a proposal to expand to 40 judges, in order to solve the bottleneck in european jurisdiction. the council, however, failed to bring the member states, which always look out for their own interests, to an agreement and, despite the urgency of the time, let this opportunity pass. now, two years later, they have made a hasty proposal of 56 judges, poorly worded (it does not provide, for example, for the extra hiring of additional judicial secretaries) and dragging on time, while rushing parliament to approve it. the large groups, as usual, have been complicit in this mess and have voted in favour, forgetting parliament's position as set out above.

in writing. ‒ this european parliament recommendation for second reading on the council position on the amendment of the regulation on the provisions applicable to fisheries in the gfcm (general fisheries commission for the mediterranean) agreement area was adopted without a vote by parliament. however, there are certain modifications which should be noted. the council's position is less ambitious than the initial proposal, especially because of insufficient weighting of the criteria for conservation of resources. it allows member states to be granted derogations under the gfcm proposals, provided that they have an appropriate national management framework with a well-defined fishing permit scheme and appropriate spatiotemporal closure measures for the limited use of certain red coral colonies. such exemptions may be corrected by the commission if the assumptions are not confirmed. it also sets out a minimum depth of catch, defines minimum dimensions for the fish and prohibits the use of remotely piloted vehicles (except in very special circumstances) and trawling in coastal areas, although it also allows member states to make exceptions.
in writing. ‒ regulation (eu) no 1343/2011 on certain provisions applicable to fisheries in the gfcm agreement area is updated, incorporating into union law the obligations arising from the conservation and control measures adopted by the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) between 2011 and 2014. it should be noted that the council reached a high degree of consensus on this proposal, since in establishing its position it took full account of the commission proposal and the position of the european parliament at first reading, and the agreements reached on the amendments to the draft recommendation were reflected in the draft recommendation which was examined by the committee on fisheries on 23 september and has now been submitted to the plenary for approval. therefore, you have my vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ this european parliament recommendation for second reading on the council position on the amendment of the regulation on the provisions applicable to fisheries in the gfcm (general fisheries commission for the mediterranean) agreement area was adopted without a vote by parliament. however, there are certain modifications which should be noted. the council's position is less ambitious than the initial proposal, especially because of insufficient weighting of the criteria for conservation of resources. it allows member states to be granted derogations under the gfcm proposals, provided that they have an appropriate national management framework with a well-defined fishing permit scheme and appropriate spatiotemporal closure measures for the limited use of certain red coral colonies. such exemptions may be corrected by the commission if the assumptions are not confirmed. it also sets out a minimum depth of catch, defines minimum dimensions for the fish and prohibits the use of remotely piloted vehicles (except in very special circumstances) and trawling in coastal areas, although it also allows member states to make exceptions.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour as the european parliament and the council reached an agreement on the incorporation into union law of several recommendations made by the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm agreement), which establishes an appropriate framework for multilateral cooperation in order to promote the development, conservation, rational management and better exploitation of living marine resources in the mediterranean and the black sea at levels considered sustainable and with a low risk of depletion.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this regulation is to transfer into eu law a number of recommendations adopted by the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean agreement area. these measures include the sustainable exploitation of red coral, the reduction of incidental catches (seabirds, sea turtles and seals), encouragement of a high level of protection from fishing activities for sharks and rays. these measures can only be viewed as a positive step and therefore i welcome this agreement.
in writing. ‒ the aim of this project is to define technical measures to preserve fisheries resources while respecting the legitimate interests of fishermen. the first problem raised by this project was the demand of the black sea member states to be able to continue to use trawls and gillnets. this request was the subject of a compromise: it will therefore be allowed, exceptionally, to use these devices in the black sea coastal zone. the second problem was raised by certain states, including spain, which requested derogations to continue harvesting red coral, an endangered species. here again, a compromise was reached, since the states which have established or will establish, in the next three years, a national management framework, will be able to continue exploiting red coral. in the event of a threat to this species, the commission will intervene to request changes to these national management frameworks. similarly, the use of remotely operated underwater vehicles (rovs) for the observation and prospecting of red coral may continue, provided that they are not used for cutting or harvesting. those derogations shall expire on 31 december 2015.
in writing. ‒ we voted against this report because we do not agree to introduce exceptions to the gfcm agreement, aimed at allowing trawling in the black sea. despite the limitations expressly set out in the agreement for the whole of the mediterranean, this concession to the black sea coast member states is seriously damaging to the ecosystems of the seabed and we believe that the european institutions should strive to protect them rather than facilitate their deterioration for third parties.
in writing. ‒ regulation (eu) no 1343/2011 on certain provisions applicable to fisheries in the gfcm agreement area is updated, incorporating into union law the obligations arising from the conservation and control measures adopted by the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean (gfcm) between 2011 and 2014. it is therefore a legislative dossier of ordinary procedure, which should be noted that it has been dealt with with a high degree of consensus since, in establishing its position, the council has taken full account of the commission proposal and the position of the european parliament at first reading, reflecting the agreements reached in the transaction amendments in the draft recommendation which was examined in the committee on fisheries on 23 september and has now been submitted for approval by the plenary. for these reasons, i voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ the aim of this report is to reach agreement between the ep, the council and the general fisheries commission for the mediterranean on the following subjects. as regards the prohibition of inshore trawling in the black sea, parliament agreed that this matter should be dealt with at member state level, while retaining the commission's right of control. the proposal is to authorise a limited number of vessels to use trawls in the black sea coastal waters on an exceptional basis. furthermore, as from 31 december 2015, the authorisations granted to member states to use remotely piloted underwater vehicles for the purpose of observing and prospecting for red coral will expire, unless member states demonstrate through scientific studies that the use of such vehicles will not have negative consequences for the sustainable exploitation of red coral. i believe that this report will be of great help in generating multilateral cooperation to promote the development, conservation, rational management and better use of living marine resources in the mediterranean and the black sea.

in writing. ‒ following the agreement reached in the tripartite dialogues, the rapporteur believes that the additional provisions applicable to fisheries in the gfcm agreement area have a sufficient level of protection. furthermore, since the agreement covers measures which have already been transposed by the member states, i consider it necessary to vote in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ with this vote, the socialists send a clear signal to the european commission: reject the proposed legislation as it would have a negative impact on the eu's agricultural sector. the socialists are missing in the european commission's proposal a greater focus on key aspects such as traceability and legislative coherence between the food and animal sectors, as well as a memory of the socioeconomic impact of the proposals. we also have reservations about the actual possibility of implementing this legislation in the single market and about legal aspects, but it is clear that, apart from these legal issues, there is a problem of public perception and political order. the socialists therefore vote in favour of the european commission withdrawing the proposal in its current form and drawing up an improved one which takes account of the shortcomings identified.
in writing. ‒ the text presented by the european commission, which in theory gives member states the possibility of restricting or prohibiting the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory, is in reality an ambiguous document in which such a prohibition or restriction would be carried out under conditions which, de facto, make its implementation impossible. for example, a member state wishing to restrict or prohibit the use of gmos on its territory would have to rely on grounds other than those relating to risks to human or animal health or the environment; it could not rely on scientific grounds, nor on grounds which are not 'duly substantiated' and based on 'compelling reasons' and which, in turn, entail proportionate and non-discriminatory measures. the commission proposal also raises other implementation problems, for example the ambiguity of the concept of 'use'. i therefore voted in favour of parliament's proposal to ask the commission to withdraw its proposal and to submit a new one.
in writing. ‒ on 22 april 2015, the commission presented a proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 in which it suggested allowing member states to restrict or prohibit, under certain conditions, the use of genetically modified food and feed (gmf) on their territory after these products have been authorised. however, the commission proposal has not been preceded by an impact assessment of the consequences for the functioning of the internal market and competition in the agricultural sector. in addition, there are reasonable doubts as to its implementation and how member states making use of the opt-out clause will in practice ensure compliance with such measures on their territory. we therefore consider that the proposal does not provide the necessary legal certainty or the appropriate instruments for member states wishing to legally restrict or prohibit the use of gmos in their territory. i therefore rejected the commission's proposal and voted in favour of requesting the commission to submit a new legislative proposal.
in writing. ‒ beyond whether or not gmos should be authorised in the eu - which is not the subject of this proposal - i reject the commission's proposal as it is not preceded by an impact assessment of its implications for the functioning of the internal market. the proposal does not provide the necessary legal certainty or the appropriate instruments for member states wishing to legally restrict or prohibit the use of gmos in their territories.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal as the european commission proposes to allow member states to restrict or prohibit, under certain conditions, the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory after these products have been authorised. the proposal runs counter to the new commission's commitments to 'better regulation' and to greater 'transparency'. i am concerned about the far-reaching consequences of the proposal for the functioning of the internal market in food and feed and for the competitiveness of the agricultural sector in the union.

in writing. ‒ there is currently a european authorisation procedure to ensure that the placing of gmos on the market does not pose a risk to human and animal health or the environment. the legislation entrusts the responsibility for scientific risk assessments to the european food safety authority (efsa), in collaboration with the scientific bodies of the member states. in addition, the current regulation already contains provisions allowing member states to take emergency measures to prevent the placing on the market and use of an authorised gmo, where it is established that the product may present a serious risk to health or the environment. i therefore believe that the legislation in place is sufficiently protective. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial instruments are used effectively.
in writing. ‒ the european commission has proposed to the parliament that member states may prohibit the use of a duly authorised gmo on their territory. this proposal was interesting a priori, but it is very similar to the trap already set by the commission in january concerning the ban on the cultivation of gmos. so, on the basis of this new proposal, the member states are clearly not sovereign. they would simply be allowed to request a ban on the use of a gmo on 'urgent' grounds, not on health or environmental grounds. the restriction of these grounds was denounced and amended by our group, the enl. in addition, the term 'use' is legally imprecise and would have deserved to be clarified, in accordance with the amendments tabled by our group. the epp rapporteur, who is also chairman of the envi committee, simply proposed that the commission's proposal be rejected. unconditional rejection was, of course, unsatisfactory and unacceptable. i therefore voted against the draft submitted by mr la via and against the commission proposal, and i expect, like many citizens, that the commission will come forward with a serious proposal to protect our health and our environment.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report to ask the commission to withdraw its proposal, as it is inaccurate. our group defends the sovereignty of peoples and, of course, also defends our food sovereignty as a result. but the inconsistencies in this report are devoid of any such concept. we agree that the market and the interests of agribusiness cannot dictate the rules on a crucial issue such as food safety. we believe that, given the division of public opinion and the scientific community on such a sensitive issue as this, it would be best to give each country freedom to self-regulate, but by defining in advance what is considered to be 'use', for example, as well as other specifications that are not detailed in the commission's report. the group will therefore be committed to ensuring that the freedom of member states to maintain their different laws - some more permissive, others more restrictive - on genetically modified food is not impeded, but that the legislative process is more democratic and that the european parliament is more involved than it has been so far in this report.
in writing. with this vote, the socialists send a clear signal to the european commission: reject the proposed legislation as it would have a negative impact on the eu's agricultural sector. the socialists are missing in the european commission's proposal a greater focus on key aspects such as traceability and legislative coherence between the food and animal sectors, as well as a memory of the socioeconomic impact of the proposals. we also have reservations about the actual possibility of implementing this legislation in the single market and about legal aspects, but it is clear that, apart from these legal issues, there is a problem of public perception and political order. the socialists therefore vote in favour of the european commission withdrawing the proposal in its current form and drawing up an improved one which takes account of the shortcomings identified.
in writing. ‒ in the proposal by the commission, member states are allowed to restrict/prohibit (under certain conditions) the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory after these products have been authorised; but such measures need to be compatible with the internal-market and the eu’s international obligations (wto). all groups in the chamber decided to reject this proposal based on the following reasons: 1. lack of an impact assessment;2. non-real democratisation of the authorisation procedure;3. problematic implementation due to the ban in ‘use’ instead of ban in ‘placing on the market’;4. compatibility of measures taken by member states with the internal market and wto, (legal uncertainty & risk for the competitiveness of the eu agricultural sector). eh bildu is politically against gmos, but in our opinion a more important reason needs to be underlined: ms can only restrict/prohibit gmos and gm food and feed on the basis of compelling grounds compatible with union law, not related to risks to human and animal health, and to the environment. and this is key. hence eh bildu has voted against the commission proposal; but in favour of the legislative resolution.
in writing. ‒ the text presented by the european commission, which in theory gives member states the possibility of restricting or prohibiting the use of genetically modified food and feed on their territory, is in reality an ambiguous document in which such a prohibition or restriction would be carried out under conditions which, de facto, make its implementation impossible. for example, a member state wishing to restrict or prohibit the use of gmos on its territory would have to rely on grounds other than those relating to risks to human or animal health or the environment; it could not rely on scientific grounds, nor on grounds which are not 'duly substantiated' and based on 'compelling reasons' and which, in turn, entail proportionate and non-discriminatory measures. the commission proposal also raises other implementation problems, for example the ambiguity of the concept of 'use'. i therefore voted in favour of parliament's proposal to ask the commission to withdraw its proposal and to submit a new one.
in writing. ‒ on 22 april 2015, the commission presented a proposal for a regulation amending regulation (ec) no 1829/2003 in which it suggested allowing member states to restrict or prohibit, under certain conditions, the use of genetically modified food and feed (gmf) on their territory after these products have been authorised. however, the commission proposal has not been preceded by an impact assessment of the consequences for the functioning of the internal market and competition in the agricultural sector. in addition, there are reasonable doubts as to its implementation and how member states making use of the opt-out clause will in practice ensure compliance with such measures on their territory. we therefore consider that the proposal does not provide the necessary legal certainty or the appropriate instruments for member states wishing to legally restrict or prohibit the use of gmos in their territory. i therefore rejected the commission's proposal and voted in favour of requesting the commission to submit a new legislative proposal.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report to ask the commission to withdraw its proposal, as it is inaccurate. our group defends the sovereignty of peoples and, of course, also defends our food sovereignty as a result. but the inconsistencies in this report are devoid of any such concept. we agree that the market and the interests of agribusiness cannot dictate the rules on a crucial issue such as food safety. we believe that, given the division of public opinion and the scientific community on such a sensitive issue as this, it would be best to give each country freedom to self-regulate, but by defining in advance what is considered to be 'use', for example, as well as other specifications that are not detailed in the commission's report. the group will therefore be committed to ensuring that the freedom of member states to maintain their different laws - some more permissive, others more restrictive - on genetically modified food is not impeded, but that the legislative process is more democratic and that the european parliament is more involved than it has been so far in this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of rejecting the european commission's proposal because i believe that there should be european consistency on gm food and feed, and it is not a good thing to let each state decide for itself. our position is also against the import, production and use of these products.

in writing. ‒ in view of the juncker commission's repeated breaches of its promises in the field of gmos and a rather weak legal proposal, i voted in favour of member states being able to restrict or prohibit the use of gmos in their own legislation.

in writing. ‒ i believe that a clear distinction needs to be made between the cultivation and the marketing of genetically modified organisms (gmos). while the control of gmo cultivation can be efficiently managed at the domestic level, allowing member states to have the final say on its marketing may bring about serious inconsistencies in the eu internal market. as the agri committee has pointed out, this proposal would mean the reintroduction of border controls between pro- and anti-gmo countries, which would be against the european spirit and would be extremely difficult to implement in practice.
in writing. ‒ with our vote in favour, the spanish socialists are committed to simplifying the authorisation procedures for novel foods. the current european regulation dates from 1997, since which time there has been a great deal of development in the sector of novel foods and their ingredients. the revision of these rules is therefore necessary to keep pace with scientific and technological progress. the new rules include the following proposals: centralising the authorisation procedure and eliminating the previous national assessment, which implies a reduction in the administrative burden for both food business operators and national authorities; implies a reduction in the time and costs to obtain an authorisation for a novel food; converts individual authorisations into generic ones and thus facilitates market access for smes; establishes a simplified procedure for traditional foods from third countries which improves the access of operators from those countries to the european market; and ensures a high level of public health through a centralised and systematic risk assessment by efsa followed by a union authorisation decision.
in writing. ‒ a 'new food' is considered to be one which was not used for human consumption to a significant degree in the union before 15 may 1997, and also includes traditional food from third countries which has been part of the usual diet of a significant number of its population for at least 25 years. there are many aspects of this report with which we disagree and which have not been improved by the proposed amendments, as they were rejected, in particular the permissiveness with regard to nanomaterials and clones and their descendants, the use of implementing acts instead of delegated acts, and the limitation of member states to prohibit novel foods. moreover, no substantive analysis is made of the non-need for these new foods, the interests of large multinationals and industry in bringing them to market, the link with regulatory convergences for international treaties (ttip, for example) and the need to promote local, seasonal, sustainable consumption and not these "new foods". that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ this proposal for a regulation on novel foods aims to ensure food safety, protect public health and ensure the functioning of the internal market, while supporting innovation in the food sector. the proposal updates the current legislation by creating a 'streamline' authorisation procedure, clarifies the definition of 'novel food', introduces a faster and proportionate safety assessment for 'traditional food' from third states with a food safety record and simplifies procedures for public authorities and private actors. the final result of the negotiations with the council includes many of the aspects which parliament has called for, such as the provisional inclusion of food from cloned animals in the scope of the regulation until specific legislation comes into force or the reintroduction of old food categories and the introduction of new ones, with a view to including food from micro-organisms, fungi and insects. although the final text contains some gaps in the list of novel food categories and in the list of foods containing nanotechnology, in order to adapt the rules on novel foods to technological and scientific progress, i have decided to vote in favour of this reform.
in writing. ‒ the current european regulation dates from 1997, since which time there has been a great deal of development in the sector of novel foods and their ingredients. the revision of these rules is therefore necessary to keep pace with scientific and technological progress, while at the same time guaranteeing the right of consumers to know everything about food, especially food innovations. i therefore voted against, because of the absence of a moratorium on food containing nanotechnology until the efsa has approved a specific strategy on the risk assessment of nanofood, and because of the lack of transitional measures for food derived from the offspring of cloned animals. it should be remembered that the european parliament has spoken out against the cloning of animals for food and that these products are now imported.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the adoption of the regulation on novel foods because i believe that the old regulation of 1997 does not allow for the legal coverage of new feeding practices. the new rules also make it possible to speed up and simplify the granting of authorizations by centralising the procedure. as the alternative rapporteur for the opinion of the committee on international trade on novel foods, i welcome the fact that this new legislation will help to ensure food safety and public health.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour, taking into account the need to update the legislation in this area in line with the enormous scientific and technological advances in the food sector, while ensuring food safety for european citizens.

in writing. ‒ with our vote in favour, the spanish socialists are committed to simplifying the authorisation procedures for novel foods. the current european regulation dates from 1997, since which time there has been a great deal of development in the sector of novel foods and their ingredients. the revision of these rules is therefore necessary to keep pace with scientific and technological progress. the new rules include the following proposals: centralising the authorisation procedure and eliminating the previous national assessment, which implies a reduction in the administrative burden for both food business operators and national authorities; implies a reduction in the time and costs to obtain an authorisation for a novel food; converts individual authorisations into generic ones and thus facilitates market access for smes; establishes a simplified procedure for traditional foods from third countries which improves the access of operators from those countries to the european market; and ensures a high level of public health through a centralised and systematic risk assessment by efsa followed by a union authorisation decision.
in writing. ‒ the authorisation and use of novel foods and food ingredients have been harmonised in the european union since 1997. the procedure has so far been that pre-market authorisation applications were first assessed by a member state, the initial assessment report was circulated by the commission to collect comments and objections from all member states and, if no substantiated safety objections were raised, the novel food could be placed on the market. the regulation we are adopting today replaces this procedure with a centralised procedure at european level, which is being carried out by the european food safety authority. this change is positive because it means, among other things, that applications for authorisation of the same food can no longer be submitted in several countries and that the timeframe for deciding whether or not to authorise a novel food in the eu will be shorter.
in writing. ‒ the nicholson report was intended to regulate the marketing of novel foods. these new foods include foods containing nanomaterials. these nanomaterials are very small particles that can give food the properties that industrialists want (color, sparkle, melt, etc.). they are suspected by the scientific community to be hazardous to health because their size allows them to pass through cell membranes. so there is a risk that tomorrow a health scandal will arise because of these new molecules. i proposed banning foods containing nanomaterials. this proposal was rejected by a majority of the assembly. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the use of genetically modified organisms. from transparency of authorizations to respect for the precautionary principle, all the proposals that the envi committee had made to protect the consumer were rejected. i therefore voted against this text.
in writing. ‒ we voted against this report, which seeks to define what is considered to be 'novel food', because, although the commission considers that this report is the result of consensus, the negotiation in the tripartite dialogue did not address issues of the utmost importance, such as, for example, the definition of the concept of 'novel food' itself. it does not include post-market monitoring or monitoring of such foods, nor does it emphasise the importance of correct labelling on the product so that the consumer can make a sufficiently informed decision on its use. as far as food safety is concerned, we believe that the precautionary principle should prevail and we consider this report to be insufficient for the proper handling of food containing nanomaterials, clones (or their descendants) and other genetic engineering applied to food.

in writing. ‒ in december 2013, the ec presented a proposal to clarify the definition of novel foods and to take into account new technologies in food making, and streamline and speed up the authorisation process; as until then it was considered as food that was not used for human consumption to a significant degree within the union before the 15 may 1997. the report of the envi committee on the matter was good; managing to include engineered nanomaterial food and food derived from cloned animals in the scope of it; however, the outcome of the trilogues does not satisfy us. of course it is better than the original ec proposal; it includes animal welfare concerns and labelling but still there some important points that should have been included. first, the responsibility of whether a food is considered novel falls into the food operators, only when they are unsure, they shall consult the ms. moreover, everything (establishing list of novel foods, adding, removing specifications, etc.) will be done by implementing acts; and also, the efsa may give its opinion on a novel food upon request of the ec. hence, following the precautionary principle, and since 1am block ams (trilogue) have been carried to the detriment of block 2ams (envi committee ams), eh bildu has voted against both the commission proposal and legislative resolution.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, because it does not include some key elements, for example: the need to observe the precautionary principle when deciding about authorisations; transparency requirements (both the list of novel foods and applications and rejected applications should be made public); the need for an opinion by the european food safety authority (efsa) in every case; detailed requirements in respect of the efsa risk assessment (e.g. to consider potential cumulative/synergistic effects, and to exclude risks not only for food safety, but also for animal welfare and the environment); mandatory post-market monitoring requirements; and requirements regarding food packaging.

in writing. ‒ the socialists support the european commission's plans to impose stricter and more binding limits on emissions of air pollutants, which must be reached between 2020 and 2030. air pollution has enormous human, environmental and economic costs, with around 400 000 people dying prematurely in the eu each year from it. some 62% of the community's territory is undergoing eutrophication, including 71% of natura 2000 ecosystems. the total costs are between €330 and €940 billion a year, including direct economic damage of €15 billion in lost working days, €4 billion in health services, €3 billion in lost crops and €1 billion in damaged buildings, according to european commission figures.
in writing. ‒ the revised proposal for an nec directive replaces the current union regime for the annual levelling of national emissions of air pollutants, as defined in directive 2001/81/ec, for four air pollutants, namely sulphur dioxide (so2), nitrogen oxides (nox), volatile organic compounds other than methane (vocs) and ammonia (nh3), until 2020. the revised nec directive sets out the controls on the different types of air pollution in each member state. it aims to halve by 2030 the number of premature deaths - estimated at 400 000 a year in the eu - caused by air pollution. the proposed revision sets new national emission reduction commitments applicable from 2020 and 2030 for the four pollutants mentioned above and also for fine particulate matter (pm2,5) and methane (ch4). although there are important points which were not adopted (the report deletes binding targets for methane), i voted in favour of this report because i consider it to be more demanding than the commission's proposal and therefore better.
in writing. ‒ air pollution is responsible for the premature death of more than 400 000 people each year and its economic cost to the health system is estimated at between eur 300 000 and eur 900 000 million annually. approximately 90% of europeans living in cities are exposed to air pollution at levels harmful to human health. in addition, vulnerable socio-demographic groups, in particular pregnant women, children and the elderly, as well as those on low incomes, are particularly affected. the proposed directive on national emission ceilings replaces the current national emission limit regime for certain air pollutants, in particular sulphur (so2), nitrogen (nox), volatile organic compounds (vocs) and ammonia (nh3) until 2020. it includes the establishment of new national emission reduction commitments applicable for 2020 and 2030 for the above air pollutants as well as for fine particulate matter (pm2,5) and methane (ch4). in addition, member states shall draw up national air pollution control programmes. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this legislative proposal, which is essential to improve air quality in europe. in addition, with the aim of helping the agricultural sector, i have supported the exclusion of methane from the scope of the directive.

in writing. ‒ air pollution is a public health problem. the eu is far from achieving its long-term goal of reaching levels that do not have a significant negative impact on health. so in today's vote i supported setting limits on emissions of all pollutants, including methane and ammonia, and i voted for having ambitious and binding targets not only for 2030, but also for 2025.
in writing. ‒ the girling report is a directive which aims to set maximum emission limits for certain pollutant emissions. the text dealt with industrial products and also included provisions on methane and ammonia, gases produced by agriculture. under the ecological guise, the goal of reducing methane was a full-scale attack on our livestock industry with only one possible outcome: the industrialization of livestock farming and the confinement of animals. the commission's proposal for a directive on the protection of the environment is a very good one. imports of industrial or agricultural products are not subject to the same binding provisions. these then become the balls at the foot of our economy. the effect is quite counterproductive: the death of our companies and farms due to lack of competitiveness for the benefit of non-european actors whose environmental concerns are lower than ours. other measures could be taken to tackle the roots of pollution, in particular stopping free trade agreements. the text was not worthy of my vote and i voted against it, because it endangers both our agriculture and our industry.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report in order to regulate certain air pollutants, such as methane emissions. 40% of greenhouse gas emissions come from agriculture. it is also an important precursor of another air pollutant, tropospheric ozone, which causes respiratory and cardiovascular diseases and, incidentally, also significant damage to agricultural crops, especially in mediterranean countries.
in writing. the socialists support the european commission's plans to impose stricter and more binding limits on emissions of air pollutants, which must be reached between 2020 and 2030. air pollution has enormous human, environmental and economic costs, with around 400 000 people dying prematurely in the eu each year from it. some 62% of the community's territory is undergoing eutrophication, including 71% of natura 2000 ecosystems. the total costs are between €330 and €940 billion a year, including direct economic damage of €15 billion in lost working days, €4 billion in health services, €3 billion in lost crops and €1 billion in damaged buildings, according to european commission figures.
in writing. ‒ in december 2013, the ec adopted a proposal-package to improve air-quality in europe, called ‘air quality package’, whose main piece was a proposal to revise the national emission ceilings directive (necd). the new ec considered withdrawing the directive in november 2014, but because of strong resistance from the ep and civil society the proposal was kept. the key points of the envi committee necd proposal are: - introduction of national ceilings for six pollutants (sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, ammonia, methane, particulate matter and non-methane volatile organic compounds) by 2030 - mercury (hg) added to the list of pollutants as caps were introduced on mercury from 2020- midpoint targets for 2025 fully binding for all pollutants, with the exception of methane - methane targets delayed until 2030 to give the agriculture sector adaptation time - removal of ce proposal for flexibility allowing member states to offset reductions in emissions from nitrogen oxides, sulphur dioxides and particulate matter from international shipping - public participation, transparency, access to justice and information this ep report is stronger than the ec-proposal, at the same time that the big aim of the directive is to put controls on different types of air-pollution with the goal to cut the number of premature deaths (about 400 000/year, caused by air pollution) by half by 2030. hence, eh bildu has voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the revised proposal for an nec directive replaces the current union regime for the annual levelling of national emissions of air pollutants, as defined in directive 2001/81/ec, for four air pollutants, namely sulphur dioxide (so2), nitrogen oxides (nox), volatile organic compounds other than methane (vocs) and ammonia (nh3), until 2020. the revised nec directive sets out the controls on the different types of air pollution in each member state. it aims to halve by 2030 the number of premature deaths - estimated at 400 000 a year in the eu - caused by air pollution. the proposed revision sets new national emission reduction commitments applicable from 2020 and 2030 for the four pollutants mentioned above and also for fine particulate matter (pm2,5) and methane (ch4). although there are important points which were not adopted (the report deletes binding targets for methane), i voted in favour of this report because i consider it to be more demanding than the commission's proposal and therefore better.
in writing. ‒ the emissions reduction directive comes at a crucial time. the growing concern of citizens about public health issues is compounded by the volkswagen scandal and the incalculable and irreversible negative effects on health and the environment. despite efforts to reduce air pollution, the european union is still far from meeting its targets. pollution kills more than three million people prematurely worldwide every year and the external health costs to society in europe are estimated at between €330 and €940 billion per year, not including environmental damage. the proposal we are voting on today is ambitious, setting new emission ceilings and binding targets for 2025 in a clear commitment to the health of europeans. i can therefore only vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ air pollution is responsible for the premature death of more than 400 000 people each year and its economic cost to the health system is estimated at between eur 300 000 and eur 900 000 million annually. approximately 90% of europeans living in cities are exposed to air pollution at levels harmful to human health. in addition, vulnerable socio-demographic groups, in particular pregnant women, children and the elderly, as well as those on low incomes, are particularly affected. the proposed directive on national emission ceilings replaces the current national emission limit regime for certain air pollutants, in particular sulphur (so2), nitrogen (nox), volatile organic compounds (vocs) and ammonia (nh3) until 2020. it includes the establishment of new national emission reduction commitments applicable for 2020 and 2030 for the above air pollutants as well as for fine particulate matter (pm2,5) and methane (ch4). in addition, member states shall draw up national air pollution control programmes. for these reasons, i voted in favour of this legislative proposal, which is essential to improve air quality in europe. in addition, with the aim of helping the agricultural sector, i have supported the exclusion of methane from the scope of the directive.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour of this report in order to regulate certain air pollutants, such as methane emissions. 40% of greenhouse gas emissions come from agriculture. it is also an important precursor of another air pollutant, tropospheric ozone, which causes respiratory and cardiovascular diseases and, incidentally, also significant damage to agricultural crops, especially in mediterranean countries.

in writing. ‒ the report refers to the upcoming revision of regulation (eu) no 211/2011 on the european citizens' initiative and to the conclusions drawn by the european commission in a recently published paper. our view is that the implementation of the european citizens' initiative has been a complete failure; in fact, of 51 registered proposals, only three have been able to meet the requirements, often because of the numerous administrative hurdles during the process of collecting signatures, which sometimes lead to the commission itself being sued in court. in addition, the european commission is not obliged to initiate any legislative amendment proposals, so their effectiveness is minimal. in this context, the final report is not critical of the procedures for this participatory tool. it also proposes that the content of the european citizens' initiative be limited if it does not comply with the union's competences and, above all, that the commission make a legislative proposal only if it has a positive opinion published by itself. for these reasons, and given the limited propositional content of the report to consolidate the european citizens' initiatives politically and legally, i have voted against it.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative is a key tool for social mobilisation and strengthening the relationship between citizens and the european institutions. we need to propose to the commission improvements in its operation and to remove certain difficulties which arise in the organization and implementation of such initiatives. it is important to provide the organisers with some legal advice and technical support, to provide technical facilities for collecting signatures in the different member states, to assess the possibility of registering only part of the initiative if it does not fall entirely within the commission's competence, etc. it is vital for european democracy that the citizens' initiative mechanism should function properly and not be seen by citizens as an inadequate element that does not produce any results. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ regarding the postponement of the european citizens' initiative by schopflin, i conscientiously abstained because i have enormous doubts about the satisfaction of my constituents. my doubts are twofold. firstly, there is a strong possibility that giving the eic the prerogative to enter into primary law would be contrary to the current wording of the treaties. secondly, if we want the eic to have access to primary law or to force parliament to act on its behalf, then, in my view, we should review the level of representativeness, the number of citizens and of states that support the eic. a million is very little for such ambitions, and we must not forget that we too represent the citizens of europe, and a greater number of them.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour with the aim of improving the operation of the initiative to make it easier to use and to remove some of the obstacles that have posed difficulties for its organisers.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens’ initiative is a concrete example of participatory democracy in the european union. it allows citizens closer proximity to the eu by enabling them to invite the commission to submit a proposal for a legal act which they believe is necessary in order to implement the eu treaties. however, we need to ensure that this initiative is used correctly and that citizens have the proper means of using it. overall, i voted in favour of the report.
in writing. ‒ we abstained on this report. we believe that european citizens' initiatives are the mechanism closest to citizens when it comes to putting projects to the union; we also believe that the mechanisms by which these initiatives can be carried out need to be improved; we also believe that without an improvement in european citizens' initiatives, the union will continue to be perceived as a strange and distant entity. we therefore need to improve the spirit and the letter of the rules of procedure, and we believe that the adoption of certain amendments has deprived this report of the force we would like it to have, which is why we abstained.
in writing. ‒ up until now, 29 initiatives out of 49 submissions have gone through the process of registration and only three of them have reached the one million signature threshold. only the eci right2water received a positive – although vague – communication from the european commission. none of the successful ecis has led to legislative follow-up. upfront the participation crisis of the eu, the schopflin report aiming to modify the ecis obtained a large consensus in the afco committee, including some innovative proposals that went beyond the existing regulation 211/2011 on eci. indeed, the report very well underlined the deceptive results of a number of the admitted initiatives and the limits of the overwhelming powers of the ec in assessing the eligibility of such initiative. moreover, it noted that the eci should be more user—friendly, transparent and procedures less complex, and recommended to extend the age of submitters from 18 to 16 irrespective to the right to vote in national or european elections. however, am4 (which transforms the eci into a bow without arrows and urges the ec to start preparing a legal act on successful ecis only after issuing a positive opinion) passed today before the final vote (eh bildu has voted against), and hence our final vote is been abstention.

in writing. ‒ today the european parliament has failed to strengthen and consolidate the european citizen’s initiative (eci). the eci provides an exceptional opportunity for eu citizens to get involved directly in eu politics and to participate in shaping eu policy. however, by not urging the commission to start preparing a legal act on successful ecis within 12 months of their submission, we have failed to allow citizens to effectively shape european policies and legislation. therefore i have voted abstention.
in writing. ‒ the european citizens' initiative needs a lot of changes. it is a tool for direct participation of the citizens which, however, has not given the expected result. few initiatives have succeeded, partly because we have not given citizens and organisers the facilities they need to apply this instrument effectively. this report sets out some remedies for these problems. however, i have identified some problems: for example, i voted against the possibility of granting public money, considering that there may be cases of fraud or private financing with public funds, or against the possibility of initiatives changing primary law, since it is necessary to give the treaties some extra protection because of the importance they have, and the channels laid down through their representatives must be followed. however, it is a good report and we hope that the initiatives will prosper after these changes.

in writing. ‒ the report on the citizens' initiative regulation was more than necessary. this possibility was already envisaged in the lisbon treaty, but it was not until 2012 that it could be put into effect. from the outset, it was marked by major shortcomings, both in terms of regulation and in terms of communication and logistics. this system has not satisfied the citizens, who face a bureaucratic challenge that is difficult to overcome. it is necessary for citizens to know the procedure for the processing and adoption of citizens' initiatives, since they are often frustrated when they discover that the initiative will not go ahead and demand explanations from the european parliament. it is time to take stock and improve the deficiencies of this system.
in writing. ‒ i believe that this report mixes positive and negative elements in the eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region. on the one hand, there is a commitment to support the economic development of these regions, focusing on aspects such as sustainability or support for smes and traditional sectors such as tourism or fisheries. it also gives the eu a leading role in a region where not all the member states are members, by imposing the adoption of the european acquis and encouraging private investment in sensitive sectors such as energy or transport. i therefore abstained.
in writing. ‒ the european commission presented last july the eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region (eusair), which establishes a third macro-region in the eu after the baltic and danube , providing a coherent framework for a regional macro-strategy and an action plan for cooperation between the eu and three more countries (eight in total). the adriatic-ionian region faces a number of common challenges, both because of historical events of the past and because of the large socioeconomic disparities between the different countries and regions. there are significant infrastructure deficits. marine and coastal ecosystems are threatened by human exploitation. administrative and institutional capacities at national, regional and local levels need to be strengthened, etc. the rapporteur seeks to find solutions to all these problems, contributing to the four pillars of the strategy (blue growth, connecting the region, environmental quality and sustainable and competitive tourism). i therefore voted in favour of this report, which finally incorporates the socialist demand for the completion of the baltic-adriatic corridor, including the extension of the ionian-adriatic corridor in its entirety.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the third eu macro-regional strategy, bearing in mind that the region's past is marked by events that have had devastating and lasting effects on development and cooperation between the countries in the region. eusair offers a unique opportunity for the countries of the region to move beyond their economic and political problems of the past by working together, under the guidance of the commission. it is also important that the eu pushes for the creation of a macro-region in the western mediterranean.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report on the eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region, which represents an opportunity to make regions and countries work more closely together and to develop synergies in the fields of tourism, fisheries, environment and maritime transport. the implementation of such a strategy will also allow the implementation of joint projects within this macro-region funded by the eu and the european investment bank.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on an eu strategy for the adriatic and ionian region. the strategy for the adriatic and ionian sea covers eight countries, four of which are eu members (croatia, greece, italy and slovenia) and four are third countries (albania, montenegro, serbia and bosnia and herzegovina). this report is a perfect illustration of the european union's desire to create crossborder macro-regions bypassing the member states. the aim is to weaken the power of central governments in favour of local authorities, which are more malleable to the european institutions. the member states concerned could indeed deal with these issues in a multilateral manner. moreover, since one legislative train may conceal another, it is clear that this type of strategy is also intended to promote future enlargements of the european union. the report thus emphasizes in several paragraphs that it is part of an integration dimension of the candidate or potential candidate countries. any further enlargement would only strengthen the power of the european institutions to the detriment of the european states and peoples.
in writing. ‒ we voted in favour, as we did in committee, taking into account that a large part of our proposals were accepted as commitments. we understand that an eu strategy in the adriatic and ionian region is expressed in multi-level coordinates which sometimes forget about concrete areas of action and green and blue policies for the region; this is not the case. we do however believe that some of the parts of the dossier need to be clarified to a greater extent, particularly those which concern sectors such as tourism, which must be guaranteed in a sustainable way and which, we believe, require separate dossiers.

in writing. ‒ in december 2012, the council invited the commission to present a strategy for the adriatic and ionian region by the end of 2014. the commission presented that proposal in june 2014. building on this proposal, the report recognises the added value of the strategy and identifies several development priorities for its four pillars: blue growth, connectivity of the region, environmental quality and sustainable and competitive tourism. we are talking about a report which has won a wide consensus in the committee on regional development and which touches on issues of great importance to the region, and i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the report is based on the european commission's 2014 communication on the europe 2020 strategy review, which set five main objectives for 2020 in employment, research and development, polluting emissions, school failure and poverty reduction. to achieve this, so-called economic governance has been promoted and applied, through specific recommendations to countries that have brought disastrous consequences for the population. the report by parliament regrets that the key role of cohesion policy has not been mentioned in this communication; it calls for the inclusion of other indicators besides gdp to measure progress; that it takes into account rural areas, areas affected by industrial transition, etc.; it calls for greater involvement of parliament in the monitoring of the policy, etc. however, it is important to note that the incompatibility of cohesion policy with the european fund for strategic investments (juncker plan) is not observed. it also calls for more attention to public-private partnerships, which are covert sources of privatization, more expensive for the public purse and less efficient. finally, once again, there is no criticism of the austerity policies of the european semester with cohesion policy. therefore, i have decided to abstain.
in writing. ‒ this report focuses on progress made towards the mid-term review of the europe 2020 strategy at the end of 2015. cohesion policy is a key instrument for achieving the 2020 strategy, closely aligned with its objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. however, due to the crisis, european funding became the only source of public funding in many member states and regions. the report hopes to improve synergies between the various european funds, while drawing attention to the need to use the objectives of each region's strategy 2020 and better adapt to their different needs. the need for a strategic debate on the future cohesion policy is also underlined, bearing in mind that the new cohesion policy legislative package will come in 2018-2019 alongside the 2019 european elections. the review of the eu strategy post-2020 should also be aligned with the new multiannual financial framework. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ this report recalls the progress made since the launch of the europe 2020 strategy, of which cohesion policy is one of the pillars. the resolution proposes a balanced review with a view to revising the europe 2020 strategy by the end of the year, in order to meet the european objectives on employment, innovation, education and sustainable development in the next five years. that is why i voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ we abstained on the report on cohesion policy and the review of the europe 2020 strategy. we believe that the union's medium-term policies, especially those involving large budgetary commitments, require a broad consensus and must aim to eliminate the abysmal differences between development and the quality of life in the various regions of the union. we can only fully support the reports on this subject if inequalities are the political a priori that makes the mediumterm strategies closer together.

in writing. ‒ this report focuses on progress made towards the mid-term review of the europe 2020 strategy at the end of 2015. cohesion policy is a key instrument for achieving the 2020 strategy, closely aligned with its objectives of smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. however, due to the crisis, european funding became the only source of public funding in many member states and regions. the report hopes to improve synergies between the various european funds, while drawing attention to the need to use the objectives of each region's strategy 2020 and better adapt to their different needs. the need for a strategic debate on the future cohesion policy is also underlined, bearing in mind that the new cohesion policy legislative package will come in 2018-2019 alongside the 2019 european elections. the review of the eu strategy post-2020 should also be aligned with the new multiannual financial framework. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ i am concerned about the practical implications of the reprogramming and suspension of european funds under article 23 of the common provisions regulation, in line with the so-called 'macroeconomic conditionality' rejected by the s&d group but incorporated in the last legislature, from the perspective that cohesion policy is often, in the context of the crisis, the only source of public investment in many regions. the report focuses on the safeguards for article 23 to be used as a measure of last resort, considering that european solidarity should not be hampered by economic governance mechanisms. the beneficiaries of funds, regions and municipalities cannot be harmed by macroeconomic failures at higher levels of the administration. the report also calls for the european parliament to be the main democratic guarantor of the proper application of the macro-conditionality of article 23, and for the commission to take account of its views. the need for constant, clear and transparent interinstitutional cooperation is therefore underlined.
in writing. ‒ the report focuses on the european commission's communication on guidelines for linking the structural funds to article 23 of regulation no 1303/2013, in which the commission itself announces that support from the structural funds should be closely linked to compliance with eu governance. it thus justifies the existence of reprogramming and suspension of funds to regions when the member states to which they belong do not meet the criteria set by the european semester to correct the degree of indebtedness (cutting policies and reforms that cut rights in labour legislation, among others). the parliament's report legitimises the existence of so-called 'macro-conditionality' as a last resort. the overwhelming majority of meps voted in favour of declaring that economic governance instruments contribute to a 'stable macroeconomic environment', ignoring the dramatic effects of austerity measures on the european population, and on the spanish population in particular. in fact, the proposal to remove the structural funds from the overall calculation of a state's public deficit was not even voted on. i have therefore obviously voted against.

in writing. ‒ we voted against the report on the european structural and investment funds proposed by josé blanco lópez. we believe that the final text adopted by the council during the vote, in its amending phase, does not deal with the problems and debt crises of countries in severe economic crisis. our amendments were to ensure that funds for countries in severe crisis were not counted as national debt. we believe that without this extra mechanism the functioning of the structural funds loses all meaning and becomes simply another mechanism, not of solidarity, but of debt-bonding of the states participating in the fund.
