madam president, commissioner, france and europe have been attacked. in the face of the great threat that hangs over us, there is no other possible response than the unity of the european union. we must respond jointly and without breach to the attack we all suffered in paris, bamako, beirut, nigeria, tunisia and, this afternoon, in roubaix. we must work together with the international community to find a solution to the 'civil' conflict in syria and the rest of the region that will allow the restoration of security and peace in that country, eliminating the terrorism of isil from the root. we must obviously work tirelessly to prevent the radicalisation of citizens living in the european union, using as a priority the necessary and indispensable integration measures as the first line of prevention, and the dati report is moving decisively in this direction. but it is also necessary and inevitable to have a joint structure, to deepen police cooperation, and that this leads to a european federal police which can take advantage of a european criminal code - which is already provided for in the treaty of lisbon - and, in the same vein, we must be able to make further progress in common policies - which we should already have - such as the common asylum policy or the common immigration policy, and to give a real sense of state to cooperation and development policy. throughout our history, europe has had to fight barbarism and nonsense on many occasions, but europe has always managed to stay, evolving to where we are today. let us make it clear once again that we will not be defeated; we will fight against all those who threaten our security and freedom. europe and democracy will endure; the terrorists will not.
madam president, commissioner, you have said that this is an opportune debate, and it is. what is not appropriate is to mix it up with a debate on foreigners, on immigration or on refugees. no, it is a debate on what europe can do to prevent european citizens from being recruited by terrorist organisations. and the added value is that we learn to intervene in the content on the net that incites violent extremism; that we learn to intervene also in the socialization of terror in prisons; that we learn to prevent not only the trafficking of arms, through these sophisticated means, but the financing of this indoctrination in terrorism; and that we freeze their assets, and we do it on a european scale. but also in learning to cooperate in policing to share information about those 5,000 europeans who have come and gone after having been trained for terrorism somewhere abroad; but also in denouncing that austerity and the collapse of education, inclusion and integration policies in marginalized neighborhoods and particularly vulnerable groups have led to many young europeans, many european-born citizens, being willing to embark on this mad spiral of destructive and self-destructive violence, and being willing not only to kill, but to die by killing. this is the challenge we have to meet and i hope that the dati report will bring european added value to this european response which is more necessary than ever.
madam president, in these matters we must not respond in hot blood: shortcuts are not worth it. we learned about 9/11 in spain: 193 dead, 1,858 wounded. in europe, military solutions are not worthwhile in the face of asymmetrical threats; xenophobic or islamophobic simplification is not worthwhile. we must remember: to end the destabilizing agendas that were employed in places like iraq, libya and syria. we must review our alliances on the ground: with the gulf countries, which finance or transmit wahhabi or takfiri hatred, and with turkey, which allows smuggling. we must not abandon the rule of law in the face of intelligence failures. we must also combat the asymmetries across the mediterranean and in our own neighbourhoods, because only with stability and justice will there be security.
i am speaking on behalf of the gue/ngl group. mr president, thank you to the rapporteur for the work and the cooperation we have been able to maintain. the metal industry is a strategic sector whose problems are those of european industry as a whole. we need an industry that minimises its environmental impact, that spans territories and is capable of generating quality employment. to achieve this, the european union must develop a genuine industrial policy which does not take competition policy as a dogma but applies it in favour of the objectives of cohesion and employment enshrined in the treaties. public investment and planning are necessary if europe's regions are to maintain their industry and not be left to seasonal and speculative sectors. it is also essential for the reduction of emissions that a global regulatory framework is developed and that environmental dumping is combated, and that the massive deindustrialization of traditional production areas in europe is not used to expand production in countries with lower emission standards and labour rights. the metal sector is central to europe and has a great future ahead of it with the right technological innovation, making us the cleanest industry in the world, the development of recycling and the circular economy in industrial areas in conversion, and improvements in energy efficiency. only a real economy that is forward-looking can help to overcome the present crisis and create quality jobs. this report is a small step towards supporting this sector, which must remain the true heart of european industry.
mr president, first of all i would like to congratulate the rapporteur, mr martin, on his report on the base metals industry, to which i have personally contributed with amendments which i tabled with several members of my group. the metal industry is a very important sector in europe - particularly in some european regions, such as mine, galicia - but this sector is currently facing serious threats to its competitiveness. i would like to stress the price of energy, which is generally higher in european countries than in other continents. other factors affecting this industry are the flight or relocation of industrial investments to third countries or, as mentioned above, unfair competition from third countries through dumping or export subsidies. but we cannot afford to let this base metal industry disappear from europe: the prosperity and employment of europeans would be greatly harmed. i therefore welcome the fact that mr martin's report proposes a series of measures to help the metal industry to remain in europe and be competitive. i ask you, commissioner, to study this proposal very carefully, to analyse this set of measures in the report which we are going to adopt tomorrow. of course, energy prices are a key sector. i am thinking, for example, of the production of aluminium. i know very well that it requires a very high consumption of electricity and we europeans must of course make it possible for electricity-intensive industries to remain on our continent, generating employment and wealth.
mr president, thank you to mr martin for his excellent report. spain is the fourth largest steel producer in the european union. it is the source of income for 80 000 families and since 2007 national production has fallen by 30%. closures and relocations are multiplying in the union. the social and environmental dumping and our high energy costs are now being compounded by global overproduction and the granting of market economy status to china, and the same threats are facing other industries, such as aluminium, which is very important in spain and particularly in my region, galicia. in view of this limiting situation, we cannot continue to encourage unfair competition in the european union through the system of compensatory state aid. while spanish producers received eur 5 million in the period 2013-2015, german producers received eur 756 million. we need a harmonised system of aid now; and we need to establish a border carbon adjustment to make importers subject to the same climate requirements as european producers and renewed and effective anti-dumping instruments. otherwise, we shall have more relocations, more deindustrialisation and more unemployment. and the european union cannot fly the flag of reindustrialisation and at the same time allow the european steel and aluminium industry to fall because of the lack of fair and adequate safeguards.
mr president, commissioner, this report is very important because it deals with the competitiveness of such important sectors as aluminium and steel, and i want to talk about them. from a political point of view, it is very important that measures are taken to ensure that these sectors remain competitive and that there is no further closing of plants in europe or moving or relocating elsewhere (to produce in china, pollute in china and then pollute to bring steel to europe). their income depends mainly on energy costs and the prices they have to pay for the purchase of emission allowances. as the report very well points out, there are three priority issues. firstly, to reach a binding agreement at the paris conference so that we all have the same level of competitiveness. i know it's difficult, but it would be necessary. secondly, a border adjustment mechanism, so that metals produced in countries without emission reduction targets are subject to some taxation that balances the costs of producing in the european union with those in the rest of the world. thirdly, harmonization in the european union of the compensation for indirect costs for the purchase of emission allowances and, in addition, proper monitoring of the different national support systems. in short, these industries need a regulatory framework to develop their activity, which will enable them to compete with third countries and among the countries of the european union themselves.
mr president, commissioner, i believe that the conditions on the steel market require the european commission to apply the legislation in force to protect our steel industry from the effects of chinese overproduction and the slowdown in its economy. it is not acceptable that a steel of inferior quality, produced under environmental and social conditions much worse than those which we demand here, is ruining our industry. we have already done so with granulated stainless steel and now we must extend this to all steel production. i am glad that an investigation like the one that led to these measures has been opened, but i ask for speed and forcefulness because the sector has been shouting for months that we are dealing with a clear case of dumping with immediate consequences for employment, which we are already seeing in highly industrialized areas such as the basque country. other uncertainties must also be removed. the chinese economy does not yet meet the conditions for a market economy. if our industry is to survive and be able to continue to invest in innovation and technology in the future, it needs legal certainty and stable medium- and long-term prospects. please, commissioner, let us react.
mr president, women farmers on family farms in europe have had and continue to have great difficulties in accessing social security. sometimes for legal reasons, sometimes for economic reasons, sometimes for cultural reasons, but in all cases on the basis of the discrimination that we suffer as women. at the end of the 20th century there were important and significant struggles on the part of austrian peasant women to obtain the right to a pension and also on the part of peasant women in galicia who were married to men who had other professions and who, as their husbands earned more than them in agriculture, were denied the right to pay social security. this meant that even today most women farmers receive lower pensions than men. mrs thyssen, i ask you to take account of farmers when you look at those priorities for reducing the pension gap. and this requires full recognition of the rights of peasant women.
madam president, the terrorists will attack us, but they will not defeat us if we maintain international cooperation; if we maintain the unity of all political forces; if we support the work of the police, judges and prosecutors; and if we respect the dignity of the victims of terrorism. the pain of the victims delegitimizes any attempt to justify violence. the islamic state is an international threat. he doesn't ask if we're from the north or the south, left or right, to kill us. to them we are guilty, we are infidels for the mere fact of being free, and for that we deserve to die. jihadism is an ideology, it's not a religion. jihadism hates freedom, that's why all of us who love freedom must stand against terrorism, united for freedom and for life, whatever our religion. and we must be consistent. we can't legislate on the fly. when they stop killing, we relax. we think they're gone, but they never go away, they're always there. if they don't kill more, it's because they can't kill more, not because they don't want to kill more. we have to keep in mind: they are always preparing their next attack. and we should always be preparing our next law against them. ladies and gentlemen, freedom and security are not mutually exclusive terms. there is no freedom without security, there is no freedom that should not be secured. security is the guarantee of the freedom of the people of europe.
madam president, coming from madrid, the city which suffered the worst attack on european soil, one has to ask oneself, a decade later, how much we have learned and how much progress we have made in preventing and combating radicalism and terrorism. the answer is that it has not been enough, that we have not advanced and learned enough. it has not been enough in terms of information: we still do not share the information necessary to attack terrorism. it has not been enough in cutting off the sources of funding for terrorist groups. it has not been enough in the social response: austerity policies have further damaged education, integration, social services, public services... nor has it been sufficient to structure a common foreign policy of the union that responds coherently to the conflicts that feed these radicalisations and these terrorist groups. nor have we done enough to build a european response. in fact, today the council is presenting a number of measures which we support, but many of these measures were within the reach of the member states, which have not used them. there is an anti-terrorist strategy since 2015. there is a counterterrorism coordinator. there is europol. there is eurojust. there is cosi. so let us use what we have and put the new instruments into operation. but if we have only a national response, terrorists will exploit the security gaps between states. if we just react to the attacks, they will determine the agenda and the timing of when they do us the most damage. if we are not able to avoid the partisan struggle, we will fall into the struggle for european values and we will not be able to ensure their validity.
mr president, my condolences to france and to all the victims and countries affected by the terror. we are facing persistent, lethal and indiscriminate attacks. i want you to recap: in the last month, they've killed 446 people. they kill, we debate. as legislators, we have an inescapable responsibility, and that is to respond to this challenge. this response is embodied in several urgent priorities. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to include the protection of personal data, in particular the protection of personal data in the context of the fight against terrorism. and i also urge, mr avramopoulos, that the new legislative proposals be launched: smart borders, updating of the frontex regulation and the fius. we owe all this, mr president, to the citizens and also to the victims. it's our contribution as legislators.
mr president, there is no consolation for the french mothers whose children were killed in paris on the night of 13 november - or for those in madrid in 2004 - or for the hundreds of thousands of syrian, iraqi, tunisian, nigerian and malian mothers. the threat is global; the strategy of jihadist terrorism is global. and so the only intelligent response has to be global. we need a europe more united than ever, and it is therefore regrettable to hear, even today, the nationalist right and the extreme right of this parliament trying to take advantage of this situation. see, i'm telling you, the refugees are not the ones trafficking in isis oil. it's not the refugees. yes, of course, the key is security, but it's not the only key. let us not give the terrorists the trophy they crave most, which is precisely the failure of our system of freedoms, the failure of our democracy and our complicity in the destruction of universal human rights. if we do that, we'll be giving the terrorists a victory. the threat is global. security is key, but it's not the only key. because if we override our values, we're giving a trophy to the terrorists.
mr president, i am well aware of the nature of terrorism because three eta terrorists shot dead my brother and his wife. that was 17 years ago in seville, but the result, the death of two innocent young people, is no different from what the terrorists in paris sought: to deprive us of our most sacred right, the right to live. i hope that the suffering of the victims will help us to legislate effectively against terrorism, without confusing our right to security with an attack on freedom. because to be free, you must first be alive. i ask the honourable members, especially those who have always blocked legislative instruments designed to protect citizens, to support them this time without any qualms, because respect should not be confused with passivity. today, more than ever, we need a european directive for victims of terrorism. and you know why? because anyone can be a victim; because, along with the victims of paris, our society has been a victim. and i wish i could look the terrorists in the face, tell them that i'm not afraid and i'm not going to give them my freedom or my will to live.
mr president, my condolences to the victims of these attacks which strike us all and my infinite solidarity with france and all the countries which are the victims of terrorism; but european citizens have a right to a legislative response which guarantees and strengthens their security in the face of fear and helplessness, and that requires learning some things with realism. the first is that this is not a debate about aliens or immigration or asylum; or even about islam. because we have to learn that it will be impossible for us to prevail if we do not get the cooperation of the islamic communities in our domestic policy and in our foreign policy - islamic communities who suffer and also fight terrorism. and the second is that the attacks that have hurt us the most - paris, madrid 2004 - were not perpetrated by people who came by plane: they lived and live among us. and that is why it is imperative to strengthen the 'european intelligence community' to know how they operate in networks, how they move their money globally, how we can intercept, freeze and confiscate it, and how we can defend our values without sacrificing our rights and freedoms.
member of the commission.– mr president, the debate today came at the right moment. it was very timely, very constructive and it sent very strong signals. allow me once again to come back to a concern that has been raised by many of you today, namely the link between migration and terrorism and the link between religion and terrorism. i will repeat what i said last night in this place – and president juncker has said it this morning: we must absolutely dissociate those who are in need of international protection – of our protection – from those who are seeking to attack our values, the very fundamental values of our societies. it is those same terrorists who refugees are fleeing from. let me also once again remind you that almost all the perpetrators of the latest attacks on european soil were european union citizens, and not all were of muslim origin. we have to ask ourselves why these young people, who are born and bred here, decide to leave, to forsake our communities and, finally, to turn against us. daesh wants us to think in opposites, in black and white and to feel the antagonism that they are creating and fomenting. let us not fall into their trap. let us not give in to fear and panic. honourable members of parliament, of various political affiliations, we are all smarter than that and we know that a united european response is the only answer to the threat. together we can improve our resilience to terrorism and address the complex causes of radicalisation. we are all collectively safer in unity and should come together. we are moving forward on the pnr negotiations and will ensure a fully operational and effective instrument, which will of course respect proportionality. as regards the checks at our external borders, in parallel with our package on european border and coast guards, we are exploring the need to include possible modifications to the provisions of checks of european union citizens against databases for public order and internal security reasons. in the meantime, member states should use all the tools available to control external borders. the tools are there. moreover, as many of you mentioned schengen, let me make this clear: schengen is the most tangible example of our greatest achievement in the european integration process. it is only by making full use of schengen that we will be able to react to the threats. but we also need more trust among ourselves to share intelligence – many in this room today have said this – and prevent the possibility of a repetition of the horrendous attacks like those in paris. europe cannot stand without trust between all of us – among the eu institutions, among the member states and among citizens. that is why it is so crucial that member states send, not just their experts, but also their intelligence to the counter—terrorism centre in europol, which will be fully operational on 1 january 2016. it is unity, solidarity, resilience, determination and cooperation that will fight terrorism. it is a moment for more europe.
president of the council. mr president, ladies and gentlemen, in the face of these heinous crimes and the threats which unfortunately persist, we need a real political will to act together and i believe that is the great lesson of this debate. the fight against this islamist terrorism, against jihadism - and we are not afraid of words - must be relentless and global. it will be a long one and will require consistency, but also discernment. nothing would be worse than amalgamation. we must work together, without letup, to implement the measures we have decided. all institutions must act quickly and decisively. i have heard the strong desire to achieve the adoption of the european pnr before the end of the year. the presidency is ready to do so and will contribute to it. our best response to terrorism is first and foremost our firm commitment to our values, to our open and democratic society based on equality, non-discrimination and inclusion and our refusal to be intimidated. but it is also, i repeat, with you, our ability to join forces, our ability to share information, and finally, to show cohesion and coherence. that is right, rhetoric is no longer enough, solidarity cannot be limited to mere declaration. ladies and gentlemen, we need concrete solidarity and the solidarity clause of article 42 (7) has been invoked. unanimous and full support was expressed by all the member states at the council meeting on 17 november. it is now necessary to implement it both internally and externally, including through offers of material assistance and support. the strengthening of our foreign policy, our external policy, as well as our security and defence policy, is on the agenda.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it recovers resources from the european data protection supervisor by refunding certain amounts not spent by the european data protection supervisor during the previous financial year. the report stresses that all these surpluses should be directed towards the relief and management of the refugee crisis and humanitarian aid to syria. this should be a priority line of union resources for the financial year 2015 due to its scale and the serious humanitarian situation faced by refugees. it is to make these resources available for the aforementioned objectives of helping migrants that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ draft amending budget no 8/2015 includes, inter alia, a revision of the estimates for traditional own resources (customs duties) to the value of eur 800 million; the budgeting of the remaining vat and gni own resources balances for the financial year 2014 to the value of eur 5 723,9 million; or the budgeting of the vat and gni own resources balances for the financial year 2015 to the value of eur 1 409,4 million. this translates into a decrease of eur 9.4 billion in the gni-based contribution from the member states. parliament sought to link this dossier to the negotiation of the 2016 budget by means of a joint statement with the council that would send a clear political signal to dedicate part of this revenue to the trust funds for syria and africa. but the council has refused. in this resolution, which i have supported, parliament therefore deeply regrets that a firm commitment to use part of these resources to address the refugee crisis has not been reached and expects member states to honour their previous commitments.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument which will allow for the implementation of immediate budgetary measures in relation to the european agenda on migration. the budget can thus be amended to include the items needed for european policies to welcome migrants, which will make it possible to set up housing or employment schemes, asylum policies, with the speeding up of the resolution of asylum applications, and rescue operations at sea. we are facing a mixed competition between the union and the member states, and our vote in favour of it presupposes a will on the part of the states which we have not seen in practice. we hope that the expenditure we have approved will be spent on what is really intended and not, as we have seen so far, on strengthening the fortress europe.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the proposal to mobilise the flexibility instrument for an amount of eur 1 530 million in commitment appropriations and eur 806 million in payment appropriations to supplement the funding of migration policy by strengthening headings 3 and 4: 'security and citizenship' and 'global europe'. the eu has now, in response to the refugee crisis, found it necessary to put in place a series of measures that promote the well-being not only of refugees but also of all member states receiving large flows of people. the problem is that there are no margins available within the multiannual financial framework to finance the mobilization. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the future of the eu's external relations.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe it is necessary for the european union solidarity fund to have the necessary resources in each financial year to be able to respond as quickly as possible to disasters that occur in any member state of the european union. the natural disasters which are occurring in europe require a rapid response and this proposal provides for the provision of funds to be able to react as quickly as possible and to be able to mitigate the effects on the citizens of the affected regions. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i am grateful for the rapporteur's work on the mobilisation of the eu solidarity fund on the payment of advances under the 2016 budget. i voted in favour of it because this fund is a resource for member states in case of need which is used in an appropriate and very useful way for those member states which request it. it is not just a form of financial support from the union but helps to send a clear political message of solidarity while providing much-needed help to the citizens concerned.
in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up to enable the union to respond to emergency situations caused by major natural disasters and to express european solidarity to regions affected by disasters. the fund can provide financial assistance to member states and countries negotiating accession in the event of a major natural disaster, i.e. when the total direct damage exceeds eur 3 billion or 0.6% of the country's gross national income. it can also be mobilised in the event of a regional disaster. the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council is not linked to a specific disaster but seeks to include in the general budget of the union for 2016 the amount of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations for the payment of advances in the event of a disaster occurring in the coming year and thus ensure the availability of budgetary resources by improving the effectiveness of the fund. that is why i voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the eu solidarity fund, which was set up to enable the union to respond to emergency situations caused by major natural disasters. this proposal seeks to enter in the general budget of the union for 2016 an amount of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations for the timely and effective payment of advances in the event of a disaster in the following year.
in writing. ‒ the european union solidarity fund (eusf) was set up to enable the union to respond to emergency situations caused by major natural disasters and to express european solidarity to the regions affected by disasters in europe. the resolution i support today seeks to enter in the general budget of the union for 2016 the amount of eur 50 million in commitment and payment appropriations for the timely and effective payment of advances in the event of a disaster in the following year. this accelerates the financial response capacity in case of disaster by providing for the possibility of an advance.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this mobilisation of the eu solidarity fund. it provides €50 million for disasters that may occur. the issue is perverse, because this money, which would be needed for the refugee crisis, has been enabled in order to prevent future ones when a current and urgent challenge is taking place. in the debate on the budget it was a battle horse, and it is an imposition of the council, which wanted to avoid spending funds for the refugee crisis. voting against it cannot be done either because it enables a fund which may be required for important issues in the future. i voted in favour, because i understand that the mobilisation of the solidarity fund is necessary, but i also understand that a critical review of how these mobilisations are carried out is necessary.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the proposal for a decision of the european parliament and of the council on the mobilisation of the european union solidarity fund, in accordance with point 11 of the interinstitutional agreement of 2 december 2013 between the european parliament, the council and the commission on budgetary discipline, on cooperation in budgetary matters and on sound financial management, to finance the payment of advances in the framework of the 2016 budget. i have done so because i believe that the main purpose of the solidarity fund is to respond quickly, efficiently and flexibly to emergency situations and to show solidarity with the population of regions affected by disasters. it is essential that the eu responds quickly and effectively to those europeans affected by a disaster. this instrument serves as a political message to europeans, who are sometimes unconnected with the decisions of 'brussels'. it is a political message of solidarity, because it provides much needed help to citizens, while providing a rapid response thanks to the advance system.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the fernandes-deprez report on the agreement reached by the conciliation committee for the 2016 budget because it puts the focus on the refugee crisis while continuing to invest in research and development policies. in addition to continuing the youth employment initiative after its evaluation, it is also serving our agricultural and livestock sector, which has been affected by the russian veto and the dairy crisis. i regret that i was unable to include a higher increase in payments for 2016 or a political commitment by member states to use the extraordinary revenue to finance their share of the european agenda on migration. finally, it should be stressed that this is the first use of the flexibility instrument, reflecting the urgent gravity of the current needs. therefore, while the mobilisation of the flexibility instrument will allow to supplement the financing of the general budget of the european union for the financial year 2016 by exceeding the ceilings of the abovementioned headings, we will need to continue to work to address the structural problems facing the european budget during the review of the multiannual financial framework in 2016.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because, despite some positive aspects, it continues the logic of austerity which prevents the eu budget from being increased to cover all payments. this report approves the conciliation committee's outcome, which contains some positive measures, such as the maintenance of horizon 2020, resources for the refugee crisis, measures for milk producers, etc. however, the outcome remains unsettled for the payments that the eu will have to make in 2017 to the member states, postponing these problems by refusing to increase the resources that the eu budget should have. that is why i have decided to vote against this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the fernandes-deprez report on the agreement reached by the conciliation committee on the 2016 budget because it gives the green light to the use of extraordinary resources to deal with extraordinary situations. it focuses on the refugee crisis while continuing to invest in research and development policies. on the other hand, in addition to having obtained a commitment to continue with the youth employment initiative after its evaluation in the course of the next few months, it serves our agricultural and livestock sector, which is affected by the russian veto and the dairy crisis. i regret, however, that i was unable to include a higher increase in payments for 2016 or a political commitment by member states to use the extraordinary revenue to finance their share of the european agenda on migration. finally, i would like to stress that this is the first use of the flexibility instrument, which reflects that, in the face of the acute severity of current needs, the 2016 ceilings for headings 3 and 4 do not allow adequate funding for urgent measures where they are needed most.

in writing. - i voted against it. although the negotiating result is not the worst possible and the budget increases and improves on that of previous years, it is still a ridiculous budget, containing strong security elements, failing to meet the eu's challenges (refugee crisis, economic crisis, ecological challenges, etc.) and mobilizing an investment plan with biased effects and uncertain results. it raises €155 billion in credit commitments, a margin of €2 331.4 million in margin, and, for what matters, €143.8 billion in payment commitments what is actually spent and a flexibility instrument of €1 506 million. it is in line with a european model favouring large transnational companies, where the youth employment initiative is to be progressively reduced and where outstanding and unresolved issues are dealt with with statements with rhetorical effects.

in writing. ‒ i consider the authorisation of use for dehp, a substance whose toxicity as an endocrine disruptor is widely demonstrated ‒ and which can cause cancers, malformations and infertility, among other adverse health effects, to be unacceptable. the commission's proposal is based on the principle of subsidiarity, and it is not a matter of the member states being able to agree on the rules. this authorisation cannot be justified on technical grounds, given the existence of substitutes for this chemical, and it puts the health of workers exposed to it at risk. this is a serious precedent and i have therefore voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ dehp is included in annex xiv of the reach regulation, due to its classification as toxic to reproduction. in fact, it was one of the first six compounds to be phased out under the regulation. on 12 november, the european commission presented a draft implementing act on the dehp. according to the opinion of the committee for risk assessment, the applicants for authorisation have not demonstrated that the risks to the health of workers arising from the uses applied for are adequately controlled in accordance with the reach regulation and that the authorisation should not be granted on this basis. the committee for socio-economic analysis also confirmed that there were significant deficiencies in the socio-economic analysis of the applicant, including a complete lack of a health impact assessment identifying the risk to workers. i have therefore supported the motion for a resolution of parliament which considers that the draft commission implementing decision exceeds the powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 1907/2006 and calls for its withdrawal and the submission of a new one rejecting the applications for authorisation.
in writing. i consider the authorisation of use for dehp, a substance whose toxicity as an endocrine disruptor is widely demonstrated, may cause cancers, malformations and infertility, among other adverse health effects, to be unacceptable. the commission's proposal is based on the principle of subsidiarity, and it is not a matter of the member states being able to agree on the rules. this authorisation cannot be justified on technical grounds, given the existence of substitutes for this chemical, and it puts the health of workers exposed to it at risk. this is a serious precedent and i have therefore voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour as dehp is included in annex xiv to regulation (ec) no 1907/2006 (reach regulation) due to its classification as a category 1b substance, toxic to reproduction, and is included in the candidate list of substances in the reach regulation due to its toxic properties for reproduction. the european institutions must legislate with the safety of european citizens in mind.
in writing. ‒ the reach regulation lists dehp as a substance with very high concern properties for which prior authorisation at european level is required. in this motion for a resolution we oppose the authorization of its use because adequate impact studies have not been carried out to assess both the risks and the benefits of using this substance.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report, which seeks to prevent the authorisation of dehp, a derivative of phthalate. this product is already identified as an endocrine disruptor, with a risk of reproductive toxicity, i.e. a risk to fertility. that is why it was not authorised in a previous application. but this time the european commission is ready to allow it, even though there are reliable substitutes. in fact, the european union has been "warned" by the us and the wto that regulations on endocrine disruptors would be bad for world trade. the us government is concerned that a possible european regulation on endocrine disruptors could "harm european imports of us agricultural products". it is therefore understandable that public health is not the priority, either of the americans or of the european commission, which stubbornly refuses to make a proposal on endocrine disruptors, thus showing a suspicious wait-and-see attitude on this subject.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this non-binding motion for a resolution calling on the commission not to authorise dehp (diethyl hexyl phthalate). it's a well-known toxic substance. it has been proposed to include it in the list of substances of very high concern for endocrine disrupting effects. it is listed in annex xiv of the reach regulation due to its reproductive toxicity. dehp is a phthalate, a group of chemicals that cause the feminization of males of exposed species. these substances affect the endocrine system of wildlife and potentially also that of humans. it can cause breast and testicular cancer, birth defects, and infertility, among other adverse health effects. due to its endocrine disrupting properties, a safe exposure threshold for dehp cannot be established with sufficient certainty. environmental, health, medical, cancer prevention advocates have joined women's organizations and medical organizations to strongly oppose the authorization of dehp in pvc materials, due to its high toxicity. european regulations have already restricted its use in toys and childcare articles.
in writing. ‒ i consider the authorisation of use for dehp, a substance whose toxicity as an endocrine disruptor is widely demonstrated ‒ and which can cause cancers, malformations and infertility, among other adverse health effects, to be unacceptable. the commission's proposal is based on the principle of subsidiarity, and it is not a matter of the member states being able to agree on the rules. this authorisation cannot be justified on technical grounds, given the existence of substitutes for this chemical, and it puts the health of workers exposed to it at risk. this is a serious precedent and i have therefore voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ dehp is included in annex xiv of the reach regulation, due to its classification as toxic to reproduction. in fact, it was one of the first six compounds to be phased out under the regulation. on 12 november, the european commission presented a draft implementing act on the dehp. according to the opinion of the committee for risk assessment, the applicants for authorisation have not demonstrated that the risks to the health of workers arising from the uses applied for are adequately controlled in accordance with the reach regulation and that the authorisation should not be granted on this basis. the committee for socio-economic analysis also confirmed that there were significant deficiencies in the socio-economic analysis of the applicant, including a complete lack of a health impact assessment identifying the risk to workers. i have therefore supported the motion for a resolution of parliament which considers that the draft commission implementing decision exceeds the powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 1907/2006 and calls for its withdrawal and the submission of a new one rejecting the applications for authorisation.

in writing. ‒ this motion for a resolution asks the commission to withdraw its draft implementing decision and to submit a new one rejecting applications for authorisation for the formulation of recycled soft pvc containing dehp, as the draft commission implementing decision is considered to exceed the powers provided for in regulation (ec) no 1907/2006. to prevent this from happening, i think it is necessary to vote in favour of this proposal.
in writing. ‒ i consider the authorisation of use for dehp, a substance whose toxicity as an endocrine disruptor is widely demonstrated ‒ and which can cause cancers, malformations and infertility, among other adverse health effects, to be unacceptable. the commission's proposal is based on the principle of subsidiarity, and it is not a matter of the member states being able to agree on the rules. this authorisation cannot be justified on technical grounds, given the existence of substitutes for this chemical, and it puts the health of workers exposed to it at risk. this is a serious precedent and i have therefore voted in favour of the motion for a resolution.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the final report of the taxe commission, which arose in the wake of the 'luxleaks' scandal, because it represents a major step forward in the fight against tax fraud and tax evasion, provided that the council follows the recommendations of the adopted document, and contains the following main elements: (a) no limitation of the automatic exchange of information to tax rulings considered 'cross-border'; (b) country-by-country reporting by multinationals; (c) possibility of sanctioning states and companies involved in harmful tax practices; (d) call on the commission to take the necessary legislative measures to introduce the common corporate tax base, including the consolidation element; (e) protection of whistleblowers of business irregularities; (g) european list of tax irregularities; (h) reform of the group's code of conduct. the report also criticises the council for excluding the commission from the automatic exchange of information system in the context of the 2011 revision of the directive. as a socialist, this matter is an absolute priority.
in writing. ‒ the work of the taxe committee has served to show that the tax agreements constituted a breach of the competition rules, as well as to highlight the complicity of mr juncker and mr dijsselbloem in this scandal. the report, however, only partially covers our demands. the report also calls for the commission to be more ambitious in its proposals for tax transparency and harmonisation. but many of these requests are well-intentioned and the links between tax-avoiding multinationals, the member states and the commission are not properly investigated, for lack of documentation and political will. that is why i have decided to abstain.

in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the taxe committee for the work it has done over the past months to enable us to vote on this important report today. parliament has carried out an extensive work plan and meetings with very high attendance to try to clarify what has come to be known as the 'luxleaks case'. i hope that, with the adoption of this report and the provisions of it, the european commission will present us with certain measures to be agreed with the council in order to eliminate the problems we have known so far in fiscal matters.

in writing. ‒ first of all, i would like to thanks the special committee for the elaboration of this report following the lux leaks scandal that highlighted questionable tax practices allowing 340 big companies to realize big tax savings. i supported this report that puts forwards recommendations to avoid aggressive tax practices and distortion of competition. i however condemn the fact that several documents that were asked by the special committee were never disclosed; i therefore voted in favour of a six-month extension of its mandate to allow the committee to complete its work. i also supported amendments calling for full access to the documents of the code of conduct group and for the creation of a public register of companies at eu level in order to prevent aggressive and harmful tax practices and fraud and improve transparency.
in writing. ‒ this report is the conclusion of the special commission on the tax rescript scandal, better known as the "luxleaks" case. for decades, countries like luxembourg have allowed multinational companies, particularly in the digital economy or finance, to off-shore their profits in order to avoid all or part of the tax. france thus suffered a shortfall of about 10 to 15 billion a year. the national front has always supported the european parliament's texts to combat tax fraud and evasion. we have thus endorsed the end of banking secrecy with switzerland on 1 january 2018 and we have voted on the reports to combat aggressive tax optimisation. it is in this continuity that i voted in favour of the final report on tax returns. it includes recommendations to the member states and the commission on tax transparency and competition. as france is one of the least competitive countries in the union in terms of taxation, the most restrictive measures will not cause us any harm...
in writing. ‒ i welcome the most important part of this report, which contains useful proposals for greater fiscal justice and reflects the negative impact of austerity on it. however, i abstained from this vote for the following reasons: responsibility for the collapse of tax systems in europe has not been fully taken on board, and the report does not call for the necessary extension of the current mandate; access to documents remains unsatisfactory on the part of the council, the commission and the member states. the multinational corporations have only responded after multiple invitations to the committee, no legal basis for the sanctions has been established and they have not been able to be thoroughly questioned; moreover, the contradictions in jean-claude juncker's speech have not been clarified. the report does not go beyond the commission's own proposals in substance. tax rulings should be made public and tax secrecy laws should be tightened. i welcome the idea of consolidating the tax base. however, i am lacking a clear commitment to widen the tax base and am critical of the transitional period before consolidation.

in writing. ‒ last year we discovered that about 340 multinationals had secured privileged deals with luxemburg in order to avoid paying taxes on their activities all over europe. other member states have done similar deals. our committee has made several proposals to fight this situation, taking into account the weak state of our finances. dear colleagues, what multinationals do not pay, smes should not compensate with a higher tax burden. simplification of our tax systems, a common corporate tax base to ensure fair competition and much higher transparency criteria in corporate financial statements – these are all fundamental reforms we need. it is disappointing that some member states like spain have been so reluctant to make public tax ruling and multinationals privileges. we catalans also want a new state to lead in this fight for a more fair and reformed tax system that does not give privileges to multinationals against smes and citizens, putting at risk our welfare state.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because i believe that multinational companies should pay taxes where they make their profits. the current competition in tax matters leads to aggressive tax planning and evasion practices. the lack of a regulatory framework at community level is detrimental to european citizens. it is not fair that large companies sometimes pay reduced taxes on their profits, while citizens and smes do pay their fair share. transparency is essential to ensure that everyone plays by the same rules.
mr president, i voted against this report because it focuses on the symptoms and not on the problems that cause them. the whole weight of the report is on the coercive measures and social controls which add to the problem of extremism the deterioration of our freedoms. we can't fight the problem with more fear, by creating more fear. as we pointed out in the seven urgent measures to combat terrorism which my delegation sent to the members of this house, to martin schulz and also to federica mogherini, legal or police measures alone are not enough. we believe that to prevent radicalisation it is essential to strengthen strategies for social cohesion and inclusion, and in particular education, as the way to offer future alternatives for a cohesive and supportive society.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is a timely exercise in what europe can do to prevent european citizens from being radicalised, especially online, and recruited by terrorist organisations. we must learn to intervene in the content of the net which incites violent extremism; to intervene also in the socialization of terror in prisons; to prevent not only the trafficking of arms, through these sophisticated means, but also the financing of such indoctrination; and to freeze their assets, all this at european level. we must learn to cooperate police to share information about those 5,000 europeans who have come in and gone out after being trained for terrorism somewhere abroad. but we must also denounce that austerity and the collapse of education, inclusion and integration policies in marginalized neighbourhoods and particularly vulnerable groups have made many young europeans willing to embark on this mad spiral of destructive and self-destructive violence, and to declare themselves willing not only to kill, but to die by killing. this is the challenge we must solve. i hope that this report will provide european added value to the terrible challenge that terrorism poses to europe.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the prevention of radicalisation and the recruitment of european citizens by terrorist organisations, because it was drawn up from the outset without any intention of addressing the root causes of inequality, the lack of prospects and alternatives, and xenophobia, which pushes young people into such positions, but simply aims to stigmatise whole groups. there are no shortcuts against terrorism, and that is precisely what this report is aiming at by recommending measures of a populist nature. in addition, the work of european agencies such as europol, which is totally opaque to scrutiny by citizens and institutions, is being strengthened, and their ties with countries with little guarantee of respect for human rights, such as the theocratic monarchies of the persian gulf, are being strengthened. it also seeks to curtail rights and freedoms on the net, recommending the possibility of removing internet content without a prior court order. another concern i have is the criminal aspect, which is that it is committed to allowing the segregation of prisoners on the basis of their cultural origin. these and other reasons are the main reasons why i voted against.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report and i share the view expressed today by the chairman of my group, guy verhofstad. terrorists do not respect national borders, so we must have security and intelligence beyond borders. if we have to choose between sovereignty and security, the security of our citizens must prevail. this leads me to ask once again for coordination between all the police forces and, in our case, coordination with the ertzaintza of the security forces of the spanish state so that, on equal terms, it can have access to the data necessary for the fight against jihadism.

in writing. ‒ i voted against the report on the prevention of radicalisation and the recruitment of european citizens by terrorist organisations, because it was drawn up from the outset without any intention of addressing the root causes of inequality, the lack of prospects and alternatives, and xenophobia, which pushes young people into such positions, but simply aims to stigmatise whole groups. there are no shortcuts against terrorism, and that is precisely what this report is aiming at by recommending measures of a populist nature. in addition, the work of european agencies such as europol, which is totally opaque to scrutiny by citizens and institutions, is being strengthened, and their ties with countries with little guarantee of respect for human rights, such as the theocratic monarchies of the persian gulf, are being strengthened. it also seeks to curtail rights and freedoms on the net, recommending the possibility of removing internet content without a prior court order. another concern i have is the criminal aspect, which is that it is committed to allowing the segregation of prisoners on the basis of their cultural origin. these and other reasons are the main reasons why i voted against.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report, which shows the total lack of clarity of the europeans in the face of the terrorist threat. far from calling into question the openness of borders and schengen, this report makes a panegyric on communitarianism and immigration. the most worrying aspect of the report is the vacuity of its proposals: it calls for the implementation of a communication strategy to prevent radicalisation, the encouragement of the exchange of good practice between member states in the face of the rise of terrorist radicalisation in prisons, and the encouragement of educational establishments to propose programmes to strengthen understanding and tolerance. the dati report goes even further in its ideological blindness by calling for the strengthening of the dialogue on security and the fight against terrorism with countries such as saudi arabia and turkey... the european parliament, however, rejected the common sense amendments tabled by our group, which proposed, among other things, the reintroduction of systematic checks at national borders, the stopping of mass immigration, the cessation of support for islamist groups in syria and the prevention of the return of jihadist fighters to europe.

mr president, i agree with the report's diagnosis: instability in employment, low wages, indiscriminate subcontracting and generally poor working conditions are factors which contribute decisively to an increase in accidents at work and to worsening health of workers. when a company does not do its duty in the field of safety, tragedies such as the one of fifty workers poisoned by mercury in the asturias zinc factory in my region, asturias, occur. and that is that occupational diseases are paid for, in the end, by all of us in the form of lost productivity in our economies and increased expenditure on our national health and social security systems. i also take the gender approach in this report because europe needs comprehensive policies of reconciliation, rather than continuing to over exploit women with double and triple working hours. and my vote for this report and its recommendations is positive, but i also want to make a warning to the european socialists, because to continue to support austerity policies and the atci means to continue to deepen the precariousness ... mr president, the precarious nature of working relationships, irregular rhythms, illegal working hours and the high turnover of contracts are the fundamental causes of the increase in accidents and occupational diseases. in my country, spain, too, after the serious labour reforms. quality employment and trade unions are crucial in risk prevention and the development of occupational health and safety strategies. we do not support the reduction of social dialogue in the responsible european agency, eu-osha, nor the cuts in its resources. that said, i would like to refer specifically to endocrine disruptors. the authorization of dehp and the desire to remove occupational health from the chemical hazard regulations (reach) are irresponsible acts. a serious public health crisis such as asbestos is brewing, and will remain unresolved as long as it remains present in buildings and facilities in europe. we demand a unified framework for the protection and compensation of those affected by asbestos and occupational diseases such as silicosis. no economic interest can take precedence over the rights of workers.
in writing. ‒ precarious working conditions, irregular work patterns, illegal working hours and high turnover of contracts are the main causes of the increase in accidents and occupational diseases. this is why quality employment and trade unions are crucial in risk prevention and the development of occupational health and safety strategies. the rapporteur's report shares this position and calls for the eu strategy to address such important challenges as the gender approach or the ageing workforce, as well as specific risks such as endocrine disruptors or exposure to asbestos. i have therefore voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the eu strategic framework for health and safety at work 2014-2020. it is a strategic framework that we must promote by emphasising that all workers have the right to the highest level of protection in the field of health and safety at work, which must be guaranteed regardless of the size of the company that employs them, the type of work, their contract or the member state in which they work. specific employment strategies covering all forms of employment provided for in union employment legislation should be developed and rules should be clearer and more efficient.
in writing. in 2014, the commission published the eu strategic framework on health and safety at work 2014-2020, which seeks to address three main challenges: further improving and simplifying existing rules, improving the prevention of work-related diseases by taking into account new risks, and addressing the ageing of the workforce. but it lacks an ambitious agenda to put forward legislative proposals to improve the situation of workers with regard to existing and emerging risks other than occupational diseases. this report sets out parliament's position on the new strategic framework, calling on the commission to come forward with concrete legislative proposals on better health and safety at work and to turn its 'strategic framework' into a real strategy on health and safety at work, so that after the planned review in 2016, more concrete legislative or non-legislative measures, as well as implementation and enforcement tools, are included in the framework. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.

in writing. ‒ the eu strategic framework on health and safety at work takes a step forward in protecting workers' rights and promotes increased protection of safety and health at the workplace. we in our group believe that it is important to protect these rights and to deal with the possible diseases of the new generation in a more specific way and adapted to the needs of the worker.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour, fully aware of the importance of improving and enforcing legislation on health and safety at work. every year, more than 4 000 workers lose their lives due to work-related accidents, and the number of fatal work-related diseases is over 150 000 each year. we must fight against the causes of the loss of european workers' lives. the degree of enforcement by member states needs to be improved in order to improve the health and safety situation of workers and to ensure a level playing field for enterprises.
in writing. ‒ more than 4 000 people die every year in the eu due to an accident at work and 150 000 suffer from work-related diseases. however 24 eu directives regulate health and safety at work which have been only partially implemented in member states. a different approach is therefore needed to address this issue. it was with this in mind that i supported this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it is part of a broad and inclusive approach to health and safety at work and incorporates many of the amendments tabled by the gue/ngl group. the most important aspect is that all workers have the right to the highest level of protection in the field of health and safety at work, regardless of the size of the company, the member state or the type of employment contract. at the same time, four key points in the text make us vote in favour: (a) smes: effective management of health and safety at work remains a challenge; providing them with information and facilities is essential; (b) labour inspections: increasing staffing and resources is essential to carrying out their functions; (c) social dialogue: further progress is proposed to provide training and promote the figure of health and safety representatives; (d) gender references: important references to ending stereotypes about the lower hazards of jobs performed mainly by women.

those who understand that society is not equal. and in the face of this figure, in the face of this reality, today, 25 november, we have the responsibility, we have the obligation to speak out, to time to stop the words and it is time to act, because women can no longer wait, because day after day we see in the media, in the news, how there are women who, for the mere fact of being women, are killed, their lives are cut short and the lives of their sons and daughters are cut short. we need to live in a more equal society. we need to make commitments: it is our duty, it is our responsibility. and that is why we are today asking the european commission a series of questions. it is not the first time that this debate has brought us to the plenary of this parliament and we hope that with today's debate we will have the european commission's commitments for all the work that needs to be done from now on. we want to know when the european commission will present its strategy for equality between men and women. this parliament has already spoken on the content of this strategy, and we believe it is essential that a large part of the policy on equality between men and women should give priority to the fight against gender-based violence. but we also want to know other things. the european institutions have already taken some steps in this area. the victim protection order was an essential element. the deadline for member states to transpose the directive has expired less than a year ago. we want to know when the european commission intends to give us its assessment of how the implementation of this european protection order has worked. but we also understand that it is fundamental, that it is essential that legislative action can be taken. it is not the first time, mrs jourová, that you have heard this complaint from the european parliament. we are not going to solve this situation by supporting the organizations and by raising awareness. legislation is necessary because legislation implies a commitment, legislation implies an obligation to comply ―with the legislation― by the member states to combat gender-based violence. we have heard many times that there is no competence level in europe to fight against gender violence, but we do not resign ourselves and we believe that things can change, because - as i have said on several occasions in these debates - if we have managed to give europe competencies in the fight against the economic crisis, we can also look for the competencies that europe must have to fight against gender violence, to fight for a more just and more equal society. so let us all look for it, let us all join together - the council, the commission, the parliament - to look for that legislative capacity, because we cannot wait any longer, we cannot continue to make announcements that are simply that, commitments, and then do not translate into reality. we are talking about the lives of women, the lives of half the population of europe. they deserve our respect, they deserve us to be aware that we have the possibility of doing much more than is being done at the moment. this is an issue that should involve all of us, all institutions, at all levels. we must now unite all our efforts because women deserve it; because the memory of all those who have been killed by sexist terrorists deserves our work; because we are talking about the future of our generation, but also that of our daughters; because it is our responsibility and it is our obligation.
member of the commission.– mr president, i would like to thank you for raising this very important and serious subject on the occasion of the international day for the elimination of violence against women. it is an important political signal that both parliament and the commission decided to join the un women’s orange day campaign to mark the international day for the elimination of violence against women and to light up their buildings in orange today. violence against women remains a challenge in every country in europe. in 2015 women are still beaten, humiliated, raped, mutilated, stalked, harassed and forced into marriage. violence happens in their homes at the hands of their partners or family members. it happens in the workplace or in education from colleagues, fellow students, professors or bosses. it can happen on the streets or online from strangers. we know that one in three women in the eu has experienced physical or sexual violence or both. violence has a lifelong impact on the health and wellbeing of victims, as well as on their families. this in turn has an impact on the economy and society as a whole. promoting gender equality and combating violence against women go hand in hand. women need to be empowered to leave abusive relationships and to challenge violence when they encounter it. they should not be hampered in fulfilling their potential in the workplace and in society. i will present in december a detailed commission plan and commitment on improving gender equality in the years to come. i am prepared to submit also to the committee on women’s rights and gender equality (femm) the proposal for the gender strategic document for the years 2016 to 2019. we have worked on this with all stakeholders throughout this year, and your input in the process was also very valuable. among the priorities it will include further measures to support member states in preventing and combating all forms of gender-based violence. regarding gender-based violence, the commission is taking a determined and comprehensive approach based on legislation, awareness-raising and funding, as well as improving knowledge and data collection. i will start by focusing on legislation. the eu adopted legislation to prevent violence against women and to protect and support its victims, including in areas such as sexual harassment, trafficking in human beings, sexual abuse and sexual exploitation of children and child pornography. our modern victims’ rights in the victims directive, on which we have worked closely with you, just entered into force on 16 november this year. this will have a huge impact on some member states, for instance those which will have to establish victim support structures, which are of key importance for gender-based violence and which do not exist in all member states yet. you can count on my commitment that the commission will be guiding and monitoring the effective implementation of this piece of legislation, as well as the broader legal framework. we have to ensure that available protection measures are actually granted to persons at risk and applied in practice. since january 2015, victims of domestic violence have benefited from reinforced protection when travelling or moving to other eu countries. protection orders granted in their home country can circulate across eu borders. the transposition situation is encouraging. thanks to enforcement procedures initiated by the commission, we now have national rules transposing the european protection orders directive in 21 member states. i am glad to inform you also that on 9 october the commission published a roadmap on future accession of the eu to the council of europe’s istanbul convention. the roadmap is a first concrete step towards accession to this powerful tool to combat violence against women and domestic violence. eu accession to the convention would reflect our commitment to combating human rights violations and discrimination, both within and beyond the eu. the commission also supports awareness-raising and concrete grassroots actions by member states, civil society organisations and european networks. this year, eur 8 million was allocated to combating violence against women under the rights, equality and citizenship programme. we have also empowered advocates for change among female genital mutilation-practising communities, trained services for victims of sexual violence in universities to better respond to incidents and young victims’ needs, and supported member states in sensitising the general public to this problem. i am proud to inform you about last week’s decision to award a total amount of eur 4.3 million to nine international projects combating violence against women linked to harmful practices. within the framework of this awareness-raising work, i am also committed to putting into place focused actions on violence against women in 2017. we are currently planning future activities and would welcome your cooperation. i would also like to say a few words about the importance of improving our knowledge about the causes of gender-based violence on a regular basis. it is essential because it allows for monitoring of the situation across the eu and also helps us to formulate and implement better policies. my services are working with eurostat and the european institute for gender equality, two key actors in this area which, i believe, can help to fill the gaps. finally, let me be clear that i see a need to address cyber-violence against women and girls – an emerging form of violence. we have eu legislation and policies on children’s – including girls’ – safety and protection from bullying, abuse and exploitation online. in addition, the commission has launched a eur 3 million call for proposals to combat sexual harassment and sexual violence against women and girls, including through new technologies and social media. proposals are now being assessed.
on behalf of the ppe group mr president, commissioner jourová, thank you for your commitment to the victims. today is the international day for the elimination of violence against women and some may still wonder why this day. well, because it's fundamental that society reacts. all efforts are inadequate to raise awareness and promote decisive action to put an end to this scourge, to which we cannot get used. the "i don't see, i don't hear, i don't speak" dynamic has to end. it is necessary to break down this wall built on the fear and loneliness of the victim, because the one who wins, in the face of this desperate silence, is the aggressor, who feels strong to continue abusing, harassing and, in the worst case, killing the woman he says he loves. most cases of violence against women come from their partner and, in the case of children, from people in their environment. it's important for victims to report, but to do so, they need to feel protected. i am therefore proud to have been rapporteur for the european order for the protection of victims, so that national restraining orders are recognised in any european country, which promotes the safety of women fleeing their abusers. there is still a long way to go in european legislation. that is why we have tabled this oral question, to find out what european strategy the commission is pursuing. greater commitment is needed to eradicate this violation of human rights, which is a consequence of inequality between men and women. it is estimated that 35% of women and girls experience some form of physical or sexual violence in their lifetime. and this has to stop, because i firmly believe that if we work on education, also on prevention, on protection for victims and, of course, on greater control of the
