in writing. ‒ i did not vote in favour of this report because i consider that the very activity of frontex, its work of militarization and defence of the borders, represents a permanent violation of fundamental rights. that is why my group has tabled amendments to the report calling for the dismantling of frontex, as it is the only effective way of putting an end to the systematic violations of human rights at the eu's borders, and thus making clear our total rejection of frontex. the mechanism adopted, which is intended to provide the possibility of lodging complaints about violations of fundamental rights in the context of the european agency's operations, also has a serious shortcoming, in respect of which we also tabled amendments which were also rejected: its lack of independence, since the agency itself is responsible for handling complaints made by its staff.
in writing. ‒ members of this parliament believe that frontex should establish a mechanism to process complaints from citizens or organisations who consider that the fundamental rights of migrants and asylum seekers have been violated. for that reason, we voted in favour of this resolution, which i support after hearing the recommendations of the european ombudsman, because i believe it is important to regulate this process to protect all parties involved and to prevent abuse.

in writing. ‒ the own-initiative report by mrs metsola and mrs keller demonstrates the commitment of this house to human rights. the ombudsman is right to point out the need for a clear commitment to human rights and for remedies in the event of non-compliance. but i also believe that it is necessary to ensure that frontex's operations are carried out properly and are not burdened with an untenable administrative burden. it is also important to remember that frontex is intrinsically linked to the full respect and protection of fundamental human rights in the fulfilment of its mandate. it is good that human rights are guaranteed and that there is a right to 'complain' in cases where abuses of any kind are taking place, provided that they are proven and duly justified. frontex currently has its own mechanisms for ensuring respect for human rights at both community and national level.
in writing. ‒ this resolution is the response to the support that this commission wants to give to all common policies with an impact on cities, where the majority of europeans live. in the face of those who think that the union's action in the urban environment is not appropriate, the socialists defend its relevance, and proof of this is that we have succeeded in getting the connecting europe facility or funds such as the efsi to finance urban nodes. we support this resolution because we share many of the proposals for safer and more sustainable urban transport, accessible to all, and in which public transport plays a predominant role. we would have liked to have clarified the reference to urban tolls. we believe that such actions must be accompanied by measures to discriminate favourably against those who have been expelled from the centre and to prevent it from becoming the exclusive preserve of the wealthy classes. nor do we think it is right to unconditionally support any form of mobility in the sharing economy, such as uber, which pits against the ropes sectors such as cooperatives and the self-employed in the taxi sector that do comply with social and labour legislation and offer a safe and quality public service.
in writing. ‒ improving urban mobility is a key step towards reducing global emissions, as well as improving air quality and traffic safety in european cities. although the final proposal of the report is not ambitious and contains contradictory elements, such as the absence of a criticism of the deregulation implicit in the 'sharing economy' or a certain voluntarism in addressing the energy transition, we believe that the support given to transport planning, its intermodal integration and the improvement of its efficiency justifies the vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ the delli report, after a long process of conciliation between the different groups, has proved acceptable to all in proposing a series of measures to tackle, among others, the problem of pollution from transport powered by fossil fuels. while it has lost some definition in quantifying objectives related to the use of public or alternative means, it proposes numerous measures, integrated and coordinated at different administrative levels, aimed at protecting the climate, health and the environment, as well as promoting welfare and safety. the aim is to promote smart and sustainable cities. that is why we voted in favour of the report.

in writing. ‒ coinciding with the cop 21 being held in paris these days, this report seems to me more than appropriate. as the summit has already stated, we are facing a climate emergency. all countries must react and make commitments to curb climate change; it is a challenge for all. we, the european union, must promote initiatives that seek to ensure the sustainability and durability of the planet. given that 80% of europeans live in cities, the challenge of achieving sustainable urban mobility is a small step in the efforts we must make to reduce emissions. in recent years we have seen a reduction in emissions from industry and agriculture. however, the transport sector has only grown. we must propose more efficient and inclusive urban transport systems for all, giving access to all people with reduced mobility. the european union must have the financial mechanisms and instruments to achieve a new model of urban mobility adapted to the needs of our times.
mr president, commissioner, we are faced with perhaps the most important debate of this parliament: the debate on the energy union. it's because it's important to combat the energy dependence that's weighing on our economy; it's because it's important to combat climate change by pushing renewable energy; and it's because we need to democratize energy and make it affordable for consumers. this requires doing more europe, guaranteeing at least 10% interconnection, and ending energy islands. this is reflected in the council conclusions, the commission communication and the european parliament's position; the treaty itself contains the necessary solidarity that must be present in the union's energy policy. all these bodies are therefore called upon to make every effort to achieve the 10% target. in that sense, i would have liked the eriksson report to have been perhaps clearer, with a more closed defence of that 10%. because i think it not only does not defend, but questions, the 15%, and introduces the necessary scientific and technical evaluation of this 10%. i would like to remind you that this is a political objective and not a scientific or technical one. i would therefore have liked a much clearer strategy to end these energy islands which are so necessary today. this is in contrast to the report on 'towards a european energy union', which clearly defends the 10% minimum; i also believe that this report, although it contains aspects which the socialist group of course cannot share, is a good report in the sense that it contains many other proposals which i consider innovative and important, such as support for self-consumption of renewable energy and the role of the consumer in energy management. finally, in order to achieve greater consistency, i would ask that the three amendments contained in the texts of the commission, the council and the european parliament in this connection be supported. (the speaker agrees to answer a question put under the 'blue card' procedure (rule 162 (8) of the rules of procedure))
, reply of 'blue card'. mr eriksson, i just want to say that - as you have said - it is not incompatible at all. the defence of regional objectives is not incompatible with the priority and first necessity of defending the minimum 10% of interconnection needed to put an end to energy islands. so, we agree. what i have said is simply that i would have liked a more firm defence of the 10% minimum needed to eliminate the three energy islands we have in the european union at the moment, because if it is not done that way, we will not eliminate them - as you know very well - in view of the progress and the figures at our disposal.
mr president, commissioner, it is clear - and it is almost tautological to say so - that if there is to be energy integration in the union, we need connections; if there are to be connections, we need to operate where there are major emergencies. in october 2014, the council therefore stated in its statement that it instructed the commission, supported by the member states, to take urgent measures to achieve a minimum target of 10% of existing electricity interconnections as a matter of urgency and by 2020 at the latest. it is clear that integration must take place at regional level, that integration must take place through this kind of interconnection for those countries which, as the rapporteur himself and other members have said, are the most disconnected, the most remote, the most island countries. that is why it is striking that this political decision of 10% is described as lacking a scientific basis. this really doesn't make any sense. it is a political objective based on a fact and therefore we must always act in a proportionate way, as has always been the case in the european union for the purposes of integration. those who have more needs, have more urgency to solve it. we must integrate and not create, well, a little bit of this unease that sometimes is created about who has priorities and who does not. i believe that the priorities are for everyone, but for some, more immediately than for others, because they are in a situation of less capacity. (the speaker agrees to answer a question put under the 'blue card' procedure (rule 162 (8) of the rules of procedure))
the answer is 'blue card'. i think we have to distinguish, mr rapporteur, between what is a political objective and what are the measures to achieve that objective. the political objective is based on a true fact. the fact is that there is a greater disintegration - a number of countries are out, not a few - and therefore that is what needs to be addressed. the truth is, calling that a lack of scientific evidence is a little strange. the list of policy objectives which would be characterized as lacking scientific evidence, as seems to be understood in this case, would be immense. so let's get through it.
mr president, a serious european union requires a common energy market which ensures the security and resilience of the system, which eliminates our dependence on third parties, which promotes decarbonisation, innovation and the integration of consumers and producers and which eliminates the problems of competition not only from outside but also from within. we have talked a lot about energy prices in the united states and china and how they compare with those in europe, but we have talked less about the distortions we have in the internal market. the effort that a basque industrialist, for example, makes in innovation, efficiency, procedures, internationalisation, is compensated by his competitors in other parts of the union with an insulting differential in the price they pay for energy. if we add to this the different credit conditions, we agree that there is no such thing as free competition in the internal market. that is why we cannot put off the target of at least 10% immediate electricity interconnection, like the legislative initiatives announced by the commissioner and 15% of interconnection by 2030.
mr president, this report contains the building blocks for transforming our energy model; it sets the stage for ensuring that citizens, and also businesses, have access to affordable energy; it promotes self-consumption from renewable energy sources and proposes clear measures to combat energy poverty; it also recognises the potential of the energy sector as a factor of competitiveness and as a driver of innovation and job creation. however, we know that the transition to this more sustainable, more democratic, more competitive and more secure model is not neutral. we must therefore resist attempts to put the principle of technological neutrality on the table and we must continue to push renewable energies decisively to ensure european leadership.
member of the commission.– mr president, the recent attacks in paris revealed once again the radical face of terrorism. we know that over the past decade several member states have been targeted and experienced tragic losses. let me mention all of them: spain, estonia, the united kingdom, france, the netherlands, greece, sweden, germany, italy, norway, bulgaria, belgium and denmark. the 2012 victims’ rights directive that entered into application in the member states last month is the major general instrument on victims’ rights at eu level. it lays down a set of binding rights for all victims of crime, including rights to protection, support and assistance that take into account the individual needs of every victim of crime. it does not, however, provide the specific measures that would respond directly to the needs of victims of terrorism. terrorist attacks leave behind individuals who have been injured, traumatised or lost their lives as a result of the attack. the victims of such attacks require specific protection, support and assistance that would respond to their specific needs related to the nature of this crime. that is why the commission decided to introduce specific provisions on victims of terrorism to the proposal for a directive on combatting terrorism of 2 december. the main objective is to oblige the eu member states to criminalise terrorist offences and offences related to terrorism such as travel and training for terrorist purposes and financing of terrorism without, however, forgetting about the victims of terrorism. this proposal responds more precisely to the needs of victims of terrorism. in particular, the proposed directive requires member states to ensure that victims of terrorism receive immediate access to professional specialist support services providing for physical and psycho-social treatment. such support will be available for as long as necessary. terrorist attacks often result in chaos and disinformation, and access to reliable information for victims of terrorism and about victims of terrorism is therefore crucial. the proposed directive requires that the support services provide access to such reliable information. under the proposed directive, the competent national authorities would be required to cooperate closely to ensure that all victims of terrorism are well informed and receive the necessary support and assistance, independently of where in the european union they live. the tailored rules on protection, support and assistance to the victims of terrorism will add to the healing process of and local police, prison and probation officers, social and health workers, teachers, civil society organisations, security officials and, last but not least, victims groups and associations. victims of terrorism deserve our solidarity and support. they also have a very prominent role to play in countering radicalisation. their testimonies can provide a crucial contribution in preventive work. within the ran, a specific working group on the remembrance of victims of terrorism has been set up. it will be instrumental in organising the 11 march remembrance day for the victims of terrorism in 2016. since the madrid bombings in 2004, the commission has been commemorating the european remembrance day of victims of terrorism on 11 march exactly, and will continue to do so with the support of the ran. the event will allow us to remember and honour those who have suffered and help the healing process of those who continue to suffer. furthermore, with the help of the ran we will make sure that the voices of the victims are heard and are openly and widely heard, especially among radicalised youth, as the stories and suffering of victims must never be in vain. these voices should make those individuals on the brink of extremism think twice before they act. i am particularly convinced of the important role victims can play in counter-narrative campaigns as well as, for example, in prison and probation. we will make sure that their experiences and stories can have a powerful but positive influence on individuals at risk or already radicalised.

member of the commission.– madam president, i would like to thank the rapporteur, mr sven schulze, for his report, which stresses the importance of adequate access to, and the availability of, finance with a direct impact on europe’s 2020 targets, fostering employment and fighting poverty and social exclusion. our ambition, as highlighted several times by president juncker, is to create quality jobs and get europe growing again. microfinance is an important tool to promote entrepreneurship and help europe get back on the path to growth and, ultimately, to reduce social and financial exclusion. i therefore welcome this report, which sheds light on the european progress microfinance facility’s achievements in making entrepreneurship an option for all, including vulnerable persons and those who would be otherwise financially excluded. to promote the potential of microfinance for enabling entrepreneurship, on 19 october this year my colleague, commissioner thyssen, opened the first european microfinance day in brussels, together with the luxembourg presidency and representatives of the european investment bank, the european parliament and the european economic and social committee. your report rightly highlights that the facility has substantially contributed to job preservation and, if i may add, to job creation with over 60 000 jobs created or maintained thanks to this facility. in addition, half of micro-borrowers reported an increase in their turnover thanks to the microloans made possible by this facility. the relevance of the facility to enabling unemployed and disadvantaged people to gain access to finance, especially in times of crisis, is well underlined in your report. indeed, progress microfinance has a track record of successful outreach to such vulnerable groups. a recently published report by the european court of auditors assisting the facility’s intervention in microfinance concluded that thanks to the use of financial instruments it has adequately addressed the needs of micro-entrepreneurs. moreover, the financial instruments under the successor eu programme for employment and social innovation (easi) could also play an important role in addressing some of the challenges posed by the intensifying refugee influx. your report precisely points to the fact that while progress microfinance can be considered successful as a whole, there is room for improvement. indeed, these improvements, such as greater outreach to target vulnerable groups and improved social impact reporting, combined with technical assistance and dedicated support for capacity-building of microcredit providers and increased complementarity with other instruments, have been taken into account in the design of the successor employment and social innovation programme, as well as specific support for social enterprises, which is a priority objective of the commission. the easi programme is making eur 193 million available until 2020. this includes eur 96 million in guarantees which can leverage more than eur 500 million to micro and social entrepreneurs. moreover, i would like to stress that the easi regulation already includes a definition of ‘social enterprise’. therefore, it would be advisable to stick to this definition. in addition to guarantees and funded instruments, easi financial instruments will offer funding for capacity building. this will help microcredit providers develop their business and better channel much—needed funds to the most excluded clients, which are often hard to reach. i am very pleased to announce that the recently launched guarantee scheme, with about eur 90 million for microfinance and social entrepreneurship, has made a very promising start. in four months, the european investment fund, which manages the scheme, has received over 30 applications, accounting for approximately half of the total budget. in conclusion, i welcome the report’s recommendation that the progress microfinance facility should be continued. however, as you know, the investment period under this instrument draws to a close in april 2016. the commission is confident that the easi programme will build upon the success of progress microfinance. it will continue and expand activity in this area and deliver on the improvements highlighted by honourable members in their findings on the progress programme, thus bringing even better results in the fight against social and financial exclusion and opening up routes to good employment.

are the main instruments for achieving the objectives of the common fisheries policy, and we should not be fooled by the concept of 'techniques' as if it were a secondary concept. in fact, this matter is of paramount political importance. technical measures are crucial to the lives of hundreds of thousands of fishermen and it is therefore important that we formulate them correctly. we believe that the current legislation, which consists of a large number of legislative acts, needs to be amended to adapt it to the new common fisheries policy by incorporating aspects such as the prohibition of discards and regionalisation. this review should allow for the simplification and reformulation of rules that have become obsolete following the reform of the cfp, as well as those that are not working or that should be improved, and of course it should serve to improve the understanding of the intricate set of legislative texts that are in force in order to facilitate compliance by the sectors concerned. we have a challenge. the new rules must be able to respond quickly to changes in resources and ecosystems and take account in real time of technical developments in more selective fishing gear. european legislation should support this development, not hinder it, and should be based on scientifically proven grounds. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of the environment in the event of a natural disaster. we need, as the sector asks us, a flexible framework, able to respond to the different circumstances and new situations we are facing at any given moment. i would also like to stress the importance of always applying proportionality criteria to avoid unavoidable socioeconomic consequences. in this report which we are debating today, i propose an architecture for the new regulation based on four pillars: three of them would be on a set of common and centralised rules, on specific rules for the most important sea basins and on a number of specific rules adopted by codecision; and a fourth pillar, subject to regionalisation, should be applied to regional rules which are subject to frequent changes. as regards multiannual plans, they are the most appropriate vehicle for the adoption and implementation of specific technical measures for the various fisheries. we must therefore ensure that they achieve their objective. we need to continue our efforts as co-legislators to reach agreements on the multiannual plans as regards the institutional competences provided for in the treaty and on the basis of the most recent relevant case law. and of course, we need to increase the involvement of stakeholders in the design and development of these plans and in all decisions concerning regionalisation. i hope that my own-initiative report will be the starting point for a constructive debate in which we should do our utmost to listen to the various fisheries sectors concerned and to reconcile their interests with the preservation of marine resources. i hope, madam commissioner, that the proposal which the commission is preparing and which we hope to hear in a few months will take account of these principles and recommendations.

madam president, it would have been good if mr juncker had stayed to hear all the speeches. i think mr juncker is also right when he says that monetary union is a political project. i agree with him. this has been clear to european citizens since the beginning of the crisis. the union's policies have increased inequality and violated the sovereignty of the countries of the south, in accordance with a political project that puts the interests of the big private and central european banks first. the integration project which we are now being presented with is moving along the same lines: increasing the union's power over budgets, tax systems and wage policies through the competitiveness councils. and with their proposal to incorporate the european stability mechanism into the european treaties they are seeking to extend the whip of austerity and blackmail to the whole of europe. with the banking union, they also promote financial concentration which raises huge giants of clay that can fall on all of us. if you really want democratic control over such a deeply unequal and unjust system, this is a farce. if you really want democracy, then promote progressive tax harmonization so that those who have more pay more, build a budget that promotes sustainable and redistributive investment in europe, create a public bank that really guarantees the social function of credit and wait to hear all the speeches of all the members.
madam president, commissioner, we are in the midst of a debate on the euro area which is at the same time a debate on its future project and also on the economic recovery which is in the making. and it is true that we have to be clear. the euro area is still experiencing a slower and weaker recovery than, for example, the european union in the 1980s: we have less investment than our competitors in monetary zones elsewhere in the world; our poverty is still unabated; we are creating employment levels, but the jobs we are creating are still weak and, above all, precarious. and in the face of all this, the question is: is the answer given to us by the european commission - the report of the five presidents - sufficient to achieve the objective of achieving a stronger economic recovery and, above all, of creating an optimal monetary area, when we have a single market with twenty-eight fragmented labour markets, a monetary union with nineteen different fiscal policies and a political union without a strong common budget to strengthen it, to cement it? i don't think it is. there are many things missing from your proposal: we see nowhere the framework for european minimum wages, which, for example, can prevent us from facing again a wage devaluation that is generalising labour poverty in the european union. the european automatic stabilisers are missing, which we must also use to deal with asymmetric shocks: the european unemployment insurance, which this house has so often called for. the mutualization of debt is also missing. we cannot live - neither the euro area nor the project for the future nor the economic recovery - only by draghi and monetary policy. we need more ambition from the european commission and we need more foresight to avoid future crises.
madam president, the euro has been a fraud on the peoples of the south. if this is not recognised, analysed and assessed, the consequences of the economic and monetary union they envisage will continue to widen inequalities and worsen poverty situations. the president of the eurogroup spoke to us again this morning about structural reforms, pension reforms, labour reforms. we are already aware of these proposals, and they have been nothing but a blackmail on the popular classes throughout the european union and, above all, on the peoples of the south. we would have liked mr juncker to speak today about how policies are going to be put in place to rescue people from poverty, how decent jobs are going to be recovered and created and how good prices for farmers are going to be guaranteed, how small businesses and small and mediumsized enterprises are going to be maintained and also how public education and health are going to be guaranteed.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the swiss confederation joining the european asylum support office (easo). this incorporation had been delayed due to new swiss legislative measures which were thought to be in breach of the geneva convention. however, following a review of the legislation, it has been concluded that this is not the case and that switzerland can access this institution, which has among its obligations to ensure compliance with international legislation in this area. we believe that coordination and support between different countries in the field of asylum policy is essential to be able to respond better to the situation and that is why we are in favour of incorporation, while at the same time demanding that coordination be more effective and that human rights be truly guaranteed.
in writing. the european asylum support office (easo) is an agency of the european union that has been operating since 2011. its tasks are to promote cooperation between member states on asylum, to support member states whose asylum and reception systems are under particular pressure and to improve the implementation of the common european asylum system (ceas). switzerland joined easo as an associated country. let's vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i have given my support to this resolution by which the european parliament gives its consent to the agreement between the european union and the swiss confederation on the modalities of its participation in, representation in and financial contribution to the european asylum support office.

in writing. ‒ this agreement allows dominican and european citizens to travel between the two territories without a visa. although i disagree with the way in which the negotiations have been conducted, with obscurantism and without the involvement of the parliaments, i voted in favour of ratifying it because we are in favour of anything that involves a lightening of the bureaucratic burden and the end of restrictions on freedom of movement.
in writing. the agreements on the short-stay visa waiver represent a further step in the deepening of relations between the european union and third countries, as well as being an additional means of strengthening economic and cultural relations and intensifying political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. in addition to these reasons, which are set out in the minutes by the rapporteur of this recommendation, we believe that we should promote the removal of barriers to the movement of people from third countries in the eu in general. that is why we voted in favour of the conclusion of the agreement between the eu and dominica.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which supports the short-stay visa waiver for dominican citizens with the aim of facilitating travel between this destination and the european union (eu). the elimination of visas in dominica will apply to travel of up to 90 days for a period of 180 days, for any tourist, cultural, scientific or business trip, except those involving a paid activity. the liberalization of visas in these countries is part of a european commission proposal that extends visa exemption to 19 countries. we also ask that full reciprocity be ensured.
in writing. ‒ following the amendment of regulation (ec) no 539/2001 by regulation (eu) no 509/2014 of the european parliament and of the council, the commonwealth of dominica was included in the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement for crossing the borders of the member states. following the adoption of that regulation, and the authorisation of the council, the commission concluded the bilateral agreement between the european union and the commonwealth of dominica between november and december 2014. the agreement was signed on 28 may 2015 and now the european parliament gives its consent to it, with my vote in favour. the agreement provides for a visa-free travel regime for citizens of the union and for nationals of the commonwealth of dominica who are travelling to the territory of the other party for a stay of up to 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver covers all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service, official or special passports) travelling for any purpose other than the pursuit of a paid activity.

in writing. ‒ this resolution promotes the exemption of short-stay visas between the european union and the commonwealth of dominica. it thus builds on the relations already established through the association agreement between the members of the african, caribbean and pacific group of states and the eu (the cotonou agreement) and the celac-eu dialogues. it is also a supplementary means of strengthening economic and cultural relations and intensifying political dialogue on various issues, such as human rights and fundamental freedoms. dominica is a small island developing state whose main economic engine is agriculture and which is struggling to diversify in this direction towards the tourism sector and the production of geothermal energy. this agreement will boost tourism, simplify travel conditions for entrepreneurs, facilitate investment and strengthen economic links between businesses. for these reasons i have voted in favour of this resolution.

in writing. ‒ this resolution promotes the short-stay visa waiver between the eu and samoa, deepening the relations already established through the cotonou agreement. in particular, it is expected to deepen economic and cultural relations and political dialogue on human rights and fundamental freedoms. samoa has one of the most dynamic economies in the pacific islands despite the heavy weight of the agricultural sector. it is hoped that this agreement will have positive results in terms of investment and the tourism sector, and in bringing the peoples of europe and the pacific closer together. as no union state has a consulate in samoa, the costs associated with obtaining visas are quite high and the visa waiver will contribute significantly to tourism and business travel from the eu. i therefore support this resolution.
in writing. ‒ the economy of samoa is one of the most dynamic in the pacific islands. the eu is negotiating a comprehensive economic partnership agreement with 14 countries in the pacific region, of which samoa is a part, and the main areas of economic cooperation between the eu and samoa are currently private sector development, the water sector and tourism development. i therefore believe that the agreement on the short-stay visa waiver will be good for these relations and will make them stronger in the future.
in writing. the agreements on the short-stay visa waiver represent a further step in the deepening of relations between the european union and third countries, as well as being an additional means of strengthening economic and cultural relations and intensifying political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. in addition to these reasons, which are set out in the minutes by the rapporteur of this recommendation, we believe that we should promote the removal of barriers to the movement of people from third countries in the eu in general. we therefore vote in favour of the conclusion of the eu-samoa agreement.
in writing. ‒ this agreement allows samoan and european citizens to travel between the two territories without a visa. although i disagree with the way in which the negotiations have been conducted - with obscurantism and without the involvement of parliaments - i voted in favour of ratifying it, as we are in favour of anything that involves a reduction in bureaucratic burdens and the end of restrictions on freedom of movement.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which supports the short-stay visa waiver for grenada's citizens with the aim of facilitating travel between this destination and the european union (eu). the visa waiver in grenada shall apply to travel of up to 90 days for a period of 180 days, for any tourist, cultural, scientific or business trip, except those involving a paid activity. the liberalization of visas in these countries is part of a european commission proposal that extends visa exemption to 19 countries. we also ask that full reciprocity be ensured.
in writing. ‒ following the amendment of regulation (ec) no 539/2001 by regulation (eu) no 509/2014 of the european parliament and of the council, grenada was included in the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement for crossing the borders of the member states. following the adoption of that regulation on 20 may 2014, and after the authorisation of the council, the commission negotiated and concluded the bilateral agreement between the european union and grenada in november and december 2014. the agreement was signed on 28 may 2015 in brussels and now the european parliament gives its consent to it, with my vote in favour. the agreement provides for a visa-free travel regime for citizens of the union and grenada travelling to the territory of the other party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver applies to all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service, official or special passports) travelling for any purpose other than the pursuit of a paid activity.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the agreement, considering that visa liberalisation will simplify travel conditions for entrepreneurs, facilitate investment and intensify economic ties between companies. this agreement will boost tourism and give new impetus to trade.

in writing. ‒ this resolution promotes the short-stay visa waiver between the eu and grenada, deepening the relations already established through the cotonou agreement, the celac-eu and eu-cariforum dialogues. in particular, it is expected to deepen economic and cultural relations and political dialogue on human rights and fundamental freedoms. grenada's economy is highly dependent on banana and spice exports, although it has already taken steps to diversify its economy. the services sector, in particular tourism and construction, has gained in importance. however, as a small country with limited resources, the visa waiver is expected to have a particularly positive effect on investment and tourism. i therefore support this resolution.

in writing. ‒ following the amendment of regulation (ec) no 539/2001 by regulation (eu) no 509/2014 of the european parliament and of the council, the democratic republic of timor-leste was included in the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement for crossing the borders of the member states. following the adoption of that regulation on 20 may 2014, and after having obtained the authorisation of the council, the commission negotiated and concluded the agreement between the european union and the democratic republic of timor-leste between november and december 2014. the agreement was signed on 26 may 2015 in brussels and now the european parliament gives its consent to it, with my vote in favour. the signed agreement provides for a visa-free travel regime for citizens of the union and for nationals of the democratic republic of timor-leste travelling to the territory of the other party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver applies to all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service, official or special passports) travelling for any purpose other than the pursuit of a paid activity.

in writing. ‒ this agreement allows emirati and european citizens to travel between the two territories without the need for a visa. although we initially agreed to the reduction of bureaucratic burdens and freedom of movement, we believe that this agreement was signed in a very obscurantist way between the european institutions and the emirati authorities. the uae also offers no counterpart to guaranteeing the rights of women or lgbtq people, and maintains legislation that is completely devoid of rights for migrant workers. we have therefore decided to abstain from ratifying the agreement.
in writing. the agreements on the short-stay visa waiver represent a further step in the deepening of relations between the european union and third countries, as well as being an additional means of strengthening economic and cultural relations and intensifying political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. in addition to these reasons, which are set out in the minutes by the rapporteur of this recommendation, we believe that we should promote the removal of barriers to the movement of people from third countries in the eu in general. however, we abstained in the case of the united arab emirates. respect for human rights must be a precondition for any kind of agreement between the eu and any country. in the case of the uae, energy and trade interests cannot be used as a pretext to relegate respect for human, labour and social rights to the background. it is not a country where human and labour rights are violated on a case-by-case basis, but systematically, and there are no democratic mechanisms to denounce or eradicate them.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report which supports the short-stay visa waiver for uae citizens with the aim of facilitating travel between this destination and the european union (eu). the visa waiver in the uae will apply to travel of up to 90 days for any period of 180 days, for any tourist, cultural, scientific or business travel, except those involving a paid activity. the liberalization of visas in these countries is part of a european commission proposal that extends visa exemption to 19 countries. we also ask that full reciprocity be ensured.
in writing. ‒ following the amendment of regulation (eu) no 539/2001 by regulation (ec) no 509/2014, the uae has been included in the list of third countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement for crossing the external borders of the member states. following the adoption of that regulation on 20 may 2014, and after the council authorised it, the commission negotiated and concluded a bilateral agreement between the eu and the uae in november 2014. the agreement was signed on 6 may 2015 in brussels and now the european parliament gives its consent to it, with my vote in favour. it is the first arab state with which the eu has concluded a visa waiver agreement, which includes the creation of a joint technical working group on human rights. the signed agreement provides for a visa-free regime for eu and uae citizens travelling to the territory of the other party for a maximum period of 90 days in any 180-day period. the visa waiver applies to all categories of persons (holders of ordinary, diplomatic, service, official or special passports) travelling for any purpose other than for gainful employment.
in writing. ‒ this agreement allows emirati and european citizens to travel between the two territories without the need for a visa. although we initially agreed to the reduction of bureaucratic burdens and freedom of movement, we believe that this agreement was signed in a very obscurantist way between the european institutions and the emirati authorities. the uae also offers no counterpart to guaranteeing the rights of women or lgbtq people, and maintains legislation that is completely devoid of rights for migrant workers. we have therefore decided to abstain from ratifying the agreement.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour, bearing in mind the important relations between the eu and the uae. more than 150 000 european citizens are established in the uae and the vast majority of them are engaged in economic activities. approximately 1.6 million europeans visit the uae every year. in 2014, some 230,000 uae citizens travelled to europe, mainly on business trips and luxury tourism. the visa waiver agreement will therefore facilitate existing relations.
in writing. ‒ the agreements on the short-stay visa waiver represent a new step in the deepening of relations between the european union and third countries, as well as being an additional means of strengthening economic and cultural relations and intensifying political dialogue on a range of issues, including human rights and fundamental freedoms. in addition to these reasons, which are set out in the minutes by the rapporteur of this recommendation, we believe that we should promote the removal of barriers to the movement of people from third countries in the eu in general. however, we abstained in the case of the united arab emirates. respect for human rights must be a precondition for any kind of agreement between the eu and any country. in the case of the uae, energy and trade interests cannot be used as a pretext to relegate respect for human, labour and social rights to the background. it is not a country where human and labour rights are violated on a case-by-case basis, but systematically, and there are no democratic mechanisms to denounce or eradicate them.
in writing. ‒ this resolution promotes the short-stay visa waiver between the eu and the uae, building on the relations already established through the 1988 cooperation agreement between the european union and the cooperation council for the arab states of the gulf. the agreement provides for visa-free travel for eu and uae nationals travelling for a maximum period of 90 days within a 180-day period. the agreement provides for a more in-depth look at economic and cultural relations between the two parties and political dialogue on issues such as human rights and fundamental freedoms, among others. the high number of european citizens established in the uae - more than 150 000 - and of travellers for tourist or economic reasons each year makes this agreement a tool that will greatly facilitate such mobility. for these reasons i am in favour of this agreement.
in writing. ‒ the visa waiver agreement between the eu and the uae is the first we have concluded with an arab state. i support this decision, which will facilitate trade and travel with a country where thousands of europeans are established and where many citizens travel to europe every year.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report as it allows the mobilisation of eur 2 623 200 following the dismissal of 1 603 workers in 69 enterprises operating in finland, in division 62 of nace revision 2, programming, consultancy and other it-related activities. this mobilization of funds is aimed at mitigating the disastrous social consequences of the economic crisis of the capitalist system. while these funds are not able to solve the problems of these workers in finland, they at least offer the possibility of alleviating a small part of the human drama. it is for all these reasons that i have decided to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. we voted in favour of this dossier insofar as it promotes funds to compensate and establish compensatory measures in cases of relocation to deal with the situation of dismissed workers, in this case in finland in the computer sector. these are measures which, if they were not taken, would leave the workers concerned in a worse position. the vote in favour, however, does not hide the fact that this type of measure is 'bread for today and hunger for tomorrow', while the question of employment and relocations should be approached differently. on the one hand, europe needs an investment plan, which is very different from the juncker plan, and a different employment policy, in order to act in the field of employment. secondly, this alternative should consist in investing in activities for the future, especially in a change of production and energy model, and not in mechanisms which ultimately make it easier for applicants (member states and, by extension, the companies concerned) to dismantle sectors, without raising measures such as the return of subsidies received by companies, or the denunciation of possible re-opening in new territories which may contribute to competitive devaluation.

in writing. ‒ the purpose of this report is to reformulate the eu trade mark regulation and the directive relating to the trade mark legislation of the member states. this and the following report are part of a package of renewal of the whole trademark system at european level. the basic functioning of the trademark system is as follows: a producer of a good or service who intends to protect the name and general characteristics of his product has to register his trademark at both national and european level, defining the name and essential characteristics of his product. this register protects the producer or company against copying, forgery or unauthorisation. the report aims to harmonize, by means of a regulation, the way in which trade marks are registered at european level. among other things, it provides for a significant reduction in the cost of online registration fees. the report contains positive aspects, but also others that raise reservations, such as the blocking system, which does not exclude generic medicines. that is why i abstained.
in writing. we abstained in the vote on this report on trade marks in the eu. we believe it is essential to protect the business fabric with a brand system that is up to the new challenges and accelerated globalisation. but we also understand that in this context, where it is not clear what the system of blocking certain products might be - assuming, moreover, that large companies would never have problems but small businesses would - we cannot vote in favour of giving a blank cheque to a system which needs to be clarified on certain points.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of updating the protection of european trade marks, which aims to promote the fight against counterfeiting and to facilitate the registration of new signs on the market. the commission has already taken a number of measures, provisionally agreed between parliament and the member states, to promote the harmonization of national and european trademark registration systems. these new rules will give greater protection to users and at the same time we have safeguarded freedom of expression, the right to parody or artistic freedom, as well as access to medicines in developing countries. the amendment also introduces greater efficiency in the registration of trade marks, cheaper for smes, and changes in the office for harmonization in the internal market (ohim), which will be renamed the european union intellectual property office.
in writing. ‒ the main objective of this proposal is to boost innovation and economic growth by making trademark registration systems more accessible and efficient across the eu. the revision of the community trade mark regulation (ec) no 207/2009, which is the only current legal instrument in terms of intellectual property rights that is controlled at european level, aims to adapt terminology, computerise the application procedures and register a european trade mark, to increase legal certainty by clarifying the rules and to create an appropriate framework for cooperation between the office for harmonisation in the internal market (ohim) and the national offices, so as to develop common tools in accordance with article 290 tfeu. i therefore voted in favour of this recommendation.
in writing. ‒ the purpose of this report is to reformulate the eu trade mark regulation and the directive relating to the trade mark legislation of the member states. this and the following report are part of a package of renewal of the whole trademark system at european level. the basic functioning of the trademark system is as follows: a producer of a good or service who intends to protect the name and general characteristics of his product has to register his trademark at both national and european level, defining the name and essential characteristics of his product. this register protects the producer or company against copying, forgery or unauthorisation. the report aims to harmonize, by means of a regulation, the way in which trade marks are registered at european level. among other things, it provides for a significant reduction in the cost of online registration fees. the report contains positive aspects, but also others that raise reservations, such as the blocking system, which does not exclude generic medicines. that is why i abstained.
in writing. ‒ the commission's main objective in the proposals is to foster innovation and economic growth by making trade mark registration systems across the eu more accessible and efficient. the purpose of the revision of the regulation is to adapt the terminology of the treaty of lisbon, to simplify the procedures for applying for and registering a european trade mark and to strengthen legal certainty in the clarifying provisions, to establish an appropriate framework for cooperation between ohim and the national offices for the development of common tools, and to align the reference framework with article 290 tfeu. our legislation needs to be updated to make the trademark protection system cheaper, faster, more accessible and more reliable, fighting counterfeiting and making it easier to register new signs on the market. all this is necessary because we must update our legislation to match the times we live in.

in writing. ‒ the convention on future multilateral cooperation in the north-east atlantic fisheries, to which the eu is a contracting party, aims to ensure the long-term conservation and optimum use of fisheries resources in the north-east atlantic and to bring sustainable environmental and social benefits. in accordance with that convention and the recommendations adopted by the north-east atlantic fisheries commission (neafc), control and enforcement measures may be adopted in respect of the fisheries concerned. this proposal aims to amend regulation (eu) no 1236/2010 in order to incorporate into union law the amendments to the scheme approved in the nap. the main changes introduced by these recommendations relate to the compliance of the scheme with the fao agreement on port state measures to prevent, deter and eliminate iuu fishing and the clarification that any vessel participating in a transhipment operation in the regulatory area as a receiving vessel shall report the port of landing regardless of whether the landing is in a port located inside or outside the convention area. given the fact that this is a matter of changing legislation which has already been adopted, we have voted in favour.

in writing. ‒ bosnia previously signed an association and stabilisation agreement with the eu which excluded 15 agricultural products as sensitive products for bosnia and herzegovina. if bosnia now accepts the trade review proposed by this resolution, these 15 sensitive agricultural products will be liberalised. i am therefore aware of the importance of limiting eu trade interference in third countries, especially those which are in situations of particular instability or are involved in political, social or economic processes of radical significance to their populations, as is the case in bosnia and herzegovina, and i have therefore voted against this resolution in order to maintain the protection of these agricultural products.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this agreement reached with the council for the amendment of ec regulation no 1215/2009 on exceptional trade measures for the western balkan countries. this extends these exceptional trade measures until 2020, thus giving the countries concerned and the eu sufficient time to adapt the preferences granted under the regulation to those provided for under the various ratified stabilisation and association agreements. in addition, the preferences granted to bosnia and herzegovina should be suspended as from 1 january 2016 if the eu fails to reach an agreement with bosnia and herzegovina on the adaptation of these exceptional trade concessions to take into account the traditional preferential trade between croatia and bosnia and herzegovina under the central european free trade agreement, which should have taken place since the accession of croatia to the eu in 2013. finally, i support the inclusion in the regulation of a provision for temporary suspension of exceptional trade measures in the event of serious and systematic violations of human rights, democracy and the rule of law.

in writing. ‒ we voted against ratifying this agreement between the european union and its europol agency and the united arab emirates on the fight against terrorism and organised crime. at the procedural level, the talks between the two sides have lacked not only transparency but also the involvement of democratically elected actors and representatives. as regards the substance, it is surprising that neither the agreement nor the report accompanying it mentions the trade in and trafficking in arms in this region, which is one of the most affected by terrorism in the world. the european union is a major arms exporter to the united arab emirates and we are aware of arms trafficking from the emirates to areas under the control of the daesh terrorist group. both the european union and the united arab emirates are looking the other way and are not proposing real solutions to this problem but prefer to enrich themselves by doing business with arms, so this agreement is an exercise in hypocrisy which we will not support.
in writing. we voted against, firstly because we consider it pointless to approve this strategic cooperation agreement now, because the council and the european parliament are currently negotiating a new regulation for europol (2013/0091 (cod)), in which the procedure for concluding international agreements as well as the relevant provisions and safeguards for the protection of personal data of european citizens will be significantly modified. we believe that it would be preferable for this international cooperation agreement to be adopted after the entry into force of the new regulation for europol. we are also against this report because it underlies the double standard of the eu's foreign policy in the fight against terrorism in its cooperation agreements with countries such as the uae. the eu is the second largest seller of arms to the region, weapons which have often ended up in the hands of rebel groups or terrorist groups. we therefore consider it hypocritical to support strategic cooperation agreements with the uae in the fight against terrorism if at the same time the sale of arms by the eu is helping to strengthen these terrorist groups.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution by which parliament gives its support to the council decision approving the conclusion of a strategic agreement between europol and the united arab emirates. the information exchanged could include expertise, general situation reports, results of strategic analyses, information on criminal investigation procedures, information on crime prevention methods, training activities, as well as advice and support in specific criminal investigations, excluding the exchange of personal data. europol's cooperation with the united arab emirates is justified by europol's finding that the usa is of increasing relevance in the fight against organised crime, given that the country is becoming an increasingly important platform for economic and financial crime. the agreement will therefore support and strengthen the fight against financial fraud and contribute to improving international cooperation in the field of financial investigations and other important criminal matters.

in writing. ‒ this report is based on the need for international cooperation to combat organised crime, and in particular economic and financial crime. it is therefore appropriate to approve a strategic agreement between europol and the united arab emirates to allow for the exchange of information on criminal investigation procedures and crime prevention methods, as well as the provision of advice and support in specific criminal investigations. the country's willingness to contribute to the fight against serious crime and terrorism is noteworthy. this strategic agreement will exclude the exchange of personal data, so the issue of data protection is not considered relevant in the present case. in my view, the conclusion of this agreement is necessary because it strengthens the fight against fraud in dealing with crimes such as vat fraud, intra-community fraud and money laundering, and it also increases international cooperation in financial investigations.
in writing. ‒ we in the european parliament welcome the agreement between europol and the united arab emirates as it will support and strengthen the fight against financial fraud and contribute to improving international cooperation in the field of financial investigation and other important criminal matters.
in writing. we voted against, firstly because we consider it pointless to approve this strategic cooperation agreement now, because the council and the european parliament are currently negotiating a new regulation for europol (2013/0091 (cod)), in which the procedure for concluding international agreements as well as the relevant provisions and safeguards for the protection of personal data of european citizens will be significantly modified. we believe that it would be preferable for this international cooperation agreement to be adopted after the entry into force of the new regulation for europol. we are also against this report because it underlies the double standard of the eu's foreign policy in the fight against terrorism in its cooperation agreements with countries such as the uae. the eu is the second largest seller of arms to the region, weapons which have often ended up in the hands of rebel groups or terrorist groups. we therefore consider it hypocritical to support strategic cooperation agreements with the uae in the fight against terrorism if at the same time the sale of arms by the eu is helping to strengthen these terrorist groups.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it contains the rungs to transform our energy model in line with the agreements reached at cop21 last weekend. from the socialist benches, we have managed to lead a majority that has once again spoken out in favour of more ambitious binding targets on climate and energy, 40% reduction in co2 emissions, 30% renewables and 40% energy efficiency. after this vote we encourage the council and the commission to take a step forward and to commit themselves to defending the objectives proposed by parliament. thanks to our contributions, the report sets out the way forward to ensure citizens' access to affordable energy, promotes self-consumption from renewable energy sources and proposes clear measures to fight energy poverty. the report also recognises the potential of the renewables sector as a factor of competitiveness and as a driver of innovation and job creation in europe, a sector we have committed ourselves to defending.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because i believe that the future of the european energy market depends on a decentralised and sovereign model of generation and distribution, based on public control, energy efficiency and the use of local energy sources (such as renewables, but also - in addition - traditional fossil resources with the appropriate technological and financial support). the approach of this proposal, in line with the commission's own approach, is very different: it is based on gigantic infrastructures and the inevitable concentration of european energy production in an oligopoly. this will go into the use of dangerous technologies such as nuclear and fracking (which i oppose) and a wasteful and predatory energy resource policy (as seen in the atci and neighbourhood policy demands).
in writing. we voted against the gróbarczyk report because we do not share the european commission's vision of the energy union. energy should not be the object of financial profit but should be considered as a common good and the cornerstone of the fight against climate change. there are no proposals in this report to solve the problem of energy poverty affecting four million people in spain. the report stands out for its clear support for nuclear energy, which seriously endangers our safety and our environment. plus, it leaves the door open to hydraulic fracturing.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report on the european energy union, which is fundamental. i would particularly like to highlight the section which refers to citizens' concern about hydraulic fracturing and the consequences that this technique can have for the climate, the environment and public health, and therefore hydraulic fracturing must comply with the strictest rules in these matters. in addition, member states intending to use it have to comply with the 2014 commission recommendation on minimum principles for the exploration for and production of hydrocarbons using high-volume hydraulic fracturing.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i believe it is essential to ensure the functioning of the energy market and the security of energy supply, to promote energy efficiency, energy saving and progress in renewable energy, and to promote the interconnection of energy networks, which is of particular relevance for the iberian peninsula. it is also of particular importance to continue the fight against climate change by significantly reducing greenhouse gas emissions, securing the energy supply of eu member states and ensuring an energy mix that allows for energy prices that make the european economy globally competitive.

in writing. ‒ while it is true that the european union has energy standards at european level, in practice there are 28 countries with 28 national regulatory frameworks. that is why this report is being drawn up: to achieve an integrated energy market. the aim is to increase market efficiency by making more efficient use of energy production facilities across the eu and ensuring affordable prices for consumers. among the many measures proposed is a new framework for consumers, whereby they can, for example, buy energy freely and without problems from a company in another member state. as regards renewable energy, we highlight the huge progress made by the eu, which is on track to reach its 20% renewable energy target in its energy mix by 2020. i think this report is very important because we need to create an internal energy market characterized by its homogeneity and by the integration of renewable energies into the market.
in writing. ‒ the framework strategy for a resilient energy union with a forward-looking climate policy presented by the european commission is a good starting point for moving towards the goals we have set for ourselves in eu energy policy. we want a policy which will help us to achieve the objectives we have set ourselves in terms of reducing polluting emissions and making us less dependent on the outside world, and which will also make a clear commitment to interconnections in order to protect, above all, the regions and countries most vulnerable in terms of energy.

in writing. ‒ the future of europe is also linked to its energy policy. a good mix of energy sources have to be found and we should avoid being dependent on a few specific countries for gas for example. renewable energies should be prioritised and in spain the investments in it should be protected and secured. this is not the case today. when thinking energy mix, we should also keep in mind the importance of the paris agreement, adopted by 195 governments on saturday 12 december at 19:30, is the first legally binding international agreement in which all countries have a shared obligation for taking concrete action to combat climate change and to keep global temperature rise within safe limits. this historic climate agreement gives a clear signal that the world has taken an irreversible step towards a low carbon economy. individuals, governments and businesses must now start implementing the agreement. only national policies and new investments priorities can give the paris outcome legs. this has to be kept in mind when deciding our future energy mix and electricity sources.

in writing. ‒ we are talking about a strategic report that touches on important aspects of the energy union such as energy security, the need to diversify energy sources and supply routes or the initiatives needed to achieve the completion of the internal energy market. after considerable work in the committee on industry, research and energy, a text with a broad commitment and an important political message has been produced. i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i could not vote in favour of this resolution, despite considering the energy interconnection between the member states of the union to be a positive one, because in the specific case of spain, the interconnection with france is being used as a false measure to solve the crisis in the renewables sector. interconnection is a necessary measure to be able to modulate the differences between the different countries of the union, producing potentially more resilient systems thanks to their networked configuration. however, in spain, the government is shielding itself from interconnection to deny the impact that its retroactive regulatory reform is having on the renewable energy sector. another problematic point in the interconnection between spain and france is the availability and increasing dependence on the import of french nuclear energy, inhibiting the development of an energy model that would allow it to be abandoned. it is for all these reasons that i abstained in the final vote on this report.
in writing. we voted against the eriksson report because interconnection can be an obstacle to the development of renewable energies in spain and facilitates the sale of nuclear energy from france to spain. the text - apart from some cosmetic paragraphs - does not place this prospect of interconnection of electricity grids within the framework of the development of renewables and the energy transition. it aims firstly at the completion of an integrated internal market in electricity, effectively ruling out any public control over energy production. in addition, this report promotes pcis (projects of common interest). these projects are a threat to the environment and are based on a hyper-centralized, opaque and corporate-friendly production model. we therefore believe that in a different situation from the electricity sector, where renewables are more widespread and established and the sector is more democratic, decentralised and under public supervision, interconnection would be a desirable objective, but we do not believe that its implementation at the present time will achieve these objectives on its own or with the few measures that the report details on this point.
in writing. ‒ in this parliament we continually speak of the importance of moving towards a genuine european energy market which is more integrated, competitive and sustainable. however, we still find that some countries have a strong energy dependence on imports, outdated infrastructure and very low electricity interconnections. i have supported this own-initiative report on the 10% electricity interconnection target because it is absolutely necessary to put an end to the above and to the situation of clear discrimination which some countries suffer because of their geographical location, in the case of spain. the energy interconnection with france, and therefore with the rest of europe, will not only enable us to participate in the european energy market, but also enable consumers to benefit from better prices. in addition, competition between electricity companies would be increased and the promotion of the dominant position of electricity companies would be limited, which would certainly help to tackle fraud such as the recent one by the spanish company abengoa.
in writing. ‒ i want to support the work done by the rapporteur on this report, as well as by the alternative rapporteurs. i have not followed my group in amendments nos 4 and 5, which refer to the importance of the commission's communication in reaching the 10% target, for which it will be necessary to mobilise all efforts at all levels with urgency. i also voted against the amendment which says that the projects included in the first list of icps were not sufficient to achieve the interconnection target by 2020. in my view, the projects included in the current list of icps are not enough.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i am convinced that it is essential to guarantee the 10% electricity interconnection target between eu member states in order to improve the functioning of the eu's internal electricity market. renewable energy, increased energy efficiency and a mix of sustainable energy sources with a view to energy saving and an internal energy market are important for the eu to have a stable, secure, independent, inclusive, transparent and competitive energy system that generates quality jobs and wealth in a sustainable, future-oriented economy.

in writing. ‒ the european union is continuing its efforts to make the common energy market the most integrated, competitive and sustainable in the world. the fruits of this integration can be seen in lower wholesale electricity prices, which means more choice for consumers, and in turn that energy suppliers have to offer better services at more affordable prices in order to compete with other suppliers. this report aims to ensure affordable, secure and sustainable energy through an interconnected network. in particular, the objective of 10% interconnection is to be achieved. among the many benefits that this interconnected network would provide are increased security of supply in europe, lower prices in the internal market, increased competition and support for sustainable development. however, to achieve these benefits, further intensification of regional cooperation is necessary. for all these reasons, i believe that the interconnection of electricity markets must be a priority for the european union, along with a future-oriented climate policy.
in writing. ‒ my support for the report in which meps are calling for a greater effort to achieve interconnection of electricity networks between all member states, which will ultimately mean a significant improvement and savings for consumers. in addition, improving electricity interconnection is key to boosting renewable energy and thus making progress towards climate change objectives, as well as making europe more competitive through lower electricity prices.

in writing. ‒ the benefits of interconnectivity is a strategic principle that should lead to a more resilient and robust network, and better prepared to distributed effectively the energy from renewable sources in the european network. what we demand is that these connections are made correctly, with respect to all the territory and the landscape through which these energy infrastructures passes through. that will eliminate the "energy islands" in europe, such as the spanish state, and enable to lower the energy costs that citizens and companies are paying for the energy because of the inefficiency of the government of this member state, especially when it deals with the solar panel companies.
