in writing. ‒ this report emphasises the need to boost interconnectivity in order to achieve a european energy market. promoting interconnectivity between the iberian peninsula and the rest of the eu is a key issue for spain. i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ access to microfinance is an essential support measure for economic recovery, provided that appropriate macroeconomic policies are developed (which implies, first of all, an end to austerity measures). despite the lack of a holistic approach, the report does place adequate emphasis on the difficulties of the european microfinance programme in functioning, which often does not reach its final beneficiaries. this diagnosis (which i share) and the emphasis on the social impact of these credits have inclined me to vote in favour.
in writing. this report focuses on the implementation of the european microfinance facility progress, a fund which aims to improve the capacity of intermediaries to increase the number of projects to provide microfinance and to guarantee loans on favourable terms for borrowers. we voted in favour because, with some exceptions, the fund is an instrument to support economic and social innovation and this report reinforces the public assessment of the social achievements of the funding and a more focused approach to social and territorial cohesion. the report also assesses the implementation of the fund and the impact of microfinance on eu companies, whose accountability we consider essential. positive aspects include: broadening geographical coverage, improving the gender balance in access to microfinance, access for potentially excluded customers (so that people without access to credit can develop their initiatives and smes can increase their investment capacity) or the possibility for non-bank intermediaries to enter the microfinance market without relying on a partner bank.
in writing. ‒ we share the general objectives of this microcredit system, both in terms of the contribution to european employment in the form of jobs created in new enterprises (almost 85% are microenterprises) and in terms of the reinforcement of the social orientation we are committed to. this instrument for entrepreneurs must be particularly sensitive as a lever for the incorporation of female talent into the economy and play a prominent role in the integration of refugees and immigrants into the labour market.
in writing. ‒ this report is about the implementation of the european progress microfinance facility in 2013. launched in 2010, this instrument is designed to increase the availability of microcredit loans below eur 25 000 for the creation of small businesses and support entrepreneurship among those who have difficulty accessing finance through the regular financial system. this instrument was replaced in 2014 by one of the three pillars of the so-called european programme for employment and social innovation (easi), which has been launched with the new eu financial programming period 2014-2020. this was a special instrument for unemployed and/or disabled people, to obtain financing to enable them to carry out an independent economic activity or self-employment business or even to create more jobs. the report therefore calls on the commission to continue the new easi programme along the lines of the progress programme on microfinance and social entrepreneurship. i have therefore voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ access to microfinance is an essential support measure for economic recovery, provided that appropriate macroeconomic policies are developed (which implies, first of all, an end to austerity measures). despite the lack of a holistic approach, the report does place adequate emphasis on the difficulties of the european microfinance programme in functioning, which often does not reach its final beneficiaries. this diagnosis (which i share) and the emphasis on the social impact of these credits have inclined me to vote in favour.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i am convinced that microcredit can have a major economic impact in the eu. progress is an important and effective instrument for achieving the eu's employment and social objectives under strategy 2020 as it is aimed at the unemployed and long-term unemployed, social assistance recipients, immigrants, members of ethnic minorities, people active in the informal economy or living in disadvantaged rural areas, and women. progress is certainly a success, but with adequate funding it could be possible to meet even greater demand.

in writing. ‒ it is important to have a microfinance instrument like progress in the eu. during its first years of operation it has proved its usefulness, although also some shortcomings that need to be corrected. i therefore support this parliament's report in which we make a number of observations which we hope will be taken into account in order to improve the effects of this instrument and to enable it to reach places or sectors where it is not being applied.

first vice-president of the commission.– madam president, illegal entries into the union have reached 1.5 million this year. that is almost double the total of the last five years. it clearly reveals a significant failure in how we manage and protect our external border. large-scale irregular flows have repercussions all across the eu. several member states have reintroduced internal border controls. what started as a problem at our external borders has come to put into question schengen itself. if we want to preserve schengen, we have to improve our common external border management. our biannual report on schengen adopted today could not be clearer on this. the current security risks, so tragically illustrated by the paris attacks, make action even more urgent. it is simply wrong to mix up refugees and terrorists. but we must be clear that external border controls are essential for our security. the growing number of europeans leaving, and returning, for terrorist purposes is just one of the many reasons why we cannot do without proper checks at the external borders. therefore, among the commission’s proposals today is an amendment to the schengen border code, so that everyone crossing the external border, including eu citizens, is systematically checked against common databases. this will help ensure that someone who is a security threat will be stopped at the external border, upon arrival or leaving. in this plenary in september, president juncker announced that the commission would bring forward proposals for a european border and coast guard. we have done so today, responding to calls from this house and the european council to strengthen the protection of our external borders, which is an integral part of the european agenda on migration. the common european border and coast guard will ensure the integrated management of the union’s external borders, in line with the objective set out in article 77 of the treaty. the principle underlying our proposal is one of shared responsibility. in an area without internal borders, managing external borders effectively is a matter of common interest. under our proposals, national border guards will remain the key actors in managing their section of the borders and in the day-to-day work. but they will work within a stronger european framework, with higher standards, integrated risk assessment, proper information flows and a proactive system to address deficiencies before they become problems. the national border guards will be supported, monitored and – when necessary – reinforced by a european border and coast guard agency. the agency will be able to deploy equipment and a standing reserve of at least 1 500 border guards from member states, instead of relying on ad hoc calls for voluntary contributions. all this should help correct many of the weaknesses that have hindered frontex over the years. the aim of this new integrated border management architecture is to prevent uncontrollable situations and to strengthen our collective ability to deal with crisis situations where a section of the external border suddenly comes under strong pressure. but we cannot exclude that there will still be exceptional situations where a member state is, for whatever reason, unable to cope with the situation on its own. in such rare cases, the agency itself must be able to quickly step in and assume the management of that specific part of the shared external border. this is a safety net, which like all safety nets, we hope will never need to be used. but it is essential if we are to restore the credibility of our border management system. in a way, it closes the loop. finally, the agency will also have considerably strengthened powers in the field of return. let me be very clear: europe will provide protection for those who need it. but those who have no right to be here cannot stay. today what we propose is an operational solution at eu level – a dedicated return office within the new agency working with member states and third countries to organise return operations and flights. i hope for the support of this house for these important proposals, and i hope that we can make progress quickly. in the meantime, we need to continue to work to improve the situation as it is today. much still remains to be done in italy and greece. all member states need to comply fully with their legal obligations. last week we initiated a number of infringement proceedings on the application of eurodac by greece, italy and croatia, and on asylum and migration in hungary. the commission has also discussed other aspects of the refugee crisis today, including progress following the leaders’ meeting on the western balkan route ahead of this week’s european council, which will be discussed by your house tomorrow morning. i have focused here on the proposals which are most relevant for this debate on the european border and coast guard. but it is clear that this is only one element of a wide range of actions we need in order to tackle the challenge of migration. the commission will continue to pursue work on all fronts, and we will come back early next year with further proposals, in particular, to review the operation of the dublin system. with your permission, madam president, i now pass the floor to commissioner avramopoulous to walk you through the substance of our proposals.
member of the commission.– madam president, this does not mean that what the first vice-president said was not substantial. on the contrary, i would say that it is the substantial framework of what we have proposed so far and are proposing today. so i would like to express my thanks to the first vice-president for his introduction. i have repeatedly underlined that the schengen framework is part of the solution to the current crisis. in recent months we have seen that sometimes the burden on the national border guard system of the frontline member states has proved impossible for them to cope with. it is therefore important that the european union can step in quickly to effectively support them. that is precisely what we are doing today with our proposal. now some elements of this proposal: we reinforce the obligations of cooperation and information sharing between the agency and national authorities; we set up a monitoring and risk—analysis centre, which will go hand in hand with reliable and up—to—date risk analysis, including on relevant internal security threats. recent experience shows that the liaison officers can enhance dialogue and good cooperation between the agency and the national authorities. liaison should therefore be seconded by the agency to specific member states determined on the basis of risk analysis. by also assessing the resources and equipment of the member states, as well as their contingency planning, the agency will determine whether they are well prepared to meet potential challenges and identify existing weaknesses. the agency will be empowered to require member states to take corrective measures. the decisions of the agency will be binding upon the member states. the most important element of the new agency is that it goes beyond what frontex was able to do. but we do not replace member states’ responsibilities and definitely not their sovereignty. basically, where deficiencies persist and national action is not taken, the commission – in cooperation with the member states – will be able to adopt a decision determining that the situation at a particular section of the external borders requires urgent action and entrusting the agency with the task of carrying out appropriate operational measures. the executive director will then have to submit an operational plan and will have to draw it up with the member states within two working days. the member state will have to facilitate the execution of the measures set out in the operational plan agreed with the executive director. let me emphasise here the strong preventive part of the regulation and the much stronger support it will provide to all member states with external borders. the ultimate objective is that, through stronger preventive actions, we can precisely avoid emergency situations where such interventions would be necessary. the management of the european borders will become a european responsibility in the true sense. for this, we also foresee adequate resources. currently, contributions of assets and expertise to frontex are provided on a voluntary basis. for example, in the case of greece, frontex asked member states to supply 743 guest officers, but only 447 have been provided so far. in the future, the agency will have at its disposal a sufficient number of well-trained experts with the appropriate profiles, as well as the relevant technical equipment, through a standing corps. as set out in the european union’s action plan on return, the agency should be able to initiate return operations and to assist member states with the acquisition of travel documents. for these purposes, a dedicated return office will be created within the structure of the agency. it will play a key role in return interventions. european return intervention teams, composed of escorts and return specialists, will be able to be deployed to member states subject to particular pressure on their return system. in urgent situations, rapid european return intervention teams could be deployed, either upon the request of a member state, or at the agency’s own initiative. alongside this, we are proposing to establish a new european travel document for the return of third-country nationals that should be promoted in the context of readmission agreements. this should ensure a wider acceptance by third countries. since we are creating a stronger agency, it is equally important to have an adequate complaint mechanism in case a person considers that his or her fundamental rights have been violated in the course of operational engagements by the agency. both parliament and the european ombudsman have stressed the importance of such a mechanism. i refer here to the reports by ms metsola and ms keller, which we discussed, as you will remember, during the last plenary. yes, this proposal includes sensitive parts. member states will have to agree to transfer part of their responsibilities in the framework of the treaties, while of course keeping their sovereignty. they will be part of the scheme. nothing – i repeat nothing – can happen without their cooperation. our proposal is a european answer to a european issue. it is a proposal which will prevent our freedom of movement in the schengen area from being put at stake. it is a proposal which proves that the current crisis does not divide us but, on the contrary, is becoming a catalyst for us to move ahead more united, more decided and more resolved. what we are proposing today is precisely what this parliament has repeatedly asked for: more europe. as always, i count on your support for this important step forward. (applause)

president-in-office of the council, on behalf of the vice-president of the commission/high representative of the union for foreign affairs and security policy.– mr president, i am pleased on behalf of the high representative, federica mogherini, to introduce this important plenary debate on the latest european parliament report on eu-china relations. first of all, may i congratulate mr bas belder who is a veteran of the past three reports on china. the valuable work by him, by the shadow rapporteurs and by afet as a whole is clearly visible in this very comprehensive report. as you know, the high representative’s interactions with china have been considerable this year. she held her first high-level strategic dialogue with china on the 14th anniversary of our diplomatic relations in may in beijing, and had further interactions at the 17th eu-china summit in brussels, the asean regional forum in kuala lumpur, and the 12th asem foreign ministers meeting in luxembourg. that is not forgetting china’s constant presence in the iran talks that helped make the deal. at the level of officials, there have been around 120 meetings and visits this year. members of the european parliament have also been active in seeking contact and visiting – not least, of course, the president of the european parliament. the first thing we wish to emphasise is the importance of the eu-china partnership for both sides. it is not just that eu-china relations are a vital source of economic dynamism in europe. we need to remember also that china needs the eu just as much as europe needs china. china knows that its relationship with europe is vital for its economic well-being and social stability. e-knowhow and technologies assist china’s economic and governance reforms and reduce vulnerabilities in its economy. recent concerns about the risk of a hard landing of the chinese economy as underlined in the report show that the eu has a huge stake in the success of china’s economic and governance reforms, and in supporting a well-managed transition to a more market-driven economy. it should be remembered that china’s gradual opening up of its economy to foreign investment has helped to stimulate the big economic growth needed to lift 600 million chinese citizens out of extreme poverty, of which fact china is rightly proud. the report acknowledges that the eu-china investment agreement negotiations represent one of the most important issues in eu-china bilateral economic and trade relations. the report underlines the need for balanced economic growth and the fact that the investment agreement contains disciplines for sustainable development. the eu is indeed pursuing such disciplines with china, as it does in all its agreements. we are aware of the difficulties eu companies face in their effort to access the market and operate their investments in china. we are committed to pursuing new market access opportunities, as well as overall improvements in china’s regulatory framework. in this respect, our eu delegation in beijing, in close coordination with member states, has participated actively in the open consultations conducted by the chinese government on the cyber-security, counterterrorism, ngo and national security draft laws. we will continue to put pressure on the chinese government and point out that these laws work directly against china’s economic interests, stifling creativity, innovation and precisely the inward investment that china cherishes and needs to avoid the middle income trap. the eu and its member states will continue to engage china and encourage it to see its own interests in fulfilling its commitments to uphold universal values and standards as recommended by your report. the eu special representative for human rights visited china this year and our human rights dialogue was held there two weeks ago. the report lists many areas where china’s human rights record does not live up to international standards. indeed, the situation there is deteriorating. the european parliament, jointly with the other eu institutions, must continue to make the argument that china’s stance risks leading to more, rather than less, instability in china. on the foreign policy front, we need to look at ways of encouraging china to do more multilaterally, especially in africa, the middle east and afghanistan. the high representative’s work with the chinese counterparts since she took office has convinced her that there is considerable potential to boost eu-china foreign policy and security cooperation. china can be a positive force in the world by making a more substantive contribution to global security and exercising its un security council role accordingly. given china’s increased willingness to work via the un, positive areas of cooperation could be developed, including in peacekeeping, humanitarian affairs, disaster risk management, economic and social rights, and health. china could also take greater responsibility internationally concerning migration. climate change, green growth, development assistance and the sustainable development goals are also important areas. here the relationship has the potential to grow and i have to say that china’s role in achieving the paris agreement on climate change has been positive. china’s forthcoming g20 presidency, the wto and fora such as the ebrd offer further avenues for eu-china cooperation on aspects of international governance. we note the position taken in the report on the south china sea. the eu takes no position on claims but remains strongly committed to unimpeded commerce, to the freedom of navigation, right of transit passage and to the freedom of aviation according to international law, in particular as reflected in the united nations convention on the law of the sea. the eu strongly opposes any attempt to assert territorial or maritime claims through the use of intimidation, coercion, force or any unilateral action which could cause further friction. here, as in many cases, we do consult with the united states and other like-minded partners, but naturally take decisions based on our own assessment, our own interests and values. finally, i wish to close on the issue of eu unity. the eu must be cohesive and effective in the pursuit of its own interests while upholding its values and international law. the eu-china framework should provide a guideline which strengthens member states in their own dealings with china. our negotiating strength will always be stronger when the rapporteur. madam president, commissioner, the united nations has called for the first world humanitarian summit to be held in istanbul next year. the commission has drawn up a communication on the road to that istanbul summit, which my report regards very positively and follows in its entirety. parliament will vote on this report tomorrow and the council has drawn up provisional conclusions which will probably become definitive next year, closer to the summit. my report seeks to answer three questions. the first question is: why is a world humanitarian summit needed now? secondly, what are the objectives we want to achieve in istanbul? and thirdly, what role should the european union play in this process? and to answer the first question, the answer is not that we need a summit now because a quarter of a century ago the global humanitarian system was approved and the passage of time requires a modification. no, the answer is deeper: because the world has changed dramatically in this quarter of a century, and the humanitarian system today is not able to respond to the new challenges we face. today we have more humanitarian crises, more severe than ever, at the highest level in many parts of the world. we also have greater crises due to natural causes and others due to war, and we have fewer means with which to respond to these crises, which last longer because in many cases for up to thirty years: 'conquered' crises. in the face of this situation, what are the consequences? the largest number of refugees ever: nearly 40 million in 2015, half of them practically children. more people in need of humanitarian assistance: nearly a hundred million people needed it last year. if we put them all together, they would make up the world's 12th largest country by population. to give us an idea, all of france and all of spain together would need humanitarian action. and we have fewer financial means, because in the last year, for example, there has been a need on the part of the united nations to cut off some provision of simple humanitarian aid in some parts of the world that are in dire need of that aid. in answering the second question, 'what should we achieve in istanbul?', my report has taken account of the global consultation process which has taken place in different parts of the world and which has accumulated proposals from different sectors involved in humanitarian action, and that is why i propose four lines of joint global action. first, to promote a global consensus for action that reaffirms the principles of humanitarian aid and focuses on the protection of people. this consensus must be reinforced by an action plan of at least five years to implement the commitments reached at the summit. secondly, to promote a code of conduct, a code of conduct drawn up jointly by all the participants, without a western-style vision, and based on respect for humanitarian principles and international law. we call for transparency and accountability to be the guiding values of the summit's conclusions. thirdly, we call for the creation of a global humanitarian fund to ensure the predictability, operational flexibility and security of multiannual contributions. the financial mechanisms have been voluntary so far; we also call for binding commitments. fourth, we support preparedness and response at the local and national level. on the other hand, we call for aid independence, we accept participation by the private sector where it can contribute its expertise and in accordance with humanitarian law, but above all we focus on the protection of human beings. as regards the third question, 'what should the european union do?', i refer to what the council has adopted provisionally: the union and its member states must commit themselves to helping the summit to be a success, both in the preparatory process and in the presence in istanbul at the highest possible level. they must use all their development tools, humanitarian, diplomatic, to achieve a vision that promotes specific initiatives that transform humanitarian aid. the aim of all this can only be to protect people, to protect lives, to guarantee their dignity, which is the only way to guarantee our own dignity.

member of the commission.– madam president, i am very pleased to announce the adoption by the commission of the proposal for the european accessibility act. this is, for me, also an occasion to thank you for the valuable input and support received from the european parliament throughout the preparation of this directive. as you know, there are still many obstacles preventing people with disabilities from fully exercising their rights in society. often they cannot choose where and how to live, and they face additional challenges in finding and keeping jobs or participating in education, to name but a few examples. technological innovation offers great potential for overcoming barriers. take the example of smartphones or e-banking and online shopping. these are changing our society and our economy, and they make our lives easier. if these products and services are made accessible, they offer new opportunities for people with disabilities to participate in society and to make independent choices. we see that demand for accessible products and services is increasing. this is also driven by demographic ageing. it is estimated that in 2020 120 million europeans will face a disability or functional limitation. the european union and its member states have committed, under the united nations convention on the rights of persons with disabilities, to making products, services and buildings more accessible. member states have started to legislate on accessibility independently in an uncoordinated way. unless we take action at european level, divergence in the national rules of the member states will increase. this would make it more difficult for industry to sell products and services across borders, and it is also bad for citizens who are most in need of accessible products and services. our aim with this proposal is to eliminate and prevent barriers between member states created by diverging national accessibility requirements. we want to establish europe-wide, functional accessibility requirements based on a design-for-all approach. this will allow industries to offer a wider choice of accessible products and services throughout europe at a better price. the functional requirements we propose in the accessibility act establish accessibility principles instead of prescribing detailed technical solutions. this leaves room for innovation and for flexibility. after intensive consultations with stakeholders, we have carefully selected key products and services from everyday life which are most relevant to supporting independent living. and let us be honest, at the end of the day, everybody’s quality of life can be enhanced by simple improvements to their accessibility. for example, we will all benefit from hearing train announcements in noisy stations more clearly, or from avoiding eye strain by working with enlarged document formats. this proposal is good for business, too. europe-wide requirements will make it easier for companies, in particular small and medium-sized enterprises, to sell in all the other member states, thereby boosting cross-border trade and enhancing competition. furthermore, when public authorities issue public calls for tenders for accessible goods, services or buildings, the businesses tendering will have certainty about the requirements they have to meet. the proposal also includes a common-sense clause which ensures its proportionality and balance, and that the situation of smes, particularly micro-enterprises, is well taken into account. the accessibility act complements the draft directive on the accessibility of public sector bodies’ websites, on which you have already given your first reading. discussions in the council on this web accessibility directive have progressed to the point where we hope for the trilogue to start. we are asking parliament to continue with its constructive and positive contribution and to facilitate the adoption of the measure as rapidly as possible. i believe this is a win-win situation for everybody. thanks to this proposal, the cost for companies and member states will be reduced. moreover, european action can also have a positive impact on public budgets in the long term by reducing the dependency of older and disabled persons. furthermore, this directive – and this is the most important aspect of it – will facilitate access by persons with disabilities to education, enhance their job opportunities and give them more freedom and more opportunities in their everyday life choices. to conclude, i would like to stress once more that it is the commission’s firm intention to enhance social fairness in europe. nobody should be left behind. this proposal underlines our commitment to ensure that economic growth and social progress can go hand in hand.

different races. awarding the sakharov prize to raif badawi is a historic and noteworthy day. it is, mr president, an act of bravery by you and by all those who voted for raif beneath this great dome. this prestigious award is the 15th international award granted to raif in less than a year. he is the first person from the gulf arab region to be awarded the sakharov prize. ladies and gentlemen, let me thank all of you for this opportunity and this honour. and i will conclude with raif badawi’s words:‘we want life for those who wish death to us; and we want rationality for those who want ignorance for us.’ (the house accorded the speaker a standing ovation)

in writing. we have voted against this report as the european parliament and the council have entered into informal negotiations on a new europol regulation (2013/0091 (cod)), which significantly changes the procedure for concluding international agreements, as well as the relevant provisions and safeguards for the protection of personal data of european citizens. this report concerns the approval of an agreement on operational and strategic cooperation between europol and bosnia and herzegovina, which aims at the exchange of information, including expertise, general status reports, results of strategic analysis, information on criminal investigation procedures, information on crime prevention methods, training and the provision of advice and support in individual criminal investigations. however, such agreements may concern the exchange of operational, strategic, technical or classified information. the agreement on operational and strategic cooperation also includes the exchange of personal data. in the absence of guarantees regarding the freedom and protection of personal data, among other things, we voted against.
in writing. ‒ national security is a concept that has been overtaken by the threat of international terrorism. the creation of a european intelligence system requires generalising the connections between all police forces operating on the european continent. this agreement with bosnia and herzegovina is therefore a step in the right direction.
in writing. ‒ parliament transmitted to the council its position on the council decision approving the conclusion by the european police office (europol) of the agreement between bosnia and herzegovina and europol on operational and strategic cooperation. bosnia and herzegovina suffers from serious problems of organised crime, which is why the council considered it appropriate to authorise the cooperation agreement with europol, in order to prosecute more effectively, inter alia, vat fraud and money laundering. the possibility of eu transfers of personal data to bosnia and herzegovina is, however, of concern. the european parliament therefore intends to ask the commission, if it approves the cooperation agreement, to assess the provisions contained in it, in particular those relating to data protection, and, if necessary, to make a recommendation to authorise the opening of international renegotiation of the agreement. however, the socialist group has not considered these safeguards to be sufficient and has therefore voted against them.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the mobilisation of the european globalisation adjustment fund: application egf/2015/006 ie/pwa international from ireland. europe and the world are engaged in a profound process of globalisation which, while a source of trade and wealth creation, can also entail risks to which we must be very attentive. as a result of this process, there are sectors which are more exposed to international competition, and the eu must therefore respond to those citizens who lose their jobs as a result of globalisation. the european globalisation adjustment fund (egf) provides support for workers who lose their jobs as a result of major structural changes in world trade patterns caused by globalisation or the global economic and financial crisis.
in writing. ‒ paw international, a company that installs and repairs machinery and equipment, mainly in the field of aeronautics, has laid off 108 workers at its dublin site. ireland then requested exceptional aid of eur 442 293 to help redundant workers get back to work. the case of paw international is a typical case of relocation. in the aviation sector, there is a recent trend towards maintenance, repair and overhaul being located or relocated near the centres of aviation expansion, i.e. in asia. the globalisation of trade has led to increased and unbalanced competition in this sector, which has led to job losses and loss of know-how. i voted for this report, which has the merit of reducing the social 'cash' even though i see that europe is trying above all to reduce its responsibility for relocations.

in writing. ‒ the irish authorities submitted the application for the financial contribution from the egf on 19 june 2015 and on 6 november the commission adopted a proposal for a decision to mobilise the egf in favour of ireland to support the reintegration into the labour market of workers made redundant at pwa international ltd. both parliament and the commission agree that all the criteria laid down are met. the egf finances personalised services to be offered to redundant workers: (i) guidance and career planning and development; (ii) egf training grants; (iii) training and continuing education programmes; (iv) higher education programmes and (v) grants of limited duration. i would stress that the irish authorities confirm that the eligible measures do not receive assistance from other union financial instruments and i would also stress that the financial contribution from the egf will comply with the procedural and substantive rules of the union on state aid. i therefore voted in favour of this proposal.

in writing. ‒ the spanish socialists have worked hard to ensure that the list of invasive species, which was voted on on 4 december in the joint committee on the environment, member states and the european commission, includes the species eichhornia crassipes, commonly known as the 'camel'. the proliferation of this plant is seriously endangering the habitats and biodiversity of the guadiana river basin as it passes through extremadura, and is already moving towards portugal. as provided for in regulation (eu) no 1143/2014 on the prevention and management of the introduction and spread of invasive alien species, the so-called 'invasive species list' should be adopted by means of an implementing regulation, as was done on 4 december. the approved list includes 'camelot' and will enter into force 20 days after its publication in the official journal of the european union. i have therefore voted against the rejection of the above-mentioned implementing regulation, because i consider it to be based on procedural arguments and not legally binding and, very specifically, because my main objective in this matter is the implementation, as quickly as possible, of measures to eliminate and combat the proliferation of this species and the speedy recovery of the guadiana river ecosystem.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this objection because i agree with the reasons and arguments given for it. for example, the list of 36 invasive species presented is incompatible with the provisions of the invasive alien species regulation, as the main harmful or fast-growing mammals and plants are not included. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament be informed of the elements and methodology of the risk analysis, and the species included in the list appear to have been listed on economic or political grounds. it is therefore important that the criteria in this list be reviewed and the list be re-drawn up.
in writing. we voted in favour considering that some invasive species have not been included in the list submitted by the commission although they should have been and that some of those included do not cause a significant negative impact on biodiversity/ecosystem.
in writing. ‒ the problem of many invasive species included in the commission's list is well established in some european areas, including particularly sensitive areas. the situation also requires immediate action at european level to act in a coordinated manner and prevent the reintroduction of these invasive species from other areas of europe where action has not been taken. that is why we voted against this report.
in writing. ‒ the commission has submitted the first list of invasive species to regulation 114/2014 by means of an implementing act and parliament, by means of this objection, opposes it, considering that it should have been a delegated act with the participation of parliament and not an implementing act in which parliament is not consulted. however, this list includes species that pose a serious threat to our biodiversity, such as the water jasmine or camalote, which is currently a huge problem in the guadiana river and specifically in extremadura. so, although parliament should have been consulted when this list was drawn up, i voted against the objection and in favour of supporting the adoption of the list as soon as possible to alleviate the devastating effects this plague is having. i understand the commission's arguments for speed in the procedure for adopting the list and i hope that updates to the list will be made by means of delegated acts, with the involvement of parliament.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this objection calling on the european commission to repeal its implementing decision (eu) 2015/2279 of 4 december 2015 authorising the placing on the market of products consisting of, containing or produced from genetically modified maize nk603 × t25 (mon-øø6ø3-6 × acs-zmøø3-2). the current procedure for authorising genetically modified food and feed is not working well and, until it is improved, any authorisation of such products should be suspended. the commission was obliged to submit a draft to parliament for its opinion before approving the marketing of this type of maize, but, despite the opposite position of parliament's committee on the environment since 1 december, it did not wait to hear parliament's opinion. i am not only in favour of this objection, but i also support any future objections to the authorization of gmos, and the commission should make a legislative proposal that respects the right of member states not to authorise gmos for human and animal feed on their territory.

in writing. ‒ we welcome the adoption of this own-initiative report which ran in parallel with the taxe committee, although it focused more on recommendations than on the investigation of the facts. we welcome the incorporation in the report of some clearly socialist achievements, such as the inclusion of compulsory country-by-country reporting, the harmonization of the corporate tax base (biccis), protection for whistleblowers, the establishment of a common definition of tax havens, or the automatic exchange of tax rulings. however, we must regret that, because of the opposition of the ppe, alde and ecr groups, we have not been able to put forward in the plenary the creation of a european fund to assist whistleblowers, as well as more regulation for tax consultancy firms. the commission has already taken a number of initiatives to improve the situation of the taxpayer, and i am sure that the commission will be able to take action in this area.
in writing. ‒ the internationalisation of production requires tax harmonisation and a clear accounting definition of taxes, in order to avoid the tax avoidance practices common among large companies. in addition, it is necessary to improve the transparency of the tax provisions of the member states in order to avoid a repetition of scandals such as luxleaks. these aspects are covered in the report, although not yet sufficiently. i believe, however, that the proposals will enable the commission and the council to be pressured to completely reformulate the current corporate taxation policies, which is why i voted in favour.
in writing. we voted in favour of this report, in which the european parliament calls on the commission to resume its work on establishing a consolidated tax base for multinationals, which would help to combat tax evasion and downward tax competition between countries. the document also contains other very interesting elements such as the protection of whistleblowers and greater control of 'tax advisory' companies, which in many cases are accomplices in tax evasion.
in writing. ‒ we share the need to add transparency, progressiveness and fairness to corporate tax policy across europe to prevent competition between national tax systems on the basis of avoidance and what has been called 'tax creativity'. we share the recommendations to prevent tax avoidance and the use of tax havens and agree to protect persons who, with their testimony, help to identify and sanction evasive or fraudulent behaviour. this protection should include the creation of a fund fund funded by money recovered from fraud or evasion so that the perpetrators of these testimonies can avoid the problems caused by their cooperation with the tax authorities. we welcome the measures to control international companies, and we particularly welcome the shared definition of a 'tax haven'.

in writing. ‒ the european parliament considers that the need to increase transparency in the field of company taxation is due to the fact that various multinationals have concluded agreements with the luxembourg authorities to reduce their tax obligations when economic activity in luxembourg was practically non-existent. these 'aggressive tax planning' practices are not only taking place in luxembourg, but are spreading across the eu. obviously, these activities should not be tolerated under any circumstances, but even less so when we are in a delicate economic situation. if multinational companies do not contribute to the implementation of these measures, this would be a contradiction with the principle of the single market, since smaller national companies would not be able to compete in these unequal circumstances. this would also have a major impact on national governments, which, in view of the reduction in tax revenue, would be forced to consider cuts in the services provided by the state. in conclusion, i believe that this report should be adopted so that the eu can implement measures of coordination and transparency in the field of corporate taxation in the union and thus achieve favourable conditions for companies that are part of the european single market.

in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it has a strong focus on the so-called 'indispensable' role of the us, and calls for a common approach with the us on china, arguing that this will help to promote the interests of the eu, something i do not agree with. it also goes into detail on issues that are not the responsibility of the eu or this report, such as denouncing china's alliance with russia to block un action on syria. that is why, although i found some interesting points on which i voted in favour, i had to vote against the adoption of this report as a whole.
in writing. we have abstained on this report. the report has two lines which make it impossible for us to vote in favour: firstly, it calls for the signing of trade agreements with china and for the exploitation of the trade opportunities of china's rise. secondly, it calls on china to follow the eu and the us in international politics. on the other hand, the criticisms of repression and lack of freedom are well developed. paragraph 62 and the second part of paragraph 51 have also been adopted, which were key for us. the second part of the agreement mentions the mandatory inclusion of a human rights clause in any bilateral treaty with china and, in paragraph 62, it imposes obligations on european companies in terms of labour law, regardless of whether they are covered by chinese law or not.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report because it contains some very necessary warnings to the chinese regime for its repeated violations of fundamental rights, and also relates to specific cases as striking as the arrest of two hundred lawyers of opposition. i also share the calls for cooperation with international stabilisation and peace operations in ukraine or syria, and i find particularly interesting the call to avoid military threats to taiwan in the event of possible secession. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.
in writing. ‒ the eu and china mark 40 years of diplomatic relations. this report, which i voted for, welcomes the recent reforms undertaken by president xi jinping, notably the new silk road initiative and the launch of the asian investment bank. the eu and china should cooperate closely on issues such as the fight against terrorism and crime, nuclear non-proliferation, control of weapons of mass destruction, cybersecurity, regulation of financial markets and climate change. however, the lack of transparency, information and statistics on government intervention in the chinese economy, as well as dumping, state subsidies and non-respect of intellectual property rights, is of concern. the commission has already taken steps to ensure that the eu's financial instruments are used to the full. as regards respect for human rights, i condemn the restrictions on freedom of expression, freedom of association and assembly, freedom of religion, the persecution of human rights defenders, bloggers and ethnic minorities, and the application of the death penalty, which must be abolished.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this report because it has a strong focus on the so-called 'indispensable' role of the us, and urges the vice-president/high representative to develop a common approach with the us on china, arguing that this will help to promote the interests of the eu, something i do not agree with. it also goes into detail on issues that are not the responsibility of the eu or this report, such as denouncing china's alliance with russia to block un action on syria. that is why, although i found some interesting points on which i voted in favour, i had to vote against the adoption of this report as a whole.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour because i am convinced that good relations and close cooperation between the eu and china can bring great benefits to both sides, and that the eu-china strategic partnership is therefore of vital importance. we must also bear in mind that china is an important trading partner of the eu, with a huge and expanding market. however, the eu must be vigilant in defending human rights and basic freedoms in china.
in writing. ‒ we have abstained on this report. the report has two lines which make it impossible for us to vote in favour: firstly, it calls for the signing of trade agreements with china and for the exploitation of the trade opportunities of china's rise. secondly, it calls on china to follow the eu and the us in international politics. on the other hand, the criticisms of repression and lack of freedom are well developed. paragraph 62 and the second part of paragraph 51 have also been adopted, which were key for us. the second part of the agreement mentions the mandatory inclusion of a human rights clause in any bilateral treaty with china and, in paragraph 62, it imposes obligations on european companies in terms of labour law, regardless of whether they are covered by chinese law or not.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report as it is a comprehensive report on eu-china relations on the occasion of the 40th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two powers, covering political, economic, environmental, social and human rights issues. on the political front, the report praises the reforms undertaken by president xi jinping. on the economic front, the report highlights the importance of the negotiations for an eu-china investment agreement that started in 2013 and shows concern about the slowdown in the chinese economy and the consequences for the global market. as regards the internal situation in china, concern is expressed at the deterioration of environmental conditions in some cities in the country. the human rights chapter is quite comprehensive. it condemns restrictions on freedom of expression, association and assembly, and religious freedom, as well as the persecution of human rights defenders, bloggers and ethnic minorities, and condemns the use of the death penalty. the report also calls for the eu to take action to prevent the spread of the virus.
in writing. – china is a key international power and one of the eu’s most important partners. the year 2015 marks the 40th anniversary between the eu and china, and it is significant to enhance the eu-china strategic partnership, which plays a key role in the relations between the eu and the people’s republic of china in terms of finding key answers to a range of global concerns (environmental protection in particular) and identifying common interests. it is also important that the eu maintains a constructive dialogue with china to encourage china’s transition to the rule of law and respect for human rights. these are the main reasons why i have voted in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the eu and china need to step up their economic and political relations. i support the report by my colleague, mr antonio lópez-istúriz, in which we call for the promotion of a comprehensive strategic partnership over the next decade, which would be very beneficial for both sides from the economic, commercial and political point of view.

in writing. ‒ i am still worried about certain fundamental freedoms and human rights not being respected in china. moreover internet freedom is not guaranteed. i note that a strong contradiction exists between the official chinese aspiration to the universality of human rights and the worsening human rights situation. recently there has been a worsening of the situation of human rights and freedoms in china that started in 2013 and has intensified an already existing crackdown on the population, limiting the space for expression and peaceful advocacy for civil society even further. the tibetan people but also the uighur population remain discriminated against and their freedom and fundamental rights are being violated. let me remind you once again that his holiness the dalai lama is not asking for independence of tibet but through the memorandum he proposed more autonomy for tibet. china should grasp this opportunity. freedom for tibet means freedom for china.

in writing. ‒ the report aims to acknowledge the weight and importance of china as an eu trading partner, while highlighting some of the eu's concerns, such as the transition of the chinese economy towards a more sustainable model, concerns about human rights in the asian giant, and the problems with hong kong and tibet. we are therefore talking about a report which not only highlights the need to continue to maintain relations with the asian giant but also points out important points on which work needs to be done. i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ the socialists have managed to consolidate a progressive position for the next world humanitarian summit (istanbul, may 2016), we put the emphasis on the key elements to reform the current humanitarian aid system, such as: ensuring the defense of humanitarian principles and the impartiality of aid from a political point of view and putting in place mechanisms to ensure that governments are accountable for their roles and responsibilities in the field of protection of the most vulnerable. key measures proposed include a global consensus on humanitarian action, greater transparency and accountability in the use of aid, a code of conduct for donors and a global fund to secure and provide sufficient resources to tackle crises such as ebola and syrian refugees. we regret that the extremist groups (left and right) in the european parliament did not support this report or abstained, without committing themselves to the protection of the most vulnerable, to human dignity and to respect for human rights. they have left in the gutter the empowerment of women, the education of children and the protection of migrants and refugees in emergency situations.
in writing. ‒ while this report can be seen as a call to strengthen and improve humanitarian aid through the support of the world humanitarian summit, making a positive reference to the need for the eu to be guided by principles of solidarity, responsibility and accountability, these wishes remain on wet paper as long as the eu and its member states maintain the current trade and foreign policy, which is the cause of many of the conflicts and the impoverishment of third countries. the report contains positive aspects such as the need to make a greater effort to guarantee the right to education in humanitarian emergencies, the inclusion of a gender approach in the entire humanitarian aid cycle and even the recognition of the need for minimum humanitarian standards to promote essential public services. but once again, it brings together public services and the private sector in a veiled defense of public-private partnerships, thus enabling european transnational corporations to do business and profit from the vulnerability of people in humanitarian emergencies. i have therefore abstained.
in writing. we abstained from voting on the report on the world humanitarian summit because, despite including positive references, such as on gender and migrants' rights, in line with the current trend in the privatisation cooperation/aid system, the report calls for a strong push for the inclusion of the private sector in humanitarian action. the report thus calls for action strategies to be aligned with business objectives. the report also calls for more public-private partnerships in humanitarian action, which have proven to be ineffective and often result in privatisation of profits and socialisation of risks and losses. we believe that humanitarian policy must be purely public policy and not be at the service of private interests; only then can we have a robust humanitarian policy capable of meeting the challenges we face.
in writing. ‒ i have supported this report because it introduces proposals and interesting contributions to improve the international humanitarian assistance system, for example by creating a global fund and reforming some concepts that are essential today to deal with some of the most serious humanitarian crises, such as that of migrants. it is essential to recognise the role of host countries and to incorporate causes into the definition of a forcibly displaced person. we also find it appropriate to mention groups that suffer double victimization in humanitarian crises, such as the disabled, women, minors or lgbti groups.
in writing. ‒ the humanitarian aid system is not up to the challenge of the ebola crisis, syria, yemen or iraq. we are seeing this with the current migration crisis in europe. this is the beginning of a new process to adapt and improve the effectiveness of humanitarian action. the first world humanitarian summit will take place in istanbul on 23 and 24 may 2016. this report summarises the main concerns of a sector threatened by the unprecedented increase in conflicts and disasters, due to lack of resources, access and protection. the council is also urged to ensure a firm common position so that our voice is heard globally and we are recognised not only as one of the largest donors, but also as a body that takes responsibility and leads by example. the report proposes three axes for joint global action: a global consensus on humanitarian action, a donor code of conduct and a global fund for humanitarian action. all this to reaffirm respect for international humanitarian law, protection, the independence of aid and the need to adapt the humanitarian response system to local needs.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the statement that we are experiencing a series of unprecedented humanitarian crises to which we must give the appropriate response. the world humanitarian summit will take place in istanbul in may 2016 with the aim of reconfiguring the humanitarian system and adapting it to a rapidly evolving emergency landscape in order to make humanitarian action more effective, efficient and appropriate. the eu, as the leading donor and key global actor, has a responsibility to drive the search for more effective and efficient ways of delivering humanitarian aid.

in writing. ‒ i fully support this resolution. whereas growing challenges, such as urbanisation, rapid population growth, demographic changes, the prevalence and increased strength of natural disasters, environmental degradation, desertification, climate change, numerous long-lasting and simultaneous conflicts with regional impact and resource scarcity, added to the consequences of poverty, inequality, migration, displacement and fragility, have consequently dramatically increased the need for humanitarian response throughout the globe. whereas the number of people in need has more than doubled since 2004 to over 100 million in 2015; whereas 250 million people are affected by humanitarian crises; whereas the number of forcibly displaced persons has reached its highest point since world war ii at nearly 60 million, including almost 40 million displaced inside their own countries; whereas over half of the world’s refugees are children. i call on the eu and its member states, as the largest donors and key operational actors, to lead by active example, and i emphasise that all eu humanitarian actions should be guided by the principles of solidarity, responsibility and accountability, and should be designed to ensure that vulnerable people are protected, both physically and psychologically.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it represents important political support for the steel industry in europe. the sector is facing a serious crisis due to the full opening of trade borders, which is preventing the maintenance of this industry which is essential for quality employment in europe. the report includes some points which we do not accept, such as the harmonization of state aid to the sector or the energy union, but it also includes fundamental measures such as the adjustment of coal at the border, the unequivocal commitment to recycling and the circular economy for the recovery of the sector, the development of public investment, the promotion and maintenance of social dialogue and the promotion of regional economic cohesion. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the community's financial resources are used to the full.
in writing. we abstained because we consider the base metals industry sector to be a strategic sector in the economy, and the document contains positive aspects in terms of social, labour and worker protection issues, and contains broad lines to support this industry and to transform it into an environmental issue. but on the other hand, we are radically opposed to their position and their tacit tolerance of the ets and the atci. the environmental guidelines set out in the document seem to us to be wholly inadequate.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the report on the development of a sustainable european base metals industry. i have differed in several votes from my group's line because i think the report has very important points such as calling for ensuring that future trade agreements include provisions that improve export opportunities and market access for european base metal products or urging that compensation be harmonised and, where justified, applied at european level to ensure a level playing field with global competitors and between european producers and to ensure effective protection against carbon leakage.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour in view of the difficulties facing the steel and aluminium sectors in the eu. i am convinced that industrial policy must have the tools and means to be able to achieve the low-carbon transition. the european base metal industries must find a strategy to adapt to the new climatic, economic and social situation, setting an example in terms of efficiency and effectiveness in the consumption of energy and raw materials, and not disappearing from the future industrial landscape. the allowances, which are currently allocated according to historical series, are to be granted for current production, not past production. we must also give free allowances to companies that invest more in innovation and improvement of their facilities to reduce their polluting emissions.

in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this own-initiative report, as since 2008 more than 60 000 direct jobs and 100 000 indirect jobs have been lost in a sector with more than 500 steelworks in 23 member states and an annual production of around 180 million tonnes. the main measure called for in the report is that, in the absence of a legally binding international agreement on emission reductions that would establish a level playing field for industry, a border carbon adjustment should be established, i.e. imports should be subject to the same rules for the purchase of emission allowances on the carbon market as european producers on the basis of the carbon content of imported metals. importers of base metals would thus be obliged to declare to customs the co2 emitted for the production of metals sold on the european market and should comply with the same rules imposed on european producers in accordance with the wto principle of non-discrimination between like products.
in writing. ‒ this report stresses the need to support the european base metals industry as it is particularly vulnerable to external competition (dumping prices) and to the union's energy and climate policy. it also addresses the problem of the acute loss of competitiveness of several commodity industries, such as those of aluminium, steel and other non-ferrous materials. in this context, it is necessary for the european union to contribute to the construction of an efficient framework for these sectors, which will enable them to recover their economic potential. the reindustrialisation of europe through investment and the promotion of a level playing field at international level in the sector are therefore the priorities of this report. since these objectives are of great importance for the economy and the progress of our nations, i am in favour of the report and have voted in favour.
in writing. ‒ the eu needs a clear policy on the development of a sustainable european base metals industry. this is a sector which has been subjected to a major crisis in recent years and hence the appropriateness of the european parliament's report, in which we advocate solutions for this industry, without forgetting our commitments in the fight against climate change.

madam president, i did not vote for this report either. i consider it very unfortunate that in this situation and at this moment we are receiving a report on the floor of the european parliament against one of the members of the european union. i am convinced that at a time when the unity of the european union is threatened, and i am therefore following up on my predecessors, when the credibility of european integration is declining, for example in the czech republic, but also in other central european states, in the visegrad countries, the adoption of such resolutions will certainly not increase the credibility of european integration and the european union in the eyes of our voters in central europe. i consider that move unfortunate, counterproductive. in my opinion, it doesn't solve anything, and i just want to respond and say one more sentence. there are countries that do not fulfil their schengen obligations and do not adequately guard their external borders. we do not criticize these countries in our resolutions. resolutions cannot really solve the situation of the european union.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of this resolution because it denounces the serious deterioration of fundamental rights in hungary and the degradation of its democracy. the text expressly condemns the ultra-nationalist government of viktor orban, a leading member of the european people's party, which is using the clout of its very large parliamentary majority to impose legislative reforms that undermine pluralism, judicial independence, the separation of powers, freedom of the press and minority rights. while today the european parliament is calling for sanctions against the orban government and disapproval of its deplorable behaviour, just over a month ago the popular european people, led by mariano rajoy, applauded the hungarian prime minister's response to the refugee crisis and cheered his xenophobic message in madrid, in which he said that 'refugees move like an army' and that they cannot be given access to 'a european life'. the people should be ashamed of this kind of action and condemn these xenophobic and anti-european statements, for by their silence they become accomplices of the xenophobia and racist ultranationalism advocated by the hungarian prime minister, viktor orban.
in writing. ‒ we supported this resolution because of the current political situation in hungary which could put at risk even its continued membership of the union, as it is violating a large part of the fundamental rights enshrined in the treaties. if so, article 7 teu, which provides for measures to be taken in such cases, could be implemented. we voted in favour of the resolution because we share the concern about the violation of fundamental rights and the attacks on minorities living in hungary, and the need to take action in this regard.
in writing. we voted in favour because the resolution on the situation in hungary focuses on the defence of human rights and denounces the fact that the hungarian government is pursuing policies which systematically violate fundamental and democratic rights in hungary. the government of viktor orban has launched multiple public campaigns criminalizing refugees, portraying them as criminals, invaders and terrorists. as part of the european union, hungary must comply with its legal and international commitments. it is also intolerable that a country of the union, with its government at the head, is pursuing xenophobic policies and spreading messages of intolerance in the face of the greatest humanitarian crisis in recent years, instead of being a guarantor of the human and fundamental rights of those fleeing war, hunger and poverty.
in writing. ‒ i am watching with concern and bewilderment what is happening in hungary. concerned about the serious danger to the rule of law and perplexed by the lack of support from many members who claim to be defenders of rights and freedoms but who have cowered in their condemnation of hungary. the systemic changes introduced into the legal framework of hungary by the government since 2010 and resulting in the recent legal measures on asylum, borders or criminal code are a prime example of the serious deterioration of fundamental rights and freedoms in the country. the european parliament, through this resolution, once again shows its concern but goes one step further by calling for the activation of article 7 of the eu treaty against hungary, which provides for sanctions in the event of a serious breach of the union's founding values. i personally think that there are and that is why i strongly support this request.
in writing. ‒ we welcome the opening of an infringement procedure against hungary in relation to asylum policies, but we also believe that the conditions exist in this member state for the commission to apply the framework for the protection of fundamental rights immediately, as there is undoubtedly a systematic violation of fundamental rights enshrined in the charter of the european union. we also believe that it is particularly appropriate to commission a specific report to the libe committee, which should make a reasoned proposal to the council to act in accordance with article 7 (1) of the teu. that is why we voted in favour of these points in the original text of the joint resolution.

mr president, ladies and gentlemen, we are faced with two decisions by the european patent office which we cannot ignore because of the insecurity and the damage they can cause to the research sector in the primary sector. it is important that the current model is maintained, with the exception of breeders, so that they can continue to use plant varieties in the agricultural sector. while it is true that intellectual property must be protected in order not to discourage certain research, for years the existing model has worked very well and has allowed a very important work of innovation and development to be carried out throughout europe, which has achieved, thanks to the efforts of all europeans who are engaged in it, that our agri-food sector reaches the highest levels of quality and recognition at world level. the breeders' exemption must be respected and research must continue to be allowed without the need to pay licences or fees. otherwise we would be starting to dig the grave of an innovation sector which is very important for the economy of many european regions, especially those linked to the rural world. and not only that, but the diversity of plant varieties we now enjoy would be seriously endangered and the freedom of choice of european consumers themselves would be restricted. i hope that the commission is fully aware of this problem which now arises from the harmful interpretation of article 53 (b) of the european patent convention by the european patent office in its recent decisions. i also hope that the means will be put in place to ensure the future of the agri-food sector.
mr president, commissioner, today all the spokesmen for all the groups in this house largely agree that the decisions of the high board of appeal of the european patent office have raised serious doubts, and i therefore believe that it is your duty to clarify this situation as part of the commission's work and especially its portfolio. these great doubts concern a directive, a model - the current one - which, i agree with mrs herranz, is a good model, but the decisions taken by the european patent office are not so good, especially the last two decisions which have caused this great confusion. in particular, it is necessary to clarify articles 4, 12 and 13 in order to ensure such legal clarity in the prohibition of patenting products obtained by essentially biological processes. as i said, the european patent office has created this doubt, which the commission must certainly clarify as regards the application of the rules.
on behalf of the alde group. i think that everything has been said, mr president, and you must be a little tired of hearing the same things over and over again, commissioner. when all the political groups in the european parliament agree and there is no dissenting voice, it means that reality is what it is and that it is extraordinarily hard. i do not want to list here the violations of human rights, something that has already been done very well by those who have used the word before. i mean, if we don't go from words to facts and statements to realities, what we're doing is a beautiful exercise in rhetoric. the necessary response from the union is therefore to ban certain people from entering the european union, freeze their assets in europe and warn tourists about the kind of tourism they are going to encounter. otherwise, we will be left with an exercise in hypocrisy, saying the right thing but doing the wrong thing.
in writing. ‒ the volkswagen emissions scandal has once again exposed the complicity of the commission and the member states with the large multinational groups, since leaks in the press have shown that they knew about the manipulation of emission limits long before the us environmental agency uncovered the scandal. these responsibilities and political connections need to be clarified urgently as the commission plans to legislate again on emission limits and to reformulate (downwards and with the participation of the multinationals themselves) transatlantic motor vehicle regulation through the atci. i think this is a fundamental issue, not only because of the serious impact of emissions on the quality of life of europeans (especially in urban areas), but because the scandal is so big that the future of the car industry and its workers in europe is at stake. the setting up of a committee of inquiry should make it possible to clarify responsibilities and lay the foundations for an environmentally and socially sustainable industrial policy.
