in writing. ‒ the eu is stuck with a slow and fragile recovery, with poverty rates still unabated and unemployment rates still excessively high. recovery cannot depend on monetary policy and the european central bank alone. a change in economic policy is needed, as is more ambition in the european project, to avoid future crises, so that the recovery is fair and balanced and reaches all european citizens. economic and monetary union (emu) must therefore be completed. the internal demand needs to be improved and investment encouraged. in addition, emu must be given its own fiscal capacity for the euro area, a strengthened budget and the achievement of banking union. i have therefore voted in favour of this resolution. because i believe that the legislative package presented by the european commission on 21 october is not sufficient to achieve these objectives, especially as regards democratic legitimacy. parliamentary scrutiny and debate at european and national level need to be improved to ensure democratic accountability and thus improve citizens' perception of euro area governance.
in writing. ‒ the five presidents' proposal for the reform of economic and monetary union is a mixture of vague and contradictory promises regarding a social pillar for economic governance alongside real neoliberal proposals that legitimize and deepen the current european technocratic interventionism. this is the case with tax or competition authorities, which were set up to give a veneer of independence to the inevitable european recommendations of further cuts in public spending or the elimination of labour rights. i have voted against this resolution because it not only means accepting this proposal but also means going backwards in relation to the commission's proposals, by endorsing only their most regressive aspects. the only apparently positive aspect - the demands for greater parliamentary control - is in this context just another exercise in legitimising (and not in democratically deepening) european economic policies.
in writing. we voted against this resolution, which is the european parliament's response to the report by the five presidents, which proposes to move forward with the integration of european monetary union by centralising economic and fiscal powers, which would consolidate the neoliberal and austerity governance model. the parliament's report accepts this view, claiming only for itself more powers and control over the other institutions. we believe that monetary union as it exists today is a source of imbalances and is doomed to failure if it continues to be subordinated to the interests of the big european central banks. the democratization of monetary union is only possible through a profound democratization of european society and the european economy which puts the interests of the people before those of the powerful.
in writing. ‒ i voted in favour of the resolution on the achievement of economic and monetary union in europe, noting the european commission's proposal to strengthen emu and recognising that steps have been taken in the right direction. but i also voted in favour of one of the amendments tabled by the gue/ngl group which recommends that urgent measures be taken in respect of the productive sectors which are vital to the different economies and which play an essential role in the potential development of each country. it concerns more specifically support for micro-enterprises, smes, cooperatives and local administrations.

in writing. ‒ the reform of our monetary zone is as urgent as it was six months ago. completing the banking union is as urgent as before. ensuring that private creditors pay first, and that the european supervision is accompanied by a european fiscal backstop prevents the failure of the banking system in a member state from forcing its government to cut its public services. it is also important to build a eurozone fiscal capacity that enables europe to react to asymmetric shocks, particularly to help those member states that have a sudden hike in unemployment. the european union loses more and more credibility every time that a member state decides not to comply with a european directive. it is happening with the two-pack and it happened with the six-pack. 1. a stronger political legitimacy for the european commission. the disrespect of national governments for european rules shows that only with a strong commission, with a president elected and accountable directly to the european people will be able to enforce the rules. 2. more regulations, less directives. the goodwill of national governments cannot be taken for granted. their application of european directives is at least ambiguous. if we want a strong and more integrated eurozone, we need first to comply with our own rules.

in writing. we abstained from this vote as we considered that this report does not add any added value to the annual reports developed by non-governmental organisations which have more experience, expertise and human and material resources on the ground. moreover, these can be assumed to be more objective than the report commissioned by a political group. although the report introduces relevant issues such as the human rights consequences of the crisis and the policies implemented, homophobia, climate refugees and the search for lasting solutions to deal with the refugee crisis, it contains intolerable biases for a report that is presented as neutral, such as the absence of concrete criticism of human rights violations within the eu, or the commitment to sanctions against trading partners who are systematically violating rights.

in writing. ‒ i express my deep concern that human rights and democratic values such as freedom of expression, freedom of thought, conscience and religion and freedom of assembly and association are increasingly under threat in many parts of the world, including under authoritarian regimes. a growing number of human rights defenders are under attack worldwide. i call on the eu and its member states to enhance their efforts to effectively place human rights and democratic values at the heart of their relations with the wider world, as they committed to so doing in the teu. in order to be credible, the eu should start by respecting democratic and human rights in its own member states, starting from the right of its catalan european citizens, for example.

in writing. ‒ we are talking about a report that highlights the tools the eu has in its hands to promote respect for human rights and democratic principles, and calls for the effective implementation of the new eu action plan on human rights and democracy for the period 2015-2019 or the promotion of the visibility and role of the eu special representative for human rights. i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour of this report.
in writing. ‒ i voted against this resolution on the 20th anniversary of the dayton peace agreement because today tensions between the three peoples are still very much present and it cannot be said that the agreement has effectively ended the divisions or resolved them, and yet this report only expresses satisfaction with the results of the agreement, and argues that the tensions which still persist between the three peoples can only be resolved by making progress in the process of european integration. we believe that the eu should let the people of bosnia and herzegovina determine their political future for themselves, and we believe that it is time to put an end to the international protectorate and to put an end to the international military presence in bosnia and herzegovina. that is why we have voted against this resolution.
in writing. we have abstained from voting on this resolution on the 20th anniversary of the dayton agreement, which ended the civil war in bosnia and herzegovina, as it refers to previous resolutions of this one-sided parliament in which not all the parties are treated equally. the resolution also states that the best way to promote reconciliation is through european integration, a matter on which the people of bosnia and herzegovina themselves should freely decide. we consider it essential that the people of bosnia and herzegovina should be allowed to decide freely on their future and on the form of state in which they wish to live.
in writing. ‒ i have signed this resolution on the dayton peace agreement which recalls the importance of the signing of the dayton peace agreement and pays tribute to all the victims of the tragic war in bosnia and herzegovina, and expresses our sincere condolences to the families of those who lost their lives. it also welcomes the results achieved in the return of refugees and internally displaced persons, reconstruction and restitution of property, in line with the provisions of annex 7 to the dayton agreement.

the commission has already submitted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. ‒ i voted in favour of this report because it proposes measures to make progress towards effective control of arms exports. in adopting the common position, the member states set themselves criteria to be able to refuse export licences if necessary, but the absence of control and sanction mechanisms and the lack of transparency on the part of some governments have unfortunately made it easier for weapons coming from europe to end up in the hands of criminals and/or terrorists. the report adopted proposes arrangements for independent verification (the pp's refusal has prevented progress towards the creation of a european control authority), as well as sanction mechanisms for those states which do not comply with the common position and the strengthening of surveillance and control systems to prevent the diversion of exports. i believe that the report is an excellent basis for further progress in the interests of global security, the credibility of the eu's foreign policy and the european commitment to human rights. i regret, however, that the pp, podemos and the united left abstained in the final vote on a text which represents a significant step forward in disciplining the arms trade in the eu.
in writing. ‒ i voted against the valero report (a8-0338/2015) on arms exports: implementation of common position 2008/944/cfsp because, while it deals with a fundamental issue such as the regulation of arms exports and recognises the need to establish sanction mechanisms for those who breach these agreements, the text insists on supporting the supply of defensive weapons in cases of 'legitimate defence', which can lead to very complex situations, and supports the decision of some member states to supply arms to ukraine, deploring the lack of cooperation and coordination in this regard. in disagreeing with this perception, my vote has been against it.

in writing. we abstain on this text because, while it introduces considerations on the appropriateness of increased controls on the export of arms and military technology to third countries which we consider necessary, it legitimises the arms industry as a fundamental pillar of both the eu's industrial development and the eu's foreign policy. we can advocate the creation of mechanisms of cooperation and dialogue between countries that do not support or participate in the global arms build-up, and for a productive model for the eu and its member states that does not depend solely on the development of an activity that is primarily and ultimately based on aggression, the death of people and the destruction of living environments.

in writing. ‒ this resolution was adopted following an oral question with the same title. i have supported the oral question because i consider it necessary to ask the commission for an explanation of the recent decision of the european patent office which envisages the possibility of patenting plant traits even when these traits have been developed from essentially biological breeding techniques or could be obtained by such techniques, thus extending the possibility of granting patents. however, i voted against this resolution because, as the amendments proposed jointly by the greens/efa, the efdd and the gue/ngl groups were not adopted, it is a much less ambitious resolution than the existing one (resolution 2012/2623 (rsp) of the european parliament of 10 may 2012) which defended the rights of farmers and a total exemption from patentability of products derived from cultivation and conventional cultivation methods. this new resolution does not provide for this full exceptional status (which would ensure that, for example, farmers would not be sued for accidental pollination by patented varieties).
in writing. we have voted against this resolution because the oral question to the commission is sufficiently clear in itself. in addition, parliament has already expressed its opinion on this matter in a satisfactory resolution on the exemption of patents on certain products in 2012, and we therefore do not think it necessary to reopen this matter with a new resolution that goes into this issue.
in writing. ‒ this resolution arises from a question to the commission on the implications of the decision of the high board of appeal of the european patent office (epo) allowing the patenting of plant characteristics, including those developed or obtained by essentially biological plant breeding techniques. this decision has implications for the innovation capacity of the plant breeding sector in developing new varieties and for the risk of monopolies on the food market by reducing the diversity of products offered to consumers. in the united states, legislation allows for the patenting of genes and the registration of new varieties (the set of genes that an individual has is registered, not each gene separately). we therefore ask the commission to clarify the existing rules in order to avoid the conflict between european regulation of plant varieties and the possibility of extending the patenting of genes from the usa to europe, in the sense of avoiding the possibility of patenting genes in the european union.

in writing. ‒ while i share the deep concern expressed in the resolution at the situation in burundi, aggravated by the murder by the security forces of at least 87 people, and at the rapid deterioration of the humanitarian situation in the country, i could not vote in favour of this text, since it welcomes the sanctions imposed by the eu and calls for the withdrawal of all european funding in the country, except strictly humanitarian funding, which currently consists mainly of european development fund funds. the resolution makes no reference to the responsibility of european multinationals and the former colonial powers for the plundering of resources or the promotion of conflict in the country. the european parliament also calls on the commission to take the necessary steps to ensure that the eu's external relations are not jeopardised by the threat of a military coup in burundi.

in writing. ‒ virunga is africa's oldest national park, but despite its protected natural area status, it has for decades been threatened by armed groups engaged in poaching, illegal logging and other forms of illegal resource exploitation, which has led to its inclusion on the list of world heritage in danger. the report stresses that irreversible damage could be caused by oil exploration and exploitation; considers it unacceptable that concessions in the park were granted in 2007 to the french oil company total and the british soco international, thus breaching the paris convention, the 1992 convention on biological diversity, the ramsar convention and congolese legislation itself. as this resolution calls for legally binding measures to bring to justice companies that have circumvented national laws and international treaties, and advocates the development of a comprehensive protection strategy for this park to the greatest extent possible, including the fight against corruption and the investigation of acts of violence committed against human rights defenders active in the drc, i have voted in favour.
in writing. we voted in favour of this resolution on virunga national park, a unesco world heritage site and the most diverse park in africa, as we consider it important that the european union and the member states coordinate joint and effective action to address the problems of violence arising from the struggle for the natural resources of the park. the resolution also urges urgent action to ensure the accountability of extractive companies in the area and compliance with international standards on social, environmental and human rights.
in writing. ‒ i would like to thank the rapporteur for the work she has done to negotiate this resolution on the protection of the virunga national park in the democratic republic of congo. it refers to the absolute need to prevent irreversible damage to this park, which was designated a unesco world heritage site in 1979 and a world heritage site in danger in 1994. i also regret that the park has become one of the most dangerous places in the world for wildlife conservation.

in writing. ‒ i want to stress with my vote the absolute need to prevent irreversible damage to the vnp, which was designated by unesco as a world heritage site in 1979 and as a world heritage site in danger in 1994. i deplore the fact that the vnp has also become one of the most dangerous places in the world when it comes to wildlife conservation; i note with deep concern that armed groups have been involved in illegal exploitation of the park’s natural resources through mining activities and charcoal production used both to sustain their military operations and for personal gain. i also deplore the fact that armed groups have been involved in large-scale poaching for food purposes and for war-sustaining trade in ivory and bush meat. let me emphasises that irreversible damage to the vnp could occur as a result of the exploration and exploitation of oil or other illegal activities.
in writing. ‒ we are talking about a resolution which aims to highlight the important need to protect the virunga national park, declared a world heritage site by unesco in 1979, and which today faces threats of exploitation and exploration that put it in grave danger. i therefore consider it necessary to vote in favour of this resolution.
